Expect a diagnostic first session before any weekly plan is fixed.
Bring recent test papers or a report card if you have one.
Lesson mode, home, online or hybrid, is set upfront and can change later.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does IB one-to-one tuition in Gurgaon need?
faqs.answer: It depends mainly on programme stage and how close the exam session is: typically one to three hours a week for PYP or early MYP, two to four per subject in mid-MYP, and two to five hours per HL subject through the DP depending on the time of year. IB Gram sets a starting range after the first diagnostic session rather than quoting a fixed number upfront, because a DP1 student in September and a DP2 student two months before May need very different weekly loads even within the same subject. The number is reviewed and adjusted every four to six weeks rather than fixed for the whole year.

faqs.question: How is a one-to-one session actually split between content and practice?
faqs.answer: Most sessions move through new content first, then guided practice, then past-paper or criterion-based questions, though the balance shifts across the year. Early in a topic more time goes to explaining and worked examples; once the basics are solid, practice with immediate correction takes over; and close to a test or the exam session itself, sessions lean almost entirely on timed past papers and markschemes, since that is where the specific way marks get awarded becomes clear. A tutor who spends every single session only teaching new content, with no practice or past-paper time, is not running a balanced plan.

faqs.question: How often is the plan reviewed, and what actually changes?
faqs.answer: The plan is reviewed roughly every four to six weeks. At each review, IB Gram or the tutor checks whether the student is closing gaps at a reasonable rate, whether current hours still match the calendar, and whether a subject that has stabilised can lose time in favour of one that has slipped. Sometimes nothing changes and that is fine; the point is that someone is actually checking rather than letting the same hours run unexamined for a whole term. Parents can also request an earlier review if something feels off before the scheduled date.

faqs.question: What happens to tuition hours right before mocks and the May session?
faqs.answer: Hours usually step up in the weeks leading into mocks and again before May, then step down sharply once exams end. A typical shape is one extra weekly session on past papers six to eight weeks before mocks, steady hours in the final two weeks before mocks rather than cramming new content, a redirection toward the papers that lost the most marks after mocks, and near-total past-paper practice in the final stretch before May. After the exam session, hours drop quickly, since there is nothing left to prepare for until the next academic year begins.

faqs.question: Will one-to-one tuition make my child dependent on a tutor?
faqs.answer: It can, if the plan is built badly, but a well-run one should reduce dependence over time, not increase it. The tutor's job is to make independent study more effective, teaching error-log habits, exam technique and self-checking the student can use alone, rather than doing the thinking for them in every session. If hours keep climbing every review without any sign of the student working more confidently alone between sessions, that is worth raising directly, since it usually means the plan needs adjusting rather than more hours added.

faqs.question: Can one plan cover several IB subjects in the same week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually does once a student is past the earliest years. A typical DP student's plan covers two or three subjects across the week, often with different tutors for different subjects since IB Gram matches specialists to each subject rather than assuming one tutor teaches everything well. Scheduling multiple subjects does mean being realistic about a student's evenings; three subjects a week on top of a full school day, sport and CAS commitments needs careful spacing, not back-to-back sessions that leave no time to do the practice set.

faqs.question: Will the tutor travel to our home in Palam Vihar or Sushant Lok on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tutoring on weekday evenings is the default across most Gurgaon corridors, including Palam Vihar and Sushant Lok, subject to tutor availability and a workable slot once school, buses and activities are accounted for. Older, denser areas like Palam Vihar are generally easier to reach on short notice than corridors further out on the Dwarka Expressway or toward Manesar. Families are asked for a rough sense of the week's fixed commitments upfront so the plan is not built around a slot that turns out to clash with something else.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session gets missed because of school activities?
faqs.answer: A missed home tuition session gets rescheduled where the tutor's week allows, rather than simply dropped, since Gurgaon school calendars regularly clash with tuition slots through sports days, extra classes or exam weeks. Persistent clashes are usually better solved by moving the fixed weekly slot rather than rescheduling every single week, so if a Tuesday keeps getting eaten by cricket practice, it is worth changing the plan's slot instead of fighting the same clash repeatedly. Occasional one-off misses are normal and do not affect the plan's overall review.

faqs.question: Does online one-to-one tuition work as well as home tuition for IB?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, reasonably well, though not identically. A shared whiteboard, screen-sharing a graphic calculator and annotated past papers cover the bulk of what a Maths, Economics or English session needs, and online removes travel time entirely, which helps families in corridors like Manesar and NH-48 south, further from where specialist tutors are based. Where home still has an edge is catching small paper-based errors in real time and holding the attention of younger students, so many families run a hybrid plan, home for subjects that need close paper work and online for the rest.

faqs.question: Can a one-to-one tutor help with the Maths IA or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only as guidance, never as a ghostwriter. Within a one-to-one plan, a tutor can help narrow a research question, check whether a method is actually feasible, review a draft against the real criteria, and point out where marks are typically lost, all within the IB's academic integrity rules. The tutor does not write or substantially rewrite the student's own words, both because that breaks those rules and because it defeats the purpose of an assessment meant to show the student's own thinking. Sessions for this kind of support are usually spaced around draft deadlines rather than weekly.

faqs.question: What if there is no visible progress after a month of tuition?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly rather than waiting, since four to six weeks is roughly when the first review should already show some movement, even a small one. If nothing has changed, IB Gram can look at whether the hours, the tutor, or the plan itself needs adjusting, and a different tutor can be arranged if the fit seems to be the actual problem. Occasionally the honest answer is that the target itself was unrealistic for the time available, in which case the plan should be reset around a more realistic goal rather than simply continued unchanged.

faqs.question: Can we try a session before committing to a weekly plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, a trial or demo session happens before any regular weekly commitment is agreed. It lets the tutor run a short diagnostic, working through a few questions or a piece of writing, and lets the family see whether the pace and explanations feel right before hours and a schedule are fixed. If the trial does not go well, IB Gram can suggest a different tutor rather than the family being locked into the first match, and the weekly plan itself is only set once everyone is satisfied with the fit.

Sometimes nothing changes and that is fine; the point is that someone is actually checking rather than letting the same hours run unexamined for a whole term. Parents can also request an earlier review if something feels off before the scheduled date.

mainEntity.name: What happens to tuition hours right before mocks and the May session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hours usually step up in the weeks leading into mocks and again before May, then step down sharply once exams end. A typical shape is one extra weekly session on past papers six to eight weeks before mocks, steady hours in the final two weeks before mocks rather than cramming new content, a redirection toward the papers that lost the most marks after mocks, and near-total past-paper practice in the final stretch before May. After the exam session, hours drop quickly, since there is nothing left to prepare for until the next academic year begins.

mainEntity.name: Will one-to-one tuition make my child dependent on a tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, if the plan is built badly, but a well-run one should reduce dependence over time, not increase it. The tutor's job is to make independent study more effective, teaching error-log habits, exam technique and self-checking the student can use alone, rather than doing the thinking for them in every session. If hours keep climbing every review without any sign of the student working more confidently alone between sessions, that is worth raising directly, since it usually means the plan needs adjusting rather than more hours added.

mainEntity.name: Can one plan cover several IB subjects in the same week?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it usually does once a student is past the earliest years. A typical DP student's plan covers two or three subjects across the week, often with different tutors for different subjects since IB Gram matches specialists to each subject rather than assuming one tutor teaches everything well. Scheduling multiple subjects does mean being realistic about a student's evenings; three subjects a week on top of a full school day, sport and CAS commitments needs careful spacing, not back-to-back sessions that leave no time to do the practice set.

mainEntity.name: Will the tutor travel to our home in Palam Vihar or Sushant Lok on a weekday evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, home tutoring on weekday evenings is the default across most Gurgaon corridors, including Palam Vihar and Sushant Lok, subject to tutor availability and a workable slot once school, buses and activities are accounted for. Older, denser areas like Palam Vihar are generally easier to reach on short notice than corridors further out on the Dwarka Expressway or toward Manesar. Families are asked for a rough sense of the week's fixed commitments upfront so the plan is not built around a slot that turns out to clash with something else.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a home session gets missed because of school activities?

acceptedAnswer.text: A missed home tuition session gets rescheduled where the tutor's week allows, rather than simply dropped, since Gurgaon school calendars regularly clash with tuition slots through sports days, extra classes or exam weeks. Persistent clashes are usually better solved by moving the fixed weekly slot rather than rescheduling every single week, so if a Tuesday keeps getting eaten by cricket practice, it is worth changing the plan's slot instead of fighting the same clash repeatedly. Occasional one-off misses are normal and do not affect the plan's overall review.

mainEntity.name: Does online one-to-one tuition work as well as home tuition for IB?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most subjects, reasonably well, though not identically. A shared whiteboard, screen-sharing a graphic calculator and annotated past papers cover the bulk of what a Maths, Economics or English session needs, and online removes travel time entirely, which helps families in corridors like Manesar and NH-48 south, further from where specialist tutors are based. Where home still has an edge is catching small paper-based errors in real time and holding the attention of younger students, so many families run a hybrid plan, home for subjects that need close paper work and online for the rest.

mainEntity.name: Can a one-to-one tutor help with the Maths IA or Extended Essay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only as guidance, never as a ghostwriter. Within a one-to-one plan, a tutor can help narrow a research question, check whether a method is actually feasible, review a draft against the real criteria, and point out where marks are typically lost, all within the IB's academic integrity rules. The tutor does not write or substantially rewrite the student's own words, both because that breaks those rules and because it defeats the purpose of an assessment meant to show the student's own thinking. Sessions for this kind of support are usually spaced around draft deadlines rather than weekly.

mainEntity.name: What if there is no visible progress after a month of tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raise it directly rather than waiting, since four to six weeks is roughly when the first review should already show some movement, even a small one. If nothing has changed, IB Gram can look at whether the hours, the tutor, or the plan itself needs adjusting, and a different tutor can be arranged if the fit seems to be the actual problem. Occasionally the honest answer is that the target itself was unrealistic for the time available, in which case the plan should be reset around a more realistic goal rather than simply continued unchanged.

mainEntity.name: Can we try a session before committing to a weekly plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a trial or demo session happens before any regular weekly commitment is agreed. It lets the tutor run a short diagnostic, working through a few questions or a piece of writing, and lets the family see whether the pace and explanations feel right before hours and a schedule are fixed. If the trial does not go well, IB Gram can suggest a different tutor rather than the family being locked into the first match, and the weekly plan itself is only set once everyone is satisfied with the fit.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you set up a year-long IB tuition timetable at home?
contentBlocks.body:
A home tuition calendar for the IB starts with the same conversation as any plan: board, programme stage, subjects, and the specific school your child attends, since school calendars in Gurgaon rarely line up exactly even for schools a few kilometres apart. IB Gram also asks, early, about the corridor you live in and which evenings school buses, sport or music already claim, because a calendar that ignores the family's actual week gets rebuilt within a month anyway.

IB tuition at home in Gurgaon starts with this conversation, not with a spreadsheet of hours. From there, IB Gram maps out a rough shape for the year before assigning a single hour: a steady weekly pattern through each term, a heavier stretch in the run-up to mocks and the May session, and a deliberately lighter or paused stretch through the major breaks. This shape gets shown to the family before a tutor is even shortlisted, so there are no surprises about how the year is expected to move.

A tutor is then matched not just for subject and level but for a workable weekday evening or weekend slot in the family's own corridor, since a tutor who cannot realistically make a Tuesday 6pm slot in, say, Sushant Lok is not a fit even if their subject knowledge is excellent. A trial session confirms both the academic fit and the practical one before the year's calendar is locked in.

Once the first month has run, IB Gram checks in again: has the weekly slot actually held, has the pace matched what the school's own calendar demanded, and does the shape mapped out for the rest of the year still make sense. Families are free to reshape the calendar at any point, not just at the official review points.

contentBlocks.heading: How does the school-year calendar differ by IB stage?
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme (PYP), ages 3 to 12, has no external examinations and is built around six transdisciplinary themes explored through units of inquiry, so a PYP calendar for home tuition follows the school's own unit breaks rather than an exam timetable. There is usually no reason to run sessions right through a break at this stage; a pause that matches the school's own pause, with maybe a light revisit of reading or numeracy, tends to serve a young learner better than continuing at full pace through the holidays. The PYP exhibition in the final year is the one calendar point worth building extra sessions around.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP), MYP 1 to MYP 5, spans roughly ages 11 to 16 across eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria, A to D, with the criterion total converting to a final grade through the IB's own grade boundaries. A calendar here has to track more than just subject content: the Personal Project deadline in MYP 5 (the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4) sits on the calendar like a second exam season, and a home tuition schedule that ignores it tends to collide with it in April or May, right when a Diploma-bound sibling's other subjects also need attention. It is exactly this kind of clash an MYP tutor in Gurgaon has to plan around, not just teach around.

The Diploma Programme (DP) calendar is the busiest: DP1 and DP2 across six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 more points toward the 45-point maximum. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May session, and each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before that. A home tuition calendar for DP2 essentially has two exam seasons to build around each year, the school's own mocks and the real thing, which is why an IB DP tutor in Gurgaon needs the full-year calendar, not just the subject content, before proposing a single slot.

MYP: the Personal Project (or Community Project) sits like a second calendar season.

contentBlocks.heading: Which subjects fit which slot in a home tuition week?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics, split into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) at Higher or Standard Level, tends to work best on a weekday evening slot soon after homework, while working memory for method steps is still fresh, rather than pushed to a tired Friday night. HL AA in particular, heavy on proof and calculus, benefits from a slot early enough in the evening that a student is not fighting fatigue on top of difficult content.

The sciences, Physics, Chemistry and Biology, carry Internal Assessment work on top of content, and IA sessions, data analysis, write-up structure, reviewing a draft against the criteria, sit more naturally on a weekend slot with more room than a compressed weekday hour allows. HL Biology's larger volume of additional content is often why families running two HL sciences ask for one weekday slot for content and a separate weekend slot dedicated purely to IA and past papers.

English A and English B behave differently in a weekly calendar: English A leans on essay practice and oral rehearsal for the Individual Oral, both of which work well as a slightly longer weekend session rather than a rushed weekday hour, while English B's structured writing and comprehension practice fits a shorter, more frequent weekday slot better. Theory of Knowledge suits a fortnightly rather than weekly slot, since it runs on discussion rather than content coverage, and Extended Essay mentoring clusters around specific draft deadlines rather than occupying a fixed weekly slot at all.

None of this is rigid. A family with only weekend availability can still run an effective plan for every subject; the point is that a slot chosen with the subject's own rhythm in mind, rather than whatever hour happens to be free, tends to need fewer emergency reschedules through the year.

contentBlocks.heading: How do Gurgaon school terms shape the home tuition calendar?
contentBlocks.body:
A Gurgaon school year is punctuated by fixed points that a home tuition calendar has to work around rather than compete with: unit tests through each term, parent-teacher meetings, sports days and CAS commitments, school-set mock examinations, and the May exam session most Gurgaon IB schools use, with a minority entering students in November, largely for retakes. Schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge each set their own term dates, mock weeks and break dates, so a tuition calendar built for one school rarely transfers cleanly to another, even for two families a short drive apart. This is why IB Gram asks for the specific school by name early on, not to build any relationship with it, but to build the calendar around the dates that school actually keeps.

This is the part of IB tuition at home in Gurgaon that a one-off weekly booking misses entirely: knowing where the calendar is headed before the family gets there. Festival breaks, Diwali in particular, and the longer winter and summer breaks, tend to be the points where a home tuition calendar needs the most deliberate thought: continue lightly through the break, pause entirely, or run a short intensive stretch right before or after it. None of these is automatically right; a DP2 student six weeks from mocks over Diwali needs a different answer than a PYP student on the same calendar.

The tutor's role stops at the tuition itself. Report cards, parent-teacher meetings and the school's own scheduling decisions stay between the family and the school; the home calendar is built to sit around that structure, not inside it.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid across a full IB year in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB home tutors in Gurgaon typically anchor this calendar: a verified tutor at the family's own table, week after week, in whichever corridor the family lives, which tends to suit the IB's paper-heavy subjects, Maths and the sciences especially, where catching a working-out error in real time matters, and where a consistent physical routine helps a younger PYP or MYP student settle into the school year.

Online sessions, sometimes searched as IB online tuition Gurgaon, earn their place at specific points in the calendar rather than as a permanent substitute: a week when travel is genuinely difficult, the monsoon season's occasional disruption on some Gurgaon roads, a family travelling during a break, or a subject where the nearest suitable specialist sits in a distant corridor like Manesar or New Gurgaon. A shared whiteboard, an annotated past paper, and a screen-shared graphic calculator cover most of what a Maths or Economics session needs, and online removes the evening's travel time entirely.

Hybrid calendars, running home sessions most weeks with online swapped in for particular weeks or subjects, are common through a full IB year rather than the exception. A family might run home tuition through most of the term and switch a Physics IA review session online simply because the specialist tutor for that subject is based across the city. IB Gram sets this pattern deliberately from the first conversation, and either mode runs subject to tutor availability.

The honest trade-off across a full year: home tuition wins on routine, attention and catching paper-based errors, but a fixed weekly slot is more exposed to disruption from travel, festivals and unpredictable school timings; online is more resilient to all three but asks more of a student's own focus, particularly a younger one. Most calendars end up using both at different points across the twelve months rather than committing to one for the whole year.

contentBlocks.heading: How are tutors checked for a year-long home tuition calendar?
contentBlocks.body:
Beyond subject, level and programme stage, an IB tutor at home in Gurgaon is checked for something a one-off lesson does not need to test: whether they can actually hold a fixed weekly slot in the family's corridor across an entire school year, through traffic, festival weeks and the ordinary churn of a term. IB Gram confirms this before shortlisting, since a brilliant tutor who cannot reliably make a Thursday 6:30pm slot in, say, Golf Course Extension Road is not the right match for a calendar built around that exact slot.

Parents should ask their own questions before the first session: how the tutor plans to handle a clash with mocks or a festival break, whether they have taught through a full academic year with another family before, and what their own approach is when a session needs to move at short notice. A tutor who has clearly thought about the calendar, not just the syllabus, tends to be the steadier long-term fit.

The trial session checks both things at once, academic fit and practical fit: does the tutor's pace and explanation suit the student, and does the proposed slot actually work once school pickup, homework and dinner are accounted for. If either does not hold up, a different tutor can be requested before the year's calendar is set.

For home visits, most Gurgaon societies register visitors at the gate, so tutors are briefed to carry identification and confirm timing in advance, particularly important across a year where the same tutor will be entering the same society dozens of times. Parents are welcome to sit in on early sessions, and most step back once the weekly routine is established.

contentBlocks.heading: What does an IB home tuition year in Gurgaon look like, month by month?
contentBlocks.body:
Most Gurgaon school years fall into a recognisable rhythm, even though exact dates differ school to school: a first term running from spring into the monsoon months, with early unit tests and a settling-in period where a home tuition calendar usually starts light, one steady weekly slot per subject while the tutor and student find their rhythm together. Through the monsoon months, occasional travel disruption on some corridors is worth building a little flexibility into the slot for, rather than assuming every week will run exactly on schedule.

The stretch from the Diwali break through the winter break is where many families either add a session or pause one, depending on the calendar ahead: a DP2 student with mocks looming in the new year often adds a session here, while a PYP or early MYP student may simply pause through the break and pick back up after. January and February typically carry the school's own mock examinations for DP students, and this is where a home tuition calendar leans hardest on past papers and markschemes, closely matched to what the mocks are actually testing.

March and April, in the run-up to the May exam session, are when hours are at their highest for DP2 students, almost entirely timed past-paper practice by this point, while younger students further from any exam season usually stay on their steady term-time slot. Once the exam session itself is over, hours drop sharply, and the summer break becomes either a genuine pause or a short catch-up stretch for a subject that fell behind earlier in the year, depending on what the family and the incoming year actually need.

Missed and rescheduled sessions are a normal part of any year-long calendar, not an exception to manage around apologetically: a school activity, an illness, an unexpected family trip. What matters is how they are handled. A single missed session gets rebooked where the tutor's week allows; a slot that keeps clashing week after week, say, a Tuesday eaten by cricket practice every single time, is usually better solved by moving the fixed slot itself rather than fighting the same clash all year. Holiday intensives, a short run of extra sessions concentrated into a break, work well for a specific, bounded goal, closing a gap in one topic before the next term starts, but rarely work as a substitute for the steady weekly rhythm the rest of the year runs on.

contentBlocks.heading: What should progress look like across a full year?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress across a year should be visible in stages, not just at the very end: fewer repeated errors within the first month or two, steadier performance on unit tests through the middle of the year, and a mock result in January or February that reflects the work put in rather than arriving as a surprise. A calendar that shows no change at any of these checkpoints is worth questioning well before May, not after.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a full year of tuition does not change that. There is no single best IB tuition at home in Gurgaon for every family; what a well-run home tuition calendar can honestly offer is a clear, ongoing read of where the student stands against real mark schemes and criteria at each stage of the year, a structure that adapts as the calendar moves rather than staying static from April to March, and an honest flag well ahead of May if a target looks out of reach given the time left.

For Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work, which usually surface at specific points on the calendar rather than every week, the tutor's role stays guidance throughout the year: discussing a research question when it comes up, reviewing a draft against the criteria near its deadline, and explaining where marks are typically lost. The tutor does not write or substantially rewrite the student's own work at any point in the year, both because it breaks the IB's academic integrity rules and because it defeats what the assessment is meant to show.

A full year also has honest limits. A calendar cannot compress two years of gaps into a single term just because mocks are close, cannot substitute for a school conversation if a subject choice is structurally wrong, and cannot guarantee that every week will run exactly as planned. Good home tuition adapts to the year as it actually unfolds; it does not pretend the year will go exactly to plan.

contentBlocks.heading: Setting up your child's home tuition calendar in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Every week, IB Gram fields requests for IB tuitions at home in Gurgaon, or simply IB home classes, phrased in a dozen different ways, and each one starts the same way: board, programme stage, subjects, grade, the school your child attends, and your corridor. IB Gram uses this to sketch a rough shape for the year, when a weekly slot should hold steady, where mocks and the exam session will need extra sessions, where breaks call for a pause, before a tutor is even proposed.

The first session is diagnostic as much as practical: the tutor works through a few questions or a short piece of writing to see where the real gaps are, and also confirms whether the proposed slot, day, time, corridor, actually holds once school pickup and homework are accounted for. Parents are welcome to sit in on this first session.

Useful to have ready beforehand: a recent test paper or report card if there is one, the school's own term and break dates if you have them to hand, and a rough sense of which weekday evenings are already taken by other activities. faqs.question: How are missed sessions handled through the year?

faqs.question: Are holiday intensives worth it, or is a steady weekly slot better?

faqs.question: What if our weekday evening slot keeps clashing with school activities?

faqs.question: Does the calendar look different for a PYP or MYP student versus a DP student?
faqs.answer: Yes, considerably. faqs.question: How much does tuition ramp up before mocks and May?
faqs.answer: For a DP2 student, hours typically climb over the two to three months before each, an added past-paper-focused session six to eight weeks out, steady hours rather than new content in the final two weeks, and near-total past-paper practice in the run-up to May itself. faqs.question: Can the tutor help with the Extended Essay or an IA across the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, but as guidance tied to the calendar's own deadlines, not as a weekly fixture and never as a ghostwriter. faqs.question: What if progress stalls partway through the year?
faqs.answer: Raise it as soon as it is noticed rather than waiting for the next scheduled check-in, since a calendar built around a full year still needs adjusting mid-course if something is not working. faqs.question: Can we try a session before committing to a full-year calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, a trial or demo session runs first, before any weekly slot or year-long calendar is agreed. It checks two things at once: whether the tutor's teaching suits the student, and whether the proposed slot actually holds once school pickup, homework and the family's own week are accounted for. If either does not work, IB Gram can suggest a different tutor or a different slot before the calendar for the year is set.

h1: IB Personal Tuition in Gurgaon: A Plan for One Student
heroTitle: One Student, One IB Tuition Plan in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: A personal IB tutor is not a sixth subject specialist; it is one person who sees the whole student. This page sets out how that plan is actually built in Gurgaon: the profile mapped in week one, the targets a student owns, and the honest limits on IA, EE and TOK support.
introSummary: IB personal tuition Gurgaon usually means home tuition built around one student rather than one subject: a tutor, or a small team of subject specialists coordinated by one lead, who maps a student's gaps, pace and confidence before deciding what a single lesson should cover. That home tuition foundation matters from the first session, because a personal plan built without knowing where a student actually struggles is just a normal subject tutor with a longer title. This page sets out how IB Gram builds that plan in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana: the learning profile built in the first weeks, how PYP, MYP and DP students each need something different from personal tuition, where Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support stops well short of doing the work, and how the plan changes at every review.

contentBlocks.heading: How We Build a Personal IB Tuition Plan in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB personal tuition Gurgaon searches often come from a specific moment: a report card that surprised the family, a student who says school is fine but grades say otherwise, or a sibling comparison that is not fair but happens anyway. Whatever the trigger, we start the same way, with a conversation that is longer than a normal tutor booking call, because a personal tuition plan is only as good as the profile it is built on.

That first conversation covers programme stage, subjects, recent school reports, and, as honestly as a parent can manage, where the student's confidence actually sits rather than where the family wishes it sat. We ask about attention span in a normal evening, not just in an ideal one, and about learning differences the school has already flagged, since a plan that ignores a diagnosed difficulty is a plan that will need rebuilding within a month.

From there we shortlist a lead tutor, sometimes supported by one or two subject specialists for a DP student carrying six subjects, matched to the student's programme stage and the family's sector. A trial session, at home or online, lets the family see the working style before committing to a term. Families comparing IB home tutors in Gurgaon across six separate subjects are often, without quite realising it, looking for exactly this coordination: what IB personal tuition Gurgaon families are usually buying, whether they use those words or not, is one person who sees the whole picture, not six unconnected tutors.

The steps below describe a first month, but personal tuition does not stop being personal after week four. Every review resets the plan against what has actually changed, not what was hoped for in week one.
items: 1. A longer first conversation maps programme, subjects, school reports and confidence.
2. A learning profile is drafted: gaps, strengths, pace and attention span.
3. A lead tutor, with specialists if needed, is matched and trialled.
4. Targets are agreed with the student, not set over their head.
5. The plan is reviewed and adjusted every four to six weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: What Stage Is Your Child In?
contentBlocks.body:
The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three programmes most Gurgaon families encounter: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) across five years from roughly age 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme (DP), a two-year course usually taken in Grades 11 and 12. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page or the International Baccalaureate. Personal tuition looks different at each stage, because the thing a student needs help with is not the same at nine as it is at seventeen.

In the PYP, learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, from Who We Are to How We Organize Ourselves, explored through units of inquiry, and there are no external examinations; personal tuition here is mostly about building reading, numeracy and inquiry habits, not exam technique. The MYP assesses every subject against four criteria, A through D, each scored out of 8, with the total converted to a final grade of 1 to 7; a personal tutor at this stage often spends more time on how to answer a criterion-based task than on raw content, since that is usually where MYP students lose marks that have nothing to do with what they actually know.

The DP asks for six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, plus up to 3 further points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, for a maximum of 45 and a minimum of 24 to pass, subject to the IB's own failing conditions. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session, with a minority using November; personal tuition for a DP student is usually about triage across six subjects at once, not depth in any single one, which is a different skill from single-subject tutoring.
items: PYP: ages 3-12, six transdisciplinary themes, no external exams.
MYP: five years, four criteria (A-D) per subject, graded 1-7.
DP: two years, six subjects, HL and SL, graded 1-7 each.
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points to the DP total.
Most Gurgaon IB schools use the May exam session.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Personal Tuition Focuses Inside Each IB Subject
contentBlocks.body:
A personal tutor coordinating IB Mathematics AA or AI first confirms which course and level a student is on, since Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation ask for different kinds of thinking even when the topic overlaps, and HL Mathematics carries 240 recommended teaching hours against SL's 150. The personal plan's job here is less about re-teaching content the school has already covered and more about closing the specific gap between what a student understands and what a Paper 1 or Paper 2 question actually demands under time pressure.

In the sciences, Physics, Chemistry and Biology, a personal tuition plan tracks the Internal Assessment alongside the theory syllabus, since the two run on separate but overlapping clocks, and a student who is coasting through classwork can still be behind on their IA timeline without anyone noticing until the school deadline is close. English A, whether Language and Literature or Literature, needs timed essay practice marked against real criteria, and the Individual Oral is its own separate skill that content revision alone does not build.

Across every subject, the personal tutor's real job is deciding what this specific student needs this specific month, not delivering a fixed syllabus. A student strong on content but weak on command terms, define versus evaluate versus discuss, needs different sessions from one who understands the terms but cannot recall the content, and a plan that treats both the same way wastes the time personal tuition is meant to save.

HL carries 240 recommended teaching hours; SL carries 150.
Science IAs run on their own timeline alongside theory content.

A lead tutor coordinating a DP student's six subjects here can often bring in a specialist for one subject without disrupting the family's evening routine, since travel between DLF's own sectors is short; IB personal tuition DLF Phase 3 families search for typically finds a lead tutor within a short, predictable commute.

Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area, taking in Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1, Sectors 29, 40, 45 and 46, and Greenwood City, sits close enough to DLF that a single lead tutor can often manage a personal plan across both corridors without the evening schedule becoming unrealistic. Evening traffic on SPR can stretch what looks like a short trip on a map, so a slightly earlier home slot, with online catching the later specialist sessions, tends to work better than fixing everything to one physical location.

contentBlocks.heading: The School Pressures Behind Every Personal Tuition Plan in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Families across Gurgaon's international schools, including Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge, carry broadly similar pressures once a student reaches the DP, even though each school runs its own calendar. IB Gram does not state which programme or curriculum any named school follows, and is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here.

A DP1 student is usually juggling six new subjects, early Internal Assessment planning and CAS commitments in the same term, while a DP2 student is managing mocks, predicted grades, finished IAs and the Extended Essay deadline against May exam preparation. A personal tutor's coordination role matters most exactly here, when six separate deadlines from six separate subjects land in the same few weeks and nobody at school is tracking all six for one student.

MYP students face a quieter but real version of the same pressure: criterion-based tasks across eight subject groups, the Personal Project in MYP 5, and for schools that offer it, an optional eAssessment. A personal tutor at this stage often does more to prepare a student for the DP's workload than for any single MYP grade, building the habit of managing several subjects' demands at once before the DP makes that unavoidable. That groundwork is often what separates a DP1 student who copes from one who is overwhelmed by week three.

DP2: mocks, predicted grades, the Extended Essay and May exams overlap.
MYP: criterion-based tasks across eight subject groups, Personal Project in MYP 5.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Fits One Student in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where most personal IB tuition plans start, because a lead tutor working face to face reads a student's confidence and fatigue far more accurately than a screen allows, and a younger MYP student especially benefits from someone physically present while a study routine is still being built. The cost is reach: the strongest specialist for a rare HL subject combination is not always within a comfortable evening commute of a family's sector.

Online sessions solve that reach problem directly. A DP2 student needing a specific HL Physics or Economics specialist can work with a tutor anywhere in Gurgaon, or beyond it, without either side losing an evening to travel, and shared whiteboards and annotated past papers cover most of what a subject session needs. IB online tuition Gurgaon families choose for a hard-to-find specialist works well precisely because it removes the travel constraint that limits a purely home-based plan. What online struggles to replace is the lead tutor's sense of a student's actual state on a bad week, the kind of thing a parent notices in the doorway and a tutor notices in the first five minutes at the desk.

Hybrid is how most personal IB tuition plans in Gurgaon actually settle: a home-based lead tutor for the coordination and confidence-building work, online sessions for specialist subjects or IA and Extended Essay check-ins that do not need a shared desk. IB personal tuition Gurgaon families who try to force everything into one format usually find themselves switching within a term anyway, so building the plan around both from the start saves that renegotiation.

Online reaches specialist subject tutors beyond a comfortable evening commute.

contentBlocks.heading: How an IB Personal Tutor Is Checked Before the First Session
contentBlocks.body:
An IB personal tutor Gurgaon families trust is checked on more than subject knowledge: experience coordinating across several subjects for one student, references from families in a similar programme stage, and, for a DP-focused lead, familiarity with how IA and Extended Essay deadlines actually land through DP1 and DP2. Subject specialists brought in alongside the lead go through the same profile verification as any single-subject tutor.

Parents should ask their own questions at the trial too: how the tutor plans to track deadlines across six subjects, what they do when a student is coasting rather than struggling, since personal tuition sometimes needs to catch complacency rather than crisis, and how often they will actually communicate with parents versus only the student.

IB Gram's own boundary here matters as much as any check: a personal tutor mentors, questions and reviews an IA, an Extended Essay outline or a TOK exhibition idea, but does not write any part of it. That line exists for the student's academic integrity, not as a formality, and a tutor who blurs it should be flagged and replaced, not tolerated because the work got easier for a term.

Verification also covers the practical side of home tutoring: identity confirmed before a first visit, an understanding of society gate and visitor registration norms across whichever corridor the family lives in, and punctuality tracked honestly from the first month rather than assumed. A parent does not need to sit through every session, but should stay reachable, and for a younger MYP student, present somewhere in the home during the early weeks while the routine settles.

References are checked against families at a similar programme stage.

contentBlocks.heading: Inside a Personal IB Tuition Plan: Profile, Targets and Limits
contentBlocks.body:
The learning profile built in the first two weeks is the actual product of the first month, more than any single lesson. It maps four things honestly: where the gaps are by subject and topic, not just by grade; what the student is already strong at, since a plan that only lists weaknesses demoralises before it helps; the pace the student actually works at on an ordinary weekday evening, tired after a full school day, not their best possible pace; and where their confidence sits, because a student who has decided they are 'bad at Physics' needs a different opening few weeks than one who is simply behind on content.

Targets come next, and the student has to own them for a personal plan to hold past the first month. A target set by a parent alone, get a 6 in Chemistry, tends to produce compliance rather than effort; a target the student helped set, framed around a specific paper or skill they can see themselves improving, tends to survive a bad week. Targets are reviewed on a fixed cycle, usually every four to six weeks, against actual marked work, not against how the student says the term is going.

Adapting for learning differences is part of a personal plan, within honest limits. A tutor who knows a student has a diagnosed difficulty, dyslexia, ADHD or something similar, adjusts pacing, materials and session structure around it, drawing on strategies the school or a specialist has already recommended. What a tutor is not is a diagnostician or a therapist; if a family suspects an undiagnosed difficulty, the honest step is a referral to a qualified professional, not a tutor guessing and adjusting informally.

Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support sits inside a firm boundary. A personal tutor can help a student choose a feasible IA topic, question a first draft's reasoning, explain what a TOK knowledge question is actually asking, or talk through Extended Essay structure within its 4,000-word limit. What the tutor never does is write a sentence of any of it. That boundary protects the student's own academic integrity, and any arrangement that crosses it is a risk the family should walk away from, whatever short-term relief it promises.
items: The learning profile maps gaps, strengths, real pace and confidence.
Targets are set with the student, not announced to them.
Reviews happen every four to six weeks against marked work.
Learning differences are accommodated; diagnosis is left to qualified professionals.
IA, EE and TOK support stops at mentoring; it never becomes writing.

contentBlocks.heading: Is Personal Tuition Actually Working for Your Child?
contentBlocks.body:
The direct answer: within the first review cycle, four to six weeks, you should see a specific, nameable change, not a vague sense of things improving. That might be a student who now attempts a full past paper unprompted, a subject where marked work shows fewer repeated errors, or simply a student who talks about a subject without the dread that used to precede every mention of it.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and personal tuition is no exception to that rule despite the closer relationship it builds. What a personal tutor can honestly promise is attention to the whole picture: a plan that adjusts when a subject is not moving, an early flag if a target now looks unrealistic given the time left, and coordination across subjects that a family managing six separate single-subject tutors would struggle to replicate alone.

There are honest limits too. A personal tutor brought in during DP2's final term cannot rebuild two years of gaps across six subjects; the realistic job at that point is triage, deciding which subjects and which specific papers can still move meaningfully. And some students, especially those who are simply overloaded rather than behind, need fewer commitments rather than another one, and a personal tutor who says so plainly is doing the job properly, even when it costs the arrangement. Ask, at every review, what specifically changed and what the tutor plans to do differently next; a review that only reports effort without a specific change is not really a review.
items: Expect a specific, nameable change within the first four-to-six-week cycle.
No tutor can guarantee a grade, including a personal tutor.
A late DP2 start means triage, not a full rebuild.
Sometimes the honest advice is fewer commitments, not another tutor.

faqs.question: Can a personal tutor help with the Extended Essay or TOK, or is that a separate specialist?

faqs.question: Is there an MYP tutor in Gurgaon within a personal tuition plan, or only DP support?

MYP personal tuition focuses on criterion-based tasks across the eight subject groups and, in MYP 5, the Personal Project, building habits, structuring an argument, using command terms correctly, that carry directly into DP-level work. faqs.question: How much does personal IB tuition cost compared with a single-subject tutor?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not publish figures, since cost depends on programme stage, number of subjects covered, session length and whether the lead tutor also coordinates specialists, but personal tuition is usually priced higher than a single-subject arrangement because of that coordination work. faqs.question: Does home tuition mean a parent has to be home during every session, and what study space does it need?
faqs.answer: Not for most MYP and DP students, though staying reachable in the home matters more than sitting beside the desk throughout. Most personal tuition plans in Gurgaon lead with home tuition for the lead tutor's coordination sessions, since reading a student's confidence and fatigue face to face matters most in that role, with specialist subject sessions filled in online where the ideal specialist is not within a realistic evening commute. What matters more than a parent's presence is a consistent, quiet study space with the right books to hand each week; a family can ask for a fully home-based plan, but should expect it to narrow the pool of available specialists for less common HL subject combinations.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram plan multi-subject IB tuition in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram starts by asking about the whole subject load, not just the one subject a parent calls about, because a DP student's Physics HL problem is often really a time problem caused by five other subjects. We ask about programme stage, board, current subjects, target grades and the school's own calendar before shortlisting anyone.

From there the process is deliberately unglamorous. A parent sends a query or books a free consultation, and IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule. It shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs, one specialist for a subject that needs deep syllabus knowledge, or a single tutor across two subjects that sit closer together, such as Chemistry and Biology at SL. A demo or trial session is arranged before the family commits to anything, so the tutor's approach can be checked against the student's actual gaps rather than a CV.

Once subjects are matched, the harder work is sequencing them. A DP1 student adding a third subject to tuition in October needs a different weekly rhythm than a DP2 student six weeks from mocks. IB Gram asks what is due when, IA drafts, EE supervision meetings, unit tests, so subject sessions land before the deadline that needs them, not after. If the fit on a subject is wrong, the family can ask for a different match rather than living with a tutor who is not working.

Lessons run at home in the family's own sector or society, online, or a mix depending on the subject and the week. A plan is not fixed for the year: IB Gram expects it to be revisited as a subject stabilises or a new pressure point appears, usually every four to six weeks. This is the core of IB subject tuition in Gurgaon done properly: matching each subject cleanly before scheduling anything, not filling slots first and figuring out the fit later.

2. We map the school's own scheme of work, test dates and mock timetable against the request.
3. A specialist is shortlisted for each subject that needs one, or one tutor for two lighter subjects.
4. A trial or demo session confirms fit before the family commits to a weekly slot.
5. The timetable is set across home, online or hybrid sessions, avoiding clashes with school and sleep.
6. Every four to six weeks we review the plan and drop or add a subject as needed.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: what each stage needs from subject tuition
contentBlocks.body:
A primary-age PYP learner rarely needs subject tuition in the way a DP student does. The programme runs from about age three to twelve, organised around six transdisciplinary themes (Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet) delivered through units of inquiry, with the ten attributes of the IB learner profile threaded through every unit. There are no external examinations, and the PYP exhibition in the final year is a school-led project, not a paper. Where tuition helps at this stage, it is reading, numeracy and study habits, not subject content drilling.

MYP changes the picture. Across MYP 1 to 5 (roughly ages 11 to 16), students work in eight subject groups, and every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's grade boundaries, so a student can be strong in content and still lose marks on a criterion they have never been taught to target directly. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, with the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional in MYP 5 at each school's own discretion.

DP is where the multi-subject question gets serious. Six subjects across six groups run for two years, DP1 and DP2, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add up to 3 more points toward a maximum of 45, with 24 the minimum for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's failing conditions, and CAS running the whole two years alongside the six subjects. A tuition plan at this stage has to treat all of that as one system, not six separate arrangements that happen to share a calendar.

A family with one child in MYP and another in DP is planning two different kinds of tuition, not a scaled-up version of the same thing, and IB Gram matches tutors separately for each stage even where sessions land on the same evening.
items: PYP tuition (rare) supports inquiry and foundational literacy or numeracy, not exam papers.
MYP tuition targets the specific criterion, A, B, C or D, where marks are being lost.
DP tuition covers six subjects at once, so sequencing matters more than in MYP.
TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS run alongside all six DP subjects, not instead of them.
A family with an MYP child and a DP child needs two separate, coordinated plans.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects need a specialist, and which don't?
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject on a student's timetable needs a tutor, and naming which ones do is most of the planning work. Mathematics is usually first: AA (Analysis and Approaches) and AI (Applications and Interpretation) are different subjects in practice, each offered at HL and SL, and a tutor fluent in AI HL is not automatically useful for AA SL. Getting the exact combination right before booking anyone saves a family from a mismatched first session.

The sciences, Physics, Chemistry and Biology, tend to need a specialist once a student moves from struggling with content to struggling with application: HL Physics problems that combine two topics, Chemistry calculations that depend on earlier bonding concepts, Biology data-based questions that reward precise command-term answers. Because each also carries an internal assessment with its own criteria, a science tutor who understands the IA alongside the syllabus is worth more than one who only drills content.

English is where families most often ask for the wrong specialist. English A, split into Language and Literature or Literature, is essay and Individual Oral work; English B is a language-acquisition subject with its own skills of comprehension and structured writing. They are rarely the same tutor's strength, and MYP Language Acquisition below them is different again.

TOK and the Extended Essay sit apart from every other subject. TOK asks knowledge questions and runs as discussion, not content delivery, and EE is a supervised research process capped at 4,000 words. A subject specialist can help a student think, but the school's own supervisor stays central to both, and IB Gram positions a TOK or EE tutor as extra structure and feedback, never a replacement for that relationship.
items: Maths AA and AI split further into HL and SL, so a specialist must match the exact combination.
Sciences (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) need a subject specialist once practical work and IA feasibility enter the picture.
English A (Language and Literature or Literature) and English B are different skills, rarely one tutor.
TOK is discussion-led and EE is research-led; neither suits a general subject tutor.
A student strong in three subjects may only need tuition in the two that are slipping.

contentBlocks.heading: IB subject tuition across New Gurgaon, Dwarka Expressway and Old Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
New Gurgaon covers Sector 82 through Sector 90, plus Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, with societies including Vatika India Next and Godrej Air. Several international schools sit within reach of this corridor, and families here often run two or three IB subjects in tuition at once because the newer sectors have fewer nearby coaching options, so a home tutor covering more than one subject is genuinely useful rather than a convenience.

Dwarka Expressway, Sector 102 through Sector 113, including Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, is growing fast and pulls families from a wide catchment, some closer to the Delhi border than to central Gurgaon. contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online lessons or hybrid: what works for several IB subjects?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's lead service is home tuition, a verified tutor teaching the student at home, in the family's own sector or society, and for most DP subjects this is still where the most careful work happens. A home tutor sitting beside the student catches the working a screen cannot: the sign error in a Maths AA step, the unit left off a Physics answer, the paragraph in an English essay that needed one more piece of evidence. For a family running two or three subjects in tuition, home classes on consecutive evenings also mean the student is not managing three different platforms and three different routines in one week.

Online lessons are a real alternative, not a downgrade, for some of the same subjects. TOK discussion works well over a screen, EE feedback on a drafted section works well by shared document and call, and a graphic display calculator or a shared whiteboard covers most of what a Maths session needs. Online also solves the specialist problem: a scarce subject tutor, Computer Science or a particular HL combination, may not be reachable at home from every corridor, and online removes that constraint entirely.

Hybrid is what most multi-subject families end up with in practice, not because it is a compromise but because different subjects genuinely suit different modes. A student might keep Chemistry as home tuition for the lab-adjacent discussion and take TOK online on a weeknight when travel does not make sense. IB Gram matches mode to subject and sector rather than defaulting to one for the whole plan, and the mix can change as mocks approach or a subject comes off the timetable. Good IB subject tuition in Gurgaon rarely settles on one mode for every subject; it settles on the right mode for each one.

contentBlocks.heading: Planning IB subject tuition in Gurgaon: priorities, timetables and when to stop
contentBlocks.body:
There is no fixed rule for which IB subject gets a tutor first, but there is a reliable way to reason about it. Start with what is graded most heavily in the near term: a subject with a mock in six weeks outranks one with no test until next term, whatever the student says troubles them most. Then weigh HL against SL, since an HL subject carries more teaching hours and more marks riding on it, and weigh a subject with an IA or coursework deadline attached against one that is purely exam-based, because a missed IA deadline cannot be undone the way a poor test score can. A student strong in three of six subjects genuinely may not need tuition in any of them; the case for tuition is weakest exactly where the school reports are already good.

A weekly timetable with two or three subjects works when it respects the rest of the student's week, not just the tutor's availability. As a rough shape: one subject on two evenings if it is the priority, the other one or two subjects on a single evening each, leaving at least one weekday evening and part of the weekend genuinely free. Cramming three subjects into three consecutive evenings after a full school day tends to produce diminishing returns by the third session, tired attention rather than real practice.

Pausing or dropping a subject from tuition is a normal part of the plan, not a failure of it. A subject that has stabilised after a school report or a mock, an IA that has been submitted, or an EE that has moved past its research phase, are all natural points to step tuition down rather than keep a slot out of habit. The reverse is also true: a subject that looked fine in DP1 can need a tutor again once HL content compounds in DP2. Reviewing the whole plan every four to six weeks, not just when something goes wrong, is what keeps a multi-subject arrangement from either overloading the student or under-serving a subject that has quietly started to slip.

Home tutoring suits the subjects where written working matters most; online suits scarce specialists and discussion-based work like TOK; most families end up with a mix that shifts term to term rather than picking one mode for the whole plan and sticking with it regardless of the subject.

contentBlocks.heading: What progress looks like across several IB subjects
contentBlocks.body:
Across a multi-subject plan, progress rarely moves at the same pace in every subject at once, and expecting it to is the fastest way to feel disappointed by tuition that is actually working. A Maths subject with clear right and wrong answers tends to show movement in test scores within a term. TOK and Extended Essay work, or an English essay skill, move more slowly and show up first as better reasoning in a draft, not a jump in a school grade. No tutor can guarantee a grade, on one subject or on six, and any promise that sounds like one is worth treating with suspicion rather than relief.

Honest limits matter here too. A subject tutor works alongside the school's own teacher, IA supervisor or EE supervisor, not instead of them, and the school's own assessment of a student's standing, reports, predicted grades, mock results, stays the primary evidence of where things actually stand. A tuition plan that ignores what the school is already saying is working from the wrong data.

If a subject shows no movement after about a month of regular sessions, that is worth a conversation, not patience for its own sake. Sometimes the fix is a different tutor for that one subject; sometimes it is fewer subjects at once so the student has room to actually absorb what is being taught; sometimes the honest answer is that the subject needs less tuition and more independent practice between sessions. A plan reviewed every four to six weeks catches this before a full term is spent on something that was not working.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started with IB subject tuition in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is a short conversation, not a commitment. A parent sends a query or books a free consultation, and IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule for every subject in the plan, not just the one that prompted the call. From there, the family and IB Gram agree a starting timetable across however many subjects are in the plan, home, online or hybrid depending on subject and corridor, subject to tutor availability. Nothing about this is locked in: a subject can be added, paused or moved between modes as the term goes on, and the first review sits about four to six weeks out, in time to adjust well before the next school test or mock rather than after it. faqs.question: How many IB subjects should be in tuition at once?
faqs.answer: Most families do best with tuition in one or two subjects at a time, occasionally three during an exam term. Start with whichever subject has the nearest test, mock or IA deadline, then add a second only if the first is manageable alongside school and sleep. A student with six DP subjects does not need six tutors; the case for adding a subject to tuition is usually a specific gap, an upcoming assessment, or a criterion the student keeps losing marks on, not a general feeling of falling behind everywhere.

faqs.question: What does a weekly timetable with two or three subjects actually look like?
faqs.answer: A workable shape is one priority subject on two evenings a week, and one or two other subjects on a single evening each, leaving at least one weekday evening and part of the weekend free. Packing three subjects into three consecutive evenings after a full school day usually produces tired attention by the third session rather than real progress. The exact mix should shift as mocks approach and ease off once a subject stabilises, reviewed roughly every four to six weeks rather than fixed for the whole term.

faqs.question: When should a subject be paused or dropped from tuition?
faqs.answer: Pause a subject once a school report, mock or submitted IA shows it has stabilised, rather than keeping the slot out of habit. It is also fine to drop a subject that a student can genuinely manage independently, freeing that time for one that is actually slipping. The reverse happens too: a subject that looked fine in DP1 can need tuition again once HL content compounds in DP2, so pausing is a normal, expected part of a multi-subject plan, not a sign something went wrong.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach more than one IB subject well?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the subjects sit close together and the tutor is genuinely strong in both, such as Chemistry and Biology at SL, or two humanities subjects with similar essay skills. It works less well across very different disciplines, Maths AA HL and English A, for instance, or where one subject is scarce and specialised. IB Gram checks a tutor's depth in each subject before matching them to more than one, and a trial session on each subject is the honest way to confirm the fit.

faqs.question: How does home tuition work for a family in New Gurgaon or Dwarka Expressway?
faqs.answer: A verified home tutor travels to the family's own sector or society for each session, subject to availability and to how many subjects are on the timetable. In corridors like New Gurgaon (Sector 82 to 90) or Dwarka Expressway (Sector 102 to 113), evening traffic between one part of Gurugram (Gurgaon) and another can stretch a short trip, so IB Gram tries to match home tuition tutors who can reach the same corridor for more than one subject rather than scattering sessions across the city.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session is missed because of traffic or a school event?
faqs.answer: A missed home session can usually move online for that week instead of being lost, especially useful for a family in Palam Vihar or Old Gurgaon already running one subject as hybrid. Let the tutor know as early as possible so the slot can be rearranged rather than simply cancelled. This flexibility matters more in a multi-subject plan, where one missed session can otherwise push the whole week's schedule out of balance across two or three subjects.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram help with the Extended Essay, TOK and IAs across several subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to matching a tutor with the right background, and always within the IB's academic integrity rules: a tutor gives feedback, structure and mentoring, and never writes the work. For a student managing IAs in two or three subjects plus the Extended Essay and TOK, IB Gram tracks which deadlines fall when so tuition sessions land before a draft is due rather than after, and a subject tutor's IA support stays separate from the school's own supervisor, not a replacement for them.

faqs.question: How is a subject tutor in Gurgaon verified before a home visit?
faqs.answer: Every tutor's profile is checked before being shortlisted for a family's request, and a demo or trial session lets the parent judge fit directly before committing to a weekly slot. Parents should still ask their own questions: the exact syllabus and paper structure for the subject, how the tutor plans to track any IA or coursework deadline, and what a typical session looks like. If a match is wrong on any one subject in a multi-subject plan, the family can ask for a different tutor for that subject alone.

faqs.question: Should a parent be present during a multi-subject home tuition session?
faqs.answer: That is entirely the family's choice; there is no requirement either way. Younger MYP students or a first session with a new tutor often go more smoothly with a parent nearby, while many DP students prefer to work independently once the tutor and student have a routine. What matters more across several subjects is a consistent, quiet study space and the right materials to hand, so a session on Physics one evening and English the next both start without losing the first ten minutes to setup.

faqs.question: What if there has been no progress in a subject after a month of tuition?
faqs.answer: That is worth a conversation with IB Gram, not something to wait out. Sometimes the fix is a different tutor for that one subject, sometimes it is fewer subjects running at once so the student has room to actually absorb what is being taught, and sometimes the honest answer is that the subject needs less tuition and more independent practice between sessions. Reviewing the whole plan every four to six weeks is designed to catch this before a full term goes by.

faqs.question: Is IB subject tuition in Gurgaon available for MYP as well as DP?
faqs.answer: Yes, though what tuition looks like differs by stage. MYP tuition usually targets the specific criterion, A to D, where a student keeps losing marks, while DP tuition has to manage six subjects, HL and SL, running at once alongside TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS. A family with children in both MYP and DP typically needs two coordinated plans rather than one, and IB Gram matches tutors separately for each stage even when sessions run on the same evening.

contentBlocks.body:
A Maths match starts narrower than most people expect, because IB Maths is not one thing. Before IB Gram suggests a single tutor, a coordinator needs to know whether your child sits Analysis and Approaches (AA) or Applications and Interpretation (AI), at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), and which stage of the exploration, if any, is already underway. A tutor strong in AA's calculus and proof work is not automatically the right fit for an AI student building statistical models, even though both are IB Maths on paper.

Once your child's course and level are confirmed, matching moves the way it does for any Gurgaon home tutor search: subject and level match first, weekday evening reach into your corridor second, and verified background always. A short call establishes AA or AI, HL or SL, and roughly where the exploration stands; the coordinator checks this against tutor profiles for the same combination and for tutors already working in or near your sector; a shortlist of two or three matched profiles follows; and a trial session at your home, online or hybrid lets your child judge the fit before anything ongoing is agreed.

This narrowness is deliberate. A parent asking for the best IB Maths home tutor in Gurgaon is not really asking for a single name; they are asking for someone who has actually taught this exact combination, AI HL with a weak Paper 3 score, say, or AA SL with strong algebra but shaky proof, often enough to know where a student like theirs usually gets stuck. If the first tutor does not turn out to be that person, ask IB Gram for another. Getting the subject and level right matters more than filling a slot quickly.

2. IB Gram checks this against tutor profiles for the same combination and corridor coverage.

contentBlocks.heading: AA or AI, HL or SL: What Should a Maths Home Tutor Confirm First?
contentBlocks.body:
Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are two different courses, not two difficulty tiers of the same course, and confusing them is the single most common mismatch IB Gram sees in Gurgaon. AA leans toward algebra, proof and calculus, taught in a traditional, workings-heavy style; AI leans toward modelling, statistics and technology, with more real-world data and less pure proof. A student confident with calculus but slow with statistical reasoning is not necessarily weak at maths generally; they may simply be on the course that fits how they think less well, and that is worth raising with the school directly rather than assuming a tutor can paper over it.

Higher Level and Standard Level split the same two courses again. SL work is assessed through Paper 1 (40% of the final grade) and Paper 2 (40%), plus the exploration (20%). HL adds a third paper, Paper 3 (20%), built around extended problem-solving, alongside Paper 1 (30%), Paper 2 (30%) and the exploration (20%). AA Paper 1 is sat without a calculator; every other AA paper and every AI paper allows a graphic display calculator (GDC). A home tutor needs to know which papers your child sits calculator-free, because non-calculator technique, exact values, algebraic manipulation, is a distinct skill from GDC-assisted problem solving and often needs separate practice time.

MYP Mathematics feeds directly into this choice. Schools often split MYP 4-5 maths into standard and extended mathematics, and extended covers the additional topics that prepare a student for DP Mathematics AA specifically. A family whose child is still in MYP 4 or 5 and searching for an MYP maths tutor in Gurgaon should ask the tutor to keep half an eye on this fork, since which track a student lands on shapes whether AA or AI is the more natural DP choice two years later. Confirm the exact course and level with the school before booking; a tutor works from what you tell them, not from a guess.

SL splits 40/40/20 across Paper 1, Paper 2 and the exploration.
