contentBlocks.heading: Building the Weekly IGCSE English One-to-One Tuition Plan
contentBlocks.body:
Early in Grade 9, one to two hours a week is generally enough, focused on identifying the exact syllabus and building the basic habit of planning before writing. By Grade 10, as coursework deadlines or exam pressure both increase, two to three hours a week is more typical, split between writing practice, reading paper technique and, for Literature or Second Language candidates, whichever additional component the syllabus requires. In the two to three months before mocks or the exam series, three to four hours a week is common, weighted heavily toward timed writing under exam conditions and past paper reading practice marked against the real scheme.

A well-structured session usually opens with a short accuracy or vocabulary warm-up, moves into the main focus, planning a directed writing task, working through a reading extract, or drafting part of a composition, and closes with feedback the student can act on immediately rather than a long list saved for later. For a coursework-route student, sessions instead track whichever draft is due next against the school's internal deadline, with feedback aimed at that specific submission rather than general exam technique.

Every four to six weeks, the plan is worth reviewing honestly: which skills, register, planning, reading accuracy, speaking fluency for Second Language candidates, are improving, and whether the weekly hours still match where the student stands. A student who has settled composition technique might shift focus entirely to the reading paper; one who has fallen behind on coursework drafts might need a temporary increase to catch the next deadline comfortably.

Stepping the plan up and down around mocks and the exam season follows a clear pattern: 1. Six to eight weeks before a mock or the real exam, increase weekly hours and shift toward full timed papers under exam conditions. 2. In exam week itself, keep sessions light, reviewing technique rather than attempting new full papers. 3. After the exam or mock, drop to a lighter schedule, or pause where the relevant component is complete, so the student is not kept on tuition for skills they have already secured.
items: Grade 9, early: one to two hours a week, focused on syllabus identification and planning habits.
Grade 10: two to three hours a week, split between writing, reading and the relevant extra component.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does Real Progress in IGCSE English Look Like?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in English is genuinely harder to see week to week than in a subject with clear right and wrong answers, which is exactly why it is worth naming what to actually look for: a draft that needed fewer structural comments than the one before it, a student who plans visibly without being reminded to, register that shifts appropriately between a formal and an informal task without the tutor pointing it out each time. These are real signals, even without a test score attached to them.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and English in particular has enough subjectivity in marking that any promise of a specific result should be treated with real scepticism. What a tutor can reasonably offer is a clear, specific account of what is holding a piece of writing back, register, structure, accuracy, or reading precision, and a realistic sense of how much that can improve in the time available. A student starting tuition only a few weeks before a mock should not expect, and should not be promised, the kind of transformation a full term of consistent work might produce.

Some honest limits are worth stating plainly. A student who reads very little outside school will improve more slowly on the reading paper than one who reads regularly, and tuition works better paired with some independent reading than as a stand-alone fix. Equally, a Second Language student who rarely speaks English outside the classroom needs sustained, structured speaking practice over months, not a burst of preparation in the final weeks before an assessment that counts speaking into the grade.

The clearest available signal is a piece of writing or a reading paper attempt, done under timed conditions and marked against the real scheme, compared with an equivalent attempt several weeks later. The specific, marked-up differences between the two tell a parent far more than a general sense of whether sessions feel like they are going well.
items: Progress shows as fewer structural comments needed, visible planning, and register shifting appropriately without prompting.
No tutor can guarantee a grade; English marking has real subjectivity, so treat firm promises with caution.
Wider independent reading supports faster progress on the reading paper.
Second Language speaking fluency needs sustained practice over months, not a short pre-exam burst.

introSummary: IGCSE English tuition at home in Gurgaon has to start with a question most families have not fully answered: which English does your child actually sit? Home tutoring is IB Gram's default here, a verified tutor working with your child at your own table in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, marking real writing by hand rather than teaching in the abstract, though online and hybrid sessions have a genuine place too. Whether your child is entered for Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511, Literature in English 0475, or one of Pearson Edexcel's English syllabuses, this page sets out the calendar, the corridors, and the specific writing and reading skills that decide the year.

contentBlocks.heading: First, Which English Syllabus Does Your Child Actually Sit?
contentBlocks.body:
There are several different exams that go by the name IGCSE English in Gurgaon, and the first job before any tutoring starts is identifying which one your child sits. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English, syllabus 0500, assumes English is close to a first language and combines a reading paper with directed writing and composition, or in some schools a coursework portfolio instead of one of the written components. English as a Second Language, syllabuses 0510 and 0511, tests reading, writing and listening, and treats speaking differently: 0511 counts a speaking mark into the overall grade, while 0510 reports speaking separately from it. Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English, 0475, is a different subject altogether, built around set texts and essay writing rather than the skills above. Pearson Edexcel runs its own versions: English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1).

IB Gram asks for the exact syllabus code before shortlisting anyone, because a tutor experienced with First Language English 0500 composition marking is not automatically the right person for an ESL student who needs listening practice and a different register altogether. Once the syllabus is confirmed, IB Gram asks about your sector in Gurgaon, your weekly availability around school hours and buses, and where your child's writing or reading currently falls short.

A shortlist of two or three verified tutors follows, matched to the exact syllabus, and a free consultation or demo session lets you see the tutor mark a piece of your child's actual writing before anything is confirmed. If the fit still is not right, IB Gram arranges a different tutor rather than asking you to make do.
items: 1. Confirm the exact syllabus code: 0500, 0510, 0511, 0475 or an Edexcel English.
2. Tell IB Gram your sector in Gurgaon and weekly availability.
3. Flag where writing, reading or speaking currently falls short.
4. Review two or three verified tutor profiles matched to that syllabus.
5. Use a free consultation or demo session before committing to anything.

contentBlocks.heading: 0500, 0510, 0475 or Edexcel: Five Different IGCSE Englishes
contentBlocks.body:
Most Gurgaon international schools that follow Cambridge enter students for IGCSE First Language English 0500 if English is effectively a first or near-first language for the student, and for English as a Second Language, 0510 or 0511, when it is not. This is a school's academic judgement based on a student's profile, not a free choice a family makes, so the starting point is always confirming which one applies, rather than assuming.

Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English, 0475, is offered as a separate subject at some schools, alongside First Language English rather than instead of it, and asks for essay-based analysis of set texts rather than the reading-and-writing skills tested in 0500 or 0510. Pearson Edexcel schools in Gurgaon may instead enter students for International GCSE English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1), or English as a Second Language (4ES1), each with its own paper structure and its own demands on a tutor.

All of these typically sit within a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, usually followed by the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or occasionally a return to CBSE or ISC for Class 11. Cambridge's exam series run in February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November; Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE series run in January and May/June. English tuition timed against the wrong series wastes exactly the weeks that matter most, so IB Gram confirms this before building any plan for home tuition or otherwise.
items: 1. Confirm whether your child sits First Language English or ESL.
2. Ask whether Literature in English, 0475, is a separate subject at your school.
3. Check the Edexcel code if your school uses Pearson: 4EA1, 4EB1 or 4ES1.
4. Note your child's exact exam series for this year.
5. Ask what English route follows Grade 10 at your school.

contentBlocks.heading: Directed Writing, Composition and the Register Question
contentBlocks.body:
Across the different IGCSE English syllabuses, two skills decide most of the marks: reading for meaning under time pressure, and writing accurately in the register a task actually asks for. A directed writing task, common to 0500 and the ESL syllabuses, gives source material and asks for a specific form, a letter, an article, a speech, aimed at a specific audience; a student who writes a technically correct paragraph in the wrong register, too informal for a formal letter, too stiff for a personal one, loses marks that have nothing to do with grammar.

Composition, whether narrative or descriptive, rewards planning more than most students expect. A tutor working through a five-minute planning habit before any composition, deciding on structure, a few key vocabulary choices and how the piece will end, before a single sentence is written, tends to produce steadier marks than a student who starts writing immediately and hopes an ending appears. Accuracy still matters throughout: consistent tense, correctly used punctuation, and sentences varied in length rather than a string of similar ones.

Where a coursework portfolio replaces a written composition component, the standard does not drop, it shifts: drafting, redrafting against feedback, and submitting a genuinely final version rather than a first attempt tidied slightly. Reading papers test skimming for gist, scanning for specific detail, and inference, working out what a text implies without stating it outright, and this is a skill that improves with repeated timed practice far more than with vocabulary lists alone.
items: 1. Match the register to the task: formal letter, informal email, speech, article.
2. Plan a composition for five minutes before writing a single sentence.
3. Keep tense and punctuation consistent across a full response.
4. Practise inference: what a text implies, not just what it states.
5. Treat coursework drafts as real drafts, not a single rushed attempt.

contentBlocks.heading: Term Tests, Mocks and the Rhythm of a Gurgaon School Year
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon's international schools, among them Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge, each run their own calendar of unit tests, half-yearly assessments and pre-board or mock exams. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; we make no claim about which curriculum or board any named school follows, and that is worth confirming with the school itself.

For English specifically, this calendar matters in a particular way: composition and directed writing improve slowly, over repeated timed practice, not in a single cram session, so a tutor who only appears before a mock exam has far less to work with than one who has been drafting and redrafting with a student since the term began. The quieter months after a session opens, before unit tests begin, are genuinely the best time to build writing habits that later hold up under exam pressure.

Working around a Gurgaon school week also means working around buses, sport, music and, in many households, a sibling's own exam calendar. None of this is unusual at all, and a home tuition tutor who plans a session only around the subject, ignoring the rest of the week, ends up with a timetable that survives on paper and nowhere else in practice.
items: 1. Unit tests and half-yearly assessments cluster mid-term.
2. Writing skills improve slowly; start before the pressure months, not during them.
3. Pre-board or mock exams sit ahead of the real exam series.
4. Bus and activity timings shift by season; confirm the current ones.
5. IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with any school listed here.

contentBlocks.heading: Should English Tuition Happen at Home, Online or Both?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is IB Gram's starting point for IGCSE English in Gurgaon: a tutor sitting beside your child, reading a draft together, marking it up by hand and talking through why a sentence does not yet work. Writing improves faster with this kind of immediate, physical back-and-forth than most families expect, particularly for a student who finds it hard to explain, over a screen, exactly where they got stuck.

Online one-to-one tuition still works well for English, more so than for some subjects, since a shared document lets a tutor edit and comment on a draft in real time, and it is the honest choice for a family in a distant corridor such as Dwarka Expressway or Manesar, or for a week the school calendar makes travel impractical. A hybrid pattern, home for most sessions and online when needed, is what many Gurgaon families land on once the year settles into its own rhythm.

A coaching centre batch suits a different need: useful for group discussion of a set text in Literature in English, or for comparing writing against peers at a similar level, but a batch rarely has time to mark and return an individual student's composition in the detail that moves a grade. For English specifically, that individual feedback loop is usually what decides progress, more than the mode it happens in, so choose based on what your child's writing actually needs rather than habit or what a neighbour's family chose for home classes.
items: 1. Home tuition: hands-on marking and immediate feedback on a draft.
2. Online tuition: works well for English, especially shared-document editing.
3. Hybrid: home most weeks, online when travel or the calendar does not allow it.
4. Coaching batch: good for peer discussion, weaker on individual feedback.
5. Detailed, individual feedback on writing usually decides English progress.

contentBlocks.heading: Vetting an IGCSE English Home Tutor Before They Visit Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram shortlists for a home visit has their profile checked first: which English syllabus they have actually taught, First Language, ESL or Literature, and references followed up rather than taken on trust. For English in particular, ask to see how a tutor marks: a vague good effort in the margin teaches a student nothing, while specific, actionable comments on register, structure or a weak paragraph do.

Use the demo session properly. Bring a recent piece of your child's writing and watch the tutor go through it live; how they explain a correction tells you far more than a list of qualifications does. Ask how often you will get an update on progress, and whether the tutor is working from your child's actual set texts, if Literature in English applies, rather than a generic reading list.

Gated societies along corridors like Golf Course Road or Golf Course Extension Road, DLF The Magnolias and M3M Golf Estate among them, usually need visitor registration arranged ahead of a first visit; share the tutor's name with your gate office in advance so the first session is not lost at the barrier while everyone waits. It is a small step, easy to forget, but it is often the difference between a session that runs on time and one that starts twenty minutes late. None of this replaces your own judgement about the home tutor sitting across the table from your child every week; verification narrows the shortlist, the final call is still yours to make.
items: 1. Confirm which English syllabus the tutor has actually taught.
2. Watch the tutor mark a real piece of your child's writing in the demo.
3. Ask how often progress will be reported, and in what detail.
4. Confirm the tutor is using your child's actual set texts, if relevant.
5. Register the tutor at your society gate before the first home visit.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Checkpoints in the Gurgaon Academic Year for IGCSE English
contentBlocks.body:
Treat the Gurgaon academic year as four checkpoints rather than one long stretch. The first, once the session opens in April and settles through May and June, is for building habits: regular timed reading practice, a weekly composition with proper planning beforehand, and, for an ESL student, listening practice worked in from early on rather than left until later. This is also when the weekly timetable itself gets fixed around school hours, the bus route and any fixed activity.

The second checkpoint, July through September, usually brings the school's first unit tests, so sessions shift to match whatever the school is assessing, while still returning weekly to a piece of directed writing or a reading comprehension under time pressure, since these skills fade quickly without regular practice. October's slower patch around Diwali is a natural point for sessions to move rather than disappear; IB Gram treats a rescheduled session as completely normal here, not an exception to manage around.

The third checkpoint, November into December, often carries half-yearly or pre-board assessments, so a tutor running IGCSE English tuition at home Gurgaon families lean on through this stretch usually shifts toward exam-condition practice: full papers, timed, marked properly against real criteria. December's winter break suits a short holiday intensive, two or three sessions a week instead of one, focused on whichever component is weakest.

The fourth checkpoint runs from January through the exam series, Cambridge's February/March series offered only in India, the shared May/June series, or January and May/June for Edexcel, with sessions almost entirely on past papers under real mark schemes. Once results land, the summer becomes a quieter stretch again, for consolidating before Grade 10 or looking ahead to the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or a board change for Class 11.
items: 1. April to June: build weekly writing and reading habits, fix the timetable.
2. July to September: sessions track the school's own unit test schedule.
3. October: Diwali sessions get rescheduled, not dropped.
4. November to December: pre-board practice, then a short holiday intensive.
5. January to the exam series: full past papers under real mark schemes.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Know IGCSE English Tuition Is Actually Working?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in English is genuinely harder to see week to week than in a subject with clear right answers, so look for specific signs rather than a general feeling. Fewer register mistakes in directed writing, a composition with a visible plan behind its structure, faster and more accurate reading comprehension under time pressure: these usually show within four to six weeks of consistent sessions. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and be wary of anyone who implies they can.

A fair review point is every four to six weeks: is the student's writing more accurate and better organised, is reading comprehension improving under real time pressure, and is the tutor adjusting the plan when a particular component is not moving. If nothing has shifted after a month of regular sessions, raise it with IB Gram directly; a different tutor is a realistic option, and changing early is far less disruptive than changing close to the exam series.

There are honest limits. A student who has avoided writing practice for years will not become a confident writer in a handful of sessions, whatever the plan promises. A student managing several subjects may benefit more from one focused, well-planned English session a week than from several rushed ones squeezed around everything else. The tutor's job is to build a student who can plan and write independently under exam conditions, not one who depends on a tutor's presence to produce a decent paragraph.
items: 1. Fewer register mistakes and a visible composition plan are early signs of progress.
2. Review progress on a four to six week cycle.
3. No tutor can guarantee a grade; question anyone who claims otherwise.
4. Raise a lack of progress directly instead of waiting for the next term.
5. The goal is independent writing under exam conditions, not permanent reliance.

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IGCSE English Tuition at Home: The First Fortnight
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started is straightforward. Send IB Gram a query, or book a free consultation, naming the exact syllabus if you know it, First Language, ESL, Literature or an Edexcel English code, your child's current level, and your sector in Gurgaon. IB Gram follows up with a few questions about the school calendar and your weekly availability, then shortlists verified tutors matched to that specific syllabus.

Before the first session, gather a few recent pieces of your child's writing, any reading comprehension scores you have, and the syllabus code if you know it. A demo or trial session happens before any commitment, and it usually works best as a real diagnostic: the tutor reads and marks a recent piece live, so the plan starts from where your child actually is, not from the beginning of a generic course.

Most families beginning IGCSE English tuition at home Gurgaon-wide find the first fortnight is as much about settling into a working rhythm, a reliable weekly slot, a shared understanding of what needs work, as it is about the subject itself. After that, the timetable is fixed around school hours and existing commitments, and revisited whenever the school's own calendar changes. If the first tutor is not right, say so early; IB Gram will arrange someone else, subject always to tutor availability for your sector and schedule. The whole point of starting with home tuition rather than a fixed course is that the plan can flex around your family, not the other way round.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with syllabus, level and sector.
2. Gather recent writing samples and comprehension scores for the first session.
3. Use the demo session as a real diagnostic, not a formality.
4. Fix the weekly timetable around school hours and existing commitments.
5. Ask for a different tutor early if the first match is not right.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE English tuition at home cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not quote fees here, since cost depends on the syllabus, session length and how many sessions a week your child needs; a quote follows once a tutor is shortlisted for the exact syllabus. The structure stays consistent though: sessions are priced per session or as a package reflecting one-to-one marking time, not a flat citywide rate, and a longer tutor commute, say to Dwarka Expressway, can factor in differently than a short one nearby. Availability always depends on tutor schedule and your sector.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor really come to my society for English lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is IB Gram's default: a verified tutor travels to your home across Gurgaon's sectors and societies, gated ones included, such as DLF The Magnolias or M3M Golf Estate, once visitor registration is arranged. Evening traffic on corridors like Golf Course Extension Road or Sohna Road can stretch a short trip, so a slot straight after school is often steadier than a later one. If your society sits along a distant corridor such as Manesar, ask about a hybrid arrangement instead.

faqs.question: What happens if an English home tuition session is missed?
faqs.answer: It gets rescheduled, not dropped; let the tutor or IB Gram know as early as possible, especially around Diwali or exam weeks when several families reschedule together. Writing and reading skills fade a little with a gap, so a missed session close to a unit test or the exam series is better moved than skipped outright. If cancellations become frequent, that does affect how reliably a slot can be held, so flag a difficult week in advance where you can.

faqs.question: Does online English tuition actually work as well as home tuition?
faqs.answer: For English, often yes: a shared document lets a tutor mark and comment on a draft in real time nearly as effectively as sitting beside your child, which is not always true for every subject. A student who needs a physical presence to stay engaged may still do better at a table, but many Gurgaon families run a hybrid pattern, home for most sessions and online when travel does not make sense, without losing much.

faqs.question: My child has shown no progress in IGCSE English after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Raise it with IB Gram directly rather than waiting for the next report; a four-to-six-week review is the normal checkpoint for a subject where progress is gradual. Sometimes the fix is a different tutor, sometimes it is more targeted practice on one weak component, directed writing or reading comprehension, rather than a general review of everything at once. A different match can be arranged, subject to availability, without treating the first tutor as final.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on IGCSE English home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: For the first session, it helps: you see how the tutor gives feedback and it settles your child into the arrangement. After that, most families step back and let the tutor work directly with the student, checking in afterwards rather than sitting through every lesson. Having recent writing samples, the set text list if relevant, and a quiet table ready before the tutor arrives matters more day to day than a parent's continuous presence.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE English syllabus my child actually sits?
faqs.answer: Ask your child's school directly; it is an academic decision the school makes, not something a family chooses. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511, and Literature in English 0475 test different skills, as do Pearson Edexcel's English Language A, English Language B and ESL codes, so this is the first thing to confirm before a tutor plans a single session.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does IGCSE English tuition at home need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which components need the most work and how close the exam series is, so IB Gram sets this during the first consultation rather than fixing a number upfront. Many students manage on one session a week through the quieter months, stepping up to two around unit tests or pre-boards, then concentrating almost entirely on past papers as the exam series approaches.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow the school's own set texts and teaching order?
faqs.answer: A good home tutor works from your child's actual set texts for Literature in English, if that applies, and tracks the school's own scheme of work for reading and writing skills, rather than running a generic course. Ask this directly in the demo session, and expect a clear answer; a tutor who cannot describe how they would align with your school's calendar is worth reconsidering.

faqs.question: Can IGCSE English tuition help a student switching from CBSE mid-course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the early sessions usually focus on register and structure, since CBSE English and IGCSE English test writing rather differently even when general fluency is not the issue. A tutor experienced with this switch will diagnose the actual gap, often in directed writing format rather than raw language ability, before building a plan around it. Expect the first few home tuition sessions to feel slower than you might like, since the tutor is mapping what your child already does well against what the new syllabus actually rewards, rather than assuming CBSE habits transfer directly onto an IGCSE mark scheme.

faqs.question: Is speaking assessed in IGCSE English, and does a home tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It depends on the syllabus: under Cambridge's ESL routes, 0511 counts a speaking mark into the overall grade, while 0510 reports speaking separately from it, and First Language English 0500 does not typically assess speaking in the same way. Where speaking counts, a home tutor can run structured speaking practice at your table, working on fluency and organising an answer under time pressure, which is difficult to replicate without another person in the room.

heroTitle: Choosing an IB Tutor in Gurgaon Who Fits
heroSubtitle: Picking the right IB tutor is a decision, not a booking. This page walks through what a genuine specialist knows that a general tutor usually does not, the questions worth asking before you commit, and what four weeks of real progress should look like.
introSummary: An IB tutor in Gurgaon worth hiring, for home tuition or otherwise, understands the exact demands of the programme your child is on, whether that is the Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) or Diploma Programme (DP), not tutoring in general. Families across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana often start by asking for 'an IB tutor' the way they would ask for a Maths tutor, then discover during the first trial that the board's own grading, from MYP's four criteria to DP's Higher Level and Standard Level structure, changes what good teaching actually looks like here. IB Gram exists to shortlist a tutor who already knows this, for home tutoring, online lessons or a hybrid of the two, rather than leave a family to work it out through trial and error over a term.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a first query become a shortlist of IB tutors?
contentBlocks.body:
The process starts with a conversation, not a list of names. You send a query through the site or book a free consultation, and IB Gram asks what programme your child is on, the exact subject and level, which school they attend, and what a workable weekly schedule actually looks like for your household.

From there:

1. Board, syllabus, level, school calendar and schedule are gathered first, so the search is narrow from the start rather than generic.
2. A shortlist of two or three verified tutors is built, each matched on subject depth for this exact level, not offered simply because they teach 'IB' broadly.
3. A demo or trial lesson is arranged, at home, online or hybrid depending on what you prefer, so you see how the tutor actually teaches before anything is agreed.
4. If the match is wrong, you ask for another one; there is no obligation to continue with the first tutor met.

What this process is trying to solve for is a common and expensive mistake: hiring a tutor who is a genuinely strong teacher in general but has never taught this specific board, and spending the first month of paid sessions on the tutor learning the syllabus alongside the student. IB Gram checks board-specific teaching experience before a profile ever reaches you, so that learning curve does not happen on your time.

A family searching for an IB tutor in Gurgaon usually wants this resolved quickly, and a narrow, well-matched shortlist gets there faster than a long list of general options.

contentBlocks.heading: What stage of the IB is your child actually working through?
contentBlocks.body:
Getting the programme stage right shapes everything else about the search, so it is worth being precise about it before you even start looking. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from ages 3 to 12 and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry and the ten attributes of the IB learner profile. There are no external examinations at this stage, and the final year brings the PYP exhibition, so a PYP tutor's job is mostly about supporting inquiry skills and confidence, not exam drilling.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A tutor who has not actually taught to these criteria before will mark work the way they would for any other board, missing what the school itself is grading against. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project (the Community Project comes earlier, in MYP 3 or 4), and some schools opt into MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations combined with ePortfolios, which each school decides on independently.

The Diploma Programme (DP) runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects from six groups, usually three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points, for a maximum of 45, with 24 as the minimum for the diploma subject to the IB's own failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Most Gurgaon IB schools use the May exam session, with November taken up by a minority of schools and retake candidates, and May results are released in early July.

contentBlocks.heading: Where a specialist IB tutor in Gurgaon earns their fee, subject by subject
contentBlocks.body:
Subject specialism matters more in IB than in most other boards, because the syllabus, the command terms and the way marks are actually awarded differ sharply from subject to subject. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each available at HL or SL, and a tutor who has taught one but not the other will not automatically transfer their method, since the exploration (the internal assessment component) and the exam style genuinely differ between them.

IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology all carry practical or data-based components alongside theory, and a specialist tutor knows where students typically lose marks: misreading a graph's uncertainty, mishandling significant figures, or misapplying a command term like 'evaluate' when the question wanted 'discuss'. A general science tutor without board-specific experience often teaches the content correctly but not the exam technique the IB actually rewards.

IB English A and B sit differently again, closer to structured argument and close reading than to content recall, and a tutor here needs to mark drafts against the assessment criteria rather than general essay-writing standards picked up teaching a different curriculum. TOK and the Extended Essay both carry their own deadlines, set by the school, and a tutor helping across several of a student's subjects needs to track TOK, the EE and any Internal Assessments as separate, parallel deadlines rather than a single pile of homework.

A general tutor, however capable, has usually learned one board deeply and adapted from there; a genuine IB specialist has taught the syllabus codes, mark schemes and criteria your child's exact subject and level use, which is the difference worth paying for.

contentBlocks.heading: The calendar pressure behind every Gurgaon IB school year
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families whose children attend schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge face broadly similar pressure points through the year, regardless of which curriculum a given school actually teaches.

Unit tests and internal deadlines cluster before each term closes, and DP2 students in particular face school-set mock examinations months before the May session, which is when families most often decide to bring a tutor on board or step up existing sessions. Command terms (define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent) recur constantly in these assessments, and past papers, mark schemes and subject reports, sourced through the school or the IB's own official channels, are how a tutor actually learns to teach to them rather than guessing.

A specialist tutor who already knows this rhythm plans ahead of it: intensifying support in the run-up to mocks, then deliberately stepping back once results come in and the student has clarity on what to fix. A general tutor without that context often reacts to the calendar rather than anticipating it, which shows up as scrambled, late-added sessions right before a mock rather than a planned build-up.

May results are released in early July, and the weeks that follow are when many Gurgaon families reassess the coming year's tutoring altogether, whether that means adding a subject, dropping one that is now under control, or switching from a general tutor to a specialist for a subject that clearly needs it.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tutor or online: which one does your child need?
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor in Gurgaon has a real edge for younger students and for subjects where physically watching a student's working matters, since a tutor in the room notices a wandering pencil, a rushed answer, or a hesitation before it becomes a wrong answer on paper. Home tutoring also lets a tutor look through the student's actual school notebook rather than a photographed page, which some families find genuinely useful, especially for handwriting-heavy Mathematics and science working.

Online suits most DP students well and opens access to subject specialists who might not physically reach every corridor in Gurgaon on a weekday evening, which matters more for a less common HL subject or an unusual subject combination than people often expect. The honest trade-off is that a screen makes a tutor's read on a student's confusion slightly harder, and some students need more deliberate check-ins to stay engaged for a full session online than they would at a table.

Hybrid arrangements, a regular home tutor supplemented by an online specialist for one subject, or the reverse, are increasingly common among Gurgaon families once they see which mode actually suits which subject. It takes a little more coordination to run than a single fixed arrangement, but it lets the family match the format to the task instead of forcing every subject through the same mode.

The right answer usually depends on the subject and the student's age more than on a family's general preference, and a tutor who has genuinely worked across all three modes can tell you honestly which one your child needs, rather than pushing whichever one they happen to offer.

contentBlocks.heading: The vetting a tutor goes through before you ever see their profile
contentBlocks.body:
Every profile is checked against the specific programme, level and subject a family has asked for, not a general 'teaches IB' claim. That means confirming the tutor has actually taught this exact stage before: PYP inquiry units, MYP criterion-based marking, or a named DP subject at HL or SL, and that they understand how that subject's marks are actually awarded, not just its content.

Beyond what happens before a profile reaches you, there is a shorter list worth asking yourself, before and during the trial. Ask the tutor to describe, in specific terms, how they mark practice work: against real IB criteria and mark schemes, or against a general sense of a good answer. Ask what happens in the first four weeks, concretely, not as a vague promise of 'personalised learning'. Ask how they track deadlines if your child has TOK, the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments running in parallel, since a tutor juggling these loosely tends to let one slip.

After the trial, ask your child two things directly: what they understood better by the end of the session, and whether the tutor asked them questions or mostly talked. A tutor who spends most of a session explaining rather than checking understanding is teaching at the student, not with them, and that pattern rarely improves on its own once regular sessions start.

No certificate or years-in-the-field claim substitutes for this. A trial lesson, watched carefully, tells you more in sixty minutes than a profile description tells you in ten.

contentBlocks.heading: What separates a real IB specialist from a general tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
The clearest tell is how a tutor talks about marking. A general tutor, asked how a piece of work will be graded, tends to describe a good answer in the abstract: clear structure, correct working, strong vocabulary. A genuine IB specialist describes the actual criteria or assessment objectives your child's subject uses, points to a specific command term and explains what depth it demands, and can show, on a real past paper, where marks are typically lost by students at this level. That difference alone, asked as a single question before a trial, filters out a surprising number of otherwise strong general tutors.

A second tell is pacing against the syllabus. A specialist knows roughly where a DP1 or MYP 3 student should be by a given point in the year, because they have taught this exact stage before and watched students move through it. A general tutor, teaching the board for the first time, is often learning that pacing alongside your child, one term behind where a specialist would already be.

Before a trial lesson, worth asking directly: which exact level and subject have you taught before, and for how many full academic years, not just how many students in passing. During the trial, watch whether the tutor references the actual syllabus or criteria by name, or speaks in general terms about 'covering the topic'. After the trial, ask your child the two questions from the previous section, and add a third: did the tutor correct anything using the school's own terminology, or their own.

None of this means a general tutor is a bad teacher; many are excellent. It means the specific value IB tutoring adds, knowing exactly how this board marks and paces its own subjects, only shows up with someone who has actually taught it before, not someone learning it on your child's time.

contentBlocks.heading: What should four weeks of IB tutoring actually show?
contentBlocks.body:
After the first session or two, your child should be able to name something specific they understand better, not just say the session 'went fine'. A tutor teaching well is asking questions and waiting for answers, correcting misunderstandings as they surface rather than only at the end, and referencing the actual syllabus, criteria or mark scheme rather than teaching in generalities.

By four weeks, look for a shift from broad explanation towards targeted work: fewer repeated errors on a specific type of question, faster and more accurate reading of command terms, and a student who is starting to predict what a question is actually asking before attempting an answer. For MYP students, that might show up as work marked more consistently against a criterion the student previously struggled with; for DP students, as steadier performance on a specific paper style or topic within a subject.

Be realistic about what four weeks can and cannot show. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a student who started very late before a mock or the exam session has less time to close gaps than one who started early in the year. Some subjects also move slower than others by nature; a Mathematics HL student closing a method gap may show visible change faster than an English A student developing a more sophisticated argument style, which takes longer regardless of the tutor's skill.

If four weeks of consistent sessions with an IB tutor in Gurgaon show no discernible change at all, that is worth raising directly and asking for a different tutor, rather than assuming it will improve with more time on its own.

faqs.question: How is an IB tutor different from a CBSE or general school tutor?
faqs.answer: An IB tutor who is a genuine specialist has taught this board's actual grading structure before, from MYP's four criteria scored out of 8 each to DP's Higher Level and Standard Level split, and marks practice work against those criteria rather than against general standards picked up teaching a different board. A general tutor can still teach content correctly but usually has not taught to the IB's specific command terms and assessment objectives, which is often where marks are actually won or lost. Ask directly which exact level and subject a tutor has taught before, and for how many full academic years.

faqs.question: What questions should we ask an IB tutor before the trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask which exact programme, subject and level they have taught before, and for how many full academic years, not just how many students informally. Ask how they mark practice work, specifically against real IB criteria or mark schemes rather than a general sense of a good answer. Ask what a typical first four weeks covers concretely. These three questions, asked directly, tend to reveal quickly whether a tutor has genuine board-specific depth or is adapting general teaching experience to IB on the fly.

faqs.question: What should we watch for during the trial lesson itself?
faqs.answer: Watch whether the tutor asks your child questions and waits for answers, rather than talking through the material continuously. Watch whether they reference the actual syllabus, criteria or command terms by name, rather than speaking in general terms about 'covering the topic'. Afterwards, ask your child what they understood better by the end, and whether the tutor corrected anything using the school's own terminology. A trial that feels vague in these respects usually stays vague once regular sessions begin.

faqs.question: Our IB tutor is not working out, what do we do?
faqs.answer: Say so directly and ask IB Gram for a different match rather than persisting quietly through a term that is not helping. A fair trigger point is four consistent weeks with no visible change: no reduction in repeated errors, no improvement in reading command terms, and no specific new understanding your child can describe. Switching tutors mid-year is common and does not require restarting the whole process, since your child's programme, level and needs are already on file.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the programme stage, subject scarcity, the tutor's own experience, session length, and whether lessons run at home or online, and IB Gram does not quote figures here since these vary by the specific match and availability. What can be said honestly is that a rare HL subject combination or a tutor with strong examining or moderating background typically commands a higher fee than a more commonly taught subject, and it is worth asking directly during the consultation how a given tutor's fee is structured.

faqs.question: What should progress look like in the first month with a new IB tutor?
faqs.answer: By four weeks, look for a shift from general explanation towards targeted correction: fewer repeated mistakes on a specific type of question, faster and more accurate reading of command terms, and a student who can name something specific they understand better. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and progress in some subjects, particularly essay-based ones, shows more slowly than in subjects with clear right and wrong method. If nothing has visibly changed after a full month of consistent sessions, raise it directly.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than an online tutor for IB in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Neither is universally better; it depends on the subject and the student's age. A home tutor suits younger students and handwriting-heavy subjects where being in the room helps a tutor read hesitation and check working closely. Online suits most DP students well and opens access to specialists who might not reach every part of Gurgaon on a weekday evening. Many families use a hybrid arrangement, a regular tutor in one mode plus a specialist in the other for a single subject.

faqs.question: Can one IB tutor cover several subjects, or do we need a specialist per subject?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subjects involved and the student's stage. A strong generalist can sometimes cover two related subjects reasonably well at MYP level, but at DP, a Mathematics HL specialist and a Chemistry HL specialist are rarely the same person, and asking one tutor to stretch across very different subjects usually means one of them gets less genuine depth. For a student juggling several difficult subjects at once, most families in Gurgaon end up with one specialist per hardest subject rather than a single generalist for all of them.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor actually reach our sector on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Matching accounts for your exact society and sector, whether that is along Golf Course Road, Golf Course Extension Road, Sohna Road or elsewhere in Gurgaon, and for realistic weekday evening timing rather than assuming any tutor can reach any sector at any hour once school traffic sets in. Where a strong specialist for a rare subject is not close by, IB Gram will say so directly and suggest an online arrangement instead of matching you with a weaker but nearer alternative purely for convenience.

faqs.question: Should a parent be present during a home tutoring session, and what study space works best?
faqs.answer: That is your call; some parents sit in for the first session or two and then step back once they see how the tutor works, and others prefer to stay out of the room entirely from the start. What matters more is the study space itself: a quiet table away from the television and younger siblings, with the student's notebooks, past papers and a calculator or other subject-specific materials already at hand before the tutor arrives, rather than hunting for them mid-session. If a home session is missed for any reason, it is rescheduled directly with the tutor rather than simply dropped.

faqs.question: How do IB tutors handle a student switching schools mid-year in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A specialist tutor who has worked across several Gurgaon IB schools before is usually faster at picking up a new school's own pacing and calendar than a tutor encountering this board for the first time, though every school still has its own specific rhythm worth discussing directly in the intake call. Bring any recent test results, mock feedback or a syllabus outline from the new school if you have them, since that speeds up the first few sessions considerably.

faqs.question: Do you offer a free trial before we commit to regular IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, a demo or trial class is arranged before any ongoing commitment, at home, online or hybrid depending on what you prefer, subject to tutor availability. This is the single most useful step in the whole process, since it is where you actually see whether the tutor questions your child, marks against real criteria, and keeps a session structured, rather than relying on a profile description alone.

A general tutor can still teach content correctly but usually has not taught to the IB's specific command terms and assessment objectives, which is often where marks are actually won or lost. Ask directly which exact level and subject a tutor has taught before, and for how many full academic years.

mainEntity.name: What questions should we ask an IB tutor before the trial lesson?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask which exact programme, subject and level they have taught before, and for how many full academic years, not just how many students informally. Ask how they mark practice work, specifically against real IB criteria or mark schemes rather than a general sense of a good answer. Ask what a typical first four weeks covers concretely. These three questions, asked directly, tend to reveal quickly whether a tutor has genuine board-specific depth or is adapting general teaching experience to IB on the fly.

mainEntity.name: What should we watch for during the trial lesson itself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Watch whether the tutor asks your child questions and waits for answers, rather than talking through the material continuously. Watch whether they reference the actual syllabus, criteria or command terms by name, rather than speaking in general terms about 'covering the topic'. Afterwards, ask your child what they understood better by the end, and whether the tutor corrected anything using the school's own terminology. A trial that feels vague in these respects usually stays vague once regular sessions begin.

mainEntity.name: Our IB tutor is not working out, what do we do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so directly and ask IB Gram for a different match rather than persisting quietly through a term that is not helping. A fair trigger point is four consistent weeks with no visible change: no reduction in repeated errors, no improvement in reading command terms, and no specific new understanding your child can describe. Switching tutors mid-year is common and does not require restarting the whole process, since your child's programme, level and needs are already on file.

mainEntity.name: How much does an IB tutor cost in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees depend on the programme stage, subject scarcity, the tutor's own experience, session length, and whether lessons run at home or online, and IB Gram does not quote figures here since these vary by the specific match and availability. What can be said honestly is that a rare HL subject combination or a tutor with strong examining or moderating background typically commands a higher fee than a more commonly taught subject, and it is worth asking directly during the consultation how a given tutor's fee is structured.

mainEntity.name: What should progress look like in the first month with a new IB tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: By four weeks, look for a shift from general explanation towards targeted correction: fewer repeated mistakes on a specific type of question, faster and more accurate reading of command terms, and a student who can name something specific they understand better. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and progress in some subjects, particularly essay-based ones, shows more slowly than in subjects with clear right and wrong method. If nothing has visibly changed after a full month of consistent sessions, raise it directly.

mainEntity.name: Is a home tutor better than an online tutor for IB in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither is universally better; it depends on the subject and the student's age. A home tutor suits younger students and handwriting-heavy subjects where being in the room helps a tutor read hesitation and check working closely. Online suits most DP students well and opens access to specialists who might not reach every part of Gurgaon on a weekday evening. Many families use a hybrid arrangement, a regular tutor in one mode plus a specialist in the other for a single subject.

mainEntity.name: Can one IB tutor cover several subjects, or do we need a specialist per subject?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the subjects involved and the student's stage. A strong generalist can sometimes cover two related subjects reasonably well at MYP level, but at DP, a Mathematics HL specialist and a Chemistry HL specialist are rarely the same person, and asking one tutor to stretch across very different subjects usually means one of them gets less genuine depth. For a student juggling several difficult subjects at once, most families in Gurgaon end up with one specialist per hardest subject rather than a single generalist for all of them.

mainEntity.name: Will a home tutor actually reach our sector on a weekday evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Matching accounts for your exact society and sector, whether that is along Golf Course Road, Golf Course Extension Road, Sohna Road or elsewhere in Gurgaon, and for realistic weekday evening timing rather than assuming any tutor can reach any sector at any hour once school traffic sets in. Where a strong specialist for a rare subject is not close by, IB Gram will say so directly and suggest an online arrangement instead of matching you with a weaker but nearer alternative purely for convenience.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent be present during a home tutoring session, and what study space works best?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is your call; some parents sit in for the first session or two and then step back once they see how the tutor works, and others prefer to stay out of the room entirely from the start. What matters more is the study space itself: a quiet table away from the television and younger siblings, with the student's notebooks, past papers and a calculator or other subject-specific materials already at hand before the tutor arrives, rather than hunting for them mid-session. If a home session is missed for any reason, it is rescheduled directly with the tutor rather than simply dropped.

mainEntity.name: How do IB tutors handle a student switching schools mid-year in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: A specialist tutor who has worked across several Gurgaon IB schools before is usually faster at picking up a new school's own pacing and calendar than a tutor encountering this board for the first time, though every school still has its own specific rhythm worth discussing directly in the intake call. Bring any recent test results, mock feedback or a syllabus outline from the new school if you have them, since that speeds up the first few sessions considerably.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer a free trial before we commit to regular IB tutoring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a demo or trial class is arranged before any ongoing commitment, at home, online or hybrid depending on what you prefer, subject to tutor availability. This is the single most useful step in the whole process, since it is where you actually see whether the tutor questions your child, marks against real criteria, and keeps a session structured, rather than relying on a profile description alone.

contentBlocks.heading: How Does IB Gram Shortlist Tutors Worth Comparing in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A parent asking for IB tutors in Gurgaon is rarely looking for a single name; most want two or three people to actually meet before deciding who teaches their child for a year. IB Gram starts by asking about board, programme stage, subject and level, then about teaching style preferences where a family already has a sense of them, patient and slow-paced versus brisk and exam-focused, for instance, since two equally qualified tutors can suit very different students. Parents searching for the best ib tutors in Gurgaon, or simply typing ib tutors near me, are usually asking how to judge fit between real options, not asking for a single ranked answer no honest platform can give.

The shortlist that comes back is deliberately narrow: two or three verified profiles, each showing programme stages actually taught, subject groups and levels, and enough about how the tutor works that a parent is not comparing blank resumes. A tutor's own teaching style, patient explainer, brisk drill-and-practice, project-based, matters as much as their subject knowledge once two profiles are both genuinely qualified, and IB Gram tries to surface that distinction rather than hide it behind identical-sounding credentials.

A trial lesson with each shortlisted tutor is where the real comparison happens, not the written profile. Some students respond to a calm, methodical tutor; others need someone brisker who keeps momentum. Neither style is objectively better, and IB Gram does not rank tutors against each other, only against what your specific child needs.

If neither profile on the first shortlist feels right after trials, ask for a fresh one. Matching is not a one-shot process, and asking again is normal rather than a sign anything went wrong the first time.

2. IB Gram returns two or three verified profiles that already match, with a note on each one's approach.

4. Confirm the tutor whose style actually suits your child, or ask for a new shortlist.

contentBlocks.heading: What PYP, MYP and DP Each Demand From a Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor right for a Primary Years Programme (PYP) student, roughly ages 3 to 12, is judged on a different scale entirely to one right for the Diploma Programme. PYP has no external examinations; it works through six transdisciplinary themes, Who we are, Where we are in place and time, How we express ourselves, How the world works, How we organize ourselves, and Sharing the planet, delivered as units of inquiry alongside the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, and finishing with the PYP exhibition in the final year. The right tutor here is patient, comfortable with open-ended questions, and not trying to import exam drills a five or eight year old does not need yet.

Middle Years Programme (MYP), spanning MYP 1 to 5 across roughly ages 11 to 16 and eight subject groups, marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, with the criterion total out of 32 converting to a 1-7 grade through the IB's own boundaries. Two tutors can both know the content well and still differ sharply here: one teaches to the criteria explicitly, the other teaches content and hopes the marks follow, and only the first genuinely helps. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, the Community Project usually in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional at each school's own discretion.

Diploma Programme (DP) runs two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each scored 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum and 24 as the minimum for the diploma subject to the IB's failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Most Gurgaon schools sit the May session, a minority use November, and results land in early July. An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon should be compared on exact HL or SL combination taught; an MYP tutor in Gurgaon should be compared on criterion-marking fluency, not just years of general experience.

An MYP tutor must teach to criteria A to D explicitly, not just to content.

CAS runs alongside DP subjects and is tracked separately from tuition.

contentBlocks.heading: How Two Tutors' Subject Depth Can Look the Same but Isn't
contentBlocks.body:
Two tutor profiles can both list 'IB Mathematics' and mean quite different things. Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) are separate courses, each offered at Higher Level or Standard Level, and a tutor strong in one does not automatically transfer to the other; ask which route and level each shortlisted tutor has actually taught before assuming 'Maths' means the same thing on both profiles. The same applies to IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology, where practical work, internal assessment expectations and command terms separate a tutor who has taught the syllabus from one who has taught the subject generally.

IB English, as Language A or Language B depending on a student's first language, needs a tutor who marks against the student's own school's criteria and engages closely with set texts rather than recycling generic essay technique from another board. Two profiles that both say 'IB English' can differ enormously here, and it is worth asking each shortlisted tutor directly which texts and which criteria they actually use in a session.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sit outside the six subject groups but carry real weight, up to 3 points combined. TOK examines how different areas of knowledge justify what they claim, through an exhibition and an essay; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece in a subject the student chooses, supervised rather than taught conventionally. When comparing two tutors for TOK or EE support, ask specifically how many students they have supervised through to submission, since general subject knowledge alone does not cover this.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: What Each Tutor on Your Shortlist Offers
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where most comparisons start, and it is IB Gram's default recommendation across Gurgaon: a tutor at the table sees a student's actual working and corrects a wrong method as it happens, which matters more for younger MYP and PYP students who focus better with someone physically present. IB home tutors in Gurgaon remain the most compared format on shortlists, and when two shortlisted tutors both offer home visits, compare not just whether they can come, but how reliably their existing route allows a fixed weekly slot rather than a shifting one.

Some tutors on a shortlist teach online only, or online as their stronger format, and that is a genuine option rather than a lesser one for the right subject. IB online tutor Gurgaon searches usually come from families needing a narrow HL combination that simply is not within home-visit distance, and a shared whiteboard with annotated past papers works well for problem-solving subjects without losing much. If one shortlisted tutor is online-only and the other offers home visits, compare them on subject depth first, since format alone should not decide the shortlist.

Hybrid tutors, offering regular home sessions with occasional online cover before a test or when travel fails, often give families the most flexibility when comparing a shortlist, since the arrangement can lean more toward whichever format suits a given week. The honest trade-off stands regardless of which tutor is chosen: home tuition costs more of a tutor's time and limits which tutors can reach you reliably; a coaching-centre batch or an online group class is cheaper per head with less individual correction; pure online removes travel risk but depends on a student showing rough working clearly on camera. Weigh format alongside subject fit, not before it.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor's Claims Are Checked Before You Compare Them
contentBlocks.body:
Before either profile reaches your shortlist, IB Gram checks what each claims: the programme stages and subjects actually taught, at what level, and whether the experience genuinely matches what you asked for rather than a nearby subject presented as close enough. A tutor who taught IB Chemistry SL is not automatically right for HL, and a profile that blurs the two gets questioned before a family sees it.

Comparing two verified profiles still needs a parent's own questions. Ask each tutor directly which subject group, level and, where relevant, syllabus code they have taught, and for how long with students at your child's actual programme stage. Ask what a typical first session covers, and how they respond when a student's working shows a wrong method rather than a wrong final number, since the answer reveals more about teaching approach than a credential list does. A free trial with each tutor, arranged before any commitment, is the real comparison: watch whether the first ten minutes go toward understanding your child's specific gaps, or whether a prepared worksheet appears regardless of who is in the room.

No certificate substitutes for the trial, for either tutor on the shortlist. A subject degree or workshop certificate shows a baseline, not classroom skill with this particular student, and the two trials, compared honestly, are the real decision point, not whichever profile reads more impressively on paper. If one tutor is reluctant to run a proper diagnostic while the other welcomes it, treat that difference itself as part of the comparison, since it usually predicts how each would actually teach across a full term rather than just in a single showcase session.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Separates Two Strong-Looking Tutor Profiles?
contentBlocks.body:
Two tutor profiles on a shortlist can look nearly identical on paper: similar years of experience, similar subjects, similar polite phrasing about personalised sessions. What actually separates them only shows up in a trial lesson, and a parent needs a deliberate way to notice it rather than trusting a general impression afterwards. Watch specifically for how each tutor opens the session: one who asks about the student's last school test and works from an actual gap is different from one who launches straight into a prepared worksheet regardless of who is sitting there.

Build a short checklist before either trial, not after both, so you are judging both tutors against the same standard rather than letting the second trial's freshness unfairly colour the comparison. Useful checklist items: did the tutor ask about the school's own scheme of work; did they diagnose a real gap rather than teach generically; how did they explain a wrong answer, patiently rebuilding the method or simply supplying the right one; did the pace suit your child or run ahead of them; and how precisely did they answer questions about their own experience with this exact level and subject. Score each trial the same evening, while it is fresh, since two trials a week apart blur together fast in memory.

Space the two trials a few days apart, and tell your child plainly that you are trying two tutors before deciding; most children handle this better than parents fear, provided nobody pretends the second trial is unrelated to the first. If neither tutor comes out clearly ahead, or the one you choose is not working after a genuine few weeks, say so and ask IB Gram for a different match. Comparing well is not a one-time judgement; it is a standard you keep applying honestly even after the first choice is made.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Know a Chosen Tutor Is Actually Working Out?
contentBlocks.body:
Once you have compared and chosen, progress in the first month looks modest: fewer repeated errors on a familiar type of problem, a student explaining a method aloud rather than just stating an answer, and homework that starts without a daily argument about it. It is not a jump in a school grade that quickly, and no tutor can guarantee a grade; a tutor who implies otherwise during the comparison stage was already a warning sign worth remembering.

By six to eight weeks in, check whether the chosen tutor is still teaching to the school's own scheme of work and marking criteria, the same standard they demonstrated in the trial that won them the comparison, and whether actual school test results, not just how sessions feel, are shifting. A tutor who was excellent in a single trial but has since settled into a generic routine is not the tutor you compared and chose.

There are honest limits regardless of which tutor was picked. A tutor started weeks before a mock cannot undo a year of gaps, and the right response is a narrower, realistic target for that mock plus a longer plan after it, not quiet disappointment that the comparison process somehow failed. A subject the student genuinely dislikes may still improve in grade without becoming enjoyable, which is a legitimate outcome. Review honestly at each check-in, and if the answer is genuinely 'not working', that is what the comparison process exists to catch, not something to feel locked into.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting With the Home Tutor You Chose From the Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Once the comparison is done and a tutor is chosen, starting properly matters as much as the choice itself. Confirm the format, home, online or hybrid, and fix a specific weekly slot around the household's real evening rather than an optimistic one on paper. For a home session, prepare an actual study space, a table rather than a bed, books and past papers ready, with enough quiet that the tutor is not competing with a television down the hall. For online, test the shared screen and whiteboard once before the first real lesson.

The first proper session, distinct from either trial, usually goes deeper: recent test papers, a school report if available, and an honest conversation about what the student genuinely finds hardest rather than what a parent assumes. From there, tutor and family sketch a rough plan for the term, tied to the school's own test and mock calendar rather than a fixed generic pace, with room to adjust as pressure rises before mocks and eases afterward.

Availability remains subject to tutor availability and depends on level and schedule, even for the tutor who won the comparison, so confirm the slot promptly rather than leaving it open. If the arrangement genuinely does not hold up after a fair attempt, despite winning the original comparison, IB Gram can put forward a different match; the comparison process does not end the day you choose, it continues quietly for as long as the tuition does.

faqs.question: How many IB tutors should I actually compare before choosing one?
faqs.answer: Two or three, in most cases. Comparing more than that rarely improves the decision and mostly adds scheduling strain, since running fair trials with five different tutors inside a busy school week is hard to manage honestly. IB Gram narrows an initial pool to two or three verified profiles that already match your board, programme stage and format preference, so the comparison you run is between genuinely close options rather than a wide field of guesses. If none of them feels right after trials, ask for a fresh shortlist rather than stretching the first one further than it should reasonably go.

faqs.question: What should I ask two tutors to tell the difference between them?
faqs.answer: Ask both the exact same set of questions, in the same order if possible, so the comparison is fair. Ask which specific subject group, level and syllabus code they have taught, how long, what a typical first session covers, and how they respond when a student's working shows a wrong method rather than a wrong answer. Two tutors who both say 'experienced with IB' can differ enormously once you push past that phrase, and the specific answers, not the general confidence, are what actually separates them.

faqs.question: How do I run two trial lessons without confusing my child?
faqs.answer: Space them a few days apart and tell your child honestly that you are trying two tutors before deciding. Children generally handle this better than parents expect, provided nobody pretends the second trial is unrelated to the first; the confusion usually comes from secrecy, not from the comparison itself. Keep both trials a similar length and similar topic where possible, and avoid scheduling either one in the same week as a school test, when a tired child will not represent either tutor fairly.
