contentBlocks.heading: How Do Two IB Home Tuitions Shortlist Profiles Compare Side by Side?
contentBlocks.body:
The honest answer is that a side-by-side comparison only works if both tutors are judged against the same fixed criteria, written down before either trial lesson, not decided afterward based on which lesson simply felt nicer. A useful comparison checklist covers five things: board experience on the exact subject and level, familiarity with the student's actual school's pacing so far as it can be known, the tutor's own explanation of how they structure a term, travel or online reliability for the family's fixed slot, and how the trial lesson itself went with the specific student, not a hypothetical one.

Running two trial lessons without unsettling the student takes a little planning. Space them a few days apart rather than back to back, so the student is not comparing two strangers in the same evening, and frame both to the student simply as trying out a tutor, not as an audition either tutor needs to win. Avoid telling the student which one is the parent's early favourite before both trials are done, since that can shape how the second session is received unfairly.

After both trials, compare notes against the original checklist rather than gut feeling alone, though gut feeling about whether the student seemed comfortable and engaged still matters and should not be dismissed. A tutor who is technically stronger on paper but whom the student visibly tensed up around is rarely the better long-term choice for IB home tuitions in Gurgaon, since consistency over months depends on the student wanting to show up for the session, not dreading it.

If the first choice does not hold up after a few weeks, in practice rather than in the trial, IB Gram can help the family return to the shortlist and try the second profile, or build a fresh one if neither fit well. This should never require the family to explain themselves at length. A short, honest note about what was not working, whether pace, communication, or subject depth, is enough to move forward with the next match.
items: Fix the comparison criteria before either trial: experience, school familiarity, term plan, reliability, trial fit.
Space two trial lessons a few days apart so the student is not comparing them in one evening.
Frame both trials to the student as simply trying out a tutor, not as a competition.
Weigh the student's comfort in the trial alongside the tutor's technical experience, not instead of it.
Return to the shortlist or build a fresh one if the first match does not hold up after a few weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Progress Look Like After Switching IB Tutors?
contentBlocks.body:
The honest answer is that progress after settling on one tutor from a shortlist should be visible within a handful of sessions, not necessarily in marks yet, but in how the student talks about the subject and approaches a problem when stuck. A student who previously froze on an unfamiliar Mathematics question should, within a month, at least attempt a method rather than leaving it blank, and a MYP student should start referencing criteria by letter rather than only asking whether an answer is right or wrong.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any claim that sounds like a guarantee is worth being sceptical of, whatever the format or the fee structure behind it. What a good tutor can commit to is a clear plan against the student's actual gaps, regular short updates to the parent on what was covered and what needs more work, and honesty when a target genuinely looks out of reach given the time left before mocks or the exam session, rather than false reassurance carried right up to results day.

Progress can also plateau for reasons that have nothing to do with the tutor: a heavy school week, a coursework deadline eating into revision time, or a student simply needing longer on a genuinely hard topic like a difficult IA methodology or a demanding TOK claim. A parent comparing IB home tuitions in Gurgaon against this backdrop should expect the tutor to name these factors honestly rather than either blaming the student or claiming everything is on track when it clearly is not.

It is also fair, and sometimes correct, for a tutor to say a student does not need continued tutoring on a particular subject, once independence has been built and school support alone is enough. A tutor who never says this, across a full year, is worth questioning. The goal of home tuition is a student who eventually needs the tutor less, not one who becomes permanently dependent on the sessions.
items: Expect visible change in approach within a handful of sessions, before marks necessarily move.
No tutor can guarantee a grade; treat any claim that sounds like one with caution.
A good tutor names honestly when a target looks out of reach given the time left.
Plateaus can come from school pressure or a genuinely hard topic, not only from the tutor.
A tutor who never suggests reducing sessions as independence grows is worth questioning over a full year.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB Home Tuitions in Gurgaon: What to Prepare
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started is deliberately simple. A parent sends a query or books a free consultation, and IB Gram asks about the board, syllabus, level, the student's school calendar so far as timing goes, the family's corridor and preferred weekday evening slot, before putting together a shortlist rather than a single suggestion. Having the student's current textbook, recent test papers, or a note of specific topics they are struggling with ready for that first conversation speeds the whole process up considerably, though it is not required to begin.

Before the first trial lesson, it helps to set aside a quiet corner at home with a table, good lighting and space for the student's books and a laptop if the subject needs one, since a home tutor working well depends partly on the environment they are teaching in. Younger students may want a parent nearby for the first few minutes to settle in; older DP students usually prefer to be left to it once introductions are done.

The first session with each shortlisted tutor should include a short diagnostic conversation about where the student currently stands, a look at recent work or a past paper if one is available, and a plan for what the next few sessions will cover, not simply a first lesson of unstructured content. A tutor who skips this and launches straight into teaching without checking the student's starting point is harder to judge fairly against one who takes the time to establish it.

Once the family settles on a match from the shortlist, lessons can run at home, online or in a hybrid pattern depending on what suits the week, and the family can ask for a different match at any point if the fit changes, subject to tutor availability. Nothing about the arrangement needs to be treated as final on day one.

Gather recent test papers or a note of struggling topics before the first trial lesson.

faqs.question: How many tutors should we actually shortlist before choosing one for IB home tuitions in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually the right number. Fewer than two removes the point of comparing at all, and more than three tends to overwhelm both the parent and the student with trial lessons that blur together rather than stand out clearly. IB Gram typically presents two or three verified profiles matched to the exact programme, subject, level and corridor, so the family is comparing genuinely relevant options rather than a long list that needs its own filtering. If none of the first shortlist feels right after trials, a fresh shortlist can be built rather than settling for a weak fourth option.

faqs.question: Is it awkward for the student to meet more than one tutor before we decide?
faqs.answer: It can feel slightly unusual the first time, but most students settle into it quickly once told plainly that trying a tutor out is normal and not a test they can fail. Spacing the two trial lessons a few days apart, rather than back to back on the same evening, helps the student engage properly with each one instead of comparing them mid-session. Framing it to the student as finding the right fit, rather than as auditions, keeps the pressure off them and on the process itself, which is where it belongs.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor actually travel to our sector on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Most home tutors on IB Gram's shortlists work a defined weekly route across specific Gurgaon corridors, so travel time is checked against that existing route before a profile is suggested, not guessed at afterward. A tutor already teaching in Sushant Lok on Tuesday evenings can often extend into nearby DLF sectors on the same evening more reliably than one starting cold from across the city. Evening traffic can still stretch a short trip on a bad day, which is why a fixed, realistic slot matters more than picking the earliest possible time on paper.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session has to be missed?
faqs.answer: A missed session should be rescheduled directly with the tutor wherever possible, ideally within the same week so the student's rhythm is not badly disrupted. Sudden school activities, a sick day, or unexpected evening traffic are common reasons in Gurgaon specifically, and a reliable tutor will usually offer an alternative slot rather than simply skipping the week. If missed sessions become a repeated pattern on either side, it is worth raising directly with IB Gram, since a shortlist match that cannot hold a stable weekly slot is not really working, whatever else about the fit seems fine.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to sit in on IB home tuitions sessions?
faqs.answer: It depends mostly on the student's age and the stage they are at. Younger MYP students often benefit from a parent nearby for the first few sessions, mainly to help settle the routine and confirm the study space is working, while older DP students generally do better with the parent stepping back once introductions are done, so the student can be direct with the tutor about what they do not understand without feeling watched. There is no fixed rule here, and it is worth simply asking the student what makes them more comfortable.

faqs.question: How much do IB home tuitions in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: Fees are not published here, since cost depends on the programme stage, subject scarcity, the tutor's own experience, session length, and whether lessons run at home, online or hybrid; a specific figure would mislead more than it would help. What can be said is that IB Gram will discuss pricing structure directly once a shortlist is built, and that comparing tutors on structure, per session, monthly, or package based, is a fairer question to ask each one than comparing on a single number pulled out of context.

faqs.question: What if we switch from CBSE or ICSE mid-course into the IB?
faqs.answer: This is common enough that most IB home tutors in Gurgaon have handled it before, though the transition suits some subjects more smoothly than others. The bigger adjustment is usually not content but assessment style, since MYP's criterion-based marking and DP's command-term-driven exam answers reward a different way of writing a response than board exams the student may be used to. A tutor who has taught students through exactly this switch before is worth prioritising on the shortlist over one who has only ever taught students already inside the IB system.

faqs.question: Does the home tutor follow our child's school's own pacing?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot access a school's internal scheme of work directly, but a good one will ask the parent or student for recent tests, topic lists or any materials the school shares, and adjust the tutoring plan to sit alongside what is being taught in class rather than running a completely separate syllabus sequence. This matters most around coursework and internal assessment deadlines, where working against the school's own timeline, not a generic one, keeps the student from being pulled in two directions in the same week.

faqs.question: What does the free trial or demo class actually cover?
faqs.answer: A trial lesson with a shortlisted tutor typically opens with a short diagnostic conversation about where the student currently stands, moves into a piece of real content or a past question worked through together, and closes with the tutor's early read on what a first few weeks of sessions would focus on. It is not a full lesson's worth of new content delivered at speed. The point is for both the family and the tutor to judge fit honestly before committing to a term of IB home tuitions in Gurgaon.

faqs.question: How soon can a tutor actually start once we choose from the shortlist?
faqs.answer: This depends on tutor availability and the specific slot the family needs, so it varies case by case rather than following one fixed timeline. Families who share their preferred weekday evening slot and corridor early in the process, at the first query stage rather than after the shortlist is built, tend to get sessions confirmed faster, since availability across a specific evening and corridor is the main constraint IB Gram is working against when matching.

faqs.question: What if we pick a tutor from the shortlist and it still is not working after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: This happens sometimes even after a good trial lesson, since a few weeks of real sessions reveal things a single trial cannot. The family can ask IB Gram for a different match, subject to availability, and a short, honest note about what specifically was not working, pace, communication, or subject depth, helps the next match be better targeted than simply starting the shortlist process over from nothing. There is no obligation to persist with a tutor who is clearly not the right fit for the student.

faqs.question: Can two siblings on different IB stages share the same home tutor?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, though it depends heavily on the subjects and levels involved rather than being a simple yes. A tutor confident across both MYP and DP Mathematics, for instance, might reasonably teach a MYP 4 student and a DP1 sibling in back-to-back sessions on the same evening, which is convenient for scheduling and travel. But a tutor stretched too thin across very different levels rarely serves either student as well as two more specialised tutors would, so this is worth weighing carefully rather than assumed purely for convenience.

heroTitle: Comparing IB Private Tutors Across Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: The first IB private tutor a family meets is rarely the right long-term fit by accident. This page is about building a short, comparable list of two or three profiles, running fair trials, and knowing when to ask for someone else instead of persisting through a bad match.
introSummary: IB private tutors Gurgaon families compare are rarely interchangeable, and choosing the first name offered is usually a mistake worth avoiding: board experience, the exact level taught, familiarity with a similar school calendar and, just as often overlooked, whether a tutor's home tutoring route actually reaches the family's sector, all vary from one profile to the next. IB Gram's default is a shortlist of two or three verified profiles rather than a single recommendation, because a fair side-by-side comparison, not a single interview, is what actually surfaces the right fit. This page sets out how that shortlist is built across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, what to weigh profile against profile, how to run trial lessons with more than one tutor without the student feeling like part of an audition, and how to ask for a different tutor cleanly if the first choice is not working.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Build a Shortlist of IB Private Tutors in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist starts the same way a single match would: a short query or a free consultation call covering programme stage, subject, the school's own pacing where it is known, and where in Gurgaon the family lives. The difference is what IB Gram does with that information next. Instead of sending one name, it puts together two or three verified profiles that genuinely differ from each other in a useful way, not three tutors who all look the same on paper.

The process runs in order:

1. IB Gram collects programme, subject, level and corridor, then filters verified profiles that fit all four before comparing anything else.
2. From that filtered set, two or three profiles are chosen so they differ on something that matters: one may have deeper HL Maths experience, another more recent work with a similar school's pacing.
3. Each profile is shared with a short note on what makes it distinct, so the family is comparing strengths rather than reading three near-identical summaries.
4. Free trial classes are arranged with more than one tutor where the family wants that, spaced out so the student is not overwhelmed in a single week.
5. The family chooses, or asks IB Gram to keep looking if none of the three is right, and a weekly slot is only fixed once that choice is made.

A shortlist of IB private tutors Gurgaon families actually use well is a short one. Three profiles that differ on something real beat five that all sound similar, and IB Gram would rather send fewer, sharper options than pad a list to look thorough.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: Which Profile Should the Shortlist Target?
contentBlocks.body:
For a PYP student, age 3 to 12, the useful comparison across a shortlist is less about exam technique, since the programme has no external examinations, and more about how comfortable each tutor is running inquiry-based sessions around the six transdisciplinary themes, who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet, and working toward the ten attributes of the IB learner profile. A tutor with PYP exhibition experience, the extended piece of independent inquiry PYP students complete in their final year, is worth asking about directly.

For MYP students, MYP 1 to MYP 5 across roughly ages 11 to 16 and eight subject groups, the comparison that matters most is how well each tutor actually understands criterion-based marking: four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, converting through IB grade boundaries to a final 1 to 7. A tutor on the shortlist who talks about getting better marks without mentioning which criterion is weak is usually less useful than one who can point to a specific criterion. MYP 5 students also need a tutor who understands the Personal Project; MYP 3 or 4 students, the smaller Community Project instead, and some schools add optional MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 worth asking each tutor whether they have prepared students for.

For DP students, the two-year DP1 and DP2 course of six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 more points and Creativity, Activity, Service required alongside, the comparison gets sharper still: which subjects has each tutor actually taught at HL versus SL, how recent is their experience with the May exam session most Gurgaon schools use, and have they worked with a DP2 student through mocks before, since May results are only released in early July and a tutor unfamiliar with that runway plans badly.

Comparing tutors across programme stage is not a formality. A profile that reads well for a DP2 Physics HL student may be entirely wrong for a younger sibling starting MYP, and IB Gram builds separate shortlists for each rather than assuming one tutor should stretch across both.
items: PYP shortlist criterion: comfort with inquiry-based, theme-led sessions.
MYP shortlist criterion: fluency in criterion-based marking, not vague praise.
DP shortlist criterion: HL versus SL experience in the exact subject.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Subject Depth Across a Shortlist of IB Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Subject depth is where two profiles that look similar at a glance usually turn out to differ most. In Mathematics, ask whether a tutor has taught Analysis and Approaches (AA) or Applications and Interpretation (AI), and at which level, since a tutor strong in AI Standard Level is not automatically the right comparison point for a student doing AA Higher Level; the exploration, the subject's internal assessment component, is worth asking about specifically, along with calculator and non-calculator paper technique.

In Physics, Chemistry and Biology, compare how each tutor talks about internal assessment and practical write-ups: a tutor who has marked or moderated IB coursework will usually describe what separates a strong method section from a weak one in specific terms, while a tutor who has only taught content tends to speak more generally. English is worth checking carefully too, since English A, which assumes near-native fluency and pushes into literary analysis, and English B, a language-acquisition course with different criteria, are not interchangeable, and a profile that lists both without distinguishing them is worth a direct question.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit outside the six main subjects but are frequently where a shortlist narrows fastest, since guiding structure, sourcing and argument within the IB's academic integrity rules is a genuinely different skill from subject teaching, and not every strong subject tutor does it well. For MYP subjects, ask specifically how a tutor scores against the four lettered criteria rather than how they would grade the work informally, since the two habits produce different feedback.

A useful comparison question across any shortlist: ask each tutor to describe, in a sentence, what a strong answer looks like against the command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, for one topic the student is currently struggling with. The answers usually reveal more about depth than a list of qualifications does.

That does not mean a shorter shortlist, though. It usually means IB Gram widens the comparison to include online-first profiles alongside home-visiting ones, so a family on Dwarka Expressway is comparing, say, one tutor who can reach Sobha City on a fixed weekday evening against one who works online but has deeper HL subject experience, rather than being limited to whichever home tutor happens to be nearest.

A family moving between these corridors, from an SPR society near Sector 68 to a New Gurgaon address near Sector 84, for instance, should expect the comparison to reset: a tutor who worked well for the old address is not automatically the strongest option once the commute changes. It is worth telling IB Gram about a planned move early, since a shortlist built around the new address, rather than adjusted after the fact, avoids a term of an awkward commute for the tutor.

Corridor is one input into the comparison, not the only one. A specialist DP Chemistry tutor working mostly online from outside these three corridors can still outrank a locally based generalist on a shortlist, if the subject is scarce enough that fit matters more than the commute.

contentBlocks.heading: School Familiarity: A Real Criterion When Comparing Tutors in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
School familiarity is one of the more useful, and more overlooked, ways to tell two similar-looking profiles apart. Families whose children attend schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali, or DPS International Edge often assume any qualified IB tutor will do; in practice, a tutor who has recently worked with a similar international school calendar tends to plan a term more accurately than one guessing at it. These names are used here only as local context: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

When comparing profiles, ask each tutor how they would find out a school's own pacing if they have not worked with that exact school before, rather than assuming familiarity that is not there. A reasonable answer involves reviewing the scheme of work or recent test papers the family can share, not guessing from the IB subject guide alone.

Calendar pressure is common across Gurgaon's international schools even where exact pacing differs: unit tests through each term, DP2 mocks set months ahead of the May session, Personal Project or Community Project deadlines in the MYP years, and EE, IA and CAS milestones building through DP2. A strong comparison question for any shortlist is how each tutor plans backward from these points rather than teaching content in whatever order feels natural that week.

None of this means a tutor without direct experience at a specific school should be ruled out automatically. It means the comparison should include the question directly, rather than assuming every profile handles calendar pressure the same way.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Home Tuition, Online and Hybrid Tutors Side by Side in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
When a shortlist includes tutors across different formats, home tuition, online and hybrid, compare them on the same basis rather than treating format as a tiebreaker. A home tutor sitting with the student at their own table, working from the student's actual notes and past papers, usually catches small things early: a rushed method, a hesitant question, a posture that suggests fatigue rather than difficulty. That advantage is real, and it is why home tuition is IB Gram's default recommendation where a corridor supports it comfortably.

An online profile earns its place on a shortlist differently, usually through subject depth or scheduling reach rather than physical presence. A live online session, run well with a shared whiteboard and annotated past papers, can outperform a mediocre home visit, particularly for a scarce HL subject where the strongest specialist simply does not have a home-visit route near the family's sector. Comparing a home tutor against an online specialist is not really comparing format against format; it is comparing convenience against depth, and the honest answer depends on which one the family is short on.

A hybrid profile, mostly home with an occasional online session before a mock or after a missed week, is worth including on a shortlist specifically when a family wants the best of both without committing fully to either. The trade-off is coordination: confirming week by week which format applies takes slightly more attention than a fixed arrangement.

The comparison question worth asking directly: for this particular student, this subject, and this stage, does undivided physical presence matter more than raw subject depth right now? The answer changes the shortlist more than any other single factor.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Each IB Tutor Profile Show Before It Reaches Your Shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Every profile IB Gram shares has already been checked for subject background, the board and level actually taught, and any relevant teaching or examining history the tutor can document. That baseline check is what makes a shortlist worth comparing in the first place; it is not, on its own, a reason to skip a trial lesson.

Once a shortlist arrives, a family can usefully compare profiles on a few specific points rather than a general impression: which level and subject has each tutor most recently taught, how each one describes their approach to a first session, whether they mention reviewing a school's scheme of work before starting, and how each one talks about reporting progress back to parents. A profile heavy on general claims and light on specifics is worth a direct follow-up question before it stays on the list.

It also helps to ask each tutor the same question and compare the answers side by side, something like how would you spend the first thirty minutes with this student, or what would make you recommend a different tutor instead of continuing. The second question in particular tends to separate tutors who are confident enough to be honest about fit from those who will simply agree to anything to secure the work.

If a tutor on the shortlist cannot answer specifically, that is useful information too. A vague answer to a direct question about method is a better predictor of a poor trial lesson than anything on the profile itself.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Run Fair Trial Lessons With More Than One Tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Running two or three trial lessons well starts with spacing, not compression. Fitting three unfamiliar tutors into one week, on top of school, buses and homework, tends to tire a student out before any of the sessions can be judged fairly; spreading trials across two or three weeks, one at a time, gives a more honest read on each one. IB Gram will schedule it either way if a family prefers to compare quickly, but spacing is the better default for most students.

To compare fairly, keep the material roughly similar across trials where possible: the same recent topic, the same past paper, or the same piece of the student's own work, rather than letting each tutor pick something different. A tutor who explains a weak IA method section clearly is more directly comparable to another tutor doing the same than to one who spent the session on an unrelated topic entirely. Watching how each tutor responds to a wrong answer, whether they explain the reasoning or just give the correct one, tends to be more revealing than watching how they teach something the student already understands.

Deciding between two reasonable options does not have to be agonising. If two tutors are both clearly capable, weigh the smaller things: which one the student seemed more comfortable asking questions to, which one's evening slot fits more reliably, which one already knows the relevant syllabus best. If neither trial felt right, say so plainly and ask IB Gram to widen the search rather than settling for the less-bad of two mediocre fits.

The student's own reaction matters more than it might seem. A parent may prefer the more experienced-sounding tutor on paper, but a student who visibly relaxes with the other one is often giving the more useful signal, particularly for a student who has been anxious about a subject for a while.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Home Tuition Progress Look Like Six Weeks In?
contentBlocks.body:
Once a shortlist of IB private tutors Gurgaon families compare has produced a chosen tutor, the comparison does not simply end; it shifts to checking, over the first six weeks, that the choice was the right one. Concrete signs are more useful than a general feeling: fewer careless errors on a type of question the student previously got wrong for avoidable reasons, more confident use of command terms in written answers, and a student who can explain an answer's structure out loud rather than just repeating it.

A parent should also expect a rough read on where the student stands against the school's own tests, or against mock results for DP2 students, by the end of a first term, along with a clear view of which topics still need dedicated attention. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and treating any claim otherwise with real caution applies regardless of how strong a profile looked during comparison; what a good tutor offers instead is a specific, checkable account of where the gaps were.

If six weeks in, progress still looks like the vague impression it started as, no concrete change, no specific update, that is a legitimate reason to revisit the shortlist rather than assume more time will fix it. The comparison that mattered before the trial matters again here: is this tutor still the best fit among realistic options, or did the strongest profile on paper simply not translate into the strongest fit in practice?

Some students, particularly younger ones in the PYP years, show progress unevenly, with a slow start followed by a faster stretch once confidence builds, so a single flat week is not on its own a signal to switch. A pattern across several weeks is the more reliable read.

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a Shortlist Into One IB Private Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Getting from a shortlist to a decision does not need a long process. Once the family has met two or three tutors, whether through trial lessons or a shorter introductory call, IB Gram asks which one the family and student both leaned toward and why, since the reasoning behind a choice is often as useful as the choice itself if a switch is ever needed later.

Before the first paid session, it helps to have on hand what made the comparison useful in the first place: any test scripts or reports shared during trials, a note on which subjects or topics were compared, and which weekday evenings actually worked across the trial period. None of this needs to be formal; a short summary is enough for IB Gram to fix a weekly slot that reflects what the comparison actually showed, rather than starting from scratch.

Choosing does not close the door on comparison entirely. If, a few weeks or a term in, the chosen tutor is not delivering what the trial suggested, IB Gram treats that as new information rather than a fixed outcome, and will shortlist again with what has been learned since, sharper this time, because the family now knows more specifically what worked and what did not.

The point of comparing several tutors in the first place was never to find a perfect match on the first try. It was to reduce the odds of a bad one, and to make switching, if it is ever needed, a quick correction rather than starting over.

faqs.question: How many IB private tutors Gurgaon families shortlist before choosing one?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually enough for IB private tutors Gurgaon families to compare meaningfully, and more than that tends to overwhelm rather than help. IB Gram deliberately narrows to profiles that differ on something real, HL versus SL experience, a specific school's pacing, home versus online reach, rather than sending five near-identical names for a family to sort through. A tighter shortlist also makes trial lessons more manageable for the student, since comparing three unfamiliar adults across a few weeks is already a lot to ask without adding more names to the list.

faqs.question: Is it awkward to run trial lessons with more than one tutor?
faqs.answer: It does not have to be. Spacing trials across a couple of weeks, rather than compressing them into one, keeps the experience closer to a normal lesson than an audition, and most students settle into the second or third trial more easily than the first. Tutors on IB Gram's shortlist understand that a trial is exactly that, a trial, not a guaranteed booking, so there is no need to apologise for comparing more than one before deciding.

faqs.question: What should be compared across trial lessons besides how the tutor teaches?
faqs.answer: How the tutor teaches matters most, but a few practical things are worth comparing too: how reliably each tutor confirmed the slot and arrived on time, whether they reviewed the student's recent work beforehand or arrived cold, and how clearly they explained what the next session would cover. A tutor who is strong in the room but consistently late or disorganised about scheduling is a real trade-off, not a minor detail, especially for a family managing evenings across a busy Gurgaon commute.

faqs.question: How do you compare tutors for a family living on Dwarka Expressway or SPR?
faqs.answer: The comparison usually widens to include online-first specialists alongside any home-visiting tutors nearby, since these corridors have a thinner pool of local tutors than older parts of Gurgaon. A family on Dwarka Expressway, for instance, might compare a tutor who can reach a Sobha City address on a fixed evening against a subject specialist who works online but has deeper HL experience, and the right answer depends on which one the family is more short on: convenience or depth.

faqs.question: What if two tutors on the shortlist both seem equally good?
faqs.answer: That is a genuinely common outcome, and it is fine to decide on smaller factors rather than searching for a decisive difference that may not exist. Which tutor the student seemed more relaxed with, whose evening slot fits more reliably around buses and activities, and who already knows the relevant syllabus best are all reasonable tiebreakers. IB Gram would rather a family pick confidently between two good options than delay a decision looking for a perfect one.

faqs.question: Can a family ask for a different shortlist if none of the first three tutors fit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a normal part of the process rather than a complaint IB Gram needs persuading to act on. Saying specifically what did not work, pace, personality, subject depth, or simply that none of the trial slots suited the family's evenings, helps IB Gram put together a sharper second shortlist rather than repeating the same near-misses. It also helps to say which parts of the first three trials were closer to right, even if none was fully right, since that narrows the second round faster than starting from a blank brief again. Families who ask for a second shortlist are not treated as difficult; the process is built to expect it.

faqs.question: When comparing home tutors, how do we check each one can actually reach our sector on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Ask directly during the shortlist stage rather than waiting to find out at the first trial. IB Gram already filters profiles by corridor before sharing a shortlist, but it is still worth asking each tutor to confirm which weekday evenings and which societies they realistically cover, since a route that works on paper can still be tight once evening traffic is accounted for. A tutor who hedges on this question, rather than giving a clear yes or no for the family's own sector, is worth comparing carefully against one who answers plainly.

faqs.question: Should a parent be home during a home tutoring comparison trial, and what if a trial session has to be missed?
faqs.answer: Being reachable in the house is reasonable for the first trial or two, especially with a younger student, but sitting in on every comparison trial can make a student perform for the parent's benefit rather than respond naturally to the tutor. If a trial session has to be missed, because of a school event or a scheduling clash, IB Gram simply reschedules it within the comparison window rather than treating the tutor as having failed the trial; a missed session is a logistics issue, not a mark against fit.

faqs.question: How much does comparing several IB tutors cost compared to hiring one directly?
faqs.answer: The free trial classes IB Gram arranges during shortlisting do not carry an extra cost for comparing more than one tutor; the family only commits once a choice is made. Beyond that, fees depend on the same factors as any private tutor, programme stage, subject, session length and format, and are explained clearly before the first paid session rather than left vague through the comparison process.

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to go from shortlist to a confirmed tutor?
faqs.answer: It depends on how quickly trial lessons can be scheduled around the student's own week, but spacing three trials across two to three weeks is a reasonable, unhurried pace for most families. A family in a rush can compress that timeline, and IB Gram will accommodate it, but a slower comparison tends to produce a more confident decision, particularly for a student who takes a session or two to warm up to anyone new.

faqs.question: What happens to the tutors who were not chosen from the shortlist?
faqs.answer: Nothing negative happens to them within IB Gram's process; a tutor simply not being the right fit for one family's student, subject or schedule does not affect their standing for the next match. It is worth remembering this if a family feels awkward about not choosing a tutor they liked during a trial, since declining after a fair comparison is a completely normal outcome, not a difficult message to deliver.

IB Gram deliberately narrows to profiles that differ on something real, HL versus SL experience, a specific school's pacing, home versus online reach, rather than sending five near-identical names for a family to sort through. A tighter shortlist also makes trial lessons more manageable for the student, since comparing three unfamiliar adults across a few weeks is already a lot to ask without adding more names to the list.

mainEntity.name: Is it awkward to run trial lessons with more than one tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: It does not have to be. Spacing trials across a couple of weeks, rather than compressing them into one, keeps the experience closer to a normal lesson than an audition, and most students settle into the second or third trial more easily than the first. Tutors on IB Gram's shortlist understand that a trial is exactly that, a trial, not a guaranteed booking, so there is no need to apologise for comparing more than one before deciding.

mainEntity.name: What should be compared across trial lessons besides how the tutor teaches?

acceptedAnswer.text: How the tutor teaches matters most, but a few practical things are worth comparing too: how reliably each tutor confirmed the slot and arrived on time, whether they reviewed the student's recent work beforehand or arrived cold, and how clearly they explained what the next session would cover. A tutor who is strong in the room but consistently late or disorganised about scheduling is a real trade-off, not a minor detail, especially for a family managing evenings across a busy Gurgaon commute.

mainEntity.name: How do you compare tutors for a family living on Dwarka Expressway or SPR?

acceptedAnswer.text: The comparison usually widens to include online-first specialists alongside any home-visiting tutors nearby, since these corridors have a thinner pool of local tutors than older parts of Gurgaon. A family on Dwarka Expressway, for instance, might compare a tutor who can reach a Sobha City address on a fixed evening against a subject specialist who works online but has deeper HL experience, and the right answer depends on which one the family is more short on: convenience or depth.

mainEntity.name: What if two tutors on the shortlist both seem equally good?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is a genuinely common outcome, and it is fine to decide on smaller factors rather than searching for a decisive difference that may not exist. Which tutor the student seemed more relaxed with, whose evening slot fits more reliably around buses and activities, and who already knows the relevant syllabus best are all reasonable tiebreakers. IB Gram would rather a family pick confidently between two good options than delay a decision looking for a perfect one.

mainEntity.name: Can a family ask for a different shortlist if none of the first three tutors fit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and this is a normal part of the process rather than a complaint IB Gram needs persuading to act on. Saying specifically what did not work, pace, personality, subject depth, or simply that none of the trial slots suited the family's evenings, helps IB Gram put together a sharper second shortlist rather than repeating the same near-misses. It also helps to say which parts of the first three trials were closer to right, even if none was fully right, since that narrows the second round faster than starting from a blank brief again. Families who ask for a second shortlist are not treated as difficult; the process is built to expect it.

mainEntity.name: When comparing home tutors, how do we check each one can actually reach our sector on a weekday evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask directly during the shortlist stage rather than waiting to find out at the first trial. IB Gram already filters profiles by corridor before sharing a shortlist, but it is still worth asking each tutor to confirm which weekday evenings and which societies they realistically cover, since a route that works on paper can still be tight once evening traffic is accounted for. A tutor who hedges on this question, rather than giving a clear yes or no for the family's own sector, is worth comparing carefully against one who answers plainly.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent be home during a home tutoring comparison trial, and what if a trial session has to be missed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Being reachable in the house is reasonable for the first trial or two, especially with a younger student, but sitting in on every comparison trial can make a student perform for the parent's benefit rather than respond naturally to the tutor. If a trial session has to be missed, because of a school event or a scheduling clash, IB Gram simply reschedules it within the comparison window rather than treating the tutor as having failed the trial; a missed session is a logistics issue, not a mark against fit.

mainEntity.name: How much does comparing several IB tutors cost compared to hiring one directly?

acceptedAnswer.text: The free trial classes IB Gram arranges during shortlisting do not carry an extra cost for comparing more than one tutor; the family only commits once a choice is made. Beyond that, fees depend on the same factors as any private tutor, programme stage, subject, session length and format, and are explained clearly before the first paid session rather than left vague through the comparison process.

mainEntity.name: How long does it usually take to go from shortlist to a confirmed tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how quickly trial lessons can be scheduled around the student's own week, but spacing three trials across two to three weeks is a reasonable, unhurried pace for most families. A family in a rush can compress that timeline, and IB Gram will accommodate it, but a slower comparison tends to produce a more confident decision, particularly for a student who takes a session or two to warm up to anyone new.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the tutors who were not chosen from the shortlist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing negative happens to them within IB Gram's process; a tutor simply not being the right fit for one family's student, subject or schedule does not affect their standing for the next match. It is worth remembering this if a family feels awkward about not choosing a tutor they liked during a trial, since declining after a fair comparison is a completely normal outcome, not a difficult message to deliver.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: the three stages a private IB tutor in Gurgaon must read correctly
contentBlocks.body:
A private IB tutor in Gurgaon has to read three quite different stages correctly, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically right for another. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12 and has no external examinations at all. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: who we are; where we are in place and time; how we express ourselves; how the world works; how we organize ourselves; and sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry and built around the ten attributes of the IB learner profile. Students complete the PYP exhibition in their final year, and a private tutor at this stage is really supporting inquiry and the learner profile, not preparing for any exam.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs from MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, with a smaller Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and some schools add optional MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year stage, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level, roughly 150 hours, each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points, so 45 is the ceiling and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's own failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), which must be completed rather than graded. Most Gurgaon schools sit the May session, with November largely reserved for a minority and for retakes. These structures apply the same way whether a family is based in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, or has just relocated from another city, and they hold regardless of which of the three stages IB private tuitions in Gurgaon is being sought for.

contentBlocks.heading: Where a private specialist earns their place: Maths, sciences, English, TOK and the EE
contentBlocks.body:
Private tuition tends to concentrate on a handful of subjects rather than the whole timetable, and in Gurgaon that handful is fairly predictable: Mathematics, the sciences, English, and support with TOK or the Extended Essay once a student reaches DP2.

Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each offered at Higher Level and Standard Level, and a private tutor should be clear about which route your child is on before the first lesson, since AA and AI diverge meaningfully in what they emphasise. A tutor who has only ever taught AI preparing a student sitting AA HL is a mismatch worth catching early, not after a mock result disappoints.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology at DP level each carry their own Internal Assessment, a piece of independent scientific investigation marked against the subject's own criteria, and a private tutor supporting this work has to guide method and analysis without writing or rewriting the work itself, since the IA has to be the student's own. English A and English B are different subjects entirely, language and literature study for a native or near-native speaker against a second-language course, and a tutor who conflates the two is not reading the syllabus correctly.

TOK asks a student to examine how knowledge itself is justified across different areas, through an essay and an exhibition, and the Extended Essay is an independent research paper in a subject of the student's choosing. Both reward a student's own thinking over a tutor's, so the private tutor's role here is closer to a sounding board and a check against academic integrity than a co-writer, and any tutor who offers to draft sections of either should be treated as a serious warning sign, not a convenience.

contentBlocks.heading: Private IB tuition at home across Old Gurgaon, Golf Course Road and Manesar

Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, Manesar and NH-48 south, and Golf Course Road are the three corridors this page covers, and private home tuition looks different in each.

Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar includes Palam Vihar itself, Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar and Sectors 4, 14, 15, 22 and 23. This is the older, denser part of the city, with narrower approach roads in places, and a private tutor working here often builds a slightly longer travel buffer than the map distance suggests, particularly around Sadar Bazar and Jacobpura during peak evening hours.

Manesar and NH-48 south covers IMT Manesar, Hero Honda Chowk, and Sectors 33, 34 and 37, an industrial and residential belt some distance from the city's core. Few tutors keep a standing evening slot out here purely for one private student, so families in this corridor often do best either securing a tutor who already lives locally or leaning toward hybrid arrangements, home on weekends when travel time matters less and online midweek.

Whichever corridor you are in, ask a shortlisted tutor plainly whether they already teach nearby, since a private arrangement depends on that slot surviving the whole term, not just the first pleasant week.

DP2 mock examinations are set by each school individually, usually months ahead of the May session, and a private tutor who treats the mock date as a fixed planning point, stepping revision up beforehand and adjusting afterward based on what the mock actually revealed, is doing the job properly. A tutor who only reacts to a bad mock result after the fact, rather than planning toward it, is behind where they should be.

contentBlocks.heading: Is a private home tutor always better than an online IB specialist in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Not always, though home tuition is where most IB private tuitions in Gurgaon start, since a home tutor sitting beside your child in a familiar room tends to build concentration faster than a video call does, especially for a younger PYP or early MYP student who is still learning to sit still and focus for an hour.

Online private tuition earns its place when the strongest available specialist, a Mathematics AA HL tutor with genuine depth, say, does not work your corridor, or when a family needs a slot late enough in the evening that travel becomes impractical either way. A shared digital whiteboard and an annotated past paper carry most of what a home lesson does, provided the connection is stable and the student has a proper desk setup, not a laptop balanced on a knee.

Hybrid arrangements suit a family managing two children on different IB stages in one house: home sessions for the younger PYP student who needs a tutor physically present, online for the older DP student who is comfortable working independently on screen and simply needs subject-specific input. It also suits the Manesar corridor, where travel time genuinely limits how often a private tutor can reasonably come in person.

A private arrangement, unlike a school-run programme, can be adjusted freely between these three modes as the term changes, before mocks, during a busy activity season, or after a family relocates within Gurgaon. Ask a shortlisted tutor honestly which mode suits their own teaching style best, since a tutor who is genuinely strong at home but distracted on video calls is the wrong choice for a family that needs consistent online sessions.

IB Gram verifies that a tutor's claimed programme stage and subject experience are genuine before a profile reaches your shortlist, checking against the specific stage, PYP, MYP or DP, and level your child needs rather than a general claim of teaching the IB. Ask how they would handle confidential information about your child's struggles, since a genuinely private arrangement should never casually mention a student's difficulties to anyone at the school without your explicit agreement.

A free trial session remains the clearest test. Watch whether the tutor asks diagnostic questions appropriate to the actual programme stage, PYP inquiry skills look nothing like a DP1 diagnostic, whether they adjust pace visibly when your child struggles, and whether something concrete comes out of the session: a marked answer, a noted gap, or a plan for the following week.

Put the basics of the private arrangement in writing after the trial succeeds: subjects covered, the agreed slot, confidentiality expectations, and how either side gives notice if the arrangement ends. This is not about distrust. It is about avoiding the kind of vague misunderstanding that quietly ends a workable private arrangement a term or two in, over something a single sentence at the start would have settled.

contentBlocks.heading: How does a private IB tutor in Gurgaon differ from the school's own extra classes?
contentBlocks.body:
A private IB tutor in Gurgaon differs from the school's own extra classes in one central way: independence. A school's remedial period or a teacher's after-hours help is convenient and often free, but it sits inside the same relationship that grades the student, and a student who struggles to admit confusion to the person marking their work may hold back exactly the questions that matter most. A private, independent tutor has no grading role at all, which tends to make honest, unguarded questions easier for a student to ask.

Comparing two or three private profiles properly means putting them on one sheet against the same criteria: programme stage and subject fit, whether the tutor has any connection to your child's school, the corridor and slot they can realistically hold, and how they structure confidentiality and communication with you as the parent. Write this down before the first trial, not after, since memory of a phone call fades and a written comparison does not.

Running trial lessons with more than one private tutor without unsettling the student works best when you are upfront with your child about it: two tutors this week, to see who is the better fit, framed as a normal part of finding the right person rather than a test the student could fail. Space the sessions a day or two apart, and ask both tutors the same follow-up question afterward, what they noticed and what they would do next, so the comparison rests on something concrete rather than a vague feeling.

If the first private match still feels wrong after real sessions, not just a single trial, say so plainly and ask IB Gram for a different one. A private arrangement that is not working rarely improves simply by continuing it, and switching early costs far less than a full term spent hoping it settles on its own.

contentBlocks.heading: Confidentiality, honesty and the limits of any private arrangement
contentBlocks.body:
A private arrangement should show early, modest signs of working rather than a dramatic turnaround. In the first two to three weeks, expect the tutor to name specific gaps, a PYP student's inquiry skills that need building, an MYP criterion a student consistently underperforms on, or a DP subject's command terms a student misreads under pressure, rather than a general reassurance that things are going fine.

By four to six weeks, ask for a short, honest review. Because the arrangement is private, this review happens only if you ask for it directly, unlike a school programme with its own built-in reporting, so build the habit of asking early rather than assuming an update will arrive unprompted.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a private arrangement sold on a promised outcome rather than a described process deserves more scepticism, not less, precisely because there is no institution standing behind the promise. What an honest private tutor offers instead is a visible plan, steady weekly movement against it, and a willingness to say plainly when something is not working, whether the cause is pacing, the subject, or simply a mismatch in working style.

Limits matter here too. A private tutor cannot replace a student's own revision time, cannot make an overloaded activity calendar lighter, and should not be treated as a substitute for a proper conversation with the school when something more serious than a subject gap is going on. Some families add a private tutor for every subject when the student genuinely only needs support in one or two, and a good tutor will often say so rather than accept the extra hours.

faqs.question: How many private IB tutors should I compare before deciding?
faqs.answer: Two or three shortlisted profiles is generally enough to make a real comparison without dragging the search out for weeks. IB Gram puts forward two or three independent, verified tutors matched to your child's programme stage and subject rather than a single name, so you can weigh school connection, subject fit and travel time side by side. faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher be hired as a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It is possible but worth thinking through carefully, since a teacher who also grades a student's work carries a built-in conflict of interest, even when both sides act in good faith. A student may hold back genuine confusion from someone who also marks their assessments, which defeats part of the point of extra help. Many families in Gurgaon deliberately choose an independent private tutor with no connection to the school specifically to avoid this, and IB Gram's shortlists are built from tutors who are not currently teaching your child at their own school. Ask directly about any school connection before the trial, whichever route you choose.

faqs.question: What should stay confidential in a private tutoring arrangement?
faqs.answer: Anything your child shares about struggling with a subject, a teacher, or school life more broadly should stay between the family and the tutor unless you explicitly agree otherwise. A genuinely private, independent tutor has no reason to mention a student's difficulties to anyone at the school, since they hold no role in that student's assessment. Raise this expectation directly in the first conversation rather than assuming it is obvious, and put it in writing once a tutor is confirmed, alongside the agreed subjects and slot. A tutor who treats this loosely, mentioning a student's struggles casually, is worth reconsidering even if their subject knowledge is otherwise strong.

faqs.question: Should I put anything in writing with a private IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, a short written note after the trial succeeds saves real confusion later: the subjects covered, the agreed weekly slot, confidentiality expectations, and how either side gives notice if the arrangement needs to end. This does not need to be a formal contract; a clear message thread or a shared note is often enough, but having it in writing means neither side is relying on memory of a single phone call from weeks earlier. contentBlocks.heading: What happens after you send your first query?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query through the site or book a free consultation, and someone from IB Gram calls to understand what your child actually needs before suggesting a single tutor. That conversation covers the programme, the exact subject and level, Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL) where it applies, the school your child attends, and when in the week an online slot realistically works around homework and sleep.

From there the process is straightforward:

1. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar and preferred schedule, so the shortlist starts narrow instead of generic.
2. Two or three verified tutor profiles are shortlisted, each matched on subject depth and programme stage, not just offered as a general 'IB tutor'.
3. A demo or trial class is arranged online at a slot that suits your evenings, so you and your child see how the tutor actually teaches before committing to anything.
4. If the fit is wrong, you ask for a different match; nobody is locked into the first tutor they meet.

What makes this useful for an IB online tutor in Gurgaon specifically is that matching has to account for equipment and screen teaching style, not only subject knowledge. A tutor who is excellent at a whiteboard in someone's living room is not automatically good at annotating a past paper on screen while talking through it, and IB Gram checks for that separately during matching, before the first session, not after a flat one.

Every profile shown to you has been through the same verification steps before it reaches your shortlist, so you are not vetting a stranger from a phone number someone passed on. Families who search for an IB online tutor in Gurgaon are usually short on evening time already, and this process is built to respect that.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which stage is your child at?
contentBlocks.body:
The programme stage changes what an online session should even look like, so it is the first thing to get right. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from ages 3 to 12 and organises learning around six transdisciplinary themes: who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet. Younger PYP students working with a tutor online need short, structured screen time built around units of inquiry and the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, not a lecture format, and there is no external examination at this stage to prepare for.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. An online MYP tutor should be marking practice work against those same criteria, not just against right and wrong answers, because that is how the school actually grades. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project (or the Community Project earlier, in MYP 3 or 4), and some schools opt into MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, which combines on-screen examinations with ePortfolios; each school decides for itself whether to offer it.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects across six groups, usually three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, taking the maximum to 45; 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's own failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May exam session, with November used by a minority of schools and by retake candidates; May results are released in early July.

MYP (MYP 1-5, roughly ages 11-16): four criteria per subject, each scored 0-8.
MYP 5: the Personal Project, or the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4.
DP (DP1 and DP2): six subjects, HL or SL, graded 1-7 each, maximum 45 with TOK and EE.
Most Gurgaon schools use the May session; November is a minority and retake session.

contentBlocks.heading: IB subjects Gurgaon students most often need help with
contentBlocks.body:
Certain subjects come up again and again when Gurgaon families ask for an IB online tutor, and each has its own screen-teaching problem to solve. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each offered at HL or SL, and a lot of the tutoring value is in worked, step-by-step method on a shared whiteboard, not just the final answer; a tutor annotating a past paper live, showing where marks are actually awarded, teaches differently online than a tutor talking at a page.

IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology all carry practical and data-handling components alongside the theory, and an online tutor cannot run a live experiment through a webcam. What an online science tutor can do well is walk through a graph, a data table or a past paper's markscheme line by line, screen-shared, at a pace the student controls, pausing to ask the student to predict the next step rather than reading it out. For students who need laboratory practice itself, that stays a school or in-person matter; the online session works best for the analysis and the exam technique around it.

IB English A and B, and command of TOK and the Extended Essay, are different again: this is close reading, argument structure and referencing, all of which sit comfortably on a shared document online, with a tutor commenting in real time the way a teacher would mark a draft. TOK essay planning and Extended Essay supervision both benefit from screen sharing a draft and talking through the reasoning behind each paragraph, since deadlines for the Extended Essay, TOK and Internal Assessments are all set independently by the school and need tracking across subjects, not just within one.

Across all of these, the honest pattern is: content explanation and exam technique translate well to video; anything that depends on physical apparatus, handwriting under exam pressure, or reading a student's body language during a long silence, needs either occasional in-person sessions or a tutor experienced enough to read hesitation through a screen.

TOK and the Extended Essay: draft review and reasoning talked through on screen.

School buses, after-school activities and CAS commitments (for DP students) all compete for the same evening hours, and an online slot is often easier to protect than a home visit because there is no commute time either side of it to absorb a late pickup. Online tutoring does not remove the calendar pressure itself, only the travel around it, and a student who is already stretched thin in exam term still needs a realistic number of sessions, not more screen time layered onto an already full week. An IB online tutor in Gurgaon who knows this calendar plans around it instead of ignoring it.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tutor, online tutor or hybrid: what actually suits an IB student?
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor teaching at your own table in Gurgaon still has real advantages for some subjects and some students: for a younger PYP or early MYP child, being in the same room helps a tutor notice fidgeting, confusion or a wandering pencil in a way a screen makes harder to catch. Home tutoring also means the tutor can look through the student's actual school notebook and physical past papers rather than a scan of them, which some families and some subjects genuinely benefit from, particularly for handwriting-heavy working in Mathematics and the sciences.

Online is the better call for most DP students and for families anywhere in Gurgaon where evening traffic makes a fixed home slot unreliable. It also opens up specialist subject tutors who might not otherwise be able to reach a given sector on a weekday evening at all, which matters for a less common Group 6 or a specific HL subject combination. The trade-off is real: a screen makes it slightly harder to read a student's confusion in real time, and some students need more active check-ins from the tutor to stay engaged for a full 60 or 90 minutes than they would in person.

Hybrid, combining a regular home tutor with occasional online sessions from a subject specialist, or the reverse, an online tutor as the main teacher with an in-person session before a mock or the exam session itself, is what a growing number of Gurgaon families choose once they see how each mode actually performs for their child. It costs a little more coordination but lets a family match the mode to the task rather than the task to whatever mode they picked first.

There is no single right answer here, and a tutor experienced across all three modes, rather than one who only offers one, is usually better placed to tell you honestly which one your child needs for a given subject.

Online suits most DP students and reaches specialists a home visit cannot.

The right mode can differ by subject, not just by family preference.

Before a tutor's profile ever reaches your shortlist, IB Gram checks it against the programme, level and subject the family actually asked for, not a generic 'IB tutor' label, and confirms the tutor has taught that stage before, whether that is PYP inquiry units, MYP criterion-based work, or a specific DP HL or SL subject. For an online IB tutor in Gurgaon specifically, that verification also covers whether the tutor is comfortable teaching on a screen: using a shared whiteboard, annotating a PDF past paper live, and keeping a session structured without the natural cues of being in the same room.

Beyond what IB Gram checks, there is a shorter list of things worth confirming yourself before or during the first trial. Ask what equipment and software the tutor actually uses for a live lesson, and ask them to demonstrate it briefly rather than just describe it. Ask how they mark practice work: against real IB criteria and mark schemes, or against a generic sense of right and wrong. Ask what a typical 60 or 90 minute online session actually covers, minute by minute, because a vague answer here is often a sign the sessions themselves will be vague.

A trial class is the honest test that no document can replace. Watch whether the tutor asks your child questions rather than talking at them, whether they check understanding before moving on, and whether the session still feels structured twenty minutes in in the way it did at the start. If a home tutor is what the family actually wants and an online trial was booked instead, or the reverse, say so early; a match can be adjusted before it becomes a term-long commitment.

No certificate, workshop attendance or years-in-the-field claim substitutes for watching a tutor teach your own child once.

contentBlocks.heading: What actually works in an online IB lesson, and what does not
contentBlocks.body:
Some tasks translate almost perfectly to a screen. Talking through a past paper's mark scheme line by line, with the paper shared and annotated in real time, works as well online as it does at a kitchen table, arguably better, because the tutor can zoom into a single command term (define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent) and show exactly how much detail each one demands. Reviewing a draft Extended Essay or TOK essay, with comments added live on a shared document, also suits a screen well, since the student watches the reasoning happen rather than receiving a marked-up printout after the fact.

Other tasks are harder. A long derivation in Mathematics or Physics that a student needs to write out by hand, under something close to exam conditions, is genuinely easier to supervise in person, where a tutor can glance at a working page without asking the student to hold it up to a webcam. Group discussion practice for TOK, or rehearsing an oral component, can feel stiffer over video than in a room, though it is not impossible, and a tutor experienced with this format knows how to compensate for it.

A practical setup makes the difference between a session that works and one that does not: a stable connection, a quiet corner away from siblings and television, a working webcam and microphone, a second device or a second screen if possible so the student can see the shared material and the tutor's face at once, and physical notebooks or a tablet ready for the student's own working, not just a keyboard. None of this is expensive or unusual, but a family setting it up for the first time should test it once before the first real lesson, not during it.

Gurgaon families choose online for reasons that are entirely practical rather than aspirational: unreliable evening traffic, a school bus that arrives at different times through the week, and access to a specialist subject tutor who genuinely could not reach every sector on a weekday evening. The honest limit is that online asks slightly more of the student's own focus, since there is no adult physically present reminding them to sit up and pay attention, and a student who struggles with that in a classroom may need a hybrid arrangement rather than online alone.

contentBlocks.heading: What should change in the first month of online IB tutoring?
contentBlocks.body:
Within the first three sessions, you should be able to tell whether an online arrangement is working, and it is worth checking deliberately rather than assuming it is fine because nobody has complained. The tutor should be asking your child questions and pausing for an answer, not talking continuously through the shared screen. Your child should be able to describe, afterwards, one specific thing they now understand that they did not before the session, not just 'it was good'. And the session should still feel structured towards the end, not drifting once the planned material runs out early.

By four weeks in, look for a shift from general explanation towards work marked against the actual criteria or mark scheme your child's subject uses, whether that is MYP's four criteria out of 8 each or a DP subject's specific assessment objectives. A tutor tracking real progress should be able to point to a specific error pattern that has reduced, a command term the student now reliably interprets correctly, or a type of question that no longer causes a stall, rather than offering a vague sense of improvement.

Be honest about limits too. No tutor, online or otherwise, can guarantee a grade, and a student who started tutoring very late before an exam session has less runway to close gaps than one who started early in the year. If a subject genuinely needs more in-person, handwriting-heavy practice than a screen can give, a good online tutor will say so rather than continuing to bill sessions that are not moving the needle. If progress genuinely is not showing after a fair month of consistent sessions, that is the moment to ask for a different tutor or a different mode, not to wait quietly for another month hoping it changes.

Progress in an IB subject rarely looks dramatic week to week; it looks like fewer repeated mistakes, faster recognition of what a question is actually asking, and a student who brings their own questions to the session instead of waiting to be told what is wrong.

The first session itself, whether a trial or the first paid lesson, should cover a diagnostic conversation with your child about what they find hardest, a look at recent work or a past paper if available, and an initial plan for the coming weeks rather than a full syllabus dive on day one.
