faqs.question: Does online IB tutoring actually work as well as a home tutor?
faqs.answer: For most DP subjects and for exam technique in any programme, yes, provided the setup is right: a stable connection, a shared whiteboard, and a tutor who actively questions the student rather than talking at them. Where it works less well is long handwritten derivations in Mathematics or Physics, where a tutor in the room can glance at working more easily, and for younger PYP or early MYP students who benefit from someone physically present to hold their focus. Many Gurgaon families use online as the default and add an occasional home or in-person session before a mock or the exam session itself, which covers most of the gap honestly rather than pretending there is none.

faqs.question: What equipment do we need for an online IB tutor in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A stable internet connection, a laptop or tablet with a working webcam and microphone, and a quiet corner away from siblings and the television are the essentials. A second screen or device helps so your child can see the shared whiteboard or past paper and the tutor's face at once, though it is not strictly required. Physical notebooks or a tablet for the student's own working matter more than people expect, since most IB subjects still need the student to write out method, not just watch it. Test the setup once before the first real lesson rather than discovering a microphone problem mid-session.

faqs.question: How do we know if an online IB tutor in Gurgaon is any good before committing?
faqs.answer: Book the free trial class and watch specifically for whether the tutor asks your child questions and waits for an answer, rather than talking continuously through the shared screen for the full session. Ask how they mark practice work: against real IB criteria and mark schemes, or against a general sense of right and wrong. A tutor who can demonstrate their screen-sharing and annotation tools briefly, rather than just describing them, is usually more experienced at teaching online specifically, not just teaching a subject that happens to be delivered over video.

faqs.question: Our child's online sessions feel like they are not helping after a month, what now?
faqs.answer: A fair month of consistent sessions should show something concrete: fewer repeated errors, faster recognition of what a question is actually asking, or better handling of a specific command term. If none of that is visible after four to six sessions, say so and ask for a different tutor rather than waiting quietly. Sometimes the honest answer is that the subject needs more handwriting-heavy, in-person practice than a screen gives, in which case switching to home tuition or a hybrid arrangement, rather than persisting with online alone, is the right call.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring cheaper than a home tutor in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Pricing structure varies by tutor, subject scarcity, the student's programme stage and level, and session length, and IB Gram does not quote fees here since these depend on availability and the specific match. What can be said honestly is that an online session generally has no travel cost built into it the way a home visit across a Gurgaon corridor sometimes does, but the tutor's own experience and subject rarity usually matter more to the fee than the mode itself. Ask directly during the consultation how a given tutor's fee is structured before committing to sessions.

faqs.question: Can an online IB tutor help with the Extended Essay and TOK?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the tasks that genuinely suits a screen well. A tutor can review a shared draft live, commenting and asking questions about the reasoning behind a paragraph the way a supervisor would mark it, without waiting for a printed copy to change hands. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Internal Assessments each carry deadlines set independently by the school, so a tutor working across several of these for one student needs to track them separately rather than treating them as one piece of work.

faqs.question: Does an online IB tutor need to be based in Gurgaon at all?
faqs.answer: Not physically, since the whole point of an online IB tutor in Gurgaon is that location stops being the constraint it is for a home visit. What still matters is that the tutor understands the school calendar most Gurgaon IB families are working against, the May exam session most schools here use, and roughly when mock exams and internal deadlines tend to cluster. A tutor who has taught other Gurgaon-based IB students before usually has that context already, which saves explaining it from scratch.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor coming to our sector on a weekday evening still an option if we start with online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Starting with an online IB tutor does not close off a home tutor later, and IB Gram can shortlist for either mode or a hybrid arrangement at any point, whether you are in a Golf Course Extension Road society, along Sohna Road, or near DLF Phase 3 and Cyber City. Many families begin online for the scheduling flexibility and add a home session closer to mocks or the May exam session, once it is clear which subjects need which kind of attention.

faqs.question: What if our internet connection drops mid-session?
faqs.answer: A brief drop is normal and most tutors simply reconnect and pick up where the session left off, though it does eat into the planned time. If connectivity is a recurring problem for your household rather than a one-off, mention it during matching, since a tutor experienced with intermittent connections in Gurgaon can plan sessions with that built in, for example working from a downloaded past paper rather than a live-streamed document that stutters.

faqs.question: How many online sessions a week does an IB student actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on the subject, the level, and how close the student is to a mock or the exam session, and there is no single right number. A DP student approaching HL mocks often needs more sessions in that window than the same student six months earlier, and stepping back down afterwards matters as much as stepping up did. IB Gram discusses a realistic weekly schedule during the intake call based on what you describe, rather than defaulting to a fixed package regardless of need.

faqs.question: Can we switch from an online tutor to home tuition partway through the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a reasonable thing to ask for if a subject turns out to need more in-person, handwriting-heavy supervision than expected, or if your family's evenings change. IB Gram can shortlist a home tutor for the relevant sector and society at that point, subject to availability, without needing to restart the whole intake process from scratch since your child's profile and needs are already on file.

heroTitle: Compare IB Online Tutors Across Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Two or three tutor profiles, compared side by side, with a fair trial lesson for each: that is how a family in Gurgaon should choose an IB online tutor. This page walks through building that shortlist, what to weigh before committing, and when to ask IB Gram for a different match.
introSummary: IB online tutors in Gurgaon are best chosen from a shortlist of two or three, not the first profile that looks promising, even though IB Gram's lead service across Gurgaon is home tutoring: fit on level, subject depth and working style only becomes clear once you compare candidates side by side. This page sets out how IB Gram builds that shortlist for families across every IB stage in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana: what a strong profile should show, a checklist for comparing candidates fairly, and how to run trial lessons with more than one tutor without confusing the student. Lessons discussed here run live online, over a shared whiteboard and annotated past papers, so setup, screen habits and sustained attention are part of what you are comparing. If neither trial feels right, IB Gram shortlists again rather than asking you to settle.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Shortlists Online Tutors for Your Family in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist starts with a conversation, not a stack of profiles. When you send a query to IB Gram, the first questions are about the student, not the tutor: board and programme stage, the exact subject and level, how the school paces its syllabus that term, and a slot that survives a real weekday evening in Gurgaon. That intake decides who even gets considered.

From there, IB Gram puts together two or three profiles rather than one. A profile worth shortlisting shows board-specific teaching experience rather than a general tutoring history, the level actually taught, whether that means Higher Level papers, criterion-based assessment, or younger inquiry-based work, some familiarity with how Gurgaon international schools structure a term, and an honest note on working style. A quiet younger IB student and an older student cramming before final exams need different personalities as much as different content knowledge, and a good profile says so plainly.

Comparing profiles side by side, before any lesson happens, is what saves a family from discovering a mismatch three weeks in. Ask each candidate the same three or four questions and write the answers down next to each other rather than trusting memory. A tutor who cannot describe how they would open a first online session with your child's exact syllabus and current gaps is not ready for the shortlist, however strong the resume reads.

None of this needs to move fast. A rushed shortlist is the most common reason a family ends up switching IB online tutors twice in one term, and a second switch unsettles a student far more than an extra week spent comparing two calm, well-matched candidates properly. Families researching IB online tutors in Gurgaon for the first time should expect this comparison step to take a week, not a single evening.
items: 1. Send a query describing board, programme stage, subject, level and preferred evening slot.
2. IB Gram asks follow-up questions about the school's syllabus pace and past gaps.
3. Two or three verified profiles are shortlisted, each with level and experience stated plainly.
4. A free trial class is arranged with each shortlisted tutor at a fair, separate time.
5. The family compares both trials against the same checklist before choosing.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Programme Stage Should Guide Your Shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Two tutors can both call themselves IB specialists and still suit completely different students, because the three programmes ask for different skills. Primary Years Programme (PYP) work, for ages 3 to 12, runs through six transdisciplinary themes such as Who We Are and How We Organize Ourselves, taught through units of inquiry rather than a fixed syllabus, and there are no external examinations to prepare for. A tutor comfortable here needs patience with open-ended inquiry and the PYP learner profile, not exam drilling.

Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans five years, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A through D, each scored out of 8, and that criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's own grade boundaries. A tutor on your shortlist for MYP should be able to explain, in one sentence, how a piece of your child's work would be marked against those criteria, not just whether the answer is right.

Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year stretch, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects across six groups, three or four taken at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to 3 more points toward a maximum of 45. A DP shortlist needs a tutor who knows the difference between HL and SL demand in that specific subject, not just the subject in general.

When you compare two online tutors for the same student, ask each one to name the exact stage: MYP criterion work looks nothing like DP2 revision, and a profile that blurs the two is one to drop from the shortlist quickly.
items: 1. PYP: six transdisciplinary themes, units of inquiry, no external exams.
2. MYP: eight subject groups, four criteria per subject, grades from criterion totals out of 32.
3. DP: six subjects across six groups, HL and SL hours, grades from 1 to 7.
4. TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points toward the 45-point maximum.
5. Ask each shortlisted tutor to name the exact stage and criteria they would teach to.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Subject Depth Across Your IB Online Tutor Shortlist in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Subject depth is the part of a shortlist that is easiest to get wrong on a resume alone, because knowing a subject and knowing how the IB assesses it are not the same skill. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each offered at HL or SL, and a tutor strong in AA HL is not automatically the right fit for a student doing AI SL: the calculator use, the style of question, and the internal assessment all differ.

The sciences, IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology, carry practical work, internal assessment components and command terms (define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent) that decide how much depth an answer needs. A tutor on your shortlist should be able to walk through a recent past paper question in your child's exact subject and point out where marks are typically lost, not just recite the syllabus content.

For English A and B, and for any subject group, ask both shortlisted tutors the same diagnostic question: what does a top-band response to a specific command term look like, and how does that differ from a mid-band one. The tutor who answers with a concrete example, ideally referencing an actual mark scheme, should move ahead of the one who answers in general terms about effort and understanding.

Where the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge sits inside a subject specialism also matters for comparison. A Physics tutor who has supervised Extended Essay work in that subject brings something a general online tutor cannot, and it is worth asking directly whether that experience exists before either trial lesson is booked.

2. Sciences carry internal assessment components and specific command terms in every mark scheme.
3. Ask for a worked example from a real past paper before booking a trial.
4. Check whether the tutor has supervised Extended Essay work in that same subject.
5. English A and B need different reading and response skills; compare accordingly.

contentBlocks.heading: Sushant Lok, SPR and New Gurgaon: What Families Compare Across These Gurgaon Corridors
contentBlocks.body:
This shortlist advice holds across Gurgaon, but three corridors come up most often when families ask IB Gram about online tutoring: Sushant Lok and South City 1 around the Millennium City Centre, the Southern Peripheral Road (SPR), and New Gurgaon. Since the lessons discussed here run online, a tutor's physical address in any of these corridors matters less than it would for a home tutor, but the corridor still shapes the shortlist in real ways.

Sushant Lok 1, Sushant Lok 2, South City 1, Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City sit close to the Millennium City Centre corridor, an area with dense broadband coverage and, in most homes, a reliable backup connection through a mobile hotspot, which matters when an online lesson cannot afford to drop mid-explanation. Families here often shortlist tutors purely on subject fit, since travel is not a constraint for a live online class.

The Southern Peripheral Road corridor, covering Sector 66 through Sector 70, Sector 72, Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and the Tata Primanti society, sits further from the city's older core, and evening internet load can vary block to block. A family here is right to ask a shortlisted tutor about their own connection stability and a backup plan, since a dropped call mid-lesson wastes a scarce weekday evening hour just as badly as a late home tutor would.

New Gurgaon, spanning Sector 82 through Sector 86, Sector 89, Sector 90, Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, including the Vatika India Next and Godrej Air societies, is still filling in with newer families, many of whom are comparing IB online tutors for the first time without a network of other parents to ask first. For this corridor especially, the side-by-side trial lesson matters more, since there is less word-of-mouth to lean on before choosing.
items: 1. Sushant Lok, South City 1 and Millennium City Centre: dense broadband, shortlisting mostly on subject fit.
2. Southern Peripheral Road, including Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and Tata Primanti: ask about connection stability.
3. New Gurgaon, including Vatika India Next and Godrej Air: fewer word-of-mouth references, so trials matter more.
4. All three corridors: physical address matters less than for home tutoring, since lessons run online.
5. Evening slot pressure still applies in every corridor, even without travel time to plan around.

contentBlocks.heading: What School Calendars Mean When You Compare Two Online Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families comparing IB online tutors in Gurgaon whose children attend international schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali or DPS International Edge deal with a shared set of calendar pressures, whatever the specific school, and a tutor's familiarity with that rhythm is worth comparing directly.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session, with a minority using November, mostly for retake candidates, and each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months ahead of May. A tutor who does not know roughly when your child's school runs mocks cannot plan a shortlist-worthy revision timeline, so ask both candidates directly rather than assuming they will ask you.

Command terms such as define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent set how much depth an IB answer needs, and past papers, mark schemes and subject reports coming through the school or the IB's own channels show how marks are actually awarded. A tutor who references these directly in a trial lesson, rather than working from generic notes, is showing you something a resume cannot.

When you compare two shortlisted tutors, ask each the same question: how would they structure the weeks immediately before your child's school-set mock date. The answer tells you more about calendar awareness than any list of qualifications.
items: 1. May is the main exam session for most Gurgaon IB schools; November suits a minority and retakes.
2. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually months before the May session.
3. Command terms decide the depth an answer needs; ask a tutor to explain one.
4. Past papers and mark schemes, from the school or the IB, show how marks are earned.
5. Compare how each shortlisted tutor would plan the weeks before your child's mock date.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: Which Fits Your Shortlist Best?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's lead service on every page, including this one, is home tutoring: a verified tutor teaching the student at the family's own kitchen table or study desk, in their own sector or society across Gurgaon. Since this page is about comparing online tutors specifically, it is still worth stating plainly that home tuition remains a real option for the same shortlist, and some families end up choosing a home tutor after starting their comparison online.

Online tutoring removes travel from the equation entirely, which matters most for a specialist subject where the strongest available tutor for a demanding Higher Level subject does not live anywhere near your sector. A shared whiteboard, screen-annotated past papers and a stable connection replace the physical classroom, and for older DP students especially, who are used to screens for schoolwork already, this format can work as well as a home lesson once both sides settle into it.

Hybrid arrangements, where most sessions run online but a tutor visits at home occasionally, for instance before a mock exam or an internal assessment deadline, combine the convenience of online scheduling with the value of an in-person check on handwriting, working, and exam technique that a screen sometimes hides. Not every shortlisted tutor offers hybrid, so ask directly if it matters to you.

The honest trade-off: home tuition gives the most direct feel for a tutor's presence and is easiest for younger students to stay focused in, online tuition gives access to a wider, more specialist shortlist and removes traffic from the evening entirely, and hybrid tries to take a bit of both at the cost of needing more coordination. There is no single right answer, only the one that matches your student and your evening.
items: 1. Home tutoring: a verified tutor teaches at your own kitchen table or study desk.
2. Online tutoring: shared whiteboards and annotated past papers replace the physical classroom.
3. Hybrid: mostly online, with occasional home visits before a mock or IA deadline.
4. Home suits younger students who lose focus on a screen more easily.
5. Online widens the shortlist to specialists who live outside a practical travel radius.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Verify Each Tutor on Your Online Shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification is not a single check; it is a short list of things a parent can reasonably confirm before a trial lesson even starts, and IB Gram does the first pass before a profile reaches your shortlist at all: board-specific teaching experience, the level actually taught, and consistency between what a profile claims and what comes up in the trial itself.

What IB Gram checks: profiles are reviewed before they are shown to a family, tutors are asked about board, syllabus, level, school calendar familiarity, location and schedule as part of building the shortlist, and a free trial or demo session can be arranged with more than one tutor before any commitment is made. None of that is a guarantee of outcome; it is a guarantee of a fair starting point.

What a parent should check personally: ask a shortlisted tutor to talk through a recent lesson with a student at the same level, listen for whether they mention specific mark schemes or criteria rather than vague praise, and notice whether they ask about your child's actual gaps in the first five minutes of a trial or simply launch into a prepared lesson regardless of who is sitting across the screen.

If a tutor's trial lesson does not match what the profile promised, that is exactly the situation IB Gram exists to fix: the family can ask for a different match rather than settling, and the shortlist process starts again with the information from that first trial folded in.
items: 1. IB Gram reviews profiles for board experience and level before shortlisting.
2. Ask a tutor to describe a recent lesson at the same level as your child.
3. Notice whether the tutor asks about specific gaps in the first minutes of a trial.
4. A trial or demo session can be arranged with more than one shortlisted tutor.
5. If a trial does not match the profile, ask IB Gram for a different match.

contentBlocks.heading: Running Trial Lessons With Two or Three Online Tutors Fairly
contentBlocks.body:
The trial lesson is where a shortlist earns its name, and running it fairly takes a bit of planning. Book both trials within the same week if possible, ideally at the same time of day, since a tired student after a long school day compares unfairly against a fresh one on a weekend morning. Tell the student honestly that this is a comparison, not a commitment, so they do not feel disloyal to whichever tutor they meet first.

During each trial, watch for the same things across both sessions: does the tutor ask diagnostic questions before teaching anything new, do they reference the actual syllabus or mark scheme rather than teaching generically, and does the student's body language change, more engaged, less guarded, somewhere between the two trials. A short written note straight after each session, while it is fresh, is more reliable than trying to remember both a week later.

It is fair, and common, for a student to prefer one tutor's teaching style over the other's credentials on paper. IB Gram weighs both signals when finalising a match: a tutor with slightly less board-specific experience but a much stronger rapport with a particular student is sometimes the better long-term choice, and a family should say so plainly rather than defaulting to whichever resume reads more impressively.

If neither trial feels right, that is useful information rather than a failure, and it happens more often than families expect. Tell IB Gram specifically what did not work, too fast, too slow, too little structure, not enough warmth, and a new shortlist can be built around that feedback rather than starting from a blank slate.
items: 1. Book both trials in the same week, at a similar time of day if possible.
2. Tell the student honestly that this is a comparison, not a commitment.
3. Note diagnostic questioning, syllabus references and student engagement straight after each trial.
4. Weigh teaching style and rapport alongside credentials when comparing two shortlisted tutors.
5. If neither trial works, describe specifically what did not, and ask for a new shortlist.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress at Home or Online Looks Like After You Choose From Your Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Once a tutor is chosen from the shortlist, progress in the first month looks unglamorous and that is normal: a clearer sense of where the student's actual gaps are, a working routine for the weekly slot, and small, checkable improvements, an internal assessment draft that finally has a clear structure, a past paper section attempted without the usual stalling, a criterion the student can now explain in their own words.

No tutor, online or at home, can guarantee a grade, a particular score, or a set improvement in marks, however confidently that gets promised elsewhere; what a good match delivers is a visible change in how the student works, which is the thing that actually moves grades over a longer stretch than any single tutor relationship covers.

Be honest about the limits too. A student who started IB tutoring only weeks before mocks will not close every gap in that window, an online lesson cannot fully replace the in-person read of body language a home tutor gets for free, and a tutor working with a student for the first time needs a few sessions just to calibrate pace and language before real progress becomes visible.

If a month in, nothing has shifted at all, not the routine, not the student's confidence, not a single specific piece of work, that is worth raising directly with IB Gram rather than waiting out the term hoping it improves on its own. Families who compared their shortlist properly at the start usually reach this point far less often than families who skipped straight to the first available profile.
items: 1. Expect a clearer picture of specific gaps within the first two or three sessions.
2. No tutor can guarantee a grade; a good match changes how the student works.
3. A late start before mocks narrows what is realistically achievable in the time left.
4. Online lessons cannot fully replace the in-person read a home tutor gets naturally.
5. If nothing has shifted after a month, raise it with IB Gram directly.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting With Your Chosen IB Online Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is simple once the shortlist has done its job. Send a query or book a free consultation, and be ready to describe board, syllabus, level, the school's approximate pace that term, and the evening slot that actually survives a normal weekday in your part of Gurgaon.

IB Gram uses that information to shortlist two or three profiles, matched on board experience, level taught and school familiarity, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule. A free trial or demo session is arranged for each shortlisted candidate before anyone commits, so the family compares real teaching rather than a written promise.

For the first proper session with whichever tutor you choose, have the student's recent tests, current unit or topic, and any specific worry, a subject, a paper, an upcoming internal assessment deadline, ready to hand over. That first session should not be a cold start; it should pick up exactly where the trial left off, with the tutor already aware of what the family flagged as most urgent.

If the fit still turns out to be wrong after a proper run, not just a bad day, the family can ask IB Gram for a different match at any point. Lessons continue at home, online or hybrid, whichever the family and the newly matched tutor settle on together, and the same shortlist-and-trial process applies to that replacement exactly as it did the first time, so nobody has to accept a rushed second choice either. Families settling on IB online tutors in Gurgaon after this process report an easier first term precisely because the comparison was done properly upfront, not skipped to save a week.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation to begin the shortlist process.
2. Describe board, syllabus, level, school pace and a realistic weekday evening slot.
3. A trial or demo session is arranged for each shortlisted tutor before committing.
4. Bring recent tests and specific worries to the first proper session.
5. Ask for a different match at any point if the fit is not right.

faqs.question: How many IB online tutors should I shortlist before choosing one?
faqs.answer: Two or three is the practical range. Any fewer and you are not really comparing, any more and trial lessons start eating into weeks the student needs for actual revision. IB Gram typically puts forward two or three profiles matched on board experience, level and school familiarity, then arranges a free trial with each so the comparison is based on a real lesson rather than a written profile. If none of the two or three feels right, a new shortlist can be built rather than settling for whichever one is left.

faqs.question: What should I compare across two IB online tutor trial lessons?
faqs.answer: Compare whether the tutor asks diagnostic questions before teaching anything new, whether they reference your child's actual syllabus and mark scheme rather than generic content, and how the student responds afterward, more confident or more guarded. Write a short note after each trial while it is fresh, since two sessions a week apart are hard to compare accurately from memory alone. Credentials on paper matter less at this stage than what actually happens once the tutor and student are in a live session together.

faqs.question: Does IB online tuition actually work as well as a home tutor?
faqs.answer: For most subjects and most students, yes, once both sides settle into the format, though the honest limit is that a screen misses some of what an in-person tutor catches, working shown on paper, body language, posture during a long problem. Online tuition also opens the shortlist to specialists who would not be practical to travel to. Some families in Gurgaon choose a hybrid arrangement precisely to get the best of both, mostly online sessions with an occasional home visit before a mock or an internal assessment deadline.

faqs.question: My child has had a month of IB online tutoring with no visible progress. What now?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly with IB Gram rather than waiting out the term. A month should show something specific: clearer gaps identified, a working session routine, small concrete wins like a past paper section attempted properly. If none of that has happened, the fit may be wrong, the pace may be off, or the slot itself may be working against the student, and any of those can be corrected by a different match rather than assumed to be the student's fault.

faqs.question: How much does an IB online tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate for IB online tutors in Gurgaon because fee structure depends on stage, subject scarcity, the tutor's experience, and session length, and it is subject to tutor availability. What can be said honestly is that one-to-one attention, whether online or at home, typically costs more per hour than a shared coaching batch, since the batch cost is spread across many students. The right way to judge value is against what a fair trial lesson actually shows, not the number alone.

faqs.question: Can I trial tutors from different corridors of Gurgaon if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the real advantages of comparing IB online tutors rather than only home tutors. A family in Sushant Lok can trial a tutor whose profile is strongest for a demanding Higher Level subject even if that tutor is based on the far side of the Southern Peripheral Road, since travel is not part of an online lesson. Corridor still matters slightly, mostly for whether a hybrid option with an occasional home visit stays practical given the usual Gurgaon evening traffic.

faqs.question: What happens if the online tutor I chose is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram specifically what is not working, whether that is pace, structure, personality fit or something about the online format itself, and ask for a different match. This is a normal part of the process, not a failure of the first choice, and it happens more often in the first month than families expect. A new shortlist can be built directly from that feedback, which usually gets the second match closer to right than the first one was.

faqs.question: Do I need to sit in on my child's online IB lessons?
faqs.answer: Not usually, though it depends on the student's age and the family's preference. Younger students sometimes benefit from a parent nearby for the first few sessions while the routine settles, while most senior students work better with some independence during the lesson itself. What matters more than presence in the room is a short conversation with the student afterward about what was covered and what still feels unclear, which IB Gram also encourages tutors to summarise briefly at the end of each session.

faqs.question: How is a one-to-one online tutor different from a live online group class in New Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A one-to-one online tutor through IB Gram teaches only your child, at a pace and slot the family sets directly, while a live online group class shares one teacher's attention across several students on a fixed schedule. Families in New Gurgaon and similar newer corridors, where many parents are comparing tutoring options for the first time without an established local network to ask, often start with a group class for cost reasons and move to one-to-one once a specific subject gap becomes clear.

faqs.question: What if my child's school switches from CBSE or ICSE mid-course to the IB?
faqs.answer: A shortlisted tutor should ask about this directly during the intake conversation, since a mid-course switch usually means gaps in IB-specific skills like command-term literacy and criterion-based assessment even when the underlying subject knowledge is solid. IB Gram factors this into the shortlist, favouring tutors with experience bringing students in from other boards, and the first trial lesson is a reasonable place to test how well the tutor diagnoses exactly what is missing rather than assuming a clean slate.

faqs.question: Are online IB lessons practical on weekday evenings given Gurgaon traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one reason families choose online tutoring specifically: evening traffic between a tutor's home and a house on Golf Course Extension Road can stretch a short trip considerably, but an online lesson removes that variable entirely. The trade-off is that the family still needs a quiet, reliable internet connection at the agreed slot, and a backup plan, a mobile hotspot, for instance, is worth having ready in corridors like SPR where evening connection load can vary.

faqs.question: What happens if a hybrid tutor's home visit is missed or needs rescheduling?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor and IB Gram as early as possible, ideally the same day, so the session can move to another weekday evening or fold into the next online lesson instead of being lost entirely. Missed sessions happen, school events, sudden traffic on Golf Course Road, a sick day, and a tutor working through IB Gram is expected to accommodate reasonable rescheduling rather than treating a missed slot as forfeited. What should not happen is a pattern of repeated cancellations from either side going unaddressed for weeks.

Each suits a different student and stage, and the honest trade-off is attention against cost, and specialism against convenience.

introSummary: IB online tuition in Gurgaon means a live, one-to-one lesson over video call, not a recorded course, and IB Gram treats it as equal in seriousness to home tutoring, matched to the same board specialists rather than a generalist willing to log on. Families across Gurgaon choose it for a specific reason: a PYP, MYP or DP specialist in the exact subject and level needed is not always within driving distance, and evening traffic can turn a short home visit into a lost hour. Shared digital whiteboards, annotated past papers and screen-recorded working carry most subjects well, though a younger student or the very first session with a new tutor usually goes better in person, whether at home or online with real deliberate setup. IB Gram checks a tutor's board and level experience before a name is shared, and a free trial class settles whether the format itself is working before anything is confirmed.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram set up IB online tuition in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram starts IB online tuition in Gurgaon the same way as it would for a home request: what board stage the student is at (PYP, MYP or DP), the subject and level, the school's rough calendar, and why online specifically makes sense for this family, whether that is a hard-to-find HL specialist, an unpredictable evening, or simply a preference. That last question matters, because online works best when it is chosen for a real reason rather than treated as the automatic default.

From there, the shortlist is built the same way as any board match: two or three verified tutors who have actually taught this subject at this level, checked for board and level experience before a profile is ever shared. For an online request specifically, IB Gram also confirms the tutor is comfortable teaching on screen, since presenting clearly through a shared whiteboard is a different skill from explaining the same idea across a kitchen table, and not every strong in-person tutor makes the switch smoothly.

A free trial class runs over video call before anything is agreed, using whatever platform and tools the tutor already teaches with, so the family sees the actual working setup rather than a demonstration built for the sales pitch. Parents are encouraged to sit in briefly, check that audio and screen sharing are clear, and see how the tutor handles a moment of confusion through a screen rather than in the room.

The process in practice:
1. Send a query naming the IB stage, subject, level and why online suits the family.
2. IB Gram asks about the school calendar and confirms online is the right starting format.
3. A shortlist of two or three verified, screen-comfortable tutors comes back.
4. A free trial class runs over video call before anything is confirmed.
5. Regular sessions begin on the agreed slot, with home or hybrid available if online is not the right fit after all.

Tutors checked not just for subject depth but for genuine comfort teaching on a screen.
A free trial class runs over video call using the tutor's actual teaching setup.
Parents can sit in briefly to check audio, screen sharing and how confusion is handled.
Home or hybrid stays available if online turns out not to be the right format.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: which IB stage suits online lessons best
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme, for ages 3 to 12, is built around six transdisciplinary themes, who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry and the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, with a PYP exhibition in the final year and no external examinations. Online works least naturally here: younger PYP students generally need a tutor physically present to manage attention, materials and inquiry-based activities, and IB Gram is honest that home tutoring, not a screen, is usually the better starting point for this age group, with online reserved for occasional catch-up rather than the regular format.

The Middle Years Programme, five years across MYP 1 to MYP 5 for roughly ages 11 to 16, assesses every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, converting through IB grade boundaries to a final 1 to 7; the Personal Project falls in MYP 5, with a Community Project usually a year or two earlier, and optional MYP eAssessment in the final year. Older MYP students, from around MYP 3 onward, tend to manage online reasonably well, particularly for subjects built around discussion and written analysis rather than hands-on practical work.

The Diploma Programme, DP1 and DP2, is where online tuition suits best in practice. Six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level with 150 hours, graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to three further points toward a 45-point maximum and a 24-point minimum for the diploma. DP students are old enough to work independently on screen, and an HL specialist reached online is often a stronger subject match than whichever generalist happens to live nearby.
items: PYP (ages 3-12) generally suits home tutoring over online, given younger students and hands-on inquiry work.
MYP students from around MYP 3 onward tend to manage online reasonably well for most subjects.
DP is where online tuition suits best: six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, graded 1-7.
PYP has no external examinations; the PYP exhibition in the final year is its capstone.
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to three points toward the DP's 45-point maximum.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects work well as online tuition, and which do not?
contentBlocks.body:
Subjects built around written analysis, discussion and worked problems generally carry well onto a screen. IB Mathematics, in both the Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation routes, works well online because a shared digital whiteboard lets a tutor watch a student's working line by line, exactly as they would on paper, and annotate a mistake the moment it happens. IB English A and B, built heavily around close reading, essay structure and discussion, also translates cleanly, since the actual working material, a text or a past paper extract, is shared on screen and the conversation around it does not need physical presence.

Theory of Knowledge, built around discussion of knowledge questions and essay planning, works well online for the same reason English does: it is a conversation with shared documents, not a hands-on subject. The Extended Essay, similarly, is largely supervision and feedback on drafts, which suits a shared document and a video call as well as it suits a desk.

Sciences are more mixed. IB Physics and IB Chemistry theory, problem sets and past paper work carry well online, but any component genuinely requiring lab apparatus is something online tuition supports through discussion and preparation rather than replaces outright, since that hands-on work belongs with the school. IB Biology sits similarly: diagrams, data analysis and essay-style answers work well on a shared screen, while practical technique is not something a tutoring session, online or otherwise, is positioned to teach directly.

The honest rule across all of these: if the work is about method, structure, feedback on a draft or an approach to a written answer, it moves online cleanly. If it is genuinely about physical practical skill, no online tool substitutes for hands-on time.

IB English A and B translate cleanly online, since the material is a shared text or extract.
TOK discussion and Extended Essay supervision both suit a video call and a shared document well.
Physics and Chemistry theory and problem sets work online; lab technique itself does not.

contentBlocks.heading: Live IB online tuition for Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon and Manesar homes
contentBlocks.body:
Online tuition matters most precisely where a home tutor is hardest to place, and Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana has several such corridors. Dwarka Expressway, covering Sector 102, 103, 104, 106, 108, 109, 110 and 113, along with large societies such as Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, is one of the fastest-growing parts of the city, and its tutor pool has not always kept pace with demand for DP HL specialists in less common subject combinations. Families here often find the strongest subject match is not the nearest available tutor but the right one reached online, with an occasional home session once a regular rhythm is established.

Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, covering Palam Vihar, Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar and Sectors 4, 14, 15, 22 and 23, is dense and well served for common subjects, but a specialist in a less usual DP combination, such as a particular HL science alongside a less common Group 6 subject, may still sit outside a reasonable home radius, which is where online closes the gap without the family compromising on subject fit.

Manesar and the NH-48 corridor south of the city, taking in IMT Manesar, the area around Hero Honda Chowk, and Sectors 33, 34 and 37, has the smallest concentrated tutor pool of the three, and honestly, most specialist DP subjects here are better served online than by stretching a home match that will not hold up on a busy weekday evening. IB Gram will say this plainly rather than offering a home slot that looks good on paper but fails within a few weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars Gurgaon IB families juggle alongside online lessons
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families across Gurgaon commonly mention schools such as Pathways World School in Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School in Aravali and DPS International Edge, simply because these are names recognised across the city, not because any curriculum claim is being made about them here.

Online lessons still need to work around the same school year every Gurgaon IB family deals with: unit tests and internal assessments through the term, a winter break that needs planning around, school-set DP2 mock examinations ahead of the May session, and a final stretch once mocks are behind. An online slot has one real advantage here, scheduling flexibility, since a tutor is not constrained by travel time between one home visit and the next, which makes it easier to add an extra session in a busy pre-mock week without displacing another family's slot.

A tutor experienced with online IB teaching also tends to know how a Gurgaon school year moves: when mid-term reports usually land, when a PYP unit of inquiry or an MYP Personal Project deadline is likely approaching, and when DP2 students are most likely to need an extra session rather than a lighter one. That pattern recognition matters as much online as it does at a kitchen table.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tutor, online tutor or hybrid: what suits IB online tuition in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring remains IB Gram's baseline recommendation for most families, and it is worth saying plainly even on a page about online tuition: a tutor sitting with a student sees pacing, body language and confusion in a way no video call fully replicates, and for a younger student or the very first weeks with a new tutor, that in-person read is genuinely valuable. Home tuition also removes any dependence on internet quality, and for hands-on science practical work, nothing online replaces sitting beside a real setup.

IB online tuition in Gurgaon earns its place specifically where a home tutor cannot realistically deliver the right subject match: a DP HL specialist in a less common subject combination, a family in a corridor such as Manesar or far along Dwarka Expressway where the local tutor pool is thin, or simply an evening where Gurgaon traffic makes a home visit unreliable. For DP students particularly, who are old enough to manage independent screen work, online often gives access to a considerably stronger subject specialist than a home-only search would find.

Hybrid, a home tutor for the bulk of the week with an occasional online session for a late slot, a hard-to-place subject or a traffic-heavy evening, is where a large number of Gurgaon families land by the second month. There is no single right answer: the honest sequence is home tutoring as the default, online where subject fit or a thin local tutor pool genuinely calls for it, and hybrid as the practical middle most families settle into once they know what their particular student actually needs.

Online closes the gap where the right subject specialist is not realistically reachable at home.
DP students, old enough for independent screen work, often benefit most from an online specialist.

contentBlocks.heading: How a tutor's setup and background are checked before your first home or online lesson
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram shortlists for an online request is checked the same way as for a home one: confirmed board and level experience, checked subject depth against the syllabus a student's school is likely following, and a verified identity and stated background before a profile ever reaches a family. For online specifically, IB Gram also confirms the tutor actually teaches this way regularly, rather than being a home tutor reluctantly agreeing to try a video call for the first time with your child.

A qualification and a verified profile confirm that a subject was studied and that the person is who they say they are; neither confirms that a tutor can hold a student's attention through a screen for ninety minutes, or explain a stuck command term clearly without the body language cues an in-person lesson allows. That is exactly what the free trial class is for, and it should be treated as testing the format as much as the tutor.

During or after the trial, ask direct questions: how does the tutor typically run an online session, what tools do they use for a shared whiteboard or annotating past papers, how do they check a student is actually following rather than just nodding on camera, and what would make them recommend switching to home or hybrid instead. A tutor experienced with online teaching answers these specifically; vagueness about their own setup is a real warning sign.

If the online format itself is not working, regardless of whether the tutor is otherwise a good fit, IB Gram's answer is straightforward: say so, and home or hybrid becomes the option, or a different tutor if the mismatch is with the person rather than the format.

contentBlocks.heading: What actually works online, and what does not, subject by subject?
contentBlocks.body:
A workable online setup is simpler than families often expect, but a few things matter. A laptop or tablet, rather than a phone, makes a shared whiteboard and annotated past papers actually readable. A stable internet connection matters more than a fast one; a connection that drops mid-explanation is far more disruptive than one that is merely a little slow throughout. A quiet room with a door that closes, away from a television or younger siblings, helps more than any piece of software, and a desk rather than a bed keeps a student in a working posture rather than a resting one. Headphones with a built-in microphone cut down background noise on both ends and make a tutor's explanation easier to follow than laptop speakers alone.

Task by task, the pattern is consistent. Explaining a method, working through a problem step by step, annotating a past paper answer against a mark scheme, and discussing an essay draft or a Theory of Knowledge outline all carry onto a screen with very little lost. What genuinely does not work as well online is a student who needs close physical correction, such as handwriting technique in a younger student, or any task requiring lab apparatus, specialist equipment or a physical model that a screen cannot substitute for.

Families choose online for real, honest reasons: a specialist subject match is not available nearby, evening Gurgaon traffic makes a home visit unreliable on a given day, or a household is managing several subjects across tight weekday evenings and a home visit for each would not fit. IB Gram is equally honest about the limits: a very young student, a first-ever session with a brand-new tutor, and any hands-on practical component are all cases where home or a supervised in-person setup usually works better.
items: A laptop or tablet, a stable connection and a closed door matter more than expensive software.
Headphones with a built-in microphone cut background noise and make explanations easier to follow.
Method explanation, past paper annotation and essay or TOK discussion all carry well onto a screen.
Handwriting technique in younger students and any lab apparatus work do not translate online.

contentBlocks.heading: How to tell within three sessions whether online IB tuition is working
contentBlocks.body:
By the third session, a family should have a clear read on two separate things: whether the tutor is right, and whether the online format itself is right, since these are not the same question and conflating them leads to the wrong conclusion. On the tutor side, look for whether the student is asking questions rather than just listening, whether the tutor adjusts pace when confusion is visible on camera, and whether homework or follow-up from the previous session is actually being checked, not just assigned again.

On the format side specifically, notice whether the student stays genuinely engaged for the full session or visibly drifts after twenty minutes, whether the shared whiteboard or document tools are actually being used well by both sides, and whether technical issues, a lagging connection or an unfamiliar tool, are eating into teaching time rather than being sorted out quickly. A student who cannot sustain attention on screen after three honest attempts is telling you something real about format, not about effort.

If the tutor seems right but the format does not, hybrid or a shift to home is a reasonable next step, not a failure of the original match. If the format seems fine but the fit with this particular tutor does not, a different online tutor from the same verified pool is the more useful change. Distinguishing between these two before assuming either the child or the process is somehow wrong saves a family from cycling through several tutors when the actual issue was the screen itself.

Either way, three sessions is enough for an honest read; a family does not need to wait a full month to raise a concern about format or fit.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB online tuition in Gurgaon: what the first online session needs
contentBlocks.body:
Starting IB online tuition in Gurgaon is a short message away: the IB stage, PYP, MYP or DP, the subject and level, the school's rough calendar if a mock or exam session is approaching, and why online is the preferred starting format for this family. IB Gram asks a few clarifying questions, mainly about the subject and the reason online suits the household, before shortlisting two or three verified, screen-comfortable tutors.

Before the trial class, it helps to test the basics: a stable connection, a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, and a quiet room with the door closed. Having a recent test paper, a mock script or the student's own notes ready lets the tutor decide where the first session should actually start, the same as it would for a home lesson, rather than opening at a random point in the syllabus.

The first session itself should include a short diagnostic conversation, a look at recent work where available, and a real working demonstration of the tutor's whiteboard and annotation tools, so both sides can judge the format and the fit honestly together. From there, subject to tutor availability, regular sessions begin on the agreed online slot, with home or hybrid available at any point if that turns out to suit the student better.

If the first match, the tutor or the format, does not feel right after a genuine trial, families are not expected to persist. A different tutor, or a shift to home or hybrid, can be requested, using what the family has already learned about what their particular child actually needs.

Test the connection, device and room setup ahead of the trial class, not during it.

faqs.question: What equipment do I need for IB online tuition?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet works far better than a phone for a shared whiteboard and annotated past papers, a stable internet connection matters more than a fast one, and a quiet room with a door that closes makes more difference than any particular app. Headphones with a built-in microphone cut down background noise on both sides and make explanations easier to follow than laptop speakers alone. None of this needs to be expensive; a basic, reliable setup outperforms an elaborate one that is not actually stable during the lesson.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects suit online tuition, and which do not?
faqs.answer: Subjects built around method, written analysis and feedback on drafts, IB Mathematics, English A and B, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision, all carry well onto a screen through a shared whiteboard and shared documents. Physics, Chemistry and Biology theory, problem sets and past paper work also translate well, but any component genuinely requiring lab apparatus or hands-on technique is something online tuition can prepare a student for through discussion, not replace outright. As a rule, if the work is about structure or approach, it moves online cleanly; if it is physical practical skill, it does not.

faqs.question: Why do Gurgaon families choose online over a home tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually for one of three honest reasons: the right subject specialist, particularly for a less common DP Higher Level combination, is not realistically reachable at home from every Gurgaon sector; evening traffic makes a home visit unreliable on a given day; or a household is managing several subjects across tight weekday evenings where a home visit for each would not fit. None of these mean home tutoring is inferior in general, only that online solves a specific access problem home cannot always solve for this particular family.

faqs.question: Is online tuition reliable for families on Dwarka Expressway or in Manesar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and these are actually two of the corridors where online tuition tends to make the most practical sense, since the local tutor pool for a specialist DP subject is thinner in Dwarka Expressway's newer sectors and along the Manesar and NH-48 stretch than in more established parts of the city. A family here searching for a specific Higher Level specialist is often better served reaching that person online than settling for whoever happens to be nearby, and IB Gram will say this plainly rather than stretching a weak home match.

faqs.question: Will my younger child manage online lessons, or does home tuition suit them better?
faqs.answer: For a younger student, particularly at the Primary Years Programme stage, home tuition is usually the better starting format, since managing attention, materials and inquiry-based activities is genuinely easier in person. Online works increasingly well from around MYP 3 onward, and very well for most DP students, who are old enough to work independently on screen. If a younger student is being considered for online, it is worth starting with a trial and watching engagement honestly rather than assuming it will work the same way it does for an older sibling.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be present during an online lesson?
faqs.answer: No, though being nearby, rather than sitting in on the call, is useful for a younger student or the first few sessions with a new tutor. It also helps to have a parent available in case of a technical hiccup, a dropped connection or an unfamiliar tool, especially early on. Older DP students generally manage independently once a routine is established, and most families step back once the first few sessions have shown the format is working well.

faqs.question: What happens if an online session is missed due to a connectivity or power issue?
faqs.answer: This is common enough that most tutors have a straightforward approach: flag it as early as possible, and the session is usually rescheduled within the same week where the tutor's availability allows, though this is not guaranteed automatically. It is worth agreeing in advance how a dropped or cut-short session due to a connection issue will be handled, particularly close to a mock or exam series, so a bad evening does not quietly cost a student real preparation time.

faqs.question: How much does IB online tuition in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not quote a fee here, since cost depends on the IB stage, subject, session length and the tutor's own experience, and no single figure is fair across every family. Online tuition is often priced somewhat lower than a home visit, since a tutor's travel time is not part of the session, though the difference varies by tutor. It is reasonable to ask a candidate tutor directly how their pricing works and to compare it against what a home tutor or a hybrid arrangement would cost for the same subject.

faqs.question: Can I switch from online to a home tutor, or the other way round?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a normal adjustment rather than a sign that something went wrong. If online is not holding a student's attention, or a home tutor's travel time from a corridor such as Palam Vihar or Dwarka Expressway is becoming impractical, tell IB Gram plainly and a shift to the other format, or to hybrid, is arranged using the same verified tutor pool. It is worth raising this within the first few sessions of noticing the issue rather than waiting out a term on a format that is not working.

faqs.question: How do I know within a few sessions whether online tuition is actually working?
faqs.answer: Watch two things separately: whether the tutor is right, and whether the format is right, since they are not the same question. By the third session, a student should be asking questions rather than mostly listening, the tutor should be adjusting pace visibly when confusion shows on camera, and technical issues should not be eating meaningfully into teaching time. If the tutor seems like a good match but attention keeps drifting on screen, that points to format, and hybrid or home is worth trying before assuming the tutor is wrong.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for Extended Essay or Internal Assessment supervision?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is one of the areas online handles particularly well, since Extended Essay supervision and coursework feedback are largely about discussing a shared document and talking through structure, which suits a video call as naturally as it suits a desk. A tutor can annotate a draft on screen in real time, the same way they would with a pen on paper, and the conversation around a knowledge question or a research question does not lose anything by happening over a call rather than in person.

faqs.question: How soon can an online tutor start after I send a query?
faqs.answer: This depends on which verified tutors are available for the specific IB stage, subject and level requested, so IB Gram cannot promise an exact number of days, but a shortlist is usually put together quickly once these details are clear, since online removes the geographic constraint a home match has to work around. The trial class over video call is scheduled as soon as a mutual slot is found, and regular sessions can begin right after, subject to both sides confirming the format is working.

By the third session, a student should be asking questions rather than mostly listening, the tutor should be adjusting pace visibly when confusion shows on camera, and technical issues should not be eating meaningfully into teaching time. If the tutor seems like a good match but attention keeps drifting on screen, that points to format, and hybrid or home is worth trying before assuming the tutor is wrong.

mainEntity.name: Does online tuition work for Extended Essay or Internal Assessment supervision?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, this is one of the areas online handles particularly well, since Extended Essay supervision and coursework feedback are largely about discussing a shared document and talking through structure, which suits a video call as naturally as it suits a desk. A tutor can annotate a draft on screen in real time, the same way they would with a pen on paper, and the conversation around a knowledge question or a research question does not lose anything by happening over a call rather than in person.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is a Shortlist of Two or Three IB Tutors Built in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist only helps a family if the two or three profiles on it actually differ in a way that matters: not three tutors who all teach the same subject the same way, but a genuine spread across experience level, teaching style or availability, so comparing them tells the family something. IB Gram builds that spread deliberately rather than handing over the first three verified profiles that match the subject and level, because three near-identical options are not really a choice at all.

The process runs in five steps.

1. The parent sends a query or books a free consultation, describing the student's programme, subject, level, school and preferred format.
2. IB Gram asks follow-up questions about the school's calendar, the corridor, and what the family is weighing, whether that is teaching style, availability or online comfort.
3. A shortlist of two or three tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs is put together, chosen to differ from each other in a useful way.
4. Trial or demo sessions are arranged with each shortlisted tutor so the family can compare them directly rather than relying on profile text alone.
5. The family chooses, or asks for the shortlist to be refreshed if none of the three trials felt right.

Availability stays conditional at every step: it depends on tutor availability and schedule, and a shortlist built around a narrow evening window, say only Tuesday and Thursday after seven, will naturally be shorter than one with more flexibility. IB Gram is upfront about that trade-off before trials are booked, rather than after two of three candidates turn out to be unavailable at the family's preferred time.

Programme, subject, level, school and format gathered before any names are shared

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Tutors Across PYP, MYP and DP Stages in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
What a family should compare across a shortlist changes with the programme stage, because the three stages of the International Baccalaureate ask different things of a tutor. In the Primary Years Programme, for children aged three to twelve, learning runs through six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet, building toward the ten attributes of the IB learner profile. There are no external examinations at this stage, so comparing PYP tutors is less about exam technique and more about how each one holds a young child's attention and builds genuine curiosity rather than rote answers.

The Middle Years Programme spans five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, with every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored zero to eight; the criterion total out of thirty-two converts to a final grade of one to seven. When comparing MYP tutors, ask each one directly how they teach to the criteria rather than just to the content, since a tutor who cannot explain the difference between criterion B and criterion C for a given subject is likely teaching content without teaching the assessment. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, with the Community Project usually in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional, decided school by school.

The Diploma Programme is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded one to seven, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together worth up to three more points toward a forty-five point maximum, and twenty-four points the minimum for the diploma. For DP comparisons, ask each shortlisted tutor about their experience with the specific Higher Level or Standard Level combination the student has chosen, not just the subject in general, since HL and SL often diverge sharply in depth and pace. Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May session, with results released in early July, which is when many families start comparing tutors again for the following academic year.
items: PYP comparison: attention and curiosity-building matter more than exam technique
MYP comparison: ask directly how each tutor teaches to criteria A-D, not just content
DP comparison: ask about experience with the exact HL or SL combination chosen
The Personal Project (MYP 5) and the Extended Essay (DP) need different mentoring skills
May results in early July often start the next round of shortlisting for many families

contentBlocks.heading: What to Compare Across Tutor Profiles Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
For Mathematics, the first thing to compare is whether a shortlisted tutor teaches Analysis and Approaches, Applications and Interpretation, or both, since these are genuinely different courses rather than two speeds of the same one; a tutor confident in AA calculus and proof is not automatically the right fit for an AI student working through statistical modelling. Ask each candidate how they would approach the exploration, the roughly twenty-page internal assessment, since a tutor who treats it as a single late-term task rather than something built up across drafts over months is a weaker choice regardless of how strong their content knowledge is.

For the sciences, Physics, Chemistry and Biology at Higher Level or Standard Level, compare how each shortlisted tutor talks about the internal assessment, the scientific investigation, and whether they can walk through a markscheme line by line in a trial session rather than only describing their approach in general terms. A tutor who can annotate a past paper live and explain exactly where marks are lost demonstrates something a CV cannot. For English A and English B, listen for how each tutor discusses command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, since a tutor who treats every essay question the same way regardless of its command term is missing something the exam markers do not.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit outside the six subject groups but are worth comparing carefully, since they contribute up to three additional points toward the diploma's forty-five point maximum and are exactly the kind of open-ended work where one tutor's mentoring style suits a student far better than another's. Ask a shortlisted TOK or EE tutor for an example of how they gave feedback on a real draft, in general terms, rather than a promise about outcomes; the way they describe that process tells a family more than a list of qualifications does.

Ask how each tutor approaches the exploration across drafts, not as a single task

English A and B: listen for how a tutor discusses command terms specifically

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: Comparing Formats Across a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition remains IB Gram's main service, and when comparing a shortlist, a home-based candidate offers something the other formats cannot fully replicate: a tutor physically present with the student's own books and notes, reading confusion off a face rather than a pause on a video call, which particularly favours younger PYP and early MYP students. If two of three shortlisted candidates are home-based, it is worth watching each trial for how they use that physical presence, not just whether they show up on time and explain the topic clearly.

An online candidate on the same shortlist earns their place differently: usually by offering a subject specialism or a teaching style not available among the home-based options nearby, or by offering a wider range of slots since travel is not a constraint. Comparing an online trial against a home trial fairly means judging both on teaching quality and rapport, not penalising the online candidate simply for being on a screen; the honest trade-off is that online asks more of the student's own focus, and a family should watch specifically for whether the student stays engaged through a full session, not just the first ten minutes.

A hybrid candidate, or a tutor willing to run sessions in either format depending on the week, is often the most flexible addition to a shortlist rather than a separate category: many families end up choosing a tutor for their teaching quality first and then agreeing the format week to week based on the school calendar and traffic. None of the three formats is inherently the better choice within a shortlist; the comparison should be built around the individual tutor's fit with the student, with format treated as one factor among several rather than the deciding one.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Verification Across a Shortlist of Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Every profile on a shortlist should already carry the same baseline check: the subject and level the tutor has actually taught, not just studied, confirmed before the profile is shown to a family. What differs across a shortlist, and what is worth comparing directly, is depth beyond that baseline, board-specific teaching experience at this exact level, familiarity with the criteria or mark schemes involved, and, for an online candidate, comfort with a shared whiteboard and a stable connection at the family's preferred slot.

A parent should ask each shortlisted tutor the same set of questions, so answers are genuinely comparable rather than shaped by whichever tutor happened to volunteer the most information unprompted. Useful questions include how long they have taught this specific board and level, how they would structure a first diagnostic session, and how they report progress to parents between sessions. Two tutors who answer these questions very differently are telling a family something real about how the working relationship would actually feel, month to month.

No certificate substitutes for the trial itself, and this matters more when comparing several candidates than when hiring just one: a workshop certificate or subject qualification looks similar across two or three profiles on paper, but a trial lesson exposes real differences in clarity, patience and pacing that a certificate cannot. IB Gram's shortlist step narrows candidates worth a trial; the trial itself is where the actual comparison happens, and skipping it in favour of comparing profiles alone leaves a family choosing on the least informative evidence available.

contentBlocks.heading: Running Fair Trial Lessons With More Than One Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing two or three tutors properly means giving each of them a genuinely equal trial, not letting the first one become the unspoken benchmark simply because they went first. A useful approach is to keep the trial sessions close together, within the same week if scheduling allows, and to cover broadly similar ground in each one, the same topic or a comparably difficult one, so the comparison is not skewed by one tutor getting an easier or harder starting point than another.

Unsettling the student is the real risk families worry about, and it is a fair concern: a teenager can sense when they are being auditioned across multiple strangers in a single week. Framing it honestly to the student, that the family is finding the right long-term match and this is a short comparison phase, tends to work better than pretending each trial is a normal ongoing session. For a younger PYP or early MYP student, keeping the total number of trial tutors to two rather than three, and spacing sessions a little further apart, usually reduces any sense of disruption.

A simple side-by-side checklist after each trial keeps the comparison honest rather than relying on a vague overall impression. Useful things to note immediately after each session: how clearly the tutor explained one specific concept, whether the student asked a question and how it was answered, whether the pace suited the student, and whether the tutor gave any concrete next step for between sessions. Writing this down the same evening, while it is fresh, makes comparing three trials from the same week far more reliable than trying to remember the details a few days later. If none of the three feel genuinely right, asking IB Gram for a refreshed shortlist costs nothing and is a better outcome than settling for the least-worst option out of three.
