contentBlocks.heading: What Should Progress Look Like After Choosing a Home Tutor From the Shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Once a tutor is chosen from a shortlist for IB online tuitions in Gurgaon, the first month should show something concrete beyond simply having settled the search: a short note after each session covering what was taught and what still needs work, a visible reduction in the specific error type the trial sessions first surfaced, and a student who can explain a topic in their own words rather than repeating the tutor's phrasing back. For an MYP student that might look like a criterion score moving from a three or four out of eight toward a five or six over several weeks; for a DP student it might mean a past paper section finally completed inside the time limit.

It is fair to expect the chosen tutor to be honest if something the trial did not reveal becomes apparent later, a gap deeper than first assessed, or a pace that needs adjusting once real sessions begin. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and comparing a shortlist does not change that; what the comparison process buys a family is a considered choice rather than a rushed one, and the option to ask IB Gram for a different tutor if, despite a good trial, the ongoing fit is not holding up.

Honest limits apply here too. Choosing carefully from a shortlist narrows the chance of a poor match, but it does not remove the deeper limits any tuition faces, a student who started the Diploma Programme badly behind in January will not close that gap entirely by May regardless of how well the tutor was chosen. What a well-chosen tutor can do is target the highest-value gaps first and be honest with the family about what is realistically achievable in the time left.

faqs.question: How many tutors should I actually trial before choosing for IB online tuitions in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Most families settle on two or three, which is enough to reveal genuine differences in teaching style without dragging the search out for weeks. Trialling only one tutor removes the comparison entirely, while trialling more than three usually adds confusion rather than clarity, since the differences between candidates four and five rarely change the decision. For a younger child, two trials rather than three tends to feel less disruptive, while an older DP student weighing a specialist subject may benefit from the wider comparison three trials offers.

faqs.question: Will comparing several tutors confuse or unsettle my child?
faqs.answer: It can, if it is not handled openly, but most students adjust well once the family explains honestly that this is a short comparison phase before settling on one person. Keeping the number of trials to two or three, scheduling them within roughly the same week, and telling the student plainly what is happening usually prevents any real disruption. A student who seems genuinely unsettled by comparing candidates is worth listening to directly, since their comfort with the eventual tutor matters more than completing every planned trial.

faqs.question: What does a good tutor profile actually show before I shortlist someone?
faqs.answer: A useful profile states the exact subject, level and board experience, not a general claim of teaching IB, along with whether the tutor covers home, online or hybrid formats and in which corridors. IB Gram verifies this information before a profile is shown to a family, so a shortlist should already be comparing profiles on a consistent baseline rather than on unverified claims. Beyond that baseline, what a profile cannot show is teaching style or rapport, which is exactly what the trial session is for.

faqs.question: How much do IB online tuitions cost in Gurgaon compared across a shortlist?
faqs.answer: Cost varies by programme stage, subject, session length and format, and comparing a shortlist on price alone misses most of what actually matters for fit. IB Gram does not quote a fee before a tutor and format are matched, since pricing before that point would be a guess. What is worth comparing instead is the structure each tutor proposes, per session, monthly or in a package, and whether that structure suits the family's own plans for the term.

faqs.question: What if none of the shortlisted tutors feel right after the trials?
faqs.answer: Ask IB Gram for a refreshed shortlist, which costs the family nothing beyond the time already spent. It is more common than families expect for a first round of two or three trials to not produce a clear favourite, particularly for a specialist Higher Level subject where genuinely strong local candidates are limited. A second round, informed by what specifically did not work in the first three trials, usually narrows things down faster than the first round did.

faqs.question: Can I compare a home tutor against an online tutor fairly on the same shortlist?
faqs.answer: Yes, and doing so directly is often useful, since it tells a family whether format genuinely matters to their child or whether teaching quality is the deciding factor regardless of screen or table. Judge both trials on the same criteria, clarity of explanation, how a question is handled, and pace, rather than assuming the home trial has an advantage simply for being in person. Some families are surprised to find the online candidate was actually the stronger teacher once the trials are compared side by side.

faqs.question: How do I compare tutors fairly if one trial covers an easier topic than another?
faqs.answer: Try to request a broadly similar topic or a comparably difficult one for each trial session, so no candidate is judged on an easier starting point than another. If that is not possible, weigh the comparison on how the tutor handled difficulty rather than on raw topic difficulty itself: did they adjust pace when the student struggled, did they check understanding before moving on, and did they leave the student with a clear next step regardless of how hard the material was.

faqs.question: Do I need to tell each tutor I am trialling more than one candidate?
faqs.answer: It is not required, but being upfront tends to work better than not mentioning it, since a shortlisted tutor who knows they are one of two or three candidates often puts more thought into the trial session itself. IB Gram frames the process this way from the outset, so tutors on a shortlist generally expect it. Most tutors respond professionally to a fair comparison process, and how a tutor reacts to knowing this is itself worth noting as part of the comparison.

faqs.question: Is it normal to switch tutors partway through the year even after comparing carefully at the start?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a careful initial comparison does not remove that option later; students change, subjects get harder, and a tutor who suited a student in September is not guaranteed to suit them by February. If the fit stops working, tell IB Gram directly and a different tutor can be shortlisted, drawing on the same comparison approach used the first time. A family who compared carefully at the start usually finds a second search faster, since they already know what to ask and what to watch for.

faqs.question: How do I compare tutors for a student who has switched from CBSE or ICSE mid-course?
faqs.answer: Ask each shortlisted tutor directly about their experience with students making that specific switch, since the real adjustment is usually to criterion-based MYP marking or DP command terms rather than to any single subject's content. A tutor who can explain plainly why a CBSE-style long answer does not automatically score well against an MYP criterion or a DP mark scheme is showing real experience with this transition, which is worth more in a trial than general subject knowledge alone.

mainEntity.name: How many tutors should I actually trial before choosing for IB online tuitions in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most families settle on two or three, which is enough to reveal genuine differences in teaching style without dragging the search out for weeks. Trialling only one tutor removes the comparison entirely, while trialling more than three usually adds confusion rather than clarity, since the differences between candidates four and five rarely change the decision. For a younger child, two trials rather than three tends to feel less disruptive, while an older DP student weighing a specialist subject may benefit from the wider comparison three trials offers.

mainEntity.name: Will comparing several tutors confuse or unsettle my child?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, if it is not handled openly, but most students adjust well once the family explains honestly that this is a short comparison phase before settling on one person. Keeping the number of trials to two or three, scheduling them within roughly the same week, and telling the student plainly what is happening usually prevents any real disruption. A student who seems genuinely unsettled by comparing candidates is worth listening to directly, since their comfort with the eventual tutor matters more than completing every planned trial.

mainEntity.name: What does a good tutor profile actually show before I shortlist someone?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful profile states the exact subject, level and board experience, not a general claim of teaching IB, along with whether the tutor covers home, online or hybrid formats and in which corridors. IB Gram verifies this information before a profile is shown to a family, so a shortlist should already be comparing profiles on a consistent baseline rather than on unverified claims. Beyond that baseline, what a profile cannot show is teaching style or rapport, which is exactly what the trial session is for.

mainEntity.name: How much do IB online tuitions cost in Gurgaon compared across a shortlist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost varies by programme stage, subject, session length and format, and comparing a shortlist on price alone misses most of what actually matters for fit. IB Gram does not quote a fee before a tutor and format are matched, since pricing before that point would be a guess. What is worth comparing instead is the structure each tutor proposes, per session, monthly or in a package, and whether that structure suits the family's own plans for the term.

mainEntity.name: What if none of the shortlisted tutors feel right after the trials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask IB Gram for a refreshed shortlist, which costs the family nothing beyond the time already spent. It is more common than families expect for a first round of two or three trials to not produce a clear favourite, particularly for a specialist Higher Level subject where genuinely strong local candidates are limited. A second round, informed by what specifically did not work in the first three trials, usually narrows things down faster than the first round did.

mainEntity.name: Can I compare a home tutor against an online tutor fairly on the same shortlist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and doing so directly is often useful, since it tells a family whether format genuinely matters to their child or whether teaching quality is the deciding factor regardless of screen or table. Judge both trials on the same criteria, clarity of explanation, how a question is handled, and pace, rather than assuming the home trial has an advantage simply for being in person. Some families are surprised to find the online candidate was actually the stronger teacher once the trials are compared side by side.

mainEntity.name: How do I compare tutors fairly if one trial covers an easier topic than another?

acceptedAnswer.text: Try to request a broadly similar topic or a comparably difficult one for each trial session, so no candidate is judged on an easier starting point than another. If that is not possible, weigh the comparison on how the tutor handled difficulty rather than on raw topic difficulty itself: did they adjust pace when the student struggled, did they check understanding before moving on, and did they leave the student with a clear next step regardless of how hard the material was.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to tell each tutor I am trialling more than one candidate?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not required, but being upfront tends to work better than not mentioning it, since a shortlisted tutor who knows they are one of two or three candidates often puts more thought into the trial session itself. IB Gram frames the process this way from the outset, so tutors on a shortlist generally expect it. Most tutors respond professionally to a fair comparison process, and how a tutor reacts to knowing this is itself worth noting as part of the comparison.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to switch tutors partway through the year even after comparing carefully at the start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and a careful initial comparison does not remove that option later; students change, subjects get harder, and a tutor who suited a student in September is not guaranteed to suit them by February. If the fit stops working, tell IB Gram directly and a different tutor can be shortlisted, drawing on the same comparison approach used the first time. contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Fix a Stable Weekly Slot With an IB Tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Finding an IB tutor in Gurgaon who can actually keep a weekly slot starts with where you live, not just which subject you need. IB Gram asks for your corridor, sector or society, your child's programme stage and subjects, the school's timing and bus schedule, and whether home, online or hybrid suits you, before it even looks at tutor availability, because a brilliant match on paper that cannot reach your address on a Tuesday evening is not a match at all.

From there, IB Gram checks which verified tutors already teach in or near your corridor, since a tutor who already has two students in Sushant Lok on Tuesday evenings can often add a third nearby with less friction than a tutor starting fresh from across the city. Corridors that sit close together, such as DLF Phases 2 to 4 and Sushant Lok, or the Southern Peripheral Road and Sohna Road, often let one tutor cover both in a single evening's route, which tends to mean steadier long-term availability than a corridor served by only one or two tutors citywide.

Weekday evenings are genuinely tight. School buses drop most students home between roughly 3.30pm and 5pm depending on the school and the corridor, homework and a short break eat into the next hour, and society gate entry for a visiting tutor can itself take ten minutes if the tutor is not already on a recognised visitor list. A slot fixed for a specific evening, say Tuesday and Thursday at 6pm, tends to survive a term far better than an 'ask each week' arrangement that both sides quietly abandon by week three.

Once a slot is fixed, IB Gram keeps it stable rather than reshuffling it for other students, and any change on the tutor's side comes with enough notice to rearrange rather than a last-minute cancellation.

2. IB Gram checks which verified tutors already serve your corridor or a neighbouring one.

4. The slot is confirmed and held, with proper notice if it ever needs to change.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Stages an IB Tutor in Gurgaon Should Know
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years Programme (PYP) students, roughly ages 3 to 12, are not sitting an external exam yet; the programme runs through six transdisciplinary themes, Who we are, Where we are in place and time, How we express ourselves, How the world works, How we organize ourselves, and Sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry alongside the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, ending in the PYP exhibition in the final year. An IB tutor in Gurgaon at this stage is really consolidating literacy, numeracy and a child's confidence talking about their own thinking, not drilling exam technique that does not yet exist.

Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, with every subject marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade from 1 to 7 through the IB's grade boundaries. An MYP tutor in Gurgaon has to teach directly to those four criteria, not just the content, since a well-written answer that ignores a criterion still loses marks. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, with the Community Project usually in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional, since each school decides whether to offer it.

Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year stretch, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points, taking the maximum to 45, with 24 the minimum for the diploma subject to the IB's failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Exam sessions run in May, the session most Gurgaon schools use, and November, with May results released in early July. An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon covering, say, HL Economics or SL Chemistry needs recent experience in that exact subject and level, not a general science or humanities background.

MYP tuition must address criteria A to D directly, not just content.
DP tuition splits by HL and SL choice across six subject groups.
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points beyond the six subjects.
An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon needs recent experience in the exact subject and level.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth Across Maths, Sciences, English and TOK
contentBlocks.body:
Subject fit matters more here than in a board where every school shares one textbook. IB Mathematics runs as Analysis and Approaches (AA) or Applications and Interpretation (AI), each at Higher Level or Standard Level, and an IB tutor in Gurgaon who has taught one route well does not automatically teach the other well. The same holds for IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology, where practical work, internal assessment expectations and command terms shape how a session is planned, not just the topic list.

IB English, offered as Language A or Language B depending on a student's first language, needs a tutor who marks against the criteria a student's own school actually uses and reads set texts closely rather than teaching generic essay technique borrowed from another board. A tutor who has only taught CBSE or ICSE English brings habits that do not transfer cleanly.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sit outside the six subject groups but carry real weight, up to 3 points combined toward the 45-point maximum. TOK asks a student to examine how different areas of knowledge justify what they claim, through an exhibition and an essay; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece in a subject of the student's choosing, supervised rather than taught conventionally. Students across Gurgaon who start both late in DP2, rather than early, tend to be the ones scrambling for a topic and a research question when there is no time left to change course.

IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology tuition should include practicals and internal assessment expectations.

contentBlocks.heading: What the School Calendar Means Across Gurgaon's International Schools
contentBlocks.body:
An IB tutor in Gurgaon is often working around the calendar of schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali, and DPS International Edge, named here only as local context; IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

The pressure that matters for tuition planning is common across international schools in Gurgaon rather than tied to one school specifically. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before the May session that most Gurgaon IB schools use, and those mocks are the clearest signal of where a student actually stands before results carry real weight. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels and show exactly how marks were awarded, which is often more useful than another block of new content close to an exam.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent, set how deep an answer needs to go, and a school trains students on this over years; a tutor has to reinforce the same standard, corridor by corridor, rather than a different one picked up from general tutoring experience. May results are released in early July, and a tutor who plans backwards from that date, not just from the exam itself, tends to time revision more realistically across a school year that already has festival breaks, unit tests and mocks competing for the same evenings.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring, Online or Hybrid Across These Corridors
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is IB Gram's starting point for most families across Gurgaon, and for a reason beyond preference: a tutor sitting with a student sees the actual working, not just a final answer, and can correct a wrong method the moment it happens. IB home tutors in Gurgaon remain the most requested arrangement, especially for MYP and PYP students who focus better with someone physically present, and a parent can judge how a session is going without having to ask.

Online lessons matter too, particularly for a corridor like Manesar or the far end of the Dwarka Expressway, where the pool of tutors able to reach on a weekday evening is genuinely smaller. IB online tutor Gurgaon searches usually come from exactly this situation: a family needing a narrow DP specialism that the nearest home tutor simply does not teach. A shared whiteboard and annotated past papers do the job for most problem-solving subjects without losing much, and online removes the traffic risk entirely, useful on evenings when Cyber City or the Dwarka Expressway is running slow.

Hybrid, home sessions in a normal week with an online session before a test or when a tutor cannot make the corridor that week, suits families who want the relationship home tutoring builds without depending on a home slot every single week without fail. The honest comparison: home tutoring gives the most individual attention but narrows which tutors can realistically reach your corridor; a coaching-centre batch or an online group class costs less per head but gives less correction; online alone removes travel risk but depends on a student being disciplined about showing rough working on camera rather than off to one side. No format is right for every corridor or every subject, and the honest answer usually depends on where you live as much as what you need taught.

contentBlocks.heading: How Tutor Profiles Are Checked Before a Home Visit
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is shown as a match for your corridor, IB Gram checks what their profile claims: the programme stages and subjects actually taught, at what level, and whether that experience is a genuine fit rather than a nearby subject stretched to sound close enough. A tutor who taught IB Chemistry SL is not automatically right for HL, and a profile blurring that line gets questioned before a family ever sees it.

A parent should check further personally. Ask which exact subject group, level and syllabus code a tutor has taught, and for how long, with students at your child's programme stage specifically. Ask what a typical first session looks like, and how the tutor responds when a student's working shows a wrong method rather than a wrong number, since that answer says more than any certificate does. A free trial before you commit to anything is the real test: watch whether the first ten minutes are spent understanding your child's actual gaps, or whether a generic worksheet appears regardless of who is sitting there.

No certificate replaces that trial. A subject degree or a workshop certificate shows a baseline, not proven classroom skill with this particular student in this particular corridor's traffic and timing reality, and IB Gram treats the trial as the real decision point, not the paperwork. A tutor unwilling to run a proper diagnostic in a first session is telling you something useful before you go further.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Corridors Pair Well in One Tutor's Weekly Route?
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor's weekly route across Gurgaon is really a small map of two, three or sometimes four students taught on the same evenings, and which corridors sit inside that map matters more than most parents realise when they are told 'the tutor is available Tuesday and Thursday'. Golf Course Road and Golf Course Extension Road, for instance, are close enough that a tutor teaching a student in DLF Phase 5 at 5.30pm can often reach Sector 58 by 7pm without the evening becoming unreasonable. The same logic connects DLF Phases 2 to 4 with Sushant Lok, and the Southern Peripheral Road loosely with New Gurgaon, though the Dwarka Expressway sits far enough west that it rarely joins either of those two routes comfortably in the same evening.

This matters practically because a tutor whose existing route already runs through your corridor is a more reliable long-term match than a tutor being asked to add your address as an isolated stop far from everything else they teach. The isolated-stop tutor may accept the first term happily, then quietly find the travel unsustainable once petrol, time and traffic add up against what a single session is worth to them, and the family is left rebuilding a shortlist mid-year. IB Gram weighs this when proposing a match, not as the only factor, but as a real one.

Corridors that sit at the edge of the city's tutoring map, Manesar and NH-48 south particularly, and to a lesser extent the far end of the Dwarka Expressway and the far end of Sohna Road near Badshahpur, simply have fewer tutors whose routes already pass through them. For families in these corridors, online lessons, or a hybrid arrangement with home sessions concentrated on weekends when a tutor can justify the longer trip, tend to hold up better over a full school year than insisting on a home tutor five evenings a week regardless of the corridor's realistic pull.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Progress Look Like Corridor by Corridor?
contentBlocks.body:
Once a tutor is matched and a slot is running, progress in the first month is unglamorous: fewer repeated errors on the same type of question, a student who can explain a method out loud rather than just stating an answer, and homework that starts without a fight most evenings. It is not a jump in a school test grade that quickly, and no tutor can guarantee a grade; treat any promise of one as a reason to look elsewhere rather than a reason for confidence.

By six to eight weeks, check whether the tutor is still teaching to the school's own scheme of work and marking criteria, whether a student is attempting the harder extension parts of an MYP criterion or the tougher command terms in a DP answer, and whether actual school test results, not just how a session feels, show the change. A tutor whose sessions feel good but whose student's school results are flat is not doing the job, regardless of how well they get along.

There are honest limits too. A tutor who starts a few weeks before a mock cannot undo a year of gaps, and that student needs a realistic, narrower target for the mock plus a longer plan after it, not false reassurance in the meantime. A subject the student genuinely dislikes may still improve in grade without ever becoming enjoyable, and that is a legitimate outcome, not a failure on the tutor's part. Ask at every review, and expect an honest answer, including an honest 'not yet, here is what changes next' when that is actually true.

By six to eight weeks, check actual school test results, not just session feel.
No tutor can guarantee a grade; a promise of one is a warning sign.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting Home Tutoring Once Your Weekly Route Is Fixed
contentBlocks.body:
Once a corridor-matched tutor is confirmed, starting is simple. Fix the format, home, online or hybrid, and a specific weekly slot rather than a loose 'sometime in the evening' arrangement, since specific slots survive a real school term far better. For a home session, have a proper study space ready, a table rather than a bed, books and past papers to hand, and enough quiet that the session is not competing with a television in the next room. For online, test the video call and shared whiteboard once before the actual first lesson, not during it.

The first real session, different from the trial, usually starts with a proper diagnostic: recent test papers, a school report if there is one, and an honest conversation about what the student actually finds hardest rather than what a parent assumes. From there the tutor and family sketch a rough plan for the term, tied loosely to the school's own test and mock calendar rather than a fixed generic pace, adjusting as school pressure rises before mocks and eases after.

Availability is always subject to tutor availability and depends on level, subject and corridor, so confirm a chosen slot promptly once matched, since a tutor's route can fill with another family's request in the meantime. If the arrangement genuinely is not working after a fair attempt, IB Gram can propose a different match; switching a tutor partway through a term is a normal correction rather than a failure, and it beats persisting through an exam year with a mismatch nobody wants to name.

Prepare a real study space, or test the video setup before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have tutors who can reach every corridor of Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Most corridors, yes, though availability varies by subject and level within each one. Golf Course Road, Golf Course Extension Road, Sohna Road, DLF Phases 2 to 4, Sushant Lok, the Southern Peripheral Road, New Gurgaon, the Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon, Palam Vihar and Manesar all have tutors whose routes pass through or near them, but a rare subject combination in a far corridor like Manesar may have fewer home options than the same subject in a central corridor like DLF Phase 3, and online tuition usually fills that specific gap.

faqs.question: Why does it matter which corridor my tutor's other students are in?
faqs.answer: A tutor whose existing route already passes near your corridor is a steadier long-term match than one adding your address as an isolated stop across the city. An isolated stop can work for a term, but travel time and cost against what a single session is worth to the tutor tend to make it harder to sustain, and families sometimes find themselves rebuilding a shortlist mid-year as a result. IB Gram weighs route fit alongside subject fit when proposing a match, not instead of it.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor practical if we live on Sohna Road near Badshahpur?
faqs.answer: It depends on which part of the corridor and which tutor's route is nearest. Sohna Road is a long stretch, and Badshahpur sits at the far end of it, further from the city's tutoring hubs than Sector 47 or Nirvana Country nearer the front of the corridor. A home tutor is still possible, but availability tends to be narrower, and a hybrid arrangement, home sessions on weekends with online during the week, often holds up better here than five weekday evening visits.

faqs.question: How does school bus timing affect the weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Most schools across Gurgaon's corridors drop students home in the late afternoon, and the slot has to sit after that, after homework and a short break, which usually lands sessions somewhere between 5.30pm and 8pm on a weekday. A slot fixed for the same two evenings each week, rather than 'whenever the bus is on time', survives a full term far better, since bus timing itself shifts slightly through the year with activities and events.

faqs.question: What happens if our society restricts visitor entry on a session day?
faqs.answer: Tell your tutor and IB Gram as early as you know, and the session is rescheduled rather than cancelled outright. Societies across Gurgaon, in corridors from DLF Phase 5 to Sobha City on the Dwarka Expressway, sometimes limit visitor entry during festivals, maintenance work or resident events, and a tutor without prior visitor registration can be turned away at the gate. Adding your tutor to a recognised visitor list, where your society allows it, avoids this becoming a recurring problem.

faqs.question: Do you need to be present during a home tutoring session?
faqs.answer: No, it is not required once a tutor is established, and most students work better without a parent at the table every week. Sitting in for the first session or two is reasonable while you judge fit, but ongoing supervision tends to make a student perform for the parent rather than work through genuine confusion. Stay reachable nearby, particularly for younger students, without hovering once the arrangement has settled.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach two subjects if we need both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the tutor's own background genuinely covers both subjects at the right level, but IB Gram will not stretch a tutor's profile to cover a subject they have not actually taught just to keep things simple. It is more common, and usually better for the student, to have two separate subject specialists on the same evening's route where the corridor supports it, rather than one generalist covering ground they know less well.

faqs.question: What if there is no tutor available in our corridor right now?
faqs.answer: IB Gram will say so honestly rather than proposing a distant match and hoping it works. Availability genuinely varies by corridor and subject, and newer corridors such as parts of the Dwarka Expressway or New Gurgaon sometimes have fewer established tutor routes than older, denser corridors. Online tuition is usually offered as the interim option, with a home match proposed once a suitable tutor's route extends to your area.

faqs.question: How soon can a tutor start once matched?
faqs.answer: It depends on that specific tutor's current route and schedule, and is subject to tutor availability. A tutor already teaching near your corridor may be able to add a slot faster than one being asked to extend into a new area for the first time, so start times genuinely vary rather than being fixed. IB Gram will tell you honestly at the matching stage roughly how soon a start is realistic.

faqs.question: What if progress stalls after starting?
faqs.answer: Say so directly rather than waiting through another month quietly. Check for the smaller signs first, fewer repeated errors, a student explaining a method rather than just an answer, and homework attempted without a fight, since a school-test grade jump takes longer than a month regardless of the tutor. If those smaller signs are also missing, the match may not be right, and IB Gram can propose a different tutor, ideally one whose route already covers your corridor.

faqs.question: Is it worth choosing a tutor purely because they are close by?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. Proximity helps with scheduling and travel reliability, but a nearby generalist teaching a subject they know only reasonably well is usually a worse choice than a slightly further specialist teaching exactly your child's level and syllabus. IB Gram weighs both, corridor fit and subject fit, when proposing a match, rather than defaulting to whichever tutor happens to live nearest.

h1: IB Tutors in Gurgaon: How to Compare and Shortlist, Sector by Sector
heroTitle: Comparing IB Tutors Across Gurgaon Sectors
heroSubtitle: Most families hire the first tutor who answers the phone. A better method takes one extra week: put two or three verified profiles beside each other, compare them on the same six points, watch each teach the same student, and keep the one who taught rather than the one who talked.
introSummary: Choosing between IB tutors in Gurgaon works better as a comparison than as a hire, and for most families the options being compared are home tutors who will travel to the flat two or three evenings a week. A shortlist of two or three verified profiles, judged on the same points and tested with the same student, tells you far more than any single conversation can. This page sets out how that shortlist is built, what each profile should show before you spend an evening on it, how to run trial lessons with more than one tutor without making a fourteen-year-old feel auditioned, and how corridor and travel quietly decide which of the two candidates will still be teaching your child in March.

contentBlocks.heading: How is a shortlist of IB tutors in Gurgaon built?
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist of IB tutors in Gurgaon is built from four inputs, in this order: the programme stage, the exact subjects and levels, the school's calendar, and the address with the evenings the household can hold. Send a query or book a free consultation and those are the questions you will be asked. What comes back is two or three verified profiles rather than a long list, because a long list is a way of making the family do the sorting.

Three is the useful number. One profile gives you nothing to judge against, and five turns a decision into a research project that quietly stalls for a fortnight while a DP2 student loses ground. With three, differences become visible immediately: one has taught your child's exact level for years but can only offer a late slot, another lives in your corridor and is free at six, the third has marked work against the same criteria but teaches mainly online. Those are real choices. A single profile is not.

Each profile should carry the same information so comparison is possible at all. Which programme stage and which levels the tutor teaches. How recently they taught that level. Which subjects they are offering you, not the full list of everything they have ever touched. Which corridor they already work in on your chosen days. And whether they are available at home, online or both, subject to their existing commitments.

Availability is always conditional, and a platform that pretends otherwise is setting you up for a rescheduling conversation in three weeks. A tutor who is genuinely free on Tuesday and Friday at half past six in Sector 49 is a narrower category than a tutor who is generally good at Chemistry, and the narrower category is the one that matters.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with subjects, levels and evenings
2. IB Gram asks about board, programme stage, school calendar, location and slot
3. Two or three verified profiles come back, each showing the same fields
4. Book a demo or trial session with the two you find hardest to separate
5. Compare the trials on teaching, not on warmth, then choose one
6. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid; ask for another match if needed

contentBlocks.heading: Match the tutor to the programme, not just to the board
contentBlocks.body:
Two IB tutors in Gurgaon can both be honest International Baccalaureate (IB) specialists and still be wrong for each other's students, because the three programmes are assessed on completely different logic. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12 and sets no external examinations. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, over eight subject groups. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year course ending in a written session.

If your child is in PYP, look for someone comfortable with units of inquiry and the six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet. The ten attributes of the IB learner profile run through all of it, and the PYP exhibition comes in the final year. A tutor who only talks about worksheets has not understood the stage.

For MYP, the question to put to every candidate is about criteria. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, scored 0 to 8 apiece, and the total out of 32 becomes a 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A tutor who cannot describe how a descriptor is applied will teach content well and leave the marks where they were. Ask also about the Personal Project in MYP 5 and the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and whether the school offers the optional MYP 5 eAssessment, which is on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios.

For DP, ask specifically about levels. Six subjects come from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) contribute up to 3 further points, giving a 45 maximum against a 24 minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, with Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) also required.
items: Ask which programme stage the candidate taught most recently, and for how long
PYP: units of inquiry, six transdisciplinary themes, the exhibition in the final year
MYP: four criteria A to D, 0 to 8 each, 32 converted to 1 to 7
DP: three or four HL subjects at 240 hours, SL at 150 hours
TOK and the EE together are worth up to 3 points of 45
Confirm whether the school offers the optional MYP 5 eAssessment

contentBlocks.heading: Which subject specialists should be on a shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the subject that is costing the most marks and refuse to widen it. Families often ask for a tutor who can handle Mathematics, Physics and English at once, and the honest answer is that such a person exists but is rarely the strongest at any of them. Two specialists on alternate evenings beat one generalist five nights a week, and cost less in wasted hours.

Mathematics is the first place a shortlist goes wrong. Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) are separate courses, each offered at HL and SL, and a candidate who has taught one for years may have taught the other never. Put the exact course name in the query. The same precision applies across the sciences: Physics, Chemistry and Biology each carry distinct HL and SL demands, and a tutor strong at SL Biology is not automatically the person for HL Chemistry.

English A and B serve different language backgrounds, and a shortlist that ignores that distinction produces two tutors who are both slightly wrong. TOK and the Extended Essay belong in a separate conversation again, because the EE is supervised inside the school and a tutor's role is to interrogate a research question and a draft, never to write. State that boundary to every candidate during the trial and watch how quickly each of them agrees.

One question separates a specialist from a competent generalist faster than any certificate: ask each candidate how marks are awarded for a particular command term. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each demand a different depth of answer. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and a tutor who works from them will answer that question in specifics while a generalist answers in adjectives.

Two subject specialists usually beat one tutor covering everything
Confirm whether the student sits English A or English B
Ask each candidate how a command term changes the expected answer

The single most predictive line on a profile is which corridor the tutor already teaches in. In Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, two candidates with identical experience can produce completely different years simply because one of them already has a Wednesday evening on your road and the other does not.

On Golf Course Road, covering DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1, Sector 42, Sector 43, Sector 53, Sector 54, Ardee City and Wazirabad, along with societies such as DLF The Magnolias, DLF The Aralias, DLF Park Place, DLF The Crest and DLF The Belaire, the shortlist usually contains more names than elsewhere and the deciding factor becomes slot rather than distance. contentBlocks.heading: Two tutors, one school calendar: whose plan actually fits?
contentBlocks.body:
Give both candidates the same calendar and see who does something with it. Families at international schools across the city deal with names such as Pathways World School, Aravali; Pathways School Gurgaon; Lancers International School; Scottish High International School; GD Goenka World School; Heritage Xperiential Learning School; The Shri Ram School, Aravali; and DPS International Edge. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and nothing here states what any school teaches.

The shape of the year is what both tutors must plan against. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May session, while November is used by a minority of schools and by retake candidates. Each school fixes its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and May results are released in early July. Hand both candidates those dates in the first conversation. One will sketch a rough sequence working backwards from the mocks. The other will say they will see how it goes. That difference is more informative than either profile.

Day-to-day timing decides whether any plan survives. School bus routes vary enormously across the city, and a child returning to Sector 70 is home considerably later than one walking back inside South City 1. Sport, music, debate and service commitments occupy specific evenings. Give both tutors the true picture and let each propose a slot; the one whose proposal survives contact with a normal Wednesday is the one to take.

Internal deadlines are the hidden pressure. Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay milestones, TOK work and the MYP Personal Project land inside term time and collide with unit tests. A candidate who asks about these unprompted during the trial has run a Gurgaon DP year before.
items: Hand both candidates the same school calendar and compare what each proposes
A tutor who plans backwards from the school's mock dates has done this before
Bus arrival times differ sharply by corridor; use the real one
Name the evenings already taken by sport, music or service
Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May session; results arrive in early July

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid when two candidates are close
contentBlocks.body:
When two profiles look equally strong, mode usually breaks the tie, and home tuition is where most Gurgaon families start. A tutor at the table watches the pen, spots the line where the reasoning collapsed, and holds the attention of a younger student in a way a screen cannot. The price is reach. A home tutor's evening carries two or three addresses, so the candidate who lives near you can offer a better hour than the candidate who teaches better.

Live online changes which candidates are available at all. That matters most in the corridors where travel is punishing: the Southern Peripheral Road sectors of Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 70 and Sector 72, along with Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and Tata Primanti; New Gurgaon across Sector 82, Sector 83, Sector 84, Sector 85, Sector 86, Sector 89, Sector 90, Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, with Vatika India Next and Godrej Air; the Dwarka Expressway sectors of Sector 102, Sector 103, Sector 104, Sector 106, Sector 108, Sector 109, Sector 110 and Sector 113, with Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon; Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, meaning Palam Vihar, Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar, Sector 4, Sector 14, Sector 15, Sector 22 and Sector 23; and Manesar with IMT Manesar, Hero Honda Chowk, Sector 33, Sector 34 and Sector 37. A family in Sector 113 comparing tutors has a far wider shortlist the moment online is allowed onto it.

Hybrid resolves most ties. One home session a week to set direction and mark work in front of the student, one online for practice and doubt-solving. Families who pick hybrid rarely lose a week to weather or a jam, and the student still has a person who knows their handwriting.

The trade-off in one line: home tuition buys attention and narrows the shortlist, online widens the shortlist and costs some attention, hybrid keeps most of each and asks the household to manage two routines. Decide which of those three you are comparing candidates within before you look at a single profile.

Allowing online lessons widens a far-sector shortlist immediately
Hybrid: one home session to direct the work, one online to practise
Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and IMT Manesar usually argue for a screen midweek
Dwarka Expressway sectors pair with Palam Vihar, rarely with Sohna Road

contentBlocks.heading: What a verified profile proves, and what it leaves to you
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram means identity and qualification documents are checked, along with the boards and levels a tutor claims to teach, before any profile reaches a family. That is a floor. It rules out the person who is not who they say they are and the person teaching a board they have never taught. It cannot tell you whether this adult will get a reluctant MYP 4 student to attempt a question on a Thursday evening, and no document ever will.

The rest is yours to check, and comparing two candidates makes it easier because you have something to measure against. Ask both the same four questions: which level did you teach most recently and for how long, which papers or criteria have you marked work against, how would you start with a student stuck on this specific topic, and what will you send me after each session. Two answers to the same question reveal more than four answers to different ones.

For home lessons, run the practical checks in parallel with the teaching ones. Fix the room, keep the door open or the table in sight from the kitchen, and register the chosen tutor at the society gate as a standing visitor so entry stops being a weekly negotiation. In a managed society such as Ireo Skyon or Sobha City that is a single visit to the facility desk; in a builder floor in Sector 23 it is a word with the guard.

Write the arrangement down, even in a message: days, session length, notice period for cancellation, and what happens if the tutor is unwell for a fortnight. Families comparing candidates often discuss teaching at length and leave these entirely unsaid, then discover in January that they disagree.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed boards are verified before shortlisting
Put the same four questions to every candidate and compare the answers
Ask what written feedback arrives after each session, and how often
Register only the chosen tutor at the gate, once, as a standing visitor
Keep home lessons in a room with an open door or clear sightline
Agree cancellation and illness terms in writing before session one

contentBlocks.heading: The side-by-side checklist for judging IB tutors in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Use six columns and nothing more, because a checklist nobody completes is worse than no checklist. Board and programme depth: which stage, which levels, how recently. Subject precision: the exact course, including AA or AI and HL or SL. School familiarity: whether they can work from your school's calendar and scheme without being handed it twice. Slot and travel: which corridor, which evenings, and whether the tutor already works near you. Feedback: what arrives in writing and when. Mode: home, online or hybrid, and what happens on a bad week.

Score each candidate out of three on each line and the table will usually decide itself. What you are looking for is not the highest total but the absence of a low score on the lines your household cannot absorb. A brilliant HL Physics tutor who can only manage nine o'clock is a poor match for a Grade 9 student, whatever the total says. A merely solid tutor who is reliably present on two fixed evenings will out-deliver them across a year.

Beware the two columns that are easy to score and mean little. Years of teaching in total tells you far less than years teaching this programme at this level. Warmth in a first conversation tells you almost nothing, because it is the easiest thing to produce and the least predictive of how a session runs in week nine. Parents comparing the best IB tutors in Gurgaon by reputation alone tend to end up back at this table three months later.

One column deserves more weight than families give it. Ask each candidate what they expect the student to do between sessions, and what happens when it is not done. A tutor with no answer is planning to re-teach the same material at your expense. A tutor with a clear, unfussy answer has thought about the twenty-three hours a week they are not in your drawing room.
items: Six columns: programme depth, subject precision, school fit, slot, feedback, mode
Score out of three, then look for low scores rather than high totals
Years teaching this level matters; total years in teaching does not
Ask what the student must do between sessions, and what if they do not
Reliability on two fixed evenings usually beats a stronger late-night option
Warmth is the easiest signal to produce and the weakest to rely on

contentBlocks.heading: Running trial lessons with two tutors without unsettling your child
contentBlocks.body:
Tell the student the truth, in plain words, before either trial happens: two teachers are coming, one will stay, and choosing is the family's job and not a test of the child. Students handle this well when it is framed honestly and badly when they work out mid-lesson that they are being compared without being told. A demo or trial session can be arranged with each shortlisted tutor before you commit to anybody.

Run them close together, ideally within the same week, and give both the same starting point: the same recent piece of marked work and the same topic the student finds hardest. Identical inputs are what make the comparison fair. Then leave the room. A trial with a parent hovering measures how a tutor handles parents.

Afterwards, ask the student two questions and no more. Which of them made you do more of the work? Which one explained the part you actually did not understand? A twelve-year-old will answer both accurately. Add your own observation of whether each tutor named a specific weakness by the end, or merely reported that your child is bright and needs more practice. One of those is a diagnosis. The other is politeness.

Progress after the choice is made runs on a slower clock than parents want. By week four you should see the student able to explain their own error, homework arriving less empty, and the tutor naming two or three concrete weaknesses. Grades follow the school's own testing calendar, so a DP student's first honest measure is the mock papers. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a candidate who offers one during a trial has answered your comparison for you.
items: Tell the student in advance that two tutors are coming and one will stay
Give both trials the same marked work and the same difficult topic
Leave the room; a hovering parent changes what you are measuring
Ask the student which tutor made them do more of the work
Look for a named weakness by the end, not general encouragement
By week four expect a self-explained error, not a changed grade

contentBlocks.heading: Asking for a different tutor in Gurgaon when the fit is wrong
contentBlocks.body:
Say it early and say it plainly. Families comparing IB tutors in Gurgaon are entitled to change their minds after the first fortnight. If the match is not working, tell IB Gram and a different tutor is shortlisted; that request is ordinary, it costs nobody anything, and it is far easier in week three than in week eleven. Families hesitate out of politeness and end up paying for four months of a relationship they doubted by the second session.

Be specific about why, because the reason shapes the replacement. A tutor who explains well but cannot hold the slot is a scheduling mismatch, so the next shortlist should prioritise corridor over credentials. A tutor who arrives punctually and teaches at the wrong level is a subject mismatch, so the next one should be pinned to the exact course and level. A tutor the student simply does not talk to is a fit mismatch, and there the trial lesson matters more than any document.

Handle the changeover cleanly. Ask the outgoing tutor for a short handover note listing topics covered and the two or three weaknesses they saw, and give it to the incoming one. That single page saves the new tutor a fortnight of rediscovery, and saves the student from being diagnosed all over again. Keep the same slot if you can, because a stable evening is harder to rebuild than a tutor.

When you are ready, send a query or book a free consultation with your sector, subjects and evenings. Whether you end up with an IB DP tutor in Gurgaon for HL Chemistry, an MYP tutor in Gurgaon working through criterion descriptors, or an IB online tutor Gurgaon families share across the Dwarka Expressway sectors, the method is the same: compare two or three, test them on the same student, and choose the one who taught.
items: Ask for a different match in week three rather than in week eleven
Name the reason: slot, level or fit, so the next shortlist corrects it
Request a short handover note of topics covered and weaknesses seen
Keep the existing evening slot if the household can; rebuild the tutor
Send a query with sector, subjects, levels and the evenings you can hold
A demo or trial session comes before any commitment, subject to availability

faqs.question: How many IB tutors should we actually compare before deciding?
faqs.answer: Two or three is the number that works. One gives you nothing to measure against, and beyond three the decision stalls while the student loses weeks. Ask for a shortlist rather than a directory, make sure each profile shows the same fields, and trial the two you find hardest to separate. If all three look identical on paper, the differences will appear within ten minutes of each trial lesson. Ask for a fresh shortlist if none of them fits, which is a normal request and not a complaint.

faqs.question: Is it unfair to the tutors to trial two of them for the same student?
faqs.answer: No, provided everyone is told. Trials exist precisely so that both sides can decide, and a professional tutor expects to be compared. Say plainly that you are meeting two candidates and will confirm within the week, then do confirm within the week. What is unfair is stringing both along for a month, or asking for repeated free sessions while you think about it. One trial each, close together, a decision, and a clear message to the tutor you did not choose.

faqs.question: What should each profile show before we spend an evening on it?
faqs.answer: Five things, at minimum: the programme stage and levels taught, how recently they taught that exact level, the specific subjects offered to you, the corridor and evenings they can realistically manage, and whether they teach at home, online or both. Verified identity and qualification checks sit behind all of that. If a profile lists twenty subjects and no levels, it is a directory entry rather than a match, and an evening spent on it is an evening you do not get back.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor cover both DLF Phase 3 and Sushant Lok 1 in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because the internal roads in these colonies are short and the two sit close together. That pairing is one reason shortlists for families in Sushant Lok 1, South City 1, Sector 29 or Sector 40 tend to come back quickly. The pairing that rarely works is one address on Sohna Road and another off the Dwarka Expressway on the same evening. Ask any candidate which homes they already teach in midweek, and you will know immediately whether your slot is realistic.

faqs.question: Our society requires visitor registration. Does that complicate weekly home classes?
faqs.answer: Only once, if you handle it at the start. Register the chosen tutor at the facility office as a standing visitor with name, phone number and photograph, and weekly entry then runs through the normal gate pass or visitor app. In larger societies such as Central Park Resorts, Ireo Grand Arch or ATS Kocoon this is a single short visit. In builder floors around Sector 46 or Palam Vihar a word with the guard covers it. Do it before the first session rather than while the tutor waits at the boom barrier.

faqs.question: The first tutor is not working out. How do we ask for someone else?
faqs.answer: Message IB Gram, say the match is not working, and name the reason. A different tutor is shortlisted, and the request carries no penalty or awkwardness. Reasons matter because they shape the replacement: a slot problem means the next shortlist should favour your corridor, a level problem means pinning the next candidate to the exact course, and a rapport problem means weighting the trial lesson heavily. Ask the outgoing tutor for a short handover note so the new one does not spend a fortnight rediscovering the same gaps.

faqs.question: Two candidates quoted different fees. How do we compare that fairly?
faqs.answer: Compare what the fee contains rather than the number itself. Session length, travel, written feedback after each lesson, marking of practice papers between sessions, and availability during the weeks before mocks all vary between tutors and all belong in the comparison. A higher fee that includes marked past papers and a weekly note may cost less per unit of useful work than a lower one that does not. Ask both candidates the same question: what exactly is included beyond the hour itself?

faqs.question: Does the trial lesson tell us anything useful, or is it just a sales pitch?
faqs.answer: It tells you a great deal if you set it up properly. Give both candidates the same recent marked work and the same difficult topic, leave the room, and afterwards ask the student which tutor made them do more of the work. A trial where the tutor talked for fifty minutes and the student nodded is itself a result. Look for whether each one names a specific weakness by the end. General praise about a bright child is the commonest way a weak trial disguises itself.

faqs.question: Should we shortlist a tutor from another corridor if they are clearly stronger?
faqs.answer: Only if the subject is scarce, and then usually online. A slightly stronger HL Physics tutor crossing the city from Sector 43 to Sector 109 twice a week will begin asking to shift the time by the second month, and the slot will erode. For common subjects and levels, the nearer candidate almost always delivers more across a year. For scarce specialisms, shortlist the stronger tutor and run the lessons on a screen instead of asking anyone to make that trip in the evening.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two subjects, or should we shortlist separately for each?
faqs.answer: Shortlist separately unless the two subjects are genuinely close. A tutor who teaches Mathematics AA SL and Physics SL well is plausible; one offering Mathematics, Chemistry and English A together is usually strong in one of them. Running two separate shortlists takes an extra conversation and produces a better result, and the evenings can still be arranged so only one tutor visits on any given day. It also makes replacing one subject's tutor possible without disturbing the other.

faqs.question: How soon should we expect the shortlist after sending a query?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the level and your corridor, so any promise of a fixed turnaround is worth treating carefully. Common subjects in dense corridors such as Sohna Road or Golf Course Road are quicker, because more tutors already teach nearby. A scarce HL specialism in Manesar or the outer Dwarka Expressway sectors takes longer, and may come back as online profiles rather than home ones. Availability remains conditional throughout, and it is better to be told that honestly than to be given a name who cannot actually attend.

h1: IB Tuition in Gurgaon: Corridor by Corridor
heroTitle: IB Tuition Across Every Gurgaon Corridor
heroSubtitle: Gurgaon is not one place for tuition purposes. A seven o'clock slot that works in DLF Phase 5 can be impossible in Sector 109. This page goes corridor by corridor: which sectors and societies a home tutor reaches on a weekday, and where live online lessons are simply the sensible call.
introSummary: IB tuition in Gurgaon usually means a verified home tutor coming to your flat or house on two or three fixed evenings a week, with online lessons kept as the fallback when traffic or a late slot makes the trip impractical. Home tuition works well in most of the city, but not equally everywhere, and the difference is measured in corridors rather than kilometres. A family in Sushant Lok 1 and a family in Sector 103 face different evenings, different gate procedures and different realistic start times. This page sets out each corridor, the sectors and societies inside it, which corridors pair naturally in one tutor's week, and how IB Gram fixes a slot that survives past the first fortnight.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB tuition in Gurgaon get matched to your sector?
contentBlocks.body:
It begins with your address and the student's weekly timetable, not with a list of names. Send a query or book a free consultation, and IB Gram asks which programme stage the student is in, which subjects and levels are causing trouble, which school sets the calendar, and where in Gurgaon you actually live. Matching IB tuition in Gurgaon starts there, because a tutor who cannot reach Sector 57 by seven in the evening is not a match, however well the profile reads.

Sector matters more here than parents expect. A tutor finishing a session in DLF Phase 5 can often take a second one in Sector 53 or Ardee City the same evening without losing anyone's time. The same tutor cannot sensibly finish in Wazirabad and start in Sector 102 forty minutes later on a working weekday. So the question asked about location is not only where you are, but which other addresses sit on that tutor's line for the whole term. A slot that ignores this holds for two weeks and then begins slipping by fifteen minutes at a time.

Every profile that reaches you has been verified: identity, qualifications, and the boards and levels the tutor says they teach. You will see which programme stage they work with, whether they have taught the paper or the criteria your child is sitting, and what they can offer in your corridor. Availability stays conditional, because it depends on subject, level and the days you need. If two of the three profiles suit, ask for a trial lesson with both before deciding anything.

Nothing here is a one-way door. If the first match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is shortlisted. No family should be stuck with a person who does not suit the student because the alternative felt awkward to raise.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation, naming your sector and society
2. IB Gram asks about board, subjects, level, school calendar, location and slot
3. You receive verified profiles of tutors who can reach that address
4. A demo or trial session is arranged before the family commits
5. Lessons begin at home, online or hybrid, on a fixed weekly slot
6. Ask for a different match at any point if the fit is wrong

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which stage is your child actually in?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask the school and confirm it before you book anything, because the three International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes are assessed in entirely different ways. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12 and has no external examinations. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year course, DP1 and DP2, that ends in a written examination session.

PYP learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes through units of inquiry: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet. The ten attributes of the IB learner profile sit across all of it, and students complete the PYP exhibition in the final year. Tuition at this stage is quiet work on reading, number sense and the habit of asking a question properly, not examination drill.

MYP is where parents in Gurgaon most often feel lost, because the marking is criterion-based. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. A student can know the content and still lose marks under a criterion they have never had explained. The Personal Project falls in MYP 5, the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional, with each school deciding whether to offer it.

DP is six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed.
items: PYP: six transdisciplinary themes, units of inquiry, the exhibition, no external exams
MYP: four criteria A to D, each out of 8, total out of 32
MYP 5 carries the Personal Project; the Community Project falls in MYP 3 or 4
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL, each graded 1 to 7
TOK and the EE add up to 3 points; 45 maximum, 24 minimum
Exam sessions run in May and November; May results arrive in early July

contentBlocks.heading: Subject depth behind a weekly IB tuition slot
contentBlocks.body:
A weekly slot is only worth what goes into it, and what goes into it differs sharply by subject. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each at HL or SL, and a student who has drifted into the wrong one loses months. Physics, Chemistry and Biology carry their own practical and written demands at HL and SL. English A and B are different courses for different language backgrounds, and mixing them up in a tuition plan wastes a term.

Command terms are where marks quietly disappear. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set the depth an answer needs, and a student who writes a beautiful description where the paper asked for an evaluation will be marked accordingly. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show exactly how marks are awarded. A tutor who works from those rather than from a private set of notes is teaching the assessment your child will actually sit.

TOK and the Extended Essay need a different kind of help again. The EE is an independent piece of research with a supervisor inside the school, so a tutor's job is to question the research question, not to write anything. The same boundary applies to any Internal Assessment (IA): the tutor can teach the method, read a draft and ask hard questions, and must stop where the student's own work begins. Say this out loud in the first session so everybody knows the line.

For most families two subjects at a time is the ceiling that actually works. Adding a third usually means the first two get less attention rather than the student getting more, particularly in DP2 when coursework deadlines start stacking up against school tests.
items: Mathematics AA and AI, each at HL or SL, are genuinely different courses
Physics, Chemistry and Biology: different practical and written demands at HL and SL
English A and B suit different language backgrounds; confirm which one applies
Command terms set the depth: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent
Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB
A tutor questions an IA or EE draft; the writing stays the student's own

High-rise societies such as DLF The Magnolias, DLF The Aralias, DLF Park Place, DLF The Crest and DLF The Belaire run strict visitor registration, so the tutor's details should be left at the gate once as a regular visitor rather than argued about weekly.

Gwal Pahari and Ghata sit far enough from the core that IB online tuition in Gurgaon is often the steadier choice for a midweek lesson.

Density is the advantage here: IB tuition on Sohna Road can often be arranged at short notice because several families share one tutor's evening line.
