faqs.answer: It depends mainly on how much individual correction the student needs right now. A student who makes the same specific error repeatedly and needs it caught in real time generally benefits more from one-to-one attention than from a batch, however well the batch is run. A confident, largely independent student who mainly wants structure, deadlines and the discipline of peer accountability can do well in a genuinely IGCSE-specific batch, where one exists, often at a lower cost per hour. faqs.question: My son is switching from CBSE to IGCSE partway through the year. What should we look for in a tutor?
faqs.answer: Look specifically for a tutor who has supported a CBSE to IGCSE transition before, not only one who has taught IGCSE from the start of Grade 9, since the switch involves adjusting to command-term based answers, evaluate, explain, describe, rather than the more formulaic patterns CBSE assessments often reward. A tutor experienced with this move typically starts with a diagnostic session to locate exactly where the gap sits before building a catch-up plan around the school's remaining term, rather than assuming a fresh start from the syllabus beginning.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travel to our sector on weekday evenings reliably?
faqs.answer: Reliability depends on the corridor and how far the tutor is genuinely travelling, which is worth asking directly during the trial conversation rather than assuming. A tutor based close to Golf Course Road committing to a regular evening slot in that same corridor is a safer bet than one travelling a longer distance down NH-48 toward Manesar on a route affected by evening traffic. If reliable weekday evening travel is a real concern for a family's specific corridor, raising it with IB Gram upfront, or considering a hybrid arrangement with occasional online sessions, is worth doing before committing to a fixed home schedule.

faqs.question: How soon can a tutor actually start once we send a query?
faqs.answer: Once a query is sent with the board, grade and subject, IB Gram typically arranges a free trial lesson within a few days, depending on which specialists are free that week for the exact tier and syllabus required. Regular sessions can usually begin the same week the trial goes well, subject to tutor availability and the family's preferred slot and format. Sending a query a few weeks ahead of mocks or a major test generally offers more choice of specialist than a request sent after assessments have already begun.

faqs.question: What should we expect from revision sessions before mock exams specifically?
faqs.answer: In the weeks before mocks, a good tutor shifts from general syllabus coverage to targeted past paper practice and timed conditions, focusing on the specific question types and command terms that have been costing the most marks in recent practice. Expect the tutor to prioritise ruthlessly rather than trying to revisit every topic equally, since the exam is now close enough that some content simply matters more than the rest. A clear account of which topics are being prioritised, and why, is a reasonable thing to ask for directly before mock week begins.

IB Gram builds that shortlist around your child's board, tier and school, arranges a trial lesson with each, and helps you compare honestly before committing to weekly sessions.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon are worth comparing before you commit to home tuition or online lessons with just one, because a subject specialist who suits one student's pace can be the wrong fit for another. IB Gram typically shares two or three verified tutors matched to the board, tier and school, arranges a trial for each, and helps the family compare on more than a first impression. This page walks through how a real shortlist is built, what to weigh side by side, how to run trials with more than one tutor fairly, and what to do if the first match is wrong, including in corridors like Sohna Road, the DLF Phases and Sushant Lok, where enough tutors already teach nearby to give a genuine choice.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds a Shortlist of IGCSE Tutors in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist of IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon starts the same way a single hire would: grade, board, Cambridge or Edexcel, current school and the subject or subjects that need support. What changes is what happens next. Instead of sending one profile and hoping it works, IB Gram puts together two or three verified tutors who all genuinely match the tier and syllabus, so the comparison that follows is between real, comparable options, whether the sessions end up being home tuition or online, rather than a first name and a backup nobody looked at closely.

Board and tier are checked before anyone is shortlisted, not after. A tutor confident on Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended is not automatically the right fit for a student sitting Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 Foundation, and putting two tutors from different boards on the same shortlist without saying so wastes a family's time. IB Gram tells you upfront where each shortlisted tutor's strength actually lies, rather than presenting three near-identical profiles that are hard to tell apart.

Each tutor on the shortlist then runs a separate trial lesson, ideally within the same week, so the comparison is fresh and fair. A trial six days apart from another is harder to judge honestly than two trials on consecutive evenings, since a student's mood, tiredness or a hard school day can colour one session more than the tutor's own teaching does. IB Gram suggests scheduling trials close together for exactly this reason.

After the trials, the real comparison happens: pace, clarity, how the tutor explains a wrong answer, syllabus knowledge specific to the tier, and whether the proposed weekly slot actually suits the household. If none of the first three feel right, that is not unusual, and IB Gram will put together a fresh shortlist rather than asking a family to settle. The goal of comparing IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon is a genuine fit, not simply filling a weekly slot with whoever answered first.

2. We shortlist two or three verified IGCSE tutors, not one, matched to board, tier and corridor.
3. Each tutor runs a separate trial lesson, so you compare an actual class, not a profile.
4. You compare side by side on pace, clarity, syllabus knowledge and the proposed weekly slot.
5. You choose one, or ask for a fresh shortlist if none of the first three fit.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE Board and Tier Should Your Shortlist Match?
contentBlocks.body:
Before comparing any IGCSE tutors, confirm the board. Cambridge IGCSE, set by Cambridge International Education, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE cover the same two years, Grade 9 and Grade 10, but grade differently and examine on a different calendar, so a shortlist that mixes boards without saying so is comparing two different things. Every profile IB Gram shares states the board and the tier the tutor is strongest at, so you are never comparing a Cambridge Extended specialist against an Edexcel Higher tutor as though they were the same offer.

Exam series timing shapes the comparison too. Cambridge runs three series, February/March, offered only in India, May/June and October/November, while Pearson Edexcel runs two, January and May/June. A tutor's revision plan only makes sense once the exact series is confirmed, so this is one of the first things worth asking each shortlisted tutor directly, rather than assuming every tutor is planning toward the same date.

Tier matters just as much as board. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, Core capping at grade C and Extended reaching A*, and Edexcel Mathematics splits into Foundation and Higher. A shortlist should only include tutors genuinely comfortable at the tier the student is actually sitting; a tutor whose recent experience is mostly Core should not be silently offered for an Extended-tier comparison, and IB Gram flags this distinction on every profile.

What comes after Grade 10 is worth factoring into the comparison too, even this early. A student likely to move into the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) benefits from an IGCSE Grade 9 and 10 tutor who builds independent study habits now, while a student continuing into A Levels on the same board benefits more from a tutor who deepens exam technique on the current syllabus. Mentioning your family's rough plan when requesting a shortlist helps IB Gram weight this in the tutors it proposes.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Each Tutor's Profile Show About Their Subject?
contentBlocks.body:
A useful profile names the exact syllabus, not just the subject. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits Core candidates across Papers 1 and 3 and Extended candidates across Papers 2 and 4; a Cambridge IGCSE tutor Gurgaon families shortlist for Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 instead should show Foundation and Higher experience, each with two calculator papers. A profile that just says Maths tells you almost nothing useful for comparing them against another Maths tutor on the same shortlist.

Sciences add another layer worth comparing directly. Cambridge IGCSE sciences weight multiple choice at 30%, theory at 50% and practical assessment at 20%, delivered through either a hands-on Paper 5 practical test or the Paper 6 written alternative; Edexcel sciences are untiered, assessed through Paper 1 and Paper 2 with practical skills folded into the written papers. An Edexcel IGCSE tutor Gurugram families shortlist for sciences should be able to say clearly which of these they have actually taught.

English is the subject where profiles vary most, because so many syllabuses exist under one name: First Language English 0500, which can be assessed by coursework portfolio or terminal paper depending on the school; English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511, which differ in how speaking is graded; Literature in English 0475; and Edexcel's Language A 4EA1, Language B 4EB1 and ESL 4ES1. A tutor's profile should say which of these they have actually taught, since coaching for a coursework portfolio is a different skill to coaching for a single terminal paper.

Finally, compare how each tutor marks. A tutor marking strictly against the real Cambridge or Edexcel mark scheme or assessment criteria gives a student an honest sense of where they stand; a tutor marking on gut feeling does not. Ask each shortlisted tutor directly how they mark practice papers, and treat a vague answer as useful information in itself when you are comparing two or three IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon side by side.
items: Which exact syllabus code the tutor has taught: 0580, 4MA1, 0500, 0510, 0511 or similar.
Whether their recent experience is mostly Core, Extended, Foundation or Higher tier.
How they mark: against the real mark scheme or assessment criteria, not a general rubric.
Any examining, moderating or official workshop experience with Cambridge or Edexcel.
Which papers or components, written, practical or coursework, they are strongest teaching.

contentBlocks.heading: How School Calendars Affect When to Start Comparing Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge all work to broadly similar calendars in Grade 9 and 10, whatever their specific school offers.

The best time to start comparing IGCSE tutors is six to eight weeks before a school's internal mock exams, while there is still enough runway to run two or three trial lessons and settle into weekly sessions before pressure builds. Starting the comparison the week before mocks means picking a tutor under time pressure, which usually means skipping the part where you actually compare.

Winter break and the festival holidays through the autumn term are a poor window to run trial lessons, since students, tutors and schools are all off their usual rhythm, and a trial during a break tells you less about how weekly sessions will actually go. Coursework and portfolio deadlines, for a syllabus like First Language English 0500 that offers a coursework route, often land months before the written exam series, so a family should start comparing tutors earlier than the general exam calendar suggests if coursework is involved.

Right after mocks is often the moment a family first decides to compare tutors, since the results make clear which subject needs real support rather than a hunch. Parent-teacher meetings can surface the same thing even earlier. Either way, starting the comparison while the specific gaps are fresh, rather than waiting for the next report card, gives a shortlisted tutor more useful information to work from in the first trial.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Comparing Formats Across Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's lead service is home tuition: a verified tutor teaching the student at your own home, in your own sector or society, in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, and most shortlists start there. Comparing tutors on home visits shows you something a profile cannot: how the tutor manages the actual student in the actual room, whether they notice when attention drifts, and whether the pace they set in a trial matches what was promised on the profile.

Online tutors belong on the same shortlist, not a separate one, particularly for a subject where the strongest specialist available does not happen to live near your corridor. A trial lesson over video call is just as comparable as a home trial, provided both run for the same length and cover similar ground; what matters is whether the tutor teaches well, not which format they use to do it. Families are sometimes surprised at how directly an online trial and a home trial can be judged side by side.

A hybrid week, one home session and one online session, is worth including as its own option on a shortlist rather than treating it as a fallback. Some students genuinely do better with a tutor who is physically present for new content and comfortable finishing revision or past papers online, and comparing a hybrid proposal against a pure home or pure online option is a fair, useful comparison, not an odd one out.

It is entirely reasonable to mix formats across a shortlist, running one trial at home and one online, especially in corridors where home tutors are harder to find for a specific subject. What should stay consistent across the comparison is the length of the trial and the material covered, since comparing a thirty-minute online demo against a full home session is not a fair test of either tutor.
items: Compare each shortlisted tutor on the same format so the comparison stays fair.
Home tuition lets you see how a tutor manages the actual student, not just the subject.
An online IGCSE tutor Gurgaon families shortlist can still run a fully comparable trial lesson.
A hybrid week is worth comparing as its own option, not a compromise between the other two.
Mixing formats across a shortlist, one home trial and one online trial, is still a fair comparison.

contentBlocks.heading: What Verification Should Every Shortlisted IGCSE Tutor Pass in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram puts on a shortlist has already passed a baseline check: subject background, the board and level they have actually taught, and, where relevant, examining or marking experience with Cambridge or Edexcel. This happens before a family ever sees the profile, so a comparison starts from a pool of tutors who have already cleared the same bar, not a mix of verified and unverified names side by side.

Within that shortlist, it is still worth asking each tutor directly about their experience at the exact tier being compared. A tutor strong on Cambridge Extended Mathematics is not automatically prepared for Foundation-tier Edexcel work, and a family comparing three profiles should ask the same specific question of each one, rather than assuming a strong general reputation covers every tier equally well. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any profile implying otherwise is worth treating with caution.

For a home tuition trial, confirm who else will be in the room and for how long, and do the same for each tutor on the shortlist so the comparison stays consistent. Gate entry and visitor registration vary by society, so it is worth checking with your own gate in advance of the first trial, particularly if two different tutors are visiting in the same week.

Before choosing, ask each shortlisted tutor the same question about rescheduling: what happens if a session cannot go ahead as planned. A tutor with a clear, calm answer to this before anything has gone wrong is usually easier to work with over a full term than one who has not thought about it. IB Gram documents replacement and rescheduling terms with the family once a tutor is chosen, so nothing is left to a verbal understanding.
items: Subject background and the level actually taught, checked before a tutor is shortlisted at all.
Board experience matched to the exact syllabus, not just the general subject.
Any examining or marking experience relevant to the tier being compared.
A clear answer on rescheduling and replacement before the first paid session.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Two or Three IGCSE Tutors: A Side-by-Side Checklist
contentBlocks.body:
A side-by-side comparison works best against a short, consistent checklist, run against every tutor on the shortlist, not adjusted tutor by tutor. Subject and tier fit comes first: has this specific tutor actually taught this specific syllabus code, at this tier, recently, rather than years ago or for a different board entirely. A tutor's confidence in the trial is not a substitute for this; confident and wrong is worse than uncertain and honest.

Teaching style matters more than most families expect going in. Watch whether a tutor explains why an answer is wrong, walking the student back through the reasoning, or simply supplies the correct answer and moves on. The first builds understanding a student can use again; the second gets through more questions in the same hour but leaves the actual gap untouched. Pace sits alongside this: a tutor who is comfortable working faster than the student needs, or slower than the student wants, will show it within the first fifteen minutes of a trial if you are watching for it.

Communication is worth asking about directly rather than assuming. Some tutors send a short note after every session; others prefer a weekly summary; some update the parent only when asked. None of these is wrong, but a family that wants regular updates should say so during the trial and see whether the tutor adjusts, since that response tells you something about how they will work over a full term.

Logistics deserve the same scrutiny as subject knowledge. A slot that looks fine on paper can collapse against a late school bus or a bad traffic evening on a stretched corridor, and it is worth asking each tutor directly how flexible they can genuinely be, not just whether the slot works in theory. Finally, trust the student's own reaction: a student who relaxes into a trial, asks a real question, or admits confusion without embarrassment has usually found a workable match, whatever the profile said on paper.
items: Subject and tier fit: has this exact tutor taught this exact syllabus code before?
Teaching style: does the tutor explain a wrong answer, or simply give the right one?
Pace: does the tutor match the student's pace, or the tutor's own preferred speed?
Communication: how and how often does the tutor plan to update you on progress?

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Change at Home After You Switch to a Better-Matched Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
The first sign a switch has worked is usually smaller than families expect. A student who used to avoid homework in a subject starts attempting it with less resistance, or starts asking a specific question, why this method and not that one, instead of a flat 'I don't get it.' That shift, from vague frustration to a specific question, tends to show up within the first two or three sessions with a genuinely better-matched tutor, whether the sessions are home tuition or online.

No tutor, however well matched, can guarantee a grade, and it is worth being honest about that even after a successful switch. What a better match reliably changes is the odds: a tutor who explains clearly, marks against the real criteria and sets a pace the student can actually follow gives a student a fairer shot at their own potential, which is different from promising a specific outcome.

A proper review, roughly every four to six weeks, should point to something concrete: a topic that used to cause panic now handled calmly, a paper technique that has clicked, a mock score that has moved. If a review after switching still sounds vague, that is worth raising directly rather than assuming the new tutor simply needs more time, since a genuinely better match usually shows its effect faster than a poor one ever did.

Occasionally, switching tutors does not fix the underlying problem, and that is useful information too. If a student struggles across multiple well-matched tutors in the same subject, the issue may sit somewhere else entirely, a gap from an earlier grade, a confidence problem bigger than one subject, or simply needing fewer subjects at once rather than a different teacher. IB Gram will say so honestly rather than proposing a fourth tutor for the same unsolved problem.
items: Homework gets attempted with less resistance within the first two or three sessions.
The student starts asking specific questions instead of saying a subject is just hard.
No tutor can guarantee a grade; a better match improves the odds, not the outcome.
A review every four to six weeks should show something concrete has shifted.
If nothing changes after a genuine switch, the problem may not be the tutor at all.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Your IGCSE Tutor Shortlist Started in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Send IB Gram a query or book a free consultation with the student's grade, current school, board and, if you know it, the tier, Core or Extended, or Foundation or Higher. Ask specifically for a shortlist of two or three tutors rather than a single recommendation, even if the first name you hear sounds promising; the comparison is where a genuinely good match tends to surface.

Once the shortlist arrives, book trial lessons as close together as your calendar allows, ideally within the same week, so tiredness or a hard school day does not unfairly colour one tutor's trial against another's. Decide in advance whether you want each trial to be home tuition, online or a mix, since availability by corridor, particularly in Sohna Road, the DLF Phases or Sushant Lok, can affect how quickly each format can be arranged.

During each trial, run the same short checklist: subject and tier fit, teaching style, pace, communication and logistics, and take a note straight after while the session is fresh, rather than trying to remember details a week later when comparing across three tutors gets harder. Ask the student directly how each session felt, since their honest reaction is often the most reliable signal in the whole comparison.

Once you have chosen, tell IB Gram which tutor and, briefly, why, since that feedback sharpens future shortlists for other families with a similar board, tier and corridor. If none of the first three feel right, say that too; a fresh shortlist costs nothing and is far better than settling for a tutor who was simply available first.
items: Send the student's grade, board, tier and school so the shortlist starts from real information.
Ask for two or three profiles, not one, even if the first sounds promising.
Schedule trial lessons close together, ideally within the same week, for a fair comparison.
Use the side-by-side checklist during each trial, not just afterward from memory.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE tutors should I compare before choosing one?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually enough. Comparing more than three rarely adds useful information and mostly delays a decision the student is waiting on. IB Gram typically shares two or three verified profiles matched to the board, subject and tier requested, and arranges a trial lesson with each so the comparison rests on an actual lesson rather than a written profile. If none of the first three feel right, a fresh set can be shared rather than stretching the search indefinitely, but going past three tutors is rarely worth the extra time.

faqs.question: Is it unfair on the student to run trial lessons with more than one tutor?
faqs.answer: Not if you are upfront with the student about what is happening and why. Most students in Grade 9 or 10 understand and even appreciate being asked which tutor felt like a better fit, rather than simply being told who they are stuck with for the term. Keep the trials close together, ideally within the same week, and keep each one the same length, so the comparison is fair to the tutors and does not tire the student out with three unequal sessions spread across a month.

faqs.question: What if the two or three shortlisted tutors all seem equally good?
faqs.answer: That happens, and it usually means the deciding factor is something practical rather than subject knowledge: which slot genuinely survives a bad traffic evening, which tutor the student felt most comfortable asking a confused question to, or which communication style suits your family. When subject fit is roughly equal across a shortlist, it is worth weighting the softer signals from the trial, since those tend to predict how the working relationship holds up over a full term better than a resume does.

faqs.question: Can we compare a home tutor and an online tutor on the same shortlist?
faqs.answer: Yes, and IB Gram often builds shortlists this way, particularly for a subject where the strongest available specialist teaches online rather than from a nearby corridor. Run both trials for the same length and similar material so the comparison is fair, and judge on teaching quality first; format is a real factor but a secondary one. Families are often surprised at how directly a home trial and an online trial can be compared once both have actually happened.

faqs.question: How soon after a trial should we decide on a tutor?
faqs.answer: Within a few days, while the sessions are still fresh in both the parent's and the student's memory. Waiting weeks to decide between three trials makes the comparison harder, not easier, since details blur together. IB Gram suggests taking a short note straight after each trial, covering pace, clarity and the student's own reaction, so the comparison does not rely purely on memory once all three trials are done.

faqs.question: What if we want to compare tutors but our corridor has very few options nearby?
faqs.answer: IB Gram widens the search to include an online tutor or two alongside whatever home options exist nearby, so the shortlist still has two or three genuine choices rather than one tutor and a weak backup. This comes up most in corridors further from where tutors already cluster; in denser corridors like Sohna Road, the DLF Phases or Sushant Lok, a home-only shortlist is usually realistic without needing to widen the search at all.

faqs.question: Do we have to tell a tutor they are being compared with others?
faqs.answer: It is not required, but most families find it easier to be upfront, since a tutor who knows they are one of two or three shortlisted options tends to bring their best trial lesson rather than a routine one. IB Gram is transparent with tutors about the shortlisting process as a matter of course, so there is rarely an awkward surprise on either side, and it keeps the comparison honest for the student watching too.

faqs.question: Does a home trial lesson need the same setup as a normal weekly session?
faqs.answer: Close to it. Have the student's current textbook, exercise book and any recent past papers or tests ready, in a reasonably quiet space, so the trial reflects what a real weekly session would actually look like rather than an artificially tidy demonstration. If a parent usually sits nearby during sessions, do the same for the trial, since changing the setup just for the trial can make the comparison less accurate than it should be.

faqs.question: What if one shortlisted tutor cancels their trial at short notice?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram, and a replacement trial, either with that tutor rescheduled or a fresh tutor added to the shortlist, will be arranged. A single cancellation before any commitment has been made is a minor inconvenience, not a red flag, but a pattern of late cancellations even at the trial stage is worth mentioning, since it tells you something about how that tutor is likely to handle a genuine weekday evening clash once term sessions begin.

faqs.question: Is it worth comparing tutors for a subject the student is already doing fine in?
faqs.answer: Usually not, unless there is a specific reason: a harder unit coming up, a tier decision approaching, or a school switch. Comparing and trialling multiple tutors takes time and can unsettle a student who was managing well, so it is worth reserving the full shortlist process for a subject that genuinely needs it, and keeping a lighter, single-tutor approach for a subject that is already on track.

faqs.question: Can we ask a tutor from a previous shortlist to rejoin a new comparison later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and IB Gram keeps a record of who was previously trialled, so a tutor who was a close second last time can be included again if a new subject or a new need comes up. Families sometimes assume starting fresh means forgetting the earlier comparison, but the opposite is usually more useful. A tutor who nearly fit before is often a stronger starting point than an entirely unknown name.

faqs.question: Will each shortlisted tutor actually travel to our sector for the trial?
faqs.answer: IB Gram only shortlists tutors whose existing route already passes near your sector or corridor, so travel is checked before a name reaches your shortlist, not discovered as a problem after a trial is booked. In denser corridors like Sohna Road, the DLF Phases or Sushant Lok, this is rarely an issue; further out, IB Gram may propose an online trial alongside a home one so the comparison still includes a genuinely local option. Either way, the tutor confirms the corridor before the trial is confirmed, not on the doorstep.

heroTitle: Comparing IGCSE Tuitions Across Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: IB Gram builds a shortlist of two or three verified IGCSE tutors for Grades 9 and 10 in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, so you compare real profiles side by side instead of hiring the first name you find. introSummary: IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon rarely mean hiring the very first tutor who replies; most families compare two or three verified profiles before choosing, and IB Gram builds that shortlist deliberately rather than handing over a single name. Home tuition is usually the starting point for comparison, since most parents want to see how a tutor works at the family's own table before deciding between candidates, though online and hybrid options sit on the same shortlist rather than as an afterthought. This page walks through how a shortlist actually gets built, what to compare across two or three profiles side by side, board experience, level taught, school familiarity, slot and travel, how to run trial lessons with more than one tutor without confusing the student, and what to do the moment the first match turns out to be wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: How Does IB Gram Build a Shortlist You Can Compare in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist starts the same way any IB Gram match does: a query or a free consultation call covering board, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, grade, tier if the school has decided Core or Extended, subject, and where in Gurgaon the family lives. What makes it a shortlist rather than a single referral is that IB Gram deliberately puts forward two or three profiles instead of one, chosen so the differences between them are actually useful to compare, not three near-identical options.

The process runs as follows:

1. Intake records board, tier, subject, grade, corridor and preferred weekday evenings for comparison purposes.
2. IB Gram selects two or three verified tutors who differ meaningfully, in experience, teaching style or availability, not just in name.
3. Each profile is shared with enough detail to compare side by side: board experience, level taught, familiarity with the family's school, and slot and travel realism.
4. Trial sessions are arranged with more than one tutor where the family wants to compare directly, not just accept the first slot offered.
5. A different profile replaces any tutor who does not work out, drawing on what the comparison already showed about that student's needs.

For IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon specifically, corridor availability shapes how meaningfully different a shortlist can be: a family in a tutor-dense corridor gets three genuinely distinct profiles to weigh, while a family in a thinner corridor may see a shortlist that leans more heavily on online options to keep the comparison real rather than padded.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: Know the Board Before You Compare Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing two IGCSE tutors only works if both are being measured against the same board, and Gurgaon schools run two different ones. Cambridge IGCSE, set by Cambridge International Education, is more widely taught across the city's international schools. Pearson Edexcel offers its own International GCSE, with separate paper codes and, for several subjects, a different grading table, so a shortlist that mixes a Cambridge specialist with an Edexcel generalist is not actually comparing like with like.

Both boards run Grades 9 and 10 as one two-year course, usually followed by the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Cambridge sits three exam series: February/March, offered only in India, May/June, and October/November. Edexcel International GCSE runs two, January and May/June, a tighter calendar that changes how soon a tutor needs to start revision work with a Grade 10 student.

Grading is a further point of comparison. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some subjects now offering 9-1 versions under separate codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects tier into Core and Extended, Core capping at a C and Extended reaching an A*, usually decided by the school around Grade 9. When comparing two tutor profiles, ask each one directly which tier they last prepared a student for, since that answer says more than years of experience alone. A shortlist that skips this question is not really comparing anything meaningful at all.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Two IGCSE Tutors Be Compared On, Subject by Subject?
contentBlocks.body:
Maths comparisons should start with the paper split. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, has Core candidates sitting Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, calculator; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4, the calculator equivalents. When comparing two Maths tutors, ask each how they balance non-calculator drilling against calculator practice, since a tutor who only reinforces the calculator paper leaves a real gap. Pearson Edexcel's Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, tiers Foundation or Higher instead, each with two calculator papers, which needs a different weekly balance entirely.

Science comparisons hinge on the practical route. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, in syllabuses examined from 2023, combine a multiple choice paper, Paper 1 Core or Paper 2 Extended, a theory paper, Paper 3 or Paper 4, and a practical component through either Paper 5, an actual test, or Paper 6, an alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. With multiple choice worth 30%, theory 50% and the practical route 20%, ask each shortlisted tutor how they weight their sessions across those three, not just whether they cover the content. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with practical skills assessed inside the two written papers directly.

English comparisons need the exact syllabus name before anything else. Cambridge offers First Language English 0500, built on a reading paper plus either directed writing and composition or a coursework portfolio, English as a Second Language in two versions, 0510 and 0511, which differ in how speaking counts toward the grade, and Literature in English 0475. Edexcel's equivalents are English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). Two tutors cannot be fairly compared on English until both are confirmed to be teaching toward the same one.

contentBlocks.heading: Where in Gurgaon a Home Tutor's Shortlist Gets Wider or Narrower
contentBlocks.body:
Corridor matters to a comparison because it decides how many genuinely different profiles IB Gram can actually put forward. Southern Peripheral Road, covering Sectors 66 to 72, Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and the Tata Primanti development, sits among the faster-growing parts of the city, and the resident tutor pool there is still catching up with demand. A family here asking for two or three home tutors to compare for a specific subject and tier may see a narrower shortlist than the same request from an older, more established part of Gurgaon.

New Gurgaon, running through Sectors 82 to 90, Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, with societies including Vatika India Next and Godrej Air, faces a similar pattern: strong demand from newly built residential towers, fewer tutors currently living close enough to commit to a weekly home visit. Comparing tutors here often means comparing one or two home profiles against an online specialist, rather than three home options side by side, and that is a fair comparison worth having rather than a compromise.

Dwarka Expressway, through Sectors 102 to 113, including Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, is growing fastest of the three and currently has the thinnest home tutor coverage. A shortlist here leans more heavily toward online tuition simply to keep the comparison meaningful; asking only for home options in this corridor for a specialist Extended-tier subject can mean waiting rather than comparing.

None of this means comparison is impossible in these corridors, only that it looks different: fewer home profiles, more online ones, and a wider net cast on tutor location since the specific society matters less once the format shifts to a screen rather than a doorstep.

contentBlocks.heading: Ask Every Shortlisted Tutor the Same Gurgaon School-Calendar Question
contentBlocks.body:
Whichever tutor a family eventually chooses, from Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali or DPS International Edge, the schools are named here only as local context. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and none of this states which curriculum or board any particular school follows.

When comparing two or three profiles, ask each one the same question about the school calendar: do they already know that a Gurgaon international school year typically opens in April, runs through a Diwali break in autumn, tightens around winter mocks or pre-boards, and closes with the exam series that follows. A tutor who answers vaguely is likely working from a generic syllabus sequence rather than a plan built around real dates.

Coursework portfolio deadlines, unit tests and report card timing vary between schools even within the same board, so a fair comparison includes asking how each shortlisted tutor plans to handle a week where two deadlines land close together. This is a more revealing question than asking about years of experience, since it tests whether the tutor actually plans around a school's calendar or simply teaches content in isolation from it.

A shortlisted tutor unfamiliar with a family's specific school is not automatically the wrong choice, but the gap should be named during comparison rather than discovered later, once a slot is already fixed.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Home Tutors Against Online Ones, Fairly
contentBlocks.body:
A fair comparison puts home tutoring first, since it is what most Gurgaon families ask for initially, then genuinely weighs online and hybrid options rather than treating them as a fallback. A home tutor working at the family's own table catches a wrong step in real time and suits younger Grade 9 students still building study habits, or subjects like Maths and sciences where watching handwritten working matters. When two home tutor profiles are shortlisted, compare them on teaching style during the trial, not just on stated experience.

Online tutors deserve an equally serious comparison, not a lesser one. A student wanting a specific Extended-tier specialist, or a family in a corridor with a thinner home tutor pool, is often better served comparing two online profiles than settling for whichever home tutor happens to be available. Online sessions also hold up better against Gurgaon's evening traffic: a home visit can be cancelled by a jam near Sohna Road or the Dwarka Expressway, while a video call rarely is.

Hybrid arrangements, comparing a tutor who offers one home session and one online session each week against a purely home or purely online alternative, suit families who want flexibility built in from the start rather than negotiated later. A student with an upcoming practical science assessment might value a hybrid tutor who can flex the format around lab preparation weeks.

The honest way to compare formats is through the trial itself: watch how a home tutor manages the physical space, and how an online tutor manages a shared screen and annotated past papers, before deciding which comparison actually matters more for that specific student.

contentBlocks.heading: What Separates a Verified Profile From a Guess?
contentBlocks.body:
Every profile IB Gram includes on a shortlist has already been checked for board experience, the specific subjects and tiers taught, and familiarity with the syllabus a student's school actually follows. That check is a starting point for comparison, not the end of it, and IB Gram tells families directly what else to look for when two or three profiles sit side by side.

Ask each shortlisted tutor the same specific questions: how long have they taught Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifically, which tier, Core or Extended, have they most recently prepared a student for, and can they describe how a recent student's grade or confidence actually changed. Comparing vague answers against specific ones is often more revealing than comparing years of experience on paper. Before a home visit, confirm photo identification for whichever tutor the family leans toward, and register that visitor in advance if the society runs its own gate desk.

The trial sessions themselves are where a verified profile earns its place on the shortlist for real. Watch how each tutor handles the same kind of wrong answer: does one walk back through the method while the other simply corrects it. Ask both the same question about their plan for the first month, and compare how each answer adjusts, or does not, once the school's actual test calendar comes up.

No paper check replaces this comparison. IB Gram verifies what is checkable in advance, board experience, subject and tier, but the difference between two verified tutors only becomes clear once both have actually taught the student, which is exactly what the trial comparison is for.

contentBlocks.heading: How to Trial Two Tutors Without Rattling Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Running two trial sessions with two different tutors sounds more disruptive than it usually is, provided it is handled openly rather than as a secret audition. Tell the student in advance that this is a comparison, not a test they can fail; framing it as helping choose the right fit, rather than judging the student, keeps the process calm. Space the two trials a few days apart rather than back to back, so the student is not comparing two strangers on the same afternoon and getting fatigued by it.

Keep the content roughly comparable across both trials where possible: the same topic, the same recent test paper, or the same syllabus section, so the comparison is about teaching approach rather than which tutor happened to get an easier starting point. Notice concrete things rather than vague impressions: did the tutor ask the student to explain their own working, did they adjust when something was not landing, did they leave the student with a clear next step. A parent comparing two trials on who my child liked more alone misses most of what actually predicts whether a match will hold up over a term.

If the family is comparing a home trial against an online one, keep that difference in mind rather than judging both purely on teaching content; a home tutor's trial should also show how they handle the physical space and the family's routine, while an online tutor's trial should show command of the shared screen and materials.

Once both trials are done, decide within a few days rather than letting the comparison drift. If neither tutor feels right, that is useful information too, and IB Gram will put forward a further profile rather than pushing a family toward whichever trial happened to go marginally better. Two trials in the first fortnight beats months of uncertainty with a single tutor who was never quite right.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging Two Shortlisted Tutors After the First Month in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A month into IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon, whichever tutor was chosen from the shortlist, progress should be visible in small ways before it shows in a test score. A student bringing school homework to the session unprompted, or explaining a method out loud rather than performing it silently, is progress worth noticing. If the family compared two tutors before choosing, it is fair to keep half an eye on whether the comparison actually predicted the right outcome, not to second-guess the decision but to sharpen the next one if a switch is ever needed.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and that holds regardless of how thorough the comparison was beforehand. What a good comparison can reasonably promise is a clearer sense of teaching style, board experience and fit than choosing blind would have given. If a chosen tutor shows no real change after a month, roughly four to six sessions, that is worth raising directly with IB Gram; the earlier comparison process, the trial notes, the questions asked, becomes useful again at this point, since it usually points toward what a replacement profile should differ on.

Honest limits still apply. A well-compared tutor cannot rebuild months of a shaky foundation in the weeks before an exam series, and no comparison process changes that. Some students, particularly those managing several subjects at once, need occasional sessions rather than a weekly commitment at all, and a good tutor says so even after winning the comparison.

Asking for a shortlist rather than a single tutor takes the same first step: a query or a free consultation call describing board, tier if known, grade, subject, and the corridor or society the family lives in. Say explicitly that you want to compare two or three profiles rather than accept the first one offered; IB Gram builds shortlists this way by default for families searching for IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon, but naming the preference clearly speeds things along.

Before the first trials, gather the same materials a single-tutor family would: the current textbook, a recent test paper with the student's own working on it, and the school's scheme of work if available. Having identical materials ready for both trial sessions makes the comparison fairer, since both tutors are working from the same starting picture rather than one having more to go on than the other.

Plan for two trial sessions, spaced a few days apart, rather than assuming the first one will obviously be right. Use the questions raised earlier, board experience, tier history, how each plans the first month, to compare notes afterward rather than relying on impression alone. If neither profile feels right, ask IB Gram for another rather than settling.

Availability across corridors and subjects varies, so a family asking early in a term gets a wider, more genuinely comparable shortlist than one asking two weeks before mocks. The only step that has to happen first is sending that initial query.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon cost when comparing a shortlist?
faqs.answer: Cost varies by profile even within one shortlist, since fees for IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon depend on the tutor's experience, subject, tier and whether sessions run at home or online; no rupee figures appear on this page. Comparing two or three profiles usually means comparing a range rather than a single number, and a shortlist deliberately including a mix of experience levels gives families a genuine choice on value, not just on teaching style. A tutor charging more is not automatically the better match; ask what the fee includes, one-to-one attention, feedback after each session, and board and tier fit, and weigh that against the specific student's needs rather than picking the cheaper or costlier option by default.

faqs.question: How many tutors should actually be on a shortlist?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually the right number; fewer rarely gives a real choice, and more becomes difficult for a family and student to fairly compare within a reasonable time. IB Gram deliberately selects profiles that differ meaningfully, in experience, teaching style, availability or format, rather than three near-identical options that make comparison pointless. A shortlist of exactly two works well when a family already has a strong preference on format, home or online, while three suits a family still deciding between formats as well as between individuals. Asking for more than three usually slows the decision down without adding useful information.

faqs.question: What should I actually compare between two shortlisted tutors?
faqs.answer: Compare board experience specific to Cambridge or Edexcel, which tier, Core or Extended, each has most recently taught, how familiar each is with your child's specific school calendar, and the realism of their slot and travel for your corridor. Beyond the profile itself, compare how each performs in a trial session: whether they diagnose before teaching, how they handle a wrong answer, and whether they leave the student with a clear next step. Avoid comparing purely on years of experience or on personality alone; a tutor a student instantly likes is not automatically the one who will hold up best over a full term of IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon.

faqs.question: Does online tuition compare fairly against a home tutor on a shortlist?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided both are judged on the same criteria, board and tier fit, teaching approach in the trial, and realistic scheduling, rather than judging online against a home-tutor standard by default. Online tuition suits a student who focuses well on a screen and a family wanting access to a specific specialist regardless of corridor, while a home tutor suits a younger student or one who needs someone physically present. A fair shortlist sometimes mixes one home and one online profile specifically so the family can compare the two formats directly through trials, rather than assuming in advance which one will suit the student better.

faqs.question: What if neither shortlisted tutor works out after the trial?
faqs.answer: Ask IB Gram for a further profile rather than settling for whichever trial went marginally better. Two disappointing trials usually still produce useful information, what specifically did not work, pace, teaching style, subject depth or simple personality fit, and that information sharpens the next shortlist considerably. It is more common than families expect for a third profile to be the one that actually fits, since the first two trials often reveal preferences the family had not articulated clearly at intake. There is no limit on how many profiles a family can see before choosing; the goal is a good match, not a fast decision at any cost.

faqs.question: Can I compare tutors if we are switching from CBSE or ICSE to IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth comparing shortlisted tutors specifically on how they would approach a mid-year board switch, since IGCSE's Cambridge or Edexcel structure, Core and Extended tiering, and paper formats do not map directly from CBSE or ICSE assessment. Ask each tutor how they would diagnose gaps in the first session rather than simply continuing forward from the current topic. Maths and sciences tend to transition faster than English, where the specific reading and writing demands of a Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus take longer to settle into, so a shortlist built for a board switch is often worth weighting toward English specialists in particular.

faqs.question: How do I run two trial lessons without confusing my child?
faqs.answer: Tell the student clearly in advance that this is a comparison to find the right fit, not a test either tutor can fail, and space the two trials a few days apart rather than scheduling them back to back. Keep the content roughly similar across both, the same topic or a recent test paper, so the comparison is about teaching approach rather than one tutor getting an easier starting point. Most students adapt to this quickly once they understand the purpose; confusion usually comes from ambiguity about what is happening, not from meeting two tutors. Decide within a few days of both trials so the process does not drag on longer than it needs to.

faqs.question: Will comparing tutors delay how soon sessions actually start in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A little, since fitting in two trial sessions rather than one adds a few days, but the delay is usually short and worth it against months with a poorly matched tutor. Families asking early in a term, rather than close to mocks, typically compare and decide within a week to ten days without losing meaningful time. For a family in a corridor such as Southern Peripheral Road or Dwarka Expressway, where the tutor pool is thinner, comparing may naturally take a little longer simply because fewer profiles are available to compare in the first place, not because the comparison process itself is slow.

faqs.question: How do I know if a tutor's profile is genuinely verified?
faqs.answer: IB Gram checks board experience, subject and tier, and syllabus familiarity before a profile is ever shortlisted, but ask each tutor directly during the trial to confirm the same details in their own words, and compare the specificity of the answers. A verified profile should be able to describe recent teaching experience concretely, which tier, which syllabus code, roughly how many students at that level, rather than speaking in generalities. Photo identification should be confirmed before a home visit, and a gated society visited for the first time should have the visitor registered in advance. No document fully replaces watching a tutor actually teach during the trial.

faqs.question: What if one shortlisted tutor seems much cheaper than the other?
faqs.answer: A lower fee is not automatically a worse match, and a higher one is not automatically better; compare what each fee reflects instead. A newer tutor may charge less while still being genuinely well matched on board and tier, while a more experienced tutor's higher fee may reflect examining experience or a track record with a specific specialist syllabus. Ask both directly what the fee includes, session length, feedback frequency, materials, and weigh that against what the trial actually showed about teaching quality. Price is one input into the comparison, not the deciding one on its own.

faqs.question: Do I need to be home for both home trial sessions?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, though sitting in on at least one home trial helps you judge teaching approach directly rather than relying only on your child's account afterward. For a home trial, a quiet study space free of siblings and television noise matters more than a parent physically present throughout; for an online trial, being within earshot works well without needing to be on camera. If comparing two home tutors specifically, being present for both, even briefly, makes the comparison more consistent, since you are judging both against the same standard of observation rather than one from the room and one from your child's report.

faqs.question: What happens if a tutor travelling to our sector for a home trial gets delayed?
faqs.answer: The home session gets rescheduled directly with that tutor, and it rarely disrupts the overall comparison as long as both trials still happen within a reasonably close window. Gurgaon traffic can delay a home visit, particularly along Golf Course Road, Sohna Road or the newer expressway corridors after 6pm, and a tutor running seriously late will usually flag it rather than arrive rushed and distracted. If a school event clashes with one of the two planned home sessions, moving it by a few days keeps the comparison fair rather than forcing a rushed visit that does not really show what that tutor can do.

IB Gram deliberately selects profiles that differ meaningfully, in experience, teaching style, availability or format, rather than three near-identical options that make comparison pointless. A shortlist of exactly two works well when a family already has a strong preference on format, home or online, while three suits a family still deciding between formats as well as between individuals. Asking for more than three usually slows the decision down without adding useful information.

mainEntity.name: What should I actually compare between two shortlisted tutors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compare board experience specific to Cambridge or Edexcel, which tier, Core or Extended, each has most recently taught, how familiar each is with your child's specific school calendar, and the realism of their slot and travel for your corridor. Beyond the profile itself, compare how each performs in a trial session: whether they diagnose before teaching, how they handle a wrong answer, and whether they leave the student with a clear next step. Avoid comparing purely on years of experience or on personality alone; a tutor a student instantly likes is not automatically the one who will hold up best over a full term of IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon.

mainEntity.name: Does online tuition compare fairly against a home tutor on a shortlist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, provided both are judged on the same criteria, board and tier fit, teaching approach in the trial, and realistic scheduling, rather than judging online against a home-tutor standard by default. Online tuition suits a student who focuses well on a screen and a family wanting access to a specific specialist regardless of corridor, while a home tutor suits a younger student or one who needs someone physically present. A fair shortlist sometimes mixes one home and one online profile specifically so the family can compare the two formats directly through trials, rather than assuming in advance which one will suit the student better.

mainEntity.name: What if neither shortlisted tutor works out after the trial?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask IB Gram for a further profile rather than settling for whichever trial went marginally better. Two disappointing trials usually still produce useful information, what specifically did not work, pace, teaching style, subject depth or simple personality fit, and that information sharpens the next shortlist considerably. It is more common than families expect for a third profile to be the one that actually fits, since the first two trials often reveal preferences the family had not articulated clearly at intake. There is no limit on how many profiles a family can see before choosing; the goal is a good match, not a fast decision at any cost.

mainEntity.name: Can I compare tutors if we are switching from CBSE or ICSE to IGCSE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is worth comparing shortlisted tutors specifically on how they would approach a mid-year board switch, since IGCSE's Cambridge or Edexcel structure, Core and Extended tiering, and paper formats do not map directly from CBSE or ICSE assessment. Ask each tutor how they would diagnose gaps in the first session rather than simply continuing forward from the current topic. Maths and sciences tend to transition faster than English, where the specific reading and writing demands of a Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus take longer to settle into, so a shortlist built for a board switch is often worth weighting toward English specialists in particular.

mainEntity.name: How do I run two trial lessons without confusing my child?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell the student clearly in advance that this is a comparison to find the right fit, not a test either tutor can fail, and space the two trials a few days apart rather than scheduling them back to back. Keep the content roughly similar across both, the same topic or a recent test paper, so the comparison is about teaching approach rather than one tutor getting an easier starting point. Most students adapt to this quickly once they understand the purpose; confusion usually comes from ambiguity about what is happening, not from meeting two tutors. Decide within a few days of both trials so the process does not drag on longer than it needs to.

mainEntity.name: Will comparing tutors delay how soon sessions actually start in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: A little, since fitting in two trial sessions rather than one adds a few days, but the delay is usually short and worth it against months with a poorly matched tutor. Families asking early in a term, rather than close to mocks, typically compare and decide within a week to ten days without losing meaningful time. For a family in a corridor such as Southern Peripheral Road or Dwarka Expressway, where the tutor pool is thinner, comparing may naturally take a little longer simply because fewer profiles are available to compare in the first place, not because the comparison process itself is slow.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a tutor's profile is genuinely verified?

acceptedAnswer.text: IB Gram checks board experience, subject and tier, and syllabus familiarity before a profile is ever shortlisted, but ask each tutor directly during the trial to confirm the same details in their own words, and compare the specificity of the answers. A verified profile should be able to describe recent teaching experience concretely, which tier, which syllabus code, roughly how many students at that level, rather than speaking in generalities. Photo identification should be confirmed before a home visit, and a gated society visited for the first time should have the visitor registered in advance. No document fully replaces watching a tutor actually teach during the trial.

mainEntity.name: What if one shortlisted tutor seems much cheaper than the other?

acceptedAnswer.text: A lower fee is not automatically a worse match, and a higher one is not automatically better; compare what each fee reflects instead. A newer tutor may charge less while still being genuinely well matched on board and tier, while a more experienced tutor's higher fee may reflect examining experience or a track record with a specific specialist syllabus. Ask both directly what the fee includes, session length, feedback frequency, materials, and weigh that against what the trial actually showed about teaching quality. Price is one input into the comparison, not the deciding one on its own.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to be home for both home trial sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily, though sitting in on at least one home trial helps you judge teaching approach directly rather than relying only on your child's account afterward. For a home trial, a quiet study space free of siblings and television noise matters more than a parent physically present throughout; for an online trial, being within earshot works well without needing to be on camera. If comparing two home tutors specifically, being present for both, even briefly, makes the comparison more consistent, since you are judging both against the same standard of observation rather than one from the room and one from your child's report.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a tutor travelling to our sector for a home trial gets delayed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The home session gets rescheduled directly with that tutor, and it rarely disrupts the overall comparison as long as both trials still happen within a reasonably close window. Gurgaon traffic can delay a home visit, particularly along Golf Course Road, Sohna Road or the newer expressway corridors after 6pm, and a tutor running seriously late will usually flag it rather than arrive rushed and distracted. If a school event clashes with one of the two planned home sessions, moving it by a few days keeps the comparison fair rather than forcing a rushed visit that does not really show what that tutor can do.

Tell IB Gram your child's board, grade, subject and corridor, and trial sessions will be arranged so you can compare directly before committing to a weekly slot. Comparing tutors properly starts before any trial lesson happens. Two or three tutors come back, chosen to be genuinely different from each other, not near-duplicates. One might have deep Extended Mathematics experience but a tighter weekday schedule. Another might have more flexible evenings but less recent exam-series experience. A third might already teach in the family's own corridor, cutting travel time to almost nothing. Comparing three tutors who all say the same thing about themselves defeats the purpose; a good shortlist gives you real trade-offs to weigh.

Every name on that shortlist has already cleared IB Gram's own checks on subject background, teaching experience and identity. That is a floor, not a verdict. A profile can read perfectly and still not suit a particular student, which is exactly what the trial stage is for, covered later on this page.

Once a family picks, the chosen tutor is confirmed for a weekly slot, subject to availability, and the arrangement can run at home, online or a mix depending on what the trial showed. The shortlist itself is not thrown away either; if the first choice does not hold up, a second name from the same list, or a fresh one, is the next step.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: What Must Every Shortlisted Tutor Know?
contentBlocks.body:
Start here, because it filters out half of a weak shortlist immediately. Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are both two-year courses across Grade 9 and Grade 10, usually followed by the IB Diploma Programme (IB DP), A Levels, or a return to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. They are not interchangeable from a tutor's point of view. Ask directly which board a candidate has actually taught, not just examined casually.

The exam calendars differ. Cambridge runs three series a year: February/March, offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits exams in January and May/June. Grading differs as well: Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some subjects now on a 9-1 scale under separate codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. A tutor's answer to which series their students have actually sat says more than a general claim of years of experience.

Tiering is the next filter. Most Cambridge subjects split into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, reaching A* but demanding more independent work. The school decides this, usually partway through Grade 9. Two shortlisted tutors who both say they teach IGCSE Maths can still be wrong for each other's tier.

None of this is complicated once it is laid out plainly, which is exactly why it belongs at the start of any comparison. A shortlisted profile that cannot answer board, series and tier clearly has not earned its place on the list.

contentBlocks.heading: Testing Subject Depth Across Maths, Science and English
contentBlocks.body:
Subject depth is where a shortlist genuinely separates itself. For Mathematics, Cambridge IGCSE 0580 splits Core candidates into Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), and Extended candidates into Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator), from the 2025 exams onward. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, runs Foundation or Higher tier, two calculator papers each. Ask a shortlisted tutor to walk through a non-calculator method on the spot; the answer tells you more than a CV line ever could.

For the sciences, Cambridge syllabuses examined from 2023 split into Paper 1 or Paper 2 for multiple choice by tier, Paper 3 or Paper 4 for theory, and either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, chosen by the school. The split runs 30% multiple choice, 50% theory, 20% practical. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, assessed through Paper 1 and Paper 2, with practical skills folded into the written paper rather than tested separately. A tutor who does not know which of these your school uses is guessing at half the syllabus.

English is the subject where a shortlist most often reveals a mismatch. Cambridge offers First Language English 0500 (reading, then directed writing and composition or a coursework portfolio), English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511, where 0511 grades speaking and 0510 reports it separately, and Literature in English 0475. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). A tutor strong on 0500 composition is not automatically the right choice for a 0511 candidate being marked on speaking.

Put these questions to every name on the shortlist, the same questions each time. It is the fastest way to separate a genuinely specialised tutor from one who is comfortable only in general terms.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Trial, Online Trial or Both: How Do You Choose Fairly?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring leads on every shortlist IB Gram builds: a verified tutor teaching the student at their own desk, in their own home. For comparing two or three tutors, a home trial is the clearest test available, because it shows the tutor working in the actual room the student will study in every week, not a tidy demo elsewhere.

Online trials trade that directness for convenience. If two shortlisted tutors live in different corridors, say one near Golf Course Road and one who would be commuting from Manesar, trialling both online in the same week is often the only realistic way to compare them quickly. What online cannot show as well is how a tutor manages a distracted student without being able to point directly at the page.

A hybrid pattern, home sessions as the default with an occasional online session when travel is genuinely difficult, particularly relevant for a Manesar or Old Gurgaon address, tends to be where families land once the shortlist narrows to one name. It keeps the personal contact of a home tutor while giving both sides a fallback.

For a fair comparison specifically, try to run at least one trial of each format rather than judging entirely on one mode. A tutor who shines online might be even better in person, or vice versa, and the only way to know is to actually see both.

Whichever mode wins the trial, tell the tutor plainly what tipped the decision. A tutor who knows they were chosen for their home manner, rather than their screen presence, can lean into that strength deliberately from the first proper session onward, instead of guessing at what the family valued.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Interview Two IGCSE Tutors Without Picking the Wrong One?
contentBlocks.body:
Treat the trial stage like a short, honest interview rather than an audition either tutor could simply charm their way through. Tell the student plainly that two or three tutors are being tried this week and why; students generally cope with this better than parents expect, once it is explained as normal rather than hidden.

Use one checklist across every trial, asked in the same order each time: did the tutor find out what the student already knew before teaching anything new; did they explain a wrong answer rather than simply correct it; did they set one small, specific task for next time; did they answer a direct syllabus question without vagueness; and did their pace and manner suit this particular student, whether quiet, restless, confident or anxious.

Space the trials out, a few days apart rather than the same evening, so the comparison is based on memory of two distinct sessions rather than a blur. Write down two or three notes after each one while it is still fresh; a week later, the details blur more than parents expect.

If neither trial convinces you, that is a useful result, not wasted time. Say plainly what was missing, too passive, too rushed, wrong tone for a nervous student, and ask for a fresh name. And if a tutor who passed the trial later stops working out mid-term, the same logic applies: switch once, early, rather than let a poor fit run for months.

contentBlocks.heading: Six Weeks In: Has the Comparison Paid Off?
contentBlocks.body:
Once the shortlist has done its job and one tutor is confirmed, the first weeks are about settling in, not about a dramatic jump in marks. Expect the first two or three sessions to be diagnostic: finding the actual gaps against the syllabus, not assuming the profile told the whole story.

By four to six weeks, look for concrete signs: the student naming a specific paper or topic instead of saying it was fine, a folder of marked work building up, and a touch more confidence in the next school test. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and how fast this shows depends on the gap the student started from, not on how carefully the shortlist was built, though a careful shortlist does shorten the odds of a wasted month.

If nothing has moved by six weeks, that is a direct conversation first with the tutor, since pacing issues are often fixable, and with IB Gram second if they are not. This is one of the honest limits worth stating plainly: even the best-compared shortlist cannot promise a fixed timeline for every student.

Starting the whole comparison process close to a mock or the exam session narrows what any tutor can achieve, however well they were shortlisted. A comparison run weeks or months ahead of that pressure point has far more room to work with, simply because there is time left to act on whatever the first few weeks reveal.

faqs.question: Does personality matter as much as subject knowledge when comparing tutors?

faqs.question: How many subjects can be compared and shortlisted at the same time?

faqs.question: Does comparing tutors online work as well as comparing them in person?

Online trials are genuinely useful for comparing tutors quickly across different parts of Gurgaon, say one near Golf Course Road and one based near Manesar, without the travel time that in-person trials require. faqs.question: What should be ready before the first comparison trial?
faqs.answer: A recent school test paper or a sample of current work, a phone photo is fine, plus a plain answer to what the student finds hardest right now. This gives each shortlisted tutor something concrete to respond to in the first twenty minutes instead of guessing at the starting point.
