contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Shortlists IGCSE Home Tuitions in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist starts with a short conversation, not a form to fill and forget. IB Gram asks which board your child follows, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, which subjects need support, whether the school has already placed the student on a Core or Extended tier, and which corridor of Gurgaon the family lives in. Weekday evenings, weekend slots, exam dates already on the school calendar, and whether the family wants a home tutor, online lessons or a mix of both, all shape who gets shortlisted.

Two or three profiles come back, and they are chosen to differ from each other on purpose. One tutor might have stronger Extended Mathematics experience and less time free on weekdays; another might have a lighter weekday schedule but less experience with Pearson Edexcel's Higher tier papers. A third might specialise in English as a Second Language rather than First Language English. The point of sending more than one profile is to give you a real choice, not three tutors who all say the same thing about themselves.

Every profile shortlisted has already been through IB Gram's own verification before it reaches a parent: subject background, teaching experience, and the checks covered later on this page. That does not replace your own judgement. A profile reads well on paper; a trial lesson tells you whether the tutor explains a mark scheme clearly, whether the student relaxes or stiffens up, and whether the pace suits a Grade 9 student differently from a Grade 10 student close to the exam session.

Once the family picks a tutor from the shortlist, IB Gram confirms the weekly slot and the subject focus, and whether home tuition continues at the same pace or moves online for a stretch, subject to tutor availability. A different tutor from the same shortlist, or a fresh one, can replace the first choice if the fit turns out to be wrong once lessons start.
items: 1. Share the board, subject, level and weekday schedule in a short query or consultation call.
2. IB Gram checks tutor availability across the requested Gurgaon corridor and syllabus.
3. Two or three shortlisted profiles are sent with subject and tier experience noted.
4. Trial lessons are arranged with each shortlisted tutor, at home, online or both.
5. The family confirms one tutor, and a different profile can replace an early mismatch.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: What Should Your IGCSE Shortlist Cover?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon almost always means one of two boards: Cambridge IGCSE, set by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Both run as a two-year course across Grade 9 and Grade 10 at most international schools here, and most students move on to the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IB DP), A Levels, or back into CBSE or ISC for Class 11. A tutor who has taught one board for years is not automatically ready for the other; the syllabus codes, paper structures and command terms differ enough that switching mid-course is its own small project.

Cambridge runs three exam series a year: February/March, which is offered only in India among Cambridge's international centres, plus the May/June and October/November series most schools use for the main session. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and May/June. Grading differs too. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, though a handful of subjects now use a 9-1 scale under separate codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. When you compare two shortlisted tutors, ask plainly which series their past students actually sat, because a tutor who has only prepared students for May/June may be less useful if your child is entering the February/March window.

Most Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers. Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A* but is harder and assumes more independent work. This decision, usually made by the school partway through Grade 9, changes what a tutor should be teaching towards. A shortlisted profile should say which tier the tutor has actually taught, not just which subject.

None of this needs to be theoretical for you. When IB Gram sends a shortlist, each profile states the board, the tier experience and the exam series the tutor has prepared students for. Comparing those three facts side by side, before a single trial lesson, rules out an obvious mismatch early and saves everyone a wasted first session.
items: Cambridge IGCSE runs February/March, May/June and October/November exam series
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May/June series only
Core tier tops out at grade C; Extended tier reaches A*
Ask which exam series and tier each shortlisted tutor has taught
Most students move to IB DP, A Levels, CBSE or ISC after Grade 10

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Maths, Science and English Depth Across Profiles
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits by tier from the 2025 exams onward: Core candidates sit Paper 1, which is non-calculator, and Paper 3, which allows a calculator; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator). Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier. When you compare tutor profiles for Maths specifically, ask which paper structure they have actually taught against; a tutor used to Edexcel's two-calculator-paper format needs a short adjustment period to teach Cambridge's non-calculator paper well.

Cambridge IGCSE sciences, in the syllabuses examined from 2023 onward, split into Paper 1 (multiple choice, Core) or Paper 2 (multiple choice, Extended), Paper 3 (theory, Core) or Paper 4 (theory, Extended), and a practical component through either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. The weighting runs 30% multiple choice, 50% theory and 20% practical. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2, and practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than as a separate component. A shortlisted profile should know which practical route the school uses, because coaching towards the wrong one wastes revision time.

English at IGCSE is not one syllabus but several. Cambridge offers First Language English 0500 (a reading paper, then directed writing and composition or a coursework portfolio), English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511 (0511 counts speaking into the final grade, 0510 reports speaking separately), and Literature in English 0475. Pearson Edexcel offers International GCSE English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). A tutor comfortable with 0500's composition paper is not automatically the right match for a family whose child sits 0511, where the spoken component is graded.

This is exactly the kind of detail that separates two shortlisted profiles who otherwise look similar on paper. IB Gram notes the exact syllabus code each tutor has taught most recently, so the comparison is about substance rather than a general claim of IGCSE experience.
items: Cambridge 0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator, Paper 4 calculator
Edexcel Maths 4MA1: Foundation or Higher, two calculator papers per tier
Cambridge sciences: Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical
0511 English as a Second Language grades speaking; 0510 reports it separately
Ask which exact syllabus code a shortlisted tutor has taught most recently

contentBlocks.heading: Where in Gurgaon These IGCSE Home Tuitions Reach
contentBlocks.body:
Golf Course Extension Road covers Sector 56 through Sector 60, Sector 62, Sector 65, Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, along with societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon. Weekday evening traffic on this stretch has grown thick as more towers have filled in, so a tutor already living or teaching along this corridor holds a real advantage over one commuting in from across the city. Society gate entry here typically means a visitor registration call ahead of the first visit; families who warn the gate desk in advance save the tutor five or ten minutes at the start of a session.

Sohna Road runs through Sector 47 to Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur, with societies including Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close. This corridor is long, and a tutor who covers Sector 47 comfortably may find Badshahpur, further down the same road, a genuinely longer evening drive. When comparing two shortlisted tutors for a Sohna Road address, ask specifically which stretch of the corridor each one already teaches in, not just whether they cover Sohna Road in general.

DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City together form a denser, more commercial corridor: DLF Phase 2, DLF Phase 3, DLF Phase 4, MG Road itself, Cyber City, Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur and Sectors 24, 27 and 28, alongside societies like DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona. Evening traffic through Cyber City and MG Road during office hours can eat into a scheduled slot, which is one reason families here often ask for a slightly later evening session or move one weekday lesson online.

IGCSE home tuitions in Gurgaon depend heavily on travel time within each corridor, which is why a shortlist built for one of these corridors weighs travel time as seriously as subject fit. Two tutors with identical Cambridge IGCSE Extended Mathematics experience are not equally good choices if one already has a Tuesday evening slot free in DLF Phase 3 and the other would be driving in from outside Gurgaon altogether.

International schools across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana run broadly similar academic years: a new term starting in April, a winter break around late December, half-term breaks tucked around festivals, and school-set mock examinations before the main IGCSE session. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. The pressure points that matter for a shortlist are predictable even without naming a specific school's calendar: unit tests every few weeks through Grade 9 and Grade 10, a set of mock exams roughly two to three months before the real session, and a run of school events, sports days and college counselling sessions that can eat into evenings without much notice. A tutor who has taught through a full Gurgaon academic year before knows to build slack into a term plan rather than assuming every week runs as scheduled.

Two shortlisted tutors can look identical on subject knowledge and still differ here. One might already expect the pre-mock crunch and plan lighter homework loads around it; another might need it explained. Asking a shortlisted tutor how they handled a previous student's mock season, during actual home tuition, is a more useful question than asking about qualifications alone.

None of this changes what IGCSE actually demands. It changes how a tuition plan is paced against the year the student is actually living through, which is exactly what a side-by-side comparison during trial lessons should surface.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: Which Trial Works Best for Comparing Tutors?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's lead service across every shortlist is home tutoring: a verified tutor teaching at the family's own home, in the sector or society where the student actually lives. For comparing two or three shortlisted tutors, home trial lessons are the clearest test: you see how the tutor manages the actual desk, actual siblings underfoot, and the specific distractions of a real Tuesday evening, not a tidy demo. Home sessions also let a parent sit in the next room for the first lesson, watching how the tutor and the student build rapport.

Online trial lessons trade that direct view for convenience. Comparing two tutors online in the same week is genuinely easier to schedule when both live outside the family's own corridor, and it removes the travel time that home tutoring depends on. What online cannot show you as clearly is how a tutor manages a distracted teenager without being able to point at the page directly, or how comfortable the student is having someone in the house rather than on a screen.

A hybrid arrangement, home lessons in term time with an online session dropped in during exam-heavy weeks or when travel is impractical, is what many families in Gurgaon settle on once the shortlist narrows to one tutor. It keeps the personal contact of home tuition while giving both sides a fallback when a society gate is closed for an event or when traffic on a corridor like Golf Course Extension Road makes a weekday evening trip unrealistic.

For the specific job of comparing a shortlist fairly, run at least one trial with each format if the family is genuinely undecided: one visit at home with the front-runner, and one online trial with the second choice, so travel and screen comfort are not the only variables deciding the outcome. Whichever format wins the trial, the same tutor can usually continue in that format or switch later, subject to availability.

Online trials suit comparing two tutors outside the family's own corridor quickly

contentBlocks.heading: How Are Gurgaon IGCSE Tutors Verified Before They Reach Your Shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Every profile IB Gram shortlists has already been checked on a few basics: subject background relevant to the syllabus taught, teaching experience at the level requested, and identity verification before a home visit is arranged. None of this is a guarantee of teaching quality on its own; it is the floor a profile has to clear before it reaches a parent at all.

What a parent should check personally, across every profile on the shortlist, goes further. Ask to see how the tutor explains a past paper question out loud during the trial, not just whether they can solve it. Ask which mark scheme or assessment criteria they actually mark against, since IGCSE examiners reward method and structure as much as a correct final answer. Ask how many students they have taken through the same syllabus code the child is sitting, not just IGCSE as a general label.

Comparing two verified profiles on these terms is far more useful than comparing two CVs. A tutor who explains their marking approach clearly during a twenty-minute trial has usually taught the syllabus long enough to know where students genuinely lose marks, which a written profile cannot show.

If something about a shortlisted profile does not add up once a trial has run, the honest step is to say so and ask for a different match rather than persist out of politeness. IB Gram can replace a tutor on the shortlist, or bring in a fresh profile entirely, if the fit is wrong.
items: Profiles are checked for subject background, teaching experience and identity before shortlisting
Ask during the trial which mark scheme or criteria the tutor marks against
Ask how many students the tutor has taught on this exact syllabus code
A twenty-minute trial reveals more about marking knowledge than a written profile
A different tutor can replace an early mismatch, subject to availability

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Run Two Trial Lessons Without Confusing Your Child?
contentBlocks.body:
Running two trial lessons in the same week works better than most parents expect, as long as the student is told plainly what is happening. Say it directly: we are trying two tutors this week to see who explains things better, rather than letting the child guess why a new face is at the dining table. Most students settle into this quickly once they understand it is not a test of them.

A short comparison checklist, applied to both trials the same way, keeps the decision from coming down to which tutor happened to be friendlier on the day: did the tutor ask what the student already knew before teaching anything new; did they explain a mistake rather than just correct it; did they leave the student with a specific, small task before the next session; did they answer a direct question about the syllabus or tier without vagueness; and did the timing and manner suit this particular child, quiet or talkative, rushed or unhurried.

Spacing the two trials a few days apart, rather than back to back on the same evening, gives the student room to actually compare rather than just remember whoever went second. It also lets a parent watch both sessions with a slightly clearer head.

If neither trial feels right, that is useful information, not a wasted week. Tell IB Gram plainly what was missing, too fast, too passive, wrong personality for a nervous student, and a fresh profile can be sent rather than settling for the better of two mediocre fits. Switching a tutor after a term has started is also entirely normal if progress genuinely stalls; better to change once than to let a mismatch run for months out of inertia.
items: Tell the student plainly why two different tutors are visiting this week
Space two trial lessons a few days apart rather than back to back
Check whether each tutor asked what the student already knew before teaching
Note whether a mistake was explained, not just corrected, during the trial
Ask for a fresh profile if neither trial fits, rather than settling

contentBlocks.heading: What Realistic Progress Looks Like After the First Month
contentBlocks.body:
Once a tutor is confirmed from the shortlist, the first month is mostly about the two of them finding a working rhythm, not about a visible jump in marks. Expect the first two or three sessions to be diagnostic: identifying which topics from the syllabus the student is shaky on, checking how they currently show working on a Maths paper or structure an English essay, and setting a realistic weekly pace.

A parent should see specific signs by four to six weeks in: the student mentioning a paper or topic by name rather than saying we did stuff, a folder of marked practice building up, and slightly more confidence asking a question in the next school test rather than staying quiet. None of these are guaranteed on any fixed timetable, and no tutor can guarantee a grade; students progress at different speeds depending on the gap they started from and how much independent practice happens between sessions.

If nothing has changed after a month and a half beyond the two sessions a week, that is worth a direct conversation with the tutor first, since a pacing mismatch is often fixable, and with IB Gram second, if it is not. This is one of the honest limits of tutoring: a tutor can teach well and a student can still need more time than a school's own timetable allows before results show.

Starting late, close to a mock or the exam session itself, narrows what any tutor can realistically fix. A shortlist and trial process built weeks or months ahead of a mock gives far more room to work with than one built two weeks before it.
items: Expect the first two or three sessions to be mostly diagnostic, not corrective
Look for the student naming specific topics and a growing folder of marked work
No tutor can guarantee a grade; progress speed varies by student
Raise a pacing concern directly with the tutor before asking for a change
Starting close to mocks narrows what any tutor can realistically achieve

contentBlocks.heading: Starting With Your Shortlisted IGCSE Home Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started is a short, unglamorous list rather than anything dramatic. Send a query through the site or book a free consultation, and be ready to say which board, which subjects, what grade, and roughly what a workable weekday evening slot looks like in your corridor, since this shapes which home tutor ends up on the shortlist.

Before the first trial lesson, have the student's recent school test papers or a sample of current work on hand; even a photo on a phone is enough for the first conversation. It gives a shortlisted tutor something concrete to react to instead of guessing at the starting point from a general description.

The first home session itself usually opens with a short conversation rather than diving straight into content: what the student finds hardest right now, what the school has already covered, and when the next test or mock falls. A demo or trial session can be arranged with more than one shortlisted tutor before the family commits to a term, and lessons continue at home, online or hybrid depending on what the trial showed worked.

If the first match is not right once real sessions begin, say so. A different tutor from the same shortlist, or a new profile altogether, can pick up where the last one left off, subject to availability, without treating the switch as a failure on anyone's part.

Most families reach a decision within one or two weeks of the first query, once both trial lessons have run and the checklist from earlier on this page has been applied honestly. There is no need to rush the choice faster than that; a slightly slower, better-compared start tends to hold up better over a full term than a fast, uncompared one.
items: Share board, subject, grade and a workable weekday evening slot upfront
Have recent test papers or sample work ready for the first trial
The first home session opens with a conversation, not straight into content
A trial or demo session can run with more than one shortlisted tutor
A different profile can continue where an early mismatch left off

faqs.question: How does IB Gram build a shortlist instead of sending just one IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: IB Gram sends two or three verified profiles rather than one, chosen to differ on purpose in board experience, tier taught and weekday availability, so there is something real to compare. IGCSE home tuitions in Gurgaon are shortlisted this way specifically so a family compares real options, not just whoever replied first. After an intake conversation covering the board, subject, level and schedule, each profile in the shortlist states the exam series and tier the tutor has actually taught, not a general claim of IGCSE experience. A trial lesson is then arranged with each shortlisted tutor before the family commits to a term, and the family chooses with real evidence rather than guesswork.

faqs.question: Can I run trial lessons with more than one tutor before deciding?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the whole point of a shortlist. A trial lesson can be arranged with each shortlisted tutor, ideally spaced a few days apart rather than back to back, so the comparison is fair to both the tutors and the student. Tell the student plainly that two different tutors are visiting this week so nobody is confused about why. Use a simple, consistent checklist across both trials: whether the tutor asked what the student already knew, whether a mistake was explained rather than just corrected, and whether the pace suited this particular child. The family decides afterward, and there is no obligation to continue with either trial tutor if neither is right.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we picked from the shortlist is not working out?
faqs.answer: Say so directly rather than waiting out a term hoping it improves. IB Gram can bring back a different profile from the original shortlist or send a fresh one, and switching after a few weeks is a normal part of getting the match right, not a failure. Be specific about what was missing, too fast a pace, too passive in the room, wrong personality for a nervous student, since that detail helps the next match land better than a vague complaint would. A short transition period is normal while a new tutor gets up to speed on exactly where the student left off, and a parent should expect one or two sessions of re-diagnosis before ordinary lessons resume.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor really need to travel to Sohna Road or Golf Course Extension Road every week?
faqs.answer: Yes, for lessons run at home, though the honest answer includes a trade-off worth knowing. Both corridors run long and see heavy weekday evening traffic, so a tutor already teaching in that stretch of Sohna Road or Golf Course Extension Road is a more reliable weekly fit than one commuting in from a different part of Gurgaon. When comparing shortlisted profiles for either corridor, ask specifically which sectors or societies each tutor already covers rather than assuming coverage of the whole stretch equally. If travel genuinely becomes unreliable on a given week, moving that one session online rather than cancelling it outright usually keeps the student's pace on track.

faqs.question: Is a parent expected to sit in during a home trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Not required, but sitting in on the first home trial is a good idea, especially with a younger or more anxious student. Watching one session with each shortlisted tutor gives a parent a direct sense of rapport and teaching style that a written profile cannot show, and most tutors expect a parent nearby for a first visit in any case. After the trial stage, many families step back and let the tutor and student work independently, checking in with a short update after each session rather than sitting through every lesson. Whether to stay depends on the child; a student who works better without an audience should be given that space once trust has been established.

faqs.question: What happens if a scheduled home session is missed because of traffic or a society lockdown?
faqs.answer: The session is usually rescheduled rather than lost, by agreement between the family and the tutor directly. Gurgaon corridors such as DLF Phase 3 and MG Road see genuine weekday evening congestion, and society gates occasionally restrict entry during events, so a missed slot is not unusual and is not treated as a broken arrangement. Some families keep a standing backup: if a home session cannot happen, that week's lesson runs online instead so momentum is not lost entirely. Repeated missed sessions on one side are worth raising directly, since a pattern is different from an occasional traffic delay or gate closure.

faqs.question: How is a Cambridge IGCSE shortlist different from a Pearson Edexcel one?
faqs.answer: The shortlisted profiles differ because the boards themselves differ in structure. A Cambridge shortlist should show tutors who know the Core and Extended tier split and the specific paper numbers for the subject in question, such as Paper 2 and Paper 4 for Extended Mathematics. A Pearson Edexcel shortlist should show tutors familiar with the Foundation and Higher tiers and codes like 4MA1 for Mathematics. IB Gram asks which board the student follows before building either shortlist, so the comparison is between tutors who genuinely teach that board rather than a general IGCSE label. Getting this wrong at the shortlist stage is the single most common cause of a mismatched trial lesson.

faqs.question: Should I compare tutors on subject knowledge alone, or does personality matter too?
faqs.answer: Personality matters as much as subject knowledge, if not more, for a student who will be working with this tutor weekly for months. Two shortlisted tutors can know the syllabus equally well and still suit very different students: one might explain patiently and slowly, which a quieter student needs, while the other moves briskly through material, which suits a confident student who gets bored easily. Use the trial lesson to watch how the tutor responds when the student gets something wrong, since that moment reveals more about fit than any qualification list. A shortlist that only compares subject depth and ignores this is missing half the decision.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can be compared and shortlisted at once?
faqs.answer: As many as the family needs, though most requests IB Gram handles involve one or two subjects at a time. A separate shortlist and trial process typically runs for each subject, since a strong Mathematics tutor and a strong English tutor are rarely the same person, and comparing them together would confuse rather than clarify the decision. Families juggling three or four subjects at once, especially close to mocks, sometimes stagger the shortlist process by a week or two per subject rather than running everything simultaneously, which keeps trial lessons from overwhelming the student's evenings all at once.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work as well as home tuition when comparing options?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is being compared for. Online tutoring removes travel time and can make it easier to trial two tutors from different parts of Gurgaon in the same week, which is genuinely useful during the comparison stage itself. What it does not replicate as well is the in-person read on rapport that a home trial gives, particularly for a younger student or one who is anxious about a new tutor. Many families use one home trial and one online trial specifically to compare both formats before deciding, rather than assuming one is simply better than the other across the board.

faqs.question: What should I have ready before the first trial lesson with a shortlisted tutor?
faqs.answer: A recent school test paper or a sample of current work, even a phone photo, along with a plain answer to what the student finds hardest right now. This gives the tutor something concrete to react to in the first twenty minutes rather than starting from a guess. It also helps if the family can say roughly when the next school test or mock falls, since that shapes how much of the first session should be diagnostic versus focused on an immediate deadline. None of this needs to be formal; a short conversation before the tutor arrives covers most of it.

h1: IGCSE Private Tutors in Gurgaon: How to Compare and Shortlist
heroTitle: Comparing IGCSE Private Tutors in Gurgaon Side by Side
heroSubtitle: Most families hire the first tutor who answers the phone. Two or three profiles, compared on the same five points and tested with the same trial task, produce a better match and a shorter argument later. This page is the method, not a sales pitch.
introSummary: If you are weighing up IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon, the useful question is not who is available but who you should compare, and against what. Nearly every family here starts with home tuition, so the shortlist is a mix of teaching quality and plain logistics: who can actually hold your evening in your sector, week after week. A shortlist of two or three verified profiles, judged on board experience, level taught, familiarity with your child's school pattern, and the slot each tutor can genuinely keep, will tell you more in a week than a month of asking around. Below is how that shortlist gets built, what to look for line by line on each profile, how to run trial lessons with more than one tutor without unsettling your child, and what to do when the first choice turns out to be wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: How is a shortlist of two or three IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon built?
contentBlocks.body:
It is built by narrowing on four filters in order: the exact syllabus and tier, the level and grade taught, the evenings and format that suit your household, and the corridor the tutor already works in. Two or three names survive all four. More than three is not a shortlist, it is a phone directory.

The sequence runs like this.
1. You send a query or book a free consultation and describe the student rather than the service: the board, the syllabus code, the grade, what went wrong in the last school test.
2. We ask about the school calendar, the level, the subjects, your location and the schedule your family can hold, and we ask what you would count as a good first month.
3. We shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches the syllabus and level, subject to tutor availability.
4. You compare those profiles side by side on the same points, rather than reading them one at a time a week apart.
5. A demo or trial session can be arranged with more than one of them before you commit to anyone.
6. If the match is wrong after a few weeks, you ask for a different one, and the earlier you ask the less work is lost.

Step four is where families gain the most and spend the least effort. Reading three profiles in a row, on the same afternoon, against the same five questions, makes differences visible that are invisible when profiles arrive days apart. Write the five questions down first. Whatever you decide they are, apply them identically.

One warning about step one. A query that says wants help with Maths produces a generic shortlist. A query that says Grade 10, Cambridge 0580, entered for Extended, loses method marks and cannot work without a calculator, free Tuesday and Thursday after six, produces a shortlist you can actually choose between. The specificity you put in is the specificity you get back.
items: Write your five comparison questions before you read any profile
Read all shortlisted profiles in one sitting, not days apart
Describe the student's last test error, not just the subject name
Three profiles is the working limit; more slows the decision down
Ask what each tutor would do in the first four sessions

contentBlocks.heading: Reading board experience on a profile: Cambridge against Edexcel
contentBlocks.body:
The single line that separates two similar-looking profiles is which board the tutor has actually taught, and for how long. IGCSE here means Cambridge IGCSE from Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, normally a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. Those are different courses, not dialects of one.

Start with the grade scale, because it tells you quickly whether a tutor is fluent. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses carrying 9 to 1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. A tutor who speaks about Cambridge results in 9 to 1 language throughout has probably taught mostly Edexcel, which is fine if your child is on Edexcel and a warning sign if they are not. Ask a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon directly how many Cambridge cohorts they have taken through to a series, and compare the answers rather than the adjectives.

Tiering is the second comparison point, and it is where a weak profile shows. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. A tutor who has worked mostly with Core candidates has a different skill set from one who routinely takes students to the top of Extended, and neither is better in the abstract. What matters is which one your child needs. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, so a tutor whose experience is entirely Edexcel science may never have made a tier judgement at all.

The third point is the series, and it changes the calendar. Cambridge series run in February/March, offered only in India, and in May/June and October/November. Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Ask each shortlisted tutor when they would want to start revision for your child's series, and you will learn more about their planning than any summary paragraph reveals. An Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Gurugram who has taught the January series will answer that question without hesitating.

Listen for whether grades are described A* to G or 9 to 1
Core caps at C, Extended reaches A*: ask which the tutor usually teaches
Ask when revision should start for your child's actual series
A tutor fluent in one board is not automatically fluent in the other

contentBlocks.heading: Subject depth: what a tutor profile should show paper by paper
contentBlocks.body:
A profile that lists Maths, Science and English tells you almost nothing. A profile that names papers tells you a great deal, and comparing shortlisted tutors at the level of papers is the fastest way to separate a specialist from a willing generalist.

Take Mathematics. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, gives Core candidates Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is arranged differently: Foundation or Higher tier, with two calculator papers per tier. So a student moving from a school that ran 4MA1 to one that runs 0580 Extended suddenly faces a non-calculator paper they have never sat. Ask each shortlisted tutor how they would handle that. The answers will not be equally good.

The sciences reward the same test. Cambridge IGCSE sciences examined from 2023 use Paper 1 multiple choice for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, Paper 3 theory for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, and practical assessment through Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. The weighting is 30 per cent multiple choice, 50 per cent theory, 20 per cent practical. A tutor who has prepared students for Paper 6 knows it is a writing discipline about variables, tables and sources of error rather than laboratory dexterity. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

English is where shortlists most often go wrong, because the word English hides four courses. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 sets a reading paper and then directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio. English as a Second Language comes as 0510 and 0511, both covering reading, writing and listening, with 0511 counting speaking into the grade while 0510 reports it separately. Literature in English 0475 is separate again. Pearson Edexcel offers English Language A, 4EA1, English Language B, 4EB1, and English as a Second Language, 4ES1. Give every shortlisted tutor the same code and see who asks a follow-up question.
items: Ask which paper your child sits; a specialist answers instantly
Compare profiles on papers taught, not on subjects listed
Paper 6 technique is written method, not laboratory skill
0511 counts speaking into the grade; 0510 reports it separately
Send the same syllabus code to every shortlisted tutor and compare replies

contentBlocks.heading: Does your Gurgaon sector limit which home tutors reach your shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Yes, and it is better to know by how much before you start rather than after. Location does not change who is a good tutor, but it changes who can sit at your table on a Tuesday evening, and in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana that is a real filter on any shortlist of IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon.

Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area is the friendliest of the three corridors covered here. It takes in Sushant Lok 1, Sushant Lok 2, South City 1, Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City. Much of it is low-rise plotted housing with quick gate entry and short internal distances, so a tutor can commit to a fixed slot without a long buffer, and families searching for IGCSE private tutors in Sushant Lok usually get a genuine choice of two or three rather than a single name. That is the ideal case: you are comparing on teaching, not on travel.

Southern Peripheral Road is different. Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 70 and Sector 72 sit along a fast road with long stretches between entries, and Ansal Esencia and Bhondsi sit further out still. Tata Primanti and the Sector 70 cluster are workable, but a tutor who agrees to a six o'clock start here is making a promise about traffic. Families looking for IGCSE private tutors on Southern Peripheral Road will often find that two of three shortlisted candidates can only offer a later slot. Ask about the slot before you fall in love with a profile.

New Gurgaon is the corridor where a shortlist most often needs widening. Sector 82 through Sector 90, along with Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road and societies such as Vatika India Next and Godrej Air, sit far enough from the central corridors that a tutor travelling in loses a large part of the evening. Home lessons here work well for common subjects and get thin quickly for specialist ones. Parents searching IGCSE private tutors in New Gurgaon, or simply typing igcse private tutors near me, are usually best served by shortlisting two home candidates and one online specialist, then comparing all three honestly rather than ruling the third out on principle.
items: Sushant Lok and South City 1: quick gates, so slots are easy to hold
Southern Peripheral Road: expect later starts, especially past Bhondsi
New Gurgaon and Kherki Daula: widen the shortlist with one online candidate
Ask about the offered slot before you compare teaching credentials
Sector 70 and Tata Primanti pair naturally with Sector 66 to 69

contentBlocks.heading: School familiarity in Gurgaon, and how much weight to give it
contentBlocks.body:
Families who write to us come from schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, nor with the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

School familiarity is worth something on a shortlist, and less than most parents assume. What it genuinely buys is calendar sense: a tutor who has worked with students following a similar pattern knows roughly when unit tests cluster, how long the gap between mocks and the series tends to be, and that coursework deadlines are set internally and arrive earlier than families expect. That saves a few weeks of guesswork in the first term. It is a tiebreaker between two otherwise equal profiles.

What it does not buy is syllabus depth. A tutor who has taught several students from one school but has never taken a cohort through Extended Mathematics is still the weaker choice for an Extended candidate, however comfortable the conversation feels. Put school familiarity below board experience and level taught on your comparison list, not above them. If you are judging between the best IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon that your shortlist can produce, the ranking of criteria matters more than the criteria themselves.

One calendar point applies to every shortlisted candidate equally, so ask all of them. International schools here start early and run long bus loops, which means the first free evening hour is later than the timetable suggests, especially for outer sectors. Ask each tutor what they would do about the three-week stretch around mocks: increase hours, switch entirely to past papers, or hold the normal plan. Three different answers to that question tell you three different things about how they teach, and it is the most useful single question on the whole list.
items: Treat school familiarity as a tiebreaker, not a headline qualification
Ask every shortlisted tutor the same question about the mock period
Get coursework and speaking deadlines from the coordinator early
Board experience and level taught outrank school names on a shortlist
Bus loops push the realistic start later than the school timetable implies

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing home tuition, online and hybrid candidates side by side
contentBlocks.body:
Put the format on the comparison sheet rather than deciding it first. Home tuition is where most families here land, and rightly so: a tutor at the same table sees the working a student half-hides, marks a script with a pen instead of a cursor, and holds the attention of a fifteen-year-old who would otherwise have four tabs open. Home classes also need nothing more than a table and an hour.

Stated plainly, the three formats trade the same two things. Home tuition gives the most attention and the least friction, and pays for it in travel, which limits the pool of tutors who can reach you at the hour you want. Online gives the widest possible pool, including specialists nowhere near your corridor, and late slots that a travelling tutor cannot offer, at the cost of a student who must stay engaged without anyone sitting beside them. Hybrid, one home session and one online session a week, keeps the in-person relationship while releasing the travel hour, which is why a hybrid candidate can often offer a better slot than a purely home-based one.

So compare formats against the same criteria you use for people. Which format gives this student the attention they need? Which one can hold the slot in your sector reliably through a full term? Which one still works in July when the roads flood? A shortlist of two home candidates and one IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon is a stronger shortlist than three home candidates, because it forces a real comparison instead of a narrow one.

And take the student's own view seriously without treating it as final. A child who says online is boring may mean their last online class was a recorded lecture with forty others in it. A live one-to-one lesson is a different experience entirely. Let a trial answer the question instead of an opinion formed before the first session.
items: Shortlist two home candidates and one online specialist, then compare
Home classes win on attention; online wins on pool and slot choice
Hybrid frees the travel hour and often opens up a better evening
Test format in a trial rather than deciding it from an opinion
Ask each candidate what happens in a week when travel is impossible

contentBlocks.heading: What is verified before a profile reaches your shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
Identity documents, the qualifications claimed, the boards and levels the tutor states they have taught, and the subjects they agree to be matched for are all checked before a profile is shown to you. A claim that cannot be supported does not stay on the profile. That is the baseline that lets you compare candidates on teaching instead of on plausibility.

Your own checks then do something different: they test fit rather than truthfulness. Ask each shortlisted tutor the same three questions and compare the answers rather than the credentials. What is the first thing you would look at in this student's last test paper? How do you know when a student has actually understood something rather than copied a method? What would you tell me after four weeks? Identical questions produce comparable answers, and comparable answers are the entire point of having a shortlist.

Be careful with certificates. A workshop certificate proves attendance at a workshop and nothing about how someone teaches your child's syllabus. A degree in a subject proves study of that subject, not the ability to explain Paper 4 marking to a fifteen-year-old at seven in the evening. Use documents to rule candidates out, never to rule one in. The evidence that decides a shortlist is the trial lesson, which is why a demo or trial session exists and why nothing should be committed before it.

For home lessons there are a few practical checks worth applying to every candidate identically. See photo identity on the first visit. Register the tutor at your society gate under their own name rather than as a casual guest. Keep the lesson in a shared room with the door open. Make sure an adult is at home. Applying these evenly across a shortlist also removes an awkwardness: nobody is being singled out, because everyone is being asked the same thing.
items: Identity, qualifications and boards taught are verified before you see a profile
Ask all shortlisted tutors the same three questions, word for word
Use certificates to rule out, never to rule in
Apply the same home-visit checks to every candidate equally
The trial lesson, not the document file, decides the shortlist

contentBlocks.heading: How do you run trial lessons with two IGCSE private tutors fairly?
contentBlocks.body:
Give both tutors the same material, the same length of session, and the same student on a comparable day, then judge them on what the student can do afterwards rather than on how the hour felt. Anything else is not a comparison, it is two unrelated experiences with a coin toss at the end.

The practical version is straightforward. Pick one piece of real work: the last school test, or a past paper question the student got wrong. Send it to both tutors in advance and say the same thing to each. Keep both sessions the same length. Run them a few days apart, not back to back, because a tired student makes the second tutor look worse than they are. Do not tell either tutor what the other said. And ask your child the same two questions after each session: what did you get stuck on, and do you now know how to fix it? A student who can describe their own error after the lesson has been taught something.

The part parents worry about is the student. Meeting two adults in one week can feel like an audition, particularly for a child who already feels behind. Frame it honestly and lightly: we are trying two people to see who explains things in a way that suits you, and you get a say. Most Grade 9 and 10 students find that reassuring rather than stressful, because it puts them in the decision rather than outside it. Two trials is the sensible maximum. Three starts to feel like a test of the child rather than of the tutors.

One thing to resist. The more charming tutor usually wins a trial, and charm is genuinely useful for a nervous student, so it is not nothing. But it is not the same as teaching. If one session was warm and vague and the other was blunt and precise, look at what the student can now do. Then choose, and when you choose, tell the other tutor plainly rather than leaving the request open.
items: Send both tutors the same past paper question in advance
Keep both trials the same length, a few days apart
Ask your child the same two questions after each session
Two trials is the sensible limit for a Grade 9 or 10 student
Judge on what the student can do afterwards, not on warmth

contentBlocks.heading: When should you ask for a different tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask as soon as you can name the problem, and do not wait for a term to end. No tutor can guarantee a grade, so the test is not results in week five. The test is whether the sessions have a direction the tutor can describe and the student can recognise.

There are three signals worth acting on. The first is a tutor who cannot tell you, by the fourth week, the single thing your child still gets wrong most often. That means the sessions have become homework supervision. The second is a student who stops preparing anything between sessions, which usually means the lesson has become a place where answers are supplied rather than built. The third is a slot that keeps moving. A home tutor who reschedules repeatedly because of travel from another sector has a route problem, not an attitude problem, and it will not fix itself.

Raise it with the tutor first, once, and be specific. Say the student cannot start a question without being prompted, or that you would like a written summary every fortnight. Some of the most useful shifts we see come from one blunt conversation. If nothing changes within two or three sessions, ask for a different match. You can do that at any point, and it is a normal request rather than a complaint about anybody's competence.

Switching costs something, so be honest about the price. A new tutor spends the first two sessions diagnosing ground the previous one already covered, and a student who has just started trusting someone has to start again. That cost is worth paying in month two and much harder to justify four weeks before a series, when triage with a known tutor usually beats a fresh start with a better one. Keep your original shortlist notes. If the second name on that list is still available, the changeover is far quicker than beginning the search again, which is one more reason to compare IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon properly at the start.
items: Week four: the tutor should name the student's most frequent error
A slot that keeps moving is a route problem, not a phase
Raise one specific change first, then ask for a different match
Switching costs two diagnostic sessions, so move early rather than late
Keep shortlist notes; the second name makes a changeover quick

contentBlocks.heading: Booking home classes: what to send with your first query
contentBlocks.body:
A useful shortlist starts with a useful query, and it takes five lines. Send the board and syllabus code, the grade and tier, what the last school test showed, your sector, and two evenings that genuinely work. Say also whether you want to compare home candidates only, or home and online together.

What happens next is short. We ask about the school calendar, the level, the subjects, your location and the schedule you can keep. We then share verified profiles that match, subject to tutor availability, and you compare them on your own five points. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, with more than one tutor if you want to compare directly. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and if the match is wrong you can ask for a different one.

For the first home session, have the last two school tests, the school's scheme of work if you have a copy, the textbook and any attempted past paper on the table. An IGCSE Grade 9 and 10 tutor who can see real work in the first hour will give you a far more specific plan than one who spends that hour asking questions you could have answered in advance.

Set up the space before the first lesson as well. A table for two, a plug point, decent light, and an hour the household treats as genuinely booked. Students take home classes as seriously as the house around them does, and that holds true for every tutor on your shortlist.
items: Five lines: board, code, grade and tier, last test, sector, two evenings
Say whether you want home candidates only or home and online
Ask for trials with more than one tutor if you want a direct comparison
Have the last two tests and any past paper on the table
A two-seat table, a plug point and an hour nobody interrupts

faqs.question: How many IGCSE tutor profiles should we actually look at?
faqs.answer: Two or three is the working number. One profile gives you nothing to judge against, so the decision becomes a gut feeling about a stranger. Four or more starts to blur, and families end up re-reading rather than deciding. Two or three verified profiles, compared on the same five points, give you enough contrast to see what each one is strong at without the process dragging on for weeks. If all three look similar on paper, that is useful information too: it means the differences will show up in the trial rather than in the summary, and the trial is where you should be spending your attention anyway.

faqs.question: Can we take a trial class with more than one tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a genuine comparison it is the only reliable way to do it. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and there is no reason to restrict that to a single candidate. Keep the two trials the same length, give both tutors the same piece of real work in advance, and space them a few days apart so your child is equally fresh for each. Judge them on what the student can do afterwards rather than on which hour felt friendlier. Two trials is the sensible maximum for a Grade 9 or 10 student, since a third starts to feel like an examination of the child.

faqs.question: Two profiles look almost identical. What should we compare?
faqs.answer: Go one level more specific than the profile summary. Ask both tutors how many cohorts they have taken through your child's board rather than how many years they have taught. Ask which paper a candidate at your child's tier sits, and note who answers instantly. Ask what they would do in the three weeks before mocks. Ask what they would tell you after four weeks. Then compare the slot each can genuinely hold, week after week, in your sector. Identical questions produce comparable answers, and it is almost always one of those five that separates two profiles that looked the same on paper.

faqs.question: Our shortlist is thin because we live in Sector 86. What now?
faqs.answer: Widen the format rather than lowering the bar on teaching. New Gurgaon sits far enough from the central corridors that a tutor travelling in loses a long part of the evening, so the pool of home candidates for a specialist syllabus is genuinely small. The practical fix is to shortlist two home tutors for the common subjects and one online specialist for the difficult one, then compare all three fairly. Another option is a weekend home session with a tutor who will travel once a week rather than twice, paired with a midweek online lesson. Both give you something real to choose between.

faqs.question: Is it unsettling for a child to meet several tutors?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect, provided you explain it honestly. Say that you are trying two people to find whoever explains things in a way that suits them, and that their opinion counts. Most Grade 9 and 10 students find that reassuring, because it places them inside the decision rather than on the receiving end of it. What does unsettle students is a long run of trials with no decision, or a parent visibly comparing tutors in front of the child. Keep it to two, space them a few days apart, and make the choice quickly once both sessions are done.

faqs.question: Can we ask for a different tutor after only two weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and early is better than late. If after a few sessions the tutor cannot describe what your child gets wrong most often, or the student has stopped preparing anything between lessons, the arrangement is not working and waiting rarely repairs it. Raise one specific change with the tutor first, since a single blunt conversation often fixes it. If nothing shifts within two or three sessions, ask for a different match. Switching costs roughly two diagnostic sessions with the new tutor, which is cheap in month one and expensive close to an exam series. Your original shortlist notes make the changeover much faster.

faqs.question: Does board experience matter more than years of teaching?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE, usually yes. A tutor with a long general teaching career but few Cambridge or Edexcel cohorts will know the content well and the assessment less well, and at this level marks are lost to assessment habits more than to gaps in knowledge. Method marks in 0580, command terms in theory papers, and the written technique that Paper 6 rewards are all board-specific. Ask each shortlisted tutor how many cohorts they have taken through to a series on your child's board. That single number separates candidates faster than any summary of experience, and it is easy to compare across profiles.

faqs.question: Will the same home tutor come every week, or does it rotate?
faqs.answer: A home arrangement is with one named tutor, and continuity is part of what you are paying for, because a tutor who has watched six weeks of a student's mistakes teaches differently from one meeting them fresh. If a session cannot happen, the usual options are a rescheduled slot or moving that week online rather than sending a substitute. Agree at the start what happens when the tutor is travelling or unwell, and put it in writing along with the notice period. Families who settle that in week one have far fewer awkward conversations in month three, whichever tutor they ended up choosing.

faqs.question: Our shortlisted tutor travels from Sushant Lok. Will our slot run late?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, before you commit, what time they leave and what else is on their route that evening. Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the area around Sector 29 have quick gate entry and short internal distances, so a tutor working within that corridor can usually hold a tight slot. A tutor travelling from there out to Sector 68 or Sector 84 is making a longer promise, and the honest ones will say so and offer a later start. A slot that repeatedly slips by fifteen minutes is a route problem and it will not correct itself, so treat the answer as a comparison point.

faqs.question: Should we compare fees between shortlisted tutors?
faqs.answer: Compare the structure rather than chasing the lowest figure. Ask each candidate whether they charge per session or monthly, whether travel to your sector affects the rate, what a ninety-minute session costs relative to sixty, and whether anything changes during an intensive revision block before the series. Those structural answers are comparable across profiles in a way that a single number is not. Then weigh it against what each tutor offered in the trial. A cheaper tutor who needs twice as many sessions to cover the same ground is not cheaper, and a costly one who cannot hold your slot is no bargain either.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both Cambridge and Edexcel students?
faqs.answer: Many can, and some do it well, but it is worth probing rather than assuming. Ask a candidate who claims both to explain the difference in Mathematics: Cambridge 0580 puts Extended candidates on a non-calculator Paper 2, while Edexcel 4MA1 gives two calculator papers at Foundation or Higher tier. A tutor fluent in both will describe that without prompting. One who has really taught only one board will generalise. This matters especially for a student switching schools mid-course, where a tutor who understands both sides of the move is worth a great deal on a shortlist.

faqs.question: How do we compare a home tutor with an online specialist honestly?
faqs.answer: Score them on the same criteria and accept that each will win different rows. The home tutor should win on attention, on catching hidden working, and on a student who stays engaged without effort. The online specialist should win on syllabus depth, on slot choice, and on being available in a week when the roads are impossible. Then ask which of those your child actually needs most this term. For a student who drifts without someone beside them, the home candidate wins even against a stronger specialist. For a scarce syllabus close to a series, the specialist usually wins outright.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: What a Private Tutor Must Match
contentBlocks.body:
A private tutor being compared for shortlist purposes needs to match more than the subject name; the board and the exam series matter just as much. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor Gurgaon families shortlist should state the exact tier taught, since Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE both cover Grades 9 and 10 over two years, but their calendars differ: Cambridge sits three series a year, a February/March sitting offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November, while an Edexcel IGCSE tutor Gurugram families compare should know the January and May/June series specifically, since Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs only those two. Two tutors shortlisted for the same subject can be preparing students for exam dates months apart, and that changes how a term's tuition should be paced.

Tiering is the second thing worth confirming before comparing two profiles side by side. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core, which tops out at grade C, and Extended, which reaches A*, and this is the school's decision, not the family's. A tutor experienced only with Extended-tier students is not automatically the right comparison for a Core-tier student, even if both are labelled the same subject on paper.

Grading itself differs by board, Cambridge mostly A* through G with some syllabuses running 9-1 variants under separate codes, Edexcel 9 through 1 throughout, and a private tutor should be able to translate a school report against whichever scale applies. Looking further ahead, Grade 10 usually leads into the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or a return to CBSE or ISC in Class 11, and a tutor worth keeping past the IGCSE years should already understand which direction suits the student.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the Paper Structure Before You Compare Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing two shortlisted tutors on Maths experience alone misses the point when the two boards structure the paper so differently. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, splits by tier: Core sits Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, calculator; Extended sits Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4, calculator. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher instead, with two calculator papers per tier. A fair comparison asks each shortlisted tutor which of these exact papers they have prepared students for, not just whether they know IGCSE Maths in general.

Sciences carry a fixed structure worth checking the same way. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, from the syllabuses examined since 2023, weight multiple choice at 30% (Paper 1 Core, Paper 2 Extended), theory at 50% (Paper 3 Core, Paper 4 Extended), and practical assessment at 20%, examined through Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, an alternative to practical, depending on the school's choice. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, sat through Paper 1 and Paper 2, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than separately.

English deserves the closest look of all when comparing tutors, since the syllabus name alone hides real differences. Cambridge alone runs First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language in two codes, 0510 and 0511, which grade speaking differently, and Literature in English 0475 as a distinct subject. Pearson Edexcel runs English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). Two English tutors on a shortlist can turn out to have taught entirely different syllabuses once you ask which code each one actually means.

A private arrangement puts more of the verification burden on the family than a school-run class would, which is exactly why IB Gram checks the basics before a profile is even shown: identity, contact details, and that the board, level and subjects stated are genuinely what the tutor has taught, not a general claim stretched to fit the search. Before comparing two shortlisted tutors, it is fair to ask each one directly: which syllabus code have you actually taught, Core or Extended, which exam series have your students sat, and how do you handle a first session with someone new. A tutor with real, specific experience answers plainly; a tutor exaggerating tends to speak in generalities that could apply to any board.

For a private arrangement specifically, it is also worth asking what happens if a session needs to be rescheduled, whether the tutor works to the school's own scheme of work or to their own separate sequence, and how they would flag it if the student is not progressing. None of these questions should feel awkward to ask before a trial; a tutor who bristles at them is telling you something worth noting.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Compare Two Private IGCSE Tutors Without Bias?
contentBlocks.body:
A fair comparison depends on holding the variables steady, which is harder than it sounds once two different personalities and two different teaching styles are involved. Before booking trial sessions, confirm both shortlisted tutors teach the same board and the same tier, since a Core specialist and an Extended specialist can sound equally confident without actually being comparable for this particular student. Giving both tutors an identical short diagnostic, a recent school test or a topic the student is stuck on, keeps the comparison about how each one handles the same material rather than two disconnected first impressions.

During each trial, watch for the same signals in both: does the tutor check what the student already knows before teaching something new, does the student get a genuine chance to attempt something and get stuck, and is the session anchored to the actual syllabus, referencing command terms and paper structure, or kept generic enough to suit anyone. Writing these impressions down straight after each trial matters more than it seems; two sessions a few days apart blur together faster than most parents expect.

Bias creeps in easily with a private arrangement specifically, because there is no school administrator or second opinion in the room, just the parent's own read. It helps to separate the student's reaction from the parent's own impression of competence and weigh both rather than letting one override the other; a technically excellent tutor the student is guarded with rarely produces steady progress over a full term.

If, after both trials, the choice still feels unclear, asking IB Gram for a fresh pair is entirely reasonable and often produces a clearer result than picking between two tutors neither of whom quite convinced you.

contentBlocks.heading: Is Home Tuition Actually Working a Month Into a Private Arrangement?
contentBlocks.body:
By four to six weeks in, there should be something concrete to show for a private arrangement: fewer careless errors on a familiar question type, a student attempting a past paper question unprompted, or a mark scheme being applied correctly without the tutor walking through every step. If nothing has visibly shifted by then, raise it directly with the tutor rather than assuming the arrangement simply needs more time.

No private tutor, home-based or online, can honestly guarantee a grade, and a tutor who offers one should be treated with more caution, not less. What a genuinely good private tutor provides instead is a clear, ongoing read of which topics are solid and which are not, delivered plainly rather than smoothed over for the parent's comfort. The occasional honest report that is not entirely positive is a sign of a tutor worth keeping, not one worth replacing.

Because the arrangement sits outside any school structure, how progress gets tracked is entirely up to what the family and tutor agree, an error log, brief notes after each session, or a short review every few weeks. Progress rarely moves in a straight line; a plateau around a genuinely hard topic, or during a stretch of heavy school tests, does not automatically mean the tutor is wrong. What matters more is the direction across a full term, and whether the tutor can explain specifically what changed whenever a dip happens. A family who switched recently, from a coaching batch to this private arrangement, should expect a short settling-in period before comparing progress to the old format feels fair.

faqs.question: How is comparing private tutors different from comparing tutors through a coaching centre?
faqs.answer: A coaching centre already vets and assigns its own tutors, so there is little for a parent to compare directly; a private arrangement puts that comparison entirely in your hands, which is exactly why IB Gram shortlists two or three verified profiles rather than one. You are weighing board experience, tier familiarity and trial-session chemistry yourself, not trusting a centre's internal assignment. It takes a little more upfront effort than accepting whichever tutor a centre offers, but it usually produces a tighter fit, since the final choice reflects this specific student rather than whoever happened to be free at the centre that term.

faqs.question: Are there fewer private tutors to choose from on Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon or Manesar?
faqs.answer: It varies by corridor. Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar tend to have a reasonably established pool of private tutors already based nearby, so a shortlist there is usually straightforward. Dwarka Expressway has grown quickly enough that coverage is still catching up, and Manesar, being furthest from the city's main tutor concentration, often means comparing fewer home options against a wider field of online specialists. None of this rules out a strong shortlist in any of the three; it simply means asking directly how long a tutor has actually served that specific stretch.

faqs.question: Should we compare a private tutor against what the school teacher already offers after hours?
faqs.answer: It is worth understanding the difference before comparing. A private tutor is entirely independent of the school and has no other relationship with the student, while a teacher's own after-school extra classes come with a potential conflict of interest and a different structure. Many families run both at different points, but they are not really substitutes for each other, and a private tutor being shortlisted here should not be judged against the school's own remedial periods, which serve a different purpose entirely.

faqs.question: What if the two shortlisted tutors seem equally good after trial sessions?
faqs.answer: This happens more often than parents expect, and it is a good problem to have. When trials leave you genuinely torn, practical factors are a reasonable tiebreaker: which tutor's schedule better survives a bad traffic evening, which one the student mentioned unprompted afterwards, or which one asked sharper questions about the school's own test calendar. There is no need to agonise for weeks; either tutor has already cleared the bar of a fair trial, so a reasonably quick decision, with the option to switch later if needed, is better than an indefinitely delayed one.

faqs.question: Will a private tutor come to our home in Manesar or would online be more realistic?
faqs.answer: Online is often the more realistic starting point for Manesar and the NH-48 corridor south specifically, given how few private tutors already live close enough to visit reliably on a weekday evening. Even so, an occasional home session, timed around a weekend or a longer holiday visit, can still be arranged for corridors like this even if a weekly home slot is not practical. Ask IB Gram to shortlist with this in mind from the outset rather than discovering the travel constraint after a tutor has already been chosen.

faqs.question: Should a parent be present during a private home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Occasionally at the start, not for every session. Sitting in for the first trial and the opening of the first few real sessions gives a useful read on how the tutor works with the student, without turning every lesson into a supervised one, which can make an older student self-conscious over time. Most families step back once a rhythm is established and rely on the tutor's own updates instead. For a younger student, or one new to working with a tutor at all, staying nearby for the first few weeks is reasonable and most tutors expect it.

faqs.question: How many private tutors should we actually shortlist before comparing?
faqs.answer: Two or three, which is what IB Gram offers by design. Comparing more than three tends to blur first impressions together rather than sharpen the decision, and a shortlist of one leaves nothing to weigh it against. Confirm each profile shares the same board and tier before booking trials, so the comparison is genuinely fair rather than comparing a Core specialist against an Extended one without realising it. If none of the two or three feel right, asking for a fresh pair is a normal, low-cost step, not a failure of the process.

faqs.question: Can we run trial sessions with both shortlisted tutors in the same week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and doing so is the fairest way to judge them, since the student's mood and the week's schoolwork stay roughly comparable across both sessions. Use the same platform or the same room for both if possible, and give the tutor the same short diagnostic exercise so you are comparing how each one handles identical material. Write down your impressions immediately after each trial rather than days later, when two similar sessions tend to blend together in memory.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to switch tutors partway through a term?
faqs.answer: It happens, and IB Gram treats it as a normal part of a private arrangement rather than an exception. Tell IB Gram plainly what was not working, whether pace, teaching style, or simply personality fit, and a fresh shortlist can be built around picking up from where the student currently is, rather than starting entirely from scratch. Most students adjust within a session or two to a new tutor's style, though it helps to tell the new tutor what the previous arrangement covered so nothing important gets repeated or skipped.

faqs.question: How much does private IGCSE tuition cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on the subject, the student's level, session length and the tutor's own experience, and IB Gram does not quote one fixed figure because these factors genuinely change the picture, subject to tutor availability. During the shortlist stage, it is more useful to ask how each tutor's fee is structured, per session, monthly, or in a package, than to fixate on a single number before you know which tutor and format you are actually comparing. A trial session costs nothing and remains the right first step regardless of budget.

faqs.question: Does switching from Cambridge IGCSE to Pearson Edexcel change who we should shortlist?
faqs.answer: Yes, since the two boards examine differently enough that a tutor experienced only with Cambridge is not automatically ready for Edexcel's paper structure, and the reverse is equally true. If a switch is confirmed or being considered, mention it when requesting a shortlist so the profiles offered already have experience with the destination board. A short overlap period, where the tutor reviews both syllabuses against the new school's scheme of work, usually smooths a mid-year switch without losing much momentum.
