You are weighing board experience, tier familiarity and trial-session chemistry yourself, not trusting a centre's internal assignment. It takes a little more upfront effort than accepting whichever tutor a centre offers, but it usually produces a tighter fit, since the final choice reflects this specific student rather than whoever happened to be free at the centre that term.

mainEntity.name: Are there fewer private tutors to choose from on Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon or Manesar?

acceptedAnswer.text: It varies by corridor. Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar tend to have a reasonably established pool of private tutors already based nearby, so a shortlist there is usually straightforward. Dwarka Expressway has grown quickly enough that coverage is still catching up, and Manesar, being furthest from the city's main tutor concentration, often means comparing fewer home options against a wider field of online specialists. None of this rules out a strong shortlist in any of the three; it simply means asking directly how long a tutor has actually served that specific stretch.

mainEntity.name: Should we compare a private tutor against what the school teacher already offers after hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is worth understanding the difference before comparing. A private tutor is entirely independent of the school and has no other relationship with the student, while a teacher's own after-school extra classes come with a potential conflict of interest and a different structure. Many families run both at different points, but they are not really substitutes for each other, and a private tutor being shortlisted here should not be judged against the school's own remedial periods, which serve a different purpose entirely.

mainEntity.name: What if the two shortlisted tutors seem equally good after trial sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: This happens more often than parents expect, and it is a good problem to have. When trials leave you genuinely torn, practical factors are a reasonable tiebreaker: which tutor's schedule better survives a bad traffic evening, which one the student mentioned unprompted afterwards, or which one asked sharper questions about the school's own test calendar. There is no need to agonise for weeks; either tutor has already cleared the bar of a fair trial, so a reasonably quick decision, with the option to switch later if needed, is better than an indefinitely delayed one.

mainEntity.name: Will a private tutor come to our home in Manesar or would online be more realistic?

acceptedAnswer.text: Online is often the more realistic starting point for Manesar and the NH-48 corridor south specifically, given how few private tutors already live close enough to visit reliably on a weekday evening. Even so, an occasional home session, timed around a weekend or a longer holiday visit, can still be arranged for corridors like this even if a weekly home slot is not practical. Ask IB Gram to shortlist with this in mind from the outset rather than discovering the travel constraint after a tutor has already been chosen.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent be present during a private home tuition session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Occasionally at the start, not for every session. Sitting in for the first trial and the opening of the first few real sessions gives a useful read on how the tutor works with the student, without turning every lesson into a supervised one, which can make an older student self-conscious over time. Most families step back once a rhythm is established and rely on the tutor's own updates instead. For a younger student, or one new to working with a tutor at all, staying nearby for the first few weeks is reasonable and most tutors expect it.

mainEntity.name: How many private tutors should we actually shortlist before comparing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two or three, which is what IB Gram offers by design. Comparing more than three tends to blur first impressions together rather than sharpen the decision, and a shortlist of one leaves nothing to weigh it against. Confirm each profile shares the same board and tier before booking trials, so the comparison is genuinely fair rather than comparing a Core specialist against an Extended one without realising it. If none of the two or three feel right, asking for a fresh pair is a normal, low-cost step, not a failure of the process.

mainEntity.name: Can we run trial sessions with both shortlisted tutors in the same week?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and doing so is the fairest way to judge them, since the student's mood and the week's schoolwork stay roughly comparable across both sessions. Use the same platform or the same room for both if possible, and give the tutor the same short diagnostic exercise so you are comparing how each one handles identical material. Write down your impressions immediately after each trial rather than days later, when two similar sessions tend to blend together in memory.

mainEntity.name: What happens if we need to switch tutors partway through a term?

acceptedAnswer.text: It happens, and IB Gram treats it as a normal part of a private arrangement rather than an exception. Tell IB Gram plainly what was not working, whether pace, teaching style, or simply personality fit, and a fresh shortlist can be built around picking up from where the student currently is, rather than starting entirely from scratch. Most students adjust within a session or two to a new tutor's style, though it helps to tell the new tutor what the previous arrangement covered so nothing important gets repeated or skipped.

mainEntity.name: How much does private IGCSE tuition cost in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the subject, the student's level, session length and the tutor's own experience, and IB Gram does not quote one fixed figure because these factors genuinely change the picture, subject to tutor availability. During the shortlist stage, it is more useful to ask how each tutor's fee is structured, per session, monthly, or in a package, than to fixate on a single number before you know which tutor and format you are actually comparing. A trial session costs nothing and remains the right first step regardless of budget.

mainEntity.name: Does switching from Cambridge IGCSE to Pearson Edexcel change who we should shortlist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, since the two boards examine differently enough that a tutor experienced only with Cambridge is not automatically ready for Edexcel's paper structure, and the reverse is equally true. If a switch is confirmed or being considered, mention it when requesting a shortlist so the profiles offered already have experience with the destination board. A short overlap period, where the tutor reviews both syllabuses against the new school's scheme of work, usually smooths a mid-year switch without losing much momentum.

contentBlocks.heading: Finding the Right Online IGCSE Tutor for Your Child in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Most families looking for an igcse online tutor gurgaon can trust begin with a short conversation about what the student is actually stuck on, not a list of available tutors. IB Gram asks which board the school follows, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the grade, and, for subjects that split by tier such as Mathematics 0580 or the sciences, whether the school has placed the student in Core or Extended. Without that detail, matching a tutor is guesswork; with it, the shortlist narrows to two or three specialists rather than a long, undifferentiated list.

A tutor is then checked against that exact requirement rather than a general claim of IGCSE experience. Someone who has taught Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry for years is not automatically the right fit for a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry student, since the paper structure and assessment weighting differ enough to matter in the first few sessions. IB Gram looks for a tutor who has taught this exact syllabus, this exact tier, and ideally students at this exact stage before, rather than someone adapting on the fly.

Every match starts with a free trial class, run online exactly as a real lesson would be, on one topic the student is currently behind on. This is deliberate: a parent should see the actual tutor teaching, not a description of them. The tutor's tone, pace, and how they respond when the student gets something wrong tell a family far more in forty-five minutes than any profile summary could.

After the trial, IB Gram asks the family directly whether the tutor feels right, before any term is booked. A student who needs a calmer, more patient tutor, or a stricter one who keeps pace tight before an exam series, is matched again with a different profile rather than being left with a mismatch. The process only ends once the family, not just the tutor, confirms the fit.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: Does Your Online Tutor Know the Difference?
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor worth booking should be able to tell a parent, without hesitation, whether their child's school follows Cambridge IGCSE, set by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and what that means practically. Cambridge runs across Grade 9 and 10 with exam series in February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November, and grades most syllabuses on the A* to G scale, though a growing number of subjects now sit newer 9-1 versions under separate codes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE follows a similar two-year structure with series in January and May/June, grading throughout on the 9-1 scale used across the syllabus.

Many Cambridge subjects also split into Core and Extended tiers, a decision the school makes, usually toward the end of Grade 9, not one the family or tutor controls. Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A* but demands more secure content knowledge to pass cleanly rather than scrape through. A tutor teaching online should already know which tier the student sits before the first proper lesson, since drilling Extended-level content with a Core-tier student wastes time neither side has to spare.

What an online tutor can do well here, better in some cases than in a home session, is pull up two syllabuses side by side on a shared screen: an Edexcel 4MA1 Higher paper next to a Cambridge Extended equivalent, useful for a family weighing whether to move boards, or Core Paper 1 next to Extended Paper 2 to show a student exactly what a tier change would demand. A tutor without a laptop and a second monitor struggles to do this as cleanly in person as they can online.

Most students move from IGCSE into the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or back to CBSE or ISC for Class 11, and a tutor who has guided that transition before, across several past students, is worth more than one meeting it for the first time with your child.

contentBlocks.heading: The Syllabus Depth a Genuine IGCSE Online Tutor Should Have
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a prospective Mathematics tutor to describe Cambridge IGCSE 0580 without prompting, and a genuine specialist will mention the 2025 paper structure unprompted: Core candidates sitting Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, calculator; Extended candidates sitting Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4, calculator. The non-calculator papers demand a different kind of drilling, clean method and layout without a calculator to check the arithmetic, and a tutor who treats both papers identically is missing something students notice quickly. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher instead, with two calculator papers per tier, so a tutor moving between boards should flag that the non-calculator discipline Cambridge demands is simply not part of the Edexcel route.

For the sciences, Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses examined from 2023 assess through a multiple choice paper, Paper 1 for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, a theory paper, Paper 3 or Paper 4, and a practical route the school selects, either Paper 5, a hands-on practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical taken as a written paper. The weighting is fixed across the syllabus: multiple choice contributes 30%, theory 50%, and practical 20%. An online tutor cannot sit in on a school's Paper 5 practical, but a genuine science specialist should be well practised at teaching to Paper 6, the written alternative, since it rewards precise, memorised description of method and apparatus, something that transfers cleanly to a screen-shared past paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered and assessed through Paper 1 and Paper 2, with practical skills folded into the written papers rather than tested separately.

English deserves particular scrutiny when checking a tutor's depth, because IGCSE English is not one syllabus but several. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 combines a reading paper with directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio where the school offers it. English as a Second Language splits into two codes, 0510 and 0511, both testing reading, writing and listening, but 0511 folds a speaking assessment into the overall grade while 0510 reports speaking separately from the main result. Literature in English 0475 sits alongside these where a school teaches it. Pearson Edexcel offers three of its own: International GCSE English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1), and English as a Second Language (4ES1). A tutor who cannot immediately confirm which of these your child's school actually teaches has not yet earned the right to plan a term.

contentBlocks.heading: What School Life in Gurgaon Demands of an Online Tutor's Schedule
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana whose children attend schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge deal with a school calendar an online tutor has to plan around, not one this page attributes to any specific school.

International schools in Gurgaon typically run internal assessments and mock exams at intervals that shift from year to year, often clustered before the winter break and again ahead of the summer holidays, and a tutor who only learns about these dates when a parent mentions them in passing is planning blind. A good online tutor asks for the school's own assessment calendar at the very start of a term and works backward from it, rather than teaching the syllabus in a fixed order regardless of when the next test falls.

Co-curricular life adds real pressure to the evening. Sport, music and Model United Nations commitments push many students' free time into early evening, and a student walking in at 6:30pm still has homework to finish before any tutoring can start. An online tutor able to offer an 8 or 8:30pm slot, after dinner, is often genuinely more useful to a Gurgaon family than one who can only manage 6pm, since a home tutor arriving that late has usually spent close to an hour travelling to reach the family in the first place.

Exam season compresses everything further. In the run-up to Cambridge's May/June series or Pearson Edexcel's own May/June papers, students are typically juggling three or four subjects at once, and a tutor who can offer a short, sharply focused 45-minute online session on one weak topic, slotted in between school commitments, is often more useful in that window than a longer but less frequent session structure.

contentBlocks.heading: Should This Tutor Teach at Home, Online or Both?
contentBlocks.body:
For most families beginning with a new tutor, home tuition is still the honest default: sitting beside a student, watching their working take shape, and correcting a habit the moment it happens carries an advantage no screen fully replicates. A younger Grade 9 student, or a student working through Mathematics where the exact layout of a calculation matters, generally benefits from that in-person contact, particularly in the first few weeks of a new relationship.

Online tuition earns its place for a genuinely different set of reasons: a specialist for a narrower syllabus, such as Literature in English 0475, who simply is not close by; a family whose evenings only leave a late slot free; or a corridor, Sohna Road at peak hours or a stretch of Gwal Pahari further from the centre, where a fixed home arrival time is hard to promise. A tutor experienced online brings a shared whiteboard, a document camera for handwritten working, and a saved recording the student can replay, which covers most, though not all, of what an in-person lesson offers. What it does not fully replace is a tutor noticing, without being told, that a student has stopped writing and drifted off three minutes ago.

Hybrid arrangements, the same tutor working at home some weeks and online others, are often the most sensible middle path once a relationship is established. A family might keep a weekly home session through the term for steady progress and shift to online sessions purely for intensive past-paper practice in the fortnight before mocks, without ever changing who is teaching the student. Continuity of tutor matters more than continuity of format for most students past the first month.

The honest trade-off: home tutoring costs travel time and depends on the corridor's traffic that particular evening; online tuition removes that constraint but asks more of the student's own focus and camera discipline; hybrid keeps a single tutor across both but requires a family comfortable managing two formats through the term. None is objectively better; the right choice depends on the student's age, the subject, and how reliably a home visit can actually happen from where the family lives.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor's Profile Is Checked Before They Meet Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile is shared with a parent, IB Gram checks that the syllabus and tier a tutor claims to teach genuinely match what they have taught before, asking pointed questions rather than accepting a broad claim of IGCSE experience. A tutor who lists Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics should describe the Core and Extended paper split without needing a prompt; one who cannot is not shortlisted for that specific subject, regardless of how strong the rest of their profile looks.

For an online tutor specifically, IB Gram also checks whether the person has actually taught over video before, because teaching well on a screen is a genuinely separate skill from teaching well in a room. A tutor who explains beautifully in person can come across flat or hard to follow online if they have never practised narrating their own working aloud while writing on a shared whiteboard, a habit that matters far more to an online student than an in-person one.

Parents should still watch three things themselves during the trial class, since no verification process replaces watching a real lesson. First, whether the screen share is genuinely readable, not cramped or badly lit, since a poor whiteboard defeats the whole format regardless of how good the tutor's explanation is. Second, whether the tutor actively questions the student through the session rather than talking at them for the full slot, since a passive online lesson is far easier for a student to quietly disengage from than a home one. Third, whether anything is sent in writing afterward, a summary, a practice set or corrected working, since an online session leaves nothing physical behind for a parent to check later.

IB Gram also expects honest availability from a tutor rather than overcommitting and rescheduling repeatedly; a tutor who is frequently late to online sessions or cancels at short notice is flagged, and removed from future shortlists if the pattern continues.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does a Good Online Tutor Do Differently on a Screen?
contentBlocks.body:
A strong online tutor treats the screen as a tool rather than a limitation, and it shows in specific habits. They narrate their own working aloud while writing, since a student cannot glance across at a page the way they would in person and pick up context silently. They check understanding more often, asking short, direct questions every few minutes rather than a single check-in at the end, because it is easier for a student to nod along on video without the tutor noticing confusion the way they would from body language in a room. And they send something concrete after each session, a summary, an annotated page, a set of practice questions, since online students have no physical notebook for a parent to glance through later.

Certain tasks suit this format particularly well. Reading and annotating a past paper together, walking line by line through a mark scheme to see exactly where marks were lost, and drilling command terms, describe, explain, evaluate, justify, all work as well online as in a room, sometimes better, since the paper can be enlarged, highlighted and saved for the student to revisit later. Essay and response planning for English or humanities subjects also translates well through a shared document, where tutor and student build a structure together in real time.

Other tasks lose something. Watching a student's full working on a maths problem, catching a sign error or a misapplied formula the instant the pen touches paper, is genuinely harder when the tutor is reading a held-up notebook page or a photograph a few seconds delayed. Science practical technique, even the written Paper 6 route, benefits from a tutor physically demonstrating an apparatus setup rather than describing one down a camera. And a student who is anxious or easily distracted often needs a tutor's simple physical presence in the room to stay focused, something no amount of screen skill fully substitutes for.

A practical setup makes a bigger difference online than families expect: internet tested before the session rather than during it, a backup device on hand if the primary camera or microphone fails, past papers ready as a PDF before the lesson rather than searched for mid-session, a quiet room with the door shut since household noise carries clearly over a microphone, and headphones, which noticeably improve how well a student hears an explanation compared with laptop speakers in a shared room. A family can tell within three sessions whether the format and the tutor together are working: a student who reviews between sessions and asks specific follow-up questions is a student the format suits; one who logs on distracted and gives one-word answers is telling the family, without saying it outright, that something needs to change.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Know an Online Tutor Is Working as Well as a Home Tutor Would?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the first month rarely shows up as a grade jump, since a single school test can move for reasons that have nothing to do with tutoring. What a family should actually look for is narrower and more specific: a student who can explain, unprompted, what a command term like evaluate or justify genuinely requires in an answer, whose working on a Core or Extended paper shows fewer careless errors on exactly the question type the tutor has been drilling, and who starts a session by raising something they got wrong in a recent school test rather than waiting to be asked.

By the end of the first month, a reasonable tutor should be able to name two or three specific, recurring gaps, not a vague sense that the student is doing fine, but the precise paper, question type or command term that keeps costing marks, with an example pulled from a recent past paper to back it up. If a tutor cannot offer that after four weeks of weekly sessions, the sessions are probably not being planned with enough intent.

Honest limits apply regardless of format. No amount of online tutoring compensates for a student doing no independent work between sessions; a weekly call is not a substitute for practice done alone with a past paper during the week. A tutor also cannot catch every gap a school teacher would notice through daily classroom contact, simply because the hours spent together are far fewer. And no tutor, online or at home, can honestly promise a specific grade; what a family should expect instead is a clear, specific account of what has been covered, what has genuinely improved, and what is still unresolved before the next assessment.

If, after a full month, nothing specific has changed and the tutor cannot point to concrete progress, that is worth raising with IB Gram directly rather than persisting out of politeness; a different tutor, a different format, or a shorter and more focused session length is often the actual fix.

faqs.answer: For most tasks, past paper practice, exam technique, essay planning and revision, a strong online tutor performs just as well as a home tutor, and the same person is often available in both formats through IB Gram. Where online genuinely loses ground is watching a student's live handwritten working on a maths problem, something a tutor sitting beside the student catches instantly and one on a screen has to ask for photographs of instead. Whether an online tutor suits your child depends more on the student's age and independence than the subject itself, which is exactly why the free trial class exists before any term is booked.

faqs.answer: Say so directly rather than continuing sessions that are not helping; asking for a different tutor is a completely normal part of the process, not an exception to it. faqs.question: Do I need a laptop, or will a phone work for online IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a reasonably sized screen works considerably better than a phone, mainly because reading an annotated past paper or a worked solution on a shared whiteboard is genuinely harder on a small screen, and a squinting student loses focus faster than families expect. A phone can work occasionally, for a short revision call while travelling, but is not recommended as the regular setup for subjects like Mathematics or the sciences, where diagrams and working need to be read clearly. A stable connection matters more than the device itself; a strong laptop on a weak signal still produces a frustrating session.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow our school's own pacing or teach in their own order?
faqs.answer: A good online tutor works around the school's pacing rather than reteaching the whole syllabus independently, since duplicating what school is already covering wastes the limited weekly time available. IB Gram asks parents to share a school's term plan or recent test dates where possible, so the tutor can target upcoming assessments directly rather than starting from the syllabus's beginning regardless of where the class actually is. Where a student is genuinely behind the school's own pace, a good tutor says so honestly and proposes a short period of catching up on foundations before matching the class pace again.

faqs.question: My daughter is moving from CBSE to IGCSE partway through the year. Can an online tutor manage that switch?
faqs.answer: Yes, and IB Gram specifically looks for tutors who have supported a CBSE to IGCSE move before, not only tutors who have taught IGCSE from the start of Grade 9. The switch usually means adjusting to command-term based answers, evaluate, explain, describe, rather than the more formulaic answer patterns CBSE assessments often reward, and getting used to past paper practice as the central revision tool rather than a textbook exercise list. A tutor experienced with this transition typically opens with a diagnostic session on exactly this gap before building a catch-up plan for the rest of the term.

faqs.question: If our regular home tutor cannot make it one week, can the same tutor run the session online instead?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and this is exactly where a hybrid arrangement earns its place: the same tutor who normally teaches at home can run that week's session online instead, from wherever they or the family happen to be, without losing continuity or introducing someone unfamiliar with the student's progress. If a scheduled home session would otherwise be missed because of travel, illness or a corridor closed for roadwork, raising it with IB Gram in advance usually means the session moves online rather than being cancelled outright, which keeps that week's momentum intact.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on online sessions with a younger student?
faqs.answer: For a Grade 9 student new to online tutoring, staying nearby, not necessarily at the screen, for the first few sessions helps confirm the setup is working and the student is genuinely engaged rather than distracted by another tab or a phone. Most families step back after the second or third session once they see the routine holding, though remaining reachable in the next room is sensible for younger students in case the tutor needs to flag something directly. Older Grade 10 students preparing independently for exams typically need no supervision once the arrangement settles.

faqs.question: How is a live online tutor different from a recorded video course?
faqs.answer: A recorded video course is built for a wide audience, cannot answer a question, and cannot notice when a student is stuck on exactly the wrong step in a method. A live online tutor matched through IB Gram is chosen for this student's exact board, tier and school pace, and can see, in real time, when an explanation is not landing and adjust immediately rather than moving on regardless. A recorded course can supplement extra revision between live sessions, but it is not a substitute for a tutor who knows precisely what this particular student has and has not understood yet.

Regular weekly sessions can usually begin the same week the trial goes well, subject to tutor availability and the family's preferred slot. h1: IGCSE Online Tutors in Gurgaon: How to Compare and Shortlist
heroTitle: Weighing Up IGCSE Online Tutors in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Two profiles can look identical and teach nothing alike. This page sets out how a short list of two or three verified online tutors is assembled, the seven lines to score each of them on, how to trial two in consecutive weeks, and how to change tutor later without losing the work already done.
introSummary: Comparing IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon is a different exercise from hiring one, and most families here are really choosing between an online candidate and a home tuition candidate rather than between two screens. The board, the tier and the papers involved are specific enough that a vague shortlist wastes weeks of Grade 9 or Grade 10 time. What follows is a method: two or three verified profiles rather than a directory, each showing the same fields, each pinned to the same syllabus code, each trialled on the same student with the same starting material, and a clear way of changing your mind afterwards if the first choice turns out wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: How do two or three IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon reach your shortlist?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon are filtered by four things before you ever see a name: the exact board and syllabus, the tier the school has entered the student for, the subjects that are genuinely costing marks, and the evening slots the household can hold week after week. Send a query or book a free consultation and those are the questions IB Gram asks, along with your location and the school's calendar. What returns is a short list, not a directory.

The reason for stopping at three is practical rather than philosophical. Grade 10 has a fixed number of weeks in it. A family that spends a month interviewing candidates has spent a month, and the student has sat through it. Three profiles produce visible differences within a single reading; eight produce a spreadsheet nobody finishes.

For comparison to mean anything, the profiles have to carry the same fields. Which board, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Which papers the tutor has actually taught, by code where possible. Which tier, Core or Extended, and how recently. Which format they offer, online only or online and home. Which evenings they can hold, and what happens on the days they cannot. A profile that lists subjects without levels is not comparable with anything.

Availability stays conditional throughout, and it depends on subject, tier and the days you need. That is not a hedge; it is why the shortlist is short. A demo or trial session can be arranged with each candidate before the family commits, and if none of the three suits, asking for a fresh shortlist is a normal request rather than a complaint.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with board, tier and subjects
2. IB Gram asks about syllabus codes, school calendar, location and workable evenings
3. Two or three verified profiles arrive, each carrying identical comparison fields
4. Trial the two candidates you cannot separate on paper, in consecutive weeks
5. Score both on the same seven lines and choose deliberately
6. Lessons run online, at home or hybrid, and the match can be changed

contentBlocks.heading: Boards, tiers and series: pinning every candidate to the same target
contentBlocks.body:
Before a single profile is compared, the target has to be fixed, because candidates who are aiming at slightly different things cannot be judged against each other. IGCSE in Gurgaon means either Cambridge IGCSE, offered by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, normally taken across Grades 9 and 10 and normally followed by the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11.

The series decides the runway, so put it in the brief you give every candidate. Cambridge series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, in May and June, and in October and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and in May and June. A candidate planning for May when the school has entered a February and March series has already given you the wrong answer, and that is useful to discover at the shortlist stage rather than in November.

Tiering changes what any tutor can honestly promise. Many Cambridge subjects are split into Core and Extended, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some syllabuses have 9 to 1 versions under different codes, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Ask each candidate what they would do differently for a Core entry than an Extended one. A specialist answers in terms of question types; a generalist answers in terms of effort.

One more line belongs in the brief: where the student is going after Grade 10. A student heading for the IB Diploma Programme needs different habits built in Grade 10 from one heading to CBSE Class 11, and an IGCSE Grade 9 and 10 tutor who asks about that unprompted is thinking beyond the next paper.
items: Fix board, tier, syllabus code and series before comparing any profiles
Cambridge: February and March in India, May and June, October and November
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: January, then May and June
Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*
Ask each candidate how a Core plan differs from an Extended one
Say where the student goes after Grade 10: IB DP, A Levels, CBSE or ISC

contentBlocks.heading: Which papers should each candidate already have taught?
contentBlocks.body:
Not subjects, papers. This is the question that separates two profiles faster than anything else, and it is easy to ask. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 from the 2025 examinations, Core candidates sit Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, calculator, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4, calculator. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher with two calculator papers per tier. Ask which of those a candidate has taught this year, not in their career.

The sciences make the point sharper. Cambridge IGCSE sciences examined from 2023 run Paper 1 multiple choice at Core or Paper 2 at Extended, Paper 3 theory at Core or Paper 4 at Extended, and a practical component that is either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, with the school choosing. The weighting is multiple choice 30 per cent, theory 50 per cent, practical 20 per cent. A candidate who has prepared students for Paper 6 knows it is a written paper about method, tables, graphs and error, and will say so. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for each separate science and practical skills assessed inside the written papers.

English is where shortlists most often contain a hidden mismatch. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 pairs a reading paper with directed writing and composition, or with a coursework portfolio. English as a Second Language is 0510 and 0511, both covering reading, writing and listening, with 0511 counting speaking into the grade while 0510 reports speaking separately. Literature in English is 0475. Pearson Edexcel offers English Language A as 4EA1, English Language B as 4EB1 and English as a Second Language as 4ES1. Two candidates confident about English can still be confident about different qualifications.

When the subject is scarce, expect the shortlist to be shorter and be willing to accept an online-only candidate. That is usually the honest trade: fewer options, better subject match, no home fallback.

0580 Extended is Paper 2 and Paper 4; Core is Paper 1 and Paper 3
Cambridge science weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%
Paper 6 is written method, tables, graphs and sources of error
Confirm the English route: 0500, 0510, 0511, 0475, 4EA1, 4EB1 or 4ES1
Scarce subjects mean shorter shortlists and often online-only candidates

contentBlocks.heading: Sushant Lok to SPR: what your address still decides about home classes
contentBlocks.body:
Even when every candidate teaches on a screen, the address shapes the shortlist, because it determines whether you have a home fallback at all. In Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana that difference is stark across three corridors.

The DLF Phase 2, DLF Phase 3 and DLF Phase 4 belt, together with MG Road, Cyber City, Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur, Sector 24, Sector 27 and Sector 28, and societies such as DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona, has plenty of tutors within reach. Families searching for igcse online tutors DLF Phase 3 are usually choosing online for a reason of their own, most often a scarce subject or a slot after eight. That means the shortlist can reasonably include one online candidate and one home candidate, and comparing across formats is worth doing rather than avoiding.

Sushant Lok 1, Sushant Lok 2, South City 1, Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City sit around Millennium City Centre with short internal roads, which is why home classes here are straightforward and why an igcse online tutors Sushant Lok search often comes from a family whose Grade 10 child simply finishes school too late to host anyone at six. Here the sensible shortlist is two online candidates and one hybrid, so the weekend home session stays available.

The Southern Peripheral Road corridor is different again. Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 70 and Sector 72, along with Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and Tata Primanti, sit far enough out that a midweek home visit costs a tutor a whole second lesson. Families looking at igcse online tutors Southern Peripheral Road should treat online as the primary format and any home session as a weekend bonus. Shortlisting a home tutor here as the main option usually produces a slot that erodes by twenty minutes a month until somebody gives up.

contentBlocks.heading: Give every candidate the same Gurgaon school calendar
contentBlocks.body:
Hand all three profiles the identical brief and read what comes back, because a plan is more revealing than a curriculum vitae. Families at international schools here mention names such as Pathways World School, Aravali; Pathways School Gurgaon; Lancers International School; Scottish High International School; GD Goenka World School; Heritage Xperiential Learning School; The Shri Ram School, Aravali; and DPS International Edge. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the International Baccalaureate, and nothing here states what any school teaches.

The brief should contain five items and nothing decorative: board and syllabus codes, tier by subject, the school's Grade 10 mock dates, the entered series, and the evenings that are already taken by sport, music or service commitments. Send it to every candidate in the same words. One will respond with a rough sequence working backwards from the mocks. One will ask a sharp question you had not considered. One will say they will assess in the first session. Those three answers are your first real comparison, and it costs you nothing.

School timings matter even for screen lessons, though differently. A student returning late does not delay an online tutor's travel, but a tired student at half past eight learns less than a rested one at seven. Ask each candidate what time they think is too late for this particular child, and note who is willing to say a slot is a bad idea rather than simply accepting the booking.

Disruption is the other test. A sports week, a school trip or an examination week will break the routine at some point. Ask each candidate how they intend to handle a fortnight with only one available evening. A tutor who has taught Gurgaon families through a full year will have an answer ready; a tutor who has not will treat the question as unlikely.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, a screen, or both: which format are you comparing within?
contentBlocks.body:
Settle this before reading a single profile, because comparing a home tutor against an online tutor on the same scorecard produces a muddle. Home tuition remains the format most Gurgaon parents want first, and for good reason. A tutor at the table sees the pen stop, notices the question being misread, and holds a Grade 9 student who would otherwise be half watching something else. Home classes also make the practical side of family life simpler, since nobody has to police a device.

Live online changes the population of available tutors rather than the quality of teaching. It is the only sensible primary format in the outer sectors, it opens up a Cambridge IGCSE tutor Gurgaon families could not otherwise reach, and it makes extra sessions before mocks physically possible because nobody is driving. Its weakness is attention, and that weakness is specific to the student rather than to the format. Some fourteen-year-olds work perfectly well on a screen. Others need a person in the room and will not admit it.

Hybrid is what a large share of families settle on: one home session each week where marked work is gone through face to face, and one or two online for practice, doubt-solving and timed papers. If hybrid is what you want, say so in the query, because it changes the shortlist. Only some candidates offer both formats, and comparing a screen-only tutor with one who can also visit is comparing two different propositions.

Stated plainly, so it can be quoted on its own: home tuition gives the most attention and the smallest pool of tutors; online gives the largest pool and the least control over attention; hybrid gives most of both and requires the household to run two slightly different routines each week. Choose the format first, then compare candidates inside it.
items: Decide the format first; scoring across formats produces a muddle
Home classes hold a distracted Grade 9 student better than any screen
Online widens the pool and makes extra pre-mock sessions possible
Hybrid: one home session weekly, one or two online, stated in the query
Only some candidates offer both formats, which narrows a hybrid shortlist
Attention is a fact about the student, not a flaw in the format

contentBlocks.heading: What do two verified profiles tell you when read side by side?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification means IB Gram has checked identity and qualification documents and confirmed the boards and levels a tutor claims to teach, before the profile is shortlisted. Read side by side, two verified profiles tell you where the candidates genuinely differ rather than where they describe themselves differently, which is the whole value of comparing rather than hiring.

Look for the gaps that only appear in contrast. One candidate lists Extended Mathematics and the other lists Mathematics; that is not the same claim. One names paper codes and the other names topics. One states which years they taught most recently and the other gives a total. Where two profiles describe the same thing at different levels of precision, the precise one is usually the one that has taught it lately.

Online arrangements need checks that a home visit makes unnecessary. Ask both candidates which platform they use, whether they write with a tablet or a pen display, how annotated past papers reach you afterwards, whether sessions are recorded and who holds the recordings, and what happens when a connection drops mid-lesson. Put the five questions to both and compare the answers rather than accepting each in isolation.

Family-side checks stay the same across candidates. Online lessons belong in a shared room with the camera on for both parties, not behind a closed bedroom door. If a hybrid arrangement is planned, register the chosen tutor at the society gate as a standing visitor before the first home session, which in a managed society is a single visit to the facility desk. Agree days, session length, notice for cancellation and what happens during illness in a written message before any money changes hands.
items: Identity, qualifications and claimed boards are verified before shortlisting
Compare precision: paper codes and recent years beat topic lists and totals
Put the same five online questions to every candidate, then compare
Agree recording, platform and dropped-connection rules in advance
Keep online lessons in a shared room with cameras on both sides
Register the chosen tutor at the gate only if home sessions are planned

contentBlocks.heading: Scoring IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon on the same seven lines
contentBlocks.body:
Score IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon on seven lines, one to three each, filled in the same sitting for every candidate. Paper-level experience: which codes, which tier, how recently. Board precision: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and whether they can name the difference in the papers rather than in the name. Diagnosis: can they say, from the marked work you sent, what is actually going wrong. Slot reliability: which evenings, and what happens in a disrupted fortnight. Written feedback: what arrives after each session, in what form. Independent work: what the student must do between lessons and what happens if it is not done. Format: online only, or online and home.

Then apply one rule that saves families months. Do not choose on the highest total. Choose by eliminating any candidate scoring one on a line your household cannot absorb. A superb Extended Mathematics tutor who can only manage nine o'clock is the wrong answer for a tired Grade 9 student, whatever the other six lines say. A merely good tutor who is reliably there on two protected evenings will deliver more across a year than a brilliant one who is present two weeks in three.

Two lines that families weight far too heavily deserve a warning. Total years in teaching is a weak signal once a candidate has a few years behind them, because teaching CBSE Class 10 for a decade is not the same as teaching Cambridge Extended papers. And rapport in a first phone call is the easiest quality in the world to produce. Parents hunting for the best igcse online tutors in Gurgaon on the strength of a warm conversation usually find themselves back at this table in the new year.

The seventh line is the one nobody asks about and the one that predicts most. What does the tutor expect the student to do in the hours they are not teaching, and how will they know whether it happened? A candidate who has thought about the other six days is planning a course. A candidate who has not is planning a sequence of hours.
items: Seven lines: papers, board, diagnosis, slot, feedback, independent work, format
Score one to three, in the same sitting, for every candidate
Eliminate on low scores your household cannot absorb, not on totals
Total years teaching is weak; years on these papers is strong
Ask what happens in the six days the tutor is not teaching
A warm first call predicts almost nothing about week nine

contentBlocks.heading: Trialling two tutors online in consecutive weeks
contentBlocks.body:
Trial IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon a week apart rather than back to back, and tell the student exactly what is happening before either one. Two teachers, one will continue, the choice belongs to the family, and nothing about it is a judgement on the child. Students cope with this easily when it is said out loud and badly when they work it out halfway through the second lesson.

Give both candidates the identical starting material: the same recent marked paper, the same topic the student finds hardest, and the same request to spend at least half the session making the student work rather than listening. Then step out of the room. What you are measuring is how each tutor teaches this student, and a parent visible on camera changes that measurement.

Afterwards, three observations decide it. Did the tutor name a specific weakness, with a paper and a question type attached, or did they report that the child is bright and needs practice. Did the student write anything during the lesson. And did the annotated paper arrive afterwards as promised. A candidate who fails the third test in a trial will fail it in February too.

Once the choice is made, judge progress on a realistic clock. By week six expect the student to attempt questions before asking, a folder of timed papers that is filling rather than empty, and marks on comparable past papers that can be shown to you as numbers. Grades themselves move on the school's own mock timetable. No tutor can guarantee a grade, the tier entry sets a ceiling the school decides, and a candidate who promises otherwise during a trial has told you where to put them on the list.
items: Trial a week apart and tell the student the plan beforehand
Give both tutors the same marked paper and the same hard topic
Leave the room; a visible parent changes what you are measuring
Check whether the annotated paper actually arrives after the trial
Week six: a filling folder of timed papers and raw marks to show
A candidate promising a specific grade has settled the comparison for you

contentBlocks.heading: Changing tutor in Gurgaon without losing the folder or the slot
contentBlocks.body:
If the match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is shortlisted. Do it in week three, not week eleven. Families hesitate because the tutor has been perfectly pleasant, and pleasantness is not the thing you were buying.

Name the reason precisely, because it shapes the replacement. Wrong tier or wrong papers means pinning the next candidate to exact codes. Unreliable attendance means weighting slot reliability above everything else. A student who has stopped speaking during lessons means the trial itself must carry more weight next time. An online arrangement that never produced independent work may not need a different tutor at all; it may need a move to home classes or hybrid.

Protect two things through the change. The first is the folder: ask the outgoing tutor for the annotated papers and a short note listing topics covered and weaknesses observed, and hand it to the incoming one. Online tutoring makes this easy, because the material is already in one shared place rather than scattered through three notebooks. The second is the slot. A protected evening is harder to rebuild than a tutor, so keep the time and change the person.

When you are ready, send a query or book a free consultation with the board, syllabus codes, tier, subjects and the evenings you can hold. Whether the shortlist ends with a Cambridge specialist, an Edexcel IGCSE tutor Gurugram families found through the same process, or a hybrid arrangement mixing a screen with one home session, the method does not change. Compare two or three, trial them on the same student, score them on the same lines, and choose the one who taught.
items: Raise a wrong match in week three, when it costs almost nothing
Name the reason: tier, papers, reliability or rapport
Collect the annotated papers and a handover note from the outgoing tutor
Keep the protected evening and change the person, not the time
Consider a format change before assuming the tutor is the problem

faqs.question: Can we shortlist one online tutor and one home tutor together?
faqs.answer: You can, but score them separately rather than on one list. The two propositions differ on reach, attention and reliability, so a single ranking hides the trade-off you are actually making. A cleaner method is to decide the format first, shortlist two candidates inside it, and keep the other format as a named fallback. Families in DLF Phase 3 or Sushant Lok often do exactly this, because both options are genuinely available there and the decision deserves to be made once rather than drifted into.

faqs.question: How do we compare two candidates who have taught different boards?
faqs.answer: Treat it as disqualifying unless the school's entry is still undecided. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE differ in papers, tiering and grading, so a candidate strong on one is not automatically useful on the other. Confirm the board and syllabus code with the school first, then require every shortlisted candidate to have taught that board recently. A tutor who says the boards are broadly similar is telling you they have not taught both, which is fine to hear early and expensive to discover in January.

faqs.question: Should both trial lessons happen in the same week?
faqs.answer: A week apart works better for most students. Back-to-back trials tire a Grade 10 child and turn the second tutor into an unfair comparison against a fresh memory. Consecutive weeks give the student a normal evening in between and let you see each lesson on its own terms. Keep everything else identical: same marked paper, same difficult topic, same instruction that the student should be working for at least half the hour. Confirm your decision within a few days of the second trial.

faqs.question: What if the student prefers one tutor and we prefer the other?
faqs.answer: Ask the student for reasons, not preferences, and weigh what you hear. A student who says one tutor explained the part they never understood is giving you real evidence. A student who prefers the tutor who asked less of them is giving you the opposite. Where the reasons are thin on both sides, take the one the student will engage with, because an hour with a tutor a teenager quietly resents produces very little. Where the student's reason is avoidance, say so plainly and choose the other one.

faqs.question: Our society in Sector 45 has strict visitor rules. Does that affect a hybrid shortlist?
faqs.answer: It affects only the home half, and only once. Register the chosen tutor at the facility office or with the guard as a standing visitor, giving name, phone number and a photograph, before the first home session rather than while the tutor waits at the gate. In managed societies around Sushant Lok, South City 1 or Tata Primanti this takes one short visit. After that, weekend home classes can be added at short notice, which is what makes a hybrid arrangement worth shortlisting in the first place.

faqs.question: Can a tutor from the SPR sectors still come home occasionally?
faqs.answer: For a weekend session, often yes; for a weekday evening, rarely on a reliable basis. Sector 66 through Sector 72, Ansal Esencia and Bhondsi sit far enough out that a midweek visit consumes a tutor's whole second lesson, so the slot tends to slip later and later. Families here get better results treating online as the primary format and booking home classes on a Saturday or Sunday morning. Ask each shortlisted candidate directly whether they will commit to a weekend visit, and how often.

faqs.question: How many subjects should one shortlisted tutor cover?
faqs.answer: One, or two if they are genuinely close. A candidate offering Mathematics, Chemistry and English together is usually strong in one of them and adequate in the rest, and adequate is expensive over two years. Running separate shortlists per subject takes an extra conversation and gives a better result, and it lets you replace one subject's tutor later without disturbing the other. It also spreads the evenings, so no single night carries two hours of tuition after a full school day.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches only online a weaker choice than one who does both?
faqs.answer: Not weaker, just narrower, and the difference matters only if you want a fallback. An online-only specialist may be exactly the right person for a scarce subject, and refusing them on format alone can cost you the best available match. What you lose is the option of moving a session to the table during a difficult fortnight. If your corridor offers no realistic home tutors anyway, that loss is theoretical and the online-only candidate should be scored on teaching alone.

faqs.question: What written feedback should we expect after each session?
faqs.answer: Two or three lines, reliably, is enough, and the reliability matters more than the length. It should say what was covered, what the student found hard, and what has been set before the next lesson. Annotated past papers should come back in the same shared folder each time rather than as photographs scattered through a chat. Ask each candidate for this during the trial and then check whether it actually arrived. A tutor who forgets after a trial lesson will forget in February.

faqs.question: How long should we give a new tutor before deciding it is not working?
faqs.answer: Six weeks, with one honest checkpoint at three. At three weeks you are judging the arrangement: is the slot holding, is work being set, is feedback arriving. At six you are judging the teaching: can the student attempt questions before asking, is there a folder of marked timed papers, can the tutor name weaknesses by paper and question type. If week three looks wrong, raise it then. Waiting until a term has passed rarely produces a different answer, only a later one.

faqs.question: Can we keep the same evening slot if we change tutor mid-year?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is worth insisting on. A protected weekday evening is harder to rebuild than a tutor, because the household has already arranged dinner, siblings and everything else around it. Tell IB Gram the slot is fixed and the person is what needs changing, and the next shortlist can be filtered on that. Hand the incoming tutor the annotated papers and a short handover note from the outgoing one, so the first session continues the work instead of starting the diagnosis again.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches an IGCSE Online Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A query for igcse online tuition gurgaon usually starts with one detail missing: which board, which tier, and which paper the student is stuck on. IB Gram asks for the syllabus (Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE), the grade, whether the school has placed the student in Core or Extended for a subject like Mathematics 0580 or the sciences, and the school's own test and mock calendar so sessions land before assessments rather than after them.

From there the shortlisting is specific rather than generic. A tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Physics is not automatically the right match for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics; the syllabus content overlaps but the paper structure, command terms and practical assessment route do not. IB Gram checks that a shortlisted tutor has taught the exact syllabus and tier the student sits, not a neighbouring one, before a profile is sent to a parent.

A free trial class follows, run online exactly as regular sessions would run, so the family sees the actual lesson rather than a sales call. The tutor works through one real topic the student is behind on, using the school's own textbook or a recent test paper if the parent shares it beforehand. Parents typically see how the tutor manages the screen, how clearly they explain a method, and whether the student stays engaged for the full slot.

After the trial, IB Gram asks directly whether the fit feels right before booking a term of lessons. If a student needs a different personality, a stricter pace, or simply a tutor free at a later slot because school activities run until seven, a second profile is offered rather than persisting with a poor match. This is how a shortlist becomes a committed tutor for the term.
items: 1. Parent shares board, tier, grade and the school's test dates for the term.
2. IB Gram shortlists two or three verified specialists on that exact syllabus.
3. A free trial class runs online, on one real topic the student is behind on.
4. Parent and student confirm the match, or ask for a different tutor.
5. Regular weekly slots are booked around the school's own timetable.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel: Which Programme Fits an Online Lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon international schools run one of two IGCSE programmes, and an online tutor needs to know which before the first slide is shared. Cambridge IGCSE (set by Cambridge International Education) usually runs across Grade 9 and Grade 10, is examined in three series a year, February/March, May/June and October/November, and grades most syllabuses A* to G, though some subjects now sit newer 9-1 versions under different codes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs on a similar two-year structure, is examined in January and May/June, and grades throughout on the 9-1 scale. A tutor who has only ever taught one board can still teach the other competently, but the first online session should confirm which one applies, since past papers, command terms and mark scheme language differ.

Within Cambridge, many subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, decided by the school, not the family, usually by the end of Grade 9. Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A* but is harder to pass cleanly if the content is not secure. An online tutor working from a screen share can pull up both tier's past papers side by side, which is genuinely easier to demonstrate on a shared screen than flipping between two printed booklets during a home visit.

What online tuition does well here is comparing syllabuses quickly: showing a student the Core Paper 1 non-calculator format next to the Extended Paper 2 equivalent, or pulling up an Edexcel 4MA1 Higher tier paper alongside a Cambridge Extended one when a family is deciding whether to move boards. What it does less well is reading a student's handwriting on scratch working in real time; a tutor has to ask the student to hold pages up to the camera or photograph and share them, which slows a maths session down compared with sitting beside the student's notebook.

Students typically move on from IGCSE into the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or back into CBSE or ISC for Class 11, and an online tutor who has taught that transition before can flag, a term ahead, which Grade 10 habits will or will not carry over.

contentBlocks.heading: What an IGCSE Online Tutor Actually Teaches, Paper by Paper
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, splits by tier: Core candidates sit Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, calculator; Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4, calculator. On screen this means a tutor drills non-calculator method and layout separately from calculator technique, because the non-calculator paper punishes messy working that a calculator paper would forgive. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier, so the non-calculator discipline Cambridge students need is less of a focus for an Edexcel student, and a tutor moving a family between boards should flag that difference early rather than assume the same drills apply.

Cambridge IGCSE sciences, in syllabuses examined from 2023, are assessed through a multiple choice paper (Paper 1 for Core, Paper 2 for Extended), a theory paper (Paper 3 or Paper 4), and a practical route chosen by the school, either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. The weighting is fixed: multiple choice contributes 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%. An online tutor cannot run the practical component itself, since Paper 5 and Paper 6 are sat under exam conditions at school, but can drill the alternative-to-practical question style, which rewards a student who has memorised apparatus diagrams and can describe a method precisely in writing, a skill that transfers well to a screen. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, examined through Paper 1 and Paper 2, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical route.

English at IGCSE varies more than families expect. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 combines a reading paper with directed writing and composition, or a coursework portfolio depending on the school's choice. English as a Second Language runs as two syllabuses, 0510 and 0511, both covering reading, writing and listening, but 0511 folds a speaking assessment into the overall grade while 0510 reports speaking separately. Literature in English 0475 sits alongside these for schools that offer it. Pearson Edexcel offers its own trio: International GCSE English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1), and English as a Second Language (4ES1). An online tutor confirms the exact syllabus code before planning a term, because 0510 and 0511 preparation genuinely differ.

Cambridge 0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator plus Paper 4 calculator.
Cambridge sciences: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20% of the final grade.
Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, assessed through Paper 1 and Paper 2 only.
English as a Second Language splits into 0510 and 0511, differing in how speaking is reported.
Edexcel English offers three separate syllabus codes: 4EA1, 4EB1 and 4ES1.

Along the Dwarka Expressway, spanning Sector 102, 103, 104, 106, 108, 109, 110 and 113, and societies such as Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, construction traffic and a still-developing road network make evening home visits genuinely inconsistent, which is one honest reason igcse online tuition Dwarka Expressway searches are common from this stretch of the city. contentBlocks.heading: School Calendars That Shape an IGCSE Online Timetable in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana sending a child through Grade 9 and 10 at schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge live inside a school calendar that an online tutor has to work around rather than compete with, and this section describes those pressures in general terms, not what any one school teaches.

International schools in Gurgaon typically run internal assessments, unit tests and half-yearly or pre-board style exams at points the family only learns about a term ahead, often clustered before winter break and again before the summer holidays. An online tutor who has worked with Grade 9 and 10 students across several school years learns to ask for the school's own assessment calendar at the start of a term and pace revision backward from it, rather than running a generic syllabus-order course that peaks at the wrong moment.

Co-curricular commitments are a genuine scheduling pressure too. Many Gurgaon schools run sport, music, Model United Nations and other activities into the early evening, and a student arriving home at 6:30pm with homework still to finish has little appetite left for a home tutor arriving at 7. An online slot at 8 or 8:30pm, after dinner, is often the only realistic window, and it is one that a home tutor cannot always offer once their own evening travel is factored in, since a 9pm arrival home is a lot to ask of anyone crossing the city.

Exam season itself adds a different pressure. In the weeks before Cambridge's May/June series or Pearson Edexcel's own May/June papers, students are often revising three or four subjects at once, and an online tutor can be booked for a short, focused 45-minute session on a single weak topic between school hours without the overhead of a full travel visit, which matters when every hour before a paper counts.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutor, Online Tutor or Hybrid: What Actually Works for IGCSE?
contentBlocks.body:
For most Gurgaon families, the honest starting point is home tuition: a tutor sitting beside the student, reading their working in real time, and correcting a habit the moment it happens. For a younger or less independent Grade 9 student, or for a subject like Mathematics where seeing exactly how a student sets out a calculation matters, home tutoring still has a real edge that no amount of screen sharing fully closes. IB Gram's default recommendation for a student who has never worked with a tutor before is often a home tutor for the first month, simply because it is easier to build a working relationship in person.

Online tuition earns its place once that relationship exists, or once the constraint is genuinely practical rather than pedagogical: no specialist tutor for a smaller syllabus like Literature in English 0475 within reach, an evening schedule that only leaves a late slot free, or a family living along a corridor like the Dwarka Expressway where travel time varies too much to promise a fixed arrival. Screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and a document camera for handwritten working cover most of what a home lesson does; what they do not fully replace is a tutor glancing at a student's posture or noticing they have stopped writing three minutes ago, out of frame.

Hybrid tuition, home sessions plus online sessions with the same tutor, is the honest middle option and often the most practical one in Gurgaon. A family might keep a weekly home session for steady subject-building and add an online session in exam weeks purely for past paper practice, without changing tutors or losing continuity. The same person who knows the student's weak topics from the sofa can run a focused past-paper session on a laptop three days before a test.

The trade-off is straightforward to state: home tutoring costs more travel time and depends on the corridor and the traffic that day; online tuition removes that constraint entirely but asks more of the student's own focus and camera discipline; hybrid keeps both options open with one tutor but needs a family willing to manage two formats. None of the three is universally better; the right one depends on the subject, the student's age, and which corridor the family lives in.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Verifies an Online IGCSE Tutor Before the First Class
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor's profile reaches a parent, IB Gram checks that the syllabus and tier claimed on the profile match what the tutor has actually taught, asking for specifics rather than accepting a general claim of IGCSE experience. A tutor who says they teach Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics should be able to name the difference between Core Paper 1 and Extended Paper 2 without prompting; one who cannot is not shortlisted for that subject, whatever else their profile says.

For an online tutor specifically, IB Gram also checks that the tutor has actually taught over video before, not only in person, since the two are genuinely different skills. A tutor who is excellent in a room can be flat and hard to follow on a screen if they have never learned to narrate their own working aloud while writing, which matters far more online than it does sitting beside a student.

Parents should still check three things themselves during the trial class, because no verification process replaces watching a lesson happen. First, whether the tutor shares their screen cleanly and the student can actually read what is written, since a cramped or badly lit whiteboard defeats the format. Second, whether the tutor asks the student questions rather than talking through the whole session, since a passive online lesson is far easier for a student to disengage from than a home one. Third, whether the tutor sends anything in writing afterward, a summary, a set of practice questions, or corrected working, since online sessions leave no physical notebook behind for the parent to glance at later.

IB Gram also asks that a tutor confirm availability honestly rather than accepting every family and rescheduling later; a tutor who is regularly late to online sessions or cancels at short notice is flagged and, if it continues, removed from future shortlists. None of this guarantees a perfect match on the first try, which is why the trial class exists before any term is booked.

contentBlocks.heading: What Works on a Screen for IGCSE, and What a Home Tutor Still Does Better?
contentBlocks.body:
Some IGCSE tasks translate to a screen almost without loss. Reading and annotating a past paper together, working line by line through a mark scheme to see exactly where marks were lost, and drilling command terms such as describe, explain, evaluate and justify are all things an online tutor does as well as, and sometimes better than, an in-person one, because the paper itself can be enlarged, highlighted and saved for the student to revisit. Essay planning for English or humanities subjects also works well online: a shared document lets a tutor and student build a plan together in real time, watching the structure take shape rather than one person writing while the other watches.

Other tasks lose something on a screen. Watching a student's full working on a maths problem, catching a sign error or a misapplied formula the moment the pen touches paper, is harder when the tutor is reading a photograph or a held-up notebook page a few seconds delayed. Science practical technique, even the theory version tested through Paper 6, benefits from a tutor physically demonstrating an apparatus setup rather than describing one on a call. And a student who is anxious or easily distracted often needs the simple physical presence of a tutor in the room to stay on task, something a screen cannot fully substitute for, however good the lesson content is.

A practical setup checklist matters more for online IGCSE lessons than families expect. A stable internet connection tested before the session, not during it; a second device or a phone as backup if the laptop's camera or microphone fails; a printed or PDF copy of the topic's past papers ready before the lesson starts rather than searched for mid-session; a quiet room with the door closed, since younger siblings and television noise carry clearly over a microphone; and headphones, which noticeably improve how well a student can hear a tutor's explanation compared with laptop speakers in a shared room.

Parents can tell within three sessions whether online tuition is working. A student who arrives to the second and third session having actually looked at what was covered in the first, who can explain in their own words what was corrected last time, and who is not visibly restless twenty minutes in, is a student the format suits. A student who logs on distracted, gives one-word answers, and shows no sign of reviewing between sessions is usually telling the family, without saying it directly, that a home tutor or a hybrid arrangement would serve them better.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Know Online Tuition Is Working After Three Sessions?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the first month of IGCSE online tuition rarely looks like a grade jump, because grades move slowly and a single test result can be affected by many things beyond tutoring. What a family should look for instead is more specific: a student who can, unprompted, explain what a past command term like evaluate or justify actually requires in an answer; one whose working on a Core or Extended paper shows fewer careless errors on the type of question the tutor has been drilling; and one who starts a session by asking about something they got wrong in a school test, rather than waiting for the tutor to raise it.

By the end of the first month, a reasonable expectation is a clearer sense of where the student's actual gaps are, not just the topics they find hard in general, but the specific paper, question type or command term that consistently costs marks. A tutor who has been paying attention should be able to name two or three of these precisely, with an example from a recent past paper, rather than offering a vague sense that the student is improving.

Honest limits matter here too. Online tuition will not compensate for a student who does no independent work between sessions; a weekly 60-minute call cannot substitute for the practice a student does alone with a past paper during the week. It also will not diagnose every gap a school teacher would catch during daily classroom contact, since a tutor sees far fewer hours with the student than a subject teacher does. And no tutor, online or in person, can promise a specific grade; what a family should expect instead is a clear account of what has been covered, what has improved, and what is still unresolved going into the next assessment.

If after a full month a parent genuinely cannot point to anything specific that has changed, that is worth raising directly with IB Gram rather than assuming it will resolve itself; a different tutor, a different format, or a shorter, more focused session length is often the fix.
items: Unprompted use of command terms like evaluate or justify is a clearer sign than a single test score.
By four weeks, a tutor should name two or three specific, recurring error types, not a vague impression.
A weekly online session cannot replace independent practice between sessions.
