faqs.question: Which corridors of Gurgaon suit a home visit, and which suit online better?
faqs.answer: Central, well-connected corridors such as DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road, Cyber City, Sushant Lok and South City 1 generally have enough home tutors to make an evening visit realistic. Corridors that are longer, newer or further out, including Sohna Road's far end near Badshahpur, the Dwarka Expressway, New Gurgaon, the Southern Peripheral Road, and Manesar and NH-48 south, tend to have thinner home tutor coverage, and online is often the more dependable weekly option there rather than a fallback. Golf Course Road and Golf Course Extension Road usually support both formats comfortably given how central they sit. The honest answer, in every case, is to ask during the intake call rather than assume, since coverage shifts as more tutors join a corridor over time.

faqs.question: How do I fix a stable weekly online slot that does not keep slipping?
faqs.answer: Pick a weekday evening window with real margin around it, not the earliest moment school and activities technically end, and test your connection and device at that exact hour once before the first real session. Treat the first two or three sessions as a trial of the slot itself as much as the tutor, watching whether the lesson actually starts on time and whether the household routine leaves the student alert rather than exhausted. If the slot keeps slipping because of a recurring clash, such as a weekly activity that runs long, change the day or time itself rather than hoping persistence fixes it. A slot protected early tends to hold for the rest of the term; one that slips in the first two weeks rarely self-corrects.

faqs.question: Which corridors pair well in one tutor's weekly route?
faqs.answer: Golf Course Road and Golf Course Extension Road sit close enough that a tutor doing home visits often serves both in one evening, and the same applies to Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the DLF phases around Cyber City, which cluster centrally. Online removes this constraint almost entirely: a tutor based centrally in Gurgaon can add a family on the Dwarka Expressway or in New Gurgaon without a travel cost at all, which is one reason online reaches those newer corridors faster than home coverage has. Pairing still matters for scheduling rather than travel, though, since a tutor juggling several families across a week plans around everyone's slot, not just yours.

faqs.question: Does gate entry or traffic affect an online lesson?
faqs.answer: Not directly, since there is no visitor to register and no drive to make, which is exactly why online works well for corridors like Golf Course Road where society gate registration can eat into a tight after-school window for a home visit. What traffic does still affect is a tutor's own evening, if they are also doing home visits elsewhere in Gurgaon before or after your online slot; a tutor running late from a Sohna Road visit can still affect your session's start time even though you are not the one driving anywhere. Confirming a tutor's evening schedule honestly during the intake call avoids this kind of indirect delay.

faqs.question: If online is not working, can we switch to a home tutor instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a genuinely common switch rather than an unusual request. Tell IB Gram specifically what is not working, whether it is a student losing focus on screen, a connection that keeps failing at the same time each week, or simply a preference for someone physically present, and ask for a shortlist built around home tuition in your corridor instead. The intake details you already gave, board, level, syllabus and school calendar, carry over, so the switch does not mean starting from zero. Families on well-covered corridors such as DLF Phases 2 to 4 or Sushant Lok usually find a home tutor quickly; families further out may be offered a hybrid arrangement instead.

faqs.question: What device and internet setup does IGCSE online tuition actually need?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a stable camera and microphone, a reliable broadband connection, and a quiet space with decent lighting cover most of what a session needs; a phone works for a quick catch-up but is a poor fit for a full session involving a shared whiteboard and annotated past papers. Test the setup at the actual time your sessions will run, not at a different, quieter hour, since Gurgaon's evening broadband load can differ noticeably from a weekend afternoon test. A second device or a mobile hotspot as backup is worth having for the rare evening the main connection drops, so a lesson can continue rather than being lost entirely to a fixable problem.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does online IGCSE tuition usually need?
faqs.answer: This depends on the subject, the Grade, and how close the exam series is, more than the format itself; online does not inherently need more or fewer sessions than home tuition for the same student. As a general pattern, one to two sessions a week per subject through most of the term, stepping up as mocks or the exam series approaches and stepping back down afterward, works for many Grade 9 and 10 students without tipping into dependency. The right number is something to agree with the matched tutor after the first few sessions, once it is clear how much a student retains between them, rather than fixed in advance.

faqs.question: Can the same online tutor teach more than one IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the tutor genuinely has depth in both subjects rather than a passing familiarity with one of them, but it is worth asking directly rather than assuming a general tutor covers everything equally well. A single tutor across two subjects can simplify scheduling into one weekly slot instead of two, which suits families who want one consistent relationship managing a student's overall IGCSE workload. For subjects where board-specific depth matters most, such as Cambridge Extended Maths or a specific English syllabus code, a dedicated specialist for that one subject, even alongside a broader tutor for another, is often the stronger combination.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE online tuition cost less than a home tutor in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily: igcse online tuition Gurgaon pricing is not automatically cheaper than a home tutor, since fee still depends on the tutor's experience, the subject, session length, and level rather than the format alone; there is no fixed rate published for either. What online usually removes is any travel-related cost or time a home visit might otherwise involve, which some families do factor in when comparing formats. Availability stays subject to tutor availability and depends on level and schedule either way, so the more useful comparison during the intake call is what each option actually includes, not an assumed price difference between the two.

faqs.question: What happens if my child's school changes its calendar mid-term?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram and your matched tutor as soon as a school confirms a change, whether that is a shifted mock date, an added activity that clashes with the usual slot, or an unscheduled break; a fixed weekly online slot is easier to move than a home visit built around a tutor's travel plan, but it still needs an actual conversation rather than assuming the tutor will notice. Most tutors experienced with Gurgaon's international school calendar expect a few of these shifts across a school year and build in some flexibility, but a pattern of last-minute changes is still worth flagging honestly so the slot can be rebuilt around a more realistic weekly rhythm.

faqs.question: Is online tuition suitable for a student who is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student, and this is a fair thing to be honest about before committing to a term of it. Some students focus better online precisely because there is less to look at than a full desk of materials, while others, especially ones who already struggle with screen time during the school day, find a second screen in the evening harder rather than easier to sit through. A short trial session is the best way to find out rather than guessing, and a hybrid arrangement, mostly online with one home session a fortnight for closer supervision, often works for a student who is borderline either way.

faqs.question: Which Gurgaon corridors have the newest online tutor coverage?
faqs.answer: The Dwarka Expressway and New Gurgaon, covering Sectors 102 to 113 and Sectors 82 to 90 respectively, are among the fastest-growing parts of the city, and their home tutor base is still catching up with the pace of new societies moving in. Online tuition currently reaches these corridors more reliably than home visits do, since a matched tutor based anywhere in Gurgaon can serve a family there without needing to physically travel out along the expressway during evening traffic. This is likely to shift as more tutors take on these corridors directly, but for now, families in these areas often get a wider choice of subject specialists by starting with an online slot.

If the slot keeps slipping because of a recurring clash, such as a weekly activity that runs long, change the day or time itself rather than hoping persistence fixes it. A slot protected early tends to hold for the rest of the term; one that slips in the first two weeks rarely self-corrects.

mainEntity.name: Which corridors pair well in one tutor's weekly route?

acceptedAnswer.text: Golf Course Road and Golf Course Extension Road sit close enough that a tutor doing home visits often serves both in one evening, and the same applies to Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the DLF phases around Cyber City, which cluster centrally. Online removes this constraint almost entirely: a tutor based centrally in Gurgaon can add a family on the Dwarka Expressway or in New Gurgaon without a travel cost at all, which is one reason online reaches those newer corridors faster than home coverage has. Pairing still matters for scheduling rather than travel, though, since a tutor juggling several families across a week plans around everyone's slot, not just yours.

mainEntity.name: Does gate entry or traffic affect an online lesson?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not directly, since there is no visitor to register and no drive to make, which is exactly why online works well for corridors like Golf Course Road where society gate registration can eat into a tight after-school window for a home visit. What traffic does still affect is a tutor's own evening, if they are also doing home visits elsewhere in Gurgaon before or after your online slot; a tutor running late from a Sohna Road visit can still affect your session's start time even though you are not the one driving anywhere. Confirming a tutor's evening schedule honestly during the intake call avoids this kind of indirect delay.

mainEntity.name: If online is not working, can we switch to a home tutor instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and this is a genuinely common switch rather than an unusual request. Tell IB Gram specifically what is not working, whether it is a student losing focus on screen, a connection that keeps failing at the same time each week, or simply a preference for someone physically present, and ask for a shortlist built around home tuition in your corridor instead. The intake details you already gave, board, level, syllabus and school calendar, carry over, so the switch does not mean starting from zero. Families on well-covered corridors such as DLF Phases 2 to 4 or Sushant Lok usually find a home tutor quickly; families further out may be offered a hybrid arrangement instead.

mainEntity.name: What device and internet setup does IGCSE online tuition actually need?

acceptedAnswer.text: A laptop or tablet with a stable camera and microphone, a reliable broadband connection, and a quiet space with decent lighting cover most of what a session needs; a phone works for a quick catch-up but is a poor fit for a full session involving a shared whiteboard and annotated past papers. Test the setup at the actual time your sessions will run, not at a different, quieter hour, since Gurgaon's evening broadband load can differ noticeably from a weekend afternoon test. A second device or a mobile hotspot as backup is worth having for the rare evening the main connection drops, so a lesson can continue rather than being lost entirely to a fixable problem.

mainEntity.name: How many sessions a week does online IGCSE tuition usually need?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the subject, the Grade, and how close the exam series is, more than the format itself; online does not inherently need more or fewer sessions than home tuition for the same student. As a general pattern, one to two sessions a week per subject through most of the term, stepping up as mocks or the exam series approaches and stepping back down afterward, works for many Grade 9 and 10 students without tipping into dependency. The right number is something to agree with the matched tutor after the first few sessions, once it is clear how much a student retains between them, rather than fixed in advance.

mainEntity.name: Can the same online tutor teach more than one IGCSE subject?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, if the tutor genuinely has depth in both subjects rather than a passing familiarity with one of them, but it is worth asking directly rather than assuming a general tutor covers everything equally well. A single tutor across two subjects can simplify scheduling into one weekly slot instead of two, which suits families who want one consistent relationship managing a student's overall IGCSE workload. For subjects where board-specific depth matters most, such as Cambridge Extended Maths or a specific English syllabus code, a dedicated specialist for that one subject, even alongside a broader tutor for another, is often the stronger combination.

mainEntity.name: Does IGCSE online tuition cost less than a home tutor in Gurgaon?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily: igcse online tuition Gurgaon pricing is not automatically cheaper than a home tutor, since fee still depends on the tutor's experience, the subject, session length, and level rather than the format alone; there is no fixed rate published for either. What online usually removes is any travel-related cost or time a home visit might otherwise involve, which some families do factor in when comparing formats. Availability stays subject to tutor availability and depends on level and schedule either way, so the more useful comparison during the intake call is what each option actually includes, not an assumed price difference between the two.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my child's school changes its calendar mid-term?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell IB Gram and your matched tutor as soon as a school confirms a change, whether that is a shifted mock date, an added activity that clashes with the usual slot, or an unscheduled break; a fixed weekly online slot is easier to move than a home visit built around a tutor's travel plan, but it still needs an actual conversation rather than assuming the tutor will notice. Most tutors experienced with Gurgaon's international school calendar expect a few of these shifts across a school year and build in some flexibility, but a pattern of last-minute changes is still worth flagging honestly so the slot can be rebuilt around a more realistic weekly rhythm.

mainEntity.name: Is online tuition suitable for a student who is easily distracted?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the student, and this is a fair thing to be honest about before committing to a term of it. Some students focus better online precisely because there is less to look at than a full desk of materials, while others, especially ones who already struggle with screen time during the school day, find a second screen in the evening harder rather than easier to sit through. A short trial session is the best way to find out rather than guessing, and a hybrid arrangement, mostly online with one home session a fortnight for closer supervision, often works for a student who is borderline either way.

acceptedAnswer.text: The Dwarka Expressway and New Gurgaon, covering Sectors 102 to 113 and Sectors 82 to 90 respectively, are among the fastest-growing parts of the city, and their home tutor base is still catching up with the pace of new societies moving in. Online tuition currently reaches these corridors more reliably than home visits do, since a matched tutor based anywhere in Gurgaon can serve a family there without needing to physically travel out along the expressway during evening traffic. This is likely to shift as more tutors take on these corridors directly, but for now, families in these areas often get a wider choice of subject specialists by starting with an online slot.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE, MYP and DP: what an IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon actually needs to know
contentBlocks.body:
A capable IGCSE tutor for hire in Gurgaon should be able to explain, without notes, the difference between Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some now offered as 9-1 under separate codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. If the subject in question is one of the many Cambridge options with Core and Extended tiers, a good tutor asks immediately which tier the student is entered for, because Core caps at grade C no matter how strong the student's work is, and Extended reaches A* but covers noticeably more ground. A tutor who does not ask this question in the first conversation has probably not taught the syllabus recently. This is exactly the expertise an IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor needs to already have, not learn on the job.

For families whose search widens into the IB Diploma Programme, the person you are hiring needs a working grasp of a two-year structure, DP1 and DP2, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level with 150 hours. Grading runs 1 to 7 per subject, and Theory of Knowledge with the Extended Essay add up to three further points, for a maximum of 45 and a minimum of 24 for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's own failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service sits alongside the six subjects as a separate requirement.

A student moving through the Middle Years Programme needs someone comfortable with criterion-based grading rather than a single mark: eight subject groups, four criteria per subject scored 0 to 8, converting through IB grade boundaries to a final 1 to 7. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, the Community Project a year or two earlier, and MYP eAssessment in the final year is optional, left to the school. A tutor for hire who cannot explain any of this on request is, whatever else they offer, not yet the specialist this search is actually looking for.

contentBlocks.heading: What subject depth should you check before hiring an IB or IGCSE tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
Hiring an IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon often comes down to one early test: how a candidate talks about marking, not just teaching. Ask them to walk through how they would mark a real past paper answer. Command terms in Cambridge IGCSE and Edexcel International GCSE, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, each demand a different structure, and a tutor who cannot immediately explain what separates an evaluate answer from a describe answer has probably not spent real time against a mark scheme. This single question, asked in a first conversation or a trial class, tells a parent more than a resume ever will.

For DP candidates, push further: ask how they would help a student plan a Theory of Knowledge essay around a specific knowledge question, or how an Extended Essay's roughly four-thousand-word research question gets narrowed from a broad interest to something answerable. Ask, too, how an Internal Assessment differs from one DP subject to the next in what it actually rewards, since a tutor who treats every IA the same way across subjects is applying a generic template rather than board-specific knowledge.

For MYP families, the test is different again: does the candidate talk about depth against a criterion, A through D, or do they talk mainly about covering more content? A tutor still thinking in terms of a single overall mark, rather than four separate criteria, is teaching MYP the way they would teach a different, simpler system.

The tutors worth hiring build lessons from real past papers, mark schemes and subject reports sourced through the school or the board's own official channels, because that is where the actual pattern of what earns marks lives, not in a generic textbook chapter.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tutor, online tutor or both: choosing the right format for Gurgaon families
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor is the right starting point for most families hiring for IB or IGCSE in Gurgaon, and the reason is simple: a person sitting across the table sees exactly where a student's pen hesitates on a written paper, notices when confidence rather than knowledge is the real problem, and adjusts without either side needing to say anything out loud. For a Grade 10 student close to an exam series, or a DP2 student weeks from mocks, that immediate, in-person read is difficult to replace. Home classes also spare a family the drive to and from a coaching centre on a school evening that is already tight.

An online tutor earns its place for a different reason: subject scarcity. Families searching specifically for an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon are usually chasing exactly this: a DP HL specialist in a less common subject combination may simply not live within a reasonable drive of every Gurgaon sector, and online is how a family in Manesar or far along SPR reaches that person anyway. A household juggling two or three subjects across different weekday evenings can also fit an online slot in where a home visit would eat too much of the evening. Shared whiteboards and annotated past papers translate well to a screen for most subjects, though a first session with a brand-new tutor still tends to go more smoothly in person.

Most Gurgaon families settle, by the second or third month, into some version of both: a home tutor for the bulk of the week and an online slot for one hard-to-place subject or a late evening that traffic would otherwise ruin. Neither format is inherently better; the honest answer depends on the specific subject, the specific student, and which sector of the city the family is searching from.

contentBlocks.heading: How is a tutor's background actually checked before you meet them?
contentBlocks.body:
Vetting an IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon starts long before a family ever meets them. Before a name reaches a family, IB Gram checks that the tutor has genuinely taught the specific board and level requested, not a related one that sounds close enough. That means confirming, as far as a profile allows, real classroom or one-to-one experience with Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, MYP or DP at the stated level, and checking subject depth against the syllabus a student's own school is likely following. Any international board tutor in Gurugram carrying an IB Gram profile goes through the same check, and profiles are revisited if a tutor's teaching focus changes.

Still, a background check is not the same as knowing whether a specific person will work well with a specific fifteen-year-old on a Tuesday evening, and IB Gram does not pretend otherwise. That is what the free trial class exists to settle, and it should be treated as the real interview, not a courtesy lesson before the real decision has already been made elsewhere.

Parents get more out of a trial by asking direct questions during or right after it: which levels has this person actually taught in the last year or two, how many students at this exact stage have they worked with recently, what would their first month's plan look like, and what would make them, honestly, suggest a different tutor instead. A specialist answers these without hedging; vagueness here is itself worth noting.

If the match does not hold up once lessons start, whether the pace is wrong or the personality does not click, IB Gram's position is simple: say so, and a different tutor is offered from the same pool. It is far cheaper, in time and in a student's confidence, to switch early than to wait out a poor fit for a full term.

contentBlocks.heading: Interview questions worth asking any IB or IGCSE tutor candidate
contentBlocks.body:
Treat the first conversation with a candidate tutor the way you would treat any hire: with specific questions, not a general chat about experience. Start with board and level: which exact syllabus have they taught, at which grade or level, and how recently. A tutor who taught DP Economics five years ago and has not touched the syllabus since is not necessarily wrong for the job, but the family should know that going in rather than assume it away.

Ask next about stage-specific experience. A tutor comfortable with DP1 introductory content is not automatically ready for a DP2 student deep into an Extended Essay draft or an Internal Assessment deadline; ask which of these they have actually done, not just which they feel confident about. For IGCSE, ask whether they have taught the specific tier, Core or Extended, since the two demand different pacing and different ambition in how far a lesson pushes.

Ask how they structure a first lesson, and listen for whether the answer involves looking at the student's actual recent work, a test script or a mock paper, before deciding where to start. A tutor who proposes to simply begin at the start of a syllabus, regardless of what the student already knows, is teaching a generic course rather than this specific student.

Finally, ask the uncomfortable question directly: what would make you tell us this is not working. A confident, specific answer, involving a plan to flag concerns early rather than let a term drift, is a far better signal than reassurance that everything will be fine. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the ones worth hiring say this plainly rather than letting a family assume otherwise.

contentBlocks.heading: Signs an IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon is actually working out
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks in, a family should be able to name something specific the tutor has changed, not just report a general sense that lessons are going fine. For an IGCSE student, that might be a past paper answer that finally follows the actual mark scheme's structure, fewer lost method marks on a Core or Extended Maths paper, or simply less dread before a written response. For a DP student, look for whether a Theory of Knowledge essay has moved from a vague topic to a real knowledge question, or whether an Internal Assessment has narrowed from a broad idea into something the student can actually execute.

A good tutor is also honest about what four weeks cannot show. A DP2 student rebuilding a subject after a rough mock is not going to look transformed in a month, and a tutor who claims otherwise is managing expectations badly, not delivering results well. What should be visible early, even in a hard case, is whether the student is doing agreed work between sessions and whether last week's mistakes are actually getting fixed rather than repeated.

A short, plain check-in around the one-month mark is a reasonable thing to expect: what has moved, what has not, and what needs more time. A tutor who cannot give a specific answer to this, or retreats into vague reassurance, is worth a direct conversation before the term goes any further.

It cuts both ways, too. A tutor cannot manufacture progress from a student who is not doing any work outside the sessions themselves, and a fair-minded tutor says this rather than absorbing blame that belongs somewhere else.

introSummary: IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon are worth comparing in twos and threes, not hired one at a time, because a single trial lesson tells a family far less than two trial lessons run back to back. IB Gram's home tuition service in Gurgaon puts forward a short shortlist of verified profiles rather than a single name, so parents can weigh board experience, the exact level taught, school familiarity and weekday travel before committing a term of evenings. A household moving a child from IGCSE Grade 9 or Grade 10 into the IB Diploma Programme often needs two different specialists rather than one generalist who claims to cover both. This page sets out how that shortlist gets built, what to place side by side on a comparison sheet, how trial lessons with more than one tutor stay fair to the student, and how to ask for a replacement when the first match at home is not working.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram build a shortlist instead of sending one name?
contentBlocks.body:
A parent typing IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon into a search bar is usually past the stage of wanting one name. You want options, and you want them fast enough that a term does not start with a mismatch already in motion.

IB Gram works from a query or a free consultation call. You are asked about the board, whether IB or a specific IGCSE syllabus, the level, which school your child attends and its general calendar, your preferred sectors or societies for a home tutor, and the slots that actually survive a week of school buses and activities. From there the process runs in three steps.

1. IB Gram shortlists two or three verified profiles that match the board, level and location, never one name presented as the only option.
2. The family runs a trial session, at home or online, with the strongest candidate first and keeps a second profile in reserve if that trial raises doubts.
3. If the fit is wrong after the trial or in the first few sessions, the family asks for a different match rather than persisting out of politeness.

A generalist who claims comfort with both IB and IGCSE is rarely the right pick for a household managing an IGCSE Grade 10 student and a DP1 sibling at the same time. The two syllabuses are marked differently, paced differently, and a specialist in one is not automatically strong in the other. A home tutor who already knows your corridor is often the stronger first pick on the shortlist, since travel reliability matters almost as much as subject depth once term begins.

Availability for any given profile is subject to tutor availability and depends on level and schedule, so the shortlist that arrives is drawn from tutors who are actually free for your slot, not a theoretical full list.

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE programme stages Gurgaon families are juggling right now
contentBlocks.body:
International Baccalaureate (IB) and IGCSE are not stages of the same ladder, though a Gurgaon student often moves through both. The Diploma Programme (DP) is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, built from six subjects across six groups. Three or four sit at Higher Level (HL, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, roughly 150 hours). Every subject is graded 1 to 7, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) together with the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the ceiling and 24 the minimum for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's own failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) runs alongside the six subjects and has to be completed, not graded. Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May session; a minority use November, largely for retakes, and May results land in early July.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs for five years, MYP 1 through MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every MYP subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, with a smaller Community Project earlier in MYP 3 or 4. Some schools also offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides for itself.

IGCSE in Gurgaon almost always means either Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, a two-year course across Grade 9 and Grade 10 before a move into the DP, A Levels, or a shift back to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Cambridge runs exam series in February and March, a series offered only in India, then May and June, and October and November, grading most syllabuses A* to G. Edexcel International GCSE sits in January and May or June, and grades everything 9 to 1. Several Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at a C, Extended reaches an A*. This structure applies the same way whether a family is based in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, or has just moved from another city.

contentBlocks.heading: What a subject-specialist tutor actually checks before the first lesson
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon on subject depth means looking past a confident answer in a phone call and asking what the tutor actually works from. A strong DP tutor teaches to the syllabus's own assessment objectives for that subject group, not a generic revision course borrowed from CBSE or ICSE. Command terms set how deep each answer needs to go: define, describe and explain ask for less than evaluate, discuss or to what extent, and a student who writes a describe-level answer to an evaluate question loses marks regardless of how much content is correct. A tutor worth shortlisting can point to this distinction in the first session, not the fifth.

Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports are the honest record of how marks are actually awarded, and they come through the school or the IB's own official channels rather than a tutor's private archive. When comparing two profiles, ask each one how they use these documents: do they mark a student's practice answer against the real scheme, line by line, or do they simply explain the content again. The first approach closes the gap between what a student writes and what an examiner rewards. The second does not.

For MYP subjects, the same logic applies through the four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8. A tutor should be able to say which criterion a student is weakest on this term and why, not offer a single vague verdict on the subject as a whole. For IGCSE, whether a subject sits at Core or Extended tier changes the ceiling on the grade and the paper a student sits, so a tutor comparing profiles should ask which tier your child is entered for, or whether that decision is still open. Getting the tier wrong late in Grade 10 is one of the more expensive mistakes a family can make, and a tutor who raises it unprompted is usually one worth keeping on the shortlist. This kind of specific, checkable knowledge is what separates a genuine subject specialist from a home tutor who is simply confident on the phone.

Three corridors account for most of the households comparing IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon on this page, and each behaves differently once the school run and evening traffic are added in.

Golf Course Extension Road covers Sector 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 62 and 65, along with Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, and societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon. This corridor has grown fast, and its road network has not always kept pace, so a home tutor's slot here often needs a wider buffer either side of school pickup than the distance on a map would suggest. Evening traffic between Sohna Road and Golf Course Extension Road can stretch a short trip considerably, which matters when picking a 6pm versus a 7:30pm slot.

Sohna Road runs through Sector 47, 48, 49 and 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur, with societies including Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close. Many of these societies register visitors at the gate, and a home tutor who has worked this corridor before knows to arrive with enough margin that gate entry does not eat into the lesson itself.

DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City is the most commercially busy of the three: DLF Phase 2, Phase 3, Phase 4, MG Road, Cyber City, Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur and Sectors 24, 27 and 28, with societies such as DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona. Office traffic through Cyber City and MG Road peaks exactly when most home lessons would start, so families here often do better with a slightly later slot, or with an online session on the evenings when a tutor's earlier appointment in Sohna Road or Golf Course Extension Road runs long.

When comparing two shortlisted tutors, ask each one plainly which of these three corridors they already work in regularly. A tutor who already has a 6pm slot in DLF Phase 3 is a more reliable fit for a DLF Phase 3 family than one commuting in for the first time, even if the second tutor's subject credentials look stronger on paper.

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar pressures behind every shortlisting decision
contentBlocks.body:
Families comparing IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon are usually already juggling one international school's calendar, and sometimes two if siblings attend different ones. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge appear here only as local context for the kind of calendar a Gurgaon family navigates, not as an indication of which board any of them follows.

What is common across schools in this category is a calendar that does not pause for a tutor's convenience. Unit tests, internal assessments, mock examinations and the real exam session all land at fixed points, and a tutoring plan built without that calendar in view tends to fall apart by the second term. DP2 mock examinations, for instance, are usually set by each school several months before the May session, and a strong tutor treats that mock date as a planning anchor, stepping revision up in the weeks before it and stepping back down once results come in and gaps are visible. Many families in this category default to home tuition partly because it fits an already packed school calendar better than a regular commute to a centre.

A shortlist comparison should include a direct question: has this tutor worked with a student on a comparable school calendar before, and can they name the kind of pressure points that calendar creates, such as a clash between a school's own internal assessment week and an Extended Essay deadline. A tutor who answers only in generalities about board exams, without engaging with calendar timing specifically, is often less prepared for the actual term ahead than one who asks for the school's assessment calendar in the first conversation.

contentBlocks.heading: How does home tuition compare with online for IB and IGCSE in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the starting point for most families comparing IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon, and for good reason: a tutor sitting at the same table as your child, in a familiar room, tends to build focus faster than a screen does, especially for a student who is already tired after a full school day. A home tutor also sees the actual books, the actual handwriting, and the actual distractions in the room, which is harder to judge over a video call.

Online tuition is not a downgrade, though. It suits a family whose best-fit subject specialist does not work their corridor, a student who needs a late evening slot after a school activity runs over, or a household managing two children's timetables in the same house at once. A shared whiteboard and an annotated past paper work almost as well on a screen as on paper, provided both sides have a stable connection and a proper setup, not a phone propped against a water bottle.

Hybrid, splitting a week between a home session and an online one, is worth considering when a subject specialist lives outside easy travel range, or when evening traffic on the intended slot's corridor is genuinely unpredictable. A family might keep the main weekly session as home tuition and move a second, shorter session online in the week before a mock or the exam session itself, when an extra hour matters more than the setting.

None of the three modes is universally correct, and a good shortlist comparison asks each tutor plainly which mode they teach best in, rather than assuming every tutor is equally strong across all three. A tutor who is excellent as a home tutor but visibly less focused on video calls is not a good fit for a family that needs online flexibility, however strong their subject knowledge is on paper. Be honest with yourself, too, about which mode your child actually concentrates in, since a parent's preference and a teenager's attention span do not always agree.
items: Home tuition: builds focus fastest, lets the tutor see real books and handwriting
Online tuition: suits a late slot, a distant specialist, or two siblings sharing a house
Hybrid: a home session most weeks, an online top-up before a mock or exam session
Ask each shortlisted tutor which mode they genuinely teach best in, not just accept
A child's real attention span matters more than a parent's preference for one mode

contentBlocks.heading: How tutor profiles are verified before they reach your shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Before any tutor reaches your shortlist, IB Gram checks that the profile's claimed board, syllabus and level are genuine, and that the tutor has actually taught the specific stage your child is at, whether that is IGCSE Grade 9, MYP 4 or DP2. This is the baseline check, not the finish line: a verified profile still needs to be tested against your own child in a trial session before you commit. This matters as much for a home tutor as for an online one, since the verification bar is the same either way.

Parents comparing two or three shortlisted tutors should run their own checks alongside IB Gram's. Ask each tutor to talk through a recent lesson plan for a student at the same level, not in the abstract but with the actual topic, the actual difficulty the student faced, and what changed by the next session. Ask how they would handle a student who is confident in class but freezes on an exam-style question, since that gap is common in both IB and IGCSE students and a tutor's answer reveals how much real teaching experience sits behind the credentials.

A free trial session, at home or online, is the real verification step. Watch whether the tutor asks diagnostic questions before teaching content, whether they adjust pace when your child hesitates, and whether the session ends with something concrete: a marked practice answer, a clear note on what to work on, or a plan for the following week. A trial that is just a friendly chat about the subject, with nothing produced by the end, tells you less than one that is.

If a trial session with the first shortlisted profile raises doubts, move to the second profile rather than persisting out of politeness or a sense that switching wastes time already spent. IB Gram can put forward a further profile if neither of the first two is right, since the goal is a match that works for the student, not a quick close.
items: IB Gram checks a profile's claimed board, syllabus and level before shortlisting
Ask for a recent lesson plan at your child's actual level, with real detail
Ask how the tutor handles a student confident in class but shaky under exam conditions
A useful trial session ends with a marked answer or a concrete next step
Move to the second shortlisted profile if the first trial raises real doubts

contentBlocks.heading: How do you compare IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon before choosing one?
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon properly means putting two or three shortlisted profiles on one sheet and scoring each against the same five or six criteria before running a single trial lesson, rather than judging tutors one at a time from memory. Write the criteria down. It sounds obvious, and most families skip it anyway.

Start with board and level fit: does the tutor teach this exact syllabus, at this exact level, right now, or is it something they taught two years ago and have not returned to since. Then school familiarity: has this tutor worked with a student at your child's school before, and do they already understand its internal assessment calendar. Then logistics: which corridor do they already work in, and does their available slot survive your child's actual weekday evening. Add a fourth column for cost structure, described only in general terms such as per-session or package pricing rather than any amount, since the two profiles may be priced differently and that difference should be visible on the same sheet as everything else. Searches for the best IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon usually mean the best fit for one specific child, not a universal ranking anyone could publish.

Running trial lessons with more than one tutor without unsettling the student takes a light touch. Tell your child plainly that you are trying two tutors this week to see who fits better, rather than letting the second trial feel like a secret test. Space the two trials a day or two apart if possible, so the student is not comparing exhaustion levels rather than teaching quality, and ask the same one or two questions of both tutors afterwards: what did they notice about your child's gaps, and what would the next session cover.

If the first match still feels wrong after two or three real sessions, not just the trial, say so and ask IB Gram for a different match. This is not unusual and it is not a failure of the process. A student who spends a term with the wrong tutor out of politeness loses more time than one whose family switched in week three.
items: Score two or three shortlisted profiles against the same five or six criteria
Compare board and level fit, school familiarity, logistics and cost structure together
Tell your child plainly that you are trying more than one tutor this week
Space trial lessons a day or two apart so tiredness does not skew the comparison

contentBlocks.heading: What a shortlisted tutor's first month should honestly show
contentBlocks.body:
Once a tutor from the shortlist is confirmed, progress should be visible without being dramatic. In the first two to three weeks, expect a clearer error log rather than a grade change: the tutor should be able to name the specific gaps found in the trial and early sessions, whether that is a weak grasp of a particular DP topic, an MYP criterion the student consistently underperforms on, or a habit of losing marks on command-term questions despite knowing the content.

By four to six weeks, ask for a short review: what has changed, what has not, and whether the plan needs adjusting. Whether the sessions run as home tuition, online or hybrid, this review should happen on schedule rather than only when a parent asks. A tutor who cannot answer concretely, or who only offers reassurance without specifics, is worth a second look even after a successful trial, since a good trial does not guarantee a good term.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any comparison built around a promised outcome rather than a described process should raise doubts, not confidence. What a strong tutor can honestly offer is a clear plan, visible weekly progress against that plan, and an honest flag when something is not working, whether that is the student's side, the pacing, or the fit itself.

Limits matter too. A tutor cannot substitute for a student's own revision time, cannot fix a subject choice made too late to change, and cannot make an overloaded week feel less overloaded. Some students genuinely do not need a tutor for every subject, and a family comparing profiles should be honest about which subjects actually need outside help this term versus which ones the student can manage with school support alone. Adding a third tutor because two are already in place is not automatically the right move, and a good tutor will sometimes say so themselves.
items: Weeks 1-3: a clearer error log and named gaps, not yet a grade change
Weeks 4-6: a concrete review of what changed and what the plan needs next

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started: your first query to your first trial lesson
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started with IB Gram is meant to be a short first step, not a commitment. Send a query through the site, or book a free consultation call, and be ready to say which board and syllabus your child follows, the exact level, IGCSE Grade 9 or 10, an MYP year, or DP1 versus DP2, the school's general calendar if you know it, which Gurgaon corridor or society you are in, and the weekday evenings that actually work once school buses and activities are accounted for. This holds whether your address reads Gurgaon or Gurugram on paper.

From that conversation, IB Gram asks a few clarifying questions if anything is ambiguous, then shortlists two or three verified profiles that match what you have described. You are not obliged to pick either the fastest reply or the most experienced-sounding profile; read both, and where possible, speak to each tutor briefly before the trial itself.

The same trial process applies whether the first session is home tuition or online. Expect the tutor to ask diagnostic questions before teaching, to work from an actual topic rather than a generic overview, and to leave you with something concrete at the end: a marked answer, a noted gap, or a plan for the coming week.

After the trial, tell IB Gram plainly whether it worked. If it did, sessions continue on the slot you agreed, at home, online or hybrid depending on what suits the term ahead. If it did not, ask for the second shortlisted profile, or a fresh one if neither original match fits. Nothing about switching mid-term is unusual, and no family should feel locked into a first choice made before a single lesson had actually happened. The whole point of comparing rather than hiring blind is that you keep this option open from week one.

faqs.question: How many IB and IGCSE tutors should I compare before choosing one?
faqs.answer: Two or three shortlisted profiles is usually enough to compare properly without dragging the decision out for weeks. IB Gram puts forward two or three verified tutors matched to your child's board, level and location rather than a single name, so you can weigh board experience, school familiarity and travel time side by side. Comparing more than three tends to slow the decision without adding much useful information, since most families can already tell after two trial lessons which teaching style suits their child. If none of the first shortlist feels right, ask for a fresh set rather than working through a long list one at a time.

faqs.question: Can I run trial lessons with two tutors in the same week without confusing my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families manage this by telling the student plainly that two tutors are being tried this week to see who fits better. Space the two trial sessions a day or two apart rather than back to back, so tiredness does not make the second trial look worse than the first. Ask each tutor the same one or two questions afterwards, such as what gaps they noticed and what the next session would cover, so the comparison is fair rather than based on a vague impression. Most students find this process straightforward once it is explained honestly, and it usually settles the choice faster than a single trial would.

faqs.question: What should I compare on a shortlist besides subject knowledge?
faqs.answer: Subject knowledge matters, but school familiarity, logistics and slot reliability decide whether a tutoring relationship actually survives a full term. Ask whether the tutor has worked with a student at your child's school before and understands its internal assessment calendar, which corridor or society they already work in regularly, and whether their available slot genuinely fits your weekday evenings once buses and activities are accounted for. A tutor who is excellent on paper but new to your corridor and unfamiliar with your school's calendar can still be a weaker practical fit than a slightly less flashy profile who already knows both.

faqs.question: How is a tutor's profile verified before it reaches my shortlist?
faqs.answer: IB Gram checks that a tutor's claimed board, syllabus and level are genuine and that they have actually taught students at the specific stage your child is at before including them in a shortlist. This is a baseline check, not a substitute for your own judgement: run a free trial session and watch whether the tutor asks diagnostic questions, adjusts pace when your child hesitates, and leaves the session with something concrete produced, such as a marked answer or a clear note on the next step. A trial that is only a friendly chat, with nothing produced, tells you less than one that is.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor actually travel to my society on Golf Course Extension Road or Sohna Road on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific home tutor and the slot chosen, which is exactly why the shortlist matters: IB Gram matches you with home tutors who already work your corridor rather than assuming any tutor will travel anywhere. Golf Course Extension Road and Sohna Road each have their own traffic patterns and, in many societies, a visitor registration process at the gate that adds real time before a lesson can start. A tutor already holding an evening slot nearby is more dependable than one commuting in for the first time. If travel genuinely does not work for a given evening, an online session that week is a reasonable substitute rather than cancelling outright.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be present during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed rule for a home tuition session, and most families decide this based on the student's age and comfort rather than any requirement from IB Gram. Many parents stay nearby in the house without sitting in the room itself, which keeps the session focused while still allowing a check-in at the end. Younger students, or those early in a new tutor relationship, sometimes do better with a parent visible in the early sessions, and this can ease off once trust is built. What matters more than presence is a quiet, consistent study space with the right books and materials ready before the tutor arrives, since a session that starts with searching for a textbook loses real teaching time.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor from my shortlist is not working out?
faqs.answer: Ask IB Gram for a different match, and this is treated as a normal part of the process rather than a complaint. Give it a fair few sessions beyond the trial itself, since a slow start does not always mean a bad fit, but if the mismatch is clear, whether in teaching style, pace or simple rapport, say so plainly rather than persisting out of politeness. The second profile from your original shortlist, or a fresh one if neither original match suits, should be available without starting the whole enquiry process again from scratch. A student who spends a full term with the wrong tutor loses more time than one whose family switched early.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work as well as a home tutor for IB and IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For most content-based teaching, yes, provided both sides have a stable connection, a shared whiteboard tool and a proper setup rather than a phone propped against something. Where a home tutor tends to have the edge is with a tired student late in the school day, since sitting at the same table with another person in the room builds focus faster for many students than a screen does. Online suits a family whose best subject specialist does not work their corridor, a late evening slot after an activity runs long, or two siblings needing sessions in the same house at once. Many families settle on a hybrid mix rather than choosing one mode exclusively.

faqs.question: How is IGCSE different from the IB Diploma Programme, and does my child need two tutors?
faqs.answer: IGCSE is usually a two-year course across Grade 9 and Grade 10 under Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, while the IB Diploma Programme is a separate two-year course, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects graded 1 to 7 and its own Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge requirements. A family with a child moving from IGCSE into the DP, or with children at both stages at once, often needs two different specialists rather than one generalist who claims comfort with both, since the marking style, pacing and workload differ meaningfully between the two. Comparing profiles by stage, not just by board name, is worth doing explicitly on your shortlist.

faqs.question: How much does comparing and switching tutors through IB Gram cost?
faqs.answer: Cost is structured per session or as a package depending on the level and schedule agreed, subject to tutor availability, rather than a fixed public rate, since a DP1 Higher Level specialist and an IGCSE Grade 9 generalist are not priced the same. The free consultation and trial session let you compare a shortlist before any commitment is made, so you are not paying to find out whether a match works. Ask IB Gram directly during your consultation for the structure relevant to your child's board, level and preferred mode, home, online or hybrid, so you can compare it against a coaching centre or online group class on the same terms.

faqs.question: What does a trial session actually show that a phone call does not?
faqs.answer: A trial session shows how a tutor teaches your specific child, not how they describe themselves on a call. Watch whether they ask diagnostic questions before launching into content, whether they notice and adjust when your child hesitates or looks lost, and whether the session ends with something concrete: a marked practice answer, a clearly named gap, or a plan for next time. A tutor who talks fluently about the syllabus on the phone but delivers a vague, unstructured trial session is a weaker choice than one who sounds less polished on the phone but runs a focused, diagnostic first lesson. Trust the trial over the pitch.

faqs.question: My child's school is near DLF Phase 3 or Cyber City. Does that limit which tutors are available?
faqs.answer: It narrows the pool somewhat during peak office traffic hours, but it does not rule out home tuition. DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City sees heavy evening traffic exactly when most lessons would start, so tutors who already work this corridor tend to build in a later slot or keep a standing online session for the evenings that run long. IB Gram's shortlist for this corridor favours tutors with a track record here specifically, since a tutor unfamiliar with Cyber City traffic can arrive late often enough to eat into lesson time. If a stable weekday evening slot genuinely is not available at home, a hybrid arrangement, home most weeks with an online session when traffic is bad, tends to work well for families here.

heroTitle: Choosing IB and IGCSE Tuition in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Home tuition is what most Gurgaon families ask for first: a verified tutor at your table, working through the syllabus your child's school actually uses. This page walks through what IB and IGCSE demand, what a specialist tutor should know, and how IB Gram matches you to one.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon works best as home tutoring: a verified tutor teaching your child at your own table, in your own sector or society, rather than a seat in a batch built for a different board. Most families searching for this come from two directions at once, a Grade 9 or 10 student on Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, or a Diploma Programme student juggling six subjects, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge against a May exam session. IB Gram matches each request to a tutor who has actually taught this board, not merely a subject. Home lessons stay the default; online and hybrid sit alongside them where travel or a late slot makes more sense. A free trial class comes before any commitment, and the family can ask for a different tutor if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a family to the right IB and IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram starts by asking what actually matters for this specific decision: the board (Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, or IB MYP and DP), the exact level, the subjects in question, the school's own pacing, and which sectors of Gurgaon work for a home session. That single conversation, on a call or through a short form, decides who even gets shortlisted; nobody is offered a tutor who has never taught this board before.

From there the shortlist itself is narrow on purpose. Two or three verified profiles come back, each one chosen because their board experience, subject depth and past level taught line up with what the family described, not because they happened to be free that evening. A tutor who has taught DP Physics HL for years is a poor match for an IGCSE Grade 9 student who needs Core tier confidence rebuilt first, even though both fall under the same broad search term.

A free trial class follows before anything is agreed. It runs at the family's home wherever that is practical, so both the student and the tutor can tell within one session whether the working style, pace and personality actually fit, not just the paperwork. Parents are encouraged to sit in for part of it, ask the tutor how they would structure the first month, and see how the tutor responds when the student gets something wrong.

The process in practice:
1. Send a query describing the board, level, subjects and preferred slots.
2. IB Gram asks a few clarifying questions about the school calendar and location.
3. A shortlist of verified, board-matched tutors comes back within a short window.
4. A free trial class runs, usually at home, before anything is confirmed.
5. Regular sessions begin on the agreed slot, with the option to request a different tutor if the fit is wrong.

Shortlist limited to two or three tutors who have actually taught this exact board.

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE programme structure: DP, MYP and the Grade 9-10 IGCSE years
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon almost always means one of two syllabuses: Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Both are usually taught across Grades 9 and 10 as a two-year course, and most students in this city move on to the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or across to CBSE or ISC for Class 11, depending on the school. Cambridge grades most of its syllabuses A* to G, though a handful now carry 9-1 versions under separate syllabus codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, and this decision matters more than families often realise: Core tops out at a C grade no matter how well a student performs, while Extended reaches A* but demands a wider syllabus. Understanding this tier decision is part of what makes an IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor different from someone teaching IGCSE content alone.

The IB Diploma Programme that many IGCSE students move into is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, built from six subjects across six subject groups. Three or four of those sit at Higher Level, with 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level, with 150 hours; each subject is graded on the familiar 1 to 7 scale. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combine for up to three additional points, taking the maximum possible score to 45, with 24 points as the minimum for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's own failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service, known as CAS, is a separate requirement that runs alongside the six subjects rather than adding to the score.

Middle Years Programme families sit between these two: MYP runs across five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, covering roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8, and that criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through the IB's own grade boundaries. The Personal Project falls in MYP 5, with a Community Project usually in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment in the final year, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, is optional and left to each school to decide.

contentBlocks.heading: What an IB and IGCSE specialist tutor knows that a generalist does not
contentBlocks.body:
Choosing IB and IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon usually comes down to this exact question: is the tutor a generalist or a specialist? A generalist tutor can usually explain a topic. A board specialist can explain how that topic is actually assessed, and that difference decides marks. In Cambridge IGCSE and Edexcel International GCSE, command terms carry real weight: define, describe, explain, evaluate and discuss each demand a different depth and structure of answer, and a student who writes a description where the mark scheme wants an evaluation loses marks regardless of how much they know. A specialist has marked enough scripts against a real mark scheme to see this pattern immediately; a general subject tutor, however capable, is guessing.

The IB DP adds another layer entirely. Beyond content, DP subjects are graded 1 to 7 against published grade descriptors, and a tutor who has actually taught this board understands how Theory of Knowledge essays are structured around knowledge questions, how an Extended Essay develops a single research question across roughly four thousand words, and how an Internal Assessment differs subject by subject in what it rewards. None of this is guesswork available from a syllabus PDF; it comes from having sat with DP1 and DP2 students through a full two-year cycle and watched what actually moves a grade.

MYP work is graded differently again, against four criteria per subject rather than a single mark, and a tutor unfamiliar with criterion-based assessment will often coach a student to write more, when what the criteria actually reward is depth against a specific descriptor. Command terms recur here too, and a specialist knows which criterion a given command term usually maps to in a given subject.

Past papers, mark schemes and examiner or subject reports, sourced through the school or the board's own official channels, are the specialist's real working material. They show exactly how marks were awarded on real answers, not how a textbook assumes they should be, and a tutor who builds lessons around this evidence teaches differently from one who only teaches the syllabus content.
items: Command terms such as define, describe, evaluate and discuss each require a different answer structure.
DP subjects are graded 1-7 against published grade descriptors, not a simple right-or-wrong mark.
MYP subjects use four criteria, A to D, so depth against a descriptor beats extra writing.
Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge each reward a specific kind of argument, not general knowledge.

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE home tuition across Sushant Lok, SPR and New Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana spans a wide geography, and where a family lives changes what tuition looks like in practice. Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre belt is one of Gurgaon's older, more settled tutoring corridors, covering Sushant Lok 1 and Sushant Lok 2, South City 1, Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City. Many of these are independent houses or older low-rise blocks rather than gated societies with a single entry gate, which usually means less time lost at security and a slightly more flexible evening slot. A tutor working this belt on a weekday evening can often fit two IGCSE or DP students back to back without a long drive between them, since the area is compact.

Southern Peripheral Road, usually shortened to SPR, is a newer and more spread-out corridor: Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 70 and Sector 72, along with Ansal Esencia and Bhondsi further out. Tata Primanti is one of the larger societies here, and like most SPR societies it runs formal gate entry with visitor registration, so a home tutor typically needs the student's help getting through the gate for a first session. Evening traffic near Golf Course Extension Road can stretch what looks like a short trip on a map, which is one reason families this far out often keep online as a backup for a bad-traffic evening rather than cancelling the session outright.

New Gurgaon covers Sector 82 through Sector 90, plus Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, and includes large societies such as Vatika India Next and Godrej Air. This corridor sits furthest from the older parts of the city, and it is also where a growing number of the international schools families search this page for are based, so demand for IB and IGCSE tuition here has grown quickly. A tutor who already teaches two or three families in Vatika India Next or a neighbouring sector can often extend to a third without a wasted trip, which is part of what IB Gram checks before offering a home slot in this corridor.

Across all three corridors, the same rule holds: if the honest answer to whether a tutor can reach this sector on a weekday evening is no, IB Gram will say so and offer online or hybrid instead of pretending a home slot works.

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars Gurgaon IB and IGCSE families plan tuition around
contentBlocks.body:
Families searching for IB and IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon are often juggling the calendar of an international school alongside the tutor's own schedule, and the two do not always move together. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; school names on this page are local context only, not a claim about which board or programme any particular school runs. Families across Gurgaon commonly mention schools such as Pathways World School in Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School in Aravali and DPS International Edge when describing their child's routine, simply because these are names parents in this city recognise.

What matters for tuition planning is not which school a student attends but the shape of the year every international-curriculum family in Gurgaon deals with: unit tests and internal assessments spread through each term, a winter break that tutors and students both need to plan around, mock examinations set independently by each school ahead of the May session, and a final push once mocks are done. DP2 families in particular tend to feel this hardest, because mock results are often the first honest signal of where the six subjects actually stand.

A tutor who has taught across several Gurgaon schools tends to recognise this rhythm even before a parent explains it: when a school's mid-term reports usually land, when activity weeks or sports events quietly eat into study time, and when a student is more likely to need an extra session than a lighter one. That pattern recognition, built from having sat through several school years' worth of calendars rather than one, is part of what a board specialist brings that a newly qualified tutor cannot yet offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which suits IB and IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where most IB and IGCSE families in Gurgaon start, and for good reason: a tutor sitting at your own table can see exactly which working habits are slowing a student down, correct posture and pacing on written IGCSE papers in real time, and adjust for a younger sibling or a noisy evening without losing the lesson. For a DP2 student close to mocks, or a Grade 10 student a few months from an exam series, that in-person read of body language and confusion is often worth more than any app. Home classes also remove the commute a coaching centre demands on an already packed school evening, which matters more in Gurgaon traffic than families sometimes expect.

Online lessons suit a different set of situations well, and this is exactly where families searching for IB and IGCSE online tuition in Gurgaon should focus this comparison. A DP HL specialist in a subject with few Gurgaon-based tutors, a family with an unpredictable evening schedule, or a household managing several tutoring subjects back to back on different weekdays can all get a stronger match online than a home slot alone would allow. Shared digital whiteboards and annotated past papers work well on screen for most subjects, and a student who is disciplined about showing working on paper loses little by working through a webcam. What online genuinely struggles with is a younger or easily distracted student, and the very first session or two, where reading a new student's habits face to face is simply faster than doing it through a screen.

Hybrid, home tuition through the week with an occasional online session for a late slot, a cancelled commute, or a specialist covering one subject only, is what a growing number of Gurgaon families settle into once the first month has shown which format the student actually responds to. There is no universally right answer here: the honest comparison is home tuition first, online second where subject fit or scheduling demands it, and hybrid as the practical middle ground most families land on by the second term.

Online suits a hard-to-find HL specialist or a family managing several subjects on tight evenings.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram verifies a tutor before your first home session
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram shortlists is checked against the specific board and level a family has asked for, not just a general teaching background. That means confirming the tutor has actually taught Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, MYP or DP at the stated level, rather than a related but different board, and checking their subject depth against the exact syllabus a student's school follows where that information is available. A tutor's identity and stated background are verified before their profile is shared with a family, and profiles are updated if a tutor changes what they teach or the levels they cover.

But verification on paper only goes so far, and IB Gram says this plainly rather than overselling a document check. A qualification confirms a subject was studied; it does not confirm a person can explain a stuck IB command term to a nervous fifteen-year-old at seven in the evening after a long school day. That is what the free trial class is actually for, and parents should treat it as part of verification rather than a formality to get through before lessons start.

During or after the trial, a parent should ask direct questions: which levels and boards has this tutor actually taught, how many DP2 or IGCSE Grade 10 students have they worked with in the last year or two, how do they plan to structure the first month, and what would make them recommend a different tutor instead of continuing. A specialist tutor answers these plainly and specifically; a vague or defensive answer is itself useful information.

If a home session does not work the way it was expected to, whether the fit feels wrong or the pace is off, IB Gram's answer is straightforward: say so, and a different match is offered. Continuity matters for board tuition, so switching is not something families should feel awkward asking for once, but it exists precisely because the first match does not always land.

contentBlocks.heading: What should you ask before and after an IB or IGCSE trial lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
Before the trial, ask about board and level match specifically: has this tutor taught this exact syllabus, at this exact tier or level, in the last year or two, not simply IB or IGCSE as a broad label. Ask whether they have taught a DP1 student moving into DP2, or only DP2 students already deep into coursework, since the demands at each stage differ. Ask how they plan the first session: most specialists want to see recent test scripts, a mock paper, or the student's own notes before deciding where to start, rather than opening a random topic and hoping it lines up with a gap that actually exists.

During the trial itself, watch how the tutor responds when the student gets something wrong. A strong specialist treats a wrong answer as diagnostic information and asks a follow-up question rather than simply supplying the correct one; a weaker tutor moves straight past the error to keep the lesson moving. Watch, too, whether the tutor references the actual command term or criterion behind a question, or only the content, since that distinction is often the clearest signal of real board experience.

After the trial, ask two things plainly: what would the tutor prioritise in the first month, and what would tell them, honestly, that this is not the right match. A tutor who cannot answer the second question specifically is not being deliberately evasive so much as inexperienced with being asked; either way, it is useful information for a family deciding whether to commit.

It is also worth asking what a tutor genuinely cannot fix. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a specialist worth hiring says so directly rather than implying otherwise. What a good trial does show is whether the tutor's diagnosis of where the student actually stands matches what the parent already suspected, or surfaces something the parent had missed; either outcome is a good sign that the trial was run properly.

Ask whether they have taught DP1-to-DP2 transitions or only settled DP2 students.
