faqs.question: How many IB and IGCSE home tutors should I shortlist before deciding?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually enough. Shortlisting more than three names rarely improves the decision; it mostly adds confusion for you and inconsistency for your child, who ends up meeting too many new faces in one week. IB Gram narrows to two or three profiles matched on board, level, subject and location, so you are comparing real differences: teaching style, availability, and how each handles a diagnostic question, not a long list of similar-sounding claims. If none of the first shortlist feels right after fair trials, ask for a second round built against what specifically did not work, rather than a fresh unfiltered list.

faqs.question: What should I compare side by side between two shortlisted tutors?
faqs.answer: Compare board and level experience first, then how each handles a diagnostic question in the trial. Ask what each has actually taught, not just claims of general experience; a DP1 Economics HL specialist and an IGCSE Grade 9 generalist are not interchangeable even if both list themselves as an IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon on a profile. Look at travel and slot fit for your sector, whether feedback after sessions is specific or vague, and how each responds when you ask about a student who is not improving. The tutor who answers with a plan, not just reassurance, is usually the stronger comparison.

faqs.question: How do I run trial lessons with two tutors without confusing my child?
faqs.answer: Book both trials in the same week and tell your child upfront that trying two people is normal. Keep the material similar, the same chapter or past paper section, so you are judging teaching approach rather than two unrelated topics. Avoid discussing your comparison notes in front of your child, especially a younger MYP student, since that can turn a normal trial into pressure to perform. After each trial, ask your child one or two specific questions, did the pace feel right, did you feel comfortable asking a question, rather than a general question that usually gets a general answer back.

faqs.question: Can I ask IB Gram for a different tutor if the first shortlisted match is wrong?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a genuine trial and a fair few weeks show the fit is wrong, pace, communication style, or a slot that keeps slipping, tell IB Gram specifically what did not work. A second shortlist is then built against that gap, board, level, subject and location checked again, rather than starting the search from a blank page. Availability for a replacement tutor is subject to schedule, so there may be a short gap, but the goal is a better match, not simply a different name filling the same slot.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor really travel to my sector in DLF, Sushant Lok or SPR on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Mostly yes, but evening traffic between corridors can stretch a short trip, so ask a shortlisted tutor honestly about their existing route before assuming a 6 pm slot will start exactly on time. A tutor already teaching in DLF Phase 3 or Sushant Lok is a steadier weekday fit for those areas than one commuting in from Southern Peripheral Road for the first time. IB Gram matches tutors partly on where they already travel, which is why the shortlist you receive should already reflect realistic sectors, but it is still worth confirming directly during the trial call.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session is missed because of school or travel?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as possible so the slot can be rescheduled rather than simply dropped for the week. Most home tutors working with IB Gram families build some flexibility into a weekly slot, since school events, sudden traffic, or a sick day are normal parts of a Gurgaon school year, not exceptions. A missed session close to mocks or an exam session matters more than one in a quiet month, so flag timing when you reschedule. If missed sessions become frequent on either side, that pattern itself is worth raising as part of comparing whether the match is working.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who charges more automatically better for IB or IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No, and treating price as the main comparison usually leads to a weaker match. What actually predicts a good fit is board and level experience matched precisely to your child, familiarity with your school's pacing, and how a tutor handles a diagnostic question in the trial, not what they charge. Fee structures vary by session, by month or by package, and IB Gram can explain the structure without ever suggesting price should be the deciding factor between two otherwise different profiles. Compare teaching fit first; let cost structure be a secondary, practical filter.

faqs.question: How do I switch from an IGCSE home tutor to a DP-focused one as my child moves up?
faqs.answer: Start the shortlist conversation a term or two before the actual move, since a tutor experienced in the IGCSE to IB DP transition can bridge the gap rather than starting from zero once DP1 begins. Many families need two different tutors across this move: IGCSE tutoring focuses on tier and exam board technique, while DP tutoring shifts toward HL and SL depth, Internal Assessment guidance and Theory of Knowledge or Extended Essay support the earlier tutor may never have touched. Ask IB Gram to shortlist specifically against the upcoming programme, not just the current one, if the move is close.

faqs.question: What if my child shows no progress a month after starting with a shortlisted tutor?
faqs.answer: A month is usually too early to judge real progress; the first few weeks are mostly diagnosis, an error log forming, gaps becoming clear, rather than visible results. If genuinely nothing has changed by six to eight weeks, no attempt at harder questions, no shift in a school test score's direction, raise it directly rather than waiting out the full term. IB Gram can look at whether the mismatch is pace, subject depth or communication style, and shortlist a different tutor against that specific gap. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a clear lack of any movement after two months is worth acting on.

faqs.question: Do I need separate tutors for IGCSE and IB subjects in the same household?
faqs.answer: Often yes, particularly once one child is deep into DP and another is still in IGCSE Grade 9 or 10, since the pacing, marking style and subject depth differ enough that one tutor rarely covers both well. Some families do find one strong generalist who can genuinely handle both stages for a single subject area, but this should be confirmed by what that tutor has actually taught, not assumed from a general label alone. IB Gram can shortlist for each child separately, in parallel, so a DP2 IA deadline and a younger sibling's IGCSE mocks do not compete for the same one person's time.

faqs.question: What does IB Gram check before a tutor ever visits my home in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Board and level experience, subject depth against what your child specifically needs, and background details are reviewed before a tutor is matched to a home visit anywhere in Gurgaon. This is the baseline check on every profile shared with you; it does not replace the questions you should ask yourself in the trial call, specific past results, how they handle a stuck student, and what a first session actually covers. If anything about a profile feels unclear once the trial starts, say so, IB Gram can offer a different match rather than leaving a poor fit to run through the term.

faqs.question: What can I honestly expect IB Gram to guarantee?
faqs.answer: Not a grade, and no tutor can promise one. What IB Gram does is ask about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlist tutors whose profiles are verified and match those needs, arrange a trial or demo session before you commit, and offer a different match if the fit is wrong. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid depending on what suits your family. Availability is always subject to tutor schedule and level, so treat any shortlist as a strong starting point for comparison, not a fixed promise of outcome.

contentBlocks.heading: IB MYP and DP, Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE: What Home Tuition Covers
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon usually means Cambridge IGCSE, set by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, both run as a two-year course across Grade 9 and Grade 10. Cambridge exam series sit in February/March, a series offered only in India, May/June and October/November, and most Cambridge subjects grade A* to G, with Core and Extended tiers on many syllabuses: Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. Edexcel International GCSE runs its main series in January and May/June and grades 9 to 1 across the board. A home tutor working on IGCSE has to know which tier your child is entered for before planning a single lesson, because Core and Extended papers test different depth, not just different difficulty.

The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every MYP subject is graded against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's own grade boundaries. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project, the Community Project comes earlier, in MYP 3 or 4, and some schools opt into MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, though this is a school choice rather than a fixed requirement.

The IB Diploma Programme (DP) is two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points between them, so 45 is the maximum and 24 is the minimum for the diploma, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), which has to be completed but is not scored. A family moving a child from IGCSE Grade 10 into DP1 is really managing two different assessment languages in one household, and a home tutor who has taught both stages, sometimes called an IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor, plans the jump instead of assuming the student will simply adjust.
items: Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses often split into Core (up to grade C) and Extended (up to A*) tiers.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades every subject 9 to 1, with January and May/June series.
MYP marks four criteria (A-D) out of 8 each; the total converts to a final 1-7 grade.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth in IB and IGCSE Home Tuition: Papers, Criteria and Command Terms
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor who is any good at IGCSE or IB moves quickly past the syllabus label and into the actual paper. IGCSE Sciences and Maths typically split into a core or non-calculator paper and an extended or higher paper, marked partly on method and partly on the final answer, so a student who shows working can pick up marks even on a wrong final answer. DP subjects are marked against published command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, and each one demands a different depth of answer; a student who describes when the question says evaluate loses marks regardless of how much they actually know.

Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports, sourced through the school or the IB's own official channels, are where a serious home tutor spends real preparation time, because they show exactly how examiners have awarded marks before, not how a textbook assumes they should. MYP criteria, A to D, each out of 8, reward specific skills per subject, knowledge and understanding in one criterion, investigation or communication in another, so a tutor has to teach toward the criterion descriptors, not just toward getting better at the subject in general.

For IB DP students, the Internal Assessment (IA) and, for some groups, coursework components sit alongside the written exams, and a home tutor's role there is to strengthen a student's own analysis and referencing, never to write or rewrite the work, which is an academic integrity line IB Gram tutors are expected to hold. The Extended Essay (EE), an independent piece of research, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) both reward a student's own argument built over weeks, and a weekly home session is often where that argument actually gets drafted, tested and rewritten rather than left to the night before a deadline.
items: Command terms (define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent) set how deep a DP answer must go.
Core and Extended IGCSE papers test different depth, not just different levels of difficulty.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online Classes or Hybrid: What Suits Your Family in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB and IGCSE home tuition in Gurgaon is the starting point for most families here: a tutor at your dining table means no travel for your child after a full school day, materials stay on the desk between sessions, and a parent can see, without asking, whether the hour was spent working or drifting. Home tuition suits younger students, IGCSE Grade 9 especially, and any subject where a tutor needs to sit beside handwritten working, Maths and the sciences most of all.

Online lessons for IB and IGCSE work well once a student is old enough to manage their own screen and materials without a parent hovering, usually from Grade 10 upward, and especially for a subject specialist who does not live near your corridor, DP Higher Level subjects most often. Families searching for IB and IGCSE online tuition in Gurgaon are usually after exactly this kind of specialist access, not a lower-effort alternative to a home tutor. A shared whiteboard and annotated past papers cover most of what a written subject needs, though a lab-based Sciences IA conversation or handwriting-heavy early Maths work usually goes better in person.

In short: home tuition wins on attention and consistency for younger students and handwriting-heavy subjects; online wins on access to a specific specialist and on evenings when Gurgaon traffic makes a home visit impractical; hybrid, one home session and one online session most weeks, is often the honest middle ground for a DP2 student balancing five or six subjects against a packed school week.

None of the three is automatically better. A family on Dwarka Expressway with a rare subject combination may do better mostly online with one home session a month for exam technique; a family on Golf Course Road with a Grade 9 student still building study habits usually gets more from a home tutor twice a week. IB Gram asks about this at the very first conversation rather than assuming a default.

contentBlocks.heading: The First Home Session: Study Space, Materials and What to Prepare
contentBlocks.body:
The first session of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Gurgaon matters more than families usually expect, because a tutor is reading your child's actual level in real time, not the level a profile or an old report card suggests. A parent does not need to sit through the lesson, but being reachable in the next room for the first fifteen minutes, in case the tutor has a question about the syllabus your child's school is actually following, helps more than hovering over every answer.

A study space does not need to be a separate room. A cleared table, decent lighting, and a chair that is not the sofa are usually enough; what matters more is that the same spot is used most weeks, so materials, a folder of past papers, a calculator, the right instrument set for Maths, do not have to be found from scratch each time. For a DP or MYP student, having last term's assessed work on hand for the first session lets the tutor see actual examiner or teacher feedback rather than working from a general impression.

Before the first home visit, it helps to have:
1. The current textbook, workbook or set text, plus any recent tests or assignments with feedback already on them.
2. A note of the exact syllabus code or tier, Cambridge Extended, Edexcel Higher, DP HL or SL, if you know it.
3. A short list of what has been hardest recently, in the student's own words if possible, not just the parent's guess.

None of this needs to be perfect. A tutor experienced with home tuition in Gurgaon has sat at dozens of different dining tables and adjusts fast; what helps most is simply not scrambling for a pen and a past paper five minutes before the tutor arrives, because that first quarter hour is where the whole term's pace gets set.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Should Look Like After a Month of Home Tuition in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Real progress in the first month of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Gurgaon rarely looks dramatic. It usually looks like a student attempting a past paper question they would have skipped four weeks earlier, or catching their own mistake in working before the tutor points it out. Grades in a single school test can move for reasons that have nothing to do with tuition, an easier topic, a lucky guess, so the more honest marker is whether the student's own error log is shrinking week to week.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any family told otherwise should be cautious. What a good home tutor can promise is a clear plan, regular feedback to parents on what was covered and what still needs work, and an honest flag if a subject needs more than one session a week to catch up before a mock or the exam session. Judging what counts as the best IB and IGCSE home tuition in Gurgaon comes down to fit and consistency measured over weeks, not a ranking claim. If four to six weeks pass with no visible change in the error log or the student's own confidence, that is the point to ask IB Gram for a different tutor or a different approach, not to wait quietly.

Starting late narrows what is realistically possible. A DP2 student beginning home tuition three months before May can still make real gains in exam technique and command-term accuracy, but is not going to close a two-year gap in content in that window, and a tutor who says otherwise is not being straight with the family. The honest version of progress is steady, checkable, and slower than marketing language usually promises.

contentBlocks.body:
Most families asking about IB and IGCSE home tuitions in Gurgaon are not looking for a single recommendation; they want two or three genuine options to weigh against each other before committing. IB Gram treats that as the normal request rather than an unusual one. The first conversation, a query or a free consultation, covers your child's board, level, subject and your sector, and from there a shortlist is built rather than a single name handed over.

Every profile on that shortlist has already been checked against the exact syllabus and level you named, so the comparison you are doing is a real one, board experience, which level they teach most, how familiar they are with your specific school's pacing, not a comparison between one verified tutor and one unverified guess. Each profile comes with a short note explaining the match, which makes comparing two or three side by side considerably faster than reading three unrelated profiles cold.

Trial classes can be arranged with more than one tutor if you genuinely cannot decide from profiles alone, and there is nothing unusual about wanting to see two people teach before choosing. Once you choose, that is not the end of the process either: if the choice does not hold up after a few weeks, IB Gram arranges a different tutor the same way, from board, level and slot, rather than treating the first choice as final and irreversible. Comparing IB and IGCSE home tuitions in Gurgaon properly, rather than settling for whichever profile replies first, is the single step families most often skip and most often regret skipping once a term has already gone by.

contentBlocks.heading: IB MYP, DP and IGCSE Side by Side
contentBlocks.body:
When you are comparing two or three tutors rather than accepting the first one, the programme structure itself becomes a useful checklist rather than background reading. The IB Middle Years Programme covers five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, and every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, with the total out of 32 converting to a final 1 to 7 grade. Ask a shortlisted tutor plainly which subject groups and which MYP years they have actually taught, since MYP experience on its own tells you very little.

The Diploma Programme runs two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level with around 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level with around 150 hours, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 more points toward a 45 maximum, 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, alongside CAS. A tutor comfortable at Standard Level is not automatically ready for the analytical depth Higher Level expects, so this is worth asking about directly rather than assuming.

IGCSE comparisons need the same precision: Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, grades most syllabuses A* to G with Core and Extended tiers on many subjects, Core capping at grade C and Extended reaching A*, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades on a 9 to 1 scale, usually without that Core and Extended split. Exam series differ too, Cambridge's February/March series runs only in India alongside May/June and October/November, Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May/June, so ask which series a shortlisted tutor's recent students actually sat, not just which board they mention.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should You Actually Compare Between Two Subject Tutors?
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing subject depth between two tutors is more useful than comparing years of experience alone, since a tutor who has taught IB Diploma Higher Level Physics for years may still be new to Cambridge IGCSE Extended Physics, and the reverse is just as common. Ask each shortlisted tutor which specific topics they have taught most recently, a particular DP unit, a particular IGCSE syllabus section, rather than accepting a general claim of subject strength.

How a tutor marks matters as much as what they know. DP command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, set how deep an answer needs to go, and a tutor who cannot explain the difference between a describe answer and an evaluate answer in a trial conversation is unlikely to mark that distinction consistently in a real session either. Ask each tutor how they would mark a specific piece of work, a Maths IA outline, an English oral response, and compare the two answers directly.

MYP comparisons need a slightly different question: ask which of the four criteria, A to D, each tutor is strongest at explaining, since a subject can be assessed unevenly if a tutor leans on the criteria they understand best and glosses over the rest. A tutor who can name a real past paper, mark scheme or subject report they have recently used with a student, sourced through the school or the relevant board's own official channels, is usually a stronger comparison point than one who speaks only in general terms about the syllabus.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Home, Online and Hybrid Tuitions Before You Choose?
contentBlocks.body:
Comparing tutors is not only about comparing people; it is often worth comparing modes of teaching too before settling on a pattern. Home tuition lets you watch, in person, exactly where a working step goes wrong or where an essay plan loses its thread, and for many families that close, hands-on marking is worth the extra travel time a tutor needs to build into their week.

Online tuition widens the pool of tutors you can genuinely compare, since a strong DP Higher Level specialist who does not live near your corridor becomes a real option rather than an impossible one. A shared digital whiteboard and annotated past papers cover most subject content perfectly well, and comparing an online trial against a home trial directly, for the same subject, is often the clearest way to see which mode actually suits your child rather than guessing.

Hybrid tuition, splitting sessions between home and online across the week, is worth comparing against a single-mode arrangement too: closer marking for an Extended Essay draft or IA outline in person, routine practice and past paper review online. A family near Golf Course Extension Road, where evening traffic can stretch a short trip considerably, sometimes finds a hybrid pattern compares favourably against committing every single session to a home visit, simply because it is easier to sustain across a full term. When you are comparing modes rather than just people, it helps to ask each shortlisted tutor which pattern they would actually recommend for your subject, since a tutor honest enough to suggest hybrid over full home tuition, when that genuinely suits the subject better, is usually worth trusting on the rest of the comparison too.

contentBlocks.heading: Checking Two Tutors' Profiles Without Wasting Anyone's Time

IB Gram verifies every shortlisted profile against the exact syllabus and level you named before it reaches you, so a genuine comparison starts from two or three tutors who have already cleared that first check, rather than one verified name and one unknown one. That still leaves real differences worth comparing yourself: teaching style, pacing, how each tutor handles a student who is stuck.

Ask each shortlisted tutor the same set of questions so the comparison is fair rather than accidental: a topic they have recently taught, how they would mark a specific piece of work, whether they can work from your school's own scheme of work. A tutor who answers with a concrete example is generally easier to judge than one who answers only in general terms, and running the same questions past both tutors makes the difference between the two answers much clearer.

Trial classes are the most useful comparison of all, and running them the same way with each tutor, same subject, similar length, ideally close together in time, keeps the comparison fair rather than skewed by one trial happening on a good day and the other on a tired evening. Write down your impressions straight after each trial rather than trying to remember both a week later, since small differences in explanation style are easy to forget once time has passed. A short list of two or three lines per tutor, covering clarity, pace and how they handled a wrong answer, is usually enough to make the eventual choice feel considered rather than rushed.

contentBlocks.heading: Running Trial Lessons With More Than One Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Running trial lessons with more than one tutor works best with a little structure rather than treating it as two unrelated appointments. Space the two trials a few days apart so your child is not juggling two new adults and two new teaching styles in the same evening, and where possible, ask both tutors to cover similar content, the same topic or a comparable difficulty level, so you are comparing like with like rather than one easy session against one genuinely hard one.

After each trial, ask your child directly which one felt clearer, not simply which tutor they liked more, since likeability and teaching effectiveness are related but not identical, and a student can enjoy a friendly session that taught them very little. Feed that back to IB Gram honestly, including anything that felt off, since it sharpens the shortlist for the choice you are about to make and for any future comparison too.

contentBlocks.heading: How to Judge Which Tutor Is Working After a Trial Month in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Choosing between two well-matched tutors after a trial does not guarantee the choice was right, and it is worth watching the following weeks honestly rather than assuming the comparison ended the moment you decided. No tutor, however impressive in a single trial class, can guarantee a grade, a score or a mark boundary, and a strong first impression sometimes fades once the novelty of a new tutor wears off.

A more reliable signal, a few weeks in, is a shrinking error log: the same type of mistake, a misapplied command term, a repeated working slip, showing up less often, rather than one dramatic test result. Confidence in a draft Extended Essay outline or a first Internal Assessment attempt often shifts before raw marks visibly catch up, since the student stops second-guessing structure before they get measurably faster at producing content.

Give the chosen tutor a genuinely fair term, roughly ten to twelve weeks, before wondering whether the one you did not choose might have been better; that comparison is rarely fair to run in your head after the fact. If progress does stall after a fair trial, going back to comparing a fresh pair of tutors is a reasonable next step, not a sign the earlier process failed, and IB Gram builds that second shortlist the same careful way as the first. Families who compared properly the first time round usually find the second comparison, if it is ever needed at all, considerably faster, since they already know what to ask and what to watch for in a trial class.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Finds and Verifies Your Private Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A parent calling about a private tutor rarely leads with a syllabus code; they lead with a person: someone their child will sit across a table from twice a week for months, so trust and chemistry matter as much as subject knowledge. Nothing about choosing an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Gurgaon should feel like picking from a catalogue; it should feel like meeting a specific person. IB Gram's first conversation asks about both sides of that: the board, syllabus and level on one hand, and on the other, what kind of person tends to work well with this particular child, whether that is someone patient and slow-paced or someone who pushes harder.

The process that follows is deliberately short.

1. Tell IB Gram the board, syllabus, level, school calendar and the kind of tutor personality your child responds to.
2. Receive a shortlist of verified, independent tutors matched on both the syllabus and, as closely as possible, that personal fit.
3. Meet the tutor properly at a free demo or trial session before any ongoing commitment is made.

If the subject knowledge is right but the person is wrong, that shows up fast in a trial lesson, and IB Gram treats a request to see someone else as completely normal. What you are ultimately choosing is not a service but a specific individual your child will work with regularly, and getting that choice right matters more than any single syllabus detail.

contentBlocks.heading: DP, MYP and IGCSE Through the Eyes of One Private Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
A single private tutor covering the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) has to hold the whole two-year picture in mind: DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum and a 24-point minimum, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Most private tutors specialise in one or two subjects rather than the whole DP, so a family often ends up with more than one private tutor across the six subjects, each chosen individually rather than as a package.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP), running five years across MYP 1 to 5 and eight subject groups, assesses every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, with the total out of 32 converting to a final 1 to 7 grade. A private tutor working with a younger MYP student, ahead of the Personal Project in MYP 5 or the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, is often as much about building consistent study habits as about any one subject, since the habits formed here carry into DP.

Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE typically run across Grades 9 and 10 ahead of the DP, A Levels, or a return to CBSE or ISC. An IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor, as families often describe the search, is really asking for one person who can carry a student credibly across that boundary; it happens, but most families end up choosing an IGCSE specialist and a separate DP specialist, the kind of international board tutor in Gurugram families look for once the stage actually changes.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Subjects Benefit Most From One Dedicated Private Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
A single, dedicated private tutor helps most in subjects where consistency over months matters more than a one-off explanation: Maths and the Sciences, where each topic builds directly on the last, and any subject with a long-running Internal Assessment (IA) or coursework piece that needs the same person tracking its progress from first draft to final submission.

Language subjects benefit in a different way: a private tutor who has worked with a student for a full year notices small, specific patterns, a habit of over-explaining in Written Assignments or an unusually strong grasp of literary technique but a weak structure, that a new tutor meeting the student for the first time simply cannot see yet. This is the real argument for keeping the same private tutor across a full academic year where possible, rather than treating tutoring as a series of unconnected sessions.

For DP subjects with a substantial IA, one private tutor following the work from topic selection through to the final draft can flag a weak research question early, months before the deadline makes it a genuine problem, while keeping the actual data collection and analysis clearly the student's own under the IB's academic integrity rules. A tutor who has taught the same student for a year also tends to know, almost instinctively, which command term the student consistently misreads, which is the kind of detail that only shows up over time, not in a single session. None of this happens in a single trial lesson; it builds gradually, session by session, which is the real case for choosing one dedicated private tutor rather than rotating between whoever is available that week.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Private Tutor Should Know About Your Child's School Calendar in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; schools are mentioned only to describe the calendar a private tutor has to work around, not to claim any relationship. A private home tutor working with a student at Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali or DPS International Edge needs to know that school's actual dates for unit tests, parent-teacher meetings and mock examinations, not a generic academic year, since most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May exam session with results released in early July.

A good private tutor asks for these dates directly in the first conversation, and adjusts the session plan around them rather than teaching to a fixed template regardless of what the school is doing that week. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually months ahead of May, and a private tutor who has not asked about them is effectively guessing at when to intensify revision.

The tutor should also understand, without being told twice, that a student juggling CAS, sports fixtures, a Personal Project deadline and a full school day has limited bandwidth, and a private tutor who pushes an ambitious plan regardless of that reality is doing the student a disservice, however well-intentioned the effort. Asking about the school calendar in the very first conversation, rather than after the first missed deadline, is one of the simplest signs a private tutor is paying attention.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutor, Online Tutor or Hybrid: Choosing the Right Format
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor remains IB Gram's most common private arrangement: one verified person who comes to your house, sits with your child at their own desk, and gets to know their handwriting, their pace and their habits over repeated sessions. For most families choosing a private tutor for the first time, a home tutor is the natural starting point, since it is the format that makes the personal relationship, which matters so much in a one-to-one arrangement, easiest to build.

An online private tutor makes sense once a family has identified a specific specialist who does not live close enough to visit, or once the relationship with a home tutor is already established and a second, harder-to-find specialist needs to be added for one subject. The personal dynamic that matters in a home arrangement, trust, consistency, a tutor who notices when a student is having an off day, works just as well over video once the pair has met properly at least once.

Hybrid tuition, splitting time between a home tutor for one subject and an online tutor for another, suits a family managing more than one private tutor at once, each chosen individually for their own subject specialism. The honest trade-off is that a family juggling two tutors in two formats has to manage two separate relationships and two separate schedules, which asks more of a parent's coordination than a single home tutor covering everything would. Most families only take on that extra coordination once they have already found one tutor they trust and simply need a second specialist for a subject the first cannot cover.

contentBlocks.heading: How We Check a Private Tutor Before They Meet Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Every private tutor on IB Gram's shortlist has a verified profile before a family ever hears their name: board and syllabus experience checked against what is claimed, the level and subjects confirmed, and a direct conversation about how they actually teach a one-to-one session, not just a list of qualifications. Because a private tutor works alone with one child, repeatedly, this check matters more here than in a group or classroom setting, and IB Gram treats it accordingly.

Parents are encouraged to ask their own questions too: which specific syllabus codes has the tutor taught in the last year, how would they describe their teaching style in their own words, and are they comfortable putting the schedule, confidentiality and cancellation terms in writing rather than as a loose verbal understanding. A tutor's answer to 'what would you do in the first session with a student you have not met' often reveals more than a list of credentials.

The free demo or trial session is where a family actually meets this specific person, watches how they explain something the child does not yet understand, and judges tone as much as competence. If the personal fit feels wrong even when the subject knowledge is strong, say so; IB Gram treats a request to try someone else as routine, since the relationship between one tutor and one child is the entire point of going private. This verification happens once, before you ever see a name, so the shortlist you receive has already cleared the basic checks rather than leaving you to do that work yourself.

contentBlocks.heading: Is Your Child's Own Teacher the Right Person to Tutor Them?
contentBlocks.body:
Usually not, and the reason is structural rather than personal: a teacher who privately tutors their own student is also the person setting classwork, marking it, and often contributing to an internal predicted grade for that same student, which creates a conflict of interest no amount of good intention fully removes.

This matters most in the moments that count. If a student is struggling and needs to say so honestly, they may hesitate to admit confusion to the same person who will later grade their work in class, which is exactly the honesty a private tutor most needs to hear. An independent private tutor, meeting the student only in the tutoring relationship, has no such conflict, and a student is often more candid with someone entirely outside the school system. Some schools explicitly prohibit staff from privately tutoring their own students for this reason, so it is worth checking your child's school policy before assuming a teacher's offer is straightforwardly acceptable.

An outside private tutor should still be mapped closely to the school's own scheme of work, not working from a generic syllabus order, and the way to do this is to ask, through the student or the school directly where allowed, what topics and assessments are coming up next. A good private tutor asks this routinely rather than once at the start, since a scheme of work shifts as a term progresses. What a student says in a private session, including what they find hard or embarrassing, should stay between the family and the tutor; a private tutor who casually mentions a student's struggles outside that relationship, even to be helpful, has broken something that is hard to rebuild.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Know Your Private Home Tutor Is the Right Fit?
contentBlocks.body:
Within the first month, a right-fit private tutor should be visible in specific, ordinary ways: the student mentions the tutor by name without being prompted, asks a question between sessions that shows they have actually been thinking about the subject, and completes homework without a daily reminder. A written note after each session, naming what was actually covered, is a simple but reliable sign that the relationship is functioning properly rather than just occupying an evening slot.

Fit is not only about subject competence. A private tutor who is technically excellent but whose manner does not suit your child, too impatient for a nervous student, too slow-paced for a confident one, will not produce results, however strong their syllabus knowledge is on paper. There is no verifiable 'best' IB and IGCSE private tutor in Gurgaon, only the person whose manner and syllabus experience actually fit your child; if a month of sessions has produced no named, specific improvement and the student seems no more comfortable with the tutor than on day one, it is worth asking for someone different rather than assuming more time alone will fix a personality mismatch.

No private tutor, however good, can guarantee a grade, and any private tutor who implies otherwise should be treated with real suspicion. Starting a private arrangement close to an exam session narrows what a new tutor can realistically achieve before results day, and an honest tutor says this plainly rather than promising a rescue in a few weeks. The relationship between one tutor and one student, sustained over months, is what makes private tutoring valuable; a family that keeps switching tutors every few weeks rarely gets that benefit.

Getting started takes one conversation. The first session is best treated as a genuine introduction rather than a lesson in the usual sense: expect the tutor to spend real time getting to know how your child thinks and works, alongside a short piece of actual work, whether a past paper question or a recent essay, so the match can be judged properly. Bring a recent test or piece of marked work if you have one; it helps the tutor start from something concrete rather than a blank slate.

After the trial, agree the schedule, cancellation notice and confidentiality terms in writing before the first paid session. faqs.question: Is it a conflict of interest for my child's own teacher to be their private tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, structurally, even when the teacher's intentions are good, because the same person setting and marking your child's classwork is also being paid privately by your family, which can make it harder for a student to admit confusion honestly. Some schools have explicit policies against staff privately tutoring their own students for exactly this reason, so it is worth checking before assuming the offer is straightforward. An independent private tutor with no classroom relationship to your child removes this conflict entirely, and many families find their child is more candid with someone entirely outside the school system.

faqs.question: How is a private tutor's background actually checked before matching?
faqs.answer: IB Gram verifies board and syllabus experience against what a tutor claims, confirms the level and subjects they say they can teach, and has a direct conversation about how they run a one-to-one session before ever shortlisting them to a family. Because a private tutor works alone, repeatedly, with one child, this check is treated more carefully than for a group setting, and it happens before you ever see a profile. You are also encouraged to ask your own questions at the free demo, including how the tutor would approach a first session with a student they have never met.

faqs.question: What if my child does not get along with the private tutor personally?
faqs.answer: Say so, and IB Gram will shortlist someone else; personal fit is treated as seriously as subject knowledge, since a private tutor who is technically excellent but whose manner clashes with your child rarely produces good results. This is one reason the free demo session matters so much: it shows tone, pace and manner, not just competence, and a mismatch usually becomes obvious within that first meeting. Switching tutors after a poor fit costs a short conversation, not a restart of the whole matching process, since your child's board, syllabus and level are already on file.

faqs.question: Should the same private tutor stay with my child for the whole academic year?
faqs.answer: Where possible, yes, because a tutor who has worked with a student for a full year notices specific patterns, a recurring weak command term or a strength that could be built on, that a new tutor meeting the child for the first time cannot yet see. Even so, a change is sometimes the right call: if the fit was never quite right, or if the student is moving from IGCSE to the DP and the syllabus demands a different specialist, switching is entirely reasonable. Continuity is valuable, not compulsory, and IB Gram supports either choice depending on what your family actually needs.

faqs.question: How much does an independent private tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on the subject, the level, whether sessions run at home or online, and how many sessions a week your family needs, so IB Gram will not quote a figure without understanding those details first during your consultation. A dedicated one-to-one private tutor is generally priced to reflect that ongoing, individual relationship rather than shared time, and the exact structure is confirmed with you directly before anything is booked. Availability for a specific subject, level and tutor personality is always subject to tutor availability, particularly close to the May exam session when demand rises.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor realistically reach us on Sohna Road every week?
faqs.answer: Many private tutors covering Sohna Road, including Sector 47 to 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2 and Rosewood City, are based somewhere along the same stretch, so a weekly evening slot here is generally reliable once the tutor's own base is factored into matching. Societies such as Central Park Resorts, Vatika City and Malibu Towne sit within this same corridor, and IB Gram asks specifically where a family lives before shortlisting so the tutor's realistic travel radius is already accounted for, not discovered after the first missed session. If a slot does slip because of Sohna Road traffic, moving that one week online is a simple fix.

faqs.question: Is DLF Phase 2 to 4 or Cyber City easy for a home tutor to reach on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, but expect the tutor to prefer a slightly later slot, since evening office traffic around MG Road and Cyber City peaks earlier than in residential-only corridors and a 6 pm slot can be harder to hold reliably than one starting closer to 7 pm. Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur and the sectors around DLF Phase 2 to 4 are otherwise well connected, and most tutors already covering this area can offer decent slot choice. If your family needs an earlier slot specifically, say so during matching, since it narrows the shortlist to tutors who have confirmed they can make that timing work.

faqs.question: Does a private home tutor need a parent in the room during lessons?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily; it depends on your child's age and what feels right for your family, though IB Gram generally suggests a parent or responsible adult being reachable in the house for at least the first few sessions while trust between tutor and student is still forming. Older DP students in particular often work better without a parent present once the relationship is established, while a younger MYP student may need someone nearby a little longer. This is worth agreeing directly with the tutor early on, alongside the schedule and confidentiality expectations, rather than assuming either way by default.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tutoring session with our private tutor is missed?
faqs.answer: It is rescheduled by direct agreement with the tutor, the same as any private appointment, and reasonable cancellation notice, ideally agreed in writing when the arrangement starts, protects both sides from last-minute confusion. If sessions keep getting missed because of a clash with school activities or travel, it is worth revisiting the weekly slot itself with the tutor rather than continuously rescheduling around a timing that no longer fits. IB Gram can help adjust the arrangement, including changing the weekly day or moving a session online, if the original plan stops being realistic for either side.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a private tutor run?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week is the usual starting point for most subjects, rising to three during exam years or once a subject has fallen behind school pace, and dropping to one for lighter, revision-focused support. A DP HL subject with 240 recommended teaching hours over two years generally needs a steadier rhythm than an SL subject at 150 hours, and the right frequency is something your private tutor should actively revisit as the term develops, not fix once and leave unchanged. Raise it directly with the tutor if the current frequency feels too light or too heavy for where your child actually is.

faqs.question: Is a coaching centre batch a reasonable substitute for a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It can work for a student who mainly needs structured, affordable practice and does not need close, individual attention, but it is not really a substitute for a private tutor if your child needs someone tracking their specific gaps, an IA draft or a particular command term over months. A batch built for CBSE, JEE or NEET in particular tends to fit IB or IGCSE syllabuses poorly, since the pacing and question style are simply different. If a batch has been tried and the student is still stuck on the same specific issue after a term, a dedicated private tutor is usually the more direct next step.

heroSubtitle: A private tutor is an arrangement your family makes directly, outside school. This page covers how deep the realistic shortlist is in your own corridor, what to settle in writing before the first lesson, and when widening the search to online beats waiting for a home slot that may never appear.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon are independent teachers a family hires directly, usually for home tuition at the family's own address, and the honest first question is how many of them your corridor actually holds. Depth varies. Sector 66 and Sector 67 on Southern Peripheral Road sit close to the corridors tutors already travel, so a shortlist of two or three profiles for a common subject is realistic. Push out to Sector 113 on Dwarka Expressway on a weekday evening and the same request may return one workable home tutor and one online specialist. This page is about that difference, about comparing fairly when the pool is thin, and about the private arrangement itself: confidentiality, the conflict of interest when a student's own school teacher takes them after hours, and what belongs in writing before the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram build a shortlist of IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, and IB Gram works backwards from what you tell it: board, syllabus, level, the school's calendar, your sector and the evenings that are genuinely free. From that it shortlists verified profiles that match, arranges a demo or trial session, and swaps the match if the fit is wrong.

The order matters, because the constraint that kills most matches is not subject knowledge. It is the slot. A tutor who has taught Diploma Programme (DP) Chemistry for years is no use to you if the only evening he can reach Sector 84 is the one your son has football.

1. Tell us the board and level exactly: Cambridge IGCSE Extended, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Higher tier, Middle Years Programme (MYP) 4, DP1 Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL).
2. Tell us the school and its calendar, particularly the month its DP2 mock examinations fall, so the plan is built backwards from the real pressure point.
3. Tell us your address at sector or society level, and the two or three evening windows left after school buses and activities.
4. We shortlist verified profiles that match all three, usually two or three, sometimes one where the subject is rare or the corridor is thin.
5. You run a demo or trial session with the profiles you want to compare, and we tell you honestly how many the corridor can support.
6. You begin, or you ask for a different match, which costs you a week and nothing else.

Everything here stays subject to tutor availability, which changes week to week. In September, when the new academic year settles and parents in New Gurgaon and along Dwarka Expressway all start looking for home tuition at once, the same request returns fewer names than it does in the quieter weeks after the May session ends.

The school's mock month, so revision is planned backwards from it
