contentBlocks.heading: Two boards in one house: IGCSE Grade 10 and the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
A Gurgaon household often runs two boards at once: one child in Cambridge IGCSE Grade 10, the elder in DP2. They are not the same job, and a private tutor who is strong at one is not automatically strong at the other. This is the single most common reason a family ends up with two tutors instead of one.

IGCSE in Gurgaon means Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses available in 9-1 versions under different codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, and the ceiling differs: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. Tier entry is a real decision, and a tutor who has never sat with a family through it will not raise it.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it.

The Diploma Programme is two years, DP1 and DP2: six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must be completed as well. So an IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor is a specific request, not a general one.
items: Cambridge Core tops out at grade C; Extended reaches A*
MYP criteria A to D, each 0 to 8, totalling 32 before boundaries
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL, each graded 1 to 7
TOK and the Extended Essay contribute up to 3 points towards 45
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is graded 9-1, on its own series
Personal Project in MYP 5, Community Project in MYP 3 or 4

contentBlocks.heading: Subject depth narrows a shortlist faster than your address does
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE Mathematics, IGCSE Physics, MYP Maths and DP Economics SL are taught widely enough that most corridors hold more than one credible private tutor. DP Higher Level Chemistry with Internal Assessment (IA) support, IGCSE Business Studies coursework, or a Group 2 language at HL will often return a single name, or none within travelling distance of your sector.

Parents sometimes ask for an international board tutor in Gurugram and mean nothing more specific than that. Push the request one level down, to the syllabus and the tier, and the shortlist changes completely. Ask any shortlisted tutor to describe the assessment rather than the topic. For Cambridge, that means the paper structure of the exact syllabus your child is entered for, whether the entry is Core or Extended, and which paper carries the non-calculator or practical work. For Edexcel, it means the January and May/June series and what 9-1 grading does to a borderline student. For the Diploma Programme, it means how HL and SL differ in that subject, the IA criteria as the subject guide words them, and the fact that the Extended Essay is supervised at school rather than by an outside tutor.

Command terms are the quickest test of all. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth of answer, and a student who writes a description where the question said evaluate loses marks he knew the content well enough to earn. A tutor who teaches command terms from the first lesson is working on marks. A tutor who only re-explains the chapter is working on content the school has already covered.

Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show exactly how marks are awarded. Ask what the tutor will do with them and when. The week before mocks is late. If the subject is rare, decide early whether you want the nearest IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon or the right one, because those are frequently different people.
items: Ask about paper structure and components, not the chapter list
Core or Extended entry changes the ceiling, so confirm the entry first
Command terms: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent
IA support means feedback on drafts, never writing the student's work
Rare HL subjects often hold one candidate per corridor, or none

contentBlocks.heading: How deep is the home tuition shortlist in your corridor of Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon is not one market for tutors. It is three or four travel plans laid over each other, and the practical question is how many home tutor profiles your corridor can hold at the hour you need. The answer changes over a few streets.

Southern Peripheral Road (SPR) is usually the deepest of the three corridors for IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon. Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69 and Sector 70 sit close together, so a tutor teaching in Sector 67 at five can reasonably take a second student in Sector 69 at seven. Tata Primanti and the neighbouring sectors pair well inside one evening. Push south to Sector 72, Ansal Esencia or Bhondsi and the pairing breaks: the trip stops being a hop and becomes the whole evening, so fewer tutors will quote for it, and those who do will want a fixed weekly slot they can protect.

New Gurgaon runs on the same logic with wider gaps. Sector 82, Sector 83, Sector 84, Sector 85 and Sector 86 are dense enough that IB and IGCSE private tutors in New Gurgaon often build a two-student evening inside Vatika India Next or between neighbouring sectors. Sector 89 and Sector 90 are workable. Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road addresses are where the shortlist thins, because a tutor crossing back at eight has lost the slot after yours. Families in Godrej Air usually do better asking for an early evening than a late one.

Dwarka Expressway is the newest corridor and the least predictable. Sector 102, Sector 103, Sector 104 and Sector 106 are reachable on most evenings. Sector 108, Sector 109, Sector 110 and Sector 113 stretch the plan, and families in Sobha City, Godrej Summit and ATS Kocoon regularly find that IB and IGCSE private tutors on Dwarka Expressway offer weekends at home and midweek online rather than five weekday evenings. That is a real constraint of Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, not a service failure, and it is far better said in advance than discovered in October.
items: IB and IGCSE private tutors on Southern Peripheral Road often pair two nearby sectors in one evening
Sector 72, Ansal Esencia and Bhondsi need a protected fixed weekly slot
Vatika India Next and Godrej Air: ask for early evening, not late
Sector 108 to Sector 113 often works as weekend home classes plus midweek online
Society gate entry and visitor registration add time to every first visit

contentBlocks.heading: When do Gurgaon families compete for the same tutors?
contentBlocks.body:
Twice a year the demand curve spikes, and both times it is the school calendar doing it. The first wave is September, once the new academic year has settled, the first unit tests are back, and DP1 students discover that Higher Level is not Grade 10 with extra homework. The second is the run-up to the DP2 mock examinations, which each school sets for itself, usually several months before the May session.

If you start looking in those weeks, expect a shorter shortlist and less choice of slot. Families at Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge are all working to their own school's internal deadlines, and those deadlines cluster in the same months. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May session; November is used by a minority of schools and by retake candidates. May results are released in early July. Cambridge series run in February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Write your own child's series down before you call anybody, because a tutor planning for May/June and a school entering for February/March are weeks out of step, and nobody notices until revision has already started late.

The quiet weeks are the ones just after a session ends and the early part of the winter break. A family that begins home tuition in July, with no test in sight, gets first pick of slots and a tutor with time to diagnose properly. A family that begins the week before mocks gets whoever happens to be free.
items: September and the pre-mock weeks are the two crowded hiring windows
Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, months before the May session
Cambridge series: February/March in India, May/June, October/November
Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June
May results are released in early July, which frees evening slots
Starting in a quiet week buys a better slot and a proper diagnosis

contentBlocks.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid: what should a Gurgaon family widen to?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the default here, and for good reason. The tutor comes to you, the student stays in his own room with his own folder of school handouts, and nobody loses ninety minutes to traffic on Southern Peripheral Road at six in the evening. A home tutor also sees what a screen hides: a Grade 10 student with no working surface, or a DP2 student whose phone sits face-up on the table through every session.

Online is the honest answer when the corridor cannot supply what the subject needs. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon may be the only person teaching a particular Higher Level option, and a live lesson with a shared whiteboard and an annotated past paper works well for problem-solving, markscheme walkthroughs and essay feedback. It works less well for a younger MYP student who needs somebody sitting beside him, and for subjects where a physical setup matters.

Hybrid is what most families in Sector 109 and Sector 113 end up with, often without planning it: a home session at the weekend when travel is easy, plus a midweek online session for doubt-solving before a class test. It keeps the relationship personal and the schedule realistic, which is more than can be said for five weekday evenings that nobody can actually protect.

The decision rule is short. If your corridor holds two or three credible home tutors for the subject, compare them and choose. If it holds one, and that one is wrong on level, on slot or on the trial, widen to online rather than settling. A mediocre home tutor at a convenient hour costs more across a year than an inconvenient hour with the right specialist. And a slot that fights the family calendar gets cancelled in the end, whatever mode it runs in.
items: Home tuition first: no travel for the student, school folder within reach
Online reaches a specialist your corridor simply does not hold
Hybrid: home classes at the weekend, online midweek for doubt-solving
Younger MYP students usually need somebody sitting beside them
Widen the search before lowering the standard on level or subject

contentBlocks.heading: How a private tutor is verified before the first home visit
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified, which means the board and level experience shown on a profile has been checked before that profile reaches you. Treat that as the floor and not the ceiling. Somebody is going to be alone in your home with your child, and you are entitled to do your own checks without apologising for them.

Ask for photo identification at the door on the first visit and register the visit at your society gate the way you would for anyone else. In Tata Primanti, Sobha City or Vatika India Next, gate entry and visitor registration take a few minutes, so warn the tutor beforehand instead of leaving him at the boom barrier while the session clock runs. Keep the study space in a common area with the door open. A home tutor working in a family room is normal practice, not a sign of suspicion, and any experienced tutor will expect it.

Then check the teaching claim itself. Send the tutor a marked school test or a past paper answer of your child's before the trial, and ask what mark he would give it and why. A specialist answers in the language of the assessment: the criterion, the command term, the markscheme point that was missed. A general tutor says the answer needs more detail.

Two questions parents forget. First, does this tutor currently teach at your child's school, and if so, does he teach your child's class? Second, what will he do with what he learns about your child? Those are the two places a private arrangement goes wrong, and both are easier to raise before money changes hands than after. A tutor who is uncomfortable answering either one has answered.
items: Photo identification at the door, and normal society visitor registration
Lessons in a common area with the door open, as standard practice
Ask the tutor to mark one of your child's past answers before the trial
Ask directly whether the tutor teaches at your child's school
Agree what the tutor may and may not say about your child to others

contentBlocks.heading: What does a private tutoring arrangement actually mean in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A private tutor is an independent teacher your family engages directly, outside the school, at your own cost, and answerable to you rather than to the school. That is the whole definition. A school's remedial period, its subject clinic and its own teachers' extra classes are something else entirely: they sit inside the school's authority, follow the school's scheme of work and report to the school. IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon work alongside all of that, never inside it.

The distinction matters most when the private tutor is your child's own subject teacher. It happens, and it is worth naming plainly. A teacher who teaches your daughter in class, assesses her internal work, and is paid by you in the evening is holding three roles at once, one of which involves marking work he has been paid to help produce. Even where everyone acts in good faith, the family has lost the independent second opinion an outside tutor exists to give. Some schools do not permit the arrangement at all. If your school does and you still want it, ask the coordinator in writing first and keep the reply. An independent tutor avoids the question altogether.

Confidentiality is the second thing to settle. Your child's difficulties are yours to disclose, not the tutor's. A private tutor should not discuss your child with other families in your society, should not pass around your child's work as a sample for other students, and should not approach the school on your behalf unless you have asked him to.

Then write down what you agree. Not a contract drawn by a lawyer, just an email both sides hold: subject, board and level, session length, days and times, the notice period for cancelling from either side, how fees are structured, whether lessons run at home or online, how progress will be reported, and a line confirming that either side can end the arrangement with reasonable notice.
items: A private tutor answers to you, not to the school or its timetable
A child's own class teacher tutoring them removes the independent second opinion
If you still want that, ask the school coordinator in writing first
Confidentiality: your child's difficulties are yours to disclose, nobody else's
Put subject, level, slot, notice period and reporting into one email

contentBlocks.heading: What four to six weeks of private tuition should show
contentBlocks.body:
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any private tutor who offers one has told you something useful about himself. Parents search for the best IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon and land on lists nobody can verify, so judge the arrangement instead of the label. What a working arrangement shows inside four to six weeks is narrower and far more checkable: the student knows what marks are actually awarded for, brings specific doubts to the session rather than a whole chapter, and starts writing answers that match the command term in the question.

Ask for a short written note every few weeks. Two lines will do: what was covered, what the student can now do unaided, what is still weak. A tutor who cannot produce that is not tracking anything, and neither are you.

Be equally honest about the limits of a thin shortlist. If your corridor holds one candidate for DP Higher Level Physics and the trial was average, three more weeks will not turn average into right. Change early. Families who wait for the mock results spend the following term doing remedial work under time pressure, which is the most expensive way to buy tutoring.

And some students do not need a tutor at all. A DP1 student scoring reasonably on five hours of sleep needs the calendar fixed first. A Grade 9 student two months into IGCSE needs time before anybody concludes anything. A student with a good teacher who has simply never opened a past paper needs a habit, not a hire. An honest shortlist sometimes ends with nobody being hired this term and a review after the next report. Availability stays conditional throughout, since slots move when a tutor's other students change their timetables, so plan the term around an hour you can protect rather than chasing the best-looking profile into an hour that does not exist.
items: Weeks one and two: a diagnosis and an error log, not new chapters
Weeks three to six: doubts get specific, answers match the command term
A two-line written note every few weeks beats a monthly phone call
An average trial does not improve with three more weeks of patience
Sometimes the right answer is to review again after the next report

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Have four things ready before you send the query and the first shortlist will be noticeably better. The exact board and level, written the way the school writes it. The last report card or unit test, ideally with the teacher's marking still on it. Your child's real weekly timetable, including the school bus, sport and anything that eats a Saturday. And your address at sector or society level, because that decides who can reach you and at what hour.

The first session is a diagnosis, not a lecture. A good tutor spends it finding out what the student can do unaided: a past paper question or two under something close to real conditions, a look at the school's last test, a conversation about how the student revises now. He should leave with a plan for the next four weeks, and you should know what that plan is.

A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, subject to tutor availability. If the fit is wrong afterwards, say so and ask for a different match. Parents searching for IB and IGCSE private tutors near me in Gurgaon often feel they have used up their one chance by choosing wrong. They have not. Changing a match in week two is ordinary, and it is far cheaper than changing one in March.

If your corridor is thin this month, take a strong online specialist for the term and revisit home classes in the quieter weeks after the session ends. Families in Kherki Daula and along Pataudi Road do exactly this every year, and their children do not learn less for it.
items: Board, level and syllabus exactly as the school writes them
The last report card or marked unit test, marking still visible
The real weekly timetable, including bus, sport and Saturdays
Your sector or society, which decides who can reach you and when
One question you want answered during the trial session itself

faqs.question: How many IB and IGCSE private tutors will I actually have to choose from?
faqs.answer: Usually two or three, and sometimes one. The number depends on the subject, the level and your corridor rather than on how many IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon exist in total. A common subject at IGCSE level in Sector 67 will produce a genuine choice. Higher Level Chemistry with Internal Assessment support in Sector 113, on a Wednesday at seven, may produce one workable profile and one online specialist. We will tell you which situation you are in before you start comparing, because a fair comparison between two real options is useful and a staged comparison between one option and a filler is not.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Sector 113 on Dwarka Expressway on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Some will, but the shortlist is shorter and the slot is less flexible. A home tutor who takes a Sector 113 or Sector 110 student on a weekday evening usually cannot take another student afterwards, so he will want one fixed weekly slot he can plan around and will resist moving it. Weekend home classes are easier to arrange along Dwarka Expressway, including in Sobha City, Godrej Summit and ATS Kocoon. Many families there settle on a weekend session at home plus a midweek online session, which survives a full term better than a weekday slot that keeps slipping.

faqs.question: Can I trial two tutors without unsettling my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided you tell him what is happening. Say that two teachers are coming to try a session and that he is helping you decide, which most teenagers quite enjoy. Keep both trials inside the same week so the comparison is fair, give both the same material, and ask both to mark the same past answer. Do not run four trials. By the third one the student is performing rather than learning, and you are comparing charm. Then ask him a single question afterwards: which lesson did you understand more of? His answer is worth more than either tutor's pitch.

faqs.question: My child's own school teacher has offered private tuition. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a conflict of interest, and it is worth thinking through before you agree. The same person would be teaching the class, assessing internal work and being paid by you privately, which leaves the family without the independent second opinion an outside tutor exists to provide. Some schools do not permit it at all. If you want to go ahead anyway, ask the school's coordinator in writing first and keep the reply. An independent private tutor removes the question entirely, and in a household running both IGCSE and the Diploma Programme that separation is usually worth more than the convenience.

faqs.question: Should anything be put in writing before lessons start?
faqs.answer: Yes, and an email is enough. Write down the subject, board and level, the session length, the days and times, how fees are structured, the notice period for cancelling from either side, whether lessons run at home or online, and how progress will be reported to you. Add one line saying either side can end the arrangement with reasonable notice. This is not distrust. It is what stops a disagreement in February about a missed session from becoming a reason to stop tuition in the middle of a Diploma Programme year, which is the worst month to change anything.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session is missed because of traffic or illness?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule at the start rather than after it happens. The usual arrangement is that a session cancelled with reasonable notice by either side gets rescheduled, and that a tutor delayed by traffic on Southern Peripheral Road either runs late into the slot or makes up the time later that week. Be realistic about how many moved sessions your week can absorb: a family with two children and a Saturday sport commitment cannot absorb many. If a tutor misses sessions regularly, that is not a traffic problem, it is a fit problem, and you can ask for a different match.

faqs.question: Will the tutor keep my child's difficulties confidential?
faqs.answer: That is yours to set, and it should be said out loud in the first week. A private tutor should not discuss your child with other families in your society, should not show your child's work to other students as an example, and should not contact the school unless you have asked him to. In a society such as Vatika India Next or Tata Primanti, where one tutor often teaches several children in the same towers, this matters more than people expect. Ask the question directly before the first session, because the answer tells you a great deal about how the tutor works.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What do I do?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, and do it now rather than after the next test. Tell us what specifically is not working: the level is wrong, the student is not talking, the sessions repeat what school already covered, the slot keeps moving. That detail makes the second shortlist better than the first was. Changing in week three costs you a week. Changing in the month before mocks costs you the revision plan. Nobody takes it personally, and students usually settle faster with a second tutor because they now know what a session ought to feel like.

faqs.question: Why is it harder to find a tutor in September?
faqs.answer: Because everybody starts looking in the same fortnight. The new year has settled, the first unit tests have come back, and DP1 students have realised that Higher Level is a different kind of work. IB and IGCSE private tutors in Gurugram fill their evening slots quickly in that window, and a second wave arrives before the DP2 mock examinations, which each school fixes for itself several months ahead of the May session. If you can start in a quieter month, you will get a better slot and a tutor with time to diagnose properly rather than one joining mid-crisis.

faqs.question: No home tutor is free in Sector 86, New Gurgaon. Should I take an online one?
faqs.answer: If the online tutor is right on subject and level, yes, at least for this term. A strong online specialist beats a nearby home tutor who has never taught your child's level, and that is the trade most families around Sector 86, Sector 89 and Pataudi Road end up making at some point. Ask for a hybrid plan: online midweek, plus a home session at the weekend if any tutor can reach you then. Revisit home classes in the quieter weeks after the exam session, when evening slots across New Gurgaon open up again.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my IGCSE child and my Diploma Programme child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for Maths and the sciences, and it is worth asking, because one tutor visiting once for two students is far easier on a weekday evening. But check the level claim separately for each child. Teaching Cambridge IGCSE Extended well and teaching Higher Level Diploma Programme content well are different jobs, and a tutor who admits to being stronger at one is telling you something useful. If the shortlist can only serve one child properly, serve the exam-year child first and plan the second tutor for the next term.

contentBlocks.heading: What DP, MYP and IGCSE Demand From Private Tuition in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A private tutor working on the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) has to plan against a two-year structure, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to 3 more points toward a maximum of 45 and a minimum of 24 for the diploma, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). For private tuition specifically, this means agreeing early which subjects the arrangement actually covers, since a family paying for HL Maths support should not find CAS or TOK quietly absorbing session time without being asked.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to 5, across eight subject groups, with every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, the total out of 32 converting to a final 1 to 7 grade through the IB's grade boundaries; the Personal Project sits in MYP 5, the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4. A private tutor supporting MYP work should be marking against those actual criteria, not a generic rubric, since a criterion-level gap is what a private arrangement is usually hired to close. A home tutor working through MYP criteria at the family's own desk can spread a single criterion across a full session in a way a school lesson rarely has time for.

IGCSE, whether Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually runs across Grades 9 and 10 before a move into the DP, A Levels, or CBSE or ISC in Class 11, and private tuition here often exists specifically to prepare a student for that next stage, not only for the current one. Families researching an IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor are really asking whether one private tutor can carry a student through both stages; occasionally yes, but it is safer to plan for two specialists, since the syllabus and marking style genuinely change. This is what Gurgaon families mean by an international board tutor in Gurugram: someone fluent in the specific HL/SL split, MYP criteria or IGCSE tier in play, not a generalist.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Subjects Need the Most From Private Tuition?
contentBlocks.body:
Subjects with a written component marked against detailed criteria, such as DP Extended Essay planning, MYP Language and Literature or IGCSE English coursework, tend to need the most from private tuition, because the gap is usually about structure and command terms rather than raw content knowledge. Maths and the Sciences follow close behind, particularly where a student has fallen behind school pace and needs focused, private time to close a specific gap before it compounds.

Private tuition works differently from a school teacher's own extra class here: an independent tutor can spend an entire session on the one criterion or command term a student keeps losing marks on, such as 'evaluate' versus 'discuss' in a DP Economics essay, without needing to also manage twenty other students in the room. This is the actual value private tuition adds over a class, whether a school class or a coaching batch: depth on the exact place a student is stuck, not broader coverage they may not need.

Private tuition should never mean doing the school's own tasks for the student. A private tutor can explain how an Internal Assessment (IA) criterion works, review structure and give feedback on a draft, but the IA itself has to remain the student's own work under the IB's academic integrity rules, just as IGCSE coursework has to remain the student's own under Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel rules. A tutor who offers to do the work rather than teach toward it should be treated as a serious red flag, not a convenience. A home tutor working at the family's own desk can watch a student's actual working line by line, which is often where a command-term weakness first becomes visible.

The honest trade-off with hybrid is coordination, since a family is now managing two schedules and, in some cases, two separate written agreements rather than one; it is worth the extra coordination only when the specialists genuinely cannot be combined into one person.

Most families who begin with weekly home tuition for every subject eventually settle into some version of this mix once the first term's rhythm becomes clear, moving one subject online while keeping the rest as a home tutor arrangement. contentBlocks.heading: Should You Hire an Outside Tutor or Use Your Child's Own Teacher?
contentBlocks.body:
An outside, independent tutor and a student's own school teacher offering private extra classes are not the same arrangement, and the honest answer is that an outside tutor is usually the safer default because it avoids a real conflict of interest: a teacher who privately tutors their own student is also the person setting and marking that student's classwork and internal assessments at school.

The conflict is not about a teacher's intentions, which are often genuinely good; it is structural. A teacher grading a student's classwork or contributing to an internal predicted grade has, even unconsciously, an incentive shaped by the private arrangement, and a student may feel unable to raise a concern about the tutoring relationship without it affecting how they are treated in class. Some schools also have explicit policies against staff privately tutoring their own students for exactly this reason, so it is worth checking before assuming it is an option.

An independent private tutor, with no connection to the school, removes this problem entirely and can be mapped to the student's actual scheme of work without needing to also manage a classroom relationship. Mapping means asking the school, through the student or directly if the school allows it, what topics and assessments are coming up, then building private sessions around that sequence rather than a generic syllabus order; a private tutor who never asks what the school is actually covering this month is not really tailoring anything.

Confidentiality matters here too: what a student struggles with privately should stay between the family and the tutor, not filter back into how a subject teacher perceives the student, which is one more reason an outside, independent arrangement is usually the cleaner choice.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should a Fair Private Tuition Agreement Include?

A fair private tuition agreement, even an informal one confirmed in a message, should cover five things plainly: the subjects and level covered, the weekly schedule and what counts as reasonable notice for a cancellation, how progress will be communicated to parents, confidentiality around what is discussed in sessions, and what happens if the fit is not right after a trial period. Progress with private tuition should be visible within the first month in specific ways: a named topic or skill that has improved, homework completed without a daily reminder, and a short note after each session describing what was actually covered rather than a general impression. If a month of weekly private sessions has not moved a specific, agreed goal, the honest step is to revisit whether the goal was realistic, whether the tutor is the right fit, or whether the student needs a different kind of support entirely, such as addressing a confidence issue before a syllabus gap. There is no verifiable 'best' IB and IGCSE private tuition in Gurgaon, only an arrangement whose terms, confidentiality and fit are right for your child; the same is true of any of the IB and IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon you might compare, or any single IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon under consideration.

No tutor, however experienced, can guarantee a grade, and this should be stated plainly in any agreement rather than implied through marketing language. Starting private tuition close to an exam session narrows what is realistically achievable, and an honest tutor will say so directly rather than promising a turnaround that a few weeks cannot deliver. A private arrangement that cannot be ended without friction, or that resists a written note of what was agreed, is not one worth continuing.

faqs.question: Is it a bad idea to let my child's own school teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It is not automatically wrong, but it creates a structural conflict of interest worth thinking through carefully, since the same person setting and marking your child's classwork or contributing to an internal grade is also the person being paid privately by your family. Many teachers manage this professionally, but the student may still feel unable to raise a concern about the tutoring without it affecting classroom treatment, and some schools have explicit policies against the practice for this reason, so check first. An independent, private tutor with no connection to the school avoids this entirely and can usually be mapped to the same scheme of work just as closely, without the structural problem attached.

faqs.question: What should we get in writing before starting a private tuition arrangement?
faqs.answer: At minimum, get the subjects and level covered, the weekly schedule, what counts as reasonable cancellation notice, how progress updates will reach you, and confidentiality around what is discussed in sessions, confirmed in a written message even if it is not a formal contract. This protects both sides: the tutor knows what is expected and the family has something to point back to if the arrangement drifts from what was agreed. A tutor who resists confirming basic terms in writing, however good their subject knowledge, is worth a second thought before committing to a full term.

faqs.question: Will a private tutor keep what my child struggles with confidential from the school?
faqs.answer: Yes, that confidentiality is a basic expectation of a private, independent arrangement, and it should be confirmed explicitly rather than assumed. What a student struggles with in a private session is between the family and the tutor, not something that should filter back to a subject teacher or affect how the student is perceived in class, which is one of the real advantages of going outside the school rather than using a teacher's own extra classes. If you are unsure, raise confidentiality directly in the first conversation and ask the tutor to confirm it in writing alongside the schedule and cancellation terms.

Private, one-to-one tuition is generally priced to reflect full individual attention rather than shared time, and the exact structure, per session, monthly or as a package, is confirmed directly with you before anything is booked. Availability for a specific subject and slot is always subject to tutor availability, particularly close to the May exam session when demand for private tutors rises across Gurgaon.

faqs.question: What if there is no progress after a month of private tuition?
faqs.answer: First check whether the original goal was specific: 'do better in Chemistry' will not show progress the way 'fix the last three topic tests' or 'restructure the IA draft' does, so revisit exactly what the tutor was asked to address. If the goal was specific and a month of sessions has not moved it, ask IB Gram for a different tutor rather than assuming private tuition itself has failed; sometimes the mismatch is teaching style or pacing, not effort. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a written record of what each session covered should exist, and IB Gram can review it with you before arranging a switch.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is normal for private IB or IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week is the common starting point for most subjects, moving to three during exam years or when a subject has fallen noticeably behind school pace, and dropping to one for lighter, revision-only support. A DP HL subject with 240 recommended teaching hours over two years generally needs a steadier weekly rhythm than an SL subject at 150 hours, and an IGCSE student nearing a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel exam series often adds a short weekly past paper session in the final term. The right frequency is set during your consultation and can be adjusted as the term develops.

faqs.question: What happens if a private home tuition session is missed?
faqs.answer: A missed session is rescheduled by direct agreement with the tutor, the same way any private appointment would be, and reasonable cancellation notice, usually agreed in writing at the start, protects both sides from last-minute surprises. If a pattern of missed sessions develops, whether due to school commitments, travel or illness, it is worth revisiting the weekly schedule itself rather than continuing to reschedule around it indefinitely. IB Gram can help adjust the arrangement, including moving to a lighter frequency or shifting a session online, if the original weekly plan is no longer realistic for the family.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor need a parent to be present during home sessions?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and it depends on the student's age and what the family is comfortable with, but IB Gram recommends a parent or responsible adult being reachable in the house, if not in the room, especially for the first few sessions while trust is still being established. Older DP or IGCSE Grade 10 students often prefer working independently once the arrangement is settled, while a younger MYP student may benefit from a parent nearby for the first month. This is worth agreeing explicitly with the tutor at the start, alongside the schedule and confidentiality terms, rather than assuming either way.

mainEntity.name: Is it a bad idea to let my child's own school teacher tutor them privately?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not automatically wrong, but it creates a structural conflict of interest worth thinking through carefully, since the same person setting and marking your child's classwork or contributing to an internal grade is also the person being paid privately by your family. Many teachers manage this professionally, but the student may still feel unable to raise a concern about the tutoring without it affecting classroom treatment, and some schools have explicit policies against the practice for this reason, so check first. An independent, private tutor with no connection to the school avoids this entirely and can usually be mapped to the same scheme of work just as closely, without the structural problem attached.

mainEntity.name: What should we get in writing before starting a private tuition arrangement?

acceptedAnswer.text: At minimum, get the subjects and level covered, the weekly schedule, what counts as reasonable cancellation notice, how progress updates will reach you, and confidentiality around what is discussed in sessions, confirmed in a written message even if it is not a formal contract. This protects both sides: the tutor knows what is expected and the family has something to point back to if the arrangement drifts from what was agreed. A tutor who resists confirming basic terms in writing, however good their subject knowledge, is worth a second thought before committing to a full term.

mainEntity.name: Will a private tutor keep what my child struggles with confidential from the school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, that confidentiality is a basic expectation of a private, independent arrangement, and it should be confirmed explicitly rather than assumed. What a student struggles with in a private session is between the family and the tutor, not something that should filter back to a subject teacher or affect how the student is perceived in class, which is one of the real advantages of going outside the school rather than using a teacher's own extra classes. If you are unsure, raise confidentiality directly in the first conversation and ask the tutor to confirm it in writing alongside the schedule and cancellation terms.

mainEntity.name: How much does private IB or IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the level, subject, whether the tutor is coming to your home or teaching online, and how many sessions a week your family needs, so IB Gram will not quote a figure without first understanding those details during your consultation. Private, one-to-one tuition is generally priced to reflect full individual attention rather than shared time, and the exact structure, per session, monthly or as a package, is confirmed directly with you before anything is booked. Availability for a specific subject and slot is always subject to tutor availability, particularly close to the May exam session when demand for private tutors rises across Gurgaon.

mainEntity.name: What if there is no progress after a month of private tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: First check whether the original goal was specific: 'do better in Chemistry' will not show progress the way 'fix the last three topic tests' or 'restructure the IA draft' does, so revisit exactly what the tutor was asked to address. If the goal was specific and a month of sessions has not moved it, ask IB Gram for a different tutor rather than assuming private tuition itself has failed; sometimes the mismatch is teaching style or pacing, not effort. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a written record of what each session covered should exist, and IB Gram can review it with you before arranging a switch.

acceptedAnswer.text: Palam Vihar and the older Old Gurgaon sectors around it are relatively well connected, so a weekday evening slot here holds up better than in some newer corridors, though school pickup and office traffic still bunch up around 6 to 7 pm. IB Gram asks about the exact slot you need during matching so the shortlist only includes tutors who have confirmed they can realistically reach Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park or Ashok Vihar at that time. If a slot repeatedly slips because of traffic, moving that one session online while keeping the rest at home is usually a simpler fix than changing the whole arrangement.

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, but plan around a slightly longer or later slot, since a tutor travelling to IMT Manesar, Hero Honda Chowk or the sectors nearby is working against a longer stretch of NH-48 that gets unpredictable depending on the hour and the day. Many Manesar families agree a weekend-heavy schedule in writing from the start rather than assuming a strict weekday evening slot will hold every week, and some choose online for one or two sessions specifically to avoid the commute altogether. IB Gram will flag this trade-off honestly during matching rather than promising a tight weekday slot it cannot reliably deliver.

Ending the arrangement with the school teacher is a separate, personal conversation your family manages directly, but setting up the new private tutor follows the same shortlist and trial process as any other enquiry, starting from your child's board, syllabus and current level rather than from scratch. Many families find the switch clarifies things quickly, since an independent tutor has no prior classroom relationship shaping how they read the student's actual gaps.

heroTitle: Comparing IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Most families here hire the first tutor who answers the phone. A better method takes one extra week: two or three verified profiles, a free trial lesson with each, and a short written comparison you can actually defend at the dinner table. This page shows you how to run that week.
introSummary: IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon are easiest to judge when you compare two or three arrangements at once instead of hiring the first tutor who calls back, and for most families here the arrangement being compared is home tuition, with a verified tutor teaching at your own dining table in your own sector. A private tuition is not the school's own extra class. It is an independent agreement between your family and a tutor, which means you choose, you compare and you can change your mind. The comparison itself is simple once you know what to look at: board and syllabus experience, the level actually taught, familiarity with how a school paces its year, and whether the slot survives a normal Gurgaon weekday. IB Gram shortlists verified tutors against that brief and arranges a demo before you commit.

contentBlocks.heading: How do we shortlist IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon start with a brief, not with a search. When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks for the board and the exact syllabus your child is entered for, the level, the school calendar you are working against, your sector, and the two or three slots that would genuinely survive an ordinary week. That last question does more work than parents expect. A tutor who is excellent and free only at four in the afternoon is not a real candidate for a child whose school bus reaches Sector 49 closer to five.

Two or three verified profiles come back against that brief. Not eight. Eight profiles feel generous and produce paralysis, because by the fourth one you are comparing half-remembered impressions rather than evidence. Two or three can each be given a proper trial lesson inside a single week, which is the only comparison that tells you anything. The profiles are matched on board, level, subject, availability in your corridor and the format you asked for, whether that is home tuition, online or a mix.

Then you test them. A demo or trial session can be arranged with each shortlisted tutor before the family commits to anything, and you are not obliged to continue with any of them. If none of the two or three fits, you say so and ask for a different match. Parents hesitate here, as though a shortlist were a contract. It is not. Asking for a different profile is a normal part of the process and costs you nothing except the week.

Lessons then run at home, online or as a hybrid of both, subject to tutor availability for the level and slot you need. The point of the whole exercise is that you end up choosing between known quantities rather than gambling on one stranger.
items: 1. Send the board, syllabus, level, school and two workable weekly slots.
2. We ask about the school calendar, your sector and travel limits.
3. Two or three verified profiles come back, matched to that brief.
4. Book a free trial or demo lesson with each shortlisted tutor.
5. Confirm one tutor, or ask for a different match, then start.

contentBlocks.heading: Which stage are you comparing tutors for: MYP, DP or IGCSE Grades 9 and 10?
contentBlocks.body:
Answer this before you look at a single profile, because the stage changes what counts as a good tutor. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP), five years running roughly from ages eleven to sixteen across eight subject groups, every subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each scored from 0 to 8. The criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade from 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. A tutor comparing well at this stage can tell you which criterion your child is losing marks in and why, rather than talking about marks in general.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is a different animal. Two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects drawn from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL, with 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well. Ask each shortlisted tutor whether they have taught your child's subject at HL or only at SL. The honest ones say so plainly.

IGCSE Grades 9 and 10 is usually a two-year course, either Cambridge IGCSE through Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some syllabuses available in 9-1 versions under different codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and the difference matters: Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*.

So a household with a child in MYP 4 and another in DP1 is rarely comparing the same tutors. Run two shortlists.
items: MYP: four criteria A to D, each 0-8, totalling 32 before conversion
DP: six subjects, three or four at HL, each graded 1-7
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to three points, maximum 45
IGCSE: Cambridge A*-G or 9-1 codes, Edexcel International GCSE 9-1
Cambridge Core stops at grade C; Extended reaches A* on tiered syllabuses
Ask each shortlisted tutor which level they have actually taught

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing subject depth: papers, criteria and command terms
contentBlocks.body:
Subject depth is the fastest way to separate two profiles that look identical on paper. Give each shortlisted tutor the same past paper question from your child's syllabus and ask them to talk you through how the marks are awarded. A tutor who knows the subject reaches for the markscheme structure without being prompted. A tutor who is improvising talks about the topic instead.

Command terms are the cleanest test of all. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent each set a different depth of answer, and a student who writes a beautiful description for a question that says evaluate has lost marks that had nothing to do with knowing the content. Ask a tutor how they would coach a child out of that habit. The useful answer involves rewriting real answers against a real markscheme, not a lecture on exam technique. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and they show exactly how marks are awarded, so any tutor who claims a private method for guessing the marker is not worth a second lesson.

At MYP, depth means criterion-level diagnosis. Two tutors can both say your child needs to improve in Sciences; only one can say the marks are going in Criterion C rather than Criterion A, and that the fix is in how investigations are recorded. At IGCSE, depth means knowing whether your child sits Core or Extended and what that ceiling means for the next stage. At DP, it means knowing the difference between HL and SL demands in that subject, and how Internal Assessment (IA) work is judged.

One caution. A tutor is not allowed to write coursework, an IA or an Extended Essay for a student, and a tutor who hints otherwise has told you everything you need to know about the rest of their teaching.
items: Give both tutors the same past paper question and compare the answers
Ask how define, describe, evaluate and discuss change the required depth
MYP depth sounds like criterion diagnosis, not general subject advice
IGCSE depth includes knowing whether Core or Extended is the entry
DP depth means HL versus SL demands and honest Internal Assessment limits

Where you live narrows the shortlist before subject fit does, and pretending otherwise wastes a fortnight. Along Golf Course Extension Road, the cluster of Sector 56, Sector 57, Sector 58, Sector 59, Sector 60, Sector 62 and Sector 65 sits close enough together that a tutor teaching in Sushant Lok 3 on a Tuesday can reasonably take a second family in Sector 57 the same evening. Ghata and Gwal Pahari sit at the edge of that run and add real distance. Gated addresses such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon need visitor registration at the gate, so tell a shortlisted tutor how entry works before the trial lesson rather than after they have been standing outside for twenty minutes.

Sohna Road behaves differently. Sector 47, Sector 48, Sector 49 and Sector 50 sit in a tight band, and Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Malibu Towne, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Vipul Greens, The Close and Central Park Resorts are all within that band. Evening traffic through this stretch can turn a short trip into a long one, which is why a seven o'clock start is often more reliable here than a six o'clock start.

The older side of the city, DLF Phase 2, DLF Phase 3 and DLF Phase 4, with MG Road, Cyber City, Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur, Sector 24, Sector 27 and Sector 28, has the densest supply of tutors and the worst weekday congestion. Families in DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona often find that a tutor who already teaches inside the same complex is worth shortlisting even if a slightly better subject match lives further away.

Be honest about travel when you compare. The best tutor on your list is the one who will still be arriving cheerfully in March.

contentBlocks.heading: What the Gurgaon school calendar does to your comparison
contentBlocks.body:
The calendar decides how much time your comparison of IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon is allowed to take. Families at international schools in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana work against a year that has more fixed points than a CBSE year does, and the fixed points arrive in clusters. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this site, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and nothing here says what any particular school offers. Families at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge all describe the same rhythm of term tests, coursework deadlines and mock examinations.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May examination session, with November used by a minority of schools and by retake candidates. Each school sets its own DP2 mock dates, usually several months before May, and those mocks are the moment a shaky subject becomes visible to everyone. May results are released in early July. Work backwards from that and the sensible times to run a comparison week become obvious: early in the academic year, or immediately after a set of term tests, when a report card has just told you which subject is actually the problem.

The worst time to compare tutors is the fortnight before mocks. A student in that fortnight has no appetite for meeting two strangers, and a trial lesson run under that pressure tells you nothing except that your child is tired. If you are already inside that window, take one tutor on a short arrangement, get through the mocks, and run the proper comparison afterwards with the mock paper in hand.

Cambridge series timing matters at the other stage. Cambridge runs series in February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November, while Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and May/June.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in Gurgaon: judging each shortlisted tutor in the right format
contentBlocks.body:
Compare IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon in the format you intend to use, not in whichever format is convenient for the trial. A home tutor who is warm and unhurried at your dining table may be flat on a screen, and an online specialist who annotates a past paper brilliantly on a shared whiteboard may lose a restless MYP 3 student in a room with a television in it. Judging one format and buying another is the commonest mistake in this whole process.

Home tuition leads for most families here, and for good reasons. The student travels nowhere, which protects a weekday evening that is already short. A home tutor sees the desk, the lighting, the phone on the table and the sibling wandering through, and can say something useful about all four. Parents overhear a little without hovering. The trade-off is availability: a home tutor can only serve a limited number of sectors in an evening, so a rare HL specialist may simply not be reachable from your address at the slot you want.

Online lessons invert that. Your shortlist stops being limited by Gurgaon geography, late slots become possible because nobody has to drive home afterwards, and a missed week in the monsoon stops being a lost week. What you give up is the room. Concentration is harder to police through a screen, younger students drift, and practical work loses something. Hybrid splits the difference honestly: the main weekly lesson at home, a shorter mid-week session online for doubt-solving and paper marking before a test.

So compare on your own terms. If two shortlisted tutors are close on subject depth and one is fifteen minutes further away, the closer one usually wins on the strength of surviving February. If the gap in subject depth is wide, take the distant specialist online and stop apologising for it.

contentBlocks.heading: What a verified profile shows, and what you should check yourself
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified, and verification means identity and the teaching claims on the profile have been checked before the profile is sent to you. It tells you the person is who they say they are and has taught what they say they have taught. It does not tell you whether this particular adult will get on with your particular fourteen-year-old, and no verification process anywhere can tell you that. The trial lesson exists for exactly that reason.

So do your own checking, and do it on specifics rather than impressions. Ask which board and syllabus the tutor has taught most recently, and at which level. Ask how many years they have worked with the exact stage your child is at, and listen for whether the answer is about teaching that stage or merely knowing the subject. Ask what they would do in the first three lessons, which is a question that separates a tutor with a plan from a tutor who will simply reteach whatever the school did that week. Ask how they will tell you when something is going wrong.

For home tuition there is a second layer, and it is yours to run. Your society controls gate entry and visitor registration, and you decide what the tutor is told about the family. Keep lessons in a room that is visible from the rest of the house, with a door that stays open. Agree from the start that sessions are logged, that you will get a short note after each one, and that the tutor speaks to you rather than only to the student.

The things nobody can verify deserve saying plainly. Nobody can verify a promised grade, and no tutor can guarantee a grade. Treat a promise of a particular score as a reason to remove that tutor from your list rather than to move them up it.

Verification cannot predict rapport, which is what the trial lesson tests

contentBlocks.heading: How do you run trial lessons with two Gurgaon tutors without unsettling your child?
contentBlocks.body:
Tell your child the truth, in one sentence, before the first trial: two teachers are coming this week, you will try a lesson with each, and then you and they will decide together. Children handle this better than parents expect. What unsettles a student is not being compared, it is being tested without being told, and discovering halfway through the second lesson that the first one was an audition they did not know they were sitting.

Run both trials in the same week, and give each tutor the same starting material. One topic your child is currently struggling with, one recent piece of marked work, and the same forty-five or sixty minutes. Identical inputs are what make the comparison worth anything. If one tutor gets the hardest topic and the other gets revision of something already understood, you have learned nothing about either of them.

Then compare on four things while they are fresh. What did the tutor find out about your child in the first ten minutes, and how did they find it out? Did the explanation change when your child did not understand the first version, or did it get louder? What did they say about the marks, specifically, with reference to a markscheme or a criterion? And what did they propose for the next three weeks? Write one line against each of the four for each tutor, on the evening of the lesson, not three days later. Memory rewrites trial lessons very quickly, and it usually favours whoever was more charming.

Let your child give a view, and treat it as evidence rather than as the verdict. A student who says nothing at all after both lessons is telling you something, and it is usually that neither tutor asked them a question they cared about answering.

When you have chosen, tell the other tutor. A short message is enough, and the courtesy matters because Gurgaon is a small world in this line of work.
items: Tell your child two teachers are coming and the family will decide
Run both trials in one week with the same topic and marked work
Score each tutor on diagnosis, re-explanation, mark detail and next steps
Write your notes on the evening of the lesson, not days later
Ask your child for a view, and weigh it as evidence rather than verdict
Message the tutor you did not pick; it takes one line

contentBlocks.heading: Is the tuition working? What the first four weeks should show
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is long enough to judge the process and far too short to judge the grade. What you should see by the end of it is a tutor who knows exactly where your child is weak and can name it, not in general terms but in the vocabulary of the course: this criterion, that paper, this command term, that step in the working. If after four lessons the diagnosis is still only that your child needs more practice, the tuition is not working, whatever the atmosphere in the room is like.

The second thing to look for is a change in what your child does alone. A student who starts checking a markscheme before asking for help, or who redoes a wrong answer without being told, has learned something the tuition gave them. Marks lag behind this shift, sometimes by a full term, particularly at MYP where criterion scores move slowly and at DP where an early HL topic can stay difficult for months. Expecting a jump in a report card after four weeks sets everybody up for disappointment, including the student.

Here are the honest limits. Starting in DP2 a few weeks before mocks narrows what is possible to triage, not transformation. A student who is not doing any independent work between lessons will plateau no matter how good the tutor is, because two hours a week cannot carry a Higher Level subject on their own. And some children need no tutor at all, only a fixed study time and somebody checking that it happens.

If it is not working, say so early. You can ask for a different tutor at any point, and a family that switches in week five loses far less than a family that waits until March out of politeness.
items: By week four the tutor should name the weakness in the course's own terms
Watch for the student checking markschemes or redoing work unasked
Marks lag behind method, often by a term, at both MYP and DP
Two hours a week cannot carry an HL subject without independent study
Starting weeks before mocks means triage rather than transformation
Ask for a different match in week five rather than waiting until March

contentBlocks.heading: Starting home tuition in Gurgaon once you have chosen
contentBlocks.body:
Once you have compared the IB and IGCSE private tuitions in Gurgaon on your shortlist, the start is quick, and a little preparation makes the first paid lesson worth more than the trial was. Have three things ready on the table: the last two marked assessments with the teacher's comments still on them, the school's scheme of work or unit plan for the current term if you can get it, and a list of the dates you already know about, term tests, coursework deadlines and mocks. A tutor who sees those in lesson one plans a term. A tutor who sees them in lesson six has been guessing until then.

Agree the practical things in the same conversation. Which day and time, how long the session runs, what happens when a session is missed and whether it is made up, how the tutor will reach you with an update and how often, and which room the lesson happens in. For home tuition, settle gate entry and visitor registration now rather than at seven o'clock on a Tuesday. If the arrangement is hybrid, decide which day is at home and which is online, and keep it stable for at least a month before changing anything.

The first session with the chosen tutor should look different from the trial. Expect a proper diagnostic, a plan for the term that survives contact with the school calendar, and a short note to you afterwards saying what was covered and what the student should do before the next lesson.

And keep the door open. If the fit turns out to be wrong in week three, you ask for a different match. That option does not expire because you have already started.
items: Keep the last two marked assessments and the teacher comments ready
Share the term's scheme of work and every date you already know
Agree slot, session length, missed-session policy and update frequency
Settle society gate entry and visitor registration before the first lesson
Expect a written note after each home class saying what was covered

faqs.question: How many tutors should I shortlist before deciding?
faqs.answer: Two or three, and no more. Each shortlisted tutor needs a proper trial lesson for the comparison to mean anything, and a family can realistically run two or three trials in one week without exhausting the student. Beyond that you stop comparing evidence and start comparing half-remembered impressions, which tends to favour whoever was most charming rather than whoever taught best. If none of the two or three fits, ask for a different match; a second short round is far more useful than one long round of eight profiles you cannot keep straight.

faqs.question: Can I really run trial lessons with two tutors in the same week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the same week is the right way to do it. Memory of a lesson fades fast, so two trials separated by a fortnight are barely comparable. Give both tutors the same topic, the same recent marked work and the same session length, then write your notes the evening of each lesson. Tell your child in advance that two teachers are coming and that the family will decide together. Students handle an open comparison far better than they handle discovering they were being assessed without being told.

faqs.question: What should I compare on each tutor's profile, side by side?
faqs.answer: Five things: the board and syllabus taught most recently, the level actually taught, familiarity with how a school paces the year, the slot they can hold every week, and the format they are offering. Everything else is decoration. Levels matter more than parents expect, since a tutor comfortable at Standard Level may not be comfortable at Higher Level in the same subject, and a Cambridge Extended entry is a different ceiling from a Core entry. Write the five down as a row for each tutor. The gaps become obvious when the profiles sit next to each other.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we chose is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, and do it in week five rather than in March. You can request another tutor at any point, and a month is enough to judge whether the teaching has a method even though it is far too early to judge a grade. The signals worth acting on are a tutor who still cannot name the weakness in the course's own terms, sessions that have become homework supervision, or a student who has quietly stopped talking about the lessons. Waiting out a bad fit out of politeness costs the student a term.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Sector 57 or Nirvana Country on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Often yes, subject to tutor availability and to where their previous lesson finished. Sector 57 sits in a tight cluster with Sector 56, Sector 58 and Sushant Lok 3, so a tutor already teaching in that group can usually add a second family the same evening. Nirvana Country sits in the Sohna Road band with Sector 49, Sector 50 and South City 2, which is similarly workable. Evening traffic through both corridors can stretch a short trip, so a seven o'clock start is frequently more reliable than a six o'clock one.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Sit in on the trial, then step back. Your presence in a trial lesson is useful because you are judging the tutor, and the student usually understands that. After you have chosen, a parent in the room changes what a teenager is willing to admit not understanding, and admitting that is most of what tuition is for. Keep the lesson in a room visible from the rest of the house with the door open, stay within earshot, and ask for a short written note after each session instead. Younger MYP students are the exception and often settle better with a parent nearby at first.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow the school's pacing or their own plan?
faqs.answer: Both, and the balance should be agreed in the first week. A private tutor is an independent arrangement outside the school, so they are not bound to the school's sequence, but ignoring it produces a student learning two versions of the same course at once. The sensible pattern is to follow the school's scheme of work for current content so the student is supported in class and in term tests, while using a parallel track to repair the gaps from earlier units. Share the school's unit plan and test dates if you can get them; it saves weeks of guessing.

faqs.question: Is it awkward to tell a tutor they were not selected?
faqs.answer: It is less awkward than not telling them. Tutors who trial for families expect that some trials end there, and a one-line message closes the loop cleanly. Say that you have decided to go with someone else and thank them for the session. Do not invent a reason, and do not leave the door ajar with a vague maybe later, because a tutor who thinks the slot is still live will hold it. Gurgaon's tutoring circles are small, and the courtesy is remembered when you come back for a second subject.

faqs.question: How soon can tuition start after I send a query?
faqs.answer: It depends on the level, the subject and the slot, so nobody can promise a date. Common subjects at MYP and IGCSE level, in a corridor with good coverage, move faster than a Higher Level Diploma Programme specialist for an evening slot that several families want. The sequence is the same either way: a query or free consultation, a shortlist of verified profiles matched to your brief, a free demo or trial with each, and then confirmation. Building in a week for the comparison itself is the part parents most often forget to plan for.

faqs.question: Does online tuition genuinely work for IB and IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For most older students, yes, and for some it works better than a home lesson. Past paper work, markscheme annotation, essay structure and criterion-level feedback all travel well through a shared screen, and an online slot can sit late in the evening because nobody drives home afterwards. The honest limits are attention and practical work. Younger MYP students drift on a screen more than they do at a table, and a tutor cannot see the phone under the desk. Many families here settle on hybrid: the main lesson at home, a short online session before a test.

faqs.question: Do we need different tutors for IGCSE Grade 10 and DP1?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth planning for. IGCSE Grades 9 and 10 run as a two-year course under Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, with tiered entries in many Cambridge subjects, and the move into the Diploma Programme changes both the depth and the kind of assessment. Higher Level carries 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and Internal Assessment work, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay arrive on top. A tutor who is strong at Grade 10 is not automatically strong at Higher Level, so run a fresh shortlist for the new stage.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session is missed because of traffic in DLF Phase 3?
faqs.answer: Agree the answer before it happens, in the first conversation. The usual arrangement is that a session cancelled by the tutor is rescheduled, and a session cancelled by the family at short notice may not be. DLF Phase 3 and the stretch through MG Road, Sikanderpur and Cyber City are among the slower weekday runs in the city, so ask a tutor serving that corridor for a realistic start time rather than an optimistic one. A standing fallback helps: if the tutor is badly delayed, the session runs online that evening instead of being lost.
