contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches an Online Tutor to Your Gurgaon Family
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, and the first conversation is entirely about your child's situation: which board, which syllabus code if you already know it, DP1 or DP2, MYP year, or the IGCSE grade, plus the school's own calendar and the evening slots that actually work. Nothing about matching an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon starts with a generic profile list; it starts with what your family has already tried and where it went wrong.

From there the process is short and stays in your control, and it runs the same three steps every time.

1. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school and the schedule you can actually hold every week, including whether Saturdays are open.
2. It shortlists tutors whose verified profiles match the syllabus and level, not just the subject name, since an IB HL Chemistry tutor and a Cambridge IGCSE Extended Chemistry tutor are rarely interchangeable people.
3. A demo or trial session is arranged before you commit to anything, over the same video setup the ongoing lessons would use, so you see the real thing rather than a sales pitch.

If the fit is wrong after the trial, or after a few real sessions, you can ask for a different match; that costs nothing but a short conversation and a day or two of scheduling. Families switching from a home tutor to an online tutor mid-year, or the other way round, go through the same three steps again rather than starting from zero. What you are buying, in effect, is not a single tutor but a matching process you can rerun.
items: Tell IB Gram the board, syllabus code, level and weekly slots you can hold.
Receive a shortlist of verified tutors matched to that exact syllabus and level.
Sit a free demo or trial session before agreeing to anything ongoing.
Ask for a different tutor if the first match is not working.
Switch between online, home and hybrid lessons without restarting the matching process.

contentBlocks.heading: DP, MYP and IGCSE: What Changes When Lessons Move Online
contentBlocks.body:
The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points toward a maximum of 45, with 24 as the minimum for the diploma and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) completed alongside. Online, an HL subject with 240 recommended hours behind it needs a tutor who can hold pace over a full academic year on screen, not just answer questions before a test; a shorter SL commitment suits an online arrangement that starts mid-year more comfortably.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to 5, across eight subject groups, and every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8, with the criterion total out of 32 converting to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's grade boundaries. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, with a Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 for younger students. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional and each school decides whether to offer it; a student heading toward eAssessment benefits from an online tutor simply because the practice format is already a screen. IB Gram also places tutors for the Primary Years Programme (PYP), though this page focuses on MYP, DP and IGCSE.

Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE usually run across Grades 9 and 10 before a student moves into the DP, A Levels, or back to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Families researching an IGCSE to IB DP transition tutor are really asking one question: does the same person carry a student through both stages, and the honest answer is usually not, since the syllabus, the command terms and the marking style genuinely change between the two. Whichever board your child follows, this is what a Gurgaon family means by an international board tutor in Gurugram or Gurgaon: someone fluent in HL/SL, MYP criteria or IGCSE tiers specifically, not a generalist.
items: DP: six subjects, HL at 240 recommended hours, SL at 150, graded 1 to 7.
TOK and EE add up to 3 points; 45 is the maximum, 24 the minimum.
MYP: four criteria A to D per subject, each out of 8, converting to 1 to 7.
MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and set by each school, not compulsory.
IGCSE Grades 9-10 often need a different specialist from the DP years that follow.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB and IGCSE Subjects Actually Work on a Screen?
contentBlocks.body:
Most subjects work well online once the right tools are in place: Maths and Sciences need a shared whiteboard or tablet for working, Languages and Humanities need a shared document for essay markup, and IGCSE Sciences need a way to annotate diagrams together rather than describe them aloud. What struggles online is anything that depends on physical apparatus in the room, such as a live titration for IGCSE or DP Chemistry, though a tutor can still walk through the method, the risk assessment and the write-up on screen.

For DP subjects with an Internal Assessment (IA), the tutor's role online is mostly about the write-up and the command terms in the criteria, not the data collection itself, since IA work has to remain the student's own under the IB's academic integrity rules. Command terms such as define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent set how deep an answer needs to go, and a screen with the past paper mark scheme open next to the student's draft is, if anything, easier to run online than at a kitchen table with one shared notebook.

Cambridge subjects with Core and Extended tiers, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers, both mark to a published scheme, and an online tutor working through a real past paper with that scheme open is one of the more reliable things a screen does well: mark the same script twice, once as the student wrote it and once with the correct method shown, side by side. A subject that mostly involves talking through ideas, such as TOK or English essay planning, tends to suit online lessons as well as, or better than, a home session, since the shared document holds the whole plan visibly for both people at once.
items: Maths and Sciences need a shared digital whiteboard, not just a voice call.
Languages and Humanities work well through a shared, live-edited document.
Practical Science apparatus cannot be replicated online; the write-up and method still can.
IA and coursework stay the student's own work under IB and exam board rules.
Past papers marked live against the real scheme translate well to a screen.

contentBlocks.heading: Online Coverage Across Sushant Lok, SPR and New Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Online tutoring exists precisely because Gurgaon is large and its corridors do not sit close to each other. In Sushant Lok 1, Sushant Lok 2, South City 1 and the stretch around Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City, home tutors are relatively easy to place because the area is dense and well connected, so families here often choose an online tutor for a specific specialist subject rather than out of necessity, keeping the rest of the week's tutoring in person.

Southern Peripheral Road (SPR), covering Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 70 and Sector 72, along with Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and societies such as Tata Primanti, sits further from the older parts of the city, and evening traffic on SPR itself can stretch a short trip considerably once school pickup and office hours overlap. An online tutor for Southern Peripheral Road families is often less about preference and more about reliably holding a 7 pm slot every week without it slipping because of a delayed arrival.

New Gurgaon, which includes Sector 82, Sector 83, Sector 84, Sector 85, Sector 86, Sector 89, Sector 90, the area around Kherki Daula and the stretch along Pataudi Road, with societies including Vatika India Next and Godrej Air, is still filling in, and a home tutor with the right IB or IGCSE specialism does not always live close by yet. An online tutor serving New Gurgaon removes that constraint entirely: a DP2 Economics HL specialist or a Cambridge IGCSE Additional Maths tutor can serve a family in Sector 90 exactly as reliably as one in central Gurgaon, since neither party is travelling anywhere.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and an online tutor scheduling around a real school calendar has to work from the actual dates a family gives, not a generic academic year. The weeks after a school's own internal exams and the weeks immediately before mocks are typically when online sessions get busiest, since that is when a family notices a gap that in-term revision has not closed.

Extracurricular commitments matter as much as the exam calendar. A student with a late sports practice, a debate club meeting or a school bus that only reaches home after 6 pm needs an online slot built around that specific evening rather than a fixed template, and this is exactly the kind of detail IB Gram asks about before shortlisting a tutor, since a slot that clashes every second week will not hold for a full term.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutor, Online Tutor or Hybrid: What Suits Your Gurgaon Evenings?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is IB Gram's lead service across Gurgaon: a verified tutor comes to your house, works at your child's own desk, and can see handwriting, exam technique under time pressure and the actual mess of a working notebook up close. For a younger MYP student, or any student who struggles to focus without someone physically present, a home tutor remains the more reliable choice, and IB Gram can arrange this instead of or alongside anything online.

Live online tutoring is the format this page is built around, and it earns its place for a specific reason: it removes travel entirely, which matters most for families managing a DP2 timetable with six subjects, extracurriculars and a school day that already runs late. A shared digital whiteboard, a video call and a document both people can edit cover most of what a Maths, Science, Humanities or Language lesson needs, and an evening slot that would be impossible for a home tutor reaching Sector 90 or Sohna Road by 7 pm is often straightforward online.

Hybrid combines both deliberately rather than by accident: one subject or one weekly session stays in person, usually the one that benefits most from hands-on marking or a younger student's need for a physical presence, while a second subject or a revision-only session moves online. Most families who start fully home-based drift toward some hybrid mix by the second term, once the student is comfortable working independently from a shared screen; the honest trade-off is that hybrid asks a family to manage two different rhythms in one week rather than one.

Online tutor: no travel, wider specialist choice, best for self-directed older students.
Hybrid: one subject or session in person, another online, split deliberately by need.

contentBlocks.heading: How We Verify a Tutor Before the First Online Session
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram shortlists has a verified profile before a family ever sees it: board and syllabus experience checked against what is claimed, the level and subjects confirmed, and a conversation about how they actually teach a lesson, not just what they say they can teach. For an online tutor specifically, that includes confirming they are comfortable running a lesson through a shared whiteboard and a video call smoothly, since a specialist who knows DP Chemistry cold but struggles with the technology wastes a family's paid time on setup rather than teaching.

Parents should still check a few things themselves before the first real session, and IB Gram encourages this rather than discouraging it. Ask the tutor directly which syllabus codes or components they have taught recently, request a short written note after the trial session describing what was covered and what the student struggled with, and watch how they handle a question they do not immediately know the answer to; a tutor who says 'let me check the mark scheme and confirm' is more trustworthy than one who guesses confidently.

The free demo or trial session is where verification becomes real rather than a claim on paper: you see the tutor teach your actual child, on the actual syllabus, before committing to anything ongoing. If something feels off after the trial, whether it is pacing, tone or simply a personality mismatch, say so; IB Gram treats a request for a different tutor as normal, not as a complaint, because the fit between two people matters as much as the qualification on paper.

contentBlocks.heading: What Makes an Online IB or IGCSE Lesson Actually Work?
contentBlocks.body:
Three things separate an online lesson that works from one that quietly wastes an hour: a shared whiteboard or annotation tool that both tutor and student can write on at the same time, a stable enough connection that the video does not freeze mid-explanation, and a student sitting somewhere in the house without a television or a phone nearby. None of these are expensive to arrange, but skipping any one of them turns a live tutor into an expensive video call where nothing gets written down.

The equipment that matters most is often the smallest: a stylus or even a finger on a tablet screen for writing working out, a second monitor or tablet if one is available so the video call and the whiteboard are not fighting for the same small screen, and headphones so background noise from the rest of the house does not bleed into a Chemistry explanation. None of this needs to be new or expensive; a family does not need to buy anything specialised before trying a trial session, since most tutors can adapt to whatever setup a household already has.

Families in Gurgaon choose online for reasons that are mostly practical rather than about preferring a screen: traffic on SPR or Pataudi Road that makes a fixed evening slot unreliable for a home tutor, a specialist for a niche subject or a specific syllabus code who simply does not live close enough to reach every corridor, and, for older DP2 students revising independently, a format that fits around a school day that already runs until 4 or 5 pm. The honest limit is attention: a student who drifts after fifteen minutes on a screen, or who needs a physical presence to stay on task, is not well served by forcing online tutoring to work when home or hybrid would serve them better. Search results for an IB and IGCSE online tutor near you in Gurgaon, or for an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Gurugram specifically, lead to the same verified pool IB Gram draws from, since Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana is one city under two names.

A stable connection; test it once before the first paid session.
A quiet space without a television or phone within reach.
A stylus or tablet for handwriting out working, not typing it.

contentBlocks.heading: When Online Should Become Home Tuition Instead
contentBlocks.body:
Progress with an online tutor should be visible within the first month in concrete ways: the student can point to a specific topic that has improved, homework between sessions gets done without daily reminders, and a written update after each session names what was actually covered rather than a vague summary. If none of that is happening by the fourth or fifth session, the honest move is to ask whether the format, not just the tutor, is the problem.

Online has real limits, and naming them plainly matters more than selling around them. A student who cannot sit still in front of a screen without a parent present is not going to improve simply because the tutor is better; a subject that leans heavily on physical demonstration, like a titration in Chemistry or a geometry construction, is genuinely harder to teach well on a call than at a desk with the actual apparatus or instruments in hand. And a family that has tried online for a term with no improvement should treat home or hybrid tutoring as the next honest step, not a failure. There is no verifiable 'best' IB and IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon, only a match whose syllabus experience and teaching style fit your child; the same is true of any of the IB and IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon you might compare on paper.

No tutor, online or otherwise, can guarantee a grade, and any claim that promises one should be treated with suspicion. What a good online arrangement can reasonably promise is a consistent weekly session, a written record of what was covered, and a tutor willing to say plainly when a topic needs another week rather than moving on because the syllabus calendar says to. Starting late in a term narrows what is realistically achievable before an exam session, and an honest tutor will say so rather than promising to catch up entirely in a few weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started with an IB or IGCSE Online Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started takes one conversation. Whether you choose an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon or a home tutor instead, the same verified shortlist and trial process applies. Send a query or book a free consultation, and be ready to share your child's board, whether that is the IB DP, MYP or IGCSE under Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, the syllabus code if you know it, the current level or grade, the school's calendar for the term ahead, and the evening slots that genuinely work around school, buses and activities.

The first session itself is best treated as a diagnostic rather than a first lesson in the usual sense: expect the tutor to ask the student to attempt a short piece of work, whether that is a past paper question, an essay plan or a problem set, so they can see the actual gap rather than guess at it from a syllabus list. Bring a recent test, a piece of marked homework or a past paper attempt if you have one; it saves the first fifteen minutes and gives the tutor something concrete to react to.

After the trial, you decide whether to continue, whether weekly or twice weekly suits the term ahead, and whether this should stay fully online or shift toward hybrid as the term goes on. Availability for a specific subject, level and slot is always subject to tutor availability, particularly for HL subjects or specialist syllabus codes close to the May exam session, so starting the conversation early gives IB Gram more room to find the right match rather than the first available one.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child need for an online IB or IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a stable camera and microphone, a reliable internet connection, and a shared whiteboard or annotation app that both the tutor and student can write on live is the core setup; nothing more exotic than that. Most tutors run sessions through a video call with a digital whiteboard alongside, so the student writes working out in real time rather than describing it verbally, which matters most for Maths and the Sciences. A second screen or a tablet used purely for the whiteboard, while the laptop carries the video call, makes annotation smoother than working on one small screen, though it is not essential to start. Test the setup once before the first real session so a technical hiccup does not eat into paid lesson time.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work as well as a home tutor for IB and IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For most subjects and most students, yes, provided the equipment is right and the student can concentrate without a parent hovering in the room. Online removes travel time entirely, which matters on an evening when Southern Peripheral Road traffic is heavy, and it opens up specialist tutors who would never reach New Gurgaon by 7 pm in person. It suits self-directed teenagers, DP2 students revising past papers, and any subject built around a shared document or whiteboard better than it suits a younger child who needs someone physically present to hold attention. If a student's focus visibly drops on screen after fifteen minutes, home or hybrid tutoring is usually the better call, and IB Gram can arrange either.

faqs.question: How do I know within a few weeks whether the online tutor is working?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions after the third or fourth session: is the student arriving with actual questions rather than a blank page, is homework getting done without a daily reminder, and has the tutor sent a short written update on what was covered. A tutor who cannot yet name a specific gap in the syllabus after three sessions is still diagnosing, which is normal for session one but should have changed by session four. If none of these are true by the fourth session, ask IB Gram for a different match rather than waiting out a full term; a mismatch rarely fixes itself and a switch costs a short conversation, not a restart.

faqs.question: What if there has been no real progress after a month of online lessons?
faqs.answer: First check whether the goal was ever specific: 'get better at Chemistry' does not show progress the way 'improve IA draft structure' or 'clear the last three topic tests' does, so revisit what the tutor was actually asked to fix. If the goal was specific and a month of weekly sessions has not moved it, ask for a different tutor rather than assuming the format has failed; sometimes the syllabus fit or the teaching style, not the online setup, was the real problem. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a session-by-session record of what was covered should exist, and IB Gram can review it with you before arranging a switch.

faqs.question: How much does an IB or IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on the level, the subject, whether it is DP HL versus SL, and how many sessions a week you need, so IB Gram will not quote a figure without knowing those details first; ask during your consultation and it will be laid out clearly before anything is booked. Online tuition is generally a cost-efficient one-to-one format since no travel time is built into the tutor's evening, though the exact structure, per session, monthly or in a package, is confirmed with you directly. Availability for a given subject and slot is always subject to tutor availability at the time you enquire, particularly close to the May exam session when demand rises.

faqs.question: My child's home tutor travels to Sushant Lok every week. Can we switch to a mix of online and home?
faqs.answer: Yes, a hybrid arrangement is one of the most common switches IB Gram sets up, usually keeping one in-person session for the subject that needs a whiteboard and hands-on marking, and moving a second subject or a revision-only session online. Families in Sushant Lok, South City 1 and around Millennium City Centre often start fully home-based and shift a session online once the student is comfortable working from a shared document without a parent in the room. The change does not require starting the matching process over if the existing tutor can also teach online; if not, IB Gram will shortlist an online specialist for that one subject while the home tutor continues the rest.

faqs.question: Is a home session ever better than online for a New Gurgaon or SPR family with a long commute for the tutor?
faqs.answer: Often yes for younger students or for subjects that genuinely need hands-on marking, but the honest trade-off is that a home tutor reaching Sector 82 or Sector 66 on a weekday evening is working against Southern Peripheral Road and NH-48 traffic that can stretch a short trip considerably, which narrows the realistic slot options. An online tutor removes that constraint entirely and can usually offer more slot choice for the same specialist. For a DP2 student revising past papers or an IGCSE student who works well independently, online is frequently the more reliable choice precisely because the slot is not held hostage to traffic.

faqs.question: What happens if an online session is missed or the internet drops mid-lesson?
faqs.answer: The session is rescheduled the same way a missed home session would be, by agreeing a replacement slot with the tutor directly, and a genuine connectivity drop is treated as a technical issue, not a missed lesson, provided it is flagged promptly. Keep a backup option such as a phone hotspot for evenings when the household internet is unreliable, since connection quality can vary by building and by weather during the monsoon months. If drops happen repeatedly, mention it during a session; most tutors will suggest lowering video quality to protect the audio and the shared whiteboard, which matter more than seeing each other's faces clearly.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an online IB or IGCSE tutor usually run?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week is the common baseline for most subjects, rising to three during exam years or when a subject has fallen behind school pace, and dropping to one for a lighter revision-only arrangement. DP HL subjects with 240 recommended teaching hours over two years generally need a steadier weekly rhythm than an SL subject at 150 hours, and an IGCSE student approaching a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel exam series will often add a short weekly past paper session in the final term. The right frequency is set during your consultation once IB Gram knows the subject, the level and how much school-taught content still needs consolidating, and it can be adjusted as the term goes on.

faqs.question: Can the same online tutor teach my child through both IGCSE and the IB DP?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, but plan for two different specialists rather than expecting one, since IGCSE Core or Extended tiers and DP Higher or Standard Level genuinely test different skills, and a tutor strong at one is not automatically strong at the other. A tutor who has taught a student well through Cambridge IGCSE Grade 10 Physics, for instance, may or may not be the right fit for DP1 Physics HL the following year, because the command terms, the depth of theory and the exam structure all shift. IB Gram will ask, at the point your child moves stage, whether to continue with the same tutor or shortlist a DP specialist, rather than assuming either answer.

faqs.question: Is a recorded video course a reasonable alternative to a live online tutor?
faqs.answer: It can supplement a live tutor for extra practice material, but it is not a substitute, because a recording cannot answer a follow-up question, mark a student's actual working, or notice a misunderstanding forming in real time the way a live online or home tutor does. A recorded course suits a student who is already strong and wants more worked examples to watch, not a student who is stuck on a specific IA criterion or a Cambridge Extended tier topic. If your child has tried recorded resources and progress has stalled, a live one-to-one session, online or at home, is usually the next honest step, since it is the only format where someone checks the actual working.

introSummary: IB and IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon are best chosen from a short list of two or three verified profiles, compared side by side on board experience, subject depth, school familiarity and slot, rather than hired from the first search result. IB Gram builds this shortlist after a short consultation, then arranges trial sessions, online, home tuition or a mix of both, so a family in Palam Vihar or off Pataudi Road can judge fit directly before committing to a term. Comparing tutors matters most exactly where specialist options are thinner: along Dwarka Expressway, through Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, and around Manesar and the NH-48 corridor south. This page sets out how to compare fairly and switch cleanly if the first choice is wrong, for families anywhere in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you compare and shortlist IB and IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist beats a single hire because two tutors who look equally strong on paper often teach very differently once a lesson actually starts. IB Gram's first step is the same short consultation every family goes through: board, syllabus, level, the subjects that need covering, and whether the household wants online lessons, home tuition or both. What changes for a comparison request is what happens next.

Rather than one recommendation, IB Gram puts together two or three verified profiles that each genuinely fit the brief, not one strong match padded out with weaker ones just to offer a choice. Each profile comes with a short note on why it was included, covering board experience, the exact level taught before, familiarity with the family's school where relevant, and whether the tutor teaches online, at home or both. This is where the process becomes a genuine comparison rather than a single decision dressed up as one.

From there, the family reviews the shortlist, decides which one or two profiles to trial first, and IB Gram arranges the sessions. A trial with each candidate should cover broadly the same ground, a diagnostic look at the student's current work, so that what the family is comparing is actually comparable, rather than one tutor doing a warm introduction and another diving straight into a past paper. After the trials, the family picks a tutor, or asks for a second round of profiles if neither felt right, which is a normal outcome, not a failure of the process.

Speed matters less here than fit. A family close to a mock examination might reasonably compress this into a single week, running two trials back to back, while a family planning ahead for the next academic year can afford to take slightly longer and be more deliberate about the comparison.
items: 1. Share board, syllabus, level and preferred format in one consultation.
2. IB Gram assembles two or three verified profiles, not a single match.
3. Each profile arrives with a note on why it fits the brief.
4. Trial sessions run with each candidate on comparable ground.
5. The family chooses one tutor or asks for a fresh shortlist.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing programme experience: DP, MYP and IGCSE are not interchangeable
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor who taught IB Diploma Programme (DP) Biology well two years ago is not automatically the right comparison partner for a tutor who has spent the same two years teaching Cambridge IGCSE Biology, even though both list Biology on their profile. The Diploma Programme runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to three more points toward a 45-point maximum and 24 as the minimum for the diploma itself. Comparing two DP tutors should mean comparing which HL and SL combinations they have actually taught, not just the subject name.

The Middle Years Programme runs five years, MYP 1 through 5, across eight subject groups, and every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, scored 0 to 8 each, converting to a final 1 to 7 grade. A tutor comparison here should include whether the candidate has handled the Personal Project in MYP 5, or the Community Project that sits earlier in MYP 3 or 4, and whether the school in question has opted into MYP eAssessment, since that changes how a term is paced.

For IGCSE, the comparison should separate Cambridge IGCSE from Pearson Edexcel International GCSE clearly, since a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. Cambridge runs a February and March series available only in India, plus May, June, October and November series, and grades most syllabuses A star to G, some with 9-1 versions under separate codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9 to 1. Whether a candidate has taught Core or Extended tier work, or both, is a fair and specific comparison question, and a tutor who also has direct experience with the IGCSE to IB DP transition brings something the school calendar alone cannot teach.

Asking each shortlisted candidate the same set of programme-specific questions, rather than a general 'do you teach IB or IGCSE', is what turns a vague comparison into a useful one.
items: DP tutors should be compared on actual HL/SL subject combinations taught.
MYP tutors should be compared on Personal Project or Community Project experience.
IGCSE tutors should be compared on Cambridge versus Edexcel and Core versus Extended.
A tutor's MYP eAssessment familiarity matters only if the school has opted in.
IGCSE to IB DP transition experience is a fair, specific comparison question.

contentBlocks.heading: What should a side-by-side comparison actually test?
contentBlocks.body:
Two tutors can both claim to be strong in IB Maths and mean very different things by it. A fair comparison during a trial session should put both candidates through roughly the same test: given a recent past paper question, can the tutor mark a student's working against the real scheme, not just check whether the final answer is right? Command terms like define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent should shape a tutor's own explanation, and a tutor who cannot naturally explain why an answer needs to evaluate rather than merely describe is weaker on this specific skill, whatever their general subject knowledge.

For Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects, a useful comparison question is how each candidate handles the Core and Extended tier decision, or the equivalent Foundation and Higher split where it applies, since a tutor who has only ever taught the higher tier may be less useful for a student whose school is still deciding where they sit. For the Middle Years Programme, ask each candidate to walk through how they would mark a sample response against Criterion A to D, since fluency here separates tutors who genuinely understand MYP assessment from those who are teaching it like a regular school subject.

Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports available through the school or the IB's own channels are the fairest shared material for a side-by-side trial, since both candidates work from the same source rather than their own separate materials, which makes differences in explanation and marking approach much easier to see. Comparing how each tutor uses a shared whiteboard or annotates a script on screen during an online trial also reveals real differences in teaching style that a written profile cannot show at all.

After two trials on the same material, most families find the choice becomes obvious, not because one tutor is objectively better in the abstract, but because one explanation clicked for this particular student and the other did not.
items: Ask each candidate to mark the same past paper question against the real scheme.
Command term fluency, evaluate versus describe, is a specific, testable skill.
Core/Extended or Foundation/Higher tier experience should be compared directly.
MYP criterion marking fluency separates genuine specialists from general tutors.

contentBlocks.heading: Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon and Manesar: where comparing matters most
contentBlocks.body:
Along Dwarka Expressway, covering Sector 102 through Sector 113 and societies including Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, families often find fewer specialist IB and IGCSE tutors offering a regular home slot than on the golf course corridors, which makes comparing an online candidate against a home candidate a genuinely useful exercise rather than a formality. A tutor who teaches well online but has no home availability here should be compared honestly against one willing to travel but with thinner subject depth, and the right answer depends on which gap matters more for this particular student.

Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, spanning Palam Vihar itself, Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar and Sector 4, 14, 15, 22 and 23, sit apart from the newer corridors where many specialist tutors are based, and a family here comparing two shortlisted profiles should ask directly how often each candidate actually teaches in this part of the city versus how far they would be travelling for the first time. A tutor already familiar with the area's traffic patterns and society layouts brings something a stronger subject profile alone does not.

Manesar and the NH-48 corridor south, including IMT Manesar, Hero Honda Chowk and Sector 33, 34 and 37, is furthest from where most IB and IGCSE specialists live, and here the comparison usually narrows quickly to online candidates, since a fair side-by-side trial with two home-based tutors may simply not be realistic on a weekday evening. Families in this corridor should weigh subject depth more heavily than local familiarity when comparing profiles, since travel time removes local familiarity from the equation almost entirely.

Across all three corridors, the comparison question is the same even though the answer differs: is the gap between two candidates about subject depth, about format, or about location, and which of those matters most for this particular student this term.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing tutors against the same Gurgaon school calendar
contentBlocks.body:
Families at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge are comparing tutors against a real calendar, not an abstract one. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; the schools are named only to describe calendar pressures families in Gurgaon generally deal with.

A fair comparison question for any shortlisted tutor is how they plan around the school's own mock examination dates, since these are set independently by each school, usually months ahead of the May session for DP2 students, rather than following one fixed national date. Ask both candidates the same question directly: how would the weeks after a mock result change what a session looks like? A tutor who has a clear, specific answer is usually more useful than one who gives a generic response about working hard before exams.

Coursework deadlines, practical assessments and oral or speaking components also differ by subject and school, and comparing two candidates on how they track these across a term, not just whether they know they exist, is a genuinely useful filter. Winter break, board exam leave and the weeks around report cards interrupt every tutor's schedule about equally, so this is one area where the comparison rarely reveals much difference between two reasonable candidates.

School bus timings and after-school activities fix the earliest a session can start on a weekday, and asking both shortlisted candidates whether their available slot actually matches the family's real evening, not an idealised one, is a simple but often skipped comparison step.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online lessons or hybrid: a comparison factor, not a fixed choice
contentBlocks.body:
Families comparing IB and IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon against home-based ones should list format as an explicit factor from the start. Home tuition remains IB Gram's lead service, and it is worth listing as an explicit comparison factor rather than assuming every shortlisted tutor offers it. A tutor who teaches at the family's own table in Sector 15 near Old Gurgaon, working from the student's actual notebook, offers something a purely online candidate cannot: presence, and the ability to read a distracted student without relying on a screen. When two candidates are otherwise close on subject depth, willingness and ability to teach at home can reasonably decide the comparison.

Online lessons open the shortlist considerably, since a specialist teaching IB Economics HL from anywhere can be compared fairly against a home-based generalist, using a shared whiteboard, an annotated past paper on screen and a document camera for handwritten working. The honest trade-off when comparing an online candidate against a home one: online removes the physical presence that helps some students concentrate, but it often brings deeper subject expertise to the comparison, especially for a family in a corridor like Manesar where local specialist options are limited.

Hybrid arrangements, where a tutor teaches at home most weeks and moves online during exam-heavy stretches or on a bad traffic evening, are increasingly common enough that they deserve to be compared as their own category, not folded into either home or online. A candidate offering hybrid naturally should be weighed against one who offers only one format rigidly, since flexibility itself is a real point of comparison, not a minor detail.

When running trial sessions specifically to compare formats, it helps to keep everything else constant: same subject, same kind of material, similar length, so that what the family actually learns from the comparison is about format and teaching style, not about one trial happening to cover easier content than the other.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you verify two tutors the same way, so the comparison stays fair?
contentBlocks.body:
A comparison only means something if both candidates were checked to the same standard before reaching the shortlist. IB Gram verifies board experience, actual level and subjects taught, and academic background against what each tutor's profile states, rather than taking a strong-sounding headline at face value, and this applies equally to every profile shown to a family, not just the one eventually chosen.

When the shortlist includes both a home-based and an online candidate, verification also covers what is specific to each format: for a home tutor, this means confirming the details on the profile match what shows up at the first session; for an online tutor, it means checking comfort with a shared whiteboard, connection stability, and the ability to mark handwritten working through a document camera or scanned image. Comparing two candidates fairly means holding both to their own relevant standard, not judging an online tutor by home-visit criteria or the reverse.

Parents should still do their own checking during the trial itself, since no verification process can fully substitute for watching a tutor actually teach: ask each candidate the same direct question about how they would handle a student who has stopped engaging, and compare not just the answer but how specific and practical it is. A vague answer from one candidate next to a concrete, experience-based answer from another is itself useful comparison data.

If, after verification and a trial, neither shortlisted candidate feels right, IB Gram treats this as ordinary and puts together a fresh shortlist rather than asking the family to settle for a weaker match.

contentBlocks.heading: Running trial lessons with more than one tutor, fairly
contentBlocks.body:
A useful shortlist has two or three profiles, not five or six; beyond that, the comparison becomes noise rather than a genuine decision. Each profile should show, at minimum, the exact board and level taught before, the subjects covered, whether the tutor teaches at home, online or both, and roughly how long they have taught that specific syllabus, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel or an IB subject guide, rather than a general teaching background.

A side-by-side comparison checklist works best when it is written down rather than kept in memory, especially once two trial sessions are a few days apart. Useful columns to compare: board and syllabus experience, command of the relevant command terms or assessment criteria, how the tutor marks a sample of the student's own work, availability against the family's real weekly slot, and whether the personality and pace suited the student, which matters as much as subject knowledge for a teenager who needs to actually want to show up each week.

Running trials with more than one tutor without unsettling the student usually means spacing them out slightly, a few days apart rather than back to back on the same evening, and being honest with the student that this is a comparison, not a test they need to perform for. Younger students especially can find it confusing to meet two new adults in quick succession without understanding why; a short, simple explanation, along the lines of trying two tutors to see who explains things best for them, usually settles this quickly.

Asking for a different tutor after a trial is not a failure of the process, and families should not feel obliged to continue with a tutor purely because a trial has already happened. If a candidate is a clear mismatch, in pace, personality or basic subject fit, saying so directly and asking for a fresh shortlist is the fastest way back to a working arrangement, and IB Gram does not treat this as an unusual request.
items: Keep the shortlist to two or three profiles; more becomes noise, not clarity.
Compare board experience, command-term fluency, marking approach, slot fit and personality.
Space trial sessions a few days apart rather than back to back.

contentBlocks.heading: What should progress look like after you choose, at home or online?
contentBlocks.body:
Whether comparing IB and IGCSE online tutors in Gurgaon or a single home tutor, a single trial session cannot show everything, and families should judge it for what it actually reveals: whether the tutor's explanation style suited the student, whether they handled a wrong answer constructively, and whether the pace felt right, rather than expecting a full verdict on long-term fit from 60 or 90 minutes. A tutor who seems quiet or undemonstrative in a first trial is not automatically the weaker choice; some of the most effective tutors take a session or two to find a student's actual working style.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, during a trial or afterward, and any strong claim along those lines during a comparison is worth treating with real caution rather than as a point in that candidate's favour. What a good trial does show is more modest and more useful: whether the tutor can meet the student roughly where they are, and whether the explanation approach seems likely to work over a term, not just for one hour.

Once a tutor is chosen, a fair first checkpoint for genuine progress sits around four to six sessions in, not the first one, since it takes that long for a real weekly rhythm to settle. Parents should expect a short update after each block of sessions covering what was taught, what is still shaky, and what comes next, rather than a vague reassurance.

If progress stalls after a proper run of sessions, the same comparison instinct that built the original shortlist applies again: ask for a different match, subject to tutor availability, rather than assuming the student simply is not good at the subject.

After the trials, choose the tutor who fits, or ask for a second shortlist if neither felt right; this happens regularly and is not treated as unusual. Lessons then continue at home, online or hybrid, whichever format the family and student actually settle on once real sessions, not just profiles on a page, have shown what works.

faqs.question: How many IB or IGCSE tutors should I shortlist before deciding?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually the right number; fewer does not give a real comparison, and more turns the decision into noise rather than clarity. IB Gram typically shortlists two or three verified profiles matched to the board, level and format a family describes, each with a short note on why it fits. Going beyond three rarely improves the decision, since trial sessions take real time and most families lose track of specific differences once more than three profiles are involved. If none of the first shortlist feels right, a fresh set of two or three is a better next step than expanding the original list.

faqs.question: Is it fair to run trial lessons with two tutors at home in the same week?
faqs.answer: Yes, spaced a few days apart rather than back to back, and told plainly to the student that this is a comparison. Running two home trials in the same week is common near corridors like Old Gurgaon or Palam Vihar and does not confuse most students once they understand why, though a short, honest explanation beforehand helps, especially for a younger child. IB Gram can also mix formats during comparison, one trial at home and one online, if the family is genuinely undecided on format as well as on the tutor.

faqs.question: What should I compare across two tutors' trial sessions?
faqs.answer: Compare how each tutor marks the same piece of the student's own work, how clearly they explain a mistake, whether the pace suited the student, and whether the personality was a good fit, not just whether the hour felt pleasant. Using the same past paper or topic across both trials makes real differences easier to see than comparing two entirely different lessons. Availability against the family's actual weekly slot and whether the tutor offers home, online or hybrid also belong on the same checklist.

faqs.question: What if my child likes both shortlisted tutors equally?
faqs.answer: This happens more often than families expect, and in that case practical factors can fairly decide it: which tutor's slot fits the week better, which offers the format, home, online or hybrid, the family actually prefers, and which has closer experience with the exact syllabus or tier the student needs. It is also reasonable to run one more session with each before deciding, rather than choosing on a coin toss, since a second session sometimes reveals a difference the first one did not.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE online tutors cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on the board, level, subject and weekly frequency, so it varies across a shortlist rather than being one fixed number. IB Gram discusses fee structure, whether sessions are priced individually, monthly or as a package, once the board, level and slot are confirmed during the first consultation. Comparing two shortlisted tutors on cost alone is usually less useful than comparing them on fit first, since a slightly higher-cost tutor who is clearly the better match for this student is typically worth more than a cheaper one who is not.

faqs.question: Can I compare a home tutor against an online tutor directly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the most useful comparisons a family in a corridor like Dwarka Expressway or Manesar can run, since local home-tutor options are often thinner there than online ones. Ask both candidates to work through the same past paper question during their trial so the comparison is about teaching quality and format fit, not about unrelated content. The honest trade-off is presence versus subject depth: a home tutor offers physical presence, an online specialist often brings deeper board experience when local options are limited.

faqs.question: One of my shortlisted tutors cancelled a trial. What now?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram and a replacement trial can usually be arranged without losing the rest of the shortlist, so this does not need to derail the whole comparison. A single cancellation is not unusual and is not treated as a mark against that tutor's profile, though a family should still ask for a firm rescheduled time rather than leaving it open-ended. If cancellations happen more than once with the same candidate, that pattern itself is fair to weigh into the comparison.

faqs.question: Do both shortlisted tutors need to follow the same school's pacing?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but both should be able to work from the student's actual school notes and recent tests rather than a generic outline, whichever school the family attends. During a trial, ask each candidate directly how they would adjust their plan around the school's own mock examination dates, since these are set independently by each school. A candidate with a clear, specific answer is usually easier to compare fairly than one who gives a vague response about working hard before exams.

faqs.question: How do I switch after choosing, if the fit turns out wrong later?
faqs.answer: Ask IB Gram for a different match, subject to tutor availability, the same way a family would during the original comparison. A mismatch that only shows up a few weeks in, rather than during the trial, is not unusual, since a trial session cannot reveal everything about weekly working style. The family does not need to justify the switch at length; naming what is not working, pace, personality, or a lack of progress, is enough to start a fresh shortlist.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram compare tutors for home tuition and online tutoring the same way?
faqs.answer: Yes, every profile is verified to the same standard regardless of format, though what is checked differs slightly: a home tutor's practical availability for the family's corridor, an online tutor's comfort with a shared whiteboard and a stable connection. When a shortlist mixes both formats, IB Gram notes clearly on each profile which format the tutor offers, so the family is comparing verified options on equal footing rather than guessing which candidate can actually do what.

faqs.question: Is a tutor found by word of mouth worth comparing against a verified shortlist?
faqs.answer: It can be, and there is no harm in trialling a personal referral alongside IB Gram's shortlisted profiles, as long as the comparison is fair: the same past paper, a similar length session, and the same direct questions about pacing and marking approach. The real difference is verification; a referral's teaching background is rarely independently checked, while a shortlisted profile has already been checked before the family ever meets the tutor, which narrows the risk in the comparison from the start.

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE Structure: What Online Tuition Has to Track
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge IGCSE, set by Cambridge International Education, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE both run as two-year courses across Grade 9 and Grade 10 in Gurgaon. Cambridge sits exam series in February/March, an option offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November, grading most subjects A* to G with Core and Extended tiers on many syllabuses, Core capped at grade C, Extended reaching A*. Edexcel runs January and May/June series, grading 9 to 1 throughout. An online specialist needs to know the tier before the first lesson, since annotating a Core paper and an Extended paper on screen calls for a different pace entirely.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria, A to D, scored 0 to 8, converting to a final 1 to 7 grade through the IB's own boundaries. MYP 5 carries the Personal Project, with the Community Project usually a year or two earlier, and MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams and ePortfolios, is a school's own choice to opt into, not a fixed requirement. Criteria-based feedback works well on a shared screen, since a specialist can mark directly against the descriptor with the student watching.

The IB Diploma Programme (DP) runs two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points, so 45 is the maximum and 24 the minimum for the diploma, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), completed but not graded. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May session, and a home tutor or online specialist working toward it needs to track each school's own DP2 mock dates individually.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB and IGCSE Subjects Suit a Screen, and Which Do Not?
contentBlocks.body:
Written subjects annotate well online. A specialist marking a DP Economics essay or an IGCSE English response can mark up the actual document live, exactly as a red pen would on paper, and the marked copy stays saved for the student to revisit before the next test. Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, translate cleanly to a screen because the specialist can highlight the exact word in the question and show, in real time, why the answer missed the mark.

Maths and the sciences need more thought. A tablet and stylus let a specialist watch working develop line by line, which covers most IGCSE and DP Maths well, but a student still learning to set out long working by hand sometimes benefits from a home tutor sitting beside the page instead. Sciences practicals cannot run through a screen at all; an online specialist can talk through a method, interpret results, and prepare a student for a written practical paper, but the physical skill of using apparatus has to come from school labs.

The Internal Assessment (IA), the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) all work well online because the real work is conversation and feedback on a written draft, not anything physical, screen-sharing the actual document during the call keeps the specialist and student looking at the same paragraph rather than describing it over a call. A tutor's role stays the same online as at home: strengthening the student's own analysis and referencing, never writing or rewriting the work.

mainEntity.name: What equipment do we actually need for IB and IGCSE online tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A laptop or tablet with a stable internet connection covers most of it, along with a stylus or writing tablet for Maths and the sciences so the specialist can watch working develop rather than just the final answer. A quiet spot with the same materials used for any tuition, textbook, calculator, past papers, matters more than expensive equipment. Testing the connection and the whiteboard tool once before the first class, rather than during it, avoids losing the opening minutes of a lesson to a technical fix.

mainEntity.name: Does online tuition work as well as a home tutor for IB and IGCSE?

acceptedAnswer.text: For some work, yes; for other work, not quite. Discussion-based subjects, essays, TOK, EE supervision, translate to a screen with almost no loss, since the exercise is conversation over a shared document either way. Step-by-step Maths working and lab-based Sciences discussion tend to still go better with a home tutor physically present, watching the page directly. Many Gurgaon families combine both, a regular online slot for a specific specialist plus one home session a month for handwriting-heavy practice.

mainEntity.name: Can a home session be added alongside online tuition if it turns out to be needed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is a common adjustment rather than a sign the online arrangement failed. If a subject turns out to need more handwriting-heavy practice than a screen comfortably supports, IB Gram can add a monthly or fortnightly home session with the same specialist where their schedule allows, or bring in a separate home tutor for that one subject. Mention early on if you expect this might be needed, since it can be planned into the arrangement from the start rather than added later as a fix.

mainEntity.name: How do I know within the first few weeks whether online tuition is actually working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Within the first three sessions, the student should be reasoning aloud rather than passively watching, the specialist should be checking understanding rather than lecturing at a shared screen, and written work reviewed against earlier attempts should show fewer repeated mistakes. If none of that is visible by session three, raise it with IB Gram directly rather than waiting to see if it improves on its own. A different specialist, a different pace, or a switch to a home tutor for that subject are all reasonable next steps.

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, where the specialist's own range genuinely spans both stages, though this should never be assumed automatically. Home tuition remains IB Gram's lead service for families who want a tutor at their own table, but many households choose live online lessons instead, for a specialist subject, an evening that traffic makes difficult, or simply a tutor who is not based nearby. Whether your child is finishing IGCSE Grade 10 or midway through DP1, the same comparison applies before you commit a term's worth of evenings to one online tutor: what to ask on the trial call, how to run two demo sessions fairly, and what to do if the first match does not click on screen.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Shortlist Online Tutors for IB and IGCSE in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A parent gets in touch, often after a first online trial elsewhere fell flat, and the conversation starts with specifics rather than a general request for "an online tutor": which board, which level, DP1 Economics HL or IGCSE Grade 9 Coordinated Science, which syllabus the school actually follows, and which evenings are realistically free once homework and activities are done. IB Gram builds the shortlist from that, not from a general pool of anyone willing to log on. That is the whole point of comparing IB and IGCSE online tuitions in Gurgaon properly instead of guessing.

The process itself stays short on purpose.

1. Board, level and subject are matched against tutors who have specifically taught online, not just tutors who happen to be available on a call.
2. Two or three verified profiles are shared, each showing subject depth, their usual online setup, whiteboard, shared documents, and their typical weekday evening slots.
3. A free consultation or a demo class can be arranged with each before you commit to a term of online sessions.

Online teaching is its own skill, not simply an in-person lesson moved to a screen, and this is where families comparing two profiles often miss something. A tutor excellent at explaining a graph in person may struggle to make the same explanation land through a shared screen with a slight lag. Ask each shortlisted profile specifically how long they have taught online, not just how long they have tutored overall. Some families keep a home tutor for one subject and add online tuition for another; IB Gram treats that as two parallel shortlists, not one.

If the first tutor does not work out after a genuine trial, IB Gram can build a second shortlist against what specifically went wrong, screen presence, pace, technical fluency, rather than starting the whole search again from nothing.

contentBlocks.heading: DP and MYP Online Support: Matching Programme Stage to Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Two shortlisted online tutors can both say "IB experience" and mean very different things, so it helps to know what each programme actually demands before you compare. The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups, with every subject marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored zero to eight; the criterion total out of thirty-two converts to a final grade of one to seven through the IB's grade boundaries. Ask a shortlisted online tutor whether they mark practice work against these criteria explicitly or just give a general verdict, since the difference shows up quickly in how useful the feedback actually is on screen.

The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 depending on the school, and supervising either one online, through shared documents and video check-ins rather than in person, is a distinct skill worth asking about directly if your child is approaching that year. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional per school, so confirm with your child's school before assuming any tutor needs to prepare for it.

The IB Diploma Programme (DP) runs two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded one to seven, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to three further points toward a forty-five maximum, twenty-four the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) is required too, separate from anything a tutor covers. When comparing two DP-focused online profiles, ask which HL and SL combinations each has actually taken students through online specifically, not just in a classroom years ago.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging Subject Depth Before You Shortlist an Online Specialist
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon means Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, usually a two-year course across Grade 9 and Grade 10, often followed by the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC for Class 11. Cambridge exam series run in February and March, a series offered only in India, plus May and June and October and November; Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May and June. When comparing two shortlisted online tutors, ask which series each has actually prepared students for, since a tutor used to one series can misjudge how much time is left before another.

Grading adds another layer to compare. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some subjects now offered as 9-1 versions under different syllabus codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1 throughout. Core and Extended tiers split many Cambridge subjects, Core capping at grade C, Extended reaching A*, and two online profiles claiming the same subject can still differ sharply here, one strong with Core entries building confidence, another experienced pushing Extended students toward the top grades.

On the DP side, a tutor confident with SL content is not automatically ready for HL's extra depth, and Internal Assessment (IA) guidance is subject-specific, with its own criteria and word limits set by the subject guide; screen-sharing a mark scheme is not the same as having actually marked several IAs against it. When two profiles both list the same subject, ask for the specific level and a concrete example of how they have used a mark scheme with a past student, not just a general claim of familiarity.

contentBlocks.heading: Online, Home or Hybrid: Weighing Two or Three Shortlisted Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where IB Gram starts most families, a tutor at your own table, correcting a half-finished working-out in person, building a rhythm week after week that a parent can watch directly rather than hear about secondhand. For some subjects and some children, particularly younger MYP students who need closer physical guidance, this remains genuinely the stronger option, and it is worth comparing at least one home tutor profile alongside your online shortlist rather than ruling it out by default.

But if you are specifically comparing IB and IGCSE online tuitions in Gurgaon, the case for online is real, not a fallback: access to a specialist who is not based near your sector, a slot that does not depend on evening traffic, and a shared screen that works nearly as well as paper for annotated past papers and worked solutions. When comparing two online profiles, ask each about their actual setup, not just whether they "do online," since a tutor with a proper shared whiteboard and screen-recording is a different experience from one on a basic video call with nothing shared at all.

Hybrid, a term built mostly around online sessions with an occasional home session added before a mock or exam, is what many families choosing between profiles end up settling on rather than deciding in advance. If one shortlisted tutor offers this and another insists on online only, that flexibility is worth weighing alongside subject fit.

The honest trade-off: online removes travel and widens your shortlist considerably, but it loses some of the shared physical working space, and the direct parental visibility, that a home session naturally has.

contentBlocks.heading: Can You Run Fair Trial Classes With More Than One Online Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
Yes, and doing it deliberately makes the comparison far more useful than trusting a first impression alone. Book both trial classes in the same week if you can, so your child's mood and the week's schoolwork form a similar background for each, rather than comparing a tired Friday session against a fresh Monday one. Use the same starting material for both trials where possible, the same past paper section or the same chapter, so the comparison is about teaching approach and online presence, not two unrelated topics.

During each trial, watch specifically for how the tutor uses the screen: do they check understanding before explaining, is the shared whiteboard actually used or mostly narrated, does the session end with something concrete, a marked task, a clear plan for next time, or does it simply run out of time without a clean close. A tutor who diagnoses before teaching, even briefly, is usually easier to build a term around than one who launches straight into new content.

Tell your child upfront that trying two tutors online is completely normal, not a test they can fail, particularly if this is a younger MYP student's first experience with online lessons at all. Older DP students often notice things worth asking about directly afterward, whether the explanation pace suited them, whether they felt comfortable interrupting to ask a question over a screen.

If the first trial goes poorly, or simply feels flat, do not treat that as proof online tuition itself does not work; it may just be that specific tutor's screen presence or pace. Go back to IB Gram with specifics, too slow, hard to follow on screen, did not check understanding, and a second shortlist can be built against exactly that gap.

contentBlocks.heading: What Changes in a Gurgaon Household After You Switch Online Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Switching to a better-matched online tutor rarely produces an immediate, visible jump; what changes first is smaller and easier to miss if you are looking for a dramatic result. In the first two or three weeks, expect diagnosis, an error log building, specific gaps in a topic becoming clear on screen, rather than a transformed test score. By six to eight weeks, look for a student attempting harder questions on their own during a session, and for movement in a specific subject's school test scores, a direction, not a single leap.

Be honest about what switching can and cannot fix. No tutor, online or otherwise, can guarantee a grade, and a family that switched expecting a fixed jump within a month is usually measuring the wrong thing. A DP student six weeks from mocks needs exam technique and past paper practice on screen more than new content; a Grade 9 IGCSE student earlier in the year has months to build foundations, and rushing that timeline online does not speed it up.

If a second online tutor repeats the same problem as the first, screen presence that does not land, pace that does not suit your child, look honestly at what actually changed between the two matches and what did not. Be specific with IB Gram about the pattern, not just a vague complaint, so the next shortlist is built against that exact gap.

Sometimes, after a genuine trial and a fair stretch of weeks, the honest answer is that online is not the right mode for this particular child or this particular subject, and a home tutoring session, occasional or regular, is worth adding back in.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting Online With IB Gram: What the First Session Needs at Home
contentBlocks.body:
Once you have chosen between your shortlisted profiles for IB and IGCSE online tuitions in Gurgaon, a short, practical list gets the first session off to a proper start, whether these are your only sessions or you also keep a home tutor for another subject. Test the platform together the day before, camera, microphone, shared screen or whiteboard, so lesson time is not spent solving a login problem. Have your child's current textbook, recent school test papers and a specific stuck topic ready to show on screen, since a tutor who can see actual recent work in the first fifteen minutes plans better than one working from a description alone.

Set up a proper space at home: a quiet corner, a reasonably stable connection, headphones if the household is busy in the evening, and good lighting so any handwritten working or shared document is easy to read clearly on screen. This matters more for online sessions than people expect, since a dim or noisy background makes a genuinely good tutor look worse than they are.

Agree the slot clearly, which weekday evenings, how long each session runs, and what happens if a session needs to move because of a school event. Availability is always subject to tutor schedule, so build in a little flexibility on both sides rather than expecting a fixed slot to hold without exception every week.

The first session itself usually opens with some diagnostic work before settling into the term's plan. From there, set a short review after two or three weeks, what has been covered, what is coming, whether the pace and the online format both suit your child. If something is not working, IB Gram can look at a different match rather than letting the term run its course on a fit that is not right.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Choose the Right IB and IGCSE Tutor for Your Sector in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Choosing the right IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon comes down to matching four things at once: the exact board and level, subject depth, genuine availability for your corridor and slot, and a teaching style your child actually responds to, and IB Gram works through all four before a name is even suggested to you.

1. Tell IB Gram your child's board (Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, MYP or DP), subject, grade, and roughly which sector or society you live in.
2. IB Gram narrows its pool of verified tutors to those who actually teach that exact syllabus and level, not simply 'IB tutors' or 'IGCSE tutors' as a general category.
3. From that narrower pool, IB Gram checks who can realistically reach your corridor on the evenings you need, or who is a strong online match if travel does not work.
4. A trial or demo class is arranged so your child meets the tutor before anything is committed to.
5. If the trial goes well, the weekly slot is fixed; if not, IB Gram offers a different tutor rather than pushing the first match.

A tutor is not interchangeable with another tutor who happens to teach the same subject. Two DP Economics tutors can have very different strengths, one strong on paper 2 data response technique, another better at building a student's confidence from a low base, and IB Gram tries to understand which your child actually needs before suggesting a name, not just which subject box to tick.

This does take a little longer for less common subjects or a Higher Level slot in a specific corridor, and IB Gram will say plainly when a match is subject to tutor availability rather than promising a tutor who does not exist yet. A family searching for an IB and IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon in January, ahead of the May exam session, generally has more choice than one starting the search in March.

Tutors are pooled by exact syllabus and level, not a general IB or IGCSE label.
A trial or demo class happens before any weekly slot is committed to.
