This page walks through when a batch, a small group or one-to-one coaching earns its place, what to check before signing up, and how IB Gram matches a family to the right format across Gurgaon, whether the search was for IB coaching near me or a named corridor.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds a Coaching Shortlist for Your Family
contentBlocks.body:
A coaching request in Gurgaon almost never starts with a name. It starts with a subject, a stage and a problem: a DP1 student who has fallen behind on IB Physics HL, a MYP 4 student whose criterion scores dipped after a term of online classes, or a family choosing between IB coaching in Gurgaon and moving straight to a private tutor. IB Gram takes that problem and works backward from it rather than pushing whichever tutor happens to be free that week.

The first conversation covers the board and programme (PYP, MYP or DP), the exact subject and level, which school the student attends only so far as pacing and calendar matter, and whether the family wants home tuition, online lessons or a mix of both. From there, IB Gram checks its pool of verified tutors for board experience at the right level, availability for the requested slot, and, for home lessons, a realistic travel plan into the family's sector or society. None of this is guesswork dressed up as matching; it is a short, specific conversation that narrows a large pool to a handful of real candidates.

A shortlist of tutors, never just one, is offered, along with a free trial or demo class so the family can see the tutor's teaching style before committing. This matters more for coaching decisions than most families expect: a tutor who is excellent for a MYP 2 group is not automatically right for a DP2 student cramming for the May session, and a demo exposes that mismatch quickly. If the first tutor turns out not to be the right fit after the trial, or even a few sessions in, the family can ask for a different match, and lessons continue at home, online or hybrid without starting the whole process over. Subject to tutor availability and the student's schedule, most families have a working match within days rather than weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: Which Stage Changes the Coaching You Need
contentBlocks.body:
Coaching that works for a PYP learner looks nothing like coaching that works for a DP2 student six weeks from the May session, and treating them the same is the most common mistake a generic coaching centre makes. In the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), for ages 3 to 12, learning runs through six transdisciplinary themes, among them How the world works and How we organize ourselves, delivered through units of inquiry rather than a fixed syllabus. There are no external examinations at this stage, so coaching here is really about building the ten attributes of the IB learner profile and preparing for the PYP exhibition in the final year, not drilling papers.

The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A through D, each scored out of 8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's own grade boundaries. That criterion structure is exactly where batch coaching struggles: a MYP tutor in Gurgaon has to know which criterion a student is weak on this term, not just whether the topic itself was covered. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, with a Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 at some schools, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional, since each school decides for itself whether to run it.

By the Diploma Programme (DP), the two-year course (DP1 and DP2) asks for six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 further points, so the maximum score is 45, with 24 as the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's own failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) runs alongside all of this. An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon needs to track a student's actual stage this closely, because a MYP criterion and a DP command term are not solved by the same lesson plan.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject and Syllabus Depth: What Coaching Should Actually Cover
contentBlocks.body:
Ask any experienced IB tutor in Gurgaon what separates a good coaching session from a wasted hour, and the answer is usually the same: syllabus depth, not syllabus coverage. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each offered at Higher Level and Standard Level, and a student who has been coached in the wrong strand for months can lose real time before anyone notices the mismatch. AA suits students heading toward pure maths, engineering or physics-heavy routes; AI suits those who will use maths in a more applied, real-world way. Coaching that does not ask which strand a student is on, or worse, teaches generic content that ignores the distinction, is coaching that wastes a term.

The sciences, IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology, are similar in that HL and SL share a common core but HL goes further into the same topics rather than adding unrelated ones, which means a tutor moving a student between levels needs to know exactly where that extra depth sits. IB English A and B are marked against command terms, words like define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent, and each one asks for a different depth of answer; a student who writes an evaluate response at describe-level depth loses marks regardless of how much they know. Good coaching drills command terms explicitly rather than assuming a student will absorb them by osmosis.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sit outside any single subject but inside every DP student's coaching plan, since together they are worth up to 3 additional points toward the 45-point maximum. TOK asks for essay-style analysis of how we know what we claim to know, and the EE is an independent piece of research the student largely drives themselves. Coaching here looks different again: less content delivery, more structured feedback on drafts, argument and referencing, spaced out across DP1 and DP2 rather than crammed at the end. A coaching format built for one subject rarely serves TOK or the EE well, which is one more reason a rigid batch struggles to cover the whole IB workload evenly.

contentBlocks.heading: The School Calendar Gurgaon's IB Families Are Coaching Around
contentBlocks.body:
Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana is home to a cluster of IB and international schools, among them Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge. What is consistent across these schools is the exam calendar. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter DP students for the May session, the one the majority of the city's families plan around, while November is used mainly by a minority of schools and by retake candidates catching up on a missed or resat paper. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, typically several months ahead of May, and those mocks are usually the point where a family first notices a subject is not on track, which is exactly when a coaching decision tends to get made in a hurry.

Coaching that ignores this calendar is coaching that arrives too late or leaves too early. A tutor should be working from the same past papers, markschemes and subject reports the student's own school uses, since these come through the school or the IB's official channels and show precisely how marks are awarded against each criterion or command term. May results land in early July, which for many Gurgaon families sets the real deadline: coaching intensity should rise in the months before mocks and the exam session itself, then step down afterward, rather than running at the same pace all year regardless of where the calendar actually sits.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring, Online or Hybrid: What Suits IB Coaching in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's starting point on every request is home tutoring: a verified home tutor teaching the student in the family's own home, at their own table, in their own sector or society. For IB coaching in Gurgaon, home tuition suits younger PYP and MYP students especially well, since a parent can see the working relationship forming, and it suits any subject where a tutor needs to watch a student's handwriting, working or diagram in real time, IB Maths and the sciences most of all. The trade-off is travel: a specialist home tutor for a less common subject combination may simply not have a realistic route into every corridor on a weekday evening.

IB online coaching in Gurgaon removes that limit entirely. A shared whiteboard and annotated past papers do most of what a physical whiteboard does, and online sessions make it possible to book a genuine subject specialist regardless of where in Gurgaon, or beyond, that tutor happens to live. Families juggling late school buses, evening activities or simply a long commute home often find online coaching easier to schedule consistently than a home visit, though it depends on a stable connection and a student who can concentrate on a screen for 60 to 90 minutes without a parent physically present to help hold focus.

Hybrid coaching splits the difference deliberately rather than compromising on both: home tuition in weeks the tutor's schedule and the family's sector line up, online for the rest, or home classes for a core subject and online for a specialist add-on like TOK. None of the three formats is objectively best. A family in New Gurgaon with a wide, quiet road and an available local home tutor may get more from home tuition than the same family would from online; a family needing a rare HL specialist may get more from online than from settling for whoever is nearby. IB Gram asks about this directly during matching, rather than defaulting every family to one format.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Verifies a Coaching Tutor, and What You Should Check Too
contentBlocks.body:
Verification is the part of coaching most families never see and most agencies never explain. IB home tutors in Gurgaon are checked by IB Gram for board experience, the specific subject and level they have actually taught, and general familiarity with how Gurgaon's international schools structure a term, before that tutor is ever shortlisted for a family. This is not a guarantee of a particular outcome; no tutor can guarantee a grade, and any coaching offer that implies otherwise is worth walking away from. It is, instead, a filter that removes the mismatches a family would otherwise only discover after paying for a term of coaching that never quite fit.

What a parent should check personally is narrower and more useful than it sounds. Ask whether the tutor has taught this exact syllabus, IB Mathematics AA rather than AI, HL rather than SL, the right MYP subject group rather than a neighbouring one, because a subject label alone hides a lot of variation. During the free trial or demo class, ask the tutor to walk through how they would mark a past answer against a real criterion or command term; a tutor who can do this fluently, on the spot, has usually taught the syllabus for real rather than adjacent to it.

It is also worth asking a coaching provider, whether that is IB Gram or anyone else, what happens when a session is missed, when the student's pace changes mid-term, or when the fit simply is not right after a few weeks. A trial class answers the subject-knowledge question; these logistics questions answer the service question, and both matter equally once a family has committed to a term of coaching rather than a single lesson. IB Gram's answer is straightforward: the family can ask for a different tutor at any point, and lessons continue at home, online or hybrid without losing the term's progress.

contentBlocks.heading: Batch, Small Group or One-to-One: How to Judge an IB Coaching Offer?
contentBlocks.body:
The various IB coachings in Gurgaon are sold in four shapes, and the honest answer to which one is best is: it depends on what the student actually needs this term, not on which format a centre happens to sell. A coaching centre batch, often built originally for CBSE boards, JEE or NEET preparation, moves at the pace of the group and follows a generic syllabus map that was never designed around the IB's criterion-based marking, command terms or HL and SL split. A batch student who is one criterion behind, or stuck on evaluate-level answers when the class has moved to discuss, tends to stay behind, because the format has no mechanism to pause for one person. Families searching for the best IB coaching in Gurgaon are really asking how to judge an offer, not which single brand to trust.

A small group of three or four students changes this only if the group is genuinely matched: same subject, same level, ideally the same school and pace. Under those conditions, a small group can work well, since students at the same stage benefit from hearing each other's questions and mistakes, and it usually costs less per student hour than one-to-one. Outside those conditions, a small group inherits the same problem as a batch, just at a smaller scale. One-to-one coaching, at home or online, removes the pacing problem entirely: the tutor adapts every session to what one student needs, at the cost of a higher hourly rate and the loss of peer discussion a group offers.

One line matters more than the format debate: IA work, the Extended Essay, TOK essays and the MYP Personal Project are individually assessed by design, and coaching these in a group setting risks answers that look too similar, which the IB's own academic integrity rules exist to catch. These tasks should always be one-to-one, whatever format a student uses for regular subject coaching. To judge any coaching offer in Gurgaon, ask six things: 1. does the tutor know this student's exact syllabus, AA or AI, HL or SL; 2. how is progress measured against real criteria or command terms; 3. is a free trial or demo class offered before payment; 4. how is IA, EE or TOK support kept individual; 5. what happens if the format is not working after a few weeks; 6. is pricing explained in structure, sessions, months or packages, rather than vague promises. A coaching offer that cannot answer these plainly is one to be wary of.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Should Look Like After a Month of IB Coaching
contentBlocks.body:
Families ask, reasonably, what a month of coaching should show, and the honest answer is narrower than most coaching adverts suggest. Real progress in the first month looks like a student handling a specific criterion or command term better than before, describe-level answers turning into evaluate-level answers, or a HL Maths student finally seeing where AA methods and AI methods diverge, rather than a jump in overall grade. Grades move slower than skills do, and any coaching provider that promises a grade outcome within weeks is promising something the IB's own assessment process does not support. No tutor can guarantee a grade, full stop, and that is true of every format covered on this page, in Gurugram or anywhere else.

A review every four to six weeks is what keeps coaching honest about this. Rather than running the same lesson plan for a whole term regardless of how the student is doing, a good tutor checks progress against the student's actual weak points and adjusts, which sometimes means more time on one subject and less on another, or a shift from new content to past-paper practice as an exam session approaches. This is where the school calendar matters again: intensity should rise before mocks and the May or November session, then step down afterward, rather than staying flat all year.

It is also worth saying plainly that starting coaching very close to a mock or the exam session itself narrows what is realistically achievable, whatever format is chosen. A DP2 student six weeks from May with three weak subjects needs a different, more triaged plan than a DP1 student with a full year ahead. And some students, honestly, do not need coaching at all, or need far less than a worried parent assumes; a single diagnostic session, which IB Gram can arrange as a trial class, is often enough to find out which situation a family is actually in before committing to a term of anything.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started with IB Coaching in Gurgaon

Starting is meant to be simple, and it is worth keeping it that way. A family sends a query or books a free consultation, describing the subject, the level (HL or SL, or the MYP subject group), and roughly where things stand this term, a first coaching request, a batch that is not working, or a switch from one format to another. What the first session should cover is a genuine diagnostic, not a sales pitch: a look at recent test or mock results, a sample past paper or piece of work marked against the real criteria, and a conversation about what the student finds hardest right now. This is true whether the eventual arrangement is one-to-one, a small group, or occasional online sessions layered onto a school's own support. A trial or demo class lets the family judge the tutor's actual teaching style, explanations, pacing, how they handle a wrong answer, before committing to anything longer.

From there, lessons run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability and the student's own schedule, and the format can change as the term goes on: a family might start with home tuition and add an online specialist for one subject, or move a struggling small-group student to one-to-one for a few weeks before the mocks. If a match is not right, even after the trial, the family can ask for a different tutor without losing momentum. The point of coaching, in whichever shape it takes, is a student who understands more at the end of a session than they did at the start, and a plan that keeps adjusting until that keeps happening reliably.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an IB coaching batch and one-to-one tutoring in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A batch teaches a fixed group at one pace, while one-to-one tutoring adapts every session to a single student. Batches, often built originally for CBSE, JEE or NEET preparation, follow a generic syllabus map that does not track the IB's criterion-based marking or command terms closely, so a student who falls one criterion behind can stay behind for weeks. One-to-one coaching, at home or online, adjusts pace and content to that one student, at a higher hourly cost. A small group of three or four sits between the two, working well only when everyone shares the same subject, level and school pace.

faqs.question: Can a small group of students share IB coaching without hurting their IA or coursework marks?
faqs.answer: Regular subject coaching can be shared in a small group, but IA, TOK essays, the Extended Essay and the MYP Personal Project should never be. These tasks are individually assessed by design, and coaching them in a group risks answers that look too similar, which the IB's own academic integrity checks are built to catch. A small group of three or four, matched for subject, level and pace, can genuinely help with regular content and past-paper practice. For any individually assessed piece of work, one-to-one guidance is the safer, and frankly the only appropriate, format.

faqs.question: Why do CBSE or JEE coaching batches often not work for IB students in Gurgaon?

CBSE, JEE and NEET coaching centres teach toward board exams and competitive tests with their own syllabus maps, marking schemes and pacing, none of which map cleanly onto the IB's criterion-based MYP marking, HL and SL split, or command-term-driven DP papers. A batch built this way can leave gaps in exactly the areas the IB actually assesses, command terms like evaluate and discuss, or the working shown in an IA. faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session is missed because of traffic or a family emergency?
faqs.answer: A missed session gets rescheduled rather than simply lost, in almost all cases, once the family lets the tutor or IB Gram know. Evening traffic on corridors like Sohna Road or Dwarka Expressway can genuinely stretch a short trip on a bad day, and school activities, buses or a sudden family matter come up too. The right response is a straightforward reschedule to another slot that week, not a penalty. faqs.question: Is one-to-one IB coaching much more expensive than a batch in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, one-to-one usually costs more than a batch, since a batch splits the tutor's time across many students. But cost per hour is not the same as value for a specific student: a batch student repeatedly stuck at the same criterion is not getting good value at any price, while a well-matched one-to-one session that closes a real gap in six weeks can be worth the higher rate. A small group of three or four often lands between the two on price while keeping some individual attention, when the group is genuinely matched on subject, level and pace. IB Gram explains pricing structure, never a fixed figure, during the first conversation.

faqs.question: Does online IB coaching really work as well as sitting with a tutor in person?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, yes, provided the connection is stable and the student can hold focus on a screen for the session length. A shared whiteboard and annotated past papers cover much of what a physical whiteboard does, and online coaching opens up specialist tutors who may not have a realistic travel route into every Gurgaon sector. Where online coaching struggles more is with younger students who need closer in-person attention, or subjects where a tutor benefits from watching handwriting and working directly. A hybrid mix, home tuition some weeks and online for the rest, often gets the best of both.

faqs.question: What should a free trial or demo class for IB coaching actually show?
faqs.answer: It should show how the tutor teaches, not just what they know. A useful trial covers a short diagnostic, a look at recent test results or a past answer marked against real IB criteria or command terms, and enough live teaching for the family to judge explanations, pacing and how the tutor responds to a wrong answer. For coaching in a small group, the trial should include the actual group the student would join, not a one-off individual demo that does not reflect the real format. If the trial does not feel right, IB Gram can offer a different tutor before any term begins.

faqs.question: How many students are usually in a small group for IB coaching, and does it actually help?
faqs.answer: Three or four students is the usual range for a small group to still function as one; beyond that it starts to behave like a batch. It helps when every student in the group shares the same subject, level and roughly the same school pace, since then hearing a peer's question or mistake genuinely reinforces the material. It stops helping the moment the group is mixed by convenience rather than by fit, a MYP student grouped with a DP student, say, because the format then inherits the same pacing problem as a full batch, just with fewer people.

faqs.question: What if my child has made no real progress after a month of IB coaching?
faqs.answer: That is worth a direct conversation within the first month, not something to wait out for a term. Ask specifically which criteria or command terms have improved and which have not, since real progress at this stage is usually visible in specific skills rather than an overall grade shift. If the format itself seems wrong, a batch that moves too fast, a small group that is not well matched, a one-to-one tutor whose teaching style does not suit the student, IB Gram can offer a different tutor or format without losing the term. contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Sets Up IB Coaching in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB coaching in Gurgaon, for the International Baccalaureate (IB), starts with a short conversation, not a sales pitch. A parent calls or sends a query, and IB Gram asks what actually matters for the match: which programme the student is in, the subject or subjects, the level, and where in Gurugram the family lives. That last detail decides more than people expect, because a tutor who teaches brilliantly in DLF Phase 1 may simply not have a free evening slot that survives the drive to Sector 84.

The process runs in five steps.
1. You send a query or book a free consultation, describing the board, programme, subject and rough schedule.
2. IB Gram asks follow-up questions about school calendar, location and preferred slot, including which sector or society you are in.
3. A shortlist of verified home tutor and online tutor profiles is drawn up, matched on subject depth, level and travel radius.
4. A demo or trial session is arranged so the student and tutor can test the fit before anyone commits.
5. If the match is wrong, the family can ask for a different tutor rather than persisting with one that is not working.

None of this promises a specific tutor count or a fixed exam result; no one can honestly promise either. What it does promise is a process that treats your corridor as a real constraint rather than an afterthought. A family near Golf Course Extension Road and a family in Manesar are not solving the same scheduling problem, even if they want the same subject taught the same way, and the shortlist reflects that from the first call.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: Which Stage Are You Coaching For?
contentBlocks.body:
IB coaching means something different depending on which programme a student is actually in, so the first useful question is not the subject but the stage. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from about age three to twelve and has no external examinations at all; learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet, through units of inquiry, ending in the PYP exhibition in the final year. Coaching here looks like support around a specific unit or a skill gap, not exam drilling, because there is no exam to drill for.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans five years, MYP 1 through MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each scored out of 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the school's grade boundaries. MYP 5 students complete the Personal Project (the Community Project sits in MYP 3 or MYP 4 instead), and some schools offer MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, though this is optional and decided school by school. An MYP tutor in Gurgaon needs to understand criterion language, not just subject content, because a well-argued answer that does not address the criterion still loses marks.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) and the rest at Standard Level (SL). Each subject is graded 1 to 7, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 extra points, taking the maximum to 45; 24 is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's own failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). A DP tutor in Gurgaon working with a family on Sohna Road or in New Gurgaon is coaching toward that structure specifically, not toward a generic school exam.

MYP runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11-16.

MYP criteria A-D each score out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade.

The DP diploma needs a minimum of 24 points, out of a maximum 45.

contentBlocks.heading: IB Subjects Gurgaon Families Ask for Coaching In Most
contentBlocks.body:
Ask what subject a family actually wants help with, and the honest answer at Diploma level is usually Mathematics. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each offered at Higher Level or Standard Level, and the two are different enough in emphasis that a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. The sciences, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, each carry a practical component alongside the theory, and coaching for these subjects has to address both, not just the content a student can recite.

English is where people mix up two different subjects. English A is a literature-based subject, close reading and comparative analysis; English B is language acquisition, built for students still developing fluency. Searching for IB coachings in Gurgaon under 'English' without checking which one a student needs will waste a term. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit outside the six subject groups but still carry real weight, up to 3 points combined, and both are marked on structured criteria that reward a specific kind of argument, not general essay-writing.

Command terms decide how deep an answer has to go: define asks for a precise statement, describe asks for detail without judgement, explain asks for reasoning, evaluate and discuss ask for a weighed argument, and to what extent asks the student to take a defensible position. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports, sourced through the school or the IB's own official channels, are where this becomes concrete. A family searching for IB coaching near me is usually really asking for a tutor who marks practice answers against these exact terms, not one who simply reteaches the textbook.

IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology, each with practical and theory components.

contentBlocks.heading: Every Gurgaon Corridor Covered, Sector by Sector
contentBlocks.body:
IB coaching in Gurgaon is not one city-wide service; it is ten different corridors, each with its own traffic pattern, society rules and travel time. Golf Course Road covers DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1 and Sectors 42, 43, 53 and 54, running through societies like DLF The Magnolias and DLF The Aralias, dense, well-connected, and usually the easiest corridor for a tutor to keep a fixed evening slot. Golf Course Extension Road, just south, covers Sectors 56 to 65 and Sushant Lok 3, including M3M Golf Estate and Ireo Grand Arch; it pairs naturally with Golf Course Road in one tutor's weekly route. Sohna Road runs long, from Sector 47 through Badshahpur, taking in Nirvana Country, South City 2, Central Park Resorts and Malibu Towne on the way; a family near Vatika Chowk is a longer drive from one near Sector 47, even though both count as 'Sohna Road'.

Closer to the centre, DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City form a dense, high-traffic corridor through Sikanderpur and Chakkarpur, while Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre sit just south of it. The Southern Peripheral Road (SPR) covers Sectors 66 to 72 and Tata Primanti, and is close enough to Golf Course Extension Road that some tutors cover both in one evening.

Further out, New Gurgaon (Sectors 82 to 90, Vatika India Next, Godrej Air) and the Dwarka Expressway (Sectors 102 to 113, Godrej Summit, Sobha City, ATS Kocoon) are newer corridors where roads are still filling in; a home tutor here needs a realistic weekday window, not an optimistic one. Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, and Manesar and NH-48 south, sit furthest from the other corridors, and online coaching is often the more honest recommendation for a fixed weekday slot from these addresses.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does The Gurgaon School Calendar Mean for Coaching Timing?
contentBlocks.body:
Families at international schools across Gurgaon, schools like Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge, deal with a calendar that does not leave much slack. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; the names are context, not an endorsement.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session, which is what most local coaching calendars are built around; November is used by a minority of schools and by students retaking a subject. May results are released in early July, which is also when many families start planning the next academic year's coaching. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and those mocks are where a coaching plan gets tested against something real rather than a textbook exercise.

Day to day, the calendar pressure is more mundane: school buses that arrive later than planned, sports or music activities on fixed evenings, homework that piles up before a unit test. A coaching slot that looked fine in September can stop working once winter sports trials start. Good coaching plans around this rather than pretending every week looks the same, asking, before the first session, which evenings are actually free for the term, and building in a buffer around pre-mock weeks when a student needs more time, not less.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Coaching, Online Coaching Or Hybrid, Which Suits Your Corridor?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's starting point for IB coaching in Gurgaon is home tutoring: a verified tutor at the family's own table, in their own sector, on a fixed weekday evening. Home tuition works because it removes the two biggest obstacles to a distracted teenager actually studying, a screen with other tabs open, and the ten minutes lost getting set up. A tutor sitting across the table can see a mistake as it happens and correct it there, which matters more for subjects like Mathematics AA HL, where a small algebra slip early in a solution invalidates everything after it.

Online coaching is not a downgrade; it is the right call for a different set of families. A student on Sohna Road near Badshahpur, or in Manesar, may simply not have a specialist tutor for a less common subject combination within a reasonable evening drive, and a live online session with shared whiteboards and annotated past papers closes that gap without the traffic. Families juggling two or three subjects across a week also find online easier to reschedule than a home visit that depends on a tutor's drive time.

Hybrid sits between the two: home sessions in term time when the corridor allows it, online during exam-week traffic spikes, festival weeks, or when a family is travelling. None of this is a fixed rule. A family in DLF Phase 3 might prefer online purely because their evenings are unpredictable, and a family in New Gurgaon might insist on home tutoring and simply accept a later slot. The honest answer to home versus online is that your corridor narrows the options; your family's evenings decide the rest.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Verifies A Tutor Before A Home Coaching Session
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor's profile reaches a shortlist for IB coaching in Gurgaon, IB Gram checks subject background and relevant teaching experience against what the family actually asked for: board, programme stage, level and subject. That is the baseline. What a parent should check themselves goes further: whether the tutor has taught this specific syllabus, AA versus AI, for instance, or MYP versus DP, which exam session their past students sat, and how they would structure the first few sessions.

A demo or trial session exists precisely so this does not stay theoretical. Watch how the tutor responds when the student gets something wrong, whether they explain the reasoning or just give the answer, and ask what the tutor plans to cover in the next two or three sessions if this one goes well. For a home tutor, it is also fair to ask practical questions: how they will confirm the appointment each week, what happens if a society's gate security asks for ID, and who at IB Gram to contact if a session is missed or the fit is not right.

No verification process, however careful, replaces this first-hand check. IB Gram's role is to narrow the field to profiles that plausibly fit; the family's role is to use the trial session properly, ask direct questions, and only then commit to a term of home tuition rather than a single session booked out of convenience.

This matters more for a home tutor than for most other services, because the relationship runs inside your home for months, not a single visit. Ask early who at IB Gram to contact if a session is missed, if the tutor is running late because of Gurgaon traffic, or if the family simply wants to pause for an exam-week break. A tutor who is comfortable answering these questions plainly, without vague reassurance, is usually a better sign than a long list of claimed qualifications.
items: Profiles are checked for subject background and board-specific teaching experience.
A demo or trial session lets the family assess fit before committing.
Parents should ask which syllabus, level and exam session the tutor has taught.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Gurgaon Corridors Pair Well In One Tutor's Route?
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor's week has a fixed number of evenings, and IB coaching works best when a family's corridor lets a tutor keep two or three students on one realistic route rather than crossing the city between each session. Golf Course Road and Golf Course Extension Road are the clearest pair: DLF Phase 5 to Sector 58, for instance, is a route a tutor can reasonably run twice in one evening without losing the whole gap between sessions to traffic. Southern Peripheral Road extends that same logic further south, toward Sector 66 to 70, and often sits on the same tutor's route as Golf Course Extension Road rather than as a separate trip.

Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre sit close to DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City, a dense, signal-heavy stretch where distance on a map understates the actual drive time, but where a tutor already working that corridor can often add a second family without much extra travel.

Further out, the logic changes. New Gurgaon and the Dwarka Expressway are near each other but a genuine trip from the older parts of the city, so a tutor serving DLF Phase 1 is unlikely to also cover Sector 106 on a weekday evening. Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar sit on their own, closer to the older city than to any of the newer corridors. Manesar and NH-48 south rarely pair naturally with anything; a family there is often better served either by a tutor who lives locally or by online coaching for weekday evenings, with home sessions kept for weekends when the drive is less of a constraint.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress In IB Coaching Gurgaon Should Look Like By Month Two?
contentBlocks.body:
Two months into a coaching relationship, a family should be able to point to something concrete, not just a feeling that things are 'going fine'. The slot itself should be stable, same evening, same time, rarely rearranged, because a coaching relationship that keeps moving around the calendar rarely gets deep enough to help before an assessment. The student should be able to describe, in their own words, what the last session covered and what homework came out of it; if they cannot, the sessions are not sticking.

Progress at this stage looks like fewer repeated errors in practice work, not a jump in marks. A DP1 student working on Mathematics AA HL might still be getting questions wrong in month two, but the mistakes should be different mistakes each time, evidence that earlier gaps are closing. An MYP student should be able to point to specific criteria (B or C, say) where their own answers are getting closer to what the mark scheme actually rewards, not just producing more writing.

No tutor, however good, can promise a specific exam outcome or a fixed improvement; anyone who does is telling you what you want to hear, not what is true. What a family can reasonably expect is a stable slot, visible engagement, and a tutor who can explain, specifically, where the student still struggles. If none of that is true by the end of month two, that is the moment to ask for a different match, not to wait through another term hoping it turns around on its own.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started: Your First Home Coaching Session
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started with IB coaching in Gurgaon takes one query or a free consultation call. Have a few things ready before that call: the student's current programme stage and level, the subject or subjects you want help with, any recent test or mock papers that show where things stand, and which weekday evenings are actually free once school, buses and activities are accounted for.

Mention your sector or society early. It changes what IB Gram can realistically offer. A family in a Golf Course Road society with straightforward visitor access is a different scheduling problem from a family in a newer Dwarka Expressway society still finishing its access roads, and being upfront about it means the first shortlist is closer to workable.

The first session, whether it is a demo or the actual opening lesson, should include a short diagnostic, a few questions or a practice problem pitched at the right level, so the tutor is not guessing where the student stands. Ask what the trial covers before it starts, and agree with yourself beforehand what would make you say yes: a tutor who explains clearly, a student who is more willing to ask questions, a plan for the next few weeks that makes sense given the school calendar. If a home tutor is not the right fit after the trial, you can ask IB Gram for a different match; lessons can run at home, online or hybrid depending on what actually works for your corridor and your evenings.

Note down which weekday evenings are genuinely free, not just theoretically free.

faqs.question: Does IB coaching in Gurgaon cover every sector, or only areas like DLF and Golf Course Road?
faqs.answer: It covers all ten corridors, not just the well-known ones. IB Gram matches families for IB coaching in Gurgaon from Golf Course Road and DLF Phase 1 through to Sohna Road, New Gurgaon, the Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon and Manesar. What changes by corridor is not whether coaching is available, but which format makes most sense: a home tutor is often practical in denser, central corridors, while families further out on Sohna Road near Badshahpur or in Manesar frequently find online coaching a more reliable weekday option, with home sessions kept for weekends.

faqs.question: How does traffic on Golf Course Extension Road affect an evening coaching slot?
faqs.answer: It can turn a short distance into a long wait, especially around peak office hours. A tutor travelling into Golf Course Extension Road, covering Sectors 56 to 65 and Sushant Lok 3, needs a slot with some buffer built in rather than one booked back-to-back with another family across town. IB Gram accounts for this when matching a home tutor to your corridor, and if evening traffic makes a consistent slot unreliable, online coaching is usually the more honest recommendation than a home visit that keeps arriving late.

faqs.question: Can one tutor realistically cover both Sushant Lok and DLF Phase 2 in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, because the two sit close together on the same dense stretch near MG Road and Cyber City. A tutor already working Sushant Lok 1 or 2 can frequently add a second family in DLF Phase 2, Phase 3 or Phase 4 without a major detour, though signal-heavy traffic there means the actual drive time is usually longer than the map distance suggests. IB Gram factors this route logic into matching, so two families on a shared corridor are more likely to land the same tutor than two families on opposite sides of the city.

faqs.question: Is IB coaching available for families in New Gurgaon and along the Dwarka Expressway?
faqs.answer: Yes, though these are newer corridors where the road network is still filling in, so travel time can run longer than the distance alone suggests. New Gurgaon covers Sectors 82 to 90 and societies like Vatika India Next and Godrej Air; the Dwarka Expressway covers Sectors 102 to 113 and societies like Godrej Summit and Sobha City. A home tutor can reach both, but families here often benefit from a realistic weekday window agreed upfront, or a hybrid arrangement that leans on online sessions during the week and home sessions at weekends.

faqs.question: How does gate entry at a Gurgaon society affect a home coaching session?
faqs.answer: Most societies require visitor registration at the gate, and a first-time tutor should expect to show ID and be logged before entering. This adds a few minutes to the start of a session, which is worth accounting for when you agree a slot, especially in gated societies along Golf Course Road or Golf Course Extension Road with stricter security desks. Letting the gate know in advance that a tutor is expected each week, where the society allows it, usually smooths this out after the first visit.

faqs.question: What happens if a home coaching session is missed because of traffic or a school activity?
faqs.answer: The family and tutor agree directly on rescheduling, since a missed session is common enough in Gurgaon's traffic and packed school calendars that it should not derail the whole term. IB Gram's role is to help you find a workable regular slot in the first place, factoring in school buses and activities, so missed sessions stay occasional rather than routine. If a particular corridor or time keeps causing clashes, that is worth raising early, since a different slot or a shift to online for that week is usually a simple fix.

faqs.question: Is online IB coaching better than home coaching for families on Sohna Road or in Manesar?
faqs.answer: For a reliable weekday evening slot, often yes. Sohna Road stretches a long way, from Sector 47 to Badshahpur, and Manesar sits furthest from the rest of Gurgaon's corridors, so a home tutor's travel time can eat into the actual teaching time or make a fixed weekly slot hard to guarantee. Online coaching removes that variable entirely and widens the pool of subject specialists available to you. Many families in these corridors choose a hybrid pattern instead: online on weekdays, with a home session at the weekend when travel is less of a constraint.

faqs.question: My child is switching from CBSE mid-year; can IB coaching in Gurgaon start straight away?
faqs.answer: Yes, a query can be sent at any point in the year, and the first conversation is exactly where a board switch like this gets discussed. IB Gram asks about the student's previous board, current programme stage and school's pacing, then shortlists tutors who can work with a student joining partway through a unit rather than at the start of one. The demo session is particularly useful here, since it shows quickly how much catching up is realistic in a term versus what needs more time.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does IB coaching in Gurgaon usually run?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student's level, the subject and how close the exam session is, so there is no single number that fits every family. A DP2 student approaching May exams typically needs more sessions than a PYP student working on a single unit of inquiry. What matters more than a fixed count is consistency: a slot that runs on the same evenings most weeks, adjusted up around mocks and down once a topic is settled, tends to work better than an irregular, high-frequency burst booked only when a test is close.

faqs.question: What does the free trial or demo session cover?
faqs.answer: It covers a short diagnostic conversation and a small piece of subject work, pitched at the student's actual level, so both sides can judge the fit before committing to a term. Expect the tutor to ask about the syllabus, recent test results and where the student feels stuck, then work through a problem or a passage together. It is a genuine two-way check: the family gets to see how the tutor explains things, and the tutor gets a first read on what the student actually needs.

faqs.question: How soon can a home tutor start after we send a query?
faqs.answer: It depends on subject and level availability in your corridor, so IB Gram cannot promise a fixed number of days, but the process starts as soon as you send a query or book a consultation. IB Gram asks about board, programme, subject, location and schedule, shortlists home tutor and online tutor profiles that fit and have availability, and arranges a trial session, all subject to tutor availability for that subject and slot. A family with a common combination, like DP Mathematics AA SL, usually sees a shortlist faster than one needing a rarer subject at a specific level.

h1: IB Classes in Gurgaon: A Term Planned Week by Week
heroTitle: Planning IB Classes in Gurgaon, Week by Week
heroSubtitle: An IB class in Gurgaon is not a single fixed timetable; frequency changes by programme stage, rises before mocks, and falls after report cards. This page sets out what a realistic weekly plan looks like at each stage, and how holidays and revision weeks fit around it without wasting either.
introSummary: IB classes in Gurgaon work best as a home-based weekly rhythm that changes with the calendar, not a fixed slot booked once and left alone. Most families start with home tuition, a tutor coming to the flat or society once or twice a week, because a consistent in-person routine is easier to hold through a demanding school term than a session that has to be logged into separately each time. This page lays out how many classes a week make sense at each stage of the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes, how a class year actually moves month by month around school breaks and mocks, what a trial class should cover, and when holiday or pre-mock revision classes genuinely earn their place instead of adding pressure for no reason.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds Your Child's Weekly Home Class Plan in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A weekly class plan for IB classes in Gurgaon should never be copied from another family's timetable, because the right frequency depends on stage, subject load and how close the next real deadline sits. When a query comes in, IB Gram asks for the programme stage first, PYP, MYP or DP, since a Grade 3 PYP learner and a DP2 student six weeks from mocks need entirely different weekly rhythms, not a scaled-down version of the same plan.

We then ask about the school's own calendar: recent test results, when the next reporting period falls, and for DP2 families specifically, the school's own mock examination date, since that single date reshapes everything in the weeks before it. A subject where a student is comfortably on pace might need one class a week; a Higher Level subject with a shaky internal assessment might justify two, at least until the immediate pressure passes. Most requests are for home classes specifically, a tutor coming to the flat each week, and IB Gram treats that as the default unless told otherwise.

From there we propose a starting frequency with the reasoning attached, not just a number, so a parent understands why twice weekly makes sense now and once weekly might be enough later. A free trial class follows to confirm the pace actually suits the student before a regular slot is booked for the term.

The plan is not fixed once agreed. IB Gram expects frequency to move as the calendar moves: stepping up before a mock or an exam session, and stepping back down once the immediate pressure passes, so a student is not sitting through unnecessary sessions in a quiet month just because that is what was booked in August.
items: 1. Tell us the programme stage, subjects and current weekly load, plus your sector in Gurgaon.
2. We ask about the school's term dates, recent test results, and upcoming mocks or deadlines.
3. We propose a starting frequency, for example twice weekly for a DP subject nearing mocks, with reasons.
4. A free trial class confirms pace before a regular weekly slot is locked in.
5. The plan is reviewed every few weeks and adjusted as the school calendar moves, not fixed for the year.

contentBlocks.heading: Weekly Class Frequency by IB Stage: PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
There is no single correct number of IB classes a week, but there are reasonable ranges, and a class plan should say why a particular number was chosen. In the Primary Years Programme, ages 3 to 12, there are no external examinations at all, and learning moves through units of inquiry at the school's own pace; one class a week is usually enough here, mainly to reinforce concepts and build the habits, curiosity and structured thinking, that later stages will need.

The Middle Years Programme, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, usually needs one to two classes a week per subject where support is wanted, since every subject is scored against four criteria out of 8 each, and building fluency in how those criteria are applied takes repetition. Frequency tends to rise around the Personal Project in MYP 5, or the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, since these run on their own timeline outside normal subject teaching.

DP1 students, in their first Diploma Programme year, generally do well on one to two classes a week per subject, enough to build steady habits across six subjects, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours and the rest at Standard Level with 150, without overloading an already demanding timetable. DP2 is where frequency often needs to rise, sometimes to two or three classes a week for a Higher Level subject, as the May session and the school's own mock examinations approach.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay run on a different rhythm entirely: fortnightly sessions usually suit better than weekly ones, since progress here is measured in drafts and structured argument rather than syllabus content covered, and cramming this into a weekly slot rarely produces better work, only more anxious deadlines.
items: PYP (ages 3-12): often one class a week is enough, since there are no external exams and learning follows units of inquiry at school pace.
MYP (MYP 1-5): typically one to two classes a week per subject needing support, rising around Personal Project or Community Project deadlines.
DP1: generally one to two classes a week per subject, building steady habits across six subjects before the pace increases in DP2.
DP2: often two to three classes a week per Higher Level subject as the May session approaches, tapering for Standard Level subjects on track.
TOK and the Extended Essay: usually fortnightly sessions rather than weekly, since progress here is paced by drafts, not syllabus content.

contentBlocks.heading: What IB Classes Cover Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
A class booked simply as "IB Maths" can go wrong immediately, because Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses with different papers and a different balance of pure theory against real-world modelling. Getting this wrong at the start of DP1 wastes weeks before anyone notices the class content does not match what the school is actually examining.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology at Higher or Standard Level share a similar structure: syllabus content taught week to week, alongside an internal assessment exploration that is marked against the IB's own criteria rather than a single overall score. A weekly class in these subjects should split time between covering new content and developing the exploration, since leaving exploration work to the final term almost always produces weaker internal assessment grades than starting it earlier and revising through several drafts.

English A and B classes look different again. English A rewards literary analysis and close reading, often building toward an oral commentary; English B, for students studying it as an additional language, rewards structured written and spoken responses to a range of text types. Command terms, describe, analyse, evaluate, set the depth every answer needs, and a class that ignores this and simply builds vocabulary misses where marks are actually awarded.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay classes are the odd ones out on a weekly timetable, because progress here is not measured by syllabus coverage. A useful class reviews a draft, questions the argument's structure, and checks citations, rather than teaching new content each week, and families who expect the same rhythm as a Physics class are often disappointed by how slowly this work visibly progresses, even when it is going well.

contentBlocks.heading: IB Classes Across Sohna Road, DLF and Sushant Lok in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:

contentBlocks.heading: Fitting IB Classes Around the Gurgaon School Calendar
contentBlocks.body:
Families at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge build their weekly class plan around a school year that runs on its own rhythm. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, or with the International Baccalaureate; these names describe the calendar pressures families deal with generally, not a claim about any one school's curriculum.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session, with a much smaller number using November, usually for retake candidates. Term generally opens in late July or early August, giving roughly ten to twelve weeks before the first serious reporting point, and a class plan that starts strong in this window tends to hold up better than one that starts reactively after a first disappointing test.

Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination date independently, usually several months before May, and this date should shape class frequency directly: stepping up in the run-up, then easing slightly once mocks are done and genuine gaps are clearer. Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports, available through the school or the IB's official channels, show exactly how marks are awarded, and a class that works from these directly, rather than generic practice questions, tends to close gaps faster.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, should be ordinary vocabulary inside a weekly class from the start of the year, not something introduced for the first time during exam-week revision.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Classes, Online or Hybrid: What Works for a Weekly IB Schedule?
contentBlocks.body:
Home classes remain the easiest format to turn into an actual weekly habit, particularly for younger students in the Primary Years or early Middle Years Programme, because there is no separate step of logging in, and a tutor physically present tends to hold a distracted ten-year-old's attention more reliably than a screen does. For a family building a new weekly routine from nothing, this matters more than it sounds like it should.

Online classes earn their place once revision becomes more paper-based than content-based, which tends to happen from DP1 onward. Annotating a past IB Physics paper, marking up a Maths exploration draft, or reviewing an English commentary line by line all work well on a shared screen, and online classes also make a scarce Higher Level specialist available to a family regardless of where in Gurgaon they live.

Stated plainly: home classes win for younger students and for building a habit that survives a demanding school week; online classes win for exam-focused revision and for reaching a specific specialist. Hybrid weeks mix home classes and online classes across the same week, common for families in longer corridors like Sohna Road or further reaches of DLF Phase 2 to 4, where a tutor cannot realistically manage two home visits without the second one running very late.

What matters most in the early months, more than the format itself, is consistency. A student who has the same class at the same time each week, whatever the format, tends to build the habit faster than one whose schedule shifts constantly to chase convenience.
items: Home classes: a tutor at your table each week, easiest to hold as a habit for younger PYP and MYP students.
Online classes: a shared whiteboard for past papers and worked examples, useful for DP revision and scarce Higher Level specialists.
Hybrid weeks mix home classes and online classes across the week, common for families in corridors like Sohna Road with longer travel.
A consistent weekly slot, whichever format, matters more for habit-building than the format itself in the early months.

contentBlocks.heading: How Are IB Class Tutors in Gurgaon Verified?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram checks a tutor's board and stage experience before any profile reaches a family, so a class booked for MYP Criterion-based marking is not handled by someone whose only real experience is CBSE content teaching. This applies the same way whether a family is asking for a home tutor or an online specialist; references are checked where they are available, and a tutor's claimed history with a specific stage or subject needs to hold up before their profile is shortlisted.

Beyond this, a useful question for parents to ask directly is how a tutor structures an ordinary weekly class, not an exam-week special, but a normal Tuesday. A tutor with real experience describes a rough shape: reviewing the previous week's homework, covering new content or practising past questions, setting the next task, because that is genuinely how their weeks run. A tutor without this experience tends to describe classes more vaguely, in terms of general improvement rather than a working rhythm.

It is also worth asking whether a tutor has run weekly classes through an entire mock cycle or exam session before, start to finish, since pacing frequency correctly around that pressure point is a skill in itself, not something that follows automatically from strong subject knowledge.

The trial class remains the clearest check available. Watch how the tutor uses a full sixty minutes: do they diagnose first or launch straight into teaching? Do they check understanding before moving on? A well-paced trial is usually a reliable preview of what a full term of weekly classes will actually look like.

contentBlocks.heading: A Month-by-Month Look at an IB Class Year in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
An IB class year in Gurgaon rarely moves at a constant pace, and a weekly plan that ignores this usually either wastes a quiet month or under-supports a demanding one. August and September, right after most schools open for the year, suit diagnostic classes and routine-building: light homework, a steady weekly slot, and time for the tutor to understand exactly where a student stands before the term's real pressure builds.

October brings a short pause around Dussehra for most Gurgaon schools, and this is where holiday classes earn their place cautiously: a light catch-up session can hold momentum through the break without turning a holiday into another obligation, but a full class load through a break a student is meant to be resting during usually backfires, producing resentment rather than progress.

November into December is typically when unit tests and reports cluster, and class frequency often needs to rise slightly to match what the school itself is demanding that term. January through March tends to settle into a steadier rhythm, though for DP2 families this is often when the school confirms its own mock examination date, and that confirmation should trigger a review of whether current frequency is still right.

April and May are where revision genuinely intensifies for exam-year students, DP2 finals and, for some schools, MYP eAssessment, and this is the period where a step up to two or three classes a week for a Higher Level subject is usually justified rather than excessive. Younger PYP and MYP students, without external exams pressing on them, generally continue at their normal frequency through this window; there is little reason to intensify a Grade 5 student's class load simply because an older sibling's exams are approaching.

Summer holidays are a genuine pause for most students, and IB Gram does not encourage classes purely to fill the break. The one exception worth considering is a short catch-up block for a student moving from DP1 into DP2, where a few sessions reviewing the first year's weaker subjects can make September noticeably less overwhelming.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should a Trial IB Class Show Before You Commit?
contentBlocks.body:
A trial class for IB classes in Gurgaon should feel like a genuine first session of a real weekly plan, not a polished demonstration designed purely to impress. Within the first ten minutes, a good tutor is asking questions, about recent school work, about what feels hardest right now, rather than launching straight into a prepared lesson that ignores where the student actually stands.

Pace matters as much as content. Watch whether the tutor adjusts when your child clearly understands something already, moving on rather than over-explaining, and equally whether they slow down properly when a concept genuinely has not landed. A tutor who runs the same fixed pace regardless of the student in front of them is not yet adapting to this specific child, whatever their general experience.

By the end of a good trial, a tutor should be able to sketch, even roughly, what the next few weeks might look like: perhaps a fortnight consolidating a weak topic before moving to new content, or two classes a week until a specific test has passed and then a step back to one. This forward view is a stronger signal of genuine planning ability than how polished the single trial session felt. A trial also shows whether home classes suit your child better than the alternative formats, or the reverse.

No tutor can promise a particular grade at the end of this, and any tutor who does should be treated with real caution. What a trial reasonably shows is fit, pace and a sensible starting plan, and if any of these three feel off, telling IB Gram directly gets a different tutor arranged before a full term is booked around the wrong match.
items: The tutor should diagnose before teaching: a quick review of recent work before launching into new content.
The pace should suit your child specifically, neither rushing ahead nor over-explaining what is already understood.
The tutor should be able to sketch a rough plan for the coming weeks, not just this one session.
By the end of the trial, you should know roughly how many classes a week this tutor recommends, and why.
No tutor can guarantee a grade; a trial shows fit and approach, not a finished result.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB Classes: What to Prepare Before Week One
contentBlocks.body:
Starting IB classes in Gurgaon well mostly comes down to giving the first session enough to work with. Have the programme stage and subject combination ready, PYP, MYP with the relevant subject groups, or DP with the exact Higher Level and Standard Level split, since this shapes which tutors even make sense for the shortlist. Bring a recent report card, a marked test, or a piece of homework so the first class can diagnose properly instead of guessing where to begin.

Confirm your sector in Gurgaon and which weekday evenings genuinely work, factoring in school buses, activities and typical traffic for your corridor, so the weekly slot agreed in week one is one that can actually hold through a full term rather than collapsing after a fortnight. Decide whether you want home classes, online classes or a hybrid mix before the trial, though this often changes once you see how each format actually feels with your child.

Agree a starting frequency with the tutor and understand it as a starting point, not a fixed commitment for the year. A subject under real pressure now may need two classes a week initially and settle to one once the immediate gap closes, and a class plan that cannot flex with the calendar is usually the wrong plan.

Give the arrangement a genuine few weeks before judging it. A single class, however good or ordinary it felt, rarely tells you as much as three or four weeks of an actual weekly rhythm does, and IB Gram would rather you wait for that fuller picture than react to one early impression.

Bring a recent report card or test paper so the first class starts with a real diagnostic, not a guess.
Confirm your sector in Gurgaon and preferred weekday evenings so a realistic weekly slot can be held.

faqs.question: How many IB classes a week does my child actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the stage and how close the next real deadline is, not a fixed number that applies to everyone. A Primary Years Programme student usually manages well on one class a week, an MYP or DP1 student often needs one to two per subject, and a DP2 student approaching mocks or the May session may need two to three for a Higher Level subject under pressure. IB Gram proposes a starting frequency for home classes with reasons attached during the first conversation, and reviews it every few weeks rather than fixing it for the whole year.

faqs.question: What happens to weekly classes during school holidays?
faqs.answer: Most students get a genuine break, and IB Gram does not push classes purely to fill a holiday. Around shorter breaks like Dussehra, a light catch-up session can hold momentum without turning the break into another obligation, and for longer holidays, particularly summer, a short revision block is usually only suggested for a student moving between major stages, such as DP1 into DP2, where reviewing weaker subjects makes the coming term noticeably easier. Otherwise, the weekly rhythm simply resumes when school does.

faqs.question: Do classes increase automatically before mock exams?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but frequency usually should rise, and a good tutor explains why rather than just adding sessions. As a DP2 student's school-set mock date approaches, a Higher Level subject under pressure might move from one class a week to two or three, while a Standard Level subject already on track may stay where it is. IB Gram expects this kind of reasoned adjustment as part of an ongoing plan, and a parent should always be told the reason behind a change in frequency, not just informed that it is happening.

faqs.question: What does a trial IB class actually cover?
faqs.answer: A trial class is a genuine diagnostic session, not a polished demonstration. The tutor reviews recent school work, asks what feels hardest right now, and works through a short piece of content or a past question so you can see the pace and teaching style directly. By the end, the tutor should be able to sketch roughly what the following weeks might look like and recommend a starting frequency with reasons. It usually runs the same length as a normal class, and there is no obligation to continue afterward.

faqs.question: Can we start with one class a week and add more later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and starting lighter is often the more sensible choice, particularly if you are not yet sure how much support your child needs. IB Gram would rather begin with one class a week and adjust upward once a genuine gap becomes clear than start heavy and have a family feel the schedule is excessive. Moving from one class to two, or the reverse, simply requires telling us directly, and the tutor's availability is checked before any change is confirmed.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor reliably reach Sohna Road or DLF Phase 3 on weekday evenings given traffic?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, though a home tutor covering longer corridors like Sohna Road or the busier DLF Phase 2 to 4 stretch near Cyber City builds some buffer time into a weekday evening slot precisely because traffic here is unpredictable. Most tutors will message ahead if they expect to run a few minutes late for a home visit, and IB Gram treats a genuine pattern of lateness as worth addressing directly rather than something a family should simply tolerate. Occasional delays tied to evening traffic are normal across most of Gurgaon.

faqs.question: What happens if a home class is missed because of a school activity or illness?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram or the tutor as early as possible, and most home classes can be rescheduled within the same week where the tutor's other commitments and travel allow it. A single missed session is rarely a problem, but a pattern of missed home visits is worth flagging, since it usually means the weekly slot itself needs to move rather than the same clash repeating every few weeks. Consistency matters more for exam-year students than for a younger child in an earlier stage of the programme.

faqs.question: How is a weekly class different from ad-hoc tutoring booked session by session?
faqs.answer: A weekly class follows an ongoing plan the tutor adjusts as the term moves, homework between sessions, a rough map of the coming weeks, frequency that rises and falls with the calendar, while ad-hoc tutoring is usually reactive, booked only when a problem has already appeared. Weekly classes tend to catch gaps earlier, before a test result forces the issue, and build a working relationship between tutor and student that a one-off session cannot. Ad-hoc sessions still have their place, particularly for a single urgent gap before a specific test.

faqs.question: Do TOK and Extended Essay classes follow the same weekly pattern as subject classes?
faqs.answer: No, and expecting them to usually leads to disappointment. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay classes tend to work better fortnightly than weekly, since progress is measured in drafts and argument structure rather than syllabus content covered each session, and cramming this into a weekly slot mostly produces rushed drafts rather than better ones. A class reviewing an Extended Essay draft, questioning its structure and checking citations, needs time between sessions for the student to actually redraft, which a weekly rhythm does not allow.

faqs.question: How does the class plan change between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1 generally suits a steadier one to two classes a week per subject, building habits across six subjects without overloading an already demanding first year. DP2 is usually where frequency needs to rise, sometimes to two or three classes a week for a Higher Level subject, as the school's own mock examination date and the May session approach. A short catch-up block over the summer between the two years, reviewing DP1's weaker subjects, often makes the jump into DP2 considerably less overwhelming.

faqs.question: Can classes be held online in Sushant Lok if travel is difficult some weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families in Sushant Lok and South City 1 use exactly this kind of flexibility, keeping a home class as the default and switching to online for a specific week when travel genuinely will not work. Because this corridor sits fairly centrally, most tutors already covering it can move a session online without disrupting the weekly plan much, and switching back to home the following week is straightforward. Tell the tutor or IB Gram as early as you can so the change does not feel last-minute.

faqs.question: How soon can weekly IB classes start after we send a query?
faqs.answer: Often within a few days, subject to tutor availability for the exact stage, subject and level you need. A widely taught MYP subject usually has a wider pool of tutors available quickly than a scarce Higher Level DP subject, so timing can vary by request. IB Gram will tell you honestly if a particular subject or level will take longer to match rather than starting your child with an unsuitable tutor just to fill the first week.

IB Gram treats the weekday evening window and the travel route as part of the fit, not an afterthought fixed later.

Matching is always subject to tutor availability in your corridor and depends on level and schedule, and a family can ask for a different tutor if the first one is not the right fit. contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: The IB Programme Stages Behind Every Gurgaon Classroom
contentBlocks.body:
International Baccalaureate (IB) classes in Gurgaon, or Gurugram, span three programmes, and what a class looks like changes completely between them. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP), for children roughly three to twelve, learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, including 'How we express ourselves' and 'How the world works', through units of inquiry rather than separate subject periods. There are no external examinations in the PYP; the final year builds toward the PYP exhibition, and a home tutor's job here is usually to support the inquiry itself rather than drill content.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A through D, each scored out of eight; the criterion total out of thirty-two converts to a final grade of one to seven through the IB's own grade boundaries. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project, while the Community Project sits in MYP 3 or 4 instead, and some schools also offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides for itself. A tutor helping with MYP classes in Gurgaon needs to know which criteria a piece of work is actually being judged against, not just whether the answer is right.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year stretch, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded one to seven, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to three further points, so the maximum score is forty-five; twenty-four is the minimum for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon working across HL and SL subjects, or an MYP tutor in Gurgaon handling criterion-based marking, needs a different kind of preparation from a tutor who only teaches CBSE or ICSE.
