contentBlocks.heading: What Separates a DP Specialist From a General Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
The honest answer is depth in a small number of specific places, not overall knowledge of "IB". A DP specialist knows the difference between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation before a student even asks, knows that an HL Biology option adds an entire extra unit an SL student never sees, and knows that a Paper 2 essay in English A is marked against different criteria than a Paper 1 commentary. A general tutor, even a strong one in CBSE or ICSE, usually needs weeks to build this picture; a DP specialist starts with it already in place.

Questions worth asking before a trial lesson: which specific DP subjects and levels has this tutor taught recently, do they know the difference between the two Mathematics routes, have they supervised Extended Essay work in that subject, and are they comfortable marking against real IB criteria rather than a generic percentage scale. Questions worth asking after the trial: did the tutor identify a specific gap, not a vague "needs to work harder", did they reference an actual command term or criterion, and did the pace suit the student rather than the tutor's own comfort with the material.

A numbered way to think about the first four weeks: week one is diagnostic, working through recent past paper answers to see exactly where marks are being lost against the command terms; week two starts closing the most costly gap first, usually exam technique rather than content; week three adds a second, smaller gap once the first is stable; week four should produce one worked past paper answer, self-marked against the actual scheme, that is visibly better than the diagnostic one. If a family cannot see a specific, describable difference by week four, that is worth raising directly with IB Gram rather than waiting it out quietly.

None of this promises a grade. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a family searching for IB DP tuition Gurgaon should be sceptical of anyone who implies otherwise. What a specialist can promise is that time spent in a session goes toward the actual gap, not a generic revision session that would help any student in any subject equally.

contentBlocks.heading: What Real DP Progress Looks Like, and Where It Has Limits
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in DP tuition rarely looks like a jump from a 4 to a 7 in a month, and a family should be wary of anyone who suggests it will. What it should look like: a student who can identify what a command term is actually asking for before they start writing, fewer marks lost to structure rather than content, and a growing ability to self-mark a past paper answer against the real scheme without a tutor pointing out every error along the way.

For a subject like TOK or the Extended Essay, progress looks different again, a research question that gets narrower and more answerable over several drafts, not one that gets more ambitious. A tutor who keeps pushing a student toward a bigger, more impressive-sounding EE topic is usually making the essay harder to score well, not easier; a 4,000-word paper answers one specific question in depth, and a specialist should say so plainly even when a student wants to be more ambitious about the scope.

There are real limits, and a good tutor names them rather than hiding them. Starting IB DP tuition six weeks before May with a subject that has been neglected all year narrows what is realistically achievable, and a specialist will say this directly rather than promising a turnaround that cannot happen in the time left. Equally, a tutor cannot fix a school-side issue, a mismatch between a student's chosen level and their actual ability, for instance, and the honest response there is a conversation with the school, not more tuition hours.

Golf Course Road and DLF traffic behave differently at 5pm than at 7pm, so a tutor already working near Sushant Lok is a better fit for an evening slot in that corridor than one crossing the city from Manesar. Fit is not only about subject knowledge; it is about whether the arrangement survives a real week, including school runs, activities and dinner.

This is where families see how a tutor explains a Paper 1 command term or works through an Extended Essay outline, in the actual room where lessons will happen. If the pace, manner or subject depth is not right, IB Gram arranges a different match; there is no obligation to continue with a tutor who is not working. Once a family confirms, the steps below show the full sequence, and sessions are scheduled around school hours, mock exams and the household's own evening routine, not a fixed template.

contentBlocks.heading: What the IB Diploma Programme actually asks of a DP1 or DP2 student
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme is a two-year commitment, split into DP1 and DP2, built around six subjects rather than the narrower subject list most Gurgaon parents remember from their own schooling. Three or four subjects are taken at Higher Level, which the International Baccalaureate (IB) recommends around 240 teaching hours for, and the rest at Standard Level, recommended at around 150 hours. That HL and SL split is the first decision a family and school make together, usually before DP1 begins, and an IB DP HL tutor in Gurugram needs to know which subjects sit where before a single lesson is planned.

Each of the six subjects is graded on a scale of 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sit outside the six subjects but still matter for the final score: together they can add up to 3 further points, taking the maximum possible score to 45. The diploma itself requires a minimum of 24 points, subject to the IB's own failing conditions around individual grades and the TOK and EE combination, so one strong Higher Level subject cannot fully cover for a subject that has fallen badly behind.

Alongside the six subjects, Creativity, Activity, Service, usually shortened to CAS, runs through both years and has to be completed for the diploma to be awarded at all, even if every subject grade is strong. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter their DP2 cohort for the May exam session; a minority use November, largely for students who are retaking a subject. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, typically several months ahead of May, and those mocks are usually the point where a family first realises a subject needs an IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon rather than more revision alone at home.

contentBlocks.heading: IB DP subjects: HL and SL, TOK and the Extended Essay
contentBlocks.body:
IB DP Mathematics is usually where a family first calls for a specialist rather than a general tutor. The Analysis and Approaches route suits a student heading toward proof-based work, while Applications and Interpretation leans toward modelling and technology; both are offered at HL and SL, and a tutor working on Maths needs to know which route the student is on before touching a past paper, because the two syllabuses reward different working. Command terms across every DP subject, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, set how much depth an answer needs, and a student who writes a 'describe' answer at 'evaluate' depth is not rewarded for the extra effort.

Theory of Knowledge has two separate assessments that a lot of DP1 students underestimate. The exhibition links three objects to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts, runs to no more than 950 words, is internally assessed, and counts for a third of the TOK grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for that specific exam session, runs to 1,600 words, is externally assessed, and carries the other two thirds. The course itself moves through a core theme of knowledge and the knower, two of five optional themes the student and teacher choose between, and five areas of knowledge spanning history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts.

The Extended Essay sits alongside TOK as the other point of failure worth taking seriously early. Both are graded on an A to E scale and combine for up to 3 of the diploma's 45 points, which sounds small until a family realises an E in either TOK or the EE is, on its own, a failing condition, regardless of how strong the six subjects are. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's own official channels, and reading a markscheme alongside an essay draft is often the single most useful hour an IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon spends with a DP2 student before mocks.

TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles released for that exam session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed, two thirds of the grade.
The Extended Essay and TOK are graded A-E and combine for up to 3 diploma points; an E in either is a failing condition.

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars and DP deadlines in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Families with children at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge deal with a calendar built around internal deadlines long before the May exam session arrives. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; these names are given only as local context for the calendar pressures Gurgaon families recognise.

DP2 mock examinations are set by each school individually, usually several months ahead of May, and they tend to be the first moment a gap in a Higher Level subject becomes impossible to ignore. Extended Essay and TOK deadlines, along with internal assessment submission dates, are staggered through both years rather than landing all at once, which means a DP1 student's calendar can look deceptively light in October and suddenly heavy in February. An IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon who has seen a few of these calendars before can help a family plan backward from the mocks instead of reacting to them late.

Winter break and the festival calendar compress the weeks on either side into something tighter than they look on paper; a break either side of Diwali or the winter holidays often eats into revision time a family assumed was still available. CAS evidence and reflections run on their own schedule too, separate from subject deadlines, and it is easy for a DP2 student under exam pressure to let CAS slide until a school reminder forces a rush. None of this is unique to any one school; it is simply what a two-year diploma with six subjects, TOK, the EE and CAS running in parallel looks like from the inside.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tutor, online or hybrid: what suits IB DP best?
contentBlocks.body:
For an IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon, home tuition is the starting point IB Gram builds around: a verified tutor at your dining table or study desk, working through past papers in the room where the student will actually sit their mocks. It suits Mathematics and the sciences particularly well, where a tutor can watch how a student sets out working in real time and correct a method error before it becomes a habit, and it suits students who focus better away from a laptop screen after a full school day already spent on one.

A family searching for an IB DP online tutor in Gurgaon is often really asking about flexibility, not rejecting home visits outright. Online lessons are the better call when the subject specialist a family wants is not based in the family's own corridor, or when the only free slot is a late one after sports practice and dinner, since a tutor joining by video is not crossing Gurgaon traffic to make it. Shared whiteboards and annotated past papers work well on screen for Maths and the sciences too; what suits a screen less well is the kind of long TOK or Extended Essay discussion that benefits from sitting across a table with a printed draft between two people.

Hybrid keeps a regular home slot each week for steady subject work and adds an online session before a mock or a deadline, without asking the tutor to double their travel across the city that week. It is a reasonable middle path for a family in a further-out corridor like Manesar or the Dwarka Expressway, where a weekly home visit is realistic but a second session in the same week is not. The honest answer, in short: home tuition for depth and habit-building, online for flexibility and specialist access, hybrid when a family wants both without overloading anyone's week.
items: Home: best for Maths and sciences with a lot of worked paper practice, and for students who focus better away from a screen.
Online: best for accessing a specific HL specialist not based nearby, and for late evening slots after other commitments.
Hybrid: a regular home slot each week plus an online session before a deadline or mock, without doubling travel.
Home tuition needs a fixed quiet space; online needs a stable connection and a second screen for shared work.
A family that starts at home and later needs a specialist unavailable nearby can move that one subject online without changing the rest.

contentBlocks.heading: How is an IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon verified before a home visit?
contentBlocks.body:
Before any tutor is allowed into a family's home, IB Gram reviews their profile against the specific subject and level requested: an HL Chemistry request is matched against someone who has actually taught HL Chemistry, not a general science background stretched to fit. Identity and background checks happen before a home visit is scheduled, not after. None of this replaces a parent's own judgment, and the checklist in this section is meant to be used, not just read.

A trial or demo session, arranged before the family commits to anything ongoing, is where a parent should watch for specific things: does the tutor ask what the student already struggles with rather than launching straight into a prepared lesson, do they ask which command terms the school's own teacher favours, do they leave the student with something concrete to try before the next session. A tutor who cannot explain, in plain terms, the difference between a subject's HL and SL demands is not ready for a Gurgaon family paying attention to detail.

Parents typing 'ib dp home tutor near me' are really asking whether a specific tutor can reach their own sector reliably, and that is exactly what the shortlist step exists for. It is still worth asking directly: which specific subjects and levels has this tutor taught before, not just 'IB' as a broad label; what happens if a session is missed, is it rescheduled or lost; and is a parent or another adult expected to be home during early sessions, which is a reasonable and normal request rather than an imposition. If a home tutor is not the right fit after the trial, IB Gram arranges a different match, with no obligation to continue with someone who is not working for the student.
items: Profile review: subject expertise and level (HL/SL) experience are checked before a name is shortlisted.
Identity and background checks are completed before any tutor is scheduled for a home visit.
A trial or demo session lets the family judge manner, pace and subject depth before committing further.
Ask directly which specific DP subjects and levels the tutor has taught, not just 'IB' broadly.
Ask what happens if a session is missed or a tutor is unavailable at short notice.
A parent or another adult being home during early sessions is a reasonable, normal request, not an imposition.

contentBlocks.heading: What happens in the first IB DP home tuition session?
contentBlocks.body:
The first IB DP home tuition session is a diagnostic, not a lesson in the usual sense. The tutor spends part of the first sixty or ninety minutes finding out what the student already knows well, where the gaps sit, and how the student prefers to work, before touching new content. This matters more for DP students than it does at younger grades, because a DP1 or DP2 student arrives with a school teacher's approach already in their head, and a home tutor who ignores that and starts from a blank slate wastes the session.

The study space matters more than families expect. A quiet desk or table, away from a television or a younger sibling's homework, with room for a laptop, a notebook and printed past papers, works far better than a shared dining table mid-meal-prep. A parent or guardian being home for the first one or two sessions is normal and expected; it is not required every week after that once the arrangement settles, though many families across Gurgaon prefer to be in the house, if not the room, throughout DP1 and DP2.

Materials worth having ready before the tutor arrives: the student's current textbook or subject guide, notes from the most recent unit test or mock, and any IA or EE feedback already received from the school. None of this needs to be organised perfectly; a tutor experienced with IB DP students can work from a messy folder as easily as a tidy one. What matters is that the first session establishes a shared starting point, so the second session can move straight into work instead of repeating the diagnostic.
items: A quiet desk or table with space for a laptop, a notebook and printed past papers works better than a shared family space.
The student's current textbook, subject guide and any recent mock or IA feedback should be ready for the first session.
A parent or guardian at home for the first one or two sessions is normal and expected, not required every week after.
Wifi is useful but not essential for a home session; the tutor brings printed material as a backup.
Fifteen minutes before the first session is enough to introduce the tutor to the study space and agree ground rules.

contentBlocks.heading: How much progress should you expect, and by when?
contentBlocks.body:
There is no single best IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon for every family, since fit depends on subject depth, manner and whether the schedule actually holds week to week. Progress does not show up as a grade jump in the first few weeks, and any arrangement that promises otherwise is overselling. What should show up within three or four sessions is a change in how the student approaches a past paper question: reading the command term properly, structuring an answer before writing it, showing working an examiner can actually award marks for. That is the honest early signal, not a mock result.

No tutor, however experienced, can guarantee a grade; the IB's own grading and moderation process sits entirely outside any tutor's control, and a family should be sceptical of anyone who implies otherwise. What a good IB DP home tutor can influence is preparation, and preparation compounds over DP1 and DP2 in a way that is hard to see week to week but obvious looking back over a term. A DP2 student who starts serious Extended Essay or revision work only in February has a narrower path than one who started structured support in DP1, and an honest tutor says so rather than promising a late rescue.

If, after a genuine month of consistent weekly sessions, a student's confidence and working habits have not shifted at all, that is a real signal worth acting on, not a phase to push through. The right response is usually to review the match itself, subject depth, teaching manner, even the time of day, rather than assuming more of the same will eventually work. IB Gram will arrange a different tutor if the fit is wrong; that is a normal, expected part of the process, not a failure.
items: Three sessions is usually enough to judge whether the pace and manner are right, before judging grades at all.
A visible change in how a student attacks a past paper question often shows before a mock grade moves.

A student who started very late before May has less room to close a gap than one who started in DP1.
If progress genuinely stalls after a month of consistent sessions, that is a reason to review the match, not push harder blindly.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started with an IB DP home tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is a query, not a form to fill in alone. A parent sends a query or books a free consultation describing the student's DP1 or DP2 stage, the subjects and HL/SL split that need support, and the sector or society the family lives in, so the shortlist favours DP1 and DP2 tutors in Gurgaon who can genuinely reach that address on a weekday evening rather than someone already stretched thin across the city.

From there, IB Gram asks a short set of questions about the school, its exam session, the mock calendar and the family's own weekly rhythm, and shortlists tutors whose verified profiles match on subject, level and location. A trial or demo session happens in the home before anything ongoing is agreed, so the family can see the tutor's manner and approach with the student present, not on paper.

Once a family confirms, lessons run at home, online or hybrid depending on level, schedule and tutor availability, and the arrangement can be adjusted, a different day, a different mode, even a different tutor, if something about the first few weeks is not working. That flexibility matters more for a two-year programme like the Diploma Programme than it would for a single exam term, because a family's needs in DP1 rarely look the same as their needs approaching May of DP2.

There is no need to have every detail settled before the first message. A rough sense of which subjects are worrying the student most, and whether Saturday mornings or weekday evenings suit the household better, is enough to start the shortlist. IB Gram fills in the rest through the questions it asks, and the trial session itself usually answers whatever is still unclear, including how the tutor handles a subject the student has been quietly avoiding.

Families in further-out corridors like SPR or the Dwarka Expressway sometimes start with home visits and move one or two sessions a month online once school activities or evening traffic make a regular weekday visit harder to sustain. faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and student are not a good match?

This is genuinely common in the first few weeks of a DP1 or DP2 arrangement, and asking for a change is not an inconvenience to raise. The clearest signal is usually the trial session itself: if the tutor's pace, manner or subject depth does not suit the student, say so before committing to an ongoing schedule rather than hoping it improves on its own. A second match, briefed on what did not work the first time, usually fits better.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP1 or DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: This depends on the subject, the HL or SL level, and how close the student is to mocks or the May exam session, so there is no single right number. A DP1 student keeping pace with school content often needs less frequent support than a DP2 student heading into mocks with a specific gap. The honest approach is to start with what the family and student can actually sustain each week, alongside school, CAS and other subjects, and adjust after the trial session and the first few weeks rather than committing to a fixed weekly number upfront.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow the school's own pace and teacher?

If a student's school moves faster or slower than expected on a topic, mention it directly so the tutor can adjust rather than assuming a generic DP timeline applies.

It happens in the family's home, at the address and time that suits the household, so the tutor's manner and pace can be judged in the actual setting lessons will run in. introSummary: An IB DP private tutor in Gurgaon is an independent arrangement, someone with no teaching relationship to your child's own school, brought in specifically to avoid the conflict of interest that comes with paying a student's own classroom teacher for extra lessons. Home tuition is IB Gram's lead service across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, and a private tutor works at your home, online or hybrid, mapped to the school's own scheme of work rather than a separate syllabus. This page covers that conflict of interest directly, what a private tutor should and should not do around school tasks like the Extended Essay, what to agree in writing before starting, and which Gurgaon corridors an independent tutor can reach.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram set up an IB DP private tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Setting up an IB DP private tutor in Gurgaon begins with a query that says more than just the subject. IB Gram asks whether the student's own school teacher already gives paid extra classes in that subject, because an independent arrangement is meant to sit apart from the school relationship, not inside it. A DP1 student needing general Maths support has different requirements from a DP2 student wanting focused help on one HL topic before a mock, and the shortlist reflects that difference from the first conversation.

The tutor shortlisted is always independent of the student's own school; IB Gram does not place a student's current subject teacher into a private tutoring role with that same student, for reasons covered in more detail further down this page. Before a single session happens, the basics get agreed in writing between the family and IB Gram: how often sessions run, how much notice a cancellation needs, and how progress gets reported back to the parent. None of this needs to be formal or lengthy, but having it written down avoids the vague misunderstandings that sink a private arrangement by December.

A trial session comes next, in the home, online or wherever suits the family, so everyone can judge fit before committing to a term. If the match is wrong, IB Gram arranges someone else. Once confirmed, the tutor works from the school's own scheme of work and current unit, not a separate syllabus imported from somewhere else, and the numbered steps below show the sequence end to end, whether the arrangement settles into regular home tuition, online sessions, or a hybrid mix of both.
items: 1. You send a query or book a free consultation, naming the subject, HL/SL level and whether any current teacher is involved.
2. IB Gram asks about the school's scheme of work, the student's current unit, and what has already been covered in class.
3. A tutor is shortlisted who is independent of the student's own school, avoiding any conflict of interest.
4. Before the first session, IB Gram and the family agree the basics in writing: schedule, cancellation notice and how progress is reported.
5. A trial session confirms fit before anything ongoing is agreed.
6. Sessions then run at home, online or hybrid, mapped to the school's own pace, not a separate syllabus.

contentBlocks.heading: Six subjects, two years: the shape of the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
A private tutor stepping into a DP1 or DP2 student's life needs to understand the shape of the two-year programme before touching a single subject, mainly because a private arrangement only works if it fits around that shape rather than competing with it. Six subjects, spread across six groups, with three or four taken at Higher Level, recommended by the International Baccalaureate (IB) at around 240 teaching hours, and the remainder at Standard Level, recommended at around 150 hours. That HL/SL split, already fixed with the school, is not something a private tutor renegotiates; it is simply the frame the tutoring has to work inside.

Each subject carries a grade from 1 to 7, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) together with the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points between them, bringing the maximum score to 45. Twenty-four points is the floor for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's own failing conditions layered on top, which is one reason a private tutor's brief usually needs to be specific: shoring up one weak HL subject matters more for the final outcome than adding general polish to a subject already going well.

Creativity, Activity, Service, CAS, runs alongside the six subjects across both years and has to be signed off independently of how well the subjects themselves are going; a private tutor is not the person who manages that, and it is worth a family knowing that boundary early. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter their students for the May exam session, with November used by a smaller number of schools and by students retaking a subject, and each school sets its own DP2 mock dates ahead of May, dates a private tutor needs from the family directly since they sit outside any public calendar.
items: Six subjects across six groups: English A, a second language, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics and an elective.
Three or four subjects at Higher Level (240 recommended hours), the rest at Standard Level (150 hours).
Each subject graded 1-7; TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 more points combined, for a 45-point maximum.
24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's own failing conditions.
CAS (Creativity, Activity, Service) runs throughout and must be completed regardless of subject grades.
Most Gurgaon IB schools use the May exam session; November serves a minority and retake candidates.

contentBlocks.heading: IB DP subjects a private tutor is actually asked to cover
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is usually the first subject a Gurgaon family looks for a private tutor over, whichever route the student is on: Analysis and Approaches, leaning toward proof, or Applications and Interpretation, leaning toward modelling, each offered at HL and SL. A private tutor working outside the school relationship still has to mark against the same command terms the school's own teacher uses, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, because a student getting two different standards from two different adults learns to guess which one is being applied rather than to actually meet either.

The sciences bring a specific boundary a private arrangement has to respect: internally assessed practical work belongs to the school, supervised and marked by school staff, and a private tutor's role is to prepare the analysis and write-up, not to conduct or oversee the practical itself. Theory of Knowledge sits outside the six subjects but still needs private support sometimes: the exhibition links three objects to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts in under 950 words and is internally assessed for a third of the grade, while the essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for that exam session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed for the other two thirds.

The Extended Essay and TOK are both graded A to E and combine for up to 3 of the diploma's 45 points, and an E in either one is, on its own, a failing condition, which is exactly the kind of detail a private tutor needs to flag early rather than assume the family already knows. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's own official channels; a private tutor working from anything else is working from the wrong material, and it is worth a parent asking directly where a tutor's practice papers actually come from.
items: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, HL or SL, often the first subject a family seeks outside help for.
Sciences: HL papers demand deeper application questions; internally assessed practical work stays with the school regardless.
English A: literary analysis and unseen commentary, marked against command terms like evaluate and discuss.
TOK exhibition: three objects, one of 35 IA prompts, up to 950 words, internally assessed, a third of the grade.
TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles per exam session, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed, two thirds of the grade.
Extended Essay and TOK are graded A-E and combine for up to 3 diploma points; an E in either is a failing condition.

Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area, covering Sectors 29, 40, 45 and 46 plus Greenwood City, sit close enough to the DLF corridor that a tutor already working one side can usually reach the other within the same evening, which keeps scheduling genuinely flexible for a family juggling a private tutor around a full school and activity calendar. The Southern Peripheral Road, SPR, covering Sectors 66 to 70 and 72, Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and Tata Primanti, is newer and lower-density than DLF or Sushant Lok, so a private tutor's travel time depends more on the exact address than the corridor name alone suggests. contentBlocks.heading: Home tutoring, online or hybrid for a private IB DP arrangement?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is the natural starting point for a private IB DP arrangement in Gurgaon: an independent tutor at the family's own table, working entirely away from school premises, which matters for families who specifically want the private arrangement kept separate from the student's day-to-day school life. It suits subjects with heavy worked practice, and it gives a parent the option of being nearby without the arrangement feeling like it is happening inside the school building itself.

Online suits a family that wants a specific independent specialist not currently based in DLF, Sushant Lok or SPR, or a late evening slot after other commitments, and it carries exactly the same confidentiality standard as an in-person session: nothing discussed with the tutor is shared back with the school without the family's own agreement. That boundary matters more for a private arrangement than for ordinary tutoring, since part of the point is a space the student can be honest in without it feeding back into how the school views them.

Hybrid works well when a family wants a steady weekly slot, home or online, with an occasional extra session added before a mock or an Extended Essay deadline. Whichever mode is chosen, the tutor maps their sessions to the school's own scheme of work and current unit, extending and reinforcing it rather than running a competing syllabus; a private tutor who ignores what the school is actually doing that week is not adding much value, however good their subject knowledge is on paper.

contentBlocks.heading: How is an independent IB DP private tutor in Gurgaon verified?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification for an independent IB DP private tutor in Gurgaon covers the same ground as any tutor on the platform, subject and HL/SL experience checked against the request, identity and background checks completed before scheduling, whether for a home tutoring session or an online one, plus one extra check specific to private arrangements: confirming the tutor has no current teaching relationship with the student's own school that would create a conflict of interest. That independence is the entire point of a private arrangement, and it is worth a family asking about it directly rather than assuming it.

The trial session is where confidentiality gets tested in practice, not just promised. Watch whether the tutor asks appropriate questions about the student's actual gaps without asking for anything that belongs to the school relationship, class rankings, other teachers' comments, that kind of thing, and whether they are clear about what they will and will not do with material like past test papers or IA drafts the family shares. A tutor vague about where that material goes or how long it is kept is worth pressing on before, not after, a term of sessions.

Before the first regular session, it is worth agreeing a few things in writing, even briefly: how much notice a cancellation needs on either side, how progress gets reported to the parent, and confirmation that nothing discussed goes back to the school without the family's agreement. None of this needs to be a formal contract, but a short written note both sides can refer back to prevents the kind of vague misunderstanding that quietly ends a private arrangement by December. If the fit is wrong after the trial, IB Gram arranges a different tutor with no obligation to continue.

contentBlocks.heading: Should your child's own school teacher be their private tutor too?
contentBlocks.body:
A student's own school teacher offering paid private lessons to that same student is common enough in Gurgaon that most families have encountered it, and it is worth thinking through before agreeing to it. The appeal is obvious: the teacher already knows exactly what is being taught in class. The conflict is just as real: that same teacher sets the student's classroom grades, writes their school reports, and decides how generously to mark borderline work, and a financial relationship on the side sits uneasily next to that. It is not that every teacher tutoring their own student behaves improperly; it is that the family has no way to know, and the student is put in an awkward position either way.

An independent private tutor removes that conflict entirely by design, but only works well if they map their sessions to the school's own scheme of work and current unit rather than teaching in a vacuum. That means the family briefing the tutor properly: which topic the class is on, which past test or mock is coming up, what the school's own teacher has already covered and how. A private tutor's job is reinforcement and depth, not a second, competing version of the subject, and definitely not doing the school's own tasks for the student, an Extended Essay outline can be discussed and structured, but the writing has to stay the student's own work, both for academic integrity and because the point of tutoring is the student learning to do it themselves.

What should be agreed in writing before the first regular session, even briefly: the schedule, how much notice a cancellation needs on either side, how and how often progress gets reported to the parent, and an explicit confidentiality line, that nothing discussed with the tutor goes back to the school without the family's own agreement. That last point matters especially for a private arrangement, since part of its value is a space where a struggling student can be honest about what they do not understand without worrying it will show up in a school conversation about them.
items: Schedule: which days and times, and for how long, agreed before the first regular session.
Cancellation notice: how much notice either side gives, and what happens to a missed session.
Progress updates: how often and in what form the parent hears back.
Confidentiality: nothing discussed with the tutor goes back to the school without the family's agreement.
Boundaries on school tasks: the tutor supports understanding, not completes homework or IA drafts on the student's behalf.

contentBlocks.heading: What should a private IB DP arrangement look like after a month?
contentBlocks.body:
A month into a private IB DP arrangement, the clearest sign of progress is not a grade but a student who can explain, in their own words, where a subject's actual gaps are, rather than a vague 'I need to revise more'. That kind of specificity usually shows up before any mock result does, and it is a better early signal than waiting for a number to move.

No tutor, however well matched, can guarantee a grade; the IB's own grading and moderation process sits entirely outside any tutor's control, and a private arrangement promising otherwise should raise a flag immediately. What a private tutor can reliably deliver is consistency: progress updates landing on whatever schedule was agreed at the start, sessions mapped to what the school is actually covering that week, and a student who feels able to admit confusion without judgment, which sometimes matters more for confidence than the subject content itself.

If, after a genuine month, confidentiality has slipped, something discussed privately has made its way back to the school, or the arrangement has quietly drifted into the tutor doing school tasks rather than supporting the student's own work, that is a clear reason to end the arrangement, not a minor issue to overlook. IB Gram will arrange a different tutor if any of this happens; a private arrangement only has value while its two defining features, independence and confidentiality, actually hold. This is true whether the sessions run as home tuition at the family's own table, online, or some mix of the two across the term.

A visible change in how a past paper answer is structured is the honest early signal, not a grade.

contentBlocks.heading: The IB Diploma Programme: what DP1 and DP2 actually involve
contentBlocks.body:
Two years, six subjects, one screen or not: the structure of the Diploma Programme does not change because lessons happen online. DP1 and DP2 students still choose three or four Higher Level subjects, recommended at around 240 teaching hours each by the International Baccalaureate (IB), and the rest at Standard Level, recommended at around 150 hours. That split, decided with the school early on, is the first thing an IB DP online tutor needs from a family before a single class is booked, since HL and SL papers are genuinely different exams, not the same paper marked more strictly.

Grading runs 1 to 7 per subject, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to 3 further points between them, for a maximum diploma score of 45. Twenty-four points is the floor for the diploma itself, and the IB applies its own failing conditions on top of that floor, so a single very weak subject or a failing TOK/EE grade can undo strong results elsewhere. None of this is any easier or harder to teach through a screen; an HL Maths paper is the same paper whether the tutor is in the next room or on video.

Creativity, Activity, Service, CAS, runs in parallel across both years and has to be signed off regardless of how the six subjects are going, and it is worth remembering CAS itself is not something an online tutor manages. Most Gurgaon IB schools sit their students for the May exam session; November is used by a smaller number of schools and by students retaking a subject. Each school fixes its own DP2 mock dates ahead of May, and those mocks are usually what pushes a family from casual revision help toward a proper weekly online tutor.
items: Six subjects across six subject groups, including English A, a second language, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics and an elective.
Three or four subjects at Higher Level (240 recommended hours), the remainder at Standard Level (150 hours).
Grades run 1-7 per subject; TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 more points combined.

contentBlocks.heading: IB DP subjects online: what changes on a screen
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics and the sciences translate onto a screen better than most parents expect, mainly because a shared digital whiteboard does the one thing a notebook does: shows working step by step, in real time, with the tutor able to circle the exact line where a method error crept in. Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, get discussed exactly the same way whether the tutor is at the kitchen table or on a laptop three kilometres away, and an HL Physics past paper marked live on a shared document works almost as well as one marked in person.

English A and Theory of Knowledge sit slightly differently. A long discussion about a text or a TOK prescribed title works fine over video, arguably better for a student who finds eye contact across a small table awkward and opens up more freely on a call. TOK itself has two very different assessments to prepare for on screen: the exhibition, linking three objects to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts in under 950 words, benefits from a tutor talking through the objects on camera, while the essay, up to 1,600 words against one of six prescribed titles released for that exam session, is better handled as a shared document than a video call, since scrolling through pages while a tutor talks is a weaker experience than both people looking at the same printed page with a pen in hand.

What a screen cannot do at all is stand in for a school's own laboratory time; internally assessed practical work in the sciences needs the equipment and supervision the school provides, and no online tutor, however good, replaces that component. An online tutor's role there is preparation and analysis: talking through the write-up, checking a method section against the criteria, not running the experiment itself. That limit is worth saying plainly, because a family sometimes assumes online tuition covers ground it simply cannot.

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home tutor or hybrid: which suits IB DP better?
contentBlocks.body:
An IB DP online tutor in Gurgaon is the intent of this page for good reason: it suits a Gurgaon family that wants a specific specialist, a particular HL Economics teacher, say, rather than whoever happens to be free nearby, and it suits a late slot that a travelling home tutor could not reasonably offer on a weekday. It also suits a DP2 student comfortable working independently on screen, who does not need a physical presence in the room to stay focused for ninety minutes, and it removes the question of which corridor a tutor lives in from the decision entirely.

Home tuition remains the better call for some DP1 students, particularly younger ones or those who focus less well at a laptop after a full day of screen-based schoolwork already. A tutor physically present can read body language a video call misses entirely, notice a student has quietly checked out five minutes before they say so, and a subject with heavy worked practice, Maths especially, sometimes benefits from someone leaning over the same page rather than the same screen.

Hybrid takes the middle path deliberately: a regular weekly online session for pace and consistency, with an occasional home visit added before mocks or the May exam session itself, when in-person paper practice under closer supervision earns its extra time. The honest comparison, stated plainly: online wins on flexibility and specialist access, home wins on presence and focus for younger or easily distracted students, hybrid wins when a family genuinely wants both and can plan the calendar around it.

contentBlocks.heading: What do you actually need for an IB DP online lesson to work?
contentBlocks.body:
The equipment list for an IB DP online tutor is shorter than most families expect. A stable internet connection matters more over two years of DP1 and DP2 than the laptop's specifications; a five-year-old machine on reliable wifi beats a new one on a connection that drops every twenty minutes. A working camera and microphone, tested once before the very first class rather than discovered mid-session, save the first ten minutes from becoming a technology troubleshooting exercise instead of a lesson.

A second screen, or even a tablet propped beside the laptop, keeps the student from scrolling back and forth between a shared document and their own notes, and it is worth having one ready before term starts rather than after the third frustrated session. Handwritten working, the actual mechanism by which a Maths or Physics examiner awards method marks, transfers over a scanner app or a clear phone photo without any special hardware; what matters is holding the page steady and good light, not an expensive setup.

Where the room itself matters is quiet, not size: a closed door in a smaller room beats an open living room with a television or a sibling's conversation in the background, because an online lesson has no way to physically shut out distraction the way a tutor sitting across the table can. What works well on a screen: worked Maths and science examples, past paper marking, TOK discussion, Extended Essay structural feedback. What struggles: long stretches of unstructured reading, and anything needing a physical lab. Knowing that split before term starts saves a family from expecting the wrong things from an online arrangement.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you know within three sessions whether online is working?
contentBlocks.body:
Three sessions is usually enough to tell whether an online arrangement is genuinely working, and the signal is not a grade, it is engagement. By the second class, the student should be talking through their own working rather than sitting quietly while the tutor explains; a student who stays silent through screen after screen is either not engaged or not being asked to participate enough, and either is worth raising directly rather than assuming it will improve.

Screen-sharing and the mechanics of the platform should feel routine by the second or third session, not still a source of friction; a tutor who is fumbling with software in week three is not spending that time teaching. What should be visible instead is a change in how the student structures a past paper answer, reading the command term properly, showing working an examiner can mark, before writing rather than during. That is the honest early signal an online arrangement is doing its job, not a mock result, since no tutor, online or in person, can guarantee a grade; the IB's own grading and moderation sit entirely outside any tutor's control.

One thing worth watching specifically for an online arrangement: whether the student seems noticeably more tired or distracted on a video call than they were in any in-person class or school lesson that day. Screen fatigue after a full school day of screen-based learning is real for some students, and if it shows up consistently rather than on an occasional bad day, that is a genuine reason to talk about switching a session or two to hybrid, not a reason to push through and hope it passes.

If the student seems noticeably more tired or distracted on video than in an in-person class, or engagement has not shifted after a genuine month of sessions, that is worth raising directly rather than waiting it out.

acceptedAnswer.text: A tutor is briefed on the student's specific school, subject and current unit before the first session, and works to reinforce what the school's own teacher is covering rather than running a separate parallel syllabus. heroTitle: How to Choose an IB Diploma Tutor in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Two years, six subjects, a core that will not wait: choosing the wrong IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon costs a family time it does not have. This page sets out what actually separates a strong tutor from an average one, the questions worth asking before a trial, and what the first month should reveal.
introSummary: An IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon is chosen, not simply assigned, and the choice matters because two years of six subjects and a demanding core leave little room to recover from a poor fit. Most families want this tutor to come home, working through home tuition sessions at the family's own table, though online and hybrid patterns suit plenty of students just as well. What separates a strong choice from a weak one is rarely charisma on a phone call; it is whether the tutor actually understands Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) hours, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) as one connected structure rather than six unrelated subjects plus some extra work. This page sets out how to judge that, what IB Gram checks before a shortlist, and what a tutor's first month should actually show.

contentBlocks.heading: The Diploma Structure Every IB Diploma Tutor in Gurgaon Should Know Cold
contentBlocks.body:
An IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon worth choosing should not need the Diploma Programme (DP) explained to them; they should be explaining pieces of it to the family. The structure itself: two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) with around 240 recommended teaching hours, the rest at Standard Level (SL) with around 150 hours. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. Ask a candidate tutor to explain this back in their own words during the first call; a tutor who fumbles it is not yet ready to plan across two years properly.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 further points, taking the total to 45, and the diploma's minimum award is 24 points, subject to the IB's own failing conditions. A good IB 45 points tutor can explain why those failing conditions matter, not just recite the point total, treating the diploma as six subjects and a core sharing two years, not a single exam. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) is required too, separate from the points but not optional for graduation.

Exam sessions sit in May and November. The large majority of Gurgaon's IB schools use May, with November mostly for a minority of schools and for retake candidates. Results from May land in early July. A tutor who plans a whole term around a vague sense of exam season, rather than the school's actual dates, is not the tutor to choose.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging a Tutor's Grip on TOK, the EE and CAS
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor's real depth shows up fastest in the core, not the six subjects. Ask how they would approach Theory of Knowledge (TOK): a good answer names both assessments unprompted, the exhibition, three objects tied to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts, around 950 words, marked in school for a third of the grade, and the essay, one of six prescribed titles released per session, around 1,600 words, marked externally for the other two thirds. They should mention the areas of knowledge, history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics, the arts, and the core theme plus two optional themes, without being prompted for detail. A tutor who cannot say any of this from memory has probably never actually taught TOK properly. This is what real IB Diploma core support in Gurugram looks like: specific, unprompted knowledge of TOK and EE mechanics, not a rehearsed pitch.

On the Extended Essay (EE), a good tutor describes their role correctly: supporting a student's own up-to-4,000-word research over roughly 40 hours, alongside the formal supervision a teacher at the student's own school provides, with reflection sessions recorded through the process, never replacing that supervisor. TOK and EE grades run A to E and combine for up to 3 points, and a tutor should know, unprompted, that an E in either is a failing condition. Because the EE guide changed for first assessment in 2027, a tutor still quoting old criterion mark breakdowns is a real red flag, not a minor slip; the family's own DP coordinator has the current version.

CAS rarely needs a tutor's direct help, but a good one still asks about it occasionally, since it is easy for a student to let it slide once six subjects and the core start crowding a week.

Each school sets its own mock examination date, usually months ahead of the May session, and a tutor who has not asked about it is planning blind. Whether a tutor works from real past papers, mark schemes and subject reports sourced through the school or the IB's own official channels, rather than recycled material from a different school entirely, is worth asking about directly; the two are not interchangeable.

A tutor's command of command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, is one of the easiest things to test in a trial lesson. contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring, Online Tutor or Hybrid in Gurgaon: Choosing the Right Pattern
contentBlocks.body:
Most families choosing an IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon start by picturing a home tutor, and that instinct usually holds up: a tutor physically present with a DP1 or DP2 student, working through the family's own past papers and notes at their own table, tends to keep a tired student's attention better than a screen does, especially at the end of a long school day. It also lets the family judge the tutor directly, in the room, which matters when choosing someone for a two-year commitment.

Choosing an IB Diploma online tutor in Gurgaon is worth doing when reach matters more than presence: a genuine specialist in a less common HL subject who is not based near the family's corridor, a late evening slot that a home visit could not realistically make work, or a family who has already found that their child concentrates fine on a screen. A shared whiteboard handles a TOK essay redraft or a maths derivation perfectly well; a Chemistry practical discussion or a student who needs someone physically present to stay engaged suits a home tutor better.

Choosing hybrid from the start, rather than defaulting to one mode and switching under pressure, tends to work best: an agreed default of home sessions with online as the planned fallback for weeks when travel does not make sense, particularly around a DP2 mock. The right choice depends less on a general preference and more on the specific student, the specific subject, and how the family's week is actually shaped.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Separates a Strong IB Diploma Tutor From an Average One?
contentBlocks.body:
Strip away credentials and manner, and a genuinely strong IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon is recognisable by a handful of concrete habits, not a general impression of competence. They ask about the school's own scheme of work before the first lesson, not after several sessions. They read command terms precisely, treating evaluate and discuss as different instructions rather than interchangeable ones, and they say so explicitly when correcting a student's answer. They know, without needing to check, that an E grade in TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition regardless of how strong the six subjects are, because that single fact shapes how seriously the core gets treated across two years.

An average tutor, by contrast, often teaches competently but generically: solid subject knowledge, reasonable manner with the student, but no real awareness of how the Diploma Programme's own structure, HL and SL hours, the 45-point maximum, the school's specific mock calendar, should shape a lesson plan. This is not always obvious in a first phone call, where warmth and confidence can substitute for depth. It usually becomes visible in the trial lesson, when an average tutor either avoids the syllabus specifics or answers them vaguely.

A genuine red flag, worth ending a conversation over immediately, is a tutor who offers to write or substantially complete a student's Extended Essay, internal assessment or coursework. That is not tutoring; it is academic dishonesty that puts the diploma itself at risk, and any tutor suggesting it, however subtly, should be removed from consideration regardless of how strong they otherwise appear. A second, softer flag is a tutor who cannot describe, specifically, what changed about their understanding of the student after a trial lesson; vague reassurance is not the same as an actual diagnosis.

None of this requires a family to become an expert in the Diploma Programme themselves. It requires asking a few pointed questions and paying attention to how specifically, not how confidently, they are answered.

Choosing the right tutor should be visible within four weeks, not as a grade change but as a specific, credible account of the student. A tutor worth keeping can say exactly which command terms the student still misreads, whether an HL subject needs real structural help or just more practice, and how TOK or the EE is actually progressing rather than being quietly set aside.

For subjects with a clear mark scheme, HL Mathematics, SL Chemistry, that account usually comes with marked past-paper evidence: specific marks gained on specific question types, not a general sense of improved confidence. For TOK and the EE, four weeks is still early by design; a TOK essay might have been through one round of feedback, and the EE's roughly 40 hours of research is nowhere near finished. A tutor who claims major movement on the core that fast has either exaggerated or misunderstood how the diploma actually works.

If the chosen tutor is starting close to a mock or the May session, the first month looks different again: more triage on known weak points than groundwork for new ones, and an honest tutor says this plainly rather than promising a turnaround the calendar cannot support. A family that hears specific, sometimes unflattering detail in that first month has very likely chosen well. A family that hears only general reassurance, however warmly delivered, should treat that as a reason to ask more pointed questions rather than relax.

faqs.question: How do I know if a tutor really understands the IB Diploma, or is just experienced with other boards?
faqs.answer: Ask them to explain the 45-point structure, HL and SL hours, and why an E grade in TOK or the Extended Essay matters, without prompting. h1: IB Diploma Tuition in Gurgaon: Choosing the Right Tutor
heroTitle: Choosing IB Diploma Tuition That Fits Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Two years, six subjects and a core that never pauses: that is what IB Diploma tuition in Gurgaon has to work around. This page sets out what a specialist tutor actually brings over a generalist, what to ask before and after the trial lesson, and what real progress looks like once the first month is done.
introSummary: IB Diploma tuition in Gurgaon means regular, structured lessons with one tutor across a term or the full two years, most often delivered as home tuition at the family's own house, with online or hybrid sessions where travel does not make sense on a given week. The real decision is not whether to get tuition, most DP families eventually do, but which tutor to choose and how to know four weeks in whether it is actually working. A specialist in this board reads a command term differently from a general tutor, plans around Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) hours, and understands how Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) compete with six subjects for the same two years. This page covers what to ask before a trial, how IB Gram matches a tutor, and what the first month should show.

contentBlocks.heading: Setting Up IB Diploma Tuition in Gurgaon: The First Few Steps
contentBlocks.body:
Most families start not with a plan but with a specific worry: a DP1 report card that shows HL Physics slipping, or a student who has gone quiet about how the Extended Essay is going. The first query does not need to be polished. Tell IB Gram the board, the grade, which subjects are HL and which are SL, and what prompted the search now rather than last term.

IB Gram then asks a set of questions most families do not expect: which exam session the school uses, whether a DP2 mock is already on the calendar, and what the student's own school has already tried, extra help periods, a subject teacher's open office hours, before a private tutor enters the picture. Answers to these shape who gets shortlisted far more than the subject name alone.

A shortlist follows, of tutors whose profiles are verified against the subject, level and board, along with their general availability. A free trial lesson is arranged next, and this is deliberately treated as a two-way audition: the tutor is assessing the student's actual gaps, not performing a sales pitch, and the family is watching whether the explanations land. Only after that trial does a regular weekly slot get fixed, along with how the tutor will report back and what happens if a week has to be skipped for a school trip or an illness. Tuition that starts this way, with real information exchanged before the first regular lesson, tends to need far fewer awkward resets later in the term.
items: 1. Describe the board, grade, HL and SL subjects, and what prompted the search.
2. Answer questions on the exam session, mock dates and what the school has already tried.
3. Receive a shortlist of tutors verified for that subject, level and board.
4. Treat the free trial as a two-way audition, not a sales pitch.
5. Fix a weekly slot, a reporting rhythm, and a plan for missed weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: The 45-Point Structure Every IB Diploma Tuition Plan Has to Respect
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor cannot plan sensible tuition without first understanding what the Diploma Programme (DP) is actually structured around. Over two years, a student takes six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL), carrying roughly 240 recommended teaching hours, and the remainder at Standard Level (SL), around 150 hours. Grading runs 1 to 7 per subject. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) then add up to 3 more points between them, which is why the maximum score is 45 rather than 42.

This is not trivia; it changes how a tuition schedule should actually be built. A student needs the diploma's minimum of 24 points to be awarded it at all, subject to the IB's failing conditions, and a subject sitting well below where it needs to be can pull the whole diploma down even if the other five are strong. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be logged across the two years too, separate from the point count but still a graduation requirement a tutoring plan should not quietly ignore.

Exam sessions run in May and in November each year. Almost every IB school in Gurgaon enters its DP2 cohort for May, with November largely reserved for a small number of schools and for students retaking a subject. Results land in early July. A tuition plan worth paying for treats these dates as fixed points to build backward from, not an afterthought mentioned once at the start of the year.

TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points toward the 45 maximum.
24 points is the minimum diploma award, subject to the IB's failing conditions.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does a Specialist Tutor Know About TOK, the EE and CAS That a Generalist Often Doesn't?
contentBlocks.body:
This is where the difference between a subject specialist and a general tutor shows up fastest. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) is assessed twice: an exhibition built from three objects tied to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts, capped near 950 words and marked inside the school for a third of the TOK grade, and an essay answering one of six prescribed titles released each session, capped near 1,600 words and marked externally for the remaining two thirds. A generalist tutor often treats TOK like an ordinary essay subject. A specialist knows it is built around a core theme, two optional themes chosen from five, and five areas of knowledge, history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts, and grades it A to E accordingly, aware that an E in TOK or the EE is a failing condition regardless of how strong the six subjects are.

The Extended Essay (EE) asks for up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of independent research, supervised formally by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions logged along the way. A specialist tutor's role is to sit beside that school supervision, sharpening a research question or pressure-testing an argument, never replacing the supervisor. Because the EE guide changed for first assessment in 2027, a tutor who still quotes old criterion mark breakdowns from memory is a warning sign worth noticing; the safer approach is always the version the student's own DP coordinator has actually issued.

CAS rarely needs subject tuition as such, but a tutor who is paying attention will notice when a student has let it slide under exam pressure and say so, rather than letting it become a July surprise.

TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles, about 1,600 words, marked externally.

contentBlocks.heading: How School Terms in Gurgaon Shape an IB Diploma Tuition Calendar
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge each run their own term calendar, and a tuition plan that ignores it is just guessing at when the student actually needs more support.

Each school fixes its own DP2 mock examination window, generally sitting some months ahead of the May session, and these dates matter more to a tuition schedule than almost anything else, because the weeks leading into a mock are when practice against real past papers and mark schemes pays off most. Those papers, along with mark schemes and subject reports, are only reliable when sourced through the school or the IB's own official channels; a tutor working from an unofficial source is a risk worth avoiding.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, quietly decide how many marks an otherwise correct answer earns, and a tuition plan that never addresses them directly is leaving marks on the table for reasons that have nothing to do with subject knowledge. Building a term's tuition around the school's own mock dates, rather than a generic exam-season assumption, is one of the clearest signs of a specialist tutor at work.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Building the Right Weekly Pattern
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where most IB Diploma tuition in Gurgaon families start, and it remains IB Gram's lead offering for good reason: a tutor at the kitchen table with a DP1 or DP2 student, working line by line through a past paper, tends to hold attention better than the same session over a screen, particularly for a student who is already tired at the end of a school day. It also lets a tutor see, directly, what materials, notes, past scripts, a school planner, the student actually has and uses.

Online tuition earns its place for different reasons. It opens access to a specialist who might not otherwise reach a particular corridor, holds up well for subjects that are mostly discussion or annotation, TOK essay feedback or a maths derivation on a shared whiteboard, and removes the commute entirely, which matters most on weeks when Cyber City traffic or a late school activity leaves little room to spare. It suits a student who is already independent and simply needs expert input at set points, less well a student who needs someone physically present to stay on task.

Most families that stick with tuition for more than a term settle into a hybrid rhythm without ever formally deciding to: home sessions in a normal week, online when travel would eat the lesson itself, and a shift to more frequent sessions, in whichever mode is practical, in the weeks before a mock or the May session. There is no single correct ratio. What works is agreeing the default pattern early and treating exceptions as normal rather than a disruption.

contentBlocks.heading: How Tutors Offering IB Diploma Tuition in Gurgaon Are Checked
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram puts on a shortlist has a verified profile: the subjects, boards and levels they actually teach, checked before that profile is ever shown to a family, alongside general availability matched to what the family has asked for. This is not a claim about how many tutors are registered or how long any one of them has been teaching, only a description of what is confirmed before a name reaches a parent.

Parents are still the last line of checking, and it is worth taking that seriously rather than treating a shortlist as a finished decision. Ask directly what the tutor's HL and SL teaching experience actually looks like, since these are genuinely different jobs even within the same subject. Ask how they would structure the first month of tuition for this specific student, not a generic answer about their teaching philosophy. Ask what they do when a student is stuck on a concept mid-session; the answer often reveals more than a CV ever could.

The free trial lesson is the real check. A specialist tutor asks about the school's syllabus pace and recent test results before teaching anything, rather than opening a textbook at a random chapter. If the trial does not go well, or the fit feels off even when the tutor is clearly competent, IB Gram can offer a different match. Tuition is meant to be a working relationship the student trusts, not an arrangement the family talked themselves into.

contentBlocks.heading: What to Ask Before and After the Trial Lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
The trial lesson is where an IB Diploma tuition decision actually gets made, not the phone call beforehand. Before it happens, ask the tutor what they will actually do in that first session: most good tutors will say some version of a diagnostic, working through recent school test questions or a past paper section to see exactly where the gaps sit, rather than starting a new topic cold. Ask, too, what they need from the family beforehand: recent test scripts, the school's own scheme of work, or simply the syllabus code and level. A tutor who asks for none of this is planning to teach in the abstract, disconnected from what the student's own school actually expects.

During the trial, watch rather than just listen. Does the tutor let the student attempt a question first, or jump straight to explaining? Do they use the command terms the IB actually uses, define, describe, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, or paraphrase loosely in a way that will not transfer to an exam answer? A subject specialist tends to reference the specific syllabus, group and paper structure naturally, the way a general tutor coming from a CBSE or ICSE background usually does not.

After the trial, the most useful question is not whether it went well but what changed. A specialist tutor should be able to say, specifically, what they noticed: a student who is strong on content but loses marks on command-term depth, or one who understands a concept but cannot yet structure a TOK-style argument around it. A vague answer, along the lines of the student seeming bright and things working out in time, is not the same as an actual read on the gaps. Families who ask this one question before agreeing to regular tuition end up with a far clearer sense of whether the tutor is actually diagnosing the student or simply being pleasant in the room.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should the First Four Weeks of IB Diploma Tuition Show?
contentBlocks.body:
Anyone comparing IB Diploma tuition in Gurgaon options by results rather than promises should look here first. Four weeks is enough time to see a pattern, not enough time to see a grade change, and any tutor who implies otherwise is overselling. What a family should reasonably expect by then is a specific, named list of gaps rather than a general sense that things are going fine: which command terms the student still misreads, whether an HL subject is genuinely behind or just feels harder, and whether TOK or the EE has been getting any attention at all under the pressure of six subjects.

For a subject with a clear mark scheme, HL Mathematics, SL Chemistry, progress by week four usually shows up as marked past-paper answers with visible improvement on specific question types, not a vague sense of more confidence. For TOK and the EE, four weeks is genuinely early; a TOK essay draft might only have gone through one round of feedback, and the EE's roughly 40 hours of research is nowhere near complete. A tutor who reports strong movement on the core inside a month is either exaggerating or not looking closely enough.

If a student is starting tuition close to a mock or the May session itself, four weeks looks different again, more triage than foundation-building, and a tutor should say so plainly rather than promise a transformation the calendar does not allow. The honest version of this page is simple: tuition should sharpen what is already there faster than the student could alone, not manufacture time that was never available.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches You With an IB Diploma Home Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A request for an IB Diploma home tutor in Gurgaon starts with practical detail, not a sales pitch: which subjects and at what level, Higher or Standard, where in Gurgaon the family lives, and which evenings actually work once school, sport and any co-curricular commitment are accounted for. IB Gram asks these questions upfront because a DP student's week is already full, and a home tutor who cannot realistically make a Tuesday 6pm slot from across the city is not a match, however qualified they are on paper.

From there, a coordinator draws from a pool of tutors whose subject and level history is already checked, filters by location within Gurgaon, and confirms availability before a single name reaches the family. This ordering matters: many services show a profile first and worry about logistics afterward, which wastes a family's time on a tutor who was never realistically available for home visits in their corridor. IB Gram reverses that, confirming reach and schedule fit before presenting a match.

A free trial session follows at the family's own home, arranged at a time that suits the student rather than the tutor's convenience. The first visit is treated as diagnostic on both sides: the tutor assesses where the student's Higher Level or Standard Level understanding actually sits, and the parent gets a direct look at how the tutor works with their child in their own space, which a video call or phone reference cannot fully replace. If the fit is not right after that first visit, IB Gram arranges a different tutor rather than asking the family to persist.
