contentBlocks.heading: The IB Diploma's 45-Point Structure, Explained
contentBlocks.body:
Six subjects, one from each of six groups, three or four taken at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, is the frame every IB Diploma home tutor in Gurgaon has to plan around, and it is worth a parent understanding before judging any tutor's suggested plan. Higher Level subjects carry 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 for Standard Level, a real difference in depth and pace that shows up in weekly workload, not just exam difficulty. Each of the six subjects is graded on a 1 to 7 scale, so the headline 45-point maximum comes from six subjects worth up to 42 points between them, plus up to 3 more from the core.

That core, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together, is where the extra points and, often, the extra stress sit. TOK and EE grades, each A to E, combine for the 3 bonus points, and the IB sets failing conditions around them: an E in either TOK or the EE fails the diploma outright, regardless of how strong the six subjects are. Twenty-four points is the minimum needed for the diploma overall, again subject to those failing conditions, which is why a home tutor should never treat TOK or the EE as an afterthought squeezed in around subject tutoring.

Creativity, Activity, Service, the third core element, has to be completed too, though it is not graded on the point scale the way TOK and the EE are. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session, with results released in early July; a minority of schools, and retake candidates, use the November session instead. A tutor working across a full two-year DP1 and DP2 cycle should be tracking all three core elements alongside the six subjects, not one at the expense of the others.
items: Six subjects: three or four at Higher Level (240 hours), the rest at Standard Level (150 hours).
Each subject graded 1-7; TOK and EE together add up to 3 more points.
45 points maximum; 24 points minimum for the diploma, subject to failing conditions.
An E in TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition regardless of subject scores.
Most Gurgaon IB schools use the May session; results are released in early July.

contentBlocks.heading: How the Core (TOK, EE, CAS) Competes for Time With Six Subjects
contentBlocks.body:
Theory of Knowledge has two separate assessments, and a home tutor should be able to explain both without hesitation. The exhibition links three objects to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts, runs to a tight 950 words, is internally assessed by the school, and counts for one third of the TOK grade. The essay, the larger of the two, answers one of six prescribed titles released for that particular exam session, runs up to 1,600 words, is externally assessed, and counts for two thirds of the grade. Across the course, students cover a core theme (knowledge and the knower), two of five optional themes, and five areas of knowledge spanning history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts, so a tutor helping with TOK needs to know which two optional themes and prompts the student's own school has actually chosen.

The Extended Essay asks for independent research: up to 4,000 words, roughly 40 hours of work spread across the two years, written within one DP subject or as an interdisciplinary piece, and supervised throughout by a teacher at the student's own school with recorded reflection sessions along the way. A home tutor's role here is support around that supervision, helping the student plan their research and refine their argument, not replacing the school supervisor's sign-off. Because the EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, a tutor should never quote specific criterion mark allocations from memory; the family's own DP coordinator issues the version that actually applies, and that is the document to follow.

CAS runs alongside all of this without a written exam, but it still needs active management: activities, reflections and a completed programme are checked by the school, and a tutor helping a family stay organised across TOK, the EE and CAS at once, on top of six subjects, is often more valuable than one focused on a single subject alone.

TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles per session, up to 1,600 words, two thirds of the grade.
Extended Essay: up to 4,000 words, about 40 hours, supervised by the student's own school.
EE guide updated for first assessment in 2027; follow the version your DP coordinator issues.
CAS has no written exam but needs active tracking of activities and reflections.

contentBlocks.heading: What the DP2 School Calendar Means for Home Tutoring in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Families at Gurgaon's IB World Schools describe a similar rhythm across the two-year Diploma, even though the details differ school to school: DP1 spent building subject foundations and starting the Extended Essay's research phase, and DP2 dominated by mock examinations, TOK essay deadlines, CAS completion and the final run-up to the May session. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; the schools below are mentioned only as general context for the calendar pressures Gurgaon DP families describe, not as a claim about curriculum or timing at any particular one.

Families with children at schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge typically report that DP2 mock examinations, set independently by each school, land several months before the May session, and that this is exactly when demand for a home tutor rises sharply, since a student's six subjects, TOK essay and any remaining EE reflection sessions all converge in the same few weeks.

A home tutor working through this period earns their place by helping a student prioritise, not by adding more to an already full evening. Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, set the depth every answer needs, and a tutor should be actively teaching a student to read them correctly under mock and exam conditions, not simply reviewing content. Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports, sourced through the school or the IB's own official channels, are what shows a student how marks are actually awarded, and a good home tutor builds every mock preparation session around them rather than generic revision.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid for the Full Diploma?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the starting point IB Gram recommends for most DP families in Gurgaon, and for a subject-heavy course like the Diploma, the reasoning is practical rather than sentimental. A tutor sitting with your child at their own desk, working from their actual notes and past papers, sees exactly where an essay-based subject like History or a lab-heavy one like Chemistry is genuinely going wrong, not just what a student reports over a call. For TOK and the Extended Essay in particular, watching how a student actually reasons through an argument face to face is often more revealing than reading a draft alone.

Online lessons still have a real place, and this page does not pretend otherwise. A family managing evening traffic from a corridor like Manesar or the far end of Sohna Road, or a student who needs a specific HL Economics or HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specialist who does not live nearby, is often better served online than by insisting on a home visit that eats an hour each way. A shared whiteboard works well for maths working and essay annotation on screen; a subject that depends on close observation of practical technique is harder to teach fully online.

Hybrid, home sessions for most weeks with online sessions during a busy patch or ahead of a mock, is what many DP families in Gurgaon settle into once they know their child's actual pattern. Put simply: home tutoring suits a student who benefits from a present, watchful teacher and lives within reasonable reach; online suits a family prioritising a specific specialist or fighting traffic; hybrid suits a family that wants both without over-committing to either. None of the three is the correct answer for every subject or every week of a two-year course.
items: Home: a tutor at the student's own desk sees exactly where reasoning breaks down.
Online: a shared whiteboard suits maths working and essay annotation well.
Hybrid: home sessions most weeks, online during a busy patch or ahead of a mock.
Choose online for a specific HL specialist who is not within easy reach.
No single mode is correct for every subject across a two-year Diploma.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is an IB Diploma Home Tutor Verified Before a Visit?
contentBlocks.body:
Before any tutor's profile is shown for a home-visit request, IB Gram checks their subject and level history against what the family actually needs: which Diploma subjects, Higher or Standard Level, and how recently they have taught the current syllabus. This checking happens before a name and location are shared with a family, not after, which matters more for a home visit than for an online lesson, since a home tutor is coming into a family's own space around a child.

Even with that checking done, a parent should still ask direct questions before the first visit. Ask which Diploma subjects and levels the tutor has taught in the last two years, not just across their career. Ask how they plan to handle a student who is behind in one subject but ahead in another, since the DP's six-subjects-plus-core structure makes this common, not an exception. And ask what happens if a scheduled evening session has to move at short notice, since a DP student's calendar shifts constantly around school commitments.

For the home visit itself, confirm the basics directly: how the tutor will identify themselves at your gate or society entrance, whether they will need visitor registration in advance, and what happens if they are running late because of Gurgaon traffic on a particular evening. Most families find it reassuring to sit in on at least part of the first session, not because anything is expected to go wrong, but because it is the only way to see, rather than hear about, how a tutor actually works with your child at your own table.
items: IB Gram checks subject, level and recent syllabus experience before sharing a name.
Ask which Diploma subjects and levels the tutor has taught in the last two years.
Ask how they handle a student ahead in one subject but behind in another.
Confirm visitor registration and gate identification with your society ahead of the first visit.
Sitting in on part of the first session is a reasonable, common request.

contentBlocks.heading: Study Space, Materials and Who Should Be in the Room
contentBlocks.body:
The first home session is usually diagnostic, not a full teaching session, and knowing this in advance helps a family set the right expectations. The tutor will typically ask about recent topics across the relevant subjects, look at a recent test, IA draft or homework if one is available, and work through a short problem or passage with the student to see how they actually reason, not just what grade they got. A useful first session ends with something concrete: a named topic or skill that needs attention first, not a vague sense that the student 'is doing okay.'

The study space matters more than families usually expect. A quiet table with room for the subject's actual materials, textbooks, a calculator for HL Mathematics, a laptop for research-heavy subjects like the Extended Essay, works far better than a shared living room with a television nearby or a bedroom desk buried under unrelated things. If a student has multiple subjects with one tutor across the week, keeping a simple folder or file per subject, rather than one general notebook, makes each session start faster and makes reviewing progress far easier later.

Whether a parent should be present is a genuine judgement call rather than a fixed rule. Younger DP1 students, or a family just getting to know a new tutor, often benefit from a parent being nearby, at least for part of the session, without hovering over every exchange. Older DP2 students, and families who already trust their tutor after a term or two, usually do better with the parent present only briefly at the start and end, since a DP student mid-exam-cycle needs to practise explaining their own reasoning without a parent filling gaps for them.

Preparing properly for that first visit makes a real difference to how useful it is. First, confirm the exact subjects, levels and any specific weak areas with the tutor beforehand, rather than leaving it to be discovered on the day. Second, have recent tests, IA drafts or past papers ready on the table, not buried in a school bag. Third, agree a realistic session length in advance, sixty or ninety minutes depending on the subject, so neither side is watching the clock. Fourth, decide who will be present and for how long, and say so upfront rather than improvising on arrival.

contentBlocks.heading: What Realistic Progress Looks Like Across a Two-Year Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
Progress across the Diploma rarely looks like a steady straight line, and a parent who expects one, subject by subject, term by term, is often measuring the wrong thing. The first month with a new home tutor is mostly diagnostic: identifying exactly where a student's Higher Level or Standard Level understanding has gaps, which command terms they consistently misread, and which subjects are quietly falling behind while attention goes to whichever deadline is loudest that week. By six to eight weeks, a parent should see something specific: a clearer IA draft, fewer basic errors in a subject that was struggling, or a student who can explain their own TOK reasoning rather than just repeating what a tutor said.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any suggestion otherwise should be treated with real scepticism regardless of how confident it sounds. A tutor's honest value is in the working shown along the way: a record of what was covered each session, a clear note on where the student still struggles, and a plan that changes as the two years progress rather than a fixed script applied regardless of how a term actually goes.

Some limits are worth stating plainly. A home tutor cannot recover a full term of neglected content in the weeks before a mock; that requires sustained work over months, not a last-minute push, and a family starting very late in DP2 should adjust expectations accordingly. A tutor also cannot do the Extended Essay's supervision for the school, since that role belongs to the student's own supervisor by design. And with six subjects plus the full core competing for the same hours, a tutor who focuses only on the subject a parent is most anxious about, while the other five quietly slip, is not actually serving the student well.

Getting started takes a short conversation, not a long form. The first session itself covers a review of recent topics, a look at whatever materials are available, and a short worked example or discussion to see how the student actually reasons through a problem, followed by a specific, honest observation from the tutor about where to start. faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than a coaching centre for a DP student, or should we do both?
faqs.answer: Neither is universally better; it depends on what a student actually needs. A home tutor gives one-to-one attention tracking all six subjects and the core together, which suits a student who needs a coordinated plan across a demanding two-year course; a coaching batch can work well for a student who is broadly on track in a subject and benefits from peer discussion at a lower cost per hour. h1: IB Diploma Tutoring in Gurgaon: An Independent Arrangement
heroTitle: An Independent IB Diploma Arrangement in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: A private tutor sits outside the school, working to the family's own schedule and confidentiality, not the school's roster. This page covers how that arrangement is set up in Gurgaon: what to agree with the tutor in writing, how lessons map to the school's scheme of work, and where a family's own teacher tutoring privately creates a conflict.
introSummary: An IB Diploma private tutor in Gurgaon is an independent professional the family hires directly, separate from the school and from any tuition centre, usually to work at home or online on a fixed weekly schedule. Most families searching for this want the same thing IB Gram's home tutoring option gives them: someone who comes to the house, keeps the arrangement confidential, and works to the school's own scheme of work rather than a generic syllabus. This matters more in the Diploma Programme (DP) than in most other courses, because six subjects, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) already compete for the same two years, and a private tutor has to fit into that structure, not add to it. What follows is how such an arrangement is actually set up, and where it differs from a school teacher's own extra classes.

contentBlocks.heading: How an IB Diploma Private Tutor Arrangement Starts in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
An IB Diploma private tutor in Gurgaon arrangement starts with a plain description of the student, not a form. Parents write in or book a free consultation and explain the board, the grade, which subjects sit at Higher Level (HL) and which at Standard Level (SL), and what is actually going wrong: a Chemistry paper 3 that keeps losing marks on method, or a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay draft that has stalled for three weeks. IB Gram asks about the school's own calendar before anything else. A tutor who does not know when a DP2 mock examination falls is guessing at timing the family already has in a school diary.

From there IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and match the subject, level and school context, never a single name pushed without alternatives. A demo or trial session comes next, usually at the family's own home or online, so the student and the tutor can work through a real past paper or TOK prompt together before anyone commits to a term. This is also where the family should raise anything about the school teacher's own extra classes, so the tutor knows not to duplicate territory the school already covers.

Once the family is satisfied, IB Gram helps set the practical terms: a weekly schedule that survives a school week already full of internal assessments and CAS commitments, how cancellations and rescheduled sessions are handled, and how often the parent hears back on progress. None of this replaces what the family and tutor agree directly, but it gives both sides a starting point instead of an awkward first conversation. If the fit turns out wrong after the trial, the family can ask for a different match rather than persist with a tutor who is not working.
items: 1. State the board, grade, HL and SL subjects, and the specific problem.
2. Share the school's mock and internal assessment dates so timing is realistic.
3. Review a shortlist of verified tutors matched to subject, level and school context.
4. Sit a free trial session working through a real past paper or TOK prompt.
5. Agree the weekly schedule, cancellation terms and how progress gets reported.

contentBlocks.heading: What the IB Diploma Actually Asks of a DP1 or DP2 Student
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) runs across two years, usually called DP1 and DP2 in Gurgaon schools, and an IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon who has not sat down with the actual structure is working blind. Six subjects are taken from six groups, three or four of them at Higher Level (HL), which carries around 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level (SL), around 150 hours. Each subject is graded on a scale of 1 to 7. That alone tells a tutor something a general tutor coming from CBSE or ICSE often misses: the job is not preparing a student for one final exam paper but for six parallel subjects that all demand attention across two years, on top of the core.

The core adds up to 3 more points through Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) combined, so the maximum a student can reach is 45. A tutor who understands this is effectively an IB 45 points tutor, someone who sees the diploma as six subjects and a core competing for the same two years, not a single exam to cram for. The minimum to be awarded the diploma is 24 points, subject to the IB's own failing conditions, which a good tutor explains honestly rather than glossing over. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) has to be completed as well, and while it does not add exam points, a school will not award the diploma without it.

Exam sessions run twice a year, in May and November. Most IB schools across Gurgaon enter their students for the May session, with November mostly used by a minority of schools and by students retaking a subject. Results from the May session are released in early July, which is the point most families finally see where the two years landed. A private tutor's work across DP1 and DP2 is to help the six subjects and the core share the hours they need without either side quietly losing out.

Higher Level (HL) carries about 240 recommended teaching hours per subject.
Standard Level (SL) subjects carry about 150 recommended teaching hours each.
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to 3 points to the total 45.
24 points is the minimum diploma award, subject to failing conditions.
Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May exam session, not November.

contentBlocks.heading: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS: Where a Private Tutor Actually Helps
contentBlocks.body:
Theory of Knowledge (TOK) is graded on two pieces of work. The exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts, runs to about 950 words of commentary, is marked inside the school, and counts for one third of the TOK grade. The essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for that exam session, runs to about 1,600 words, is marked externally, and carries the other two thirds. A private tutor can help a student unpack a prompt, test whether an example actually supports the claim being made, and read a draft against the areas of knowledge (history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics, the arts) the course covers alongside the core theme and two optional themes. What a tutor should never do is write toward the mark scheme for the student; TOK and EE grades run A to E, they combine for up to 3 diploma points, and an E in either is one of the IB's failing conditions, so the stakes are real even though the points look small.

The Extended Essay (EE) is an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words, roughly 40 hours of a student's own work, written in one DP subject or across two as an interdisciplinary essay. It is formally supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded as the essay develops. A private tutor sits alongside that supervision, not instead of it: helping the student narrow a research question, structure an argument, or prepare for the next reflection session. Because the EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, a careful tutor never quotes old criterion mark allocations from memory and instead works from whatever version the student's own DP coordinator has issued. This is what IB Diploma core support in Gurugram actually looks like in practice: steady help with TOK and the EE alongside the six subjects, not a rushed session before a deadline.

CAS asks for evidence across creativity, activity and service, logged over the two years. A tutor's role there is usually small, mostly a reminder that CAS still needs attention when six subjects and the core are eating every free hour.
items: TOK exhibition: three objects, one of 35 IA prompts, about 950 words.
TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles, about 1,600 words, marked externally.
Extended Essay: up to 4,000 words, about 40 hours, supervised at school.
An E grade in TOK or the EE is a failing condition for the diploma.
The EE guide changed for first assessment in 2027; follow the coordinator's version.

contentBlocks.body:

Families at schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge deal with the same underlying pressure: a DP2 mock examination date set by the school itself, usually several months before the May session, that quietly becomes the real deadline a private tutor works towards.

Each school sets its own mock schedule, and a private tutor's first real job in any new arrangement is finding out what that schedule actually is, rather than assuming it matches a generic IB calendar. Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's own official channels, and these are what show how marks are actually awarded, far more reliably than a tutor's memory of a similar question from a previous year. A tutor who has never sat with the school's own past paper set is working from guesswork.

Command terms carry real weight in DP answers: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, and to what extent each ask for a different depth of response, and a student who answers a discuss question at describe depth loses marks that have nothing to do with subject knowledge. A private tutor's work with the school calendar is mostly about protecting the weeks before a mock or the May session itself, when a student needs consolidation and past-paper practice, not new content arriving at the last minute.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring, Online or Hybrid: What Fits an IB Diploma Private Tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is the arrangement most families ask for first when they search for an IB Diploma private tutor in Gurgaon, and it is IB Gram's lead option for a reason: a tutor sitting across the table from a DP2 student, working through an actual past paper with the family's own study materials at hand, still gets a level of focus a screen does not always match. It also keeps the private nature of the arrangement, no shared platform, no account the school might ever see, which matters to families who specifically want confidentiality.

Online lessons trade some of that for reach and flexibility. Families who cannot arrange a home visit some weeks move to an IB Diploma online tutor in Gurgaon instead, then return to home sessions when the schedule allows. A subject specialist who does not live near Golf Course Road or Manesar becomes available, evening slots are easier to hold when neither side is fighting NH-48 traffic, and a shared whiteboard works well for annotating a TOK essay draft or a maths solution line by line. What online does not do as well is a subject that leans on physical materials, lab technique discussion, or a student who genuinely needs someone present in the room to stay focused through a two-hour session.

A hybrid pattern is what most private arrangements settle into by the second month: home sessions when the week allows it, online when travel time would eat into the actual lesson, especially in the weeks around a DP2 mock when every hour matters more than usual. The honest answer is that no single mode is right for every subject or every family. A Chemistry practical discussion often wants to be in person; a TOK essay redraft works perfectly well over a shared document online. The private tutor and the family are usually the ones best placed to decide, session by session, which one a given week needs.

Online lessons widen access to specialists beyond a family's own corridor.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Verifies a Private Tutor Before the First Session
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram shortlists as one of its IB Diploma tutors in Gurgaon has a verified profile before a family ever meets them: subject background, the boards and levels they actually teach, and their availability against what the family needs. This is checked before a shortlist goes out, not left for the family to discover on a first call. None of this is a claim about how many tutors are on the platform or how long anyone has been teaching; it is simply what gets confirmed before a name reaches a parent.

Parents should still check things themselves, and a private arrangement makes this more important, not less, because there is no school administration standing behind the tutor. Ask what boards and levels the tutor actually teaches day to day, not just what they say they can cover. Ask how they would approach the specific subject at hand; HL Chemistry looks nothing like SL Business Management in what a lesson needs. Ask what happens if a session has to be cancelled or moved, and get that answer in writing before the first regular week starts, alongside the schedule and how progress will be reported back.

Parents often ask how to find the best IB Diploma private tutor in Gurgaon; the honest answer is that 'best' depends entirely on subject fit, school pacing and whether the student and tutor actually work well together, which is exactly what a free trial or demo session tests. Watch how the tutor handles a genuine question the student is stuck on, not a rehearsed explanation, and whether they ask about the school's own scheme of work before diving into a topic. If the fit is wrong after the trial, IB Gram can offer a different match; there is no obligation to continue with a tutor who does not suit the student, and saying so early costs far less than persisting through a term that is not working.

contentBlocks.heading: Private Tutor or the School's Own Teacher: What Changes for an IB Diploma Family?
contentBlocks.body:
Some Gurgaon families are offered extra classes by their child's own school teacher, sometimes informally, sometimes as a paid arrangement outside school hours. It is worth naming the conflict plainly: a teacher who also grades a student's internal work, or who reports to the same DP coordinator overseeing the diploma, is not in a neutral position when that same teacher is also being paid privately by the family. It is not that this arrangement is always wrong, but a family should go into it with eyes open about where the teacher's incentives sit, and an independent IB Diploma private tutor in Gurgaon removes that question entirely by sitting outside the school altogether.

An independent private tutor works to the school's own scheme of work without being part of the school. That distinction matters in practice. A good private tutor asks what topic the class is on, what the next internal assessment covers, and what the mock exam will test, then plans lessons around that rather than running a separate syllabus. What a private tutor should never do is complete a student's school tasks for them: an internal assessment write-up, a lab report, a piece of coursework submitted under the student's name. That crosses from tutoring into academic dishonesty, and IB schools take it seriously. The honest line is support with understanding and practice, not production of the work itself.

Confidentiality is often the real reason a family chooses private over school-based help in the first place. A student struggling with a subject, or dealing with something the school does not need to know about in detail, gets a tutor whose only obligation is to the family. That only holds if it is agreed clearly at the start: what the tutor will and will not report to anyone at school, how session notes are kept, and whether the family wants updates verbally or in writing. None of this needs to be a formal contract, but a short written note covering the schedule, cancellation terms, confidentiality and how progress gets communicated saves an awkward conversation three months in, when memories of what was agreed have already started to differ.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Progress Look Like With a Private IB Diploma Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any private arrangement that claims otherwise is not being honest with the family. What a reasonable arrangement can show, within the first four weeks, is a clearer picture of where the student actually stands: which command terms they consistently misread, whether an HL subject needs more structural support than an SL one, how close a TOK essay draft is to answering the actual prescribed title rather than a version of it the student prefers.

Progress in a subject with a defined syllabus, like HL Mathematics or SL Economics, tends to show up in marked practice against real past papers and mark schemes, where a parent can see specific marks gained on specific question types. Progress in the core is slower to see. A TOK essay improves draft by draft, not lesson by lesson, and an Extended Essay's roughly 40 hours of research does not compress into a few sessions no matter how good the tutor is. A family expecting fast, visible movement on the EE or TOK inside a month will likely be disappointed, and a private tutor who says so honestly at the start is more useful than one who promises otherwise.

Starting later in DP2, close to mocks or the May session, narrows what is realistically possible. A tutor coming in during that window is usually triaging rather than teaching from scratch, and a family should hear that plainly rather than be told everything can still be fixed. The most useful private tutors are the ones who say, early, what four weeks can and cannot change.

faqs.question: Is a private IB Diploma tutor different from IB Gram's regular tutoring service?
faqs.answer: Not in how IB Gram sets it up, only in framing: 'private' here usually means a family wants an independent, confidential arrangement rather than a class through the school. IB Gram already works this way by default, matching a verified tutor to the student's board, subjects and level, running the trial and first sessions, and leaving the schedule, confidentiality and reporting to be agreed directly between the tutor and the family. There is no separate 'private' product to opt into; it is simply the standard shape of the arrangement.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher be their private tutor?
faqs.answer: It is possible, but it carries a real conflict of interest that families should think through before agreeing. A teacher who also grades the student's internal work or reports to the same DP coordinator is not fully neutral once money changes hands privately for extra classes outside school. Many families prefer an independent IB Diploma private tutor for exactly this reason: no grading relationship, no reporting line back into the school, and a clearer confidentiality boundary. If a family still chooses the school teacher route, it helps to agree openly what stays separate from the classroom.

faqs.question: Will the tutor do my child's Extended Essay or internal assessment for them?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor who offers to is not someone to work with. The Extended Essay (EE) is formally supervised by a teacher at the student's own school, with reflection sessions recorded along the way; a private tutor supports the student's own research and drafting around that supervision. The same applies to internal assessments and coursework: a tutor helps the student understand, plan and practise, never produces the work under the student's name. IB schools treat this as academic dishonesty, and it puts the diploma itself at risk.

faqs.question: What should we agree with a private tutor before starting?
faqs.answer: Get the schedule, cancellation terms, confidentiality and how progress will be reported agreed in writing before the first regular week, even if it is a short note rather than a formal contract. Cover what the tutor will tell the school, if anything, how session notes are kept, and what happens if a session needs to move. Families who skip this step often find themselves disagreeing later about what was actually promised. IB Gram can help set these practical terms once a tutor is shortlisted, but the final agreement is between the tutor and the family.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Diploma private tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not quote fees here because cost depends on the level, HL or SL, the subject, and the schedule agreed with the tutor, and it should be discussed directly once a shortlist is ready. What is fixed is the structure around it: a free trial or demo session before anything is agreed for the term, and availability that depends on the subject and level requested. Ask for the cost structure in writing alongside the schedule, so there is no ambiguity once regular sessions begin.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor travel to our society on Golf Course Road on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, and Golf Course Road, covering DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1 and the sectors around it, is where a lot of home tuition for IB Diploma students already happens. Gate entry and visitor registration at societies such as DLF The Magnolias or DLF The Aralias add a few minutes to the start of a session, which a tutor plans for rather than treats as a delay. Evening slots are the most requested time, and availability depends on the specific tutor and subject, so it is worth confirming timing early in the shortlist conversation.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we picked is not working out?
faqs.answer: Say so as soon as it is clear, rather than waiting out the term hoping it improves. IB Gram can offer a different match if the fit is wrong, whether that is teaching style, pace, or simply not clicking with the student. This is easier to fix early, before a family has invested weeks in a pattern that is not helping. A private arrangement should not feel like something to endure; if a tutor is not moving the student forward after a fair trial, changing is the practical choice.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor need to be present in our home during the session?
faqs.answer: A parent does not need to sit in on the lesson itself, though most families stay reachable in the house, especially for the first few sessions while trust builds. What matters more is a quiet space with a desk, the student's own materials and past papers, and a reasonable amount of privacy for a subject the student may find difficult to discuss. Some families in Palam Vihar and similar areas prefer the first session with a parent nearby, then step back once the pattern is established; that choice is entirely the family's to make.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB Diploma student typically need?
faqs.answer: This depends on the subject, the level, and how close the student is to a mock or the May session, so IB Gram discusses frequency once the board, grade and specific problem are known rather than fixing a number in advance. A student in DP1 exploring a new HL subject may want a different weekly pattern than one in DP2 finishing coursework before a mock. Frequency can also change through the year, stepping up before assessments and easing off after, which is normal and worth agreeing with the tutor as the term goes.

faqs.question: Does the private tutor need to follow the school's own pacing?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearest differences between a good private arrangement and a generic one. A tutor who plans lessons around a separate syllabus, ignoring what the class covered that week, ends up working against the school rather than alongside it. IB Gram asks tutors to work from the school's scheme of work and recent test or mock results where the family can share them, so lessons reinforce what the student is already being taught rather than adding a second, disconnected curriculum on top.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor help before a DP2 mock examination in Manesar or Golf Course Road?
faqs.answer: Yes, though what helps most changes close to a mock: less new content, more marked practice against real past papers and mark schemes, and a focus on command terms the student keeps misreading. Families in Manesar and along NH-48 sometimes shift to online sessions in this period if evening traffic makes a home visit impractical on a tight week, which is a reasonable trade-off when time before the mock is short. The goal in these final weeks is consolidation, not new material.

A request for an IB Diploma online tutor in Gurgaon starts differently from a home-visit one: location within Gurgaon barely matters, since nothing needs to be reached by road, but the exact subject, level and syllabus specificity matter more, because the whole point of going online is usually to access a genuinely well-matched specialist rather than whoever happens to live nearby. From there, a coordinator checks tutor profiles for subject and level history, filters for tutors experienced specifically in teaching online, not just tutors who happen to be available on a call, since the two skills are not the same. A tutor who is excellent in person does not automatically explain a graph clearly through a shared screen, and IB Gram's shortlist accounts for that distinction rather than assuming it does not matter.

A free trial session follows, run exactly as a regular online lesson would be, so the family sees the real setup: how the tutor uses a shared whiteboard, how they share and annotate a past paper, and how clearly they explain over a screen rather than in person. contentBlocks.heading: The Diploma's 45 Points, Explained for an Online Lesson Plan
contentBlocks.body:
Every subject in the IB Diploma is graded on the same 1 to 7 scale, whether it is taken at Higher Level or Standard Level, and an online tutor needs to plan around that scale from the first session rather than treating all subjects as equally weighted in the family's attention. A student takes six subjects, one from each of six subject groups, with three or four at Higher Level, carrying 240 recommended teaching hours, and the remainder at Standard Level, carrying 150 hours; that hours difference is real and shows up in how much an online tutor can realistically cover per session across a busy week.

On top of the six subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combine for up to 3 more points, taking the maximum to 45, with 24 points as the minimum needed for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, including an automatic fail if either TOK or the EE is graded E. An online tutor discussing a student's overall standing should be precise about this structure rather than vague, since a family often assumes every point counts equally when the core and the six subjects actually interact through separate rules.

Creativity, Activity, Service sits alongside all of this, ungraded on the point scale but still a completion requirement, and does not fit neatly into an online lesson the way subject content does; it is better tracked through a short check-in than taught as a topic. Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May exam session, with results out in early July, while a minority of schools and any retake candidates use November instead, a distinction an online tutor working across a full DP1-DP2 cycle should confirm with each family rather than assume.

Higher Level carries 240 recommended teaching hours; Standard Level carries 150.
TOK and EE combine for up to 3 extra points, toward a 45-point maximum.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Parts of TOK, the EE and Six Subjects Suit a Screen?
contentBlocks.body:
Theory of Knowledge translates onto a screen reasonably well for the essay side of the assessment: the essay answers one of six prescribed titles released for a given exam session, runs up to 1,600 words, is externally assessed and carries two thirds of the TOK grade, and drafting, structuring and refining an argument is work that a shared document and a video call handle comfortably. The exhibition is trickier online: it links three objects to one of 35 prescribed IA prompts, stays under 950 words, is internally assessed by the school, and counts for the remaining third of the grade, and because it depends on real, physical objects the student has chosen, an online tutor is better used to sharpen the written commentary around the objects than to replace the process of choosing them.

The Extended Essay, an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of work across the two years, supervised throughout by a teacher at the student's own school with recorded reflection sessions, suits online support well for the writing and argument stages, since a shared document with tracked comments lets a tutor mark up a draft precisely. It suits it less well for the earlier research stage, where a student benefits from working alongside someone who can point directly at a source or a method, not just discuss it after the fact. Because the EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, an online tutor should never quote specific criterion mark allocations; the version the student's own DP coordinator issues is the one to follow, full stop.

Across the six subjects themselves, a screen suits a worked mathematics problem, an annotated past paper, or an essay-structure discussion very well through a shared whiteboard, but suits practical laboratory technique, oral language practice with real-time correction of pronunciation nuance, or art and design portfolio critique in physical media considerably less well, and a family should weigh this honestly by subject rather than assume online works equally for all six.

TOK exhibition depends on chosen physical objects; online is better for sharpening the commentary.
EE writing and argument stages suit tracked-comment document review; the research stage suits it less.
A shared whiteboard suits worked maths problems and annotated past papers well online.
Practical lab technique and physical-media art critique suit a screen far less well.

Across all three corridors, the honest trade-off is the same: online buys back time and widens specialist access, but it does not replace a tutor physically present to watch a student's working on paper in real time, which is exactly why IB Gram keeps home tutoring and hybrid genuinely available for any family in these corridors who wants it, not just as a footnote.

contentBlocks.heading: The DP2 Calendar an Online Tutor Should Already Know
contentBlocks.body:
Online tutoring works best when a tutor already understands the calendar a DP student is working against, rather than treating every session as a blank slate. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; schools are named only to describe the general calendar pressures Gurgaon DP families report, never as a claim about any school's own curriculum or programme.

Across schools such as Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge, families describe DP2 mock examinations, set independently by each school, landing several months ahead of the May exam session, with TOK essay drafts, EE reflection sessions and CAS completion all converging in the same stretch of term. An online tutor should ask a new family directly when these fall this year rather than assuming a generic timetable, since a session plan built around the wrong dates wastes weeks a DP2 student does not have.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, govern the depth every exam answer needs, and this is one area where a shared screen genuinely helps: a tutor can pull up a real past-paper question, highlight the command term, and talk a student through exactly how much depth it demands, live and in the moment. Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports from the school or the IB's own official channels remain the actual source of how marks are awarded, and a good online tutor builds sessions around them rather than generic revision notes.

contentBlocks.heading: Online Leads Here, But Home Tutoring and Hybrid Are Real Options
contentBlocks.body:
For this page, online is the starting point, and for good reason: a live one-to-one session on a shared screen, with a digital whiteboard and annotated past papers, removes travel entirely and opens up specialist tutors across all of Gurgaon rather than just the ones near a particular sector. For a Higher Level subject where genuinely strong subject-specific tutors are thin on the ground, online is often simply the more practical starting point, not a compromise.

Even so, home tutoring is a real option, not a lesser one, and some students and some subjects need it. A student who is easily distracted without someone physically present, a younger DP1 student still building study habits, or a subject like laboratory-based Chemistry where watching technique in person matters, often does better with a home tutor. A parent should not assume online is automatically the more convenient default; for some families, a tutor sitting at the table changes how seriously a session gets taken.

Hybrid, online for most weeks with an occasional home session, particularly around a mock or a difficult topic, is what a good number of families using this page eventually settle into, treating the two modes as complementary rather than competing. In plain terms: choose online first when specialist fit and eliminating travel matter most; choose home tutoring when presence and focus matter more than reach; choose hybrid when a family wants the best of both across a demanding two-year course, and revisit the choice honestly if the first few weeks show it is not working as expected.

Home tutoring: better for easily distracted students, younger DP1 students, and lab-based subjects.
Hybrid: online for most weeks, home around a mock or a genuinely difficult topic.
Online widens access to a strong Higher Level specialist regardless of where they live.
Revisit the choice honestly if the first few weeks show it is not working.

contentBlocks.heading: How Are Online IB Diploma Tutors Verified in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Without a home visit, verification has to work differently, and IB Gram treats that seriously rather than lightly. Every tutor's subject and level history is checked before their profile is shown, along with specific experience teaching online, not just general subject expertise, since explaining a graph clearly through a shared screen is a distinct skill from explaining it in person. This checking happens before a family ever sees a name, so a shortlist for an online tutor is not simply whoever happened to be free on a call.

A parent should still ask direct questions before committing. Ask how the tutor structures a session on screen: do they use a shared whiteboard, how do they annotate a past paper live, and what happens if the connection drops mid-explanation. Ask how they check a student is actually following along rather than just nodding at a webcam, since this is genuinely harder to judge online than in person. And ask for a specific example of how they have adapted a subject, laboratory science especially, for online delivery, since a vague answer here is a real warning sign.

During the trial session, watch whether the tutor's screen-sharing and annotation actually work smoothly, whether they check understanding with real questions rather than a generic 'does that make sense,' and whether the session ends with a clear plan rather than trailing off. A parent sitting in briefly on part of the trial, even for an online session, is a reasonable way to judge this directly rather than relying on the student's own report afterward.

contentBlocks.heading: Setting Up an Online Lesson That Actually Works
contentBlocks.body:
A good online lesson depends more on a handful of practical basics than on expensive equipment, unlike a home tutoring session where the tutor brings adaptability with them; getting the basics right before the first session avoids most of the friction families run into. A laptop or desktop with a stable internet connection matters more than a phone or tablet for most subjects, since a shared whiteboard, an annotated PDF and a video call running together need a proper screen and a keyboard nearby; a phone can work for a quick check-in but struggles for a full lesson involving working shown on screen. A quiet, well-lit room with a proper desk, not a bed or a sofa, keeps a student in a working frame of mind the way a physical classroom does, and a decent pair of headphones cuts down background noise on both sides, which matters more in a busy Gurgaon household in the evening than families often expect.

What suits a screen and what does not varies genuinely by task, not just by subject. A worked mathematics problem, with the tutor and student writing on a shared digital whiteboard in real time, transfers to a screen almost as well as it works in person, and an annotated past paper, marked up live with a stylus or a mouse, is often clearer on screen than on paper because both sides see exactly the same marks at the same time. Essay planning and argument structure, for TOK or the Extended Essay, also suits a shared document well, since edits and comments are visible and trackable in a way a handwritten margin note is not.

What suits a screen less well is anything that depends on physical presence: laboratory technique in Chemistry or Biology, where a tutor needs to see a student's actual hand movements and lab safety habits up close; oral language work requiring precise, real-time correction of pronunciation; and any subject where a student's body language, fidgeting, disengagement, genuine confusion, is easier to miss through a small video window than across a table. A good online tutor names these limits honestly rather than pretending a screen handles everything a home tutoring session would.

Families choose online for reasons that are usually specific rather than vague: escaping evening traffic on a particular corridor, reaching a Higher Level specialist who simply does not live nearby, fitting a session in during a genuinely packed DP2 week where even a short commute is one commitment too many, or a student who is simply more comfortable and less self-conscious on a screen than in person. None of these reasons is wrong, but a family should be honest with themselves about which one actually applies, since the honest reason usually points to whether online, home or hybrid is the better long-term fit.

contentBlocks.heading: Is the Online Diploma Tutor Working After Three Sessions?
contentBlocks.body:
Three sessions is usually enough to judge whether an IB Diploma online tutor in Gurgaon is genuinely working, and a family does not need to wait a full term to find out. After the first session, check whether the technical setup actually worked, no dropped calls, clear audio, a whiteboard both sides could use comfortably, since a shaky setup undermines everything else regardless of how good the tutor's teaching is. If the technical side is fine but the student seems disengaged, that is worth naming directly rather than assuming it will improve on its own.

By the second or third session, look for a specific sign of actual teaching, not just time spent: has the tutor identified a concrete gap in the student's understanding, given a piece of work with real feedback rather than a generic 'well done,' and adjusted their approach based on how the previous session went. A tutor delivering the same style of session regardless of what happened last time is not adapting, and that is a fair basis to raise a concern or ask for a different match.

Watch the student too, not just the tutor. A student who engages more openly with a specific tutor by the third session, asking their own questions rather than only answering the tutor's, is usually a good sign that the online format and the tutor's style both suit them. A student who stays passive, camera off, one-word answers, minimal engagement, across three sessions despite the tutor's efforts may simply need the physical presence a home tutor provides instead, and that is a legitimate conclusion, not a failure of the online format in general.

No tutor, online or otherwise, can guarantee a grade, and a family should treat any claim otherwise with real scepticism. What a good online tutor can offer is honest, session-by-session feedback and a plan that adjusts as the two-year Diploma progresses, not a fixed script delivered the same way regardless of how the student is actually responding.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started With an Online IB Diploma Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started with an IB Diploma online tutor in Gurgaon is straightforward. Tell IB Gram the subjects and levels needed, confirm the device the student will use (a laptop is strongly preferred over a phone for most subjects), and share evening slots that realistically work around school and other commitments. If a mock or an EE deadline is close, mention it, since it changes how the shortlist is prioritised.

Before the first session, do a short technical check: confirm the video platform works on the chosen device, test the camera and microphone, and make sure the student's desk has space for a notebook alongside the screen, not just the screen alone. None of this needs to be elaborate; five minutes the evening before is usually enough to avoid the first session being eaten by technical troubleshooting.

The first session itself is diagnostic, much like a home tutoring visit would be: the tutor reviews recent topics, looks at a past test or draft if one is available, and works through a problem or passage on the shared whiteboard to see how the student actually reasons. It should end with a specific, named observation, not a vague sense that things went fine. Parents should expect a brief check-in at the start to confirm the plan, even for an online session.

If the online arrangement is not the right fit after the trial or the first few sessions, IB Gram will arrange a different tutor, or switch the family to home tutoring or hybrid lessons instead, subject to availability. Regular sessions can usually start within the same week, and the first few weeks are treated as a settling-in period where either side can flag an adjustment.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram also offer home tutoring for the IB Diploma, or is it online only?

faqs.question: Can a home session be arranged occasionally even if we mostly want online lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is exactly what hybrid arrangements are for, and IB Gram supports switching between modes rather than locking a family into one permanently. Many families keep online as the default for weeknights and add an occasional home tutoring session on a weekend, particularly before a mock or when a subject needs closer, in-person supervision. Mention this preference when setting up your shortlist so a tutor comfortable with both modes is matched from the start.

faqs.question: What if a parent wants to be present during an online lesson?
faqs.answer: That is entirely reasonable and common, particularly for a younger DP1 student or in the first few sessions with a new tutor. A parent can sit within view of the screen, or simply be in the house and check in at the start and end, without disrupting the lesson itself. Most tutors are used to this and structure the session normally regardless of whether a parent is watching closely or checking in briefly.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Diploma online tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate, since cost depends on the subject, level and session length; a coordinator discusses the structure directly once your requirements are confirmed. What stays consistent is the process: a verified tutor with specific online-teaching experience, a free trial session run exactly like a normal lesson, and the option to switch to a different tutor, or to home tutoring or hybrid lessons, if the fit is not right.

faqs.question: What happens if the internet connection drops during a lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask this directly before committing, since it happens occasionally in any online arrangement. A good tutor has a simple fallback, reconnecting quickly, continuing by phone briefly if needed, or picking up exactly where the session left off next time, rather than treating a dropped call as a lost session. A stable connection on both sides reduces how often this comes up, but no online arrangement is entirely immune to it.

faqs.answer: Usually within the same week, since online tutors are not limited by travel time to a particular corridor of Gurgaon, such as DLF Phases 2 to 4 or Sohna Road, the way home tutors sometimes are, which often makes matching faster. faqs.question: What if a scheduled online session needs to move because of school commitments?
faqs.answer: This is common given how a DP student's evenings shift, and a good online tutor should handle it without friction, often more easily than a home tutoring visit since there is no travel to reschedule around. contentBlocks.heading: What the MYP Actually Demands, Year by Year
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme runs across five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly Grades 6 to 10, and it does not grade the way CBSE or ICSE report cards do. Every subject is marked against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8. A student's criterion total out of 32 is then converted into a final grade from 1 to 7 using the International Baccalaureate's own grade boundaries, which is why two students with similar effort can land on different final grades if one is consistently weak on a single criterion.

This structure changes what a tutor should actually be doing in a session. Improving a Criterion C mark in MYP Language and Literature is a different exercise from improving Criterion A in MYP Mathematics, and a tutor who treats every subject the same way, drilling content without reference to the criteria, will not move the mark much. A good MYP tutor works from the actual rubric language the school uses and shows the student what separates a 5 from a 7 on each criterion, not just what the right answer is.

Two milestones sit inside this five-year run and deserve early attention. The Community Project, usually completed in MYP 3 or MYP 4, asks students to plan and carry out a piece of service or action learning and reflect on it. The Personal Project, in MYP 5, is a longer independent piece of work supervised by the school, and it is often the first time a student has had to manage a term-long deadline alone. Some schools also offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations combined with ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides for itself whether to run it, so check with your child's coordinator rather than assuming.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP Subject Criteria: Maths, Sciences and Language
contentBlocks.body:
Ask what a specific subject actually rewards, because the four criteria are not the same shape in every subject, and a tutor who does not know the difference is guessing. MYP Mathematics is assessed on Criterion A, Knowing and Understanding; Criterion B, Investigating Patterns; Criterion C, Communicating; and Criterion D, Applying Mathematics in Real-Life Contexts. Many schools split MYP 4 and MYP 5 maths into standard and extended pathways, and the extended route covers additional topics that matter later, since it is the pathway that prepares a student for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. A tutor should know early which pathway your child is on, since revising the wrong one wastes weeks.

MYP Sciences uses its own four criteria: Knowing and Understanding, Inquiring and Designing, Processing and Evaluating, and Reflecting on the Impacts of Science. Criterion B and C usually sit inside practical or investigation work, and students who are strong on recall but weak on designing a fair test often lose marks here without realising why, which a subject specialist should spot within the first session or two.

MYP Language and Literature is marked on Analysing, Organizing, Producing Text and Using Language, while MYP Language Acquisition, for a second or additional language, runs on Listening, Reading, Speaking and Writing across six phases rather than year groups. A student's phase, not their grade level, decides what they are actually assessed on in Language Acquisition, and it is common for a Gurgaon family to move a child up a phase mid-year once fluency improves, which a tutor working from the wrong phase would miss entirely.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP Timelines at Gurgaon's International Schools
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon has a cluster of international schools running the IB continuum, and families moving between CBSE, ICSE and the MYP often underestimate how differently these schools pace the school year around the programme's own milestones rather than a single annual board exam. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; we mention schools only to describe the calendar pressures families here actually deal with.

Most MYP schools in Gurgaon run on a term system with internal assessments spread across the year rather than one exam season, so a student can be handing in a Sciences investigation, preparing a Language and Literature oral, and starting Community or Personal Project work within the same few weeks. That overlap is normal in the MYP, but it catches families off guard when they are used to a single board exam calendar, and it is exactly when a tutor's help matters most, not the week before a single big test.

Report timing also varies by school: some issue criterion-level feedback every term, others only twice a year, and a tutor who has not seen the actual report format can waste a session explaining a grading system rather than closing a gap. Ask your child's coordinator for the exact dates of internal assessments, Community or Personal Project checkpoints and report issue, then share that calendar with the tutor early, so lessons are timed to what is actually due rather than a generic revision schedule. Families who share the school calendar in the first week consistently get more useful early sessions than those who wait.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Suits Your MYP Student?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is IB Gram's default for MYP because a tutor sitting beside the student, working through the same rubric the school uses, catches small misunderstandings that are easy to miss on a screen: a criterion phrase misread, a working step skipped, a diagram drawn slightly wrong. For a student in Class 7 or 8 still building independent study habits, having someone physically present tends to hold attention better across a 60 or 90 minute session than a video call does.

Online lessons suit different situations well. If the family needs a specific MYP Sciences or Language and Literature specialist who is not based near their sector, or if evening traffic on a corridor like SPR makes a home visit unreliable on a given day, an online session with a shared whiteboard and annotated past criterion work can cover the same ground. Online also makes late weekday slots easier, since the tutor is not travelling between two lessons.

Hybrid, mixing home and online across a week or a term, is what many Gurgaon families settle into by month two: home sessions when deep, criterion-by-criterion work is needed, online sessions for shorter check-ins or when the calendar or traffic makes a home visit hard that week.

In short: choose home tuition for younger MYP students and for subjects needing close, in-person marking; choose online when the right specialist is not local or the schedule is tight; choose hybrid once you know your family's actual weekly rhythm. None of these is universally better, and a tutor who insists on only one mode regardless of what a subject or a week needs is not adapting to your child.

We look for direct experience with MYP's four-criteria structure in the subject you need, not just general subject knowledge, because a tutor who has never marked against Criterion B or D in Sciences will take weeks to catch up to a tutor who has. We also check that a tutor's stated availability actually matches your schedule, since a shortlist built on an outdated calendar helps no one.

There is also work you should do yourself before the first home visit or the first online call. Ask the tutor directly which MYP subjects and years they have taught, and ask for one example of how they would mark a piece of your child's actual work against the criteria, not a hypothetical. If a home tutor is coming to your society, confirm they are comfortable with your gate's visitor registration process and will arrive within the agreed window. contentBlocks.heading: What Separates an MYP Specialist From a General Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
A general tutor can usually help a student revise content. An MYP specialist does something more specific: they can look at a criterion-level comment on a report, for instance 'limited use of mathematical language to communicate reasoning' under Criterion C, and translate it into exactly what the student should practise differently next week. That translation is the actual value of a specialist, and it is what a family should be paying for when they search for an IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon rather than a general school-subjects tutor.

Ask a prospective tutor to explain, in their own words, what separates a 6 from an 8 on one criterion in your child's subject. A specialist answers specifically, pointing to command terms, the level of independence expected, or how much justification a criterion wants. A general tutor tends to answer vaguely, talking about working harder or being more careful, which tells you they have not actually taught inside this system.

After the trial lesson, ask three more things. First, what did they notice about your child's current level on each relevant criterion, not just whether the answer was right. Second, what would the next four weeks of sessions actually focus on, and why that order. Third, how would they know within a month whether it is working, since a student seeming more confident is not evidence and a specific criterion moving is.

A tutor who has taught MYP Personal or Community Project supervision is worth asking about separately if your child is in MYP 3, 4 or 5, since guiding independent, term-long work is a different skill from subject tutoring and not every subject specialist does it well. None of this replaces the school's own teacher, who remains the authority on what is actually being assessed; a good MYP tutor works alongside that, not around it.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should MYP Progress Look Like After a Month?
contentBlocks.body:
By four weeks, you should be able to point to something specific: a criterion score that has moved, a type of question the student now answers without help, or a habit, like showing full working in maths or referencing sources properly in Individuals and Societies, that has become automatic rather than prompted. If a month has passed and you cannot name anything concrete, that is worth raising directly with the tutor rather than assuming it will resolve itself.

Progress in the MYP is rarely a straight line. A student can improve steadily on Criterion A while staying flat on Criterion C for a while longer, because the two skills develop at different rates, and a tutor should be able to tell you which criterion they are prioritising this month and why, not present every session as equally focused on everything.

Be honest about limits too. A tutor cannot guarantee a grade, and any tutor who promises one should be treated with caution rather than relief. Starting tutoring two weeks before a report is due narrows what is realistically achievable to exam technique and gap-filling rather than deeper understanding, and it is better to say that plainly than to promise a jump that criterion-based assessment does not really allow in a fortnight. Equally, some students genuinely do not need a tutor at all, just a clearer study routine at home and slightly more structured revision before internal assessments, and a good tutor will say so rather than keep a family on indefinitely.

If, after a fair run of six to eight weeks, nothing specific has changed, that is a signal to ask IB Gram for a different match rather than a reason to give up on tutoring altogether.
