faqs.question: Is a general tutor enough for MYP, or does my child need a specialist?
faqs.answer: A general tutor can help with content revision, but MYP is marked against four criteria per subject, and someone unfamiliar with that system will struggle to explain why a piece of work scored a 5 rather than a 7. For a student who is broadly fine but needs occasional homework support, a general tutor may be adequate. For a student losing marks on a specific criterion, term after term, a subject specialist who has taught inside MYP's criterion-based assessment will close that gap faster, because they know exactly what each criterion is actually asking for.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: You can ask IB Gram for a different tutor at any point, and we will shortlist another match rather than asking you to persist with a bad fit. A tutor not working out usually shows up as flat criterion scores, a student who has stopped engaging, or sessions that feel like revision without direction. Tell us specifically what is not working, whether it is pace, subject depth, or personality, since that helps us shortlist better the second time. There is no obligation to continue with a tutor who is not helping your child.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for MYP, or is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: Both work; the better choice depends on the subject and the student. Online lessons, with a shared whiteboard and annotated criterion-marked work, cover most MYP content well, and many families use online for a specialist who is not based near their sector, or for late weekday slots when a home visit is hard. Home tuition tends to suit younger MYP students and subjects needing close, in-person marking of working or written text. Many Gurgaon families end up with a hybrid arrangement, home sessions for deeper work and online for shorter check-ins across the week.

faqs.question: My child is switching from CBSE to a school running the MYP mid-year, will a tutor help?
faqs.answer: Yes, a tutor experienced with the MYP can make that switch considerably smoother, since the criterion-based system is genuinely different from a percentage-based board and the adjustment is more about approach than content. The first few sessions usually focus on what each criterion is actually asking for and how command terms like 'evaluate' or 'justify' differ from what CBSE assessments expect, rather than reteaching subject content the student already knows. Most students adapt within a term once they understand how their work is being read, and a tutor who has made this transition before will get there faster.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an MYP student need?
faqs.answer: Most MYP students manage well with one or two sessions a week per subject, though this depends on the year, the subject and how close a report or project deadline is. A student generally on track might need one session a week for maintenance, while a student preparing for a Personal Project deadline or catching up after a weak report may need two sessions in a subject temporarily. IB Gram will suggest a starting frequency based on what you describe, and it can be adjusted after the first few weeks once the tutor has a clearer picture.

faqs.question: What does the free trial or demo class actually cover?
faqs.answer: The trial is a real lesson, usually working through a recent piece of your child's actual work or a topic the school is currently teaching, so you and the tutor can both judge fit before committing. You will see how the tutor explains criteria, how they handle a mistake, and whether the pace suits your child, rather than a sales pitch about the tutor's background. There is no obligation to continue after the trial, and if it does not feel right, IB Gram will shortlist a different tutor.

faqs.question: How soon can a tutor start?
faqs.answer: Start times depend on tutor availability for the specific subject, year and schedule you need, so it is worth sending your query as early as possible rather than the week before a report is due. Once IB Gram has your requirements, shortlisting and arranging a first trial session usually happens quickly, subject to the matched tutor's schedule. If your timeline is urgent, a mock or internal assessment coming up in two weeks, say so in your first message, since it changes which tutors we prioritise showing you.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travel to our society in Sushant Lok on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, Sushant Lok is one of the corridors IB Gram's home tutors reach comfortably on weekday evenings, since travel between societies in this part of Gurgaon is generally manageable even during peak traffic hours. You should still confirm your society's gate entry and visitor registration process with the tutor before the first visit, since that can add a few minutes either side of the lesson. If your evening slot is tight because of school pickup or an activity, mention it upfront so the tutor plans travel time around it.

faqs.question: What if there is no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly with IB Gram rather than waiting it out; a month with no nameable change, no criterion score moving, no habit becoming automatic, is a fair point to review the match. Sometimes the fix is a change in what the tutor is focusing on, and sometimes it means a different tutor suits your child better. Progress in the MYP is rarely a straight line across all four criteria at once, so ask specifically which criterion the tutor has been prioritising before assuming nothing is happening.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help with the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Yes, within academic integrity rules: a tutor can help a student plan their timeline, talk through their process journal, and give feedback on drafts, but the Personal Project must remain the student's own independent work, supervised by the school. Guiding a term-long independent project is a different skill from subject tutoring, so it is worth asking a prospective tutor specifically about their experience with Personal or Community Project supervision if your child is in MYP 3, 4 or 5. The school's own project supervisor remains the final authority on what is submitted.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who cover DLF or Southern Peripheral Road for evening slots?
faqs.answer: Yes, IB Gram matches home and online tutors across Gurgaon, including corridors like Southern Peripheral Road, though evening availability there depends more on the specific tutor's base and the traffic on a given day than in more central areas. For SPR families, many settle into a pattern of one or two home evenings plus a weekend slot, with online available as a backup on days when a home visit is not practical. Mention your exact sector when you send your query so we can match availability realistically.

contentBlocks.heading: The Middle Years Programme, Decoded for Parents New to It
contentBlocks.body:
If your family is new to the Middle Years Programme (MYP), the first thing to unlearn is the percentage. A report that says 5, 6, 7, 5 across four criteria is not a percentage in disguise; it is a direct statement about four separate skills, and the International Baccalaureate (IB) wants you to read it that way. The programme runs five years, MYP 1 through MYP 5, for students roughly aged 11 to 16, Grades 6 to 10 in the way schools across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, usually describe it, across eight subject groups.

Every one of those subjects is marked the same way: four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8. The total out of 32 converts to a final grade from 1 to 7, but through grade boundaries the IB sets independently for each subject and session, not a fixed formula a tutor or a parent can calculate at home. This is precisely why a tutor unfamiliar with MYP tends to focus on the wrong thing, chasing a total score rather than the specific criterion holding it down.

Two projects sit outside the regular subject groups. The Community Project, usually completed in MYP 3 or MYP 4, and the Personal Project, completed in MYP 5, are both marked on planning, research and reflection rather than subject content, and both carry real weight in how a school views a student's overall engagement with the programme. MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios offered in MYP 5, is optional, and whether a given school runs it is entirely that school's own decision, something worth confirming directly with the school rather than assuming from an older sibling's experience or a neighbour's account.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP Maths, Sciences and Language: What a Specialist Actually Marks
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor who genuinely knows MYP Mathematics can tell you, within a session, which of the four criteria is actually weak, and that distinction changes everything about how the lessons run. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is technique, and it responds fastest to straightforward revision. Criterion B, investigating patterns, asks a student to spot a rule across a set of numbers or shapes and justify it, a skill built through deliberate practice rather than repetition of familiar question types. Criterion C, communicating, judges whether working is laid out so another person could follow it, and it is often the quickest criterion to improve once a tutor points out the specific habits losing marks. Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, tends to move slowest, because it depends on judgement in an unfamiliar scenario rather than a rehearsed method. Many Gurgaon schools split MYP 4 and MYP 5 mathematics into standard and extended; extended feeds directly into Diploma Programme (DP) Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA), and a good tutor should be able to say early which pathway suits your child.

MYP Sciences follows a parallel structure across Biology, Chemistry and Physics: A tests recall, B tests whether a student can design a fair investigation, C tests processing and evaluating data, and D asks for reflection on the impact of science on society and the environment, a criterion often under-prepared because it reads less like conventional science.

Language subjects split similarly. MYP Language and Literature marks analysing, organising, producing text and using language, so a fluent writer can still lose marks on B if the argument is not structured. MYP Language Acquisition tracks listening, reading, speaking and writing separately across phases 1 to 6, meaning a student's phase can differ by skill, and a specialist tutor plans around exactly that pattern rather than treating the subject as one undifferentiated skill.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Works Best for MYP in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is IB Gram's starting point for IB MYP tuition in Gurgaon, and the reasons are practical rather than sentimental. A tutor at the family's own table can see exactly how a student works through a maths problem, catch a habit that is quietly losing marks on criterion C, and hold a younger student's attention more reliably than a screen tends to. For MYP 1 to MYP 3 students especially, home remains the format most families settle into, and it is the one IB Gram recommends by default unless something about your schedule or location points elsewhere.

Online earns its place for real, specific reasons rather than as a downgrade. A family on the Dwarka Expressway corridor whose evening traffic is unpredictable, a household with a late school pickup, or a search for a specialist in a subject where the strongest local match happens to live across the city, all point toward online as the more reliable choice some or all weeks. The trade-off is honest: a distracted younger student can drift on a screen in a way they would not at a table, though older MYP 4 and MYP 5 students, closer to the independence DP will demand, often adapt to it easily.

Hybrid suits families who do not want to choose permanently between the two. A regular home session in term time, switched to online during a hectic week, a family trip, or a stretch of bad traffic, keeps the tutor relationship and the plan intact without forcing a rigid commitment to one format. None of the three is treated as a lesser option on this page; the honest answer is that the right one depends on the student's age, the subject, and which evenings your household can actually protect.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does a Real MYP Specialist Know That a General Tutor Does Not?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a general tutor, however experienced with CBSE or a generic syllabus, to describe how MYP Language and Literature is marked, and the gap usually shows immediately: they will talk about grammar, vocabulary and essay quality in general terms, rather than naming criterion A, analysing, criterion B, organizing, criterion C, producing text and criterion D, using language, as four separate, specifically defined skills. A real specialist does not need to look this up. That single test, asked plainly in a first conversation, tells you more than a CV.

The deeper difference is diagnostic. A general tutor tends to see a weak report and start with content: more practice questions, more revision. A specialist looks at which of the four criteria is actually dragging the total down and starts there, because a student strong on criterion A but weak on criterion D needs a completely different kind of lesson from a student weak across the board. This distinction is the single biggest predictor of whether tuition moves the needle within a term or simply keeps a student occupied without changing the pattern on their report.

A specialist also understands what sits outside the regular subject criteria: the Community Project in MYP 3 or MYP 4, the Personal Project in MYP 5, and the fact that MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and decided independently by each school. Getting any of this wrong, treating the Personal Project as just another piece of homework, for instance, is a reliable sign that the tutor has not actually taught this programme before, whatever their general tutoring experience elsewhere might suggest.

contentBlocks.heading: What to Ask Before, and After, the Trial Lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
Before the trial, ask two questions that separate a genuine MYP specialist from someone who has simply added the board to a general profile. First: can you name the four criteria for this specific subject, and describe in plain terms what separates a level 5 from a level 7 on the one my child is weakest at. A tutor who answers fluently, without hesitation or a vague generalisation, has almost certainly taught this before. Second: have you actually taught students at this MYP phase, not just tutored the board in general; a tutor strong with MYP 4 and MYP 5 extended mathematics is not automatically the right fit for a MYP 1 student still building basic number sense.

During the trial itself, watch rather than just listen. Does the tutor ask to see recent work, a test, an exercise book, before diving into content? Do they reference the actual criteria out loud while teaching, rather than only at the end? Does the pace match your child, neither rushing past confusion nor moving so slowly that an able student disengages?

After the trial, the most useful question is not "did you like the tutor" but "what specifically did the tutor correct, and can you explain it back to me". A student who can restate, even roughly, what changed in their approach has had a session that actually taught something, as opposed to one that simply felt pleasant. Ask, too, whether the tutor gave any indication of what they would work on next and why, since a specialist should leave a trial with a rough plan already forming, not a vague sense that "we'll see how it goes". If the answers to these questions feel thin, that is worth acting on before committing to a regular slot, not after a term has already passed.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Four Weeks of IB MYP Tuition Actually Show?
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is early, but it is enough time to see a direction, if not a destination. What to look for is not a jump in grade, which no honest tutor would promise this quickly, but a specific, small, checkable sign of movement: a student who is now setting out working the way the tutor showed them, a first attempt at applying criterion D-style reasoning that was clumsy but present where it was previously absent, a Personal Project outline that finally has a workable research question. These small signs matter more at week four than any single test score.

Ask the tutor directly for an honest read at this point, and expect specifics rather than reassurance. "It's going well" is not useful; "criterion B was a 3, we've worked on pattern-spotting for three sessions, and the last two attempts show early signs of the right approach" is. A tutor who cannot offer this level of detail after four weeks either has not been tracking progress carefully or is avoiding an honest conversation, and either is worth addressing directly rather than letting another month pass.

No tutor, and no platform, can guarantee a grade or a specific criterion level; the International Baccalaureate sets its own grade boundaries independently each session, and this remains true no matter how good the tuition is. What is reasonable to expect by week four is a clear, specific update and an early sign of movement on the criterion that prompted the tuition in the first place. If neither is there, ask plainly what the plan is for the next four weeks, and if the answer is vague twice in a row, it is a fair moment to ask IB Gram for a different tutor.

faqs.question: How is IB MYP tuition different from CBSE or ICSE tuition?
faqs.answer: The biggest difference is how progress is measured: MYP uses four criteria per subject, each scored out of 8, not a percentage or a single overall mark, so a tutor needs to teach toward specific criteria rather than generic content revision. A tutor experienced only with CBSE or ICSE often defaults to percentage thinking and misses which specific skill, analysing, investigating, communicating or applying, is actually holding a student back. Ask any tutor directly whether they have taught MYP specifically, not just tutored a similar age group on a different board.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask before booking the trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the tutor can name the four criteria for your child's specific subject, and what separates a level 5 from a level 7 on the one your child is weakest at. Also ask whether they have taught this exact MYP phase before, since a tutor strong with MYP 5 extended mathematics is not automatically right for a MYP 1 student. A confident, specific answer to both usually means a genuine specialist; a vague or general answer is worth noting before you commit to a regular schedule.

faqs.question: What should I check after the trial lesson, before agreeing to regular sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask your child what specifically the tutor corrected, and see if they can explain it back in their own words; that is a better test than asking whether they enjoyed the session. Check whether the tutor referenced the actual MYP criteria while teaching, not just general praise or correction, and whether they mentioned any plan for the next few sessions. If the answers feel thin or generic, it is reasonable to try a different tutor before committing to a weekly slot.

faqs.question: What should four weeks of tuition actually show?
faqs.answer: A small, specific, checkable sign of movement on the criterion that prompted tuition in the first place, not a jump in overall grade, which no honest tutor would promise this quickly. Ask for a specific update: which criterion, what has been worked on, and any early sign it is landing, rather than a general "going well". If the tutor cannot offer this level of detail by week four, or the update stays vague for two reviews running, it is a fair point to ask IB Gram for a different match.

introSummary: IB MYP home tutor Gurgaon searches usually come from a parent who wants lessons at their own dining table or study desk, not a drive across the city after a long school day, and home tuition is exactly what this page is built around. IB Gram verifies a tutor's profile before a home visit is even suggested, and this page walks through what that verification covers, what the first home session actually looks like, who should be present, and which Gurgaon corridors a home tutor reaches comfortably on a weekday evening. The Middle Years Programme runs across five years, MYP 1 to 5, with every subject assessed against four criteria scored 0 to 8, and a tutor working in your home should already understand that structure before the first session begins.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Verifies an MYP Home Tutor in Gurgaon Before a Visit
contentBlocks.body:
A request for an IB MYP home tutor in Gurgaon starts the same way every other request does, a parent describing the subject, the MYP year, one to five, and the school, but the next step is different from a general tuition enquiry: IB Gram treats the home visit itself as part of what gets verified, not just the subject knowledge.

Before any tutor's profile reaches a shortlist, IB Gram checks their MYP subject and criteria background, whether they have taught the specific subject group at this student's year, and confirms they understand criterion-related marking, four criteria per subject, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, rather than a percentage system. This matters for a home tutor specifically because a criteria-based misunderstanding is harder to notice from outside a session than a factual error would be.

Once a shortlist is ready, IB Gram asks about the family's sector or society, gate and visitor procedures if relevant, and preferred weekday evening slots, since a home tutor's ability to actually keep a fixed weekly time matters as much as their subject depth. A free trial session is arranged next, held in the home itself wherever possible, so the family can judge both the teaching and the practical fit of having this person in the house weekly.

If the visit or the teaching does not work out, IB Gram arranges a different tutor without asking the family to justify the change at length; a home tuition relationship that starts awkwardly rarely improves simply by persisting.

3. Sector, society and gate or visitor procedures are confirmed before a shortlist is shared.

contentBlocks.heading: Understanding the MYP Structure Before a Tutor Sits Down With Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme runs across five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, spanning eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8, so a criterion total runs to 32 per subject, and that total converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's own grade boundaries rather than a straightforward percentage conversion.

This criterion structure is precisely why a general tutor, even a capable one used to CBSE or ICSE marking, can misjudge an MYP student's actual position. A student might score well on criterion A, knowing and understanding, while losing marks consistently on criterion C or D, applying or reflecting, and a tutor unfamiliar with the four-criteria format may simply not notice the pattern, let alone correct it.

MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, an independent piece of work a student plans and carries out largely outside class time, with the Community Project sometimes appearing earlier in MYP 3 or 4 instead. Some schools also offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations combined with ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides for itself whether to run it, so a family should confirm with the school directly rather than assume.

A home tutor working across these five years also needs to keep half an eye on what comes after: MYP 5 is the final year before the jump to the Diploma Programme, and habits built here, structured notes, criterion-aware self-checking, carry forward directly into DP1.

contentBlocks.heading: What the MYP Criteria Actually Demand, Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria: A, knowing and understanding; B, investigating patterns; C, communicating; D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each out of 8. Many Gurgaon schools split MYP 4 and 5 Mathematics into standard and extended routes, and extended covers additional topics that prepare a student specifically for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches later, so a tutor should know which route a student is actually on before assuming the depth needed.

MYP Sciences use a parallel structure, A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science, again each scored 0 to 8. Criterion B and C together usually carry the practical, investigative side of the subject, and a home tutor helping with a lab write-up needs to know exactly which criterion that piece of work is being judged against, not just whether the science content itself is correct.

MYP Language and Literature runs on A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language, while MYP Language Acquisition, a second or additional language, uses a different set, A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, taught across phases 1 to 6 rather than by year group directly. A tutor working on English or a second language at home should be clear about which of these two criteria sets applies, since they reward genuinely different skills.

Across every subject, the pattern is the same: a student's mark depends on which specific criterion is weak, not a general sense of the subject being "hard", and a home tutor's first real job is identifying that criterion precisely, ideally within the first one or two sessions.

contentBlocks.heading: The MYP Calendar Gurgaon Schools Set, Year by Year
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families across Gurgaon's international school belt, at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali, and DPS International Edge, each follow a calendar the school itself sets, though the broad shape of MYP, criterion-based assessment across the term, a Personal Project year in MYP 5, and a growing expectation of independent work, repeats everywhere.

Is the Personal Project timeline already published for an MYP 5 student. Does this school run MYP eAssessment, and if so, when do the on-screen components happen. Younger MYP students, in MYP 1 or 2, generally need more structure and check-ins from a home tutor than an MYP 5 student managing a Personal Project largely independently, and school expectations shift accordingly: less homework-style support, more coaching toward independent planning and time management as a student moves through the five years.

A home tutor who has worked with students at more than one Gurgaon international school tends to have a broader sense of how criterion-based assessment actually gets applied day to day, which varies more between schools than families often expect, even within the same MYP framework.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Works Best for MYP?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is IB Gram's lead recommendation for MYP students specifically, more so than for older DP students, because MYP-age children, eleven to sixteen, generally benefit from a consistent physical routine and direct supervision that online lessons cannot quite replicate at that age. A home tutor sees the actual study space, notices when materials are missing before a session starts rather than partway through, and builds a working relationship face to face that tends to matter more for a younger student's confidence.

Online MYP tuition still has a place, particularly for a specific subject where the right criteria-aware specialist is not based near the family's corridor, or during periods when evening traffic on a longer route makes a reliable home visit genuinely difficult. Most MYP content, working through a criterion-based rubric together, annotating a piece of writing, reviewing a Mathematics investigation, translates reasonably well to a shared screen once both sides settle into the format.

Hybrid works well for MYP families balancing more than one subject or a longer corridor: a home session for the subject that benefits most from in-person marking and discussion, a Language and Literature essay draft, say, and an online session for a subject where the closest strong specialist happens to teach remotely. IB Gram reviews the mix again each term, since a pattern that suited MYP 2 does not automatically suit the same student heading into MYP 5's Personal Project year.

The honest trade-off: home tuition wins on routine, supervision and the kind of rapport a younger student needs, online wins on specialist access and on evenings where travel genuinely does not work, and for most MYP families here, home is the right default with online or hybrid as the practical exception, not the other way round.

IB Gram verifies a tutor's subject and MYP-year background before a profile reaches a shortlist, whether they have taught the four-criteria system specifically and at the relevant year, MYP 1 through 5, rather than a general "all levels" claim. This is the standard every IB MYP home tutor Gurgaon families shortlist must meet before a visit is even proposed, and for a home tutor specifically, verification also covers whether they are used to teaching in a family's own home rather than a classroom or centre setting, since the two require genuinely different habits, managing materials, working around household routine, keeping a session focused without a classroom's usual structure.

Parents should still ask their own questions once a shortlist arrives. Which MYP subjects and years has this tutor actually taught recently. How do they plan a first session with a new student, do they start with a diagnostic look at recent criterion-marked work. What do they expect to need in terms of materials or space in your home. A tutor who answers with specifics is generally a safer choice than one offering only general reassurance about experience.

The free trial session is where all of this becomes concrete rather than theoretical. It should be a real lesson, working through an actual piece of the student's recent work against a real criterion, not a generic introductory chat, and by the end a parent should have a clear sense of whether this specific person, in this specific home, is a good fit going forward.

If it is not, IB Gram treats a request for a different tutor as entirely normal. A mismatch discovered early, before a routine sets in, costs far less than one that only becomes obvious after several weeks of a student quietly disengaging from a subject.

contentBlocks.heading: Preparing for the First MYP Home Tuition Session: A Checklist
contentBlocks.body:
The first home session sets the pattern for everything after it, so it is worth preparing for deliberately rather than treating it as just another appointment. Who should be present matters: a parent introducing the tutor for the first few minutes is normal and helpful, but most MYP students, particularly from MYP 3 onward, work better once the actual teaching begins without a parent sitting in the room throughout.

The study space matters more than families often expect. A consistent desk or table, reasonably quiet, with the student's actual books, laptop if the subject needs one, and any recent criterion-marked work already gathered, saves real time in a first session that should be spent diagnosing gaps, not searching for a missing exercise book. A space that changes every week, the dining table one day, a bedroom the next, makes it harder for a home tutor to build the kind of routine an MYP student benefits from.

A simple numbered way to prepare: first, gather the student's two or three most recent pieces of graded or criterion-marked work; second, note which subject and criterion feel weakest in the parent's own words, since this is often more accurate than waiting for the tutor to diagnose from scratch; third, confirm a fixed weekly time that survives a normal school week, activities and all; fourth, set aside the actual study space and make sure the student knows it is happening before the tutor arrives, not as a surprise.

What the first session itself should produce: a specific answer to which criterion, A, B, C or D, is the weakest, one small piece of work completed or reviewed together, and a plan for the next few weeks that a parent can describe back in a sentence. A vague "it went well" after the first home visit is worth following up on directly.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress at Home Should Look Like, and Its Limits
contentBlocks.body:
Progress with a home tutor rarely means every criterion improving evenly. What it should look like is more specific: the weakest criterion identified in the first session showing a describable change within a few weeks, fewer marks lost specifically on that criterion in the next piece of school-marked work, and a student who can name which criterion they are working on rather than describing the subject only in general terms.

For a student in MYP 5 working on the Personal Project, progress looks different again: a project goal that becomes clearer and more specific over several sessions, a product or outcome that stays realistic given the time actually available, and a growing habit of independent planning rather than a tutor managing the whole project for the student, which would defeat its purpose entirely.

There are honest limits a home tutor should name rather than hide. A student who has fallen behind across multiple subjects at once needs a conversation about priorities, not an attempt to fix everything in one weekly session; a home tutor covering one subject cannot substitute for a wider look at how a student is coping across the whole MYP year, which is sometimes a conversation for the school, not the tutor.

If six to eight weeks pass with no describable change in the identified weak criterion, that is the point to ask IB Gram for a different tutor rather than assuming the student cannot improve. A mismatch in approach, not a lack of effort, is the more common reason for a stall.

A private arrangement starts from a different place than a general tuition enquiry. contentBlocks.heading: MYP Criteria, Not Percentages: What a Private Tutor Should Already Know
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a private tutor unfamiliar with the Middle Years Programme (MYP) how a student is doing, and many will reach for a percentage out of habit, because that is how most other boards report. The International Baccalaureate (IB) does not work that way. Every subject across the programme's eight groups is marked against four criteria, labelled A through D, each scored out of 8, and it is the pattern across those four numbers, not a single overall score, that tells you where a student actually stands. Any IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon, private or otherwise, should be reading that pattern from the first report you show them, not learning the system on your child's time.

The five years of MYP, MYP 1 through MYP 5, run roughly from age 11 to 16, matching Grades 6 to 10 in the way schools across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, usually describe them. The criterion totals out of 32 across the four convert to a final grade from 1 to 7 through grade boundaries the IB sets itself, separately for each subject and exam session; no tutor, however experienced, sets or influences those boundaries, and any private tutor who suggests otherwise should be treated with caution.

Two milestones sit outside the eight subject groups entirely: the Community Project, usually completed in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school, and the Personal Project, completed in MYP 5, both marked against their own planning, research and reflection criteria rather than subject content. MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams and ePortfolios offered in MYP 5, is entirely optional, and each school decides independently whether to run it, which is one more reason a private tutor needs to ask your school directly rather than assuming the same structure applies everywhere.

The Community Project falls in MYP 3 or MYP 4; the Personal Project falls in MYP 5.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Private MYP Maths or Sciences Tutor Actually Marks
contentBlocks.body:
A private tutor who only drills content is working against the grain of how MYP Mathematics is actually marked. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, rewards accurate technique and is genuinely the easiest of the four to raise quickly. Criterion B, investigating patterns, asks a student to notice a rule in a sequence of numbers or shapes and justify why it holds, which no amount of past-paper repetition builds on its own; it needs deliberate practice at spotting structure. Criterion C, communicating, checks whether working is laid out clearly enough for someone else to follow, and it is the criterion where private tutoring tends to help fastest, since a tutor can correct sloppy layout habits in a handful of sessions. Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is usually the slowest to move, because it depends on judgement in an unfamiliar scenario rather than a rehearsed method. A MYP maths tutor in Gurgaon working privately should say plainly, and early, which pathway your child is realistically working toward, since Gurgaon schools commonly split MYP 4 and MYP 5 mathematics into standard and extended, and extended feeds directly into Diploma Programme (DP) Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA).

MYP Sciences mirrors this across Biology, Chemistry and Physics: A for recall, B for designing a fair investigation, C for processing and evaluating data, and D for reflecting on the wider impact of science, a criterion many otherwise strong students neglect because it reads less like traditional science and more like an argument.

Language subjects follow their own logic. MYP Language and Literature marks analysing, organising, producing text and using language, so a fluent writer can still lose marks for a poorly structured argument. MYP Language Acquisition is tracked by phase, 1 through 6, across listening, reading, speaking and writing separately, meaning a student's phase in speaking can sit well behind their phase in reading, and a private tutor needs to know which phase applies to which skill before planning anything.

Standard and extended mathematics often split in MYP 4-5; extended leads toward DP Mathematics AA.

MYP Language and Literature: A Analysing, B Organizing, C Producing text, D Using language.
MYP Language Acquisition: A Listening, B Reading, C Speaking, D Writing, across phases 1 to 6.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Works for a Private MYP Arrangement in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home is where most private MYP arrangements in Gurgaon begin, and for a specific reason beyond convenience: a lesson at the family's own table keeps the whole arrangement contained, without a shared platform link or account that could, in theory, be traced back by anyone at the student's school. For a family whose main concern is that their child's own teacher or classmates never learn a private tutor is involved at all, home tuition offers the most control, provided the tutor's visits are timed around when the house is otherwise quiet. A MYP home tutor in Gurgaon found through a general listing may still have loose connections to your child's wider school circle; a private arrangement through IB Gram is checked specifically for independence, which a general home tuition search usually does not verify.

Online tutoring suits a private arrangement for different, equally practical reasons. Some families prefer it precisely because fewer people, including domestic staff or visiting relatives, need to know a tutor is coming at all; a closed door and a laptop is less visible than a stranger at the gate every week. This is the same discretion many families researching an IB MYP online tutor Gurgaon option also value, though a private arrangement adds the written confidentiality agreement on top of it. It also opens access to a specialist with no connection whatsoever to any school in Gurgaon, which matters more here than on a general tutoring page, since the entire point of a private arrangement is independence from the student's own school circle. The honest trade-off is the same as anywhere: a session can lose focus without someone physically present, and any written work still needs to be reviewed carefully rather than skimmed on a shared screen.

Hybrid works well for families managing a private arrangement around an unpredictable week, home on the evenings that are free, online when a family event, travel or exam-week traffic makes a home visit impractical. What should not change between formats is the confidentiality agreed at the start: whichever format is used that week, what happens in the lesson and what a student shares in it stays between the tutor, the student and the parents who arranged it, not anyone else in the household or the school.

Online: useful when discretion about who visits the house matters, or when the right specialist is not local.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is an Independent MYP Tutor in Gurgaon Checked Before You Commit?
contentBlocks.body:
For a private arrangement specifically, verification carries one extra layer beyond the general subject and MYP experience check every tutor on IB Gram goes through: confirming the tutor has no current or recent teaching or grading connection to your child's own school. This is worth asking about directly and plainly at the shortlist stage, not assuming it because the tutor was recommended through IB Gram; a straight answer here tells you a great deal about how seriously a tutor treats the independence a private arrangement is meant to offer.

Parents should check a few things themselves at the trial, beyond the usual questions about subject fit and pace. Ask how the tutor would handle a situation where a student shares something unrelated to academics during a lesson, exam stress, a friendship problem, a difficult comment from a teacher; a private tutor is not a counsellor, but how they respond to this in the trial tells you whether they will treat a student's trust carefully or carelessly. Ask, too, exactly what the tutor would and would not do if the student asked for help with an actual school assignment or test preparation that crosses into academic integrity territory; a tutor who hesitates or gives a vague answer here is a warning sign, not a small detail. There is no single best ib myp private tutor in Gurgaon on paper; the right one is whoever passes these specific checks for your child's situation.

Confidentiality should be confirmed in writing before the first regular session, not left as an assumed courtesy. contentBlocks.heading: Why Not Just Ask Your Child's Own Teacher for Extra Classes?
contentBlocks.body:
It is a fair question, and worth answering honestly rather than deflecting. When a student's own subject teacher offers extra classes privately, outside school hours, for a fee, there is a real conflict of interest built into the arrangement, whether or not anyone intends it: the same person who sets homework, marks classwork and reports a criterion level to the school is also being paid privately by the family to improve that same criterion level. It creates pressure in both directions, a student reluctant to say the extra class is not helping, and a teacher whose in-class assessment of that student is no longer entirely separate from their private income. This is not a claim that every teacher offering extra classes acts improperly; it is a structural conflict that an independent private tutor, with no grading relationship to the student at all, simply does not carry.

An independent tutor is also better placed to map lessons directly to the school's own scheme of work without doing the school's tasks for the student. This distinction matters and is easy to blur under pressure before a deadline: a tutor should teach the underlying skill, an essay structure, a mathematical method, a lab-report format, using practice material and past general questions, never the actual assignment or test paper a student is due to submit or sit at school. A tutor who offers to "just help finish" a piece of coursework or a Personal Project section that is meant to be independent work is crossing into territory that risks the student's own academic integrity standing, not just a grey area.

What should be agreed in writing before lessons begin: the schedule and cancellation notice on both sides, how and how often the tutor updates parents on progress, what stays confidential between tutor, student and parents, exactly which tasks the tutor will and will not help with, and what happens if the arrangement is not working, whether that means a conversation, a pause, or asking IB Gram for a different tutor. None of this needs to be a formal legal document; a short written note both sides have seen is usually enough to prevent the misunderstandings that end private arrangements badly.
items: Schedule: fixed day and time, plus how much notice either side gives to cancel.
Progress updates: how often, and in what form, whether a short note or a call.
Confidentiality: what stays between tutor, student and parents, agreed before lessons start.
Scope: which subjects and tasks the tutor covers, and what remains the school's own work.
What happens if the fit is wrong: how the arrangement ends or a new tutor is found.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should a Private MYP Arrangement Show After a Month?
contentBlocks.body:
A month into a private MYP arrangement, look for the same signal that matters in any tutoring relationship: has a specific criterion actually moved, visible in a piece of work the school itself has assessed, not just homework set and marked by the tutor. A student who is more confident discussing MYP Sciences at the dinner table is a nice sign, but it is not proof; the proof sits in the next unit assessment or report.

Check, too, whether the terms agreed at the start are actually holding. Is the schedule being kept, with proper notice on either side when a session needs to move. Is confidentiality being respected, meaning nothing discussed in a lesson has surfaced elsewhere without the family's knowledge. Is the tutor still working from general scheme-of-work topics and practice material rather than drifting toward helping directly with school assignments, which is worth checking honestly even a month in, since the pressure to cross that line tends to rise closer to a deadline, not fall.

No tutor, and no platform, can guarantee a grade or a specific criterion level; the International Baccalaureate sets its own grade boundaries independently each session, regardless of how good the private arrangement is. Anyone who implies a guaranteed outcome should be treated with real caution. What a private tutor can reasonably deliver is a clear plan against the actual criteria, honest updates kept confidential as agreed, and visible movement within a reasonable window, usually four to six weeks for the first sign and a full term for something more solid.

If a full term passes with no shift in the criterion that started the arrangement, that is a reason to review the plan itself, and sometimes the fit between tutor and student, rather than assuming more of the same will eventually work. Sometimes the actual gap was never content at all, and a private tutor who has been paying close attention should be the first to say so. This is what a well-matched IB MYP private tutor Gurgaon families keep for more than a term looks like in practice: steady, checkable movement, not a vague promise.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know our school's test dates?

faqs.question: Can a private arrangement work for a student in Sushant Lok on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tutoring for a private arrangement is arranged across Sushant Lok, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area, subject to availability for your preferred evening slot. Travel times in this corridor tend to be shorter and more predictable than corridors further from central Gurgaon, which suits a private arrangement well, since a late first session can unsettle a relationship that depends on trust. If a particular evening is consistently difficult, a hybrid mix of home and online sessions usually solves it without disrupting the whole week.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor report progress the same way a school does?
faqs.answer: No, and it should not try to; a private tutor gives you their own honest read of a specific criterion, agreed in writing at the start as part of the confidentiality and update terms, separate from the school's own reporting. Expect a short note or a brief call after sessions, at whatever frequency you agreed, rather than a formal report card. faqs.question: Is a small group with a friend cheaper and just as good as a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It can cost less per student, but it is not the same as a private arrangement: attention is shared, confidentiality extends to the other family involved, and the lesson has to move at a pace that suits both students, not just yours. A small group of three or four can work well if both students are at a similar level and the families are comfortable sharing that information with each other. contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches an IB MYP Online Tutor Gurgaon Families Trust
contentBlocks.body:
Most families do not start with a subject; they start with a problem. A Sector 84 parent calls because a report card shows criterion B stuck at 4 out of 8 in MYP Sciences, three terms running, and nobody at school has explained what changing that number actually requires. IB Gram's first job is turning that problem into a brief a tutor can act on: which subject group, which of the four criteria (A to D) is weak, what the school's own scheme of work covers next, and whether the family wants an IB MYP online tutor Gurgaon evenings can accommodate or a tutor who comes to the house.

A search for an IB MYP online tutor near me on its own usually returns a long list sorted by nothing more useful than distance or a star rating. contentBlocks.heading: What the Middle Years Programme Actually Assesses
contentBlocks.body:
The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, for students roughly aged 11 to 16, or Grades 6 to 10 in the way schools across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, usually describe it. It covers eight subject groups, and every one of them is assessed the same way: four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8. There is no percentage on an MYP report in the way a CBSE mark sheet works. A student's real position sits in which criterion is weak, not in a single number, and that is the first thing a specialist tutor should be able to read off a report card in under a minute.

The criterion totals, out of 32 across the four, convert to a final grade from 1 to 7 through the IB's own grade boundaries, set separately for each subject and session. This is why two students with the same total can land on different final grades depending on the subject, and why a tutor who only teaches content, without checking which criterion is dragging the average down, ends up fixing the wrong thing. Families searching for IB MYP tutors in Gurgaon should ask, in the very first conversation, whether the tutor can name the criterion by letter, not just the subject.

The Community Project, completed in MYP 3 or MYP 4 depending on the school, and the Personal Project, completed in MYP 5, sit outside the eight subject groups and are marked against their own criteria, built around planning, research and reflection rather than subject content. MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios offered in MYP 5, is optional, and whether a school runs it is the school's own decision, not something IB Gram or any tutor controls. Families moving between MYP phases, or comparing a child's report against a sibling's from an earlier year, should check with the school's own coordinator before assuming the structure is identical, since schools do phase in changes at different points.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP Maths, Sciences and Language: What the Criteria Actually Test
contentBlocks.body:
Ask what MYP Mathematics tests and most students say "algebra" or "geometry". That is criterion A, knowing and understanding, and it is usually the easiest of the four to teach. Criterion B, investigating patterns, asks a student to spot a rule from a set of numbers or shapes and justify it, a skill that content revision alone does not build. Criterion C, communicating, marks whether working is set out so another mathematician could follow it, which is why a student who gets the right answer can still lose marks. Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is the one most Gurgaon students find hardest, because it asks for judgement about a messy, real scenario rather than a clean textbook question. Schools often split MYP 4 and MYP 5 into standard and extended mathematics; extended brings in topics that make the jump to Diploma Programme (DP) Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA) noticeably smoother. A MYP maths tutor in Gurgaon worth choosing should be able to tell you early, usually by the second session, which pathway your child is realistically on.

MYP Sciences uses a parallel structure across Biology, Chemistry and Physics: criterion A tests recall, B tests whether a student can design a fair investigation, C tests whether they can process data and evaluate its reliability, and D asks them to reflect on the impact of science on society and the environment, a criterion many strong students under-prepare for because it feels less like "real" science.

Language subjects split the same way. MYP Language and Literature marks analysing, organising, producing text and using language; a student who writes fluently but never structures an argument will lose marks on B regardless of how good A and D look. MYP Language Acquisition, taught in phases 1 to 6 rather than by grade, marks listening, reading, speaking and writing separately, so a student can be at phase 4 in reading and phase 2 in speaking at the same time, and a tutor working online should know which phase each skill sits at before planning a single lesson.

What a tutor needs to know is not which school teaches which board, but the shape of the term: when unit assessments typically cluster, when the Personal Project deadline in MYP 5 tends to sit relative to the rest of the school year, and how much notice families usually get before a report goes home. A student who has been quietly losing marks on criterion C for two units running will not show it on a single test score; it only becomes visible when someone looks at the pattern across several pieces of work, which is exactly what a specialist tutor should be doing from the first session rather than waiting for the report.

Online lessons fit this calendar well because they can be booked at short notice around a school's own test week, without needing to coordinate a home visit around evening traffic. contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Which Suits Your MYP Child in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where most Gurgaon families start, and for good reason. A tutor sitting across the table from an 11 or 12 year old in MYP 1 or MYP 2 can see exactly which working is copied and which is understood, correct a grip on a compass or a graphing error in seconds, and keep a younger student's attention in a way a screen sometimes cannot. For families who can offer a fixed evening slot and a home where the tutor's visit is straightforward to arrange, a MYP home tutor in Gurgaon remains the most natural fit, and home tuition is IB Gram's lead service on every one of these pages for that reason. This page, though, is built around the online alternative, since that is usually what brought you here.

Online tutoring earns its place for different, equally real reasons. A family on the Dwarka Expressway corridor whose evenings are unpredictable because of construction traffic, or a household where both parents work until 7pm and a home visit before 8pm is not realistic, often finds online the only format that reliably happens every week. It also opens up specialists who do not live near Gurgaon at all: the right MYP Sciences criterion D specialist, for instance, might simply not be based in this city, and online removes that constraint entirely. The honest trade-off is that a distracted younger student can drift on a screen in a way they would not at a table, and a tutor cannot physically point at a diagram the way they can in person.

Hybrid is the practical middle path many MYP families in Gurgaon settle into after a term or two: home sessions when the schedule allows, online sessions in exam weeks, during a family holiday, or on evenings when traffic makes a home visit unreliable. Neither format is graded down for being the fallback; a family that runs mostly online with one home session a month is still getting the same tutor, the same plan and the same criterion tracking. What matters is picking the format your child actually concentrates in, which a free trial in each setting will usually show within one or two sessions rather than a month of guessing.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is an IB MYP Online Tutor in Gurgaon Verified?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification, for IB Gram, means confirming a tutor's subject background and their actual experience teaching or tutoring the Middle Years Programme before their profile is shown to any family, then matching that profile to the specific phase, subject and criterion gap a parent describes at the first query. It does not mean a guarantee about how any one lesson will go; no platform can promise that, and any page that implies otherwise is not being straight with you.

What a parent should check themselves matters just as much. Ask the tutor directly, in the trial session, to name the four criteria for your child's weakest subject and describe what separates a level 5 from a level 7 on the one your child is stuck at. Any genuine IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon who has actually taught MYP Mathematics or MYP Sciences will answer this without hesitation; a general tutor who has only taught CBSE or a generic syllabus usually cannot, and that gap shows up fast once you ask a specific question rather than a general one like "have you taught IB before".

For an online lesson specifically, ask how the tutor plans to share and mark work: a shared whiteboard app, an annotated PDF of a past paper, or a document both of you can see and edit live. A tutor who says they will "just explain over video" without any shared working surface is not set up to teach a criterion-based subject properly online, because so much of MYP marking depends on seeing exactly how a student reached an answer, not just whether the final number is right. There is no single, objective best ib myp online tutor in Gurgaon; the right one is whoever answers these specific questions well for your child's actual gap, which is precisely what the trial is for.

IB Gram arranges a free trial before any regular commitment in every format, precisely so this checking happens before money or a term's schedule is on the line. If the first tutor does not hold up to these questions, ask for a different match rather than persisting out of politeness; that is a normal, expected request, not an awkward one.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Works in a Live Online MYP Lesson?
contentBlocks.body:
A live online MYP lesson works when it is set up like a proper classroom, not a phone call with homework attached. That means a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, because a shared whiteboard or an annotated past paper is close to unreadable on a small screen; a stable connection, since a lesson that keeps freezing loses more time than a short commute would; a quiet room with the door closed; and, often overlooked, the same physical exercise book the student uses at school kept open beside the laptop, because a tutor working entirely on-screen cannot see whether classroom habits are actually changing.

By task, online suits some MYP work better than others. Reviewing a past paper works well online: the tutor can annotate directly on a shared PDF, circle exactly where a mark was lost against criterion C, and the student can see it happen in real time. Talking through an essay plan for MYP Language and Literature, or working through a maths problem step by step on a shared whiteboard, also translates well. What suits a screen less is anything needing physical materials, a science practical for criterion B, inquiring and designing, or a younger MYP 1 student who needs a hand steadied on a compass; those sessions are usually better at home or done as a hybrid week.

Why do families keep searching for an IB MYP online tutor Gurgaon evenings actually fit, rather than defaulting to home tuition? Mostly it comes down to three things: the evening slot after school pickup and homework that a home tutor's travel time cannot always fit; access to a specialist for a specific weak criterion who is not based nearby; and, honestly, traffic, since a short trip across a corridor like Dwarka Expressway can stretch unpredictably at exactly the hour most families want a lesson. The honest limit is attention: a student who cannot sit through forty minutes without checking their phone under the desk will not magically focus better because the tutor is elsewhere.

You can usually tell within three sessions whether online is working for your child. Ask whether they can repeat, unprompted, what the tutor corrected last time; check whether the shared whiteboard or annotated paper is actually being saved and reviewed between sessions; and watch whether the next school assessment shows any shift in the specific criterion that was the reason you started. If none of these show up by the third session, switching that student to home or hybrid is a reasonable next step, not a failure of the format.

A stable connection; a wired or strong Wi-Fi link matters more than a fast processor.
A quiet room with the door closed, away from a television or younger siblings.

contentBlocks.heading: How Fast Should an Online MYP Tutor Show Results?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the Middle Years Programme is easiest to see when you look at criteria, not a general feeling that things are better. If your child started at a criterion B level of 3 in MYP Sciences, ask specifically whether that has moved, and by how much, at the next school assessment, not just whether the tutor "seems happy" with how sessions are going. A tutor who cannot point to a specific criterion shift after six to eight weeks is either teaching the wrong thing or has not been given enough time yet, and it is worth asking which before assuming the tutor is at fault.

Homework set by the tutor improving is a weaker signal than it looks, because a student can perform well on material chosen and paced by the person teaching it. What actually matters is whether that improvement shows up in the next unit test or piece of assessed work set independently by the school. This is also why a review conversation with the tutor every four to six weeks matters more than a weekly check-in: enough work has usually been assessed by the school in that window to judge honestly.

No tutor, and no platform, can guarantee a grade or a specific criterion level; the International Baccalaureate sets its own grade boundaries independently each session, and no amount of tutoring changes that fact. This holds true whether the arrangement is home tuition, online lessons or a hybrid mix of the two. Be wary of anyone who implies otherwise. What a good tutor can reasonably promise is a clear plan tied to the actual criteria, honest updates on where your child stands, and enough evidence within a month to know whether the arrangement is working.

If a full term passes with no visible shift in the criterion you started with, that is a sign to review the plan itself, not necessarily to blame the tutor outright. Sometimes the subject was never the real issue: exam technique, timing under pressure, or confidence after a bad test can matter more than content, and a good tutor should say so honestly rather than continuing to drill content that was never the actual gap.

A change visible in the next unit assessment at school, not only in tutor-set homework.

Getting started takes a short query: your child's board, their MYP phase, the subject or subjects you want help with, and a preferred format, online, home or hybrid. If you have a recent report or know roughly which criterion is weak, mention it; it saves a round of questions and lets IB Gram shortlist tutors who have actually taught that specific gap before, not just the subject in general. IB Gram then asks a few more questions: your school's calendar and how much notice you typically get before assessments, your address or corridor if a home or hybrid session is wanted, and your preferred evening slot. A shortlist of verified tutors matched to that brief usually follows within a day or two, each one with real experience against the criteria your child needs, not a generic MYP label.

The first session is a free trial, in whichever format you choose, and it is designed to be judged honestly rather than sat through politely. Bring one real piece of recent work, a test, a piece of homework, a Personal Project draft, so the tutor can see the actual level rather than working from a description alone. Ask the questions covered earlier in this page: which criterion, what changed in the last two assessments, how the tutor plans to teach it online if that is the format chosen.

After the trial, you decide: confirm a regular weekly slot, ask for a different tutor if the fit was not right, or take more time before committing. Nothing is owed beyond the trial itself, and lessons only begin once you are ready, subject to tutor availability for your preferred day and time. faqs.question: Does an IB MYP online tutor really work as well as a home tutor?
faqs.answer: For most MYP students, yes, provided the setup is right: a laptop, a shared whiteboard and a quiet room, not a phone call. Online works especially well for reviewing past papers and talking through written work, since a tutor can annotate a shared screen in real time. It suits younger MYP 1 or MYP 2 students less well, since a table and physical materials often hold attention better. Try both in the free trial phase; most families can tell within two or three sessions which their child genuinely concentrates in, and switching formats later is straightforward.

faqs.question: What do I need at home for an online MYP lesson to actually work?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet, a stable internet connection and a quiet room are the essentials. A shared whiteboard app or an annotated PDF lets the tutor mark working the way a school would, which matters more for criterion-based subjects than a plain video call. Keep your child's actual exercise book beside the screen rather than replacing it, since a tutor working only on-screen cannot otherwise see whether classroom habits are changing. Headphones help in a busier household. None of this needs to be expensive; a functioning laptop and a decent Wi-Fi connection cover almost every MYP subject.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come to our society on the Dwarka Expressway on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tutors are arranged across the Dwarka Expressway corridor, including societies like Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, subject to a tutor's availability for your evening slot. Traffic on this stretch can be unpredictable, which is exactly why many families here run a hybrid arrangement: home sessions on quieter evenings, online on the days traffic looks bad. Visitor registration at the society gate can also add a few minutes, so a slightly earlier start is worth agreeing with the tutor. If evenings are consistently tight, an online-first plan usually runs more reliably.

faqs.question: What if the online tutor is not working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Ask IB Gram for a different match; this is a normal request, not an awkward one. Sometimes the subject content is fine but the pace or teaching style does not suit your child, and a second tutor with a different approach solves it immediately. If the problem seems to be the online format itself rather than the tutor, switching that student to home or hybrid lessons is worth trying before assuming tutoring in general is not helping. Either way, raise it directly rather than persisting through a term that is not showing results, since four to six weeks is usually enough to tell.

faqs.question: My child is at Pathways School Gurgaon and needs help with the Personal Project. Can an online tutor help?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Personal Project specialist can work with your child online, reviewing drafts on a shared screen and marking them against the project's own criteria for planning, research and reflection. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Pathways School Gurgaon or any other school named on this page; the tutor works from your child's own project brief and the general Personal Project criteria, not from any school's internal materials. Since the Personal Project deadline in MYP 5 is set by the school and often falls early in the final term, starting tutor support a few months ahead gives more room for genuine revision between drafts.

faqs.question: Is a general online tutor fine, or do we need an MYP specialist?
faqs.answer: An MYP specialist is worth insisting on for anything beyond basic homework help, because the Middle Years Programme is marked against specific criteria a general tutor unfamiliar with the format usually cannot name. Ask any online tutor, in the trial session, to describe the four criteria for your child's subject and what separates two adjacent levels; a genuine MYP specialist answers this immediately, without checking notes. A general tutor can still help with foundational content, but criterion-specific feedback, the part that actually moves a report card, needs someone who has taught this exact structure before.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an MYP student typically need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the phase and how far behind a specific criterion is, so there is no single right number; a tutor will suggest a starting frequency after the trial and adjust it at the first review. Many families begin with one session a week per subject and increase before a Personal Project deadline or a run of unit assessments, then step back down once a criterion has clearly moved. Two subjects at once is manageable for most MYP students; three or more, added all at once, risks the sessions competing for the same evening hours rather than actually helping.

faqs.question: Does the online tutor follow our school's own pacing, or teach a fixed syllabus?
faqs.answer: The tutor follows your child's actual school work: whatever unit or topic is current in class is what a session builds on, adjusted for the specific criterion that needs attention. This matters because two MYP schools in Gurgaon can be at different points in the same subject group in the same month, and a tutor teaching a fixed, generic sequence would be out of step with either. Bring your child's current classwork or a note of what was covered that week to each session so the tutor can plan directly against it rather than guessing.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss an online session?
faqs.answer: Message the tutor or IB Gram as early as you can, and the session is usually rescheduled to another evening that week, subject to the tutor's availability. Online sessions are generally easier to move than home visits, since there is no travel to re-plan around, which is one reason some families keep at least one subject online even if they prefer home tuition for the rest. Repeated late cancellations can make a regular weekly slot harder to hold, so a quick message as soon as a clash appears helps more than waiting until the day itself.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach MYP Maths and MYP Sciences together online?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the tutor has genuine depth in both subjects, but it is worth checking rather than assuming, since strong MYP Sciences knowledge does not automatically mean strong MYP Mathematics teaching, especially at the extended level. IB Gram will say clearly whether a shortlisted tutor covers both properly or whether two specialists would serve your child better. Combining subjects with one tutor can simplify scheduling, but only if the depth in each subject is genuinely there; a shallow cover of two subjects is usually worse than a strong cover of one.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring available for a student in New Gurgaon or is it mainly for central sectors?
faqs.answer: Online tutoring works identically regardless of which Gurgaon corridor you are in, including New Gurgaon, covering Sectors 82 to 90, Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road. Distance simply does not affect an online lesson the way it affects a home visit, so a family in Vatika India Next has exactly the same access to a specialist tutor as a family in central Gurgaon. Home and hybrid lessons in New Gurgaon are also arranged, subject to a tutor's travel availability for that specific evening, but online remains the most consistent option regardless of which part of the city you are in.

contentBlocks.heading: The Primary Years Programme: Structure Without Exams
contentBlocks.body:
The IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from ages 3 to 12 and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; and Sharing the planet. Each theme becomes a unit of inquiry lasting several weeks, and every unit is meant to build one or more of the ten attributes of the IB learner profile alongside its subject content.

There are no external examinations anywhere in the PYP, and this single fact should shape how you judge a prospective tutor. A tutor who talks about "preparing for tests" or brings a stack of timed worksheets to the first session has misunderstood what this stage of the programme actually asks for. The right tutor talks instead about the current unit, the learner profile attributes it develops, and where the child's specific gaps sit within that.

In the final year, students complete the PYP exhibition, a collaborative, student-led inquiry into a real issue, presented to the wider school community. A tutor supporting a child through exhibition year needs to understand that their role is to coach the process, not produce the output; ask directly how they see their role here before the exhibition term begins, since this is one of the clearest places a generalist tutor overreaches.

Because there is no scored exam to point to, judging whether a tutor understands the programme has to happen through conversation and observation rather than a results sheet. This is exactly why interview questions and the trial class itself carry more weight for an IB PYP tutor than they would for a tutor preparing an older student for a graded paper.

Three more: How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet.

contentBlocks.heading: Literacy, Numeracy and the PYP Exhibition, Explained for Parents
contentBlocks.body:
A genuine PYP tutor teaches literacy and numeracy inside the current unit of inquiry rather than as isolated subjects from a generic workbook. For a young reader, that means phonics or sight-word work chosen to match the child's actual reading level, paired with a picture book or inquiry text connected to the unit; for numeracy, it means open-ended, reasoning-first problems in the same style the PYP classroom uses, not timed drills lifted from an unrelated curriculum.

Attention span dictates the shape of a good session more than almost anything else at this age. A tutor working with a five- or six-year-old should plan several short activities with a change of pace between them, watching for genuine attention drop rather than running the clock to a fixed forty minutes regardless of how the child is coping. An older PYP student closer to the exhibition year can sustain longer, more independent stretches, with the tutor coaching from the side rather than directing every minute.

The PYP exhibition deserves its own mention because it is where an unqualified tutor most often oversteps. A tutor should help the child narrow a broad question into something researchable, find and organise age-appropriate information, and rehearse the final presentation, but should never write the child's argument or do the research for them. Ask any prospective tutor directly how they would support exhibition work without taking it over; a specific, careful answer is a strong signal.

Because the PYP does not test in the conventional sense, a tutor's read on whether literacy or numeracy work is actually landing depends on close observation across sessions rather than a mark. A tutor worth hiring can describe, concretely, what has changed in a child's reading fluency or number confidence after a handful of sessions, not just offer a general impression.
