Bring the most recent report card or test paper to the first session, not just a general description of struggles.
Confirm your sector or society address so a home tutor's travel time is realistic before the trial is booked.
Decide in advance whether you want home, online or hybrid lessons, though this can change after the trial.
Set aside 45 to 60 minutes for the first session without interruptions, so the diagnostic conversation is not rushed.

faqs.question: How is international school tuition different from regular CBSE tuition in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: It is different mainly in how work is marked and paced. CBSE tuition usually targets marks out of 100 on a fixed syllabus; international school tuition works against IB criteria scored 0-8, or IGCSE mark schemes with method marks and grade boundaries that vary by syllabus. A tutor for a PYP or MYP student is watching inquiry skills and criterion levels rather than test scores, and a DP or IGCSE tutor needs to know Higher Level versus Standard Level, or Core versus Extended tier, before the first session. General CBSE experience alone usually is not enough.

faqs.question: What does a trial class for international school tuition actually cover?
faqs.answer: A trial class is a working diagnostic, not a sales pitch. The tutor looks at recent school work or a report card, asks what your child finds hardest, and works through a short piece of content or a past question live so you can see how they explain, correct, and pace themselves. It usually runs the same length as a regular session, 45 to 60 minutes. You are free to ask questions throughout, and there is no obligation to continue afterward; if the fit feels wrong, IB Gram will arrange a different tutor.

faqs.question: How much does international school tuition cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed rate, because fees depend on programme level, subject scarcity, session length and whether lessons are at home or online. A Higher Level Diploma subject with a scarce specialist generally costs more per session than a Middle Years Programme subject with wider tutor availability, and travel across corridors like Golf Course Road can factor into a home tutor's structure too. IB Gram will discuss the fee structure for your specific request once the shortlist is ready, always subject to tutor availability and the exact level involved, rather than quoting a blanket figure in advance.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor really teach the IB Diploma Programme properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor has actually taught at that Higher Level or Standard Level before. A DP home tutor sitting at your dining table can cover subject content, walk through internal assessment structure, and mark past paper questions against real mark schemes just as effectively as a centre-based tutor, often more effectively, because the pace is set entirely by one student. What matters is verifying the tutor's actual DP experience before the first session, not assuming a strong subject degree automatically translates into strong DP teaching, which it does not always do.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor really travel to our sector on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, within reason, and IB Gram accounts for this when shortlisting. A tutor already working evenings around Sushant Lok or DLF Phase 5 can often add a nearby family without much extra travel, while a request from further out, say Manesar, may narrow the shortlist to tutors already covering that stretch or lead us to suggest a hybrid week instead. Evening traffic between corridors can stretch a short trip, so being specific about your sector when you send a query helps us match a tutor who already knows the route rather than one learning it on the first visit.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session is missed or the tutor runs late?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram as soon as you know, and we will help arrange a reschedule with the same tutor where possible. Occasional lateness because of Gurgaon traffic happens, and most tutors will message ahead if a session is going to run short or start later than planned. A pattern of missed or late sessions, however, is worth raising directly, since consistency matters more for exam-year students than for a younger child in the Primary Years Programme, and IB Gram will look into it if it becomes a repeated issue rather than a one-off.

faqs.question: Is online international school tuition as effective as tuition at home?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes, particularly for specific subject help or exam-focused sessions with a specialist who does not live nearby; for younger children or students who are easily distracted, a tutor physically present at home usually works better. Online sessions rely on a shared screen for annotating past papers and working through mark schemes, which suits IGCSE and DP revision well, but they depend on a stable connection and a student who can stay engaged without someone sitting beside them. Many Gurgaon families settle on a hybrid week rather than choosing one format permanently.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not the right fit after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so, and IB Gram will arrange a different match; persisting with a mismatched tutor rarely improves things and can dent a student's confidence further. Sometimes the issue is pace, sometimes personality, and sometimes a tutor who looked right on paper turns out not to know this specific board as deeply as their profile suggested. None of that is unusual, and switching early costs far less time and stress than switching three months in, in the middle of a mock cycle.

faqs.question: How soon can international school tuition start after we send a query?
faqs.answer: Often within a few days, subject to tutor availability for the exact board, level and subject you need. A common subject at a widely taught level, say MYP Individuals and Societies, usually has a wider pool of available tutors than a scarce Higher Level subject with few specialists in Gurgaon, so timing can vary. IB Gram will tell you honestly if a particular request will take longer to match rather than rushing an unsuitable tutor into a trial just to fill the slot quickly.

faqs.question: Do you arrange international school tuition for families in Manesar or further out?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tuition reaches Manesar and the NH-48 south stretch, though the pool of tutors willing to make that commute regularly is smaller than for more central corridors, and evening traffic between here and the rest of Gurgaon can stretch a short trip considerably. Many families in this belt settle on one home session a week plus one online session, rather than asking a tutor to travel twice. Tell us your exact location when you send a query so we can be upfront about what is realistic.

faqs.question: How is progress reported to parents during international school tuition?
faqs.answer: Expect a short update after the first month, and then at agreed points afterward, usually written rather than a long call unless you prefer otherwise. A useful update names what has actually improved, method marks on a specific question type, tighter Criterion B responses, more confident Theory of Knowledge discussion, rather than a vague comment that things are going well. If updates stop arriving or feel generic, ask directly; IB Gram expects tutors to report honestly, including when progress has stalled.

faqs.question: Our child just moved from a CBSE school into an international school. Does tuition help with that transition?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more common reasons families first call. A student moving from CBSE into IGCSE or the MYP has to adjust to criterion-based or method-marked assessment, different command terms, and often a faster pace on independent work, and a tutor who has guided other students through the same move can shorten that adjustment considerably. Expect the first few weeks to focus on how marks are actually awarded in the new system, not just new content, since that is usually the bigger shift.

heroTitle: Finding the Right International Curriculum Tutor in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Not every tutor who teaches CBSE well can teach the International Baccalaureate or Cambridge IGCSE well. IB Gram matches your child with a verified specialist in the exact programme and subject, arranges a trial lesson before you commit, and runs lessons at home, online or a mix of both across Gurgaon.
introSummary: Searching for an international curriculum tutor Gurgaon parents can rely on usually means one thing: you want someone who has taught IB or IGCSE assessment itself, not just the subject content those boards happen to sit on. IB Gram's first job is to find a specialist whose profile matches your child's programme, subject and level, for home tutoring, online lessons or both. In Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, IB Diploma, MYP and IGCSE families juggle three overlapping demands: coursework that carries real marks, command terms that change what an answer needs, and a school calendar that rarely lines up with a tutor's other students. Home tuition is where most families start, because a tutor at your table catches errors a screen sometimes misses.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches an International Curriculum Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Matching sounds like a small word for what actually has to happen before a tutor walks into your home or logs into a video call. An international curriculum tutor Gurgaon families choose off a marketplace listing, with no verification behind the profile, is a gamble; IB Gram instead checks programme experience before a name ever reaches you. A tutor who has taught DP Physics HL for three years is not the same specialist as one who has taught CBSE Physics and picked up an IB textbook last month, even if both list "IB" on a profile.

The process starts with your query, not with a list of available tutors, because the board, the level and the exact subject decide who is even eligible for the shortlist. A parent asking for help with MYP Individuals and Societies criterion work needs someone fluent in criteria A to D; a parent asking about IGCSE Physics needs someone who knows the difference between the Core and Extended papers before a first lesson is booked.

Every match gets a trial lesson before anything is confirmed, at home, online or a mix of both, because a tutor's manner in that first hour tells you more than any profile can. Some students need a tutor who drills past papers from minute one; others need thirty minutes of rapport before any content lands. IB Gram treats the trial as a genuine checkpoint, not a formality, and a family that is not convinced can ask for a different match with no awkwardness.

None of this replaces your own judgment. Ask the tutor directly which syllabus they last taught, request a sample of how they mark a practice essay or problem set, and ask what they will do differently in week two if week one shows a gap. A specialist answers these questions in specifics; a generalist reaches for reassurance instead.
items: 1. You send a query describing the board, programme, subject, grade and the sectors or societies you want lessons in.
2. IB Gram asks follow-up questions: HL or SL, the exact syllabus if you have it, and your preferred evening slots.
3. A shortlist of two or three verified tutors is sent, each matched to that programme and level, not just the subject name.
4. A free trial lesson is arranged at home, online or hybrid, so you see the tutor's method before committing to anything.
5. After the trial, you confirm the match or ask for a different tutor, and regular sessions are scheduled around the school week.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What an International Curriculum Actually Demands
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, with six subjects from six subject groups. Three or four sit at Higher Level, 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level, 150 hours; each is graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add up to 3 further points, so the maximum is 45 and the diploma minimum is 24, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service, usually just called CAS, has to be completed too, and it is easy for a busy DP2 student to let it slide until the last term.

The Middle Years Programme covers five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, graded differently from what CBSE or ICSE families expect. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A through D, each out of 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1-7 grade through the IB's own boundaries. A tutor who just marks an answer right or wrong, instead of teaching to those criteria, is teaching the wrong thing. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project, with the Community Project usually in MYP 3 or 4, and MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, is optional and left to each school to decide.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session; November is used by a minority of schools and by retake candidates, and May results are released in early July. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually months ahead of May, and those mocks matter more than families sometimes treat them. Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, set the depth every answer needs, and a student who writes a "describe" answer to an "evaluate" question loses marks that have nothing to do with subject knowledge.
items: Diploma Programme students take six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, graded 1 to 7 in each.
Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add up to 3 more points, maximum 45, minimum 24 for the diploma.
Middle Years Programme subjects are marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, then converted to a 1-7 grade.
The Personal Project falls in MYP 5, after the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4.

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE Subjects Where Gurgaon Students Need a Specialist
contentBlocks.body:
Ask an international curriculum tutor Gurgaon parents are considering which syllabus they last taught, and watch how quickly the answer comes. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are not interchangeable, even in the same subject. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some subjects now also offered as 9-1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel grades every International GCSE 9 to 1. A tutor who cannot tell you which one your child's school follows has not actually taught it recently.

Many Cambridge subjects, Maths and the sciences especially, split into Core and Extended tiers, decided by the school partway through the two-year course. Core tops out at a grade C; Extended reaches A* but carries harder content and a faster pace. Getting this decision wrong, or tutoring toward the wrong tier, wastes months a student does not have in Grade 10. A specialist tutor asks which tier a student is entered for before the first lesson, not after.

On the Diploma Programme side, subject choice is not really six separate decisions. Three or four Higher Level subjects at 240 recommended hours and the rest at Standard Level at 150 hours together decide how a student's two years are paced, and a change in one subject can ripple into how much time is left for the others. Group choices interact: a student weak in mathematics who has chosen a HL science carries risk in two places at once, and a tutor who only sees one subject in isolation misses that.

Across both IB and IGCSE, command terms, and the equivalent instruction words in IGCSE mark schemes, decide what an answer actually needs. A student who has memorised content but never practised against a real mark scheme or set of criteria loses marks for structure, not knowledge. Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports, available through the school or the exam board's own channels, are the clearest evidence of how marks are really awarded, and any tutor claiming subject expertise should already be using them.
items: Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses are graded A* to G, though some now also run 9-1 versions under separate codes.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades every subject 9 to 1, unlike the older A*-G scale.
Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*.
DP subjects sit within six subject groups, shaping HL and SL choices across both years, not just one paper.

contentBlocks.heading: How Does International Curriculum Home Tuition Work Across Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Golf Course Extension Road covers Sectors 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 62 and 65, along with Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, and it is one of the busier corridors for an international curriculum tutor Gurgaon families book here in the evening. Societies like M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon run visitor registration at the gate, which can add ten to fifteen minutes before a lesson starts. Evening traffic near the toll plaza can stretch a short trip, so families here often ask for a slightly later start.

Sohna Road stretches from Sector 47 through Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur, with societies including Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close. It is a long corridor, and a tutor who covers Sector 47 comfortably may find Badshahpur, at the far end, a genuinely different commute. Families near Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur often do better with an earlier evening slot, before the corridor's own rush hour builds.

DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City, including Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur and Sectors 24, 27 and 28, sit at the commercial heart of Gurgaon, and weekday evening traffic here can be the worst in the city right as office and school traffic overlap. Societies such as DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona are well used to visitor entry procedures, but the drive in from outside the corridor is where time actually gets lost, not the gate itself. Where evening traffic in this corridor makes a fixed slot unreliable, switching one weekly session to online, while keeping the rest at home, is often the better call than losing a session altogether.

contentBlocks.heading: International Schools in Gurgaon: The Calendar Every Tutor Must Track
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon is home to a number of well-known international schools, among them Pathways World School in Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School in Aravali and DPS International Edge. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; these names are mentioned only because families searching for a tutor are usually thinking about their own child's school calendar, not because of any relationship between IB Gram and the school.

Every school sets its own term dates, internal test windows and deadlines, and two students on the same board at different schools can be weeks apart in what is due when. A tutor who plans lessons around a generic IB or IGCSE calendar, rather than the actual dates your child's school has set, will end up revising the wrong thing in the wrong week. This is one of the first questions worth asking a prospective tutor directly: do they ask for your child's own school calendar, or do they assume one?

The pressure points repeat every year but rarely at convenient times. DP2 mock examinations, set independently by each school, usually land months before the May session, and they often coincide with a younger sibling's own unit tests or a school event that eats into the week. Sports days, exhibitions, university counselling sessions and inter-school events are a normal part of international school life in Gurgaon, and a realistic tuition plan works with the school's own pacing, building in some slack, rather than assuming every week runs exactly to schedule.
items: Term dates, unit tests and internal deadlines vary school to school, even for students on the same board.
A DP2 student's mock exams can land in the same month as a younger sibling's unit tests.
Sports days, exhibitions and inter-school events regularly eat into a week a family had planned for revision.
A tutor who does not track your child's specific school calendar will schedule around the wrong deadlines.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Classes, Online or Hybrid: Which Suits an International Curriculum Tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is where IB Gram starts most families, and for good reason. A tutor sitting beside your child at the dining table sees the actual working, not just the final answer, and catches a wrong method in real time, before it turns into a habit that shows up again in the mocks. For an international curriculum tutor Gurgaon families book for home lessons, this matters more than usual, because IB and IGCSE mark schemes reward method and process, not just a correct final number.

Online lessons are not a compromise, though; they solve a different problem. A shared screen works well for reviewing past papers, marking essays line by line, or running a doubt session late on a weekday evening when travel across a congested corridor is not realistic. Families juggling exam weeks, a sudden school event or simply a bad traffic day often find one online session a week keeps momentum going without cancelling altogether.

Hybrid is the honest middle ground for many Gurgaon families: most sessions at home, where the tutor can read the student's handwriting and habits, with one session moved online when the week gets difficult. The trade-off is fairly simple, and worth being honest about. Home tuition gives a tutor the clearest read on a student but depends on traffic, gate entry and a workable study space; online removes all of that but asks more of the student's own focus and internet connection. Younger students and anyone new to a subject usually do better with more home sessions early on; older, self-directed students preparing for exams often manage a heavier online mix without losing much.
items: Home lessons let a tutor see the actual notebook, catch a wrong method before it becomes a habit.
Online lessons cut out travel entirely, useful during exam weeks or heavy Gurgaon traffic.
Hybrid works well for families who want most sessions at home but flexibility during a busy fortnight.
Younger students, especially in MYP, often focus better with a tutor physically in the room.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is an International Curriculum Tutor in Gurgaon Verified?
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on paper is only half the job; a parent's own questions do the rest. IB Gram checks a tutor's programme and subject experience before a profile is even shortlisted, so you are not the one doing background checks from scratch. But no platform, however careful, replaces the value of asking direct questions yourself once a name is in front of you.

Ask which syllabus or programme level the tutor last taught, and for how long, not just which board. "I teach IB" means very little on its own; "I have taught DP Chemistry HL for four sessions" tells you something. Ask for a short sample of marked work, an essay annotated against real criteria or a problem set marked the way an examiner would, so you can see how they actually assess, not just how they present.

Confirm who will be in the room. It sounds obvious, but in a few informal arrangements the person who does the sales call is not the person who turns up to teach, and a family should never discover that mismatch after the first session. IB Gram matches you directly with the tutor who will teach, and that person is who joins the trial lesson. Treat that trial lesson itself as a verification step: ask the tutor to work through one real problem live, and watch how they explain a mistake. A specialist answers in specifics; someone reaching for general reassurance is telling you something too.
items: Programme and subject experience is checked before a profile is shortlisted, not after a complaint.
Ask directly which syllabus or programme level the tutor last taught, and for how long.
Request a short sample of marked work, an essay or problem set, before the trial lesson.
Confirm who will actually teach the lesson; the person on the call should be the person at the table.

contentBlocks.heading: What Separates a Real Specialist From a General Tutor?
contentBlocks.body:
The gap between a specialist and a general tutor rarely shows up in the first five minutes of a conversation; both can sound confident. It shows up in the second question. Ask what changes between MYP 4 and MYP 5 for a subject, or what a DP1 student should be doing differently from a DP2 student in the same course, and a specialist answers immediately, because they have actually taught across those years. A generalist pauses, or answers in generalities that would apply to any board.

Before the trial lesson, ask three things: which syllabus or level they taught most recently, how they will structure the first session, and what they will look at to judge whether the match works. A vague answer is worth noting. After the trial, ask what they noticed in your child's work that you did not mention, and what they would change in week two. A specialist can point to something specific from that one hour.

What an international curriculum genuinely demands, and a general tutor often underestimates, is that a right answer is not always full marks. Coursework counts toward the final grade in a way it usually does not on other boards; command terms decide the depth an answer needs before a single mark is awarded; and criterion or mark-scheme marking rewards process as much as outcome. This is also where research-led tasks, the Extended Essay, the Personal Project, IGCSE coursework components, ask a student to work somewhat independently, with the tutor guiding structure and process rather than producing content. A tutor teaching purely to "get the right answer" is teaching for the wrong exam.
items: A specialist can name the exact syllabus, paper structure and command terms without looking it up.
A specialist marks against real criteria or mark schemes, not just their own sense of a good answer.
A specialist knows what changes between DP1 and DP2, or MYP 4 and MYP 5, for that subject.
A generalist often over-relies on a textbook written for a different board entirely.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Progress Look Like After Four Weeks?
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is not long enough to move a grade, and any tutor who implies otherwise is telling you what you want to hear rather than what is true. No tutor can guarantee a grade; what four weeks should show is direction, not a destination. By the end of the first month, the tutor should be able to describe specific gaps found in week one, and specific work done on them since, rather than a general sense that things are going well.

Look for concrete signs. Is homework or practice work coming back with actual feedback, marked against a real criterion or mark scheme, or just assigned and briefly checked? Can your child explain, in their own words, what a command term like "evaluate" or "discuss" is actually asking for? These are small, checkable things, and they tell you more than a general impression of whether lessons are "going well".

A short update to parents, even an informal one, should happen at least once across the four weeks: what has been covered, what is still shaky, and what the plan is for the next stretch. And if, honestly, nothing has moved after four weeks, that is useful information too, not a reason to keep waiting quietly. It might mean the subject needs a different specialist, the student needs a different pace, or the gap runs deeper than tuition alone can fix in an hour or two a week. Raising it early, and asking for a different match if needed, costs far less than another term of the same thing not working.
items: The tutor can name specific gaps found in week one, not just a general 'doing fine'.
Homework or practice questions are being returned with feedback, not just assigned.
The student can explain a command term's meaning in their own words, unprompted.
If nothing has changed by week four, that itself is useful information, not a reason to wait longer.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started With International Curriculum Tutoring in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started is simple by design. Send a query through IB Gram, or book a free consultation call, with as much detail as you have: the board, the programme, the subject, the grade, and roughly which sectors or societies work for a home session. The more specific the query, the faster and more accurate the shortlist that comes back.

IB Gram will ask a few follow-up questions if anything is missing: Higher Level or Standard Level, the exact syllabus if you know it, your child's school calendar if there is an upcoming mock or deadline, and your preferred evening or weekend slots. None of this is a sales process; it is what actually decides which tutor on the platform is a genuine fit, as opposed to just available.

The first session itself, once a trial is arranged, usually starts with the tutor understanding where your child actually stands, not launching straight into new content. Bring a recent test paper, school report or piece of marked work if you have one; it saves the tutor a session's worth of guessing and gets useful teaching started sooner. From there, lessons run at home, online or a mix of both, on a schedule built around the school week rather than a fixed template. If the first tutor is not the right fit after all, subject to availability, a different match can be arranged without the process starting over from scratch. None of this needs to happen in one sitting; families often send a short first message and fill in the detail once IB Gram writes back with a question.
items: Have the board, programme and subject ready: DP Chemistry HL is more useful than just 'IB tutor'.
Note the syllabus if you have it, from a textbook, school portal or previous report.
Decide your preferred slots and whether home, online or hybrid suits the week ahead.
Keep the last school report or a recent test paper on hand for the first session.

faqs.question: How is an international curriculum tutor different from a regular subject tutor?
faqs.answer: A specialist has actually taught IB or IGCSE assessment, not just the subject content the board happens to use. They know the exact command terms, mark schemes or criteria your child's board applies, and they plan lessons around your child's actual syllabus and level rather than a generic textbook. A general tutor can be excellent at the subject itself and still miss how marks are really awarded on an IB or IGCSE paper, which shows up in exam technique long before it shows up in content knowledge. Ask directly which syllabus or programme level a tutor last taught before booking a trial.

faqs.question: How much does an international curriculum tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on the board, level, subject and whether lessons are at home, online or hybrid, so a fixed figure is not quoted here; a consultation call covers this directly once your child's needs are known. What is fixed is the process: a free trial lesson happens before you commit to anything, and pricing is discussed clearly before regular sessions are confirmed. Availability and scheduling are always subject to the tutor's calendar and your preferred slots.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our home near DLF Phase 3 or Golf Course Extension Road?
faqs.answer: Yes, home lessons are available across Golf Course Extension Road, Sohna Road and the DLF Phase 2 to 4 and Cyber City corridor, subject to tutor availability for your child's board and level. A tutor matched to DLF Phase 3 or near M3M Golf Estate on Golf Course Extension Road will factor in visitor registration at the gate and evening traffic when agreeing a slot. If a corridor is difficult to reach reliably in the evening, IB Gram will suggest hybrid lessons instead of promising a fixed slot that traffic keeps breaking.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson is a real lesson, not a sales pitch: the tutor works through a piece of your child's actual coursework or a practice question live, so you can see their method before committing to anything. It typically covers a quick diagnostic of where your child stands, one worked example, and a short conversation about what the tutor noticed. After the trial, you can confirm the match, ask questions, or request a different tutor with no obligation either way.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for IB and IGCSE, or is home tuition always better?
faqs.answer: Both work, for different things. Online tutoring works well for reviewing past papers, marking essays and running doubt sessions, and it removes Gurgaon's evening traffic from the equation entirely. Home tuition works best when a tutor needs to see a student's actual working in real time, which matters most for younger students or anyone building a method from scratch. Many families here run a hybrid mix rather than choosing one exclusively, moving a session online when the week is difficult.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so as early as possible rather than waiting out a term hoping it improves. IB Gram can arrange a different tutor if the fit is not right, whether that is a mismatch in teaching style, pace or simply personality; this happens more often than families expect and is not a failure on either side. The sooner a mismatch is raised, the less time and momentum is lost before a better match is found.

faqs.question: Is there real progress after a month, or does it take longer?
faqs.answer: A month is enough to see direction, not a finished result, and no tutor can guarantee a grade in that time or any time. By four weeks, the tutor should be able to name specific gaps found early on and describe concrete work done on them, and your child should be able to explain a command term or criterion in their own words. If none of that is visible after four weeks, it is worth raising directly rather than assuming it will resolve on its own.

faqs.question: Can a session run on a weekday evening after school, given Gurgaon traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes, weekday evening slots are the most common request, and IB Gram matches tutors who already work that corridor and timing. In busier stretches, like DLF and Cyber City around 5 to 7 pm, a slightly later slot or one online session a week can keep lessons reliable instead of repeatedly starting late. It helps to mention your preferred time window and sector when you send your query, so the shortlist already accounts for it.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be present during home lessons?
faqs.answer: It is not required, but many families with younger students prefer a parent or house help to be home during the session, mainly for comfort and to handle the door for the tutor's arrival. Older DP or IGCSE students studying independently often do not need a parent in the room, though a short check-in at the end of the session is common. This is worth agreeing with the tutor directly in the first week.

faqs.question: How do I know if my child needs a specialist or just extra revision help?
faqs.answer: If your child is broadly keeping pace but wants extra practice before a test, a good general tutor or revision sessions may be enough. If the concern is coursework that counts toward the final grade, an Extended Essay, Internal Assessment, or understanding what a command term actually demands, a specialist familiar with that exact programme is the safer choice, because mistakes there are harder to undo close to a deadline. When in doubt, a free consultation call can help you work out which situation you are in.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: What Kind of Tuition Does Each Need?
contentBlocks.body:
The right kind of tuition depends on programme as much as grade, and the two aren't the same conversation. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) student doesn't need exam coaching, since PYP has no external exam, tuition here is about reading stamina, number sense and the confidence to explain thinking aloud, built steadily rather than crammed.

A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student, across the five years of MYP 1 to MYP 5 and eight subject groups, is assessed against four criteria, A through D, each scored 0-8, with the criterion total converting to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. Tuition here needs to teach the criteria directly, not just the topic, since a student can know the content and still lose marks against a criterion never addressed. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, with a Community Project earlier in MYP 3 or 4 at some schools, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, is optional and decided school by school.

A Diploma Programme (DP) student needs tuition matched to level as much as subject: three or four subjects at Higher Level (HL, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, around 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum, with 24 as the minimum for the diploma, and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) runs alongside as a non-graded requirement. An international syllabus tutor Gurugram families bring in for a DP1 student building foundations works differently from one supporting a DP2 student four months from May, even in the same subject.

contentBlocks.heading: IB and IGCSE Subjects: Where a Specialist Earns Their Keep
contentBlocks.body:
A general tutor can usually teach the content of a subject. A specialist knows how that specific board marks it, and the gap between the two shows up first in exam technique, not topic knowledge. Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate qualifications with different grading, Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, some now with separate 9-1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1, and a tutor who's only ever taught one can misjudge the other's mark scheme badly in the first few sessions.

Tier is a second layer a specialist tracks closely. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, Core capped at a C, Extended reaching A*, and preparing a student for the wrong tier's demands wastes real weeks before anyone notices.

On the DP side, a specialist knows that Higher Level (HL, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours) and Standard Level (SL, around 150 hours) in the same subject are different courses, not the same one taught faster or slower, and prepares a student differently depending on which one they're sitting.

Command terms run through both boards: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, and decide how much depth an answer is worth regardless of topic. A general tutor often teaches content well but never explicitly trains a student to read the command term, and that gap costs marks in every internal assessment and every exam paper, IB or IGCSE alike.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Specialist Tutor Knows That a General Tutor Doesn't
contentBlocks.body:
A general tutor, someone comfortable across CBSE, ICSE and international boards, can genuinely help an international curriculum student, especially with foundational content in a subject like Maths where core skills overlap heavily across boards. But there's a ceiling to what general competence covers, and it shows up exactly where international curricula differ most from the boards a general tutor usually knows best. Many international curriculum tuitions in Gurgaon look similar on paper, so this is the actual test worth applying.

The clearest gap is coursework that counts toward the final grade. A DP student's Internal Assessment, an MYP student's Personal Project, an IGCSE student's coursework component where the syllabus includes one, all carry real weight in the final outcome, and all are marked against published criteria or mark schemes rather than a single correct answer. A specialist has actually read those criteria, knows which words in a mark scheme separate a strong answer from an adequate one, and can tell a student specifically what a top-band response needs that a middling one doesn't. A general tutor, unfamiliar with the criteria's exact language, tends to give feedback that sounds right but doesn't map onto how the work is actually scored.

Command terms are the second gap. Define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, each demands a different depth of answer, and a specialist drills this explicitly because they've seen students lose marks for years on technically correct answers that ignored what the command term actually asked for. A general tutor often teaches subject content thoroughly but never separately trains a student to parse the command term, leaving a gap that only shows up in the exam room.

Research-led tasks are the third. An Extended Essay, an Internal Assessment, a Personal Project, all ask a student to develop their own research question and defend it with evidence, a skill closer to early undergraduate work than to a typical school assignment. A specialist has coached students through this process enough times to know where it typically goes wrong, a question too broad to answer in the word limit, evidence that doesn't actually address the question asked, and can catch it early rather than after a full draft is written.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Four Weeks of Tuition Actually Show?
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks in, expect something specific and nameable, not a general sense that lessons are going well. Perhaps your DP1 Physics student now shows full working instead of jumping to an answer, closing the exact gap the trial class identified. Perhaps an IGCSE English student's essays finally address the command term instead of writing around it. Small and specific is the standard, not a big jump in confidence alone.

No tutor, however good, can guarantee a grade, a 7, an A* or a fixed number of marks, and any tutor or platform implying otherwise should be questioned rather than trusted. There's no single best international curriculum tuition in Gurgaon in the abstract, only the best fit for your child's board, level and school calendar. What four weeks of good tuition should show is a tutor who can point to exactly what's improved and what's still being worked on, tied to your child's actual coursework and test results, not a general impression.

Progress rarely moves evenly. A student might sharpen quickly on one paper component while a separate weakness takes longer to shift, and that's ordinary rather than a warning sign on its own. What is worth noticing is a tutor who reports uniform improvement every single week without being able to point to anything specific, since that usually means the sessions aren't being assessed closely.

If, after four to six genuine sessions, nothing concrete has changed and the tutor can't name what's being worked on, that's a fair point to ask IB Gram for a different match rather than continuing through an exam term hoping it improves.

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask whether the tutor identified something specific about your child's understanding that you didn't already know, whether they referenced the actual mark scheme or criteria rather than speaking generally about the subject, and whether your child felt comfortable admitting what they didn't understand. acceptedAnswer.text: Expect something specific and nameable, not a general sense that lessons are going well: full working shown on Maths problems instead of jumping to answers, an essay finally addressing the command term, a clearer research question for an Internal Assessment draft. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a 7, an A* or a fixed mark improvement, so treat any such promise as a warning sign rather than reassurance. mainEntity.name: Is online tuition as effective as home tuition for the IB DP?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the subject and the student rather than being universally true either way. A DP2 student deep into past-paper practice in a subject they're already fairly strong in can often do just as well online, and scheduling gets easier for both sides. A DP1 student still building foundational understanding in a demanding HL subject, or one who simply works better with someone alongside them, usually benefits more from home tuition's closer, in-person read of what's actually going wrong. contentBlocks.heading: What must an international board tutor know about DP and MYP?
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor claiming to teach the IB Diploma Programme should be able to explain, unprompted, why a student is carrying six subjects across six groups rather than a narrower set: three or four at Higher Level, each carrying 240 recommended teaching hours, and the remainder at Standard Level, at 150 hours, with every subject graded on the 1 to 7 scale. They should know that Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add up to 3 further points on top of the six subjects, that 45 is the theoretical ceiling and 24 the minimum for the diploma itself, and that Creativity, Activity, Service runs the whole two years and has to be completed in full, not simply logged as started. A tutor who cannot rattle off this structure has probably not taught many DP students under real conditions.

For MYP, the test is different. A genuine specialist explains the four assessment criteria, labelled A through D and scored out of 8 each, and how that criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through the IB's own grade boundaries, not a tutor's private guess. They should know MYP runs across five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, and that the Personal Project belongs to MYP 5 specifically, with a Community Project usually sitting in MYP 3 or MYP 4 instead. Some schools additionally run MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, entirely at the school's own discretion, and a tutor who does not think to ask whether a family's school offers it is working from assumption rather than fact.

When you interview a prospective tutor, ask them to explain, in their own words, how a DP subject grade differs from an MYP subject grade. A tutor who blurs the two together is telling you something important before the first lesson has even started.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you judge a tutor's real subject expertise?
contentBlocks.body:
Credentials on a profile only go so far, so the useful test happens in conversation, before or during the trial lesson. A tutor who cannot describe a real example, only general encouragement, is likely newer to this kind of guidance than their profile suggests.

For Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge support, the test is different again: ask how they help a student narrow an overly broad research question, since this is the single most common place DP students lose time and confidence, and a tutor with real experience will have a concrete process rather than a vague answer about brainstorming. For an MYP subject, ask which of the four assessment criteria a tutor finds students most often struggle with in that subject, since a genuine specialist will have a clear, specific answer rather than needing to think about it for the first time in front of you.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tutoring, online or hybrid: which style fits your child in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring tends to suit a student who needs visible structure and a set routine to actually sit down and work, since a tutor physically at the table removes the option of quietly drifting off to another tab or another room. It also lets a tutor read a student's body language directly, catching the moment a student has stopped following well before the student admits it out loud, which matters enormously for a quieter child who will not say "I'm lost" unprompted.

Online sessions suit a different kind of student rather better than families sometimes expect: an older, more independent DP2 student who mainly wants a focused subject conversation without the social pressure of someone sitting across the table, or a student who works well with shared annotation tools and screen-based working. Online also widens the pool of available tutors considerably, useful for a less common DP subject or a specific MYP elective where the right personality match may not live in a family's own corridor.

Hybrid, in practice, is less a fixed plan and more an honest acknowledgment that a student's needs change across a school year and even across a single term. A student anxious before a Personal Project deadline may want a tutor physically present for a stretch of weeks, then comfortable shifting back online once that pressure eases. heroTitle: Choosing International Board Tuition in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: IB Diploma, MYP, Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE each run on a different structure, a different grading scale and a different school calendar, so a tuition programme built for one rarely fits another without real changes. This page sets out what a genuine international board tuition programme in Gurgaon should look like, week to week.
introSummary: International board tuition in Gurgaon is regular, structured teaching support built around the exact programme a student is on, IB Diploma, IB Middle Years Programme, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, rather than a one-size revision class. Most families that search this phrase want home tuition to start with: a verified tutor teaching in the family's own sector or society, with online and hybrid sessions offered alongside it once term-time traffic or a clashing school activity makes an evening slot difficult. Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana has students spread across several of these programmes at once within the same school, sometimes the same family, so a tuition provider needs to plan around each child's own syllabus rather than a single generic timetable. IB Gram builds that plan from the first query: board, level, subject and schedule, then matches a verified tutor and arranges a free trial before anything regular begins.

contentBlocks.body:
A tuition arrangement that actually works starts with specifics, not a general request for "an international board tutor." IB Gram asks a family to name the programme first, IB Diploma, MYP, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, then the subject, the level within that programme (Higher Level or Standard Level for DP, the MYP year, the tier for IGCSE) and the family's Gurgaon sector or society. Without this, a shortlist is guesswork.

A coordinator calls within a working day to confirm the school's own pacing and any deadline already on the calendar, a DP2 mock date, an MYP Personal Project deadline, or an IGCSE coursework cut-off, because a tuition plan that ignores these dates ends up reactive rather than useful. From there, tutors are shortlisted against the exact programme and level, not a general international-schools label, and their profiles are shared with the family before anything is booked.

A free trial class follows, at home, online or hybrid, and this is where the plan actually gets tested against a real student rather than a description on paper. If the trial goes well, regular tuition is scheduled around the family's week, typically the same one or two evenings so the rhythm holds through a school term. If it does not go well, IB Gram offers a different tutor and a new trial rather than asking the family to persevere with a poor fit. The whole sequence is designed to reach a working weekly arrangement quickly, without skipping the step where the family actually sees the tutor teach.

contentBlocks.heading: What do the IB Diploma Programme and MYP actually require?
contentBlocks.body:
The IB Diploma Programme runs across two years, DP1 and DP2, and asks a student to carry six subjects from six subject groups at once, three or four of them at Higher Level, which carries 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level, at 150 hours. Each subject is graded on a scale of 1 to 7, and Theory of Knowledge together with the Extended Essay contribute up to three further points on top of that, taking the theoretical maximum to 45, though 24 points is the minimum needed for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's own failing conditions around individual subject and core scores. Creativity, Activity, Service, known as CAS, runs alongside all of this and has to be completed, not merely started. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session, though a minority use November, and results from the May session are released in early July.

The Middle Years Programme sits underneath the Diploma, running across five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, over eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8, and that criterion total out of 32 converts to a final grade of 1 to 7 through the IB's own grade boundaries, which a tuition provider should be reading rather than guessing at. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project, with a Community Project typically sitting in MYP 3 or MYP 4 instead. Some schools also offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen examinations combined with ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides for itself whether to run it, which is exactly the kind of detail a tuition plan needs to confirm rather than assume.

A tuition programme that treats DP and MYP as the same thing, just "IB at different ages," misses how differently they are actually assessed. DP grading is largely exam-driven with substantial internal assessment weight; MYP grading runs entirely through criterion levels a subject teacher applies continuously through the year. Preparation for one does not automatically prepare a student for the other.

contentBlocks.heading: Which subjects need the most tuition support across these boards?
contentBlocks.body:
Subject demand tends to cluster, and a tuition provider who has actually taught across these boards in Gurgaon will recognise the pattern instantly rather than treat every subject request as equally common. Within DP, Higher Level Mathematics and the Higher Level sciences draw the heaviest tuition demand, partly because they carry the most teaching hours and partly because Internal Assessment work in these subjects needs sustained one-to-one guidance rather than a single revision session before a deadline. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, sitting across the whole diploma rather than inside one subject, also generate steady tuition demand, usually focused on structuring an argument and applying command terms correctly rather than reteaching content from scratch.

Within MYP, tuition tends to concentrate around the criterion-based subjects where a student's classroom marks have started slipping across two or three of the four criteria at once, since a drop in one criterion, say Criterion C on applying knowledge, quietly caps the whole grade even when the others are strong. The Personal Project in MYP 5 is its own tuition need entirely, less about subject content and more about research process, time management and the reflective write-up the project demands.

Across Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE within this same international-board umbrella, Mathematics and the sciences again lead demand, for the same reason as at DP level: these are the subjects where working shown on paper earns marks directly, so a tutor's ability to mark against a real scheme, not just explain a concept, matters more than in an essay-based subject. Whatever the specific subject, the common thread across every one of these boards is that command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, set the depth an answer needs, and a tutor who does not drill this distinction explicitly is leaving marks on the table that have nothing to do with subject knowledge.

Along Golf Course Road, covering DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1, Sector 42, Sector 43, Sector 53, Sector 54, Ardee City and Wazirabad, tuition slots tend to sit easily on weekday evenings once a tutor is established in the area, though societies such as DLF The Magnolias, DLF The Aralias, DLF Park Place, DLF The Crest and DLF The Belaire each run their own visitor sign-in, so a first session usually needs a few extra minutes at the gate that later sessions do not.

Societies here, M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon among them, are used to tutors visiting regularly, and a fixed weekly slot tends to work better than an ad-hoc one because security and the family both know to expect the tutor.

Sohna Road covers the largest area of the three: Sector 47 through Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur, with societies including Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close. contentBlocks.heading: What the international school calendar means for tuition planning in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Families at schools including Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge each work through a school year with its own internal rhythm, and a tuition plan that ignores it tends to arrive at the wrong intensity at the wrong time. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; these names are offered only to describe the calendar pressures families in Gurgaon generally face.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter their DP2 cohort for the May exam session, and each school sets its own mock examination dates for that cohort, usually several months ahead of May, which gives a tuition programme a natural checkpoint to build toward. Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's own official channels, and a tuition provider should be using these directly rather than improvising practice questions that do not match the command terms an examiner actually expects.

Across MYP and IGCSE years within the same school, internal deadlines, a Personal Project submission, a piece of IGCSE coursework, a speaking assessment, typically land weeks before the board's own cut-off, because a school needs time to moderate the work before sending it on. A well-run tuition programme tracks these internal dates on its own calendar, not just the final exam session, and steps up intensity in the weeks before each one rather than running the same pace year-round regardless of what is actually due.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: what suits international board study in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the starting point for most families arranging international board tuition in Gurgaon, and for a good practical reason: a tutor working at the family's own table can watch a student's Internal Assessment draft take shape over several weeks, flag a criterion drifting off track before it becomes a pattern, and leave the student with marked-up working to revisit before the next session. For subjects graded through sustained coursework, DP Internal Assessments, the MYP Personal Project, IGCSE coursework components, this kind of continuity is genuinely harder to replace remotely.

Online tuition earns its place for different reasons. It removes the travel variable entirely, which matters on the evenings when Sohna Road or Golf Course Extension Road traffic makes a fixed slot unreliable, and it opens access to a subject specialist who may not regularly work a family's specific corridor, useful for a less commonly requested DP subject or a niche MYP elective. Screen-sharing and annotation tools handle worked mathematics or a marked essay draft reasonably well, even if they cannot quite replicate sitting beside a student while they write.

Most families settle into a hybrid pattern across a school year without ever deciding it as a single choice: home sessions through the calmer stretches of term, a switch to online around a school trip, a festival week or bad traffic, then back to home sessions once the calendar clears. IB Gram treats this as the default plan, agreed at the outset, rather than an emergency fallback arranged in a rush, because tuition that has to be renegotiated every time the week gets busy tends to quietly stop happening at all.

contentBlocks.heading: Switching between international boards in Gurgaon: what actually transfers?
contentBlocks.body:
Families relocating to Gurgaon, or moving a child between schools within it, ask this constantly, and the honest answer depends heavily on which two boards and which year group are involved. Moving from CBSE into an international board, most often into MYP or into IGCSE at the start of Grade 9, is generally the most manageable transition when it happens at a natural entry point, since the student is starting the programme's own two-year or five-year structure from the beginning rather than joining mid-stream. Subject knowledge in Mathematics and the sciences usually transfers reasonably well; the bigger adjustment tends to be assessment style, since CBSE's exam format differs sharply from MYP's criterion-based marking or an IGCSE mark scheme's method-mark structure.

Moving from IGCSE into the IB Diploma Programme after Grade 10 is the most common transition within the international-board world itself, and it is generally well supported precisely because Cambridge and Edexcel design their IGCSE syllabuses with progression into DP or A Levels in mind. What genuinely changes is workload structure: DP demands six subjects simultaneously alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, a heavier concurrent load than most IGCSE years carry, and a tuition plan for a student entering DP1 should treat the first term as an adjustment period rather than assume the student will manage the load on day one.

Moving between MYP and a different international programme mid-cycle, say MYP 3 to an IGCSE-based school, is the transition that needs the most care, because MYP's criterion-based assessment does not map cleanly onto an exam-driven syllabus, and a student can arrive with strong classroom habits that simply do not translate directly into exam technique. In every case, the honest first step is not a tuition plan at all, but a conversation with the new school's academic coordinator about exactly what year group and syllabus the student is entering, since a tutor working from an assumption rather than a confirmed placement wastes real time.

contentBlocks.heading: What should four weeks of international board tuition show?
contentBlocks.body:
After four regular sessions, a family should expect something concrete: a short note naming what was covered against the actual programme, a specific DP topic, an MYP criterion worked on, an IGCSE syllabus point, plus what comes next and where the student is still struggling. If a provider cannot produce even an informal version of this after a month, it is worth asking for directly rather than assuming the tuition is on track.

On the academic side, four weeks is realistically enough time to see a change in how a student approaches work, tighter structure in an essay draft, cleaner working on a Mathematics problem, a Personal Project research question that has sharpened from vague to answerable, but it is not enough time to move a full grade band or guarantee a particular outcome, DP points included. Any provider promising a specific grade change within a month should be treated with real scepticism, because assessment in these programmes, whether IB's criteria or a board's mark scheme, does not move that predictably.

Limits matter here too, and a good tuition provider states them plainly. A student starting DP tuition in the middle of DP2, close to mocks, has a narrower set of realistic goals than one starting in DP1, and pretending otherwise sets a family up for disappointment. If four weeks reveal that a student's actual difficulty is workload management across all six subjects rather than one subject's content, the right response is to say so and adjust the plan, not to keep adding hours to the subject the family originally asked about.

contentBlocks.heading: Setting Up a Home Visit in Gurgaon: How IB Gram Matches Your Family
contentBlocks.body:
A home lesson is not just a video call moved into your living room. Someone is coming into your house, sitting with your child, and you want to know who that person is before they ring the doorbell. Finding an international school home tutor Gurgaon families can actually trust starts there: a tutor's programme experience and subject background are checked before a profile ever reaches you, and only tutors who already work in or near your part of Gurgaon are shortlisted for a home visit.

Your first message shapes everything that follows. Board, programme, subject and grade decide who is even eligible; your sector or society decides who can reasonably reach you on a weekday evening. A family in Sohna Road asking for an IGCSE Maths tutor gets a different shortlist from a family in New Gurgaon asking the same question, because travel time is part of the match, not an afterthought.

A free trial session happens at your home before anything is confirmed. This is deliberate: a tutor's manner in your child's own study space, at your own table, tells you things a phone call cannot. Does the tutor bring their own materials or expect yours? Do they set ground rules for the first ten minutes, or launch straight into content? You are watching for fit, not just competence.

If the visit does not feel right, say so. IB Gram will arrange a different tutor rather than leave you persisting with someone your child is uncomfortable with in their own home. Regular sessions are only scheduled once you are genuinely satisfied, not once a trial has simply happened.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What Changes Depending on Your Child's Stage
contentBlocks.body:
Younger children at Gurgaon's international schools are usually on the Primary Years Programme, for ages 3 to 12. Learning here is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, Who We Are, Where We Are in Place and Time, How We Express Ourselves, How the World Works, How We Organize Ourselves and Sharing the Planet, taught through units of inquiry rather than separate subject periods. There are no external examinations at this stage; a home tutor's job is less about exam technique and more about reinforcing the ten attributes of the IB learner profile and building genuine confidence before the PYP exhibition in the final year.

Between roughly ages 11 and 16, students move into the Middle Years Programme, five years, MYP 1 to 5, across eight subject groups. Every subject is graded against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, with the criterion total out of 32 converting to a 1-7 grade. A home tutor working with an MYP student needs to teach toward those criteria directly, not just toward a right answer, and the Personal Project in MYP 5, with the Community Project usually in MYP 3 or 4, needs planning support well before the deadline.

By the Diploma Programme, two years, DP1 and DP2, a student is taking six subjects, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum and a 24-point diploma minimum. A home tutor at this stage is often working around exam-season pressure directly, since most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May session, with results out in early July.
items: The Primary Years Programme has no external exams; a home tutor's role is confidence and inquiry, not test prep.
MYP subjects are marked against four criteria out of 8 each, converting to a 1-7 grade.
The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, the Community Project usually a year or two earlier.
DP students split subjects between Higher and Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7 toward a 45-point maximum.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth: What a Home Tutor Should Already Know
contentBlocks.body:
For IGCSE students, whether the school follows Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel changes what a home tutor should bring to the table. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some now also offered as 9-1 versions under separate codes; Edexcel grades every International GCSE 9 to 1. A tutor who does not ask which board your child's school follows before the first session is guessing.

Many Cambridge subjects, particularly Maths and the sciences, split into Core and Extended tiers partway through the two-year course. Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*, and the two demand genuinely different pacing. A home tutor should know which tier a student sits before planning any lesson, because practising Extended-level problems with a Core-tier student wastes an evening neither of you gets back.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, run through IB assessment at every level, and the equivalent instruction words shape IGCSE mark schemes too. At home, this is where a tutor earns their place: not reteaching content the school already covered, but working through what an answer actually needs to score full marks against the real mark scheme or criteria, ideally with past papers and subject reports on the table rather than a generic worksheet. That distinction, between knowing a subject and knowing how it is marked, is the whole value of a home lesson over an evening spent alone with a textbook. Ask about all of this before the first session, not after homework starts coming back marked in ways that do not match what the school itself is doing.
items: Ask whether the school follows Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel before booking a subject specialist.
Confirm Core or Extended tier for Cambridge subjects before the first lesson is planned.
A home tutor should bring past papers and mark schemes, not a generic worksheet.
Command terms decide the depth an answer needs; content knowledge alone is not enough.

Golf Course Road, covering DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1, Sectors 42, 43, 53 and 54, Ardee City and Wazirabad, sits close to several international schools, and societies here, DLF The Magnolias, The Aralias, Park Place, The Crest and The Belaire, are used to visitor protocols at the gate. Golf Course Extension Road, Sectors 56 to 65 plus Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, with M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon among its societies, sits a little further out, and evening traffic near the toll can stretch a short trip. DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City, taking in Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur and Sectors 24, 27 and 28, is central but congested at exactly the hour most home lessons are booked. Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area around Sectors 29, 40, 45 and 46 sit close to this cluster and are generally straightforward for a tutor already working nearby.

Sohna Road runs from Sector 47 through Badshahpur, taking in Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend and Vatika Chowk, with societies like Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close; it is a long stretch, and a tutor comfortable near Sector 47 may find Badshahpur, at the far end, a different commute entirely. contentBlocks.heading: International Schools in Gurgaon and Why the Calendar Matters at Home
contentBlocks.body:
Families booking a home tutor here are often thinking of a specific school: Pathways World School in Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School in Aravali or DPS International Edge, among others. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; these names come up because a home tutor's schedule has to work around a specific school's calendar, not because of any partnership.

A home tutor who does not know your child's own school calendar will plan the wrong week. Unit tests, mocks and project deadlines differ school to school, even for students on the same board, and a session booked the evening before a school event is rarely a productive one. It is worth sharing your child's term calendar with a prospective tutor in the first message, not waiting for them to ask.

School buses, after-school activities and sports fixtures also shape when a home session can realistically start. A student arriving home at 4:30 pm most days but 6 pm on activity days needs a tutor willing to adjust, not a fixed slot that assumes every weekday looks the same. This kind of flexibility is exactly what a home tutor should be able to offer that a fixed-timing coaching batch cannot. None of this is complicated, but it is easy to overlook until a session is wasted covering the wrong topic in the wrong week.

School bus and activity timings vary day to day; a good home tutor adjusts rather than insisting on one fixed slot.

A home tutor's real value is fitting around your school's calendar, not working against it.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Lessons, Online or Hybrid: What Actually Works Best?
contentBlocks.body:
For an international school home tutor Gurgaon families book, home lessons are IB Gram's starting point for a reason. A tutor at your child's own desk sees the actual notebook, the actual handwriting, the actual mistake as it happens, and can correct a wrong method before it hardens into a habit. For a younger PYP or early MYP student especially, having someone physically present, asking questions out loud, tends to hold attention far better than a screen. This is also where materials matter: books, past papers and a proper desk, rather than a laptop balanced on a knee.

Online lessons have a real place too, particularly for older DP students reviewing past papers or marking essays, where a shared screen does the job just as well as a shared table, and there is no commute to plan around. On a heavy traffic evening, or during exam-season revision when back-to-back sessions with different subject specialists make sense, online can simply be more practical.

Hybrid is what most families settle into over a term: mostly home sessions, with one moved online when a corridor's evening traffic makes the timing unreliable, or when the family is travelling. The honest trade-off is this: home tuition gives the clearest read on a student but asks more of the calendar, gate entry and study space; online asks less logistically but more of the student's own focus. Neither is universally better; the right mix depends on the student's age, the subject and the week ahead.
items: Home sessions suit younger students and anyone building a method from scratch.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is a Home Tutor Verified Before They Visit?
contentBlocks.body:
Letting someone into your home for a weekly lesson is a different decision from enrolling in a coaching batch, and it deserves a different level of checking. IB Gram verifies a tutor's programme and subject experience before a profile is shortlisted for a home visit, so the background work is already done by the time a name reaches you.

Still, do your own checking too. Ask for the tutor's full name and confirm the person arriving is the person you spoke with. Ask what they will bring to the first session, and whether they expect your child to have specific books or past papers ready. A specialist will have clear, specific answers; someone improvising will not.

For the first visit specifically, confirm the timing with some buffer either side, since Gurgaon's evening traffic rarely respects a fixed slot exactly. If your society requires visitor registration, mention it in advance so the tutor is not stuck at the gate for the first fifteen minutes of a session you are paying for. Small logistics like this decide whether a home arrangement runs smoothly or becomes a recurring irritation. None of this is unusual to ask; a tutor used to home visits will expect these questions and answer them without hesitation. It is worth asking the same about an online or hybrid session too: how the tutor plans to share materials, mark work remotely, and keep a record of what has been covered, so nothing gets lost moving between one mode and another.

Ask what materials the tutor brings versus what your child should have ready.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does the First Home Session Actually Look Like?
contentBlocks.body:
The first session is not the first real lesson; it is closer to a diagnostic. A good tutor spends the opening minutes understanding where your child actually stands, not launching into new content, and asks to see recent schoolwork, a test paper or homework, if you have it ready. This is why it helps to have something concrete on hand rather than starting from nothing.

A proper study space matters more than families sometimes plan for. A clear desk, a chair at the right height, decent lighting and no television running in the next room make a measurable difference to how much a first session actually achieves. If your usual dining table is the only option, that works fine, as long as it is cleared and reasonably quiet for the hour.

Whether a parent should be in the room depends mostly on your child's age and the subject. Younger children, especially on the Primary Years Programme, often do better with a parent nearby, at least for the first few sessions, while older DP and IGCSE students studying independently usually prefer the room to themselves, with a brief check-in at the end. Either way, it is worth agreeing this with the tutor directly rather than assuming.

Materials worth having ready: the textbook or workbook currently in use, any recent test papers or marked homework, a notebook for working, not just the final answer, and, where relevant, a laptop or tablet if the tutor plans to use past papers digitally. None of this needs to be perfect on day one; a tutor experienced with home visits will work with whatever is actually available.
