contentBlocks.heading: What Should Change After a Month of Home Lessons?
contentBlocks.body:
A month of weekly home sessions is not enough to move a grade, and no tutor can honestly promise otherwise. What it should show is a visible change in how your child works, not just what they know. Are they opening their notebook before being asked? Are they attempting a hard question instead of skipping to the next one?

The tutor should be able to describe, specifically, what was found in the first session and what has shifted since, rather than a vague 'doing well.' Homework or practice questions should be coming back marked, with comments, not just a tick or a cross. If your child can explain a command term or a criterion in their own words, unprompted, that is a genuine sign of progress, however small it looks from the outside.

Home tuition also has honest limits. It will not fix a student who is fundamentally not doing the independent work between sessions, and it will not compensate for a mismatch between the tutor's pace and your child's actual level for very long. If a month in, the sessions still feel like a struggle to get through rather than useful, say so directly and ask for a different match; that is a normal part of the process, not a failure. IB Gram would rather rematch early than have a family quietly persist with something that is not working. This is normal, and it says more about fit than about effort on either side; a tutor who has been doing this for a while will usually say so themselves before you have to ask.

Clear a desk or table, keep the TV or other distractions out of the room for the hour, and have your child's current textbook and notebook within reach. Decide in advance whether you or another adult will be home during the session, particularly for a younger child, and mention your society's visitor registration process if there is one, so the tutor is not held up at the gate. If your evening slot sits inside a busy corridor, build in a few minutes of buffer either side rather than assuming the tutor will arrive exactly on time.

After the first session, IB Gram will check in on the fit before the second one is scheduled. If it is right, regular home lessons continue on the timing you agreed; if not, subject to availability, a different tutor can be arranged without losing the momentum you have already started.

heroTitle: Hiring an Independent Private Tutor in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: A private tutor works for your family alone, with no connection to your child's school and no conflict of interest to navigate. IB Gram verifies independence and subject experience, arranges a free trial lesson, and supports lessons at home, online or hybrid across Gurgaon, on terms you agree directly.
introSummary: An international school private tutor Gurgaon families engage for home tutoring is someone hired directly and independently, outside any coaching centre or school structure, usually because privacy, a conflict of interest, or simply full attention matters to that family. IB Gram verifies a tutor's programme experience and confirms they have no existing connection to your child's school before a profile is shortlisted, then supports lessons online or hybrid too, whichever suits your household. In Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, this arrangement comes up often when a family is weighing whether their child's own class teacher should tutor privately, a genuine conflict of interest worth thinking through, or when a family simply wants a specialist with no ties to the school at all. This page covers that decision, what to agree in writing, and how a private arrangement actually runs week to week.

contentBlocks.heading: Setting Up an Independent Tutor in Gurgaon: The Process
contentBlocks.body:
An independent tutor is, by definition, someone with no other role in your child's school life: not a class teacher, not a school-appointed remedial instructor, just a specialist you have engaged directly. Setting one up through IB Gram starts with the same basic information any tutor needs, but the emphasis is different, because privacy and independence are the point, not an afterthought. Finding the right international school private tutor Gurgaon families can rely on for genuine independence takes a little more care than a standard match.

Your query should say what kind of independence matters to you: perhaps you specifically do not want anyone connected to the school, or perhaps you simply want someone who will not discuss your child's difficulties with anyone else. IB Gram checks a tutor's programme and subject background, and confirms they have no existing relationship with your child's school before a profile is shortlisted.

A trial lesson follows, at home, online or hybrid, and this is where you can raise confidentiality directly: ask how the tutor keeps notes, whether they ever discuss a student's progress with anyone at the school, and how they would handle a scenario where your child's class teacher asked about the arrangement. A private tutor comfortable with these questions has usually thought about them before.

Once the arrangement is confirmed, IB Gram's role steps back; the ongoing relationship is between you, your child and the tutor, with IB Gram available if you want a different match later. This is different from a coaching centre relationship, where the institution stays involved throughout.
items: 1. You send a query describing the board, subject, grade and why independence or privacy matters to your family.
2. IB Gram confirms the tutor has no existing role at your child's school before shortlisting a profile.
3. You review two or three verified, independent profiles matched to your subject and level.
4. A trial lesson is arranged, at home, online or hybrid, where you can raise confidentiality and scheduling directly.
5. Once confirmed, you agree the details in writing and regular sessions begin on your schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What a Private Tutor Needs to Track
contentBlocks.body:
Private tutoring is less common at the Primary Years Programme stage, ages 3 to 12, where learning runs through six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry rather than separate graded subjects, and there are no external examinations to prepare for. Where a family does engage a private tutor here, it is usually for confidence, English or maths fluency, or support with the PYP exhibition in the final year, not exam coaching, since none exists yet.

From MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, converting to a 1-7 grade. An independent tutor working privately needs to understand those criteria as well as any school teacher does, because a student's own class teacher is the one setting internal deadlines for the Personal Project in MYP 5, and the Community Project usually a year or two earlier, and a private tutor has to work around those, not duplicate them.

The Diploma Programme runs two years, DP1 and DP2, six subjects, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay contributing up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum and a 24-point minimum for the diploma. Private DP tutoring often concentrates around the Extended Essay and Internal Assessment components, precisely the areas where academic integrity and the line between guidance and doing the work matter most.
items: PYP has no external exams; private tutoring here usually means confidence or fluency, not exam prep.
MYP criteria, A to D out of 8 each, apply whether a tutor is private or school-assigned.
The Personal Project in MYP 5 is set and deadlined by the school, not the private tutor.
DP's Extended Essay and Internal Assessment are where private tutoring needs the clearest integrity boundaries.

contentBlocks.heading: Syllabus Depth a Private Tutor Must Match Exactly
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are graded differently, A* to G, with some 9-1 syllabuses, versus 9 to 1 for every Edexcel subject, and an independent tutor should know which one applies before agreeing to take on a subject at all. This is a basic check a family can make in the first conversation.

Core and Extended tiers, common in Cambridge Maths and sciences, change what a private tutor should even be teaching. Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*, and a tutor unaware of which tier a student sits risks preparing them for the wrong paper entirely, wasting sessions that are harder to recover privately than in a school setting with other safety nets around a student. This is especially true for a family relying on private, one-to-one home tuition rather than a school's own extra classes or peer support.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, and their IGCSE mark-scheme equivalents, decide how an answer earns marks. An independent tutor's real value is working through past papers and mark schemes against these terms directly, something a class teacher managing many students rarely has time to do one-to-one, and something a private tutor should be doing from the first proper session. This is worth asking about directly: which past papers, and from which syllabus, the tutor actually plans to use. None of this is exotic knowledge; it is simply what a specialist keeps current, term after term.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Classes, Online or Hybrid: What Suits a Private Arrangement?

Home lessons remain the default for most private arrangements in Gurgaon, since the point of privacy is often undermined by a public or shared setting. A tutor at your own table, working through your child's actual notebook, keeps the arrangement contained to your household, which matters more here than in a coaching-centre or online-batch context. Materials, exercise books, past papers, coursework drafts, also stay physically in the home rather than circulating anywhere else.

Online sessions still have their place, particularly for reviewing an Extended Essay draft or Internal Assessment write-up, where screen-sharing a document works as well as sitting side by side, and some families specifically prefer the extra layer of distance an online-only arrangement offers for sensitive subjects.

Hybrid suits families who want the closeness of home classes most weeks but flexibility when travel, exams or a busy fortnight gets in the way. The honest trade-off: home sessions keep everything private and give the clearest read on a student, but ask more of scheduling and space; online is more flexible but slightly less contained, and confidentiality depends more on the tutor's own discipline with digital records.

For families new to private arrangements, home tuition is usually the easiest starting point precisely because it requires the least explanation: the tutor arrives, sees the actual student and the actual materials, and begins. contentBlocks.heading: How Is an Independent Tutor in Gurgaon Verified?

contentBlocks.heading: Should Your Child's Own School Teacher Tutor Them Privately?
contentBlocks.body:
It happens often enough in Gurgaon that it is worth addressing directly: a class teacher offering, or being asked, to tutor a student privately outside school hours. The arrangement can work, but it carries a real conflict of interest that families sometimes do not think through. The same person who marks a student's classwork, sets internal deadlines and influences how the student is perceived by the school is now also being paid privately by that student's family.

This can, in practice, tilt in two directions: a teacher may unconsciously favour a paying private student in how attention or leniency is distributed in class, or a teacher may overcorrect and be unusually hard on that student to avoid any appearance of favouritism. Neither is necessarily deliberate, but both are real risks, and they are exactly why many families deliberately choose an independent tutor with no connection to the school at all.

An independent private tutor solves this by design, but introduces a different job: mapping lessons to the school's own scheme of work without ever having direct access to it. This means asking the family for whatever the school shares, textbooks, syllabus outlines, recent tests, and working from that, rather than guessing at a generic curriculum. What it must never mean is doing the school's own tasks for the student: writing a piece of coursework, completing homework, or producing an Internal Assessment draft the student then submits as their own.

The distinction matters academically and ethically. Guidance, structure, feedback and practice are all legitimate; producing the actual submitted work is not, on IB, IGCSE or any board's own integrity rules. A good private tutor is explicit about this boundary from the first session, not vague about it when a deadline gets close.

contentBlocks.heading: Confidentiality and Honest Limits of a Private Arrangement
contentBlocks.body:
Confidentiality is one of the main reasons families choose private tutoring in the first place, and it deserves to be treated as a real commitment, not a vague assurance. A private tutor should not discuss your child's specific struggles with other families, other students, or anyone at the school, without your explicit agreement. Ask directly, before the first session, how the tutor would respond if the school itself asked about the arrangement.

Even so, a private arrangement has honest limits too. It works best for a specific, nameable gap, a subject, a skill, a piece of coursework, not as a vague catch-all for a student who is struggling broadly across school life. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a private tutor working in isolation, without any visibility into what is happening in class, occasionally misses something a class teacher would catch. This is simply the honest shape of one-to-one, independent home tuition, and a family that understands it going in tends to get more value from the arrangement than one expecting a school's full support structure replicated at home. Treat the tutor as one part of a wider picture, not a complete substitute for everything the school provides.

Watch for concrete signs of progress rather than a general sense of reassurance: specific gaps named early, work returned with real feedback, and a student who can explain, unprompted, a concept the tutor covered weeks earlier. If, after a reasonable stretch, none of this is visible, it is worth reconsidering the arrangement rather than continuing quietly out of habit.

contentBlocks.heading: What to Agree in Writing Before the First Private Lesson
contentBlocks.body:
A private arrangement benefits from a small amount of structure, even an informal written note exchanged over message, covering the basics: the subject and level, the agreed weekly schedule, and what happens if a session needs to be cancelled or rescheduled.

Confidentiality is worth stating explicitly, even briefly: that the tutor will not discuss your child's progress with anyone outside the immediate family without permission, and how records or notes on your child's work will be kept or eventually discarded.

Progress updates are worth agreeing upfront too: how often, in what form, a quick message or a short call, and what they will actually cover. This avoids the common situation where a family assumes updates will happen automatically and a tutor assumes silence means no update is expected.

None of this needs to be formal or intimidating; a short message confirming these points after the trial lesson is usually enough. IB Gram can help set the initial terms of a match, board, subject, schedule and mode, and the rest is a conversation directly between your family and the tutor.

For a family specifically searching for an international school private tutor Gurgaon options with genuine independence, this written note is what turns a good trial lesson into a dependable weekly arrangement, rather than something that quietly fades after a few sessions. Keep it simple, keep it somewhere you can find again, and revisit it if anything about the schedule or expectations changes.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: Which Programme Is Your Child In?
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a parent what programme their child is in and you often get the grade, not the programme name. That gap matters, because a home tutor preparing a Primary Years Programme (PYP) child for confident reading is doing completely different work from one preparing a Diploma Programme (DP) student for a May exam session.

The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years with no external exam to build toward, a home tutor here is building habits: reading stamina, number sense, the ability to explain thinking out loud, since PYP assessment is largely internal and inquiry-led. Skipping ahead a level or drilling exam technique too early usually backfires at this stage.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, and every subject is marked against four criteria, A through D, each scored 0-8. An international syllabus tutor Gurugram families bring in for an MYP student needs to know those criteria cold, not just the topic, because a student can know the content and still lose marks against a criterion they never addressed directly. The Personal Project lands in MYP 5, with a Community Project earlier in MYP 3 or 4 at some schools, and MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, is optional and decided school by school, so a home tutor should ask which route your child's school has chosen rather than assume.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is what most Gurgaon parents mean by the IB: two years, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL) and the rest at Standard Level (SL), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum, with 24 as the minimum for the diploma itself, and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) sits alongside as a non-graded requirement. A home tutor for a DP1 student is laying foundations for two years of work; for a DP2 student six months from May, the job is narrower and more urgent.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE and IB Subjects a Home Tutor Should Know Cold
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor who says I teach IGCSE without naming the board is telling you less than it sounds like. Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different grading. Cambridge grades most of its syllabuses A* to G, though some now run separate 9-1 versions under different syllabus codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. An international curriculum tutor in Gurgaon who has taught one for years can still misjudge the other's mark scheme in the first few sessions.

Tier matters as much as board. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended: Core tops out at a C, Extended reaches A*, and choosing wrong, or a school choosing wrong for a student, caps what's possible before a single lesson happens. A home tutor should ask which tier your child is entered for, not assume Extended because a student is capable.

On the DP side, subject depth means knowing what Higher Level (HL, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours) demands against Standard Level (SL, around 150 hours) in the same subject, HL Maths and SL Maths are not the same course taught faster. A tutor moving a student from SL to HL, or supporting an HL subject the school itself is light on, needs to know exactly where the syllabus diverges.

Command terms run through both boards and decide how much an answer is worth. Describe wants what happened; explain wants why; evaluate and discuss want a judgement weighed against evidence; to what extent wants a stance defended with limits acknowledged. A home tutor who drills content but never trains a student to read the command term is leaving marks on the table in every internal assessment and every exam paper, IB or IGCSE alike, for any of the best international curriculum home tutor in Gurgaon searches turn up.
items: Cambridge IGCSE grades most syllabuses A* to G; some have separate 9-1 versions.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades every subject 9-1, no letter scale.
Core tier tops out at grade C; Extended tier reaches A* on Cambridge syllabuses.
DP Higher Level asks for roughly 240 teaching hours against 150 for Standard Level.
Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, set how much an answer needs.

What matters for a home tutor is the shape of the year, not which of these schools your child attends. Most Gurgaon schools running the Diploma Programme enter students for the May exam session, so DP2 mocks land several months earlier, usually in the preceding winter, and a home tutor working toward that date structures sessions differently in October than in March. A minority of schools use the November session instead, and retake candidates often sit November regardless of when they first attempted a subject.

For IGCSE, the school sets which exam series a student is entered for, Cambridge runs series in February/March, May/June and October/November, with the February/March window offered specifically in India, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in January and May/June. An international curriculum tutor Gurgaon families ask about this should confirm which series and which tier your child is entered for directly with the school, since a mismatch discovered late narrows what preparation can achieve.

Between terms, unit tests, progress reports and parent-teacher meetings create their own smaller pressure points. A home tutor who tracks the actual school calendar, not a generic exam-season assumption, times revision, coursework support and mock preparation against dates that matter to your child specifically, rather than a fixed syllabus.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Works Best in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
For most Gurgaon families, home tuition is the default IB Gram recommends first, because a child usually studies better away from a screen. The tutor sits at your child's actual desk, sees the textbooks and past papers already in use, and can look over hand-written working in real time, something a shared screen struggles to replicate for a subject like Maths or Chemistry where the method matters as much as the answer.

An international curriculum online tutor Gurgaon families turn to is the honest alternative when travel doesn't work: a family in Sector 65 on a Wednesday evening in monsoon traffic, or a tutor whose best subject match happens to live across the city. Screen-sharing handles most subjects reasonably well, and scheduling is easier since neither side is moving. What online loses is the tutor's read of a tired, distracted or overwhelmed student, the small cues that tell an experienced tutor to change the plan for that session, harder to catch through a screen.

Hybrid, home tuition most weeks with an online session in the ones where the calendar or the weather doesn't cooperate, is what many Gurgaon families settle into, especially through the exam term when a missed week matters more than usual. IB Gram sets this up at the start rather than mid-course, so switching a single session doesn't feel like a renegotiation.

None of the three is universally right. A younger PYP or early MYP child usually benefits more from home tuition's steady, in-person structure; a DP2 student deep into past-paper practice can often work just as well online, freeing up the tutor's time for the sessions that matter most, closer to the exam.

contentBlocks.heading: How Is a Home Tutor Verified Before Entering Your Home?
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor is verified before a shortlist is even shared with you, not after you've already agreed to a first visit. IB Gram checks a tutor's identity and academic background, degree, subject specialisation, prior teaching experience with the specific board, before that profile is matched against your query, so verified international curriculum tutors in Gurgaon are the only ones your shortlist draws from. This happens whether the first session is at home, online or hybrid, but it matters more before someone comes into your home specifically.

What IB Gram checks is only half the picture; the other half is what you should check yourself. Ask for the tutor's full name and confirm it matches what IB Gram has shared. Ask which subjects and levels they've actually taught, not just tutored casually. For a home visit, note down the tutor's expected arrival time and have a household member aware of the schedule, particularly for a first session when no routine exists yet. If your society requires visitor registration at the gate, share the tutor's details with security in advance so the first session isn't lost to a ten-minute delay at the gate.

Trust builds over the first few sessions, not the first phone call. Watch whether the tutor arrives prepared with a plan for that specific session, whether they ask about the school's current topic rather than starting from a generic syllabus outline, and whether your child's own account of the session matches what the tutor reports. If something feels off, a tutor who is vague about qualifications, or inconsistent about what was actually covered, say so, and IB Gram will offer a different match rather than asking you to persist with a poor fit.

contentBlocks.heading: What the First Home Session Actually Looks Like
contentBlocks.body:
The first home session is diagnostic, not a lesson delivered at full pace. A tutor arriving for an international curriculum student, IB or IGCSE, usually spends the opening twenty minutes understanding where your child actually is: which topics are solid, which are shaky, and how your child talks about their own work, before opening a single textbook. This matters more here than it would for a national board, because international curricula lean heavily on coursework that counts toward the final grade, criterion-based marking rather than a single right-answer scheme, and command terms that shape how much an answer is worth.

Who should be present varies by age. For a younger PYP or early MYP student, a parent nearby for the first fifteen minutes helps the tutor understand routines and expectations, then can step back. For an older MYP or DP student, most tutors prefer the student alone with them from the start, since a parent's presence can make a teenager guarded about admitting what they don't understand, the opposite of what a diagnostic session needs.

The study space doesn't need to be elaborate: a desk or table with enough room for a laptop and papers side by side, decent lighting, and a household quiet enough for forty minutes without interruption. What matters more is what's already there, the textbook the school actually uses, recent test papers, any feedback from teachers on an Internal Assessment or a Personal Project, because a tutor working from your child's actual materials, rather than a generic worksheet, gets to the real gaps faster.

By the end of a first session, a good tutor should be able to name, specifically, what the next four to six weeks need to cover: a command term your child consistently misreads, a criterion they lose marks against every time, a paper component that needs more practice than the rest. If a tutor can't say anything more specific than we'll build confidence after an hour in your home, that's worth noticing.

Bring the actual school textbook and recent test papers to the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Should Look Like After the First Month?
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks in, you should be able to name something concrete that's changed, not a grade jump, which no tutor can promise, but a specific gap that's closed or narrowing. Maybe your child now shows working on Maths problems instead of jumping to an answer. Maybe an IGCSE English essay finally addresses the command term instead of writing around it. Maybe a DP student's Internal Assessment draft has moved from a vague research question to one that's actually answerable within the word limit. Small and specific beats big and vague.

What a home tutor cannot do is guarantee an outcome. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a 7, an A* or a fixed number of marks, and be wary of any tutor or platform that implies otherwise, international curricula are marked against criteria and mark schemes that no amount of home tuition can shortcut. There is no single best international curriculum home tutor in Gurgaon in the abstract, only the best fit for your child's board, level and school calendar. What a good tutor can do is make the path to a realistic outcome clearer and steadier than it was before sessions started.

Progress is uneven, especially at first. A student might show real improvement in one area of a subject and stay stuck in another for several sessions before it shifts. That's normal, and a tutor who reports uniform improvement every single week is probably not looking closely enough. Ask your tutor what specifically has changed, not just how the sessions went, the answer tells you whether the home tuition is doing its job.

If after a genuine month, four to six sessions, not one or two, nothing concrete has shifted and the tutor can't point to what's being worked on, that's a fair moment to ask for a different match rather than waiting it out through an exam season.
items: Look for a specific, named change, not a general sense of improvement.
No tutor can guarantee a grade, a 7, an A* or a fixed mark improvement.
Progress is often uneven across topics within the same subject.
Ask what specifically changed each session, not just how the session went.
After four to six sessions with no concrete shift, ask for a different tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: Preparing for Your First Home Tutoring Session in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Whatever brought you to search international curriculum home tutor gurgaon this week, getting started from here is simple by design. Send IB Gram a query, or book a free consultation, with your child's board, programme, grade, the subjects you want covered and your Gurgaon sector. Before your first home session, it helps to have three things ready: your child's current textbook and any recent test papers, a note of the next school deadline, a unit test, a mock, an Internal Assessment or Personal Project date, and a quiet desk free for the session's duration.

The first session itself covers three things in order. First, the tutor gets to know your child's current level against the actual syllabus, not a generic assumption about the grade. Second, the tutor identifies two or three priority areas worth the next month's focus, specific enough to name. Third, you and the tutor agree a realistic weekly rhythm for IB IGCSE curriculum help, how many sessions, which evenings work around school and activities, and whether a hybrid week is likely during exam term.

You are not committing to anything at the trial stage. If the pace, subject depth or simply the personal fit isn't right, say so, and IB Gram will offer a different match without asking you to start the search over. Availability is subject to tutor schedules and your sector, so an evening slot popular across Gurgaon, the hour after school pickup, may take a little longer to confirm than an off-peak one.

Once regular home tuition begins, most families settle into a fixed weekly slot within the first two to three sessions, adjusted around school events as the term goes on rather than fixed and forgotten.

Note the next school deadline: test, mock, IA or Personal Project date.
Keep a quiet desk free for the full session length.
Agree a realistic weekly rhythm at the end of the trial, not before.
Ask for a different tutor at any point if the fit isn't right.

faqs.question: What if the home tutor and my child don't get along?
faqs.answer: Say so, and IB Gram will offer a different match without asking you to justify it at length or restart the whole process. Personal fit matters as much as subject expertise for a home tutor, since the relationship runs for months, not one exam season, and a student who is guarded or uncomfortable rarely makes real progress even with a well-qualified tutor. faqs.question: Is online better than a home tutor for the IB DP?
faqs.answer: Not universally, it depends on the subject and the student. A DP2 student deep into past-paper practice for a subject they're already fairly strong in can often work just as well online, and it frees up scheduling on both sides. A DP1 student still building foundational understanding in a demanding HL subject, or one who works better with someone physically alongside them, usually benefits more from home tuition's closer, in-person read of what's actually going wrong. Many DP families settle into a hybrid pattern: home tuition through most of the term, online in the weeks travel or the calendar doesn't cooperate.

faqs.question: How soon can a home tutor start after we send a query?
faqs.answer: Timing depends on tutor availability for your specific board, programme, level and sector, so IB Gram can't promise a fixed number of days. In practice, a free trial class is usually arranged within the first week once your query includes enough detail, board, grade, subjects and location, for a shortlist to be built. Requests close to an exam session or during a period when many families are searching at once can take a little longer to match well, since IB Gram would rather find the right fit than the fastest one. Being specific in your first message speeds this up.

faqs.question: What should I check myself before the first visit, beyond IB Gram's verification?
faqs.answer: Confirm the tutor's full name against what IB Gram sent you, and ask directly which subjects and levels they've actually taught, not just tutored informally. If your society requires visitor registration at the gate, share the tutor's details with security ahead of the scheduled time so the first session isn't lost to a delay at entry. During the session itself, notice whether the tutor arrives with a plan specific to your child's current topic rather than a generic outline, and afterwards, ask your child what was actually covered, their account is often the clearest signal of whether the fit is right.

faqs.question: Do you offer home tutoring for MYP students, or only DP?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring through IB Gram covers the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme, not DP alone. An MYP tutor needs to know the four assessment criteria, A through D, for each subject, and how the Personal Project in MYP 5 or the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 is structured, which is quite different work from DP exam preparation. Tell IB Gram which programme and MYP year, or DP1 versus DP2, when you send a query, since the right tutor for a MYP 2 student is rarely the right one for a DP2 student six months from May.

faqs.question: How many home sessions a week does an international curriculum student typically need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the level and how close the next deadline is, so treat any fixed number as a starting point, not a rule. A DP2 student six to eight weeks from mocks, or an MYP student with a Personal Project deadline approaching, often needs more frequent sessions temporarily than the same student earlier in the year. Many families start with one or two sessions a week per subject and adjust after the first month, based on what the tutor reports about where the gaps actually are. Your tutor should be able to justify the frequency, not just default to a fixed weekly number.

contentBlocks.heading: Setting Up an Independent Private Tutor in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A private arrangement starts with a conversation most families haven't had explicitly before: is this tutor replacing something the school isn't doing well, or supplementing something it's already doing right? An international curriculum private tutor gurgaon families bring in mid-year usually falls into the first camp; one brought in from Grade 9 onward, building toward Grade 10 exams steadily, usually falls into the second. IB Gram asks which, because it changes who gets shortlisted.

One question IB Gram always asks, and most agencies don't: does your child's own class teacher already tutor students privately? If a school's English teacher offers private lessons on the side, and that teacher also teaches your child in class, IB Gram will flag the conflict before matching rather than after. An independent tutor with no classroom relationship to your child removes that problem entirely, and for most families that independence is the whole point of going private.

Once the shortlist is built, IB Gram checks that a tutor can work from your child's actual scheme of work, the sequence of topics the school itself is teaching, rather than a generic syllabus timeline that might be three weeks ahead or behind. A free trial class confirms two things: whether the pace suits your child, and whether the tutor genuinely intends to work from agreed material rather than running their own separate curriculum. After the trial, IB Gram helps you set out the practical terms, schedule, cancellation notice, how progress gets reported, confidentiality, in writing, so nothing is assumed later.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What a Private Tutor Needs to Know
contentBlocks.body:
A private tutor's usefulness depends on knowing which programme, not just which grade, your child is actually in. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) has no formal external exam, so private tuition here is really about supporting habits the school is already building, reading stamina, curiosity, the confidence to explain reasoning aloud, rather than preparing for any single test.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 through MYP 5, across eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria, A through D, scored 0-8 and converted to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. A private tutor working outside the school needs the same criteria the school's own teacher marks against; without them, feedback that sounds encouraging can still miss what the criteria actually reward. The Personal Project sits in MYP 5, with a Community Project earlier in MYP 3 or 4 at some schools, and each carries its own deadline separate from regular subject work, something a private tutor should track alongside subject tuition, not instead of it.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, around 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum, with 24 as the minimum needed for the diploma. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) runs alongside, ungraded but required. A private tutor brought in for a single HL subject in DP2 has a narrower, more urgent brief than one supporting a DP1 student across a full first year.
items: PYP has no formal exam; a private tutor here supports habits, not test technique.
MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0-8.

A Personal Project in MYP 5, or Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, needs its own timeline.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE and IB Subjects: Where Private Coaching Adds the Most
contentBlocks.body:
Private tuition tends to concentrate on one or two subjects rather than a whole timetable, which makes syllabus precision matter even more than it does for a general arrangement. Cambridge IGCSE (Cambridge International Education) and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate qualifications: Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some now offering separate 9-1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. A tutor confident in one can still be shaky on the other's mark scheme in the opening sessions, so ask directly which board they've actually taught, not tutored around.

Tier adds another layer. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, Core capped at a C, Extended reaching A*, and a private tutor working from the wrong assumption about which tier your child sits can waste real time before anyone notices the mismatch.

On the DP side, Higher Level (HL, roughly 240 recommended teaching hours) and Standard Level (SL, around 150 hours) in the same subject are genuinely different courses, not the same content compressed or stretched. A private tutor brought in for HL Chemistry, say, while the class moves through content the school's own teacher is pacing, needs to track that pacing closely rather than working ahead independently.

Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, run through both boards and set how much depth an answer needs regardless of subject. An international curriculum tutor Gurgaon families hire independently should be drilling command-term reading alongside content from the first session, since a technically correct answer that ignores the command term still loses marks.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Fits a Private Arrangement in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A private arrangement in Gurgaon most often means home tuition, the tutor coming to your child's own desk, because a one-to-one relationship built at home tends to hold together better over a full academic year than one conducted purely on screen. The tutor sees the actual books, the actual handwriting, the actual distractions of a real evening, and adjusts accordingly in a way a shared screen makes harder.

Online lessons are the sensible alternative when the independent tutor best suited to your child, by subject depth or by simply having no connection to your child's school, lives across the city rather than nearby. For a private arrangement specifically, online also solves a quieter problem: keeping the tutoring private from household or building staff who might otherwise know every visitor. Some families choose online for exactly that reason, not because home tuition doesn't suit them.

Hybrid, home most weeks with online filled in around a bad-traffic evening or a school event, is common once a private arrangement settles into its second or third month. Because the relationship is usually longer-term than a batch booking, IB Gram sets the hybrid split as part of the initial written agreement, not something renegotiated every time travel becomes inconvenient.

None of the three suits every private arrangement equally. A younger student usually needs the steadier structure of home tuition; an older DP2 student, already independent in how they study, can often manage a private arrangement fully online without losing much, freeing the corridor question entirely.

contentBlocks.heading: Your Child's Own Teacher as a Private Tutor: Should You Say Yes?
contentBlocks.body:
It happens more often in Gurgaon than families expect: a school teacher, sometimes your child's own class teacher, offers private lessons on the side, and it can feel like the obvious, low-friction choice. They already know the syllabus, the school's pace, even your child's handwriting. But the arrangement carries a conflict most families don't examine closely enough before agreeing.

A teacher who both grades your child in class and tutors them privately has an interest in how that dual relationship is perceived, by the school, by other parents, by your child. Grading choices, however fair in practice, become harder to trust as purely academic once money and a private relationship enter the picture, and your child may feel pressure, spoken or not, to keep attending the private lessons regardless of fit, simply because the same person marks their coursework or Internal Assessment at school. This isn't an accusation against any individual teacher; it's a structural problem that exists whether or not the teacher acts on it.

An independent tutor, with no classroom relationship to your child and no grading authority over them, removes that structural problem entirely. Feedback is feedback, not a factor in how school marks land. Your child can be honestly confused, or honestly behind, without it affecting anything at school, and a tutor who isn't also a school employee has no institutional interest to protect if things genuinely aren't working.

None of this means every teacher offering private lessons is acting improperly; many are simply trying to help a struggling student outside class hours with good intentions. But if you're weighing the choice, ask yourself whether you'd be comfortable raising a concern about the tutoring directly with that same person in their role as your child's teacher. If the honest answer is no, that discomfort is telling you something worth listening to before you commit an entire term to the arrangement.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should a Private Arrangement Deliver After a Month?
contentBlocks.body:
A month into an international curriculum private tutor gurgaon arrangement, look for something specific your child can point to, not a general sense that things feel better. Perhaps a Grade 10 IGCSE student now structures an English essay around the command term instead of writing everything they know about the topic. Perhaps a DP1 student's lab reports finally follow the criteria the school's own teacher uses, not a private tutor's separate version of good practice. Specific and small beats vague and large.

No private tutor, however good, can guarantee a grade, a 7, a 9, an A* or any fixed improvement, and an arrangement that promises one should be questioned rather than trusted on faith. What a private tutor can reasonably deliver is a clearer sense of exactly where your child's understanding breaks down, and a plan addressing that gap specifically, mapped to the school's own scheme of work rather than run alongside it.

Progress within a private arrangement is rarely even across every subject or topic at once. A student might sharpen quickly in essay structure while a separate weakness, in exam timing, say, takes longer to shift. That unevenness is ordinary, not a sign the arrangement isn't working, and a tutor who claims uniform weekly improvement across everything is probably summarising rather than actually assessing.

If, after four to six genuine sessions, your child still can't describe what the private tutor is working on with them, and the tutor can't either, that's a fair point to revisit the arrangement rather than continuing on trust alone.

faqs.question: Should I hire my child's own school teacher as a private tutor?
faqs.answer: No single answer fits every family, but think carefully before saying yes. A teacher who tutors your child privately while also grading them in class carries a structural conflict of interest, whatever their intentions: grading choices become harder to trust as purely academic once a paid, private relationship is layered on top, and your child may feel pressure to keep attending regardless of fit. An independent tutor with no classroom relationship to your child removes that problem entirely. If you're still considering the school teacher option, ask yourself honestly whether you'd raise a concern about the tutoring directly with that same person in their role as your child's teacher.

faqs.question: What should we put in writing before starting a private arrangement?
faqs.answer: Four things: the weekly schedule and what counts as adequate cancellation notice, how and how often the tutor reports progress to you, confidentiality, specifically that your child's difficulties stay between you, the tutor and IB Gram, and what the tutor will not do around school tasks, working from the scheme of work rather than completing coursework or an Internal Assessment. Putting these in writing before the first regular lesson avoids the awkward conversations that come from assuming everyone agreed on something nobody actually said aloud. IB Gram helps set these terms out once the trial class confirms the tutor is a good fit.

faqs.question: How does a private tutor avoid duplicating what the school teaches?
faqs.answer: By working from your child's actual scheme of work, the exact sequence of topics the school is teaching that term, rather than a separate syllabus timeline that might run weeks ahead or behind. A private tutor who teaches content the class hasn't reached yet often confuses more than it helps, and one working from a different sequence entirely duplicates effort your child doesn't have time for. Ask your tutor to request the scheme of work, or share it with them yourself, at the very start of the arrangement, and check in every few weeks that they are still pacing against it rather than their own separate plan.

faqs.question: Will the private tutor keep my child's difficulties confidential from the school?
faqs.answer: Yes, that is part of what IB Gram agrees in writing before regular lessons start: your child's difficulties stay between you, the tutor and IB Gram unless you choose to involve the school yourself. This matters more in a private arrangement than in a batch, since the whole point of going private is often precisely to keep struggles from becoming visible within the school community. Ask the tutor directly how they handle this, particularly if they have any other connection to your child's school, and if IB Gram has screened out any tutor with a conflict, confidentiality is one less thing to negotiate from scratch.

faqs.answer: Yes, Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area sit centrally enough that home tuition can usually hold a consistent weekday evening slot without a long commute either way for the tutor. Because a private arrangement tends to run for a full term or longer, tutors matched to this corridor generally prioritise families who can offer a fixed weekly time over a family wanting an occasional or irregular session. faqs.question: What if my child needs a tutor near DLF Phase 3 specifically?

faqs.question: Can a private tutor complete coursework or an Internal Assessment for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and be cautious of any tutor who offers to. A private tutor can guide your child through structuring an Internal Assessment, explain how the criteria work, and review drafts for clarity, but writing the work itself breaches the academic integrity rules both IB and IGCSE boards enforce, and it can put your child's actual grade at risk if discovered. The honest, useful role for a private tutor is process guidance: helping your child develop their own answerable research question, structure their own argument, and understand their own mistakes, not producing the work in their place.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to cancel a session at short notice?
faqs.answer: Tell your tutor as early as possible, and this is exactly why cancellation notice belongs in the written agreement from the start rather than being negotiated in the moment. Most private arrangements work well with a simple rule, a set number of hours' notice for a routine change, with genuine emergencies handled case by case. A tutor who repeatedly cancels at short notice without good reason is a fair reason to reconsider the match; a family who does the same is generally still owed the courtesy of an honest conversation rather than a quiet drop-off.

faqs.question: How is an independent private tutor different from a coaching centre tutor?
faqs.answer: An independent private tutor gives your child undivided attention and no institutional connection to worry about, while a coaching centre batch typically splits attention across fifteen to thirty students working through content built for a mixed cohort rather than your child's specific school and syllabus. A private tutor costs more per hour precisely because the attention is not shared, and the arrangement can be mapped precisely to your child's own scheme of work in a way a fixed batch curriculum usually cannot be. A coaching batch can still suit a student who studies well in a group and wants a lower cost per hour.

In practice, once your query includes enough detail for a proper shortlist, board, grade, subject and whether the tutor should have any connection to your child's school, a free trial class is usually arranged within the first week. Requests during a period when many families are searching at once, close to mocks or the exam session, can take a little longer to match well.

faqs.question: What if the private tutor and my child aren't a good match?
faqs.answer: Say so, and IB Gram will offer a different match without asking you to justify it at length. Fit matters as much as subject expertise in a private arrangement meant to run for a full term or longer, and a student who is uncomfortable rarely makes real progress even with a well-qualified tutor. It's easier to raise this after the trial class or the first two or three regular sessions than to wait it out hoping it resolves on its own. Because IB Gram already has your board, programme, school calendar and any confidentiality terms on file, a new match doesn't mean starting the whole arrangement over.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be present during home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: It depends on your child's age and what you both agree with the tutor. For a younger student, a parent nearby for the opening sessions of home tuition can help establish routine before stepping back. For an older MYP or DP student, most private arrangements work better with the student and tutor alone at home, since a teenager is often more honest about what they don't understand without a parent in the room, which is exactly what a private tutor needs to know in order to help. Agree this upfront as part of the written terms, rather than deciding session by session.

mainEntity.name: Should I hire my child's own school teacher as a private tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: No single answer fits every family, but think carefully before saying yes. A teacher who tutors your child privately while also grading them in class carries a structural conflict of interest, whatever their intentions: grading choices become harder to trust as purely academic once a paid, private relationship is layered on top, and your child may feel pressure to keep attending regardless of fit. An independent tutor with no classroom relationship to your child removes that problem entirely. If you're still considering the school teacher option, ask yourself honestly whether you'd raise a concern about the tutoring directly with that same person in their role as your child's teacher.

mainEntity.name: What should we put in writing before starting a private arrangement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four things: the weekly schedule and what counts as adequate cancellation notice, how and how often the tutor reports progress to you, confidentiality, specifically that your child's difficulties stay between you, the tutor and IB Gram, and what the tutor will not do around school tasks, working from the scheme of work rather than completing coursework or an Internal Assessment. Putting these in writing before the first regular lesson avoids the awkward conversations that come from assuming everyone agreed on something nobody actually said aloud. IB Gram helps set these terms out once the trial class confirms the tutor is a good fit.

mainEntity.name: How does a private tutor avoid duplicating what the school teaches?

acceptedAnswer.text: By working from your child's actual scheme of work, the exact sequence of topics the school is teaching that term, rather than a separate syllabus timeline that might run weeks ahead or behind. A private tutor who teaches content the class hasn't reached yet often confuses more than it helps, and one working from a different sequence entirely duplicates effort your child doesn't have time for. Ask your tutor to request the scheme of work, or share it with them yourself, at the very start of the arrangement, and check in every few weeks that they are still pacing against it rather than their own separate plan.

mainEntity.name: Will the private tutor keep my child's difficulties confidential from the school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, that is part of what IB Gram agrees in writing before regular lessons start: your child's difficulties stay between you, the tutor and IB Gram unless you choose to involve the school yourself. This matters more in a private arrangement than in a batch, since the whole point of going private is often precisely to keep struggles from becoming visible within the school community. Ask the tutor directly how they handle this, particularly if they have any other connection to your child's school, and if IB Gram has screened out any tutor with a conflict, confidentiality is one less thing to negotiate from scratch.

mainEntity.name: Is home tuition in Sushant Lok easy to arrange on weekday evenings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Sushant Lok 1 and 2, South City 1 and the Millennium City Centre area sit centrally enough that home tuition can usually hold a consistent weekday evening slot without a long commute either way for the tutor. Because a private arrangement tends to run for a full term or longer, tutors matched to this corridor generally prioritise families who can offer a fixed weekly time over a family wanting an occasional or irregular session. Tell IB Gram your exact sector when you send a query so the shortlist reflects realistic travel for a regular weekly visit, not just a one-off trial.

mainEntity.name: What if my child needs a tutor near DLF Phase 3 specifically?

acceptedAnswer.text: DLF Phase 3, along with the rest of DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City, is one of the more straightforward areas for a private tutor to reach, dense and well-connected enough that an evening slot straight after school pickup usually holds reliably. Societies in this corridor, DLF Beverly Park and Heritage City among them, typically have established visitor registration processes, so sharing the tutor's details with security once at the start of the arrangement is usually enough for the rest of the term, rather than re-registering every week.

mainEntity.name: Can a private tutor complete coursework or an Internal Assessment for my child?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and be cautious of any tutor who offers to. A private tutor can guide your child through structuring an Internal Assessment, explain how the criteria work, and review drafts for clarity, but writing the work itself breaches the academic integrity rules both IB and IGCSE boards enforce, and it can put your child's actual grade at risk if discovered. The honest, useful role for a private tutor is process guidance: helping your child develop their own answerable research question, structure their own argument, and understand their own mistakes, not producing the work in their place.

mainEntity.name: What happens if we need to cancel a session at short notice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell your tutor as early as possible, and this is exactly why cancellation notice belongs in the written agreement from the start rather than being negotiated in the moment. Most private arrangements work well with a simple rule, a set number of hours' notice for a routine change, with genuine emergencies handled case by case. A tutor who repeatedly cancels at short notice without good reason is a fair reason to reconsider the match; a family who does the same is generally still owed the courtesy of an honest conversation rather than a quiet drop-off.

mainEntity.name: How is an independent private tutor different from a coaching centre tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: An independent private tutor gives your child undivided attention and no institutional connection to worry about, while a coaching centre batch typically splits attention across fifteen to thirty students working through content built for a mixed cohort rather than your child's specific school and syllabus. A private tutor costs more per hour precisely because the attention is not shared, and the arrangement can be mapped precisely to your child's own scheme of work in a way a fixed batch curriculum usually cannot be. A coaching batch can still suit a student who studies well in a group and wants a lower cost per hour.

mainEntity.name: How soon can a private tutor start after we send a query?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timing depends on tutor availability for your specific board, programme, level, subject and sector, so there's no fixed number of days IB Gram can promise. In practice, once your query includes enough detail for a proper shortlist, board, grade, subject and whether the tutor should have any connection to your child's school, a free trial class is usually arranged within the first week. Requests during a period when many families are searching at once, close to mocks or the exam session, can take a little longer to match well.

mainEntity.name: What if the private tutor and my child aren't a good match?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so, and IB Gram will offer a different match without asking you to justify it at length. Fit matters as much as subject expertise in a private arrangement meant to run for a full term or longer, and a student who is uncomfortable rarely makes real progress even with a well-qualified tutor. It's easier to raise this after the trial class or the first two or three regular sessions than to wait it out hoping it resolves on its own. Because IB Gram already has your board, programme, school calendar and any confidentiality terms on file, a new match doesn't mean starting the whole arrangement over.

mainEntity.name: Does a parent need to be present during home tuition sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your child's age and what you both agree with the tutor. For a younger student, a parent nearby for the opening sessions of home tuition can help establish routine before stepping back. For an older MYP or DP student, most private arrangements work better with the student and tutor alone at home, since a teenager is often more honest about what they don't understand without a parent in the room, which is exactly what a private tutor needs to know in order to help. Agree this upfront as part of the written terms, rather than deciding session by session.

You'll be asked whether the tutor should have any connection to your child's school. contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Programme Stage Needs One-on-One Attention?
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme runs from age three to twelve, organised around six transdisciplinary themes: who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet, with no external examinations until the PYP exhibition in the final year. One-on-one support rarely makes sense at this stage beyond the odd confidence-building session; the format matters more as assessment becomes more formal.

The Middle Years Programme, MYP 1 through MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, marks every subject against four criteria, A through D, each scored out of eight, converting through IB grade boundaries to a final grade of one to seven. In a classroom of twenty, a teacher marking a stack of work against these criteria has limited time to explain exactly why one student's answer sits low in Criterion B while another's sits high; one-on-one, that explanation happens in the same sitting the work is done, which is precisely where a lot of MYP progress actually lives. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project (the Community Project sits in MYP 3 or 4), both of which benefit from an adult who can ask pointed questions without a room full of classmates listening in.

The Diploma Programme, two years across DP1 and DP2, six subjects from six groups with three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), graded one to seven with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to three more points toward a forty-five maximum, is where one-on-one attention often earns back the most time. A DP2 student six weeks from the May session, working through a past paper alone with a tutor, gets immediate correction on exactly where an answer lost marks, rather than a general class debrief days later.
items: PYP: little formal need for one-on-one beyond occasional confidence work.
MYP: criterion-level feedback (A-D, each out of 8) happens in real time, one-on-one.
DP: HL subjects (240 hours) and SL subjects (150 hours) both benefit from immediate correction.
MYP 5's Personal Project and the Community Project (MYP 3/4) suit focused, one-on-one questioning.
DP scoring: 1-7 per subject, up to 3 extra from TOK and the EE, maximum 45.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Does One-on-One Attention Matter Most in IB Subjects?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Mathematics, split into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) at both Higher and Standard Level, rewards one-on-one work more than almost any other subject, because a wrong method on a calculus proof or a modelling question is invisible until someone watches the actual working line by line. A tutor sitting beside one student catches the exact step where a sign error or a misapplied command term, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, changes the mark, something a marked set of twenty scripts handed back a week later cannot do.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology carry internal assessment components that depend on a student's own investigation and write-up; one-on-one time is well spent on the specific weaknesses in that individual piece of work rather than generic lab technique. English A and English B sit at different ends of the subject group, literature and language analysis against language acquisition, and one-on-one time in both is most useful for the thing a group setting makes awkward: reading a student's own weaker paragraph aloud together and rebuilding it line by line, which most students will not volunteer to do in front of classmates.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, sitting outside any single subject group, are naturally one-on-one work already, since both ask a student to develop an individual line of argument; a tutor here is closer to a thinking partner than an instructor, asking the next question rather than supplying the next fact, which only works when there is one student in the room to ask it of.

Command terms (define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent) are easiest to correct in real time.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Small Group: What Suits One-on-One IB Tutoring in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A one-on-one IB tutor in Gurgaon most often starts with home tutoring, and it is where the attention shows up most clearly. A tutor at the dining table sees a student's actual working line by line, notices a hesitation before a wrong answer rather than just the wrong answer itself, and can slow down or speed up within the same sentence based on what the student's face is doing. It also removes an evening commute for a student who has already had a full school day, which matters more the later the slot runs.

Online one-on-one keeps the same individual attention while trading the physical room for reach. A family in New Gurgaon or along the Dwarka Expressway who wants a specific HL specialist not based nearby gets a shared whiteboard and an annotated past paper instead of a long weekday drive; it works well for talking through a method or marking a paper, less well for the kind of quiet observation a tutor makes just from watching how a student holds a pen through a tricky question.

A small group of two or three, where it exists at all in this context, is a different thing entirely from one-on-one, and the honest comparison sits later on this page: attention drops noticeably the moment a second student is added, even a very well-behaved one, because a tutor's questions now have to be shared rather than aimed.

For most families the answer is not fixed for the whole year. A DP2 student close to the May session usually benefits from home sessions where a tutor can sit through a full past paper beside them; the same student revising vocabulary or short-answer definitions a few days later might do just as well online.

One-on-one teaching is its own skill, distinct from managing a room of twenty, and a tutor's profile should reflect that distinction, not just general subject competence.

A parent proposed a tutor is entitled to ask directly how they handle a student who goes quiet under pressure, since that is exactly the situation one-on-one attention is meant to help with, and how they would adjust pace for a student who needs more thinking time than a group setting ever allowed them. contentBlocks.heading: What Does a Tutor Notice in One-on-One That a Group Misses?
contentBlocks.body:
In a class or a batch, a tutor's attention is a shared resource, and a student who answers confidently, even wrongly, tends to get called on again while a quieter student who is actually closer to the right idea goes unheard. One-on-one removes that competition entirely. A tutor working with a single student notices the half-second pause before an answer that signals a genuine guess rather than real understanding, the specific point in a multi-step Maths problem where confidence drops, and the difference between a student who did not know an answer and one who knew it but doubted themselves out of saying it.

This shows up most clearly with quieter students. This is one of the clearest arguments for home tutoring over a batch. A student who never raises a hand in a class of twenty, not because they lack the answer but because they are weighing whether it is worth the risk, gets asked directly and answers because there is no one else to defer to. Over several sessions, that shift, from waiting to be asked to volunteering an answer unprompted, is one of the more reliable signs that one-on-one attention is doing more than covering content; it is changing how confidently a student engages with the subject at all.

Pace is the other thing that changes completely. A group moves at a speed set by its average, which means a stronger student is sometimes bored and a struggling one is sometimes lost, both at once, in the same lesson. One-on-one, pace is set entirely by the one learner in the room: a tutor can spend fifteen minutes on a single tricky step if that is what the student genuinely needs, or move on in two minutes if the student clearly already has it, without checking that decision against anyone else's needs.

Quieter students who defer in a group often answer directly one-on-one.

contentBlocks.heading: What Are the Honest Downsides of One-on-One IB Tutoring?
contentBlocks.body:
A one-on-one IB tutor in Gurgaon is not automatically the right answer for every student, and the attention is not free of drawbacks either, so pretending otherwise does families no favours. The most obvious one is that there is nowhere to hide: a student used to coasting through a group lesson by nodding along cannot do that with one tutor asking direct questions, and for some students the first few sessions feel more exposing than helpful before they settle into it. A tutor who understands this eases a student in rather than treating the intensity as a feature from session one.

There is also no peer discussion. A genuine benefit of a well-run small group, hearing another student's wrong answer and working out why it is wrong, or hearing a different way of explaining the same idea, simply does not exist one-on-one; a tutor can simulate some of that by playing devil's advocate, but it is not the same as watching a peer struggle with the identical problem. Some students, particularly ones who learn well by comparing their thinking to others, may progress faster in a small, well-matched group than alone with a tutor.

Cost per hour of individual attention is also structurally higher than a shared format, since the tutor's time is not divided among several students, and a family should weigh that against the actual gap being addressed rather than defaulting to one-on-one as automatically superior. For a small, specific gap close to an exam, one-on-one is usually worth it; for broad, general revision months out, a well-run small group can do nearly as much for less exposure and less pressure on the student.

None of this changes the honest bottom line: for a student who needs to be seen, corrected and paced individually, one-on-one remains the format that does that most directly. It simply is not automatically right for every student or every stretch of the year.
