contentBlocks.heading: How Weekly 1:1 Hours Should Change Before and After a Mock or the May Session
contentBlocks.body:
Planning 1:1 hours well means treating the weekly number as something that moves, not a figure fixed once and left alone for a whole school year. A sensible starting point for most DP1 students is one to two hours a week per HL or SL subject needing support, enough to build habits and catch gaps early without crowding out independent study or CAS. As a DP2 mock approaches, usually a step up to two hours a week per subject is reasonable, shifting the session content toward timed past papers under exam conditions rather than untimed practice.

The real inflection point comes after the mock result, once specific weak areas are visible in a way September planning could not have predicted. A student who mocked well in content but lost marks on timing needs a different eight-week plan from one who mocked weakly on a specific topic; this is exactly why a flat weekly-hours number chosen in September and never revisited wastes the most useful data point the whole year produces. Between the mock and the May session, two to three hours a week concentrated almost entirely on past papers and mark-scheme review is typical for a subject the student is relying on for a strong grade.

A review every four to six weeks, not just at report card time, is where this actually gets decided: what changed, what is still weak, and whether the weekly hours should move up, down or stay the same. Blending 1:1 hours with independent study matters just as much as the number itself; a student who only ever works on IB content during a paid session, and never revises independently between them, tends to plateau regardless of how many hours are booked, since 1:1 time works best as guided direction for independent effort, not a replacement for it.
items: 1. Start most DP1 subjects at one to two hours a week to build habits early.
2. Step up to roughly two hours a week per subject in the mock run-up, timed papers.
3. After the mock result, target the specific weak areas it revealed, not a generic plan.
4. Between mock and May, two to three hours a week on past papers is typical.
5. Review every four to six weeks; do not wait for report cards to adjust hours.
6. Independent study between sessions is what turns 1:1 direction into real progress.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress From 1:1 IB Tutoring Should Look Like
contentBlocks.body:
In the first few weeks of 1:1 tutoring, progress rarely looks dramatic, and treating a lack of an immediate mock-score jump as a sign of a bad match is one of the more common ways families misjudge otherwise good tutoring too early. The early signal worth watching for is a student who starts explaining, unprompted, why a piece of work lost marks against a specific criterion or mark scheme point, a sign that the weekly hours are actually landing rather than just being spent.

By around two months in, ask for something more specific than a general 'doing well': which command term, criterion or paper type the student has genuinely improved on, and which is still weak. A tutor who can answer that precisely is demonstrating that the session-by-session plan is actually being tracked, not just filled. If the answer stays vague after two months despite the hours being kept, that is worth raising directly with the tutor rather than assuming more hours alone will fix it.

No tutor, however well matched or however many weekly hours are booked, can guarantee a particular grade or IB score, and any claim to the contrary should be read as a warning sign rather than reassurance. What a well-planned 1:1 arrangement can honestly deliver is a tutor who adjusts the weekly-hours split as the student's actual gaps change, honest term-by-term feedback, and a plan that steps up and down with exam proximity rather than staying fixed, subject to tutor availability throughout the year.

A free trial session is then arranged, at home, online or hybrid depending on what suits the family and the corridor, subject to tutor availability, with nothing committed to beyond that single session.

The first real session usually opens with a short diagnostic conversation about what the student finds hardest, giving the tutor something concrete to build the first few weeks' plan around. From there, using the trial and the family's own read of the fit, weekly hours and format get agreed, understanding that this starting number is expected to move, up before a mock, down after one that went well, as the four-to-six-week reviews accumulate through the year. faqs.question: How many 1:1 hours a week does an IB student actually need?
faqs.answer: There is no single number for a 1:1 IB tutor in Gurgaon; it depends on programme stage and how close the next assessment is. An MYP student with steady coursework often needs just one to two hours a week per subject, while a DP2 student eight weeks from the May session may need two to three hours a week concentrated on past papers. PYP students rarely need a standing weekly hour at all. IB Gram proposes a starting number based on the programme, grade and assessment proximity, then reviews it every four to six weeks rather than leaving it fixed for the year.

faqs.question: How does a 1:1 session split between content, practice and papers?
faqs.answer: Early in a course, a session usually runs close to half new content, a third guided practice and the rest error review from the previous week. As a mock or the May session approaches, that balance shifts toward mostly past papers and mark-scheme review, with new content largely finished. IA and Extended Essay work is best scheduled as separate sessions rather than folded into a regular content hour, since it needs a different kind of attention, structuring an argument rather than covering a syllabus point.

faqs.question: What happens at the four-to-six-week review?
faqs.answer: The review is where the weekly-hours plan actually gets adjusted, not just discussed. IB Gram or the tutor checks what has changed since the last review, which command terms or criteria the student has genuinely improved on, and which are still weak, then the weekly hours move up, down or stay the same based on that, not on a fixed calendar assumption made back in September. Families who skip this step tend to keep paying for the same plan long after the student's actual needs have shifted.

faqs.question: Won't too many paid hours make my child dependent on the tutor?
faqs.answer: It can, if the hours are not deliberately blended with independent study between sessions. A well-planned 1:1 arrangement uses paid time to give direction, what to practise, which mistakes to fix, and expects the student to do that practice independently before the next session, rather than only ever working on IB content when the tutor is present. If a student plateaus despite steady hours, reducing paid time while increasing structured independent practice is sometimes the right adjustment, not adding more hours.

faqs.question: Does the tutor travel to our home in Golf Course Road or Manesar on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tutoring across Golf Course Road, Manesar, Golf Course Extension Road and the wider Gurgaon corridors is the format most families start with, subject to tutor availability and a realistic evening slot. Manesar sits further out along NH-48, so IB Gram tries to match a tutor already based near that corridor where possible, or suggests a hybrid week if travel time would otherwise eat into the session. If a specific evening consistently runs into traffic, switching that week to online while keeping the same tutor is usually the simplest fix.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in during the 1:1 session?
faqs.answer: Most families are not in the room for the whole hour, though introducing the tutor and checking in briefly at the start and end works well, especially in the first few weeks. A parent present throughout can make a student more self-conscious about visibly getting something wrong in front of the tutor, which works against what focused 1:1 time is meant to achieve. What matters more than presence is a quiet table with room to spread out past papers, notebooks and working.

faqs.question: Is online 1:1 tutoring as effective as home tutoring for IB?
faqs.answer: For most content and practice work, yes, a shared digital whiteboard and annotated past papers cover much of what a home session does. The honest limit is that a tutor cannot point directly at one line of working the way they can in person, and some tasks, a lab diagram or a DP Art portfolio review, benefit from being in the same room. Many Gurgaon families run a hybrid week, home as the default with online as a fallback around travel or a late CAS evening.

faqs.question: What if a 1:1 tutor is not working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: The family can ask IB Gram for a different match at any point, and the process restarts from the shortlist rather than from scratch, since the programme, grade and subject details are already on file. Being specific about what was not working, pace, personality, or depth at the wrong level, HL versus SL for instance, helps IB Gram shortlist a genuinely better fit rather than simply another name. A trial session with the new tutor happens before anything further is committed to.

faqs.question: Can a 1:1 tutor help with switching from CBSE or ICSE mid-course into IB?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the weekly-hours plan usually needs to be higher at the start than for a student who has always followed IB, since the switch often means adjusting to criterion-based MYP marking or a DP subject's own command terms for the first time. IB Gram asks about the previous board and where the gaps are likely to be, then proposes a starting plan that typically steps down in hours once the student is comfortable with how IB itself assesses work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram cover Golf Course Extension Road for 1:1 home sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Golf Course Extension Road corridor, including Sector 56 through Sector 65, Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, is covered for 1:1 home sessions, subject to tutor availability for the specific evening. Parts of this corridor sit further from the main road network, so evening traffic can stretch a short trip more than it would closer to central Gurgaon, and IB Gram tries to account for that when matching a tutor's own base to the family's society.

faqs.question: How soon can a 1:1 IB tutor start in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Starting a 1:1 IB tutor in Gurgaon depends on subject, level and tutor availability, which is why IB Gram asks for the programme, grade and subject upfront rather than promising a fixed timeline. A free trial session is generally the fastest way to find out, since it surfaces whether a suitable tutor is available for the family's evenings within days rather than weeks. Specialist HL subjects or a narrow evening window, particularly in corridors like Manesar, can take a little longer to match well.

heroTitle: Planning 1:1 IGCSE Tutoring Hours in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: This page is for a parent deciding how many hours a week a 1:1 IGCSE tutor should sit with their Class 9 or Class 10 child in Gurgaon, how a single session should be spent, and when that plan needs to change before Cambridge or Edexcel exams.
introSummary: A 1:1 IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon should be booked in blocks of hours that change with the stage of the two-year course, not a flat number that stays the same from Class 9 to the week before finals. Home tutoring is the format most families here choose, because a private tutor at the kitchen table can adjust pace and hours as the exam date gets closer, something a fixed timetable class cannot do as easily. Most students on Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE start Class 9 with two structured sessions a week, review that plan every four to six weeks against test results, and step up once past papers begin. The right number depends on the subject, the tier and how well the student manages independent revision, not on one rule that fits every household.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds a 1:1 IGCSE Hours Plan for Gurgaon Families
contentBlocks.body:
A family looking for a 1:1 IGCSE tutor Gurugram households can commit to for a full term does not start with a name or a photograph. It starts with a short conversation: which board, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, which grade, Class 9 or Class 10, which subjects need one-to-one time, and roughly how many hours a week the family has in mind. A search for a 1:1 IGCSE tutor near me on a listings site usually returns a phone number with no way to check the teaching history behind it, and that is the gap IB Gram's intake exists to close.

IB Gram then asks about the school's pacing: whether unit tests are coming up, how a recent internal exam went, and what the school's scheme of work covers next. This is matched against verified tutor profiles for the exact board and tier, Core or Extended for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor Gurgaon families are considering, Foundation or Higher for an Edexcel IGCSE tutor Gurugram households might prefer, rather than a loose subject match. A tutor who has taught Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended for three years is not automatically right for a Core candidate who needs slower pacing and more worked examples.

A free trial session follows before anything is committed to. The tutor works through a short diagnostic exercise, the family watches how a wrong answer gets corrected, and the weekly hours are agreed based on what that session actually shows rather than what the family guessed at the start. Sessions can then run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability, and this four-step approach is why a 1:1 IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon found through IB Gram comes with a verified board and tier match, not just a subject label.

If the fit is wrong, the family can ask for a different match without restarting the whole conversation, and the hours plan itself is revisited on a fixed schedule rather than left to drift for months.

2. IB Gram asks about school pacing, recent test results and your target weekly hours.
3. Verified tutor profiles are shortlisted for the exact board and tier, not just the subject.
4. A free trial session shows how the tutor teaches before you commit to anything.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE Structure Sets the Tutoring Plan?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon means one of two boards, and the tutoring plan should say which one before it says how many hours. Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, is the board more commonly seen among Gurgaon's international schools, usually taught across Grades 9 and 10 as a two-year course. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE follows the same two-year shape but grades every syllabus 9-1, while Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G, with a smaller number of syllabuses now offered as 9-1 under separate codes. An IGCSE Grade 9 and 10 tutor plan built for one board does not automatically transfer to the other, because the paper structure, the command terms and the grading scale differ.

Inside Cambridge IGCSE, many subjects split into Core and Extended tiers. Core tops out at grade C and suits a student who needs a secure foundation without the hardest content; Extended reaches A* but demands more from every session. Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics is tiered as Foundation or Higher instead, a similar idea under a different name. Getting the tier decision right, usually made by the school in consultation with parents, changes what the tutor should be practising in every single session, not just the difficulty of the homework.

Exam series matter for the hours plan too. Cambridge exam series run in February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. Most Gurgaon schools enter students for the May/June session, so a Class 10 hours plan usually steps up sharply from February onward. After Grade 10, students typically move into the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or back into CBSE or the Indian School Certificate (ISC) for Class 11, and the last few months of Class 10 tutoring often start laying groundwork for whichever of those comes next.
items: IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon families should confirm board first: Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Papers That Decide How Many Hours a Session Needs
contentBlocks.body:
Weekly hours are not just a stage decision, they are a subject decision, because different IGCSE syllabuses put weight in different places. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, splits Core candidates into Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator); a non-calculator paper usually needs a different kind of practice hour, heavy on mental method and layout, compared with a calculator paper's focus on efficient use of the tool. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier, so a Higher tier student's tutoring hours often go toward harder algebra and problem-solving rather than calculator technique itself.

Sciences add a third strand. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, for syllabuses examined from 2023, split into a multiple choice paper (Paper 1 for Core, Paper 2 for Extended), a theory paper (Paper 3 or Paper 4), and a practical component through Paper 5 or Paper 6, whichever the school selects, weighted 30% multiple choice, 50% theory and 20% practical. A tutoring hour aimed at the practical paper looks nothing like one aimed at theory recall, and a plan that ignores this split wastes hours on the wrong skill. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 carrying the separate science content and practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than as a standalone component.

English is its own decision entirely. Cambridge offers First Language English 0500 (reading, then directed writing and composition or a coursework portfolio), English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511 (0511 counts speaking into the grade, 0510 reports it separately), and Literature in English 0475, while Pearson Edexcel offers English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). A student on a coursework-portfolio route needs fewer sit-down exam-practice hours and more structured drafting and feedback time, which changes the weekly plan again.

Edexcel 4MA1: Foundation or Higher tier, two calculator papers, heavier weight on problem-solving at Higher.
Cambridge sciences: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20% through Paper 5 or Paper 6.
Edexcel sciences: untiered, Paper 1 and Paper 2, practical skills assessed inside written papers.
English syllabus choice, coursework portfolio or exam route, changes how tutoring hours are spent.

Most schools here run unit tests through the first term, a set of internal or half-yearly assessments before the winter break, and pre-board or mock exams in the months leading into the Cambridge or Edexcel exam series. Each of these creates a natural pressure point for a home tutoring plan: hours often rise in the two to three weeks before a school test, then settle back once the test is behind the student, rather than sitting at one constant level all year.

School buses, after-school activities and weekend commitments also fix which evening slots are realistically available, and this varies by grade as much as by school; a Class 9 student with sport practice twice a week has fewer open evenings than a Class 10 student who has scaled back activities to focus on the exam year. An hours plan that ignores the school's own test calendar tends to either overload a student in a light week or leave a heavy week under-supported, and reviewing the plan every four to six weeks is largely about catching that mismatch before it compounds.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: What Actually Changes the Weekly Hours?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is where most Gurgaon families searching for a 1:1 IGCSE tutor start, and for good reason: a tutor at the kitchen table can watch handwriting under exam conditions, catch a habit of skipping working on a maths paper, and use the family's own printed past papers without anything getting lost over a video call. For sciences with a practical component, a home session also makes it easier to talk through diagram work and lab-report structure with pen and paper side by side, which is harder to do cleanly on screen.

An IGCSE online tutor Gurgaon families sometimes prefer suits a different situation: a subject where the right specialist does not live nearby, a family managing evening traffic across two corridors on the same day, or a Class 10 student who has one late free slot after activities finish. A shared digital whiteboard and an annotated PDF of a past paper cover most of what a home session does, though the tutor cannot physically point at a line of working the way they can across a table, and a slow internet connection on a bad evening can eat into the hour.

Hybrid plans, some weeks at home and some online, work well around travel, illness or a school trip, and many families here settle into hybrid without planning it that way, simply keeping home tuition as the default and switching to online when the week does not allow for travel. Whichever mode is chosen, the weekly hours plan itself should not change with the mode; what changes is only how the hour is delivered, not how much of it the student needs.

contentBlocks.heading: How a 1:1 IGCSE Tutor in Gurgaon Gets Verified
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor shown to a family has been checked against specifics that matter for IGCSE: which board they have actually taught, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, which tier, and at what grade level. A subject degree alone does not confirm any of this, and IB Gram's verification step exists precisely because a generic "IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon" search result rarely tells a parent whether a home tutor on the other end has taught Extended tier chemistry or only ever tutored Core.

Parents should still check some things themselves, and a verified profile does not remove that responsibility. Ask to see how the tutor marks a past paper against the real mark scheme rather than just giving a verbal answer; ask whether they know the difference between Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, for the specific subject; and use the free trial session as a genuine test, not a formality to get through before hours are booked. Choosing a 1:1 IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon this way takes longer than picking the first name on a list, but it is the difference between a tutor who happens to know maths and one who knows exactly how Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended is marked.

No certificate substitutes for watching a real session unfold, and there is no single best 1:1 IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon for every family, only the one whose trial session shows the right fit for this student. A workshop certificate or a teaching qualification says something about training, but it does not say how a particular tutor explains a wrong answer to this particular student, on this particular board. That is why the trial session, not the paperwork, is where the actual decision gets made, and why IB Gram treats it as a required step rather than an optional extra.

contentBlocks.heading: How Many Hours a Week Does 1:1 IGCSE Tutoring Actually Need?
contentBlocks.body:
There is no single number, but there are honest ranges. In the early part of Class 9, when the two-year course is just starting, two sessions of sixty to ninety minutes a week per subject is a common starting point for a student who is not already behind. As Class 9 moves into its second half and topics start to build on each other, some families add a third session for a subject the student is finding harder, while other subjects stay at two. By the middle of Class 10, once past papers become the main material, three sessions a week per subject is common for a student aiming at Extended or Higher tier, and it can rise further in the final two months before the May/June exam series that most Gurgaon schools use.

A single session should not be spent entirely on new content. A useful rough split for a student who is roughly on pace is about a third of the session on new content or a weak topic, a third on guided practice with the tutor correcting method in real time, and a third on past paper questions marked against the real scheme, though this shifts hard toward past papers in the final term before exams. For a student who is behind, more of the early sessions go to content and less to past papers, until the gap closes enough for past-paper work to be useful rather than discouraging.

The plan should be reviewed every four to six weeks against actual evidence: school test scores, how past papers are going, and whether the student still needs the tutor to hold every session or has started catching some of their own errors. A review is also where hours step down, not just up; a student who has closed a gap and is managing school homework independently again does not need to stay at three sessions a week out of habit. The goal of 1:1 IGCSE tutoring is a student who eventually needs the tutor less, not one who becomes dependent on being walked through every question, and a family that treats the tutor as a supplement to independent study, not a replacement for it, tends to see hours fall rather than rise over the two years.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Should Look Like After Eight Weeks of IGCSE Tutoring
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the first two or three sessions usually looks small and unglamorous: fewer careless errors on a paper the student has done before, a slightly faster start to a question that used to cause a freeze, or a student who can now explain, out loud, why an answer is wrong before the tutor points it out. These are the honest early signs, not a jump in a mock exam score, which usually takes longer to show up and depends on more than tutoring alone.

By around eight weeks, a family should expect to see some pattern in school test results, even if the movement is modest, along with a tutor who can point to specific recurring mistakes rather than a general "doing well" comment. Ask for this kind of specific feedback rather than accepting a vague update; a tutor who cannot name what the student is still getting wrong after two months has probably not been tracking closely enough.

No tutor, however experienced, can guarantee a particular grade, and any claim that promises one should be treated as a warning sign rather than reassurance. What a good IGCSE home tutor in Gurgaon can honestly promise is a structured plan, honest feedback on where the student stands, and hours that adjust as the picture becomes clearer. If eight weeks in there has been no change at all, in either school results or in how the student approaches a paper, that is the signal to review the plan itself, the subject fit, the tier decision or the tutor, rather than simply adding more hours to the same approach.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a 1:1 IGCSE tutor actually need in Class 9?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week of sixty to ninety minutes per subject is a common starting point in Class 9, rising only if a specific subject is clearly behind. Families sometimes over-commit to three subjects at three hours each from day one, which usually exhausts the student before the course has properly started. It is better to begin at a manageable pace, watch how the first month of school tests goes, and add hours to a subject that is genuinely struggling rather than spreading extra time evenly across everything. IB Gram's intake conversation is built around finding that starting point rather than assuming the highest number is always safest.

faqs.question: How should the weekly plan change as Cambridge or Edexcel exams get closer?
faqs.answer: Hours typically rise in the final term before the May/June exam series, with more of each session shifting to past papers marked against the real scheme. A student who was managing on two sessions a week in Class 9 often moves to three in the run-up to finals, particularly for Extended or Higher tier subjects. This is not the moment to introduce a brand new subject or tutor, since a new working relationship takes a few sessions to settle; it is the moment to intensify what is already working. The plan should step back down again once the exam series is over.

faqs.question: What actually happens in a 1:1 IGCSE session, content, practice or past papers?
faqs.answer: A balanced session usually splits into roughly a third new content or a weak topic, a third guided practice with the tutor correcting method as it happens, and a third past paper questions marked against the real mark scheme. Early in the course, more time goes to content; closer to exams, past papers dominate. A session that is entirely new content every single week, with no return to past paper practice, tends to leave a student who understands a topic in isolation but struggles to apply it under exam timing. Ask the tutor directly how a typical session is structured before committing to hours.

faqs.question: How often should the tutoring plan actually be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Every four to six weeks is the right interval for most Class 9 and Class 10 students, timed against school test results and how past paper scores are trending. Reviewing more often than that rarely gives enough new evidence to act on, while waiting longer risks a mismatch compounding, hours staying too low for a subject that has quietly fallen behind, or staying too high for one the student has already mastered. A review is also the moment to ask whether the student is starting to catch their own errors, which is one of the clearer signs that hours can step down.

faqs.question: Can too many tutoring hours make a student dependent on the tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the honest trade-offs of 1:1 tutoring: a student who is walked through every question in every session can lose the habit of attempting hard problems alone. The fix is not automatically fewer hours, but sessions that deliberately include independent time, past papers attempted alone first and then reviewed together, rather than every minute being tutor-led. A good plan blends paid hours with independent study at home, and a family should expect the tutor to be actively working toward the student needing them less over the two years, not more.

faqs.question: Does the tutor travel to our home in DLF Phase 3 or Sohna Road on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tutoring across DLF Phase 3, Sohna Road and the wider Gurgaon corridors is the format most families choose, subject to tutor availability and a realistic travel window for the specific slot. Evening traffic around Cyber City or Vatika Chowk can stretch a short trip, so IB Gram tries to match a tutor whose own base makes the corridor practical rather than promising an exact arrival minute. If a slot consistently runs into travel trouble, switching that particular week to online, while keeping the same tutor, is usually simpler than changing the time.

faqs.question: Should a parent be in the room during a home tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Most families are not in the room for the full session, though a parent introducing the tutor at the start and checking in briefly at the end works well for the first few sessions. A parent hovering through the whole hour can make a student more self-conscious about getting something wrong in front of the tutor, which works against the point of one-to-one attention. What matters more than physical presence is a quiet, reasonably lit space with a table, since IGCSE practice involves a lot of written working that needs room to spread out.

faqs.question: What happens if a home session gets missed because of school activities or traffic?
faqs.answer: A missed session should be rescheduled within the same week where possible, rather than simply dropped, since IGCSE topics build on each other and a two-week gap on the same subject can undo momentum. Families juggling school buses, sports practice and traffic across a Gurgaon corridor should expect the occasional clash, and agreeing a fallback online slot in advance, for exactly this situation, avoids losing the week entirely. This is worth raising directly with the tutor in the first few sessions rather than after the first missed one.

faqs.question: Is online 1:1 tutoring as effective as home tutoring for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For most content and practice work, yes, a shared digital whiteboard and an annotated past paper cover much of what a home session does. The honest limit is in physically pointing at a line of working or talking through a hand-drawn science diagram, which is smoother across a table than a screen, and a slow connection on a bad evening can eat into the hour. Many Gurgaon families use online for a specialist subject tutor who is not nearby, or for evenings when travel across a corridor is not practical, while keeping home sessions as the default.

faqs.answer: The family can ask IB Gram for a different match, and the process restarts from the shortlist rather than from the beginning, since the board, grade and subject information is already on file. It is worth being specific about what was not working, pace, personality, explanation style or something else, since that detail shapes who gets shortlisted next. A trial session with the new tutor still happens before hours are committed, exactly as with the first match, so the family is not asked to commit blind a second time either.

faqs.answer: The trial session usually opens with a short diagnostic exercise across a few topics the student finds hardest, so the tutor has something concrete to work from rather than starting cold. The family gets to see how the tutor explains a wrong answer, corrects working and paces the conversation with the student, which tells you more in sixty minutes than any profile description can. comparison.heading: How Does a 1:1 Plan Compare With Group IGCSE Options in Gurgaon?
comparison.intro: Each format below suits a different student. contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: Which IB Stage Is Your Child In?
contentBlocks.body:
A home based IB tutor Gurgaon families ask for needs to be matched to the right programme stage before anything else, because PYP, MYP and DP are structured completely differently. The IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12 and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, including Who we are, Where we are in place and time, How we express ourselves, How the world works, How we organize ourselves, and Sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry and the ten attributes of the IB learner profile. There are no external examinations at PYP; students complete the PYP exhibition in their final year.

The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8; the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. The Personal Project comes in MYP 5, with a Community Project in MYP 3 or 4. Some schools also offer MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, combining on-screen examinations with ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides for itself.

The IB Diploma Programme (DP) is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded 1 to 7. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add up to 3 more points, for a maximum of 45, with 24 the minimum for the diploma. An MYP tutor in Gurgaon and a DP tutor are, in practice, doing quite different jobs.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Home-Based IB Tutor Actually Teaches, Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
At DP level, the subjects families most often bring a home based IB tutor in for are IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) or Applications and Interpretation (AI), Physics, Chemistry and Biology, English A or B, and, closer to submission deadlines, support around Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE). A Mathematics AA tutor and an AI tutor are not interchangeable; AA suits a student heading toward proof-based and abstract mathematics, AI suits one applying maths to modelling and real-world contexts, and the HL and SL versions of each carry different depth again.

In the sciences, an IB DP tutor in Gurgaon working with a Physics, Chemistry or Biology student at HL is managing 240 recommended teaching hours' worth of content against 150 for SL, so pacing across two years matters as much as any single topic. TOK and the Extended Essay sit outside the six subjects but combine for up to 3 of the 45 available points, and a tutor who only teaches subject content while ignoring these two components is leaving marks on the table that many families do not realise are separate from the six-subject grades.

Below DP, an MYP tutor in Gurgaon is teaching toward the four assessment criteria in whichever subject group is weakest, not toward a single end-of-year exam, since MYP has no external examinations by default. A PYP-stage home tutor works differently again, supporting a unit of inquiry through reading, writing and number skills embedded in that unit's theme rather than teaching a subject in isolation. Recognising which of these three quite different jobs a family actually needs is the first thing a good home based IB tutor should get right.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring, Online or Hybrid: What Suits an IB Student Best?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is the starting point IB Gram leads with for most families: a verified tutor at the family's own table, in a slot built around school, buses and siblings' own schedules. For a younger PYP learner, home tutoring usually works best because the environment is familiar and a tutor can fold the unit of inquiry into things already in the house. For a DP2 student close to exams, home tutoring means a tutor sees the actual desk, the actual past paper annotations, and the actual working, not a screen recreation of it.

An IB online tutor Gurgaon families choose is often the right call for a specific reason: a DP subject combination, HL Physics with Mathematics AA at HL, say, is a smaller pool of genuinely qualified tutors, and the right specialist may simply not live close enough for weekly home visits. Online keeps that expertise reachable, and shared whiteboards or annotated past papers work well on a screen for most DP content, though a younger or easily distracted student, especially at PYP or early MYP, tends to focus better with someone physically in the room.

Hybrid, home sessions through most of the term with online during exam-season travel, illness, or when a specific HL topic needs a specialist the family's regular home tutor is not, gives some families the best of both without asking either side to compromise permanently.

The honest trade-off: home tutoring wins on focus and on reading a student's actual working; online wins on reaching the right specialist regardless of distance; hybrid trades a little of each for flexibility. contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Set Up a Study Space That Actually Works for IB?
contentBlocks.body:
A study space for IB work does not need to be a separate room, but it needs to be consistent: the same table or desk, session after session, with enough surface for a laptop, a notebook and a past paper side by side. A student who studies in a different spot every session spends the first ten minutes settling in rather than working, and that adds up across a school year of weekly sessions. Good light and a chair the student can sit in for an hour without shifting constantly matter more than anything decorative.

Siblings and household noise are the most common thing that derails an otherwise good home tutoring session, and it is worth planning for rather than hoping it does not happen. A younger sibling wandering in mid-explanation, a television in the next room, or a domestic helper moving through the space are all normal in a Gurgaon household and not something to apologise for, but agreeing on a rough do-not-disturb window with everyone at home before the session starts prevents most of it.

Where a parent sits matters more than most families expect. Sitting in on the first session is genuinely useful, since it shows how the tutor works and whether the pace suits the student. Beyond that, hovering over every answer tends to make a student, particularly a teenager in MYP or DP, perform for the parent rather than think for themselves; stepping back to a nearby room within earshot, but out of the direct sightline, usually works better once the routine is established.

Keeping materials organised between sessions is a small habit that protects a lot of time: one folder or box per subject, past papers filed by topic rather than by date, and a running note of what was covered last time so the next session does not start by re-explaining where things left off.

If progress is only ever described in general terms, that is worth asking the tutor to make specific.

No tutor can guarantee a grade or a set of IB points, and a home based IB tutor working honestly will say so rather than imply otherwise. The household routine itself, whether sessions happen consistently, whether materials stay organised, whether a parent's presence helps or distracts, shapes outcomes nearly as much as the teaching does, and a good tutor will say when the routine, not the subject content, is the thing actually holding a student back.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between PYP, MYP and DP?

acceptedAnswer.text: PYP covers ages 3 to 12 and is built around six transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, with no external examinations. MYP runs five years, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, with every subject assessed against four criteria scored 0 to 8 that convert to a final 1-7 grade. DP is the two-year Diploma Programme, six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1-7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum. A home based IB tutor needs to work quite differently across the three.

mainEntity.name: Will the same home tutor teach my child through PYP, MYP and DP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not usually, and it is worth being wary of a tutor who claims equal strength across all three without evidence. PYP tutoring is about supporting a unit of inquiry through embedded skills, MYP is about criterion-based marking across eight subject groups, and DP is about deep subject content at HL or SL alongside TOK and the Extended Essay. contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: Getting the Syllabus Right at Home
contentBlocks.body:
Before a home tutor sets foot in the house, it is worth the family confirming exactly which IGCSE their child sits, because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are run by different boards with different calendars. Cambridge holds three exam series a year: February/March, a sitting offered only in India, plus the more widely used May/June and October/November windows. Most Cambridge subjects grade A* through G, though a handful of syllabuses now run 9-1 versions under separate codes, so it is worth checking the school's own paperwork rather than assuming.

Pearson Edexcel runs a leaner calendar, January and May/June, and grades everything on the 9-1 scale, a system some families switching over from CBSE find easier to read at a glance since it mirrors newer numeric grading elsewhere. Where Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, capping at grade C for Core and reaching A* for Extended, that decision is usually made partway through Grade 9 and quietly reshapes what a home tutor should be drilling for the rest of the course.

A Cambridge IGCSE tutor Gurgaon families bring into the house and an Edexcel IGCSE tutor Gurugram parents search for are not doing identical jobs, even on the same subject, because the papers, timing and mark schemes differ enough to matter. After Grade 10 the routes split further still, toward the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or back into CBSE or ISC for Class 11, and a tutor aware of where the student is headed teaches the current two years with that destination in view rather than in isolation.

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects a Home-Based IGCSE Tutor Covers, Paper by Paper
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is usually the subject that brings a family to search for a home based IGCSE tutor first, and the paper structure explains why practice at home needs to be deliberate. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Core candidates sit Paper 1, non-calculator, and Paper 3, calculator; Extended candidates sit Paper 2, non-calculator, and Paper 4, calculator. A tutor working at a family's dining table should be running timed non-calculator drills separately from calculator practice, since students who only ever revise with a calculator nearby tend to freeze on the non-calculator paper regardless of how well they actually know the topic. Edexcel's Mathematics A (4MA1) splits into Foundation and Higher tiers, each carrying two calculator papers, a different rhythm again.

The sciences add a third component beyond the usual written papers: practical assessment. Multiple choice sits in Paper 1 or Paper 2, theory in Paper 3 or Paper 4, and practical skills in Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, an alternative to practical, whichever the school has chosen. The split is fixed at 30% multiple choice, 50% theory and 20% practical, and a home tutor who never touches how observations should be recorded or a method written up is quietly ignoring a fifth of the grade. Edexcel's sciences fold practical skills into the written papers instead, without a separate practical paper.

English is where families most often get the syllabus wrong at home, since IGCSE offers several distinct versions: Cambridge First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language in two forms, 0510 and 0511, where 0511 counts speaking into the final grade and 0510 reports it separately, and Literature in English 0475, alongside Edexcel's own English Language A, Language B and English as a Second Language syllabuses. A tutor should confirm the exact code before the first session, not assume from the subject name alone.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Build a Study Space That Works for IGCSE?

The physical setup matters less for its furniture than for its consistency. A fixed spot, the same corner of the dining table or the same desk every session, with room to spread a textbook, a notebook and a past paper side by side, saves a student from losing the first stretch of every session to simply settling in. Reasonable light and a chair that does not need constant readjusting matter more than anything that looks impressive.

Siblings and general household noise are the single most common thing that interrupts an otherwise solid IGCSE session, and it is far easier to plan around than to fix after the fact. A younger brother or sister wandering in partway through a Mathematics explanation, a television left on in the next room, or household staff moving through the space are ordinary in most Gurgaon homes, and agreeing a rough quiet window with the household before the tutor arrives heads off most of it.

Where the parent sits during a session is worth deciding deliberately rather than by habit. After that, sitting close enough to correct every small error tends to push a Grade 9 or 10 student toward answering for the parent's benefit rather than thinking it through themselves; staying nearby but out of the direct line of sight usually serves the student better once things settle.

Between sessions, a simple filing habit protects far more time than it costs: one folder per subject, past papers sorted by topic rather than by date sat, and a short note after each session on what was covered so the next one does not start by retracing old ground.

mainEntity.name: What does a workable IGCSE study space at home actually look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is defined by consistency rather than furniture: the same desk or table every session, enough room for a textbook, notebook and past paper side by side, decent light, and a chair the student is not constantly shifting in. It does not need its own room. A student who studies in a different spot each session spends the first stretch of every lesson simply settling in rather than working, and across a school year that adds up to real lost time. Clearing the space of the day's other clutter just before a session begins does most of the remaining work.

mainEntity.name: How should we manage siblings and noise during a home tuition session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree a rough quiet window with everyone in the house before the tutor arrives, rather than hoping it sorts itself out. A younger sibling wandering in mid-explanation, a television left on nearby, or household staff moving through the space are ordinary in most Gurgaon homes and nothing to apologise for. A good home based IGCSE tutor expects some interruption and paces sessions around it. If it happens often enough to genuinely disrupt a lesson, raise it directly with the tutor so the room or the slot can be adjusted rather than letting it quietly repeat.

mainEntity.name: Should a parent stay in the room during IGCSE home tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sitting in for the first session is worth doing, since it shows directly how the tutor works and whether the pace suits the student. Beyond that, correcting every small error from close by tends to push a Grade 9 or 10 student to answer for the parent rather than work it out themselves, so staying nearby but out of direct sightline usually works better once a routine is settled. Some students genuinely prefer a parent close by for longer, and that is fine too; IB Gram leaves the decision with the family rather than prescribing one answer.

mainEntity.name: How do we keep IGCSE notes and past papers organised between sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep it simple: one folder per subject, past papers filed by topic rather than by the date they were attempted, and a short note after each session on what was covered so the next one does not start by retracing old ground. For subjects with tiered papers, keep Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, materials clearly separated, since mixing them makes revision confusing later in the year. This matters more with a home based tutor than at a coaching centre, since the materials travel with the student rather than staying in one classroom.

mainEntity.name: What is the actual difference between Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cambridge IGCSE runs three exam series a year, February/March in India only, plus May/June and October/November, and grades most subjects A* to G, with some newer syllabuses on a 9-1 scale under separate codes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs two series, January and May/June, and grades everything 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, Core capping at grade C and Extended reaching A*; Edexcel's equivalent split is Foundation and Higher. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon and an Edexcel IGCSE tutor are not automatically interchangeable, even on the same subject.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Home IB Tutor Is Matched to Your Family in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A family usually starts with a short query or a free consultation call, not a form. IB Gram asks what programme stage the student is in, whether Diploma Programme subjects are at Higher Level or Standard Level, which school the student attends, and which evening slots are actually free once school buses, sport and homework are accounted for. That last question matters more in Gurgaon than it sounds: a 6 pm slot on Sohna Road during evening traffic is a different commitment than the same slot in Sushant Lok.

Matching then runs through a short sequence. 1. IB Gram reviews the request against tutor profiles verified for the exact programme and level, not just "IB" as a label. 2. A shortlist is narrowed to tutors whose travel pattern already covers the family's sector, or who are confirmed for online delivery if the sector is far from their usual route. 3. A trial class is arranged in the family's home, on the slot the family actually asked for, so the first impression is the real one. 4. After the trial, the family says yes, asks for a different match, or asks for changes to timing or approach before the arrangement continues.

Nothing here is instant. A Higher Level Physics specialist for a DP2 student near an exam session is a narrower search than a general MYP tutor, and honest availability language reflects that: a match happens subject to tutor availability, and a family is told when a search is taking longer than the ordinary case in Gurgaon. What does not change is the sequence itself, because skipping the trial to save a week is usually what leads to a tutor being replaced twice instead of once.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Programme Stage Is Your Child In?
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme runs from age three to twelve and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet. Learning happens through units of inquiry built around the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, and there are no external examinations until the PYP exhibition in the final year. Most PYP families in Gurgaon do not need formal tuition at all; where a parent wants extra support, a home tutor's job is to reinforce the inquiry already happening in class, not to run a parallel curriculum.

The Middle Years Programme covers five years, MYP 1 through MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, across eight subject groups. Every subject is marked against four criteria, A through D, each scored out of eight, and the criterion total out of thirty-two converts to a final grade of one to seven through the IB's published grade boundaries. This is where home tuition earns its keep: a tutor who marks a student's own work against the actual criterion language, rather than a generic mark scheme, catches the gap between a good answer and a criterion-complete one. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project (the Community Project sits in MYP 3 or 4), and some schools also run optional MYP eAssessment, on-screen exams plus ePortfolios, though that decision sits with the school, not the family.

The Diploma Programme is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, built from six subjects across six groups, with three or four taken at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours). Each subject is graded one to seven, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combine for up to three more points, and the maximum score is forty-five, with twenty-four the minimum for the diploma itself, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service runs alongside the academic subjects. Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session; a minority use November, mainly for retakes, with results released in early July. Home tuition in DP1 and DP2 tends to concentrate on the Higher Level subjects and on IA, TOK and EE deadlines that a school timetable does not always leave room to discuss one to one.

MYP (MYP 1-5): four criteria A-D per subject, each out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade.
DP (DP1-DP2): six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, the rest at Standard Level.
DP scoring: subjects out of 7, plus up to 3 points from TOK and the Extended Essay, maximum 45.
MYP 5 adds the Personal Project; the Community Project sits in MYP 3 or 4.
Most Gurgaon IB schools use the May exam session; November mainly serves retakes.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does IB Subject Support Really Require?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each offered at Higher and Standard Level, and the two are not interchangeable: AA leans on calculus and proof, AI leans on modelling and technology. A home tutor working on AA HL past papers at the dining table needs the actual formula booklet the school uses and the command terms the IB sets for every question: define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent. Getting the command term wrong is a common reason a technically correct answer loses marks, and it is exactly the kind of thing that is easy to miss in a batch of twenty and obvious in a room with one student.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology carry their own internal assessment components alongside the written papers, and a tutor who has actually marked IB-style lab write-ups is worth more here than one who only knows the content. English A (literature or language and literature) and English B (as an additional language) sit at opposite ends of the subject group; a home tutor for English A is reading texts closely with the student, while an English B tutor is often building written and oral fluency from a different starting point entirely.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay do not belong to any one subject group, which is exactly why they get squeezed out of a normal school timetable. A student researching an Extended Essay in Economics or preparing a TOK exhibition linking two areas of knowledge benefits from a tutor session that is not also trying to cover next week's Maths homework. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's own channels; a home tutor's role in Gurgaon is to work from those, not to replace them with invented material or guessed grade boundaries.

contentBlocks.heading: School Calendars and IB Deadlines Across Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families in Gurgaon whose children attend IB World Schools, including Pathways World School in Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School in Aravali and DPS International Edge, deal with a school calendar that a home tutor has to work around rather than compete with. That means unit tests through the term, a run of internal assessments concentrated in DP1 and DP2, a school-set mock examination some months before the May session, and the ordinary pressure of CAS logging, Personal Project deadlines in MYP 5 and Extended Essay drafts that all land in the same few weeks if nobody is tracking them separately.

None of this is unique to one school; it is the shape of an IB year everywhere in Gurgaon. What changes school to school is pacing: some schools front-load content in DP1 and leave DP2 mostly for revision and internal assessments, others spread new content further into DP2. A home tutor who does not know a specific school's pacing in advance should ask early, in the first or second session, rather than assume the syllabus is being taught in textbook order.

The practical effect for scheduling a home IB tutor in Gurgaon is that the weeks before a mock or the May session are not the moment to start looking for help; families who begin a search in that window get matched, but with a narrower set of tutors already free on short notice. Starting a term earlier gives more room to find the right specialist rather than the first available one, and it gives a home tutor time to actually learn a student's school before the pressure builds.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid Tuition: What Works Best in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home IB tuition in Gurgaon is the starting point for most families searching for IB support here, and for good reason: a tutor at the dining table can see a student's actual working, not just the final answer, catch a handwriting habit that costs marks in an exam, and work directly from the same exercise book the student uses at school. It also removes the commute a student would otherwise make to a centre after a full school day, which matters more the later the slot gets.

Online tuition trades that physical presence for reach. A family in New Gurgaon or on the Dwarka Expressway who wants a specific HL Physics or Economics specialist, and finds that specialist lives on the other side of Gurgaon, gets a shared whiteboard and an annotated past paper instead of a commute problem. Screen-based work suits structured practice, past-paper marking and revision well; it suits a student who is easily distracted, or subjects that depend on watching handwritten working in real time, less well.

Hybrid tuition, a weekly home session plus an occasional or alternating online one, is how many families in the outer corridors, SPR, New Gurgaon, Dwarka Expressway, Old Gurgaon and Manesar, actually end up working once a term settles down. It keeps the in-person relationship for the subjects that need it and uses online sessions to absorb a bad traffic evening or a specialist who cannot make the drive every week.

None of the three is automatically right. A DP2 student six weeks from mocks generally benefits from home sessions where a tutor can sit beside them through a full past paper; the same student revising vocabulary or definitions the week after mocks might do just as well online. The honest answer is that the mode should follow the task and the week, not a fixed rule set in September.

Online tuition: reaches specialists outside a family's corridor, works well for structured revision.

contentBlocks.heading: How Are Home IB Tutors Verified Before a First Visit?
contentBlocks.body:
Before any tutor is suggested for a home visit, IB Gram checks the profile against the request: whether the tutor has taught the exact programme stage (PYP, MYP or DP), the subject and level (HL or SL, or the MYP criteria at that year group), and whether their availability genuinely fits the family's slot rather than a similar one nearby. That is the baseline; it does not replace what a parent should check for themselves once a tutor is proposed.

A parent is entitled to ask a proposed home tutor directly about their board experience, which levels they have taught, and how they would handle the specific gap the student has, before the first session even happens. It is reasonable to ask for the trial class to be treated as a real evaluation, not a formality: watch how the tutor responds when the student gets something wrong, not just whether they can explain the topic well when everything goes smoothly. A tutor who becomes impatient or vague under a wrong answer in a trial is unlikely to be different in week six.

For a home visit specifically, it is also reasonable to confirm who else will be in the house during the session, whether a younger sibling needs to be elsewhere, and what happens if the tutor is delayed by traffic on a corridor like Golf Course Extension Road or Sohna Road at peak hours. None of this replaces trusting a match once it is made; it simply means the first two or three sessions are treated as a genuine test, with the option to ask for a different match if something about the fit, not just the subject knowledge, is not working.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should the First Home IB Tuition Session Include?
contentBlocks.body:
The first session in a family's home is usually diagnostic before it is instructional. A tutor coming into a new home for IB tuition should spend part of the first sitting understanding where the student actually is against the syllabus, not just what the school's last report said, by looking at a recent test, a set of notes, or a past paper attempt. For a DP1 student this might mean identifying which topics from the first term need revisiting before new content builds on them; for an MYP student it might mean looking at how the last piece of work scored against the four criteria and where the gap to the next boundary sits.

A workable study space at home does not need to be elaborate. A cleared table, decent lighting, the student's own textbooks and exercise books rather than photocopies, and a reasonably quiet room for the length of the session are what actually matter; a formal study or a home office is a bonus, not a requirement. Whether a parent should be in the room is a judgement call families make differently: some sit in for the first session to see how the tutor works, then step out once they are comfortable; others prefer to leave the two working alone from the start so the student speaks up rather than deferring to a parent in the room.

Before the first home visit, it helps to prepare a short list: the last two or three school reports or test results, the current unit or topic list from the school, the recommended textbook or the school's own resource pack, and a note of which evening slot is genuinely free once travel time, dinner and any other activity are accounted for. Getting this ready before the tutor arrives means the first session goes to diagnosing the actual gap instead of gathering paperwork.
items: 1. Have the last two or three school reports or recent test results ready.
2. Pull together the current topic list or unit plan from the school.
3. Confirm the genuinely free evening slot, allowing for travel and dinner.
4. Set up a cleared table with the student's own textbooks and notebooks, not photocopies.
5. Decide in advance whether a parent will sit in for the first session or the second.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does Real Progress in Home IB Tuition Look Like in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in home IB tuition in Gurgaon rarely shows up as a sudden jump in a single test; it shows up as fewer of the same mistake repeating across sessions, tighter answers to command terms like evaluate and discuss, and a student who starts a past paper without needing the first question explained. For an MYP student, a more reliable sign is criterion-level movement: work that used to sit low in a criterion band starting to touch the boundary above it. None of this is guaranteed by tuition alone; a student who does not do the practice between sessions will not move much no matter how good the tutor is, and no tutor can promise a specific grade.

A reasonable timeline is four to six weeks before a family should expect to see any pattern at all, longer for a subject where the student is starting from a genuine gap rather than a small one. If six weeks pass with no change in the mistakes a student is making, in test scores, or in how they talk about the subject, that is worth raising directly with the tutor, and worth asking IB Gram for a different match if the conversation does not lead anywhere.

Home tuition also has real limits worth saying plainly. It will not substitute for a student doing the reading, the past papers or the CAS commitments the school expects; it will not fix a mismatch between a student's chosen HL subjects and their actual interest; and it is not a way to outsource the Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment, both of which the IB expects to be a student's own work with only appropriate guidance. What it can do, session by session, is make the gap between where a student is and where the syllabus expects them to be smaller.

Starting home IB tuition in Gurgaon is a short conversation, not a commitment. A family sends a query or books a free consultation, and IB Gram asks about the student's programme stage, board and level, the school's calendar, the sector the family lives in, and the slot that is actually free on a normal week. From there, a shortlist of tutors whose profiles are verified for that exact programme, subject and level is matched to the family, weighted toward tutors who already work the family's corridor where that is possible.

A free trial class comes before any ongoing commitment. It runs in the family's home on the agreed slot, so the family sees exactly how the arrangement would work week to week rather than judging a tutor on a phone call. After the trial, the family decides: continue with that tutor, ask for a different match, or adjust the timing or approach before continuing. Lessons then run at home, online or in a hybrid pattern depending on what the family and the corridor make practical, and that pattern can change later if a school term gets busier or a specialist subject needs a different tutor for a stretch.

Nothing about this process asks a family to decide everything on day one. Book a consultation, sit through one trial session at the actual table where the work will happen, and use that to judge fit, subject depth and whether the slot genuinely works, before agreeing to anything ongoing in Gurgaon.

faqs.answer: Corridors close to the centre of Gurgaon, Golf Course Road, Golf Course Extension Road, DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road, Cyber City and Sushant Lok, generally have the most tutors already living or working nearby, so evening slots after school are the most reliable there. faqs.question: Should a parent be in the room during home IB tuition?
faqs.answer: There is no single right answer; it depends on the student's age and how the arrangement settles. Many families sit in for the first session or two to see how the tutor teaches and how the student responds, then step out once they are comfortable, especially for older DP students who tend to speak more freely without a parent listening. faqs.question: What happens if a home session is missed or the tutor is delayed by traffic?
faqs.answer: Evening traffic on corridors like Golf Course Extension Road or Sohna Road can stretch a short trip longer than expected, and IB Gram expects that to happen occasionally rather than treating it as unusual. A missed or shortened session is normally rescheduled within the same week rather than simply dropped, and a family that finds delays becoming a regular pattern with a particular tutor should raise it directly, since it usually points to a slot or corridor mismatch that is worth fixing rather than tolerating term after term.

faqs.question: Does home IB tuition work for both MYP and DP students?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the shape of a session differs. An MYP session tends to focus on building consistent habits against the four assessment criteria, term by term, well before DP begins. A DP session, particularly in DP2, is more often built around Higher Level content, past papers and the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and TOK deadlines that a school timetable rarely leaves much one-to-one time for. Both benefit from the same thing at home: a tutor working from the student's actual notebook and the school's own pacing, rather than a generic outline of the syllabus.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor help with the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: A tutor can support the thinking around an Extended Essay or a TOK exhibition, discussing structure, argument and how a topic connects to an area of knowledge, and can talk through drafts the way a good study partner would. What a tutor cannot do is write or substantially rewrite the work, since the IB expects the Extended Essay and TOK tasks to be the student's own, with only appropriate guidance from any adult. A home session is a useful place to talk through a stuck point between the student's own drafts, not a place to outsource the essay itself.

faqs.question: What if the first home tutor is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it is not treated as a failed search. If the trial class or the first few sessions show that the subject knowledge is fine but the working style is not, or the slot keeps clashing with something at school, a family can ask IB Gram for a different match rather than persevering out of politeness. The earlier this is raised, the easier the switch is, since less time and continuity has been built up with the wrong tutor. A second match draws on the same verified profile pool as the first.

faqs.question: Is online tuition better than home tuition for a specialist HL subject?
faqs.answer: It depends on how scarce the specialist is and where the family lives in Gurgaon. A family in central Gurgaon looking for a common HL subject usually finds a strong home match without much trouble. A family further out, on the Dwarka Expressway or in New Gurgaon, looking for a less common HL subject or an examiner-level specialist, may find that the best-matched tutor for the subject does not live nearby, in which case a weekly online session with that specialist often beats a less-suited tutor who happens to be closer.

faqs.question: What should we prepare before the first home IB tuition visit?
faqs.answer: Have the last two or three school reports or recent test results ready, along with the current unit or topic list from the school and, if there is one, the textbook or resource pack the school actually uses. Confirm which evening slot is genuinely free once travel, dinner and any other activity are accounted for, rather than the slot that looks free on paper. Clear a table with reasonable lighting and have the student's own books and notebooks out rather than photocopies. None of this needs to be elaborate; it just saves the first session for diagnosis rather than paperwork.

faqs.question: How is progress communicated to parents during home IB tuition?
faqs.answer: A tutor should be able to tell a parent, in plain terms after each session or on a short regular check-in, what was covered, where the student is still weak, and roughly what the next few sessions will focus on. IB Gram is also a point of contact if a parent wants a second read on how things are going or wants to raise a concern without going through the tutor directly. What no one can honestly offer is a running prediction of a final grade; progress is tracked through fewer repeated mistakes and stronger practice, not a number promised in advance.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor follow the school's own pace, or teach the syllabus separately?
faqs.answer: A good home tutor asks about the school's pacing in the first or second session and works from it, rather than teaching the syllabus in a fixed order that may run weeks ahead of or behind what the student is doing in class. Schools vary: some front-load Diploma Programme content in DP1 and spend DP2 mostly on revision and internal assessments, others spread new content further into DP2. Following the school's own order matters most in the months before a mock or the May exam session, when a student needs practice on exactly what is about to be tested.

contentBlocks.heading: Matching a Home IGCSE Tutor to Your Family
contentBlocks.body:
Getting matched starts with a short call or an online query, not a lengthy form. IB Gram asks which syllabus your child actually sits, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, which grade they are in, whether subjects run tiered (Core or Extended for Cambridge, Foundation or Higher for Edexcel Maths), and which evening slot survives homework, sport and dinner intact. That syllabus question matters more than it looks: a Cambridge-trained tutor moving to an Edexcel household without checking first can spend a session teaching the wrong paper structure before anyone notices.

From there, matching follows a fixed sequence. 1. Profiles are filtered to tutors verified for the exact syllabus, Cambridge or Edexcel, and the specific tier or subject code where one applies. 2. The shortlist narrows to tutors whose travel already covers the family's corridor, or who are confirmed for online delivery where it does not. 3. A trial class runs in the student's own home, on the slot the family actually asked for. 4. After the trial, the family confirms, asks for someone else, or adjusts the plan before anything continues.

A Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended tutor and an Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 Higher tutor are not interchangeable, even though both are teaching Grade 9 or 10 maths, and a family that does not yet know which syllabus their child sits should say so honestly rather than guess. Matching stays subject to tutor availability, and a search for a less common combination, say Edexcel ESL alongside Cambridge sciences, is told upfront that it may take a little longer than a single-syllabus request.

Tutor profiles are filtered by exact syllabus and subject code, not just "IGCSE".
A home trial class runs on the slot the family actually requested.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: Which Syllabus Is Your Child On?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon almost always means one of two boards: Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Both are usually taken as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and both are commonly followed by the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or a move into CBSE or ISC for Class 11, which is worth knowing before choosing how a home tutor spends Grade 10: a student heading into DP Higher Level Maths needs different groundwork than one moving into a CBSE Class 11 stream.

The two boards run on different calendars and grade differently. Cambridge holds exam series in February and March (a series offered only in India), May and June, and October and November, so a Gurgaon student has more retake and progression flexibility than the exam calendar alone suggests. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May or June. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, though some subjects now have 9-1 versions under different syllabus codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9 to 1. A tutor who does not know which grading scale applies is guessing at what a target grade actually means for a given student.

Tiering is where the two boards diverge most for a home tutor's planning. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*, and entering a student for the wrong tier either caps their potential grade or exposes them to content they are not ready for. Getting that tier decision right, subject by subject, is one of the most useful things a home tutor does before Grade 10 begins in earnest.

Cambridge exam series: February/March (India-only), May/June, October/November.
Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June.
