contentBlocks.heading: What a Subject-Specialist Exam Tutor Needs to Know Cold
contentBlocks.body:
An exam tutor who does not know a syllabus's paper structure cold is guessing at what to prioritise, and guessing is expensive this close to a session. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, that means knowing Core candidates sit Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator); for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1), it means knowing the Foundation or Higher tier structure, with two calculator papers per tier. A Maths exam tutor should be drilling the non-calculator paper as its own discrete skill, since students comfortable with a calculator often lose straightforward method marks the moment it is taken away.

For sciences, a tutor needs to know the weighting, not just the content. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, examined from 2023, weight multiple choice (Paper 1 Core, Paper 2 Extended) at 30%, theory (Paper 3 Core, Paper 4 Extended) at 50%, and practical assessment through Paper 5 or Paper 6 at 20%, chosen by the school. An exam tutor who spends every session on theory content and never touches the practical paper's specific command words, describe, explain, evaluate, is quietly under-preparing a fifth of the marks. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, assessing practical skills inside the written papers directly rather than as a separate component.

For English, a tutor needs to know which of several distinct syllabuses a student is actually entered for: Cambridge First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511, Literature in English 0475, or Edexcel's English Language A (4EA1), Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). These are marked differently enough that a tutor fluent in one can genuinely underperform teaching another; ask any prospective English exam tutor directly which of these they have most recently taken students through, rather than assuming English is English. This kind of syllabus fluency matters just as much whether the session runs as home tuition or online, since it is the tutor's knowledge, not the format, that determines whether revision time is well spent.

contentBlocks.heading: A Home Exam Tutor, Online, or Both: What Actually Works Best?
contentBlocks.body:
A home exam tutor is IB Gram's usual starting recommendation for this stage, because watching a student attempt a timed paper in the room shows things a submitted script never will: hesitation before a question, handwriting that deteriorates as the clock runs down, a section skipped entirely and never returned to. For Gurgaon families deciding between a home exam tutor, an online one, or a hybrid pattern, the honest position is that each format trades something for something else, and the right choice depends on what the student specifically needs corrected.

A home exam tutor wins on reading real exam behaviour under pressure and on physically walking through a marked script side by side, pointing at exactly where a mark was lost. It loses on flexibility once exam season gets busy, since a tutor covering several students across one corridor has less room to shift a slot at short notice than earlier in the year. An IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon wins on reach: a specialist who does not live near a family's sector is still available on a screen, which matters more in these final weeks when subject-specific expertise counts for more than proximity. It loses some of the fine-grained view of exam behaviour, though a shared screen and a visible timer still carry a surprising amount of that information.

For most families in the final six weeks, a hybrid pattern works best in practice: a home exam tutor for full timed past papers, supervised in person, with a shorter online session mid-week to review what went wrong and drill the specific pattern before the next attempt. Neither format alone captures everything a student needs in this stretch, and a tutor willing to work across both, rather than insisting on one, is usually the more useful match.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should an Exam Tutor Actually Be Doing Each Week?
contentBlocks.body:
What an exam tutor should actually be doing each week changes as the session gets closer, and a parent who understands the shape of it can tell fairly quickly whether a tutor is planning properly or just filling an hour. Eight to ten weeks out, a good exam tutor is splitting time between closing the last real content gaps and introducing the first full past papers under loosely timed conditions, still teaching some, but increasingly testing. Six weeks out, content should be essentially settled, and the tutor's week should be dominated by timed practice with detailed marking after every attempt, not a score alone but a specific account of where marks went.

In the final two to three weeks, an exam tutor's job narrows almost entirely to full papers under strict exam timing, careful line-by-line marking against the real scheme, and short, targeted drilling of whatever specific error keeps recurring, rather than a broad re-teach of anything. This is where the difference between a good exam tutor and an average one shows most clearly: an average tutor keeps assigning full papers regardless of what the marking reveals, while a good one adjusts each week's focus based specifically on the last paper's pattern of lost marks.

Past papers used without proper marking teach very little, and a tutor who assigns papers without walking through the scheme afterward is not really doing exam tutoring, just supervised practice. The useful weekly rhythm is: attempt a paper under real time pressure, mark it line by line against the actual scheme together, identify what specifically was lost, not enough working shown, a command term misread, time that ran out on the final question, and then drill exactly that gap before the next attempt. A tutor following this rhythm consistently, week after week, is doing the job properly; one who is not is charging exam-tutor rates for ordinary tuition.

How you know an exam tutor is actually earning their sessions, rather than simply running out the clock each week, comes down to specific, checkable signs rather than a feeling. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any exam tutor who implies one after a single mock or trial session should be treated with caution rather than relief. What a parent can reasonably expect across two or three weeks is narrower: the same category of error appearing less often in successive timed papers, a student who can explain in their own words what went wrong on the last attempt, and marked scripts a parent can actually look at, not just a verbal summary of it went well.

Ask to see the marked papers directly rather than relying on a general update. A tutor who is genuinely working through the scheme with the student will have scripts with specific annotations, where a mark was lost, what the correct approach would have scored, not a single tick or cross at the end. Parents sometimes search for the best igcse exam tutor in Gurgaon, but this close to an exam, the more useful question is not which tutor has the best reputation but whether this specific tutor can produce that kind of specific, checkable evidence of progress session after session.

It is also fair to expect an exam tutor to be honest about limits. A student with several large content gaps six weeks out is not going to close all of them and also build strong exam technique in equal measure; a good tutor says plainly which one matters more given the time left, rather than promising both. If two or three practice papers pass with no visible change in the pattern of lost marks, that is worth raising directly with IB Gram rather than continuing the same sessions and hoping the actual exam goes differently.

faqs.question: How is an exam tutor different from the subject tutor my child already has?
faqs.answer: A subject tutor working across the year typically balances new content, homework help and steady progress; an exam tutor brought in for the final stretch has a narrower brief: mark real past papers against the actual scheme, correct exam technique, and drill whatever error pattern is costing the most marks. Some families keep the existing subject tutor and simply shift their focus for the final weeks; others bring in a second, exam-specific specialist alongside the regular tutor for one particular subject that needs sharper, more current syllabus expertise. Either can work well, and it is worth discussing directly with IB Gram which suits your situation.

faqs.question: Does the exam tutor need to have taught at my child's specific school?
faqs.answer: No, and it is a less useful filter than families sometimes assume. What matters far more is recent, current experience with the exact board, syllabus and tier, since the exam itself is set externally and does not vary by school. A tutor unfamiliar with a specific school can still ask for the scheme of work or recent test papers to understand the school's particular pacing, which takes one conversation rather than requiring prior familiarity. Prioritising a tutor by syllabus expertise over school familiarity generally gets a stronger match for this specific, exam-focused role.

faqs.question: Can one exam tutor handle two subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, though it depends heavily on the specific subjects and the tutor's genuine depth in both. A tutor confidently fluent in both Physics and Chemistry at Extended level, for instance, can work well for a student needing both, and it simplifies scheduling to one relationship rather than two. But a tutor who is strong in one subject and merely adequate in the second is usually not the better choice over two separate specialists, particularly this close to an exam when depth matters more than convenience. Ask directly, in the trial for each subject, rather than assuming competence carries across.

faqs.question: What if there is no improvement even close to the exam?
faqs.answer: If two or three timed papers in a row show no real change in the pattern of lost marks despite consistent sessions, treat that as a signal to act rather than to wait out the remaining weeks hoping for a shift. Sometimes a change in approach, narrower drilling on one specific weakness instead of full papers every session, is enough; sometimes a different tutor's explanation style genuinely gets through in a way the first one did not. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a tutor should be able to explain plainly why the current plan is not moving and propose something specific to change, rather than repeating the same pattern and hoping the actual exam goes differently.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds Your Exam Tuition Plan in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
An ib exam tuition gurgaon plan starts differently to ordinary tutoring: the first question is not "what subject" but "which date, and how many weeks remain." IB Gram asks for the board, programme, subjects, the confirmed or expected mock date, and which papers or components the student is weakest on, before suggesting anyone. A parent can send a query directly or book a free consultation, and the answer shapes everything that follows, including whether the plan runs at home, online or as a mix of both. This holds whether the search was ib exam tuition gurgaon or ib exam tuition Gurugram; the intake does not change with the spelling.

From intake to a running plan, the steps stay the same for every family.
1. IB Gram maps the weeks available against the subjects and papers named, flagging where time is already tight.
2. It shortlists two or three verified tutors with real experience preparing students for this exact exam session, not general subject tutors.
3. A trial or demo session runs first, usually built around one past-paper question, so the family can see the marking style before committing.
4. If the pace or style is wrong for the weeks remaining, IB Gram arranges a different tutor immediately rather than losing a week to indecision.

Speed matters here in a way it does not for ordinary tuition; a family with six weeks to the exam session cannot afford a slow, exploratory first month. But speed does not mean skipping the trial. A rushed match still costs more time than it saves if the tutor's marking style does not match what the school's own examiners expect, which is exactly what the trial session is there to catch before a plan is locked in.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Exam Session Is Your Child Actually Working Towards?
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme (DP) is examined at the end of a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, across six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours), each graded one to seven. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) add up to three more points on top of that, so forty-five is the maximum and twenty-four the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions, alongside Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Most Gurgaon IB schools sit the May session; a minority use November, alongside retake candidates, and May results are released in early July, which is worth knowing when planning what comes after, which is why an IB DP tutor in Gurgaon spends real time on this distinction rather than treating every subject the same.

Middle Years Programme (MYP) students are not sitting a single terminal paper in the DP sense; instead, every subject across eight groups is assessed against four criteria, A to D, scored zero to eight each, and the criterion total out of thirty-two converts to a final one-to-seven grade. MYP 5 students may also sit MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, though this is optional and each school decides whether to offer it; a MYP tutor in Gurgaon preparing a student for eAssessment needs criterion literacy under screen conditions specifically, not just subject knowledge. Where a school does not offer eAssessment, the Personal Project in MYP 5 (or the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4) carries more weight instead.

Primary Years Programme (PYP) students, roughly ages three to twelve, sit no external examinations at all, working instead towards the PYP exhibition in their final year, so exam tuition in the sense this page means does not really apply below MYP. Knowing exactly which of these your child is working towards changes what exam tuition should even contain: a DP2 student six weeks from May needs paper-by-paper drilling against real mark schemes, while an MYP eAssessment student needs criterion-referenced practice under screen conditions; confusing the two wastes weeks a family often does not have.
items: DP: six subjects, results May session mostly, released early July, graded one to seven each.
MYP: eight subject groups, four criteria A to D out of eight, converted to one to seven.
MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional; each school decides whether to offer it.
PYP has no external examinations; the final year builds towards the PYP exhibition instead.
TOK and the Extended Essay add up to three points beyond the six DP subjects.

contentBlocks.heading: Command Terms, Papers and Components: What Each Subject's Exam Actually Tests
contentBlocks.body:
Command terms decide how deep an answer needs to go, and mixing them up costs marks even when the underlying knowledge is correct. "Describe" asks for a detailed account with no justification; "explain" needs a reason or mechanism; "evaluate" and "discuss" want a weighed judgement, evidence on more than one side, not a one-line opinion. Exam tuition drills this directly: give a student a command term cold and time how long it takes them to name what kind of answer it demands, then repeat until the gap disappears.

For IB Mathematics, the split between Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI) also decides how a student should be spending exam-prep hours, since AA leans on algebraic proof technique while AI leans on modelling and technology use; calculator and non-calculator papers additionally demand separate timed practice, since a student fast on a calculator paper is not automatically fast without one. For Physics, Chemistry and Biology, past papers matter less for content revision at this stage and more for timing: how long a six-mark "evaluate" question should actually take against the clock, and where a student is consistently losing minutes rereading a question rather than answering it.

For English A and English B, exam tuition in the final weeks shifts toward timed practice under the same conditions as the real paper, not further content study; a student who knows the texts well but has never timed a full paper is often surprised by how little time remains for the final section. Across every subject, past papers and mark schemes are the actual material of exam tuition, not a supplement to it: a session built around one full past paper, marked properly and discussed line by line, teaches more in ninety minutes than a week of passive revision.

The mock result itself matters less than what it reveals: which papers are strong, which command terms are being consistently misread, and how much time genuinely remains before May. A student who mocks well can often step exam tuition down to targeted gap-filling; a student who mocks poorly needs the opposite, a fuller weekly commitment, and needs it decided in the first week after the mock, not drifted into over a month of hoping things improve on their own.

Past papers, mark schemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels and show exactly how marks were awarded on real scripts; exam tuition should be built directly around these, not around a tutor's memory of how marking "usually" goes. contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: What Works Best in the Final Weeks?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the default for exam tuition in Gurgaon for a practical reason: timed practice is easier to run properly in person, where a tutor can see a student's actual pacing on paper, not just a final typed or photographed answer. A tutor sitting across the table can also interrupt a wasted three minutes on a question a student is clearly stuck on, something harder to catch reliably over a screen with any lag at all.

Online sessions earn their place in exam season too, and IB online tuition Gurgaon families use it most often for two reasons: access to a specialist tutor for one difficult paper who does not otherwise work a family's corridor, or a fixed slot that a corridor's evening traffic keeps threatening in the final stretch. A shared screen with a past paper and a visible timer covers most of what timed practice needs; what it loses is the tutor's direct view of handwriting speed and physical exam stamina, which matters more for a three-hour DP paper than a shorter MYP assessment.

Hybrid is common by the final six weeks, and for good reason: a family might keep home sessions for full timed past papers, where in-person pacing matters most, and move quick command-term drills or a single weak topic to a short online session that does not need a whole evening blocked out. Neither format is a downgrade from the other in exam season; the honest trade-off is that home protects pacing observation and online protects the schedule when travel becomes the bottleneck, and a family under time pressure should pick based on which risk is more dangerous for their child specifically.

Online: access to a specialist for one weak paper regardless of corridor.

contentBlocks.heading: How Are IB Exam Tutors in Gurgaon Verified?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram checks every tutor's subject, programme and board background, and exam-session experience specifically, before a profile reaches a family; a tutor who has taught the syllabus generally is not automatically one who has run focused exam tuition against a countdown before. This is the baseline check, done before the family ever sees a name. An ib exam tuition near me search usually means the family wants to start this week, not next month, and the checks above are why that first shortlist can still be trusted rather than rushed blind.

What a family should check themselves is slightly different in exam season to ordinary tuition. Ask which past papers and mark schemes the tuition plan will actually use, current ones from the school or the IB's own channels, not a tutor's private archive of uncertain age. Ask how the tutor plans to use the mock result: which papers get more time, which command terms get drilled, and by when a second checkpoint is planned. Ask, plainly, how a wasted or slow session in the final weeks gets caught and corrected, since there is less time in exam season to notice a plan quietly not working.

contentBlocks.heading: The Six-Week Countdown to the IB Exam Session
contentBlocks.body:
A countdown plan works backwards from the exam date, not forwards from where the syllabus happens to be. Once the mock result is in, exam tuition should identify, within the first week, which two or three papers or components carry the most marks left to recover, and build the remaining weeks around those first, not around whichever topic feels most comfortable to revise. A weak paper ignored until three weeks out rarely recovers fully in that time; the same weeks spent earlier usually would have been enough.

Past papers and mark schemes are the actual curriculum of this stretch, not a supplement to lessons. The pattern that works: attempt a full paper or a substantial section under timed conditions, mark it properly against the real scheme, then spend the following session only on what the marking revealed, not on a general re-teach of the topic. A student who scores five out of eight on a criterion needs to know specifically why the other three were lost, not simply told to practise more.

Command terms and timing under pressure deserve dedicated drilling separate from content revision. A student can know a topic cold and still lose marks by writing a "describe" answer where "evaluate" was asked for, or by running out of time on the final question because the first two took too long. Timed drills, ten minutes on a single command term across several past questions, catch this faster than another full past paper attempt.

The final six weeks change the mix rather than the intensity. Earlier weeks can still introduce new content or fill genuine knowledge gaps; the final six weeks should be almost entirely timed practice, review of marked scripts, and command-term drilling, with new content kept to the smallest gaps that remain. A tutor still teaching fresh topics in week two before the exam is usually behind the plan, not ahead of it.

contentBlocks.heading: What Real Exam Progress Looks Like Between Mocks and Finals
contentBlocks.body:
Progress between a mock and the final session rarely looks like a clean upward line; it looks like specific, marked gains on specific papers, some weeks faster than others. A student might move from losing marks on every "evaluate" question to losing marks on only the hardest ones within two or three weeks of focused drilling, while a genuinely weak paper takes the full six weeks to close even partway. Both are normal, and a tutor who cannot point to which specific gap closed and which is still open is not tracking progress closely enough for exam season. Comparing options for IB tuitions in Gurgaon in exam season, this is the single clearest sign of a plan that is actually working, more than any single mark.

Timelines are tighter here than in ordinary tuition, and that is worth saying plainly rather than softening. Six weeks is enough to fix a timing problem, a command-term misreading, or a single weak component; it is rarely enough to build genuinely new subject fluency from a low base, and a family starting exam-specific tuition very late should be told this honestly rather than sold false reassurance. No tutor can guarantee a grade, in exam season or otherwise, and any promise to the contrary is worth walking away from.

There are real limits worth naming too. A tutor cannot compensate for a student who has not slept properly through the exam season, and exam-season pressure sometimes needs a conversation about workload and rest as much as another past paper. A tutor also cannot fix a gap that needed addressing a full term earlier; exam tuition narrows what is fixable to what the remaining weeks genuinely allow, and an honest tutor says so rather than promising everything is still recoverable.

What IB Gram commits to is a verified, matched tutor, a trial before committing, and a different match if the first is not working, subject to availability and how many weeks remain.

The first session itself is usually built around one past-paper question or a short section, worked and marked live, so both the tutor and family can see the actual gap rather than guess at it from a report card. faqs.question: How many sessions a week does exam tuition need in the final six weeks?
faqs.answer: Most families move to three or four sessions a week in the final six weeks, up from the usual one or two earlier in the term. The exact number depends on how many papers still need work and how the mock result split marks across components; a student weak on only one paper may need fewer, more targeted sessions rather than simply more hours. Frequency should be reviewed roughly every two weeks against progress on marked past papers, not fixed at the start and left unchanged, since a plan that is working can sometimes hold steady while one that is not needs adjusting quickly, given how little time is left.

faqs.question: How should we use past papers properly, not just attempt them?
faqs.answer: A past paper should be attempted under real timed conditions, marked against the actual scheme, and then discussed specifically for what was lost, not simply completed and filed away. The value is almost entirely in the marking and the follow-up session, not in the attempt itself; a student who does ten papers without proper marking often repeats the same errors ten times. It helps to keep a running note of which command terms or paper sections recur as weak points across several papers, since a pattern across three papers matters more than one bad result on a single attempt.

faqs.question: What changes in the tuition plan after a poor mock result?
faqs.answer: The plan should shift within the first week after a mock, prioritising whichever two or three papers or components lost the most recoverable marks. A poor mock is not a verdict on the exam; it is data, and the honest response is to rebuild the remaining weeks around what it actually showed rather than continuing the original plan unchanged. This sometimes means dropping planned new content entirely in favour of targeted drilling on the weakest areas, even if that content was scheduled weeks ago, because six weeks is not enough time to do everything a full syllabus review would ideally cover.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travel to Sadar Bazar or Civil Lines in Old Gurgaon on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Yes, home tutoring reaches Sadar Bazar, Civil Lines and the wider Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar corridor on weekday evenings, subject to tutor availability. This is a denser, older part of the city with narrower internal roads, so sharing clear landmark directions for a first visit, rather than relying on a map pin alone, usually saves a delayed start. Once a tutor has visited once, a regular weekly slot in exam season tends to run reliably, and if a specific evening genuinely will not work because of traffic or timing, the session can move online rather than being lost entirely.

faqs.question: Does exam tuition work if we start with only six weeks left?
faqs.answer: Yes, though what six weeks can realistically fix is narrower than what a full term allows. A timing problem, a misread command term, or one specific weak paper can usually be addressed properly in that window; building genuinely new subject fluency from a low base cannot, and an honest tutor says so directly rather than promising a full turnaround. Starting late still beats not starting at all, provided the plan targets the two or three highest-value gaps immediately rather than trying to cover the whole syllabus in the time remaining.

faqs.question: Can exam tuition run at home near Dwarka Expressway, or is online better there?
faqs.answer: Yes, home exam tuition runs across the Dwarka Expressway corridor, including the sectors and societies here, subject to tutor availability for that specific evening slot. Parts of this corridor are still developing their road network, so travel time on a weekday evening can vary more than the map distance suggests, which is worth building a buffer around rather than discovering on the first visit. Where a slot genuinely cannot be guaranteed reliably, some families move weekday home sessions online and keep weekend timed-paper practice at home, which protects both the countdown and the routine.

faqs.question: What if there is no improvement after two weeks of exam tuition?
faqs.answer: Two weeks is often too early to expect visible movement in marks, though it is a fair point to raise with the tutor rather than assume the plan is failing. Ask specifically which past papers have been marked and what pattern the marking shows, since a shift in error type, fewer timing losses, better command-term reading, usually appears before an overall score does. If genuinely nothing has changed after two full weeks of consistent, timed sessions, IB Gram can arrange a different tutor immediately, since exam season leaves little room to wait and see for much longer than that.

faqs.question: How do command terms actually get drilled in a session?
faqs.answer: Command terms are drilled by isolating them from content: giving a student a term cold, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, and timing how quickly they can name the depth of answer it needs, before ever writing a full response. This is then applied directly to a real past question, comparing the student's answer against how the mark scheme actually rewarded depth, not just correctness. Repeating this across several questions and several command terms over a week or two usually closes the gap faster than another full past paper attempt on its own.

faqs.question: What if the current tutor is not working out this close to the exam?
faqs.answer: A different tutor can still be arranged close to the exam; a mismatch costs more time the longer it continues, so raising it immediately matters more in exam season than it does earlier in the year. IB Gram treats a late-stage replacement as urgent rather than routine, prioritising a fast handover with whatever marked scripts and progress notes already exist so the new tutor does not start from zero. This is not an ideal position to be in with weeks remaining, but persisting with a tutor who clearly is not working is the worse option.

faqs.question: Does online exam tuition really work as well as home sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most of what exam tuition in the final weeks needs, though it suits some tasks better than others. Marking a past paper on a shared screen with a visible timer works well, and IB online tuition Gurgaon families use in exam season often see little difference from a home session for this. What online loses is a tutor's direct view of handwriting pace and physical exam stamina, which matters more for a full three-hour DP paper attempt than for shorter, targeted drilling sessions, so many families keep full timed papers at home and move quicker drills online.

faqs.question: Switching from CBSE or ICSE mid-year: does exam tuition still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the first session or two need to check specifically how the student's existing exam skills translate, since CBSE and ICSE assessment style differs from IB command terms and criterion-based marking even when subject content overlaps. A student switching boards close to an exam session needs this checked immediately rather than assumed, since time lost to a mismatched approach is harder to recover with only weeks remaining. Once the gap is identified, exam tuition proceeds the same way as for any other student: past papers, marked properly, against the real scheme the exam actually uses.

faqs.question: What should we prepare before the first exam tuition session?
faqs.answer: Bring the most recent mock paper and its mark if one exists, along with any past papers already attempted and the school's remaining assessment timetable. This lets the first session start on real evidence of where marks were lost, rather than a general impression of needing more practice, and saves a session that would otherwise be spent rediscovering what a marked script already shows. If no mock has happened yet, bring the most recent graded classwork instead; the first session can still identify a starting point without a formal mock in hand.

Booking IGCSE exam tuition in Gurgaon usually starts with one specific date: the Cambridge or Edexcel session your child is entered for. IB Gram asks for that date first, then works backwards from it rather than starting with a generic tutor profile search. Among the many IGCSE tuitions in Gurgaon on offer, this exam-specific kind is judged mostly by how precisely it targets the student's actual gaps. The process itself is simple:

What separates this from a generic revision booking is the specificity of that first conversation. A tutor excellent at building long-term study habits across a full year may not be the right fit for a family six weeks from May/June needing dense, targeted past-paper work; IB Gram asks directly which kind of support a family actually wants, rather than assuming exam tuition and ordinary tuition are interchangeable.

Home sessions are the usual starting point, since a tutor sitting beside a student with a marked script in front of both of them catches timing problems, blank spaces left under pressure, an answer abandoned halfway, that a phone call about grades never would. contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel Exam Series: Working Backwards From Your Session Date
contentBlocks.body:
Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana families preparing for IGCSE exams are usually working toward one of several fixed windows, and knowing exactly which one changes the whole revision plan. Cambridge IGCSE exam series run in February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June instead. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon working toward the October/November series is planning a very different calendar from an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Gurugram working toward January, even for the same subject.

Grading matters just as much for how revision is prioritised. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G, with some subjects offered as 9-1 versions under separate codes; Edexcel International GCSE grades everything 9-1. Core tier tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*, and this tier decision, made by the school, determines which past papers are even worth practising; drilling Extended-only questions with a Core-entered student wastes revision time neither family nor tutor can afford this close to the session.

The two-year structure means exam tuition can start earlier than families often assume. An IGCSE Grade 9 and 10 tutor working exam tuition specifically should apply the same past-paper discipline at both stages: a Grade 9 student sitting their first proper mock in the spring benefits from the same timed-practice approach as a Grade 10 student six weeks from the real thing, just applied at lower stakes and with more room to experiment with technique before it actually counts. Waiting until Grade 10 to introduce timed practice for the first time is one of the more common and avoidable mistakes families make.

contentBlocks.heading: Command Terms, Papers and Mark Schemes: What the Exam Actually Rewards
contentBlocks.body:
Revision that ignores how a subject is actually marked wastes hours a family this close to an exam does not have. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, splits Core candidates across Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), and Extended candidates across Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator); Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) runs Foundation or Higher tier with two calculator papers each. Exam tuition for Maths should drill the non-calculator paper separately and deliberately, since students who are strong on a calculator often lose easy method marks the moment the calculator is taken away.

Sciences add a weighting problem most students never think about until exam tuition points it out. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, examined from 2023, weight multiple choice (Paper 1 Core, Paper 2 Extended) at 30%, theory (Paper 3 Core, Paper 4 Extended) at 50%, and practical assessment through Paper 5 or Paper 6 at 20%, chosen by the school. A student who spends the final six weeks only reviewing theory content while ignoring the practical paper's command words, describe, explain, evaluate, each demanding a different kind of answer, is leaving a fifth of the marks under-revised. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered and assess practical skills inside the written papers directly.

Command terms deserve their own attention in any exam tuition programme, because a student can know the content and still lose marks by answering the wrong kind of question. State wants a fact, no explanation needed; explain wants a mechanism, the how or why; evaluate wants a judgement weighed against evidence. Across these schools, the internal mock exam is usually the single biggest signal a family gets before the real Cambridge or Edexcel session, and exam tuition should be built around it deliberately. A mock result four to eight weeks before the actual exam is close enough to the real thing to be genuinely diagnostic, and far enough out that a focused revision push can still change the outcome. Treating the mock as a dress rehearsal rather than a final verdict, and using its marked script line by line to decide what the remaining weeks of tuition actually cover, is one of the clearest ways exam tuition earns its keep.

Term timing around the mock varies school to school, but the pattern is broadly the same: a mock in the weeks before a winter or spring break, followed by a stretch where school-set homework tapers off and the calendar genuinely opens up for concentrated revision. An exam tutor who knows this pattern will front-load intensive past-paper work into that gap rather than spreading it evenly across the term, since an evenly spread revision schedule usually just means the busiest school weeks get skipped anyway.

The stretch of the calendar in the final six weeks before the actual session is different again: school teaching largely winds down toward revision itself, and exam tuition's job shifts from teaching technique to maintaining it under increasing time pressure, full past papers under strict timing, rather than topic-by-topic drilling.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Revision Sessions, Online or Hybrid: Which Wins in the Final Weeks?
contentBlocks.body:
Home revision sessions are IB Gram's usual starting point for exam tuition, because sitting beside a student with an actual marked script in front of both people catches things a phone call about a grade never would: an answer abandoned halfway through under time pressure, handwriting that gets worse as the clock runs down, a habit of re-reading the same question three times instead of moving on. For families in Gurgaon weighing home, online and hybrid revision in the final weeks, honesty about trade-offs matters more than ever, since there is less time left to recover from the wrong choice.

Home sessions win on reading a student's actual exam behaviour under pressure, since a tutor watching in real time sees hesitation, rushed working, or a question skipped entirely in a way a submitted PDF does not show. They lose on flexibility in exam season specifically, when a tutor working several students across one corridor has less room to shift a slot at short notice. IGCSE online tuition in Gurgaon wins on access to a genuine subject specialist regardless of where they live in the city, which matters more in the final weeks when a student needs someone who knows this exact syllabus's mark scheme cold, not just a generalist. It loses some of that real-time read on exam behaviour, though a shared screen with a timer still shows a great deal. Self-study with past papers, done well, is not nothing either: a student working alone through a paper under timed conditions builds genuine stamina, but without someone checking the marking against the real scheme, a student can walk away confident about an answer that would actually have scored zero.

For most families, the practical answer in the final six weeks is hybrid: home sessions for full past papers under real timing, with a shorter online check-in mid-week to review what came up as recurring errors and keep them from repeating for the next attempt.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Check an Exam Tutor Actually Knows This Syllabus?
contentBlocks.body:
How you check an exam tutor actually knows this syllabus, rather than just the subject in general, is worth more scrutiny than most families give it, especially this close to an exam session. IB Gram verifies a tutor's subject and syllabus background and confirms recent experience with the current version before a profile is shortlisted, which rules out a tutor who last taught a syllabus five specification changes ago.

Beyond that baseline, the trial session itself is the real test. Hand the tutor a past paper question your child has already attempted and ask them to mark it live, out loud, against the actual scheme, not from memory of roughly what examiners want. A tutor who is genuinely current with this board will reference specific mark scheme language, method marks, own-figure rule, specific command term expectations, without hesitation. One who is not will speak in vague terms about showing more working or writing more detail without pointing at anything concrete in the actual answer.

It is also fair to ask directly how many students on this exact tier and syllabus a tutor has taken through to the exam session recently, and what typically goes wrong for students at this stage. A tutor who has genuinely done this before will have specific, sometimes slightly uncomfortable answers, common careless errors, a particular paper students underperform on, rather than reassuring generalities. This is not about certificates, though a workshop certificate or subject qualification is a reasonable thing to ask to see; it is about whether the tutor can demonstrate, in front of you, that they know exactly what this specific exam rewards.

For a home tutor arriving in these final weeks, it remains reasonable to confirm identification before the first visit, particularly if this is a new match rather than a continuing relationship, and to have someone else home for that first session.

contentBlocks.heading: How Many Weeks Out Should Revision Really Intensify?
contentBlocks.body:
How many weeks out revision should really intensify depends on the subject and the student, but a rough shape holds across most IGCSE exam tuition: eight to ten weeks out, the focus is still mixed, closing content gaps alongside the first full past papers under loosely timed conditions. Six weeks out, content should be essentially covered, and the split shifts firmly toward timed practice with detailed marking after each attempt, not just a score. In the final two to three weeks, the work becomes almost entirely paper-based: full papers under strict exam timing, careful review of exactly where marks were lost, and short, targeted drilling of whatever error keeps recurring rather than a broad re-teach of the whole topic.

Past papers and mark schemes, used properly, are the backbone of this whole countdown, and used properly is doing real work in that sentence. Attempting a paper without marking it against the real scheme afterward teaches almost nothing; a student can walk away from an unmarked paper feeling confident about an answer that would have scored a third of the marks. The useful sequence is: attempt under real time pressure, mark line by line against the actual scheme, identify the pattern in what was lost, not enough working shown, a command term misread, timing that ran out on the last question, then drill that specific pattern before the next full paper. Working through ten unmarked papers teaches a student less than working through three papers marked this carefully.

What changes in the final six weeks is not the content, which should largely be settled by then, but the discipline: timing under pressure becomes the main thing being trained. A student who knows every fact but has never practised finishing a paper with five minutes to spare for checking is at a real disadvantage against one who has drilled that exact skill, however well the content itself is known. Exam tuition in these final weeks differs from ordinary tuition precisely here: it is less about teaching anything new and almost entirely about performance under the conditions of the actual session.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should Change Between the Mock Result and the Final Paper?
contentBlocks.body:
Parents reasonably want to know what should actually change between a disappointing mock and the real exam a few weeks later, and the honest answer is specific, not a vague promise of improvement. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any exam tutor implying otherwise after seeing one mock script should be treated with real caution. What a family can reasonably expect to see is narrower and more checkable: the same category of error, the same command term misread, the same paper section rushed, showing up less often across successive timed attempts, and a student able to explain, in their own words, what specifically went wrong on the mock rather than a general sense of having done badly.

A mock is one data point, taken under conditions that are not always identical to the real exam, an unfamiliar invigilator, a different room, a week the student was unwell, so a single disappointing result should prompt analysis before panic. The mark scheme itself, gone through question by question with the tutor, usually tells a more precise story than the overall grade does: a student might have lost most marks in one specific paper or topic area rather than uniformly across the whole exam, which changes what the remaining weeks should actually focus on. Parents sometimes search for the best igcse exam tuition in Gurgaon, but with weeks left before an exam, the more useful question is whether a specific tutor can demonstrate current, specific knowledge of this exact syllabus, not a general reputation.

It is fair to expect an exam tutor to be honest about what is realistically achievable in the time left. A student six weeks from the session with several large content gaps is not going to close all of them and also build strong timed-exam technique; a good tutor says which one to prioritise rather than promising both. And if a mock result shows no meaningful improvement across two or three subsequent practice papers despite consistent tuition, that is worth a direct conversation with IB Gram rather than continuing the same approach and hoping the final paper is different.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the exam should we start exam tuition?
faqs.answer: Eight to ten weeks out is a reasonable point to shift from ordinary tuition into a dedicated exam tuition pattern, since that leaves enough time to close remaining content gaps and still build real timed-practice stamina before the session. Starting later, four to five weeks out, is still worth doing and can meaningfully help, but the work becomes narrower: mostly timed papers and pattern-specific error correction rather than broader content review. Starting right after a poor mock result, whenever that falls in the calendar, is usually the more useful trigger than counting weeks on its own, since the mock tells you specifically what still needs the time.

faqs.question: What should a good exam tutor do in the first session?
faqs.answer: A good exam tutor's first session is diagnostic, not instructional: working through a recent past paper or mock script with the student to see exactly where marks were lost, not assuming the whole syllabus needs equal attention. This usually means going question by question through a marked or attempted paper, checking whether errors are content gaps, misread command terms, or timing problems, before deciding what the remaining sessions should focus on. If a tutor's first session jumps straight into teaching a topic without this diagnostic step, it is fair to ask why, since a plan built without evidence is really just a guess about where the time will be best spent.

faqs.question: What if the mock result was much worse than expected?
faqs.answer: A mock significantly below expectations is worth treating as information rather than a verdict: go through the marked script question by question with the tutor to see whether the marks were lost broadly across the whole paper or concentrated in one topic or paper section, since the two call for very different responses in the weeks left. Conditions on the day, an unfamiliar room, feeling unwell, unusually high anxiety, can also genuinely affect a mock result without reflecting the student's real level, though this should be treated as a possible factor rather than an excuse to avoid the diagnostic work. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a specific, evidence-based plan built from that mock script is usually more useful than either panic or dismissing the result.

faqs.question: How does IB Gram verify a tutor knows the current syllabus version?
faqs.answer: IB Gram checks a tutor's subject and syllabus background and confirms recent teaching experience with the current specification before a profile is shortlisted for exam tuition specifically, since syllabuses do change and a tutor working from an outdated version can teach the wrong emphasis confidently. Beyond that, the trial session is the clearest check available to a parent: ask the tutor to mark a real past-paper answer live and explain their reasoning against the actual scheme, method marks, command term expectations, rather than a general impression of what examiners want. A tutor who cannot do this specifically and confidently for the exact syllabus code your child sits is not the right match for this final stretch.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start exam tuition three weeks before the exam?
faqs.answer: It is late, but rarely too late to help. Three weeks out, exam tuition usually narrows to full timed papers, careful marking, and drilling whatever specific error pattern is losing the most marks, rather than any broader content review, since there simply is not time for that anymore. A tutor should be honest at this stage about what is realistically achievable: modest, targeted gains in specific papers or question types are a fair goal, and a tutor promising a dramatic overall transformation in three weeks is overselling what any amount of tuition can do this close to the date.

faqs.answer: Yes, Sohna Road, from Sector 47 through Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City and Badshahpur, is a corridor IB Gram regularly matches exam tutors across, though evening traffic here can be heavier than in other parts of the city, so families booking exam-season sessions on this stretch generally do better confirming a slightly wider time window rather than a fixed exact hour. Booking the final weeks' schedule two to three weeks ahead, rather than session by session, tends to hold up better against this corridor's congestion than trying to arrange each week separately as the exam approaches.

faqs.question: Can online exam tuition really replace in-person sessions in the final weeks?
faqs.answer: It can work well for some students, particularly for reaching a specific syllabus specialist quickly this late in the term, but it depends on what the student still needs most. A student mainly needing timed papers marked and technique corrected does this well on a screen, since the marked script itself carries most of the useful information regardless of format. A student who tends to lose focus or rush under pressure in ways that are hard to see through a camera often benefits from at least some in-person sessions in these final weeks, where a tutor can see hesitation and body language a screen may miss.

faqs.question: What if there is no improvement between practice papers?
faqs.answer: If two or three consecutive timed papers show no real improvement in the same error category despite consistent tuition, that is a signal worth acting on rather than continuing unchanged and hoping the actual exam goes differently. Sometimes the fix is a change in approach, more focused drilling on one specific weakness rather than full papers every time; sometimes it is a different tutor whose explanation style finally makes something click. No tutor can guarantee a grade, but a tutor should be able to explain clearly why the current plan is not moving the needle and propose a specific change, rather than simply repeating the same pattern of timed papers and hoping for a different result.

heroTitle: What Sets an IB Tutor's Fee in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: This page explains every factor that genuinely moves an IB tutor's fee in Gurgaon, from programme stage to subject scarcity to session format, and how pricing is usually structured. No figures are quoted; the focus is on what to ask so you can judge whether a fee is worth paying.
introSummary: IB tutor fees in Gurgaon are rarely a single number a tutor quotes and a parent accepts; the honest answer to what shapes them lies in a handful of factors that change from one family's request to the next, starting with home tutoring itself, since a tutor travelling to your home in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana factors in something a purely online specialist does not. Programme stage, subject scarcity, a tutor's board-specific experience, session length, and whether coursework guidance is involved each pull the fee up or down, and understanding how these factors interact matters more than chasing the lowest number quoted on a phone call. This page sets out those factors in order of how much they actually move a fee, explains how pricing is typically structured, per session, monthly or as a package, and gives you the questions that separate a fair fee from a warning sign, whether a fee looks suspiciously low or unusually high.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds Your Gurgaon Shortlist Before Any Fee Is Discussed
contentBlocks.body:
IB tutor fees in Gurgaon come up later in the conversation with IB Gram, not first, and that order is deliberate. Talking about a fee before the actual need is understood usually produces a number that has nothing to do with your child, so the first step is simply describing what you need: the grade, the programme stage, the subject, and roughly what has been going wrong.

From there, you are asked more specific questions: which syllabus and level, whether the subject sits at Higher Level or Standard Level, how the school's calendar is running, which sector or society you are in, and what slot actually works around school, buses and activities. Each of these answers shapes which tutors even belong on your shortlist, because a Higher Level Mathematics specialist with Internal Assessment experience is simply a different tutor, doing different work, from someone teaching a broad MYP subject set, and their fees reflect that difference honestly rather than arbitrarily.

Only once the shortlist is built does a fee conversation make sense, and even then, it is framed around a demo or trial session first. You see how the tutor actually works before any payment is agreed for ongoing lessons, and if the fit is wrong, you are free to ask for a different match. Lessons then run at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability and depending on level and schedule, and the format you choose is itself one of the levers on the final fee, covered later on this page.

2. IB Gram asks about programme stage, level, school calendar, location and schedule.
3. A shortlist is built from tutors whose verified experience actually matches that need.
4. A demo or trial session happens before any ongoing fee is agreed.
5. You can ask for a different match if the fit is not right.

contentBlocks.heading: Programme Stage: The Biggest Lever on an IB Tutor's Fee
contentBlocks.body:
More than any other single factor, which IB stage your child is in decides what kind of tutor you need, and that decides the fee more than anything discussed later on this page. The Primary Years Programme, for ages three to twelve, is built around six transdisciplinary themes, who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organize ourselves, and sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry with no external examinations at all. A PYP tutor is usually generalist, supporting a theme or a skill, and fees at this stage tend to sit lower simply because the specialism required is narrower.

The Middle Years Programme, five years across MYP 1 to 5, ages roughly eleven to sixteen, introduces criterion-based marking: every subject assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored zero to eight, converting through the IB's own grade boundaries to a final one-to-seven grade. A tutor here needs to understand how a criterion total actually becomes a grade, and that specific knowledge, plus guiding the Personal Project in MYP 5 or the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, is worth more to a family than general subject teaching, which shows in the fee.

The Diploma Programme carries the highest fees on average, and for good reason. Two years, six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours, the rest at Standard Level with 150, grading one to seven per subject, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to three more points toward a maximum of 45, with 24 the minimum for the diploma subject to failing conditions, and Creativity, Activity, Service running alongside all of it. A DP2 tutor, working close to the May exam session, is usually the most experienced and therefore the most expensive tutor a family hires across the whole IB journey, and that expense reflects genuinely higher stakes, not simply a higher list price.
items: PYP tutoring is usually generalist; no external exams mean lower specialism, lower fees.
MYP tutors need to understand criterion A-D marking and grade boundary conversion.
MYP Personal Project sits in MYP 5, Community Project in MYP 3 or 4.
DP Higher Level, 240 recommended hours, typically commands the highest fees of any stage.
DP2, closest to the May session, usually needs the most experienced tutor available.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Subjects Command a Higher Fee, and Why?
contentBlocks.body:
Subject scarcity is the second biggest factor after programme stage, and it works exactly the way it sounds: fewer tutors genuinely qualified in a subject means each one can reasonably charge more, because demand simply outstrips supply. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each offered at Higher Level or Standard Level with distinct calculator and non-calculator components, and a tutor who can teach AA HL well, including the harder algebraic and proof-based content, is rarer and therefore priced higher than one comfortable only with AI SL.

The sciences add another layer: IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology all carry Internal Assessment components marked against specific criteria, and a tutor who has actually marked or examined against those criteria, not just taught the content, is worth a genuine premium. This is where a tutor's experience matters as much as the subject itself; someone with examining or moderating experience for the IB understands exactly how marks are awarded in a way that content knowledge alone does not replicate, and that experience is one of the clearest reasons a fee sits higher than a general tutor's.

IB English A and B, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay round out the picture differently. English A's literary analysis and English B's language acquisition focus call for different specialists entirely, while TOK and EE guidance, both marked against structured criteria and real word limits, are often billed separately from subject tuition because they demand a distinct kind of coaching, closer to academic mentoring than content teaching. Command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss, to what extent, run through every subject and every fee conversation, since a tutor who teaches students to read these correctly is doing work that pays for itself across every paper the student sits.

contentBlocks.heading: The Gurgaon School Calendar You Should Know Before Agreeing a Fee
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families across Gurgaon deal with international school calendars that share a broad shape even though each school sets its own exact dates: a long first term, internal assessments and unit tests spread through the year, DP2 mock examinations set several months ahead of the May session, and results released in early July for the students who sat that session. Most Gurgaon IB schools use May; a minority use November, along with retake candidates.

This calendar affects fees in a way families often miss: a tutor asked to start two weeks before a mock, with no prior relationship with the student, is doing compressed, high-pressure work, and a fee that reflects urgency is not automatically an inflated one. The fairer comparison is a tutor engaged from early in the term, who can pace sessions around the calendar rather than cramming against it, and whose fee, session for session, is doing calmer, more sustainable work even if the total spent across the year ends up similar.

Past papers, markschemes and subject reports, available through the school or the IB's official channels, matter to a fee conversation too. A tutor who already works from your child's actual school markscheme, rather than a generic bank of questions, is paying for that familiarity in preparation time before the first session even happens, and that upfront work is a reasonable part of what a considered fee reflects.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Which Format Justifies Which Fee?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition typically carries the highest fee of the three formats, and travel is only part of why. A home tutor gives your child their full, undivided attention in a familiar setting, sees handwriting and working habits directly, and for a younger PYP or MYP student, that physical presence often does more for confidence and routine than a screen session ever could. Home classes also remove the burden of getting a tired student somewhere else on a school night, which is worth something even if it is hard to price precisely.

Online tutoring is usually priced lower, and the reason is straightforward: no travel time means a tutor can see more students in an evening, which brings the per-family fee down even for the same specialist. It also opens access to a much wider pool, a DP2 student needing a scarce Higher Level specialist is far more likely to find the right fit online than by limiting the search to tutors willing to visit a specific sector, and that wider access is itself a form of value even before the fee is compared.

Hybrid tutoring blends the two by design rather than compromise: a family might choose home tuition for a younger child's foundational subjects, where presence matters most, and online sessions for a scarce DP specialist or a late evening slot a home visit could not fill. The honest trade-off is this: paying more for home tuition buys presence and routine, paying less for online buys access and flexibility, and neither is automatically the better-value choice. What justifies a given fee is whether the format actually matches what your child needs, not which one costs less on paper.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does IB Gram Verify Before You Ever Discuss a Fee in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is even shortlisted, IB Gram checks board experience, the level and subjects actually taught, and familiarity with the syllabus your child's school follows. This verification is the foundation a fee should sit on, but it is not the whole picture, and a family judging whether a quoted fee is fair should go further than trusting a verified profile alone.

Ask about the specific experience behind the fee: how many years teaching this exact subject at this exact level, whether the tutor has any examining or moderating background with the IB, and how many students they are currently teaching alongside your child, since a tutor spread too thin across many families may struggle to give the attention a higher fee implies. None of these questions are rude to ask; a tutor confident in their own value will answer them plainly.

Check practical things yourself too: whether the fee includes preparation time and feedback notes or covers only the session itself, whether coursework or Internal Assessment guidance is billed separately, and how rescheduling or a missed session is handled financially. Getting these details clear before the first paid session avoids the far more common and more expensive problem: a fee that seemed reasonable at the first call turning out to cover far less than the family assumed.

It also helps to ask how the tutor keeps track of progress between sessions, since a fee that includes short written notes after each lesson, however brief, is doing more for your child's continuity than one that offers nothing beyond the hour itself. A tutor who cannot describe how they will update you, roughly how often and through what channel, is not necessarily a bad tutor, but that gap is worth raising before the term begins rather than discovering it three sessions in, when the pattern is already set and harder to change without an awkward conversation.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Moves IB Tutor Fees in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Ranked roughly from biggest to smallest effect, five factors explain most of the variation in IB tutor fees across Gurgaon. Programme stage and level come first: a DP2 Higher Level subject close to the May session simply demands more from a tutor than an MYP subject or a PYP theme, and fees follow that demand honestly. Subject scarcity comes second: sciences with Internal Assessment guidance, Higher Level Mathematics, and coursework-heavy subjects like TOK and the Extended Essay are taught well by fewer tutors, and scarcity moves a fee regardless of how good a tutor's general teaching is.

A tutor's experience, third on this list, includes far more than years taught. Examining or moderating experience with the IB, familiarity with a specific school's scheme of work, and a track record with students at the same stage all justify a fee difference that raw years alone would not explain. Session length and format come fourth: a ninety-minute session naturally costs more than a sixty-minute one, and home tuition typically costs more than online for the travel reasons already covered, while a hybrid arrangement sits somewhere between the two depending on how the weeks are split. Coursework or Internal Assessment mentoring, when it is involved, is the fifth factor, and it is often billed as a distinct component because guiding a student through IA structure, TOK essay planning or Extended Essay research questions within academic integrity rules is genuinely different work from weekly subject tuition, closer to structured mentoring than content teaching.

How pricing is structured matters as much as what it reflects. Most tutors work on one of three models: a per-session fee paid as you go, a monthly fee covering an agreed number of sessions, or a package arrangement, often used for coursework mentoring or a concentrated pre-mock block. Each has a different trade-off: per-session offers flexibility but less commitment from the tutor's side, monthly billing suits a steady weekly routine, and packages suit a defined, time-bound need such as Extended Essay support in a single term. None of these structures is inherently better; the right one depends on whether your family needs flexibility or consistency more.

Red flags run in both directions. A fee that looks unusually low for a DP2 Higher Level subject close to mocks is worth questioning directly: ask about the tutor's actual experience at that level, whether Internal Assessment guidance is genuinely included, and how many students they are juggling at once, since an unsustainably low fee often means an unsustainable amount of the tutor's attention spread across too many families. A fee that looks unusually high deserves the same scrutiny in the other direction: ask what specifically justifies it, examining experience, a scarce subject, or genuinely tailored coursework mentoring, and be wary of a fee justified only by vague claims about quality rather than anything checkable. A fair fee is one a tutor can explain clearly in one or two sentences; one that cannot be explained plainly is worth questioning before you commit a term's budget to it.
items: 1. Programme stage and level: DP2 Higher Level close to mocks demands the most.
2. Subject scarcity: sciences with IA, HL Maths, TOK and EE guidance cost more.
3. Tutor experience: examining background and school-specific familiarity, not just years taught.
4. Session length and format: longer sessions and home visits typically cost more.
5. Coursework or IA mentoring: often billed separately as structured, distinct work.

contentBlocks.heading: Is This Fee Actually Worth It?
contentBlocks.body:
Judging value honestly means looking past the number itself and asking what changed for your child because of it. In the first few weeks, that looks small: fewer careless errors on a familiar question type, a student who can name the specific command term or criterion they missed rather than shrugging, homework that comes back more complete than before. These are not dramatic, but they are the earliest honest signal that a fee is buying something real.

By six to eight weeks, look for something more concrete: an Internal Assessment draft that addresses the criteria more directly than the first attempt, visibly better timing on a mock paper section, or simply a student who stops dreading a subject they used to avoid. If none of this has shifted and the fee has stayed the same regardless, that is a fair moment to ask the tutor directly what the plan actually is, and if the answer is vague, it is a legitimate reason to ask IB Gram for a different match.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a fee that comes with an implied promise of one should be treated with real caution rather than reassurance. What a fair fee buys is expertise, structure, and honest communication, not a result. A tutor who is upfront that a late start in an already crowded term will take longer to show progress is offering more real value for the same fee than one who promises a quick turnaround to win the booking, and that honesty is itself worth paying for.

If you are weighing home tuition against online, mention your sector, particularly if you are further out along a corridor like Southern Peripheral Road, since that honestly affects what a home visit will cost compared with an online alternative.

The first session should function as a genuine diagnostic, and what a fair fee buys becomes clearer once you have seen it: a tutor who reviews your child's actual work, explains where marks are being lost against real criteria, and leaves you with a specific plan rather than a vague impression. Lessons then run at home, online or hybrid depending on level, subject and schedule, subject to tutor availability, and if the fit or the fee does not feel right after that first honest look, you can ask IB Gram for a different match before committing a term's budget to it.
