faqs.question: What determines an IB tutor's fee in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Five things move it most: programme stage and level, subject scarcity, the tutor's experience including any examining background, session length and format, and whether coursework or Internal Assessment mentoring is involved. A DP2 Higher Level science close to mocks, taught by someone with examining experience, sits at one end; a PYP theme supported by a generalist tutor sits at the other. Rather than asking a tutor to quote a flat number, ask which of these factors apply to your child's actual situation, since that tells you far more about whether a fee is fair than the number alone.

faqs.question: Is DP tutoring more expensive than MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it reflects real differences in demand. The Diploma Programme's two years of six subjects, Higher Level content at 240 recommended teaching hours against Standard Level's 150, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments, calls for deeper subject and assessment expertise than most MYP tutoring, which spans a broader base of subjects assessed through the four A-D criteria. A DP2 tutor working close to the May session is typically the most experienced, and therefore the highest-fee tutor, a family hires across the whole IB journey.

faqs.question: Why do some tutors charge more for Internal Assessment guidance?
faqs.answer: Because IA guidance is different work from weekly subject tuition, closer to structured mentoring than content teaching. A tutor guiding an Internal Assessment needs to understand exactly how the assessment criteria are applied, help a student shape a research question or investigation that can actually score well, and review drafts against those criteria without crossing into doing the work for the student, which academic integrity rules do not allow. That combination of assessment literacy and careful boundary-setting is a genuine skill, separate from teaching content, and it is often billed as its own component for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: Is it normal for fees to be structured monthly rather than per session?
faqs.answer: Yes, monthly billing is common and suits a steady weekly routine, though per-session and package arrangements are equally normal depending on the need. Per-session fees offer flexibility if your schedule changes often; monthly billing suits a family committed to a regular weekly slot across a term; a package, often used for Extended Essay or Internal Assessment mentoring, suits a defined, time-bound piece of work. None of these structures is inherently better value, and a tutor should be able to explain clearly why they use the one they do.

faqs.question: Should I be worried if a quoted fee looks unusually low?
faqs.answer: It is worth questioning directly rather than assuming it is simply good value. Ask about the tutor's actual experience at the exact level and subject, whether Internal Assessment or coursework guidance is genuinely included or billed separately later, and how many other students they are teaching at the same time, since an unsustainably low fee often means attention spread too thin across too many families. A tutor confident in their own value will answer these questions plainly rather than deflecting them.

faqs.question: Should I be worried if a quoted fee looks unusually high?
faqs.answer: The same scrutiny applies in the other direction. Ask what specifically justifies the fee: examining or moderating experience with the IB, a genuinely scarce subject like Higher Level Mathematics or a science with Internal Assessment guidance, or tailored coursework mentoring rather than standard subject tuition. Be cautious of a fee justified mainly by vague claims about quality with nothing checkable behind them; a fair fee, high or low, is one a tutor can explain in one or two clear sentences.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor cost more in DLF Phase 3 than online?
faqs.answer: It can, though less than in corridors further from where most specialist tutors are based, since DLF Phase 3 and the surrounding Cyber City and MG Road area already have many tutors working nearby. The main driver is still travel time rather than the sector itself: a tutor already circulating through that corridor factors in relatively little extra travel, while online removes that component altogether regardless of where you live. If a quoted home fee feels high for this particular corridor, it is worth asking directly what travel time the tutor is actually accounting for.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Sushant Lok or the Southern Peripheral Road on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Most tutors serving Sushant Lok and South City can offer a fairly reliable weekday evening slot, since the corridor sits centrally enough for regular travel. Southern Peripheral Road, covering Sectors 66 to 70 and 72, sits further out, and evening traffic between corridors can stretch a short trip considerably, so a tutor willing to travel there regularly is often pricing in that time. Confirm the exact slot and travel expectation honestly during the trial conversation, before assuming a fee is comparable to a more central sector.

faqs.question: What happens if a home tuition session is missed?
faqs.answer: It should be rescheduled rather than simply lost, and this is worth agreeing with your tutor in the first week rather than after it happens. Ask whether a missed session is made up on a weekend, shifted to an online slot for that week, or handled differently, and get clarity on whether a missed session affects the fee for that period. A tutor who has no clear answer to this before the first session is worth asking about directly.

faqs.question: What should the free demo clarify before I agree to any fee?
faqs.answer: A useful demo shows how the tutor actually diagnoses a student's gaps, not just how they teach a topic. Watch for whether they review your child's recent graded work, explain a concept more than one way if the first attempt does not land, and end the session with a specific plan for the coming weeks rather than a vague impression that things went well. The demo is also the natural moment to ask directly what the ongoing fee includes: preparation time, written feedback, and how coursework guidance is handled, if relevant.

faqs.question: What if the tutor isn't working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Say so and ask IB Gram for a different match; that is a normal part of the arrangement and not something that needs lengthy justification. Give the first few weeks a fair chance, since early sessions are often diagnostic and slower than they later become, but if there is no clear plan and no change in how your child talks about the subject by six to eight weeks, raise it directly with the tutor, and switch if the conversation does not produce a real improvement.

None of these structures is inherently better value, and a tutor should be able to explain clearly why they use the one they do.

mainEntity.name: Should I be worried if a quoted fee looks unusually low?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is worth questioning directly rather than assuming it is simply good value. Ask about the tutor's actual experience at the exact level and subject, whether Internal Assessment or coursework guidance is genuinely included or billed separately later, and how many other students they are teaching at the same time, since an unsustainably low fee often means attention spread too thin across too many families. A tutor confident in their own value will answer these questions plainly rather than deflecting them.

mainEntity.name: Should I be worried if a quoted fee looks unusually high?

acceptedAnswer.text: The same scrutiny applies in the other direction. Ask what specifically justifies the fee: examining or moderating experience with the IB, a genuinely scarce subject like Higher Level Mathematics or a science with Internal Assessment guidance, or tailored coursework mentoring rather than standard subject tuition. Be cautious of a fee justified mainly by vague claims about quality with nothing checkable behind them; a fair fee, high or low, is one a tutor can explain in one or two clear sentences.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a home tuition session is missed?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should be rescheduled rather than simply lost, and this is worth agreeing with your tutor in the first week rather than after it happens. Ask whether a missed session is made up on a weekend, shifted to an online slot for that week, or handled differently, and get clarity on whether a missed session affects the fee for that period. A tutor who has no clear answer to this before the first session is worth asking about directly.

mainEntity.name: What should the free demo clarify before I agree to any fee?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful demo shows how the tutor actually diagnoses a student's gaps, not just how they teach a topic. Watch for whether they review your child's recent graded work, explain a concept more than one way if the first attempt does not land, and end the session with a specific plan for the coming weeks rather than a vague impression that things went well. The demo is also the natural moment to ask directly what the ongoing fee includes: preparation time, written feedback, and how coursework guidance is handled, if relevant.

mainEntity.name: What if the tutor isn't working out after a few weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so and ask IB Gram for a different match; that is a normal part of the arrangement and not something that needs lengthy justification. Give the first few weeks a fair chance, since early sessions are often diagnostic and slower than they later become, but if there is no clear plan and no change in how your child talks about the subject by six to eight weeks, raise it directly with the tutor, and switch if the conversation does not produce a real improvement.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match a tutor to a Gurgaon family before any fee is discussed?
contentBlocks.body:
IB tuition fees in Gurgaon only make sense once the match is right, so IB Gram starts with the specifics rather than a price list. You send a query or book a free consultation and describe the board, level, subject and what the school is currently covering; IB Gram then asks about the syllabus, school calendar, location and preferred schedule before anyone is shortlisted. Skipping this step, taking the first available tutor without describing the actual need, is one of the most common reasons a family later feels a fee was not worth it: the fee was fine, the fit was not.

From the details you give, IB Gram builds a shortlist of profiles that are verified and matched to the exact level and subject, not just the board in general. A DP Higher Level Physics request and an MYP 3 Individuals and Societies request are treated as genuinely different searches, because the tutor who suits one rarely suits the other equally well. Where more than one matching profile is available, the family sees options rather than a single name, which is also the point at which any difference in experience or session length between profiles becomes visible.

contentBlocks.heading: How the programme and stage shift what a fee reflects
contentBlocks.body:
Stage is usually the first thing that shifts a fee, because it changes what a tutor is actually being asked to do. The Primary Years Programme (PYP), for ages 3 to 12, has no external examinations; a tutor here is supporting units of inquiry built around six transdisciplinary themes, among them how the world works and sharing the planet, and helping the student build the ten attributes of the IB learner profile ahead of the PYP exhibition in the final year. This tends to be lighter, more general work than the stages above it, and fees reflect that difference in scope.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, across eight subject groups, and every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8 points, with the criterion total out of 32 converting to a final grade of 1 to 7. A tutor working at this stage needs to understand how criteria are worded, not just the subject content, which is a more specialised skill than general subject teaching and is usually priced accordingly. MYP 5 brings the Personal Project, and some schools run MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, as an optional addition the school itself decides on.

The Diploma Programme (DP), two years across DP1 and DP2, is where fee structures get most detailed. Six subjects from six groups, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adding up to 3 further points toward a maximum of 45 and 24 points as the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. A tutor teaching HL content, particularly close to the May exam session, is usually working at a level of depth that a general subject tutor cannot match, and that depth is one of the clearest drivers of fee difference between tutors.
items: PYP tutoring supports units of inquiry; there are no external exams to prepare for.
MYP fees reflect criterion-based marking skill, not just subject knowledge.
MYP 5 adds the Personal Project and, at some schools, optional eAssessment.
DP splits subjects into Higher Level and Standard Level, each priced differently for depth.

contentBlocks.heading: Why do some IB subjects cost more to tutor than others?
contentBlocks.body:
Subject scarcity is one of the biggest, least visible drivers of an IB tutor's fee in Gurgaon. IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) at Higher Level draws on a smaller pool of tutors who are comfortable with proof-based, multi-step questions than IB Mathematics Applications and Interpretation (AI) does, and that scarcity shows up in the fee even though both are the same subject on paper. The sciences, IB Physics, IB Chemistry and IB Biology, follow a similar pattern: a tutor who can teach the Higher Level paper components confidently, including data-based and extended-response questions, is rarer than one who can only support Standard Level content.

IB English A and English B sit apart because they are marked on argument and use of evidence against explicit criteria, not on correct grammar alone, which means a tutor's real skill is close reading and structured feedback on drafts rather than content delivery. Command terms such as define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent set how deep an answer needs to go, and a tutor who teaches students to read these correctly is doing something more specialised than reviewing content, which tends to be reflected in what they charge.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, worth up to 3 additional points toward the DP's 45, sit at the specialised end of the fee scale for a clear reason: genuinely useful help here usually comes from someone who has examined or moderated against IB criteria, not simply taught the subject. A tutor's examining or moderating experience is one of the clearest, most checkable signals of that depth, and it is worth asking about directly rather than assuming a strong subject background automatically covers TOK or EE guidance as well.

Location changes a fee mainly through travel, and Gurgaon's newer corridors sit at different distances from where many specialist tutors are already working. New Gurgaon, covering Sector 82 through Sector 90, Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, along with societies such as Vatika India Next and Godrej Air, is still filling in with international schools and tutors, so a family here searching for IB tuition fees in New Gurgaon may find fewer specialist options within a short travel radius than in more established parts of the city, which can push the fee for a very specific HL subject slightly higher purely on travel.

The Dwarka Expressway corridor, taking in Sector 102 through Sector 113 including Sector 104, 106, 108 and 110, with societies like Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, is growing fast, and the same logic applies: a tutor already living or working along that stretch will usually charge differently for travel than one crossing from the other side of Gurgaon on a weekday evening. Evening traffic on the expressway itself can stretch a short-looking trip on the map into a much longer one in practice.

Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, including Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar and Sectors 4, 14, 15, 22 and 23, is an older, denser part of the city where narrower roads and more built-up traffic can add time even over a short distance. A family here is often better served by a tutor who already knows the area's specific traffic patterns than by the nearest-looking tutor on a map. Across all three corridors, online tuition removes the travel variable from the fee question entirely, which is worth weighing seriously wherever a home visit adds meaningful travel time on top of the lesson itself.

contentBlocks.heading: The school calendar that shapes when fees rise in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Families at schools such as Pathways World School, Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and DPS International Edge across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana each work to a calendar set by their own school, and that calendar is a large part of why fees tend to rise and fall through the year rather than stay flat.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May exam session; a minority use November, along with candidates retaking a subject. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and demand for tutors tends to spike in the weeks before those mocks, which is when session length and frequency, not the base fee itself, most often change. May results are released in early July, and this is also when many families renegotiate or reconfirm arrangements for the coming academic year.

Command terms, past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's official channels, and a tutor who works closely from those rather than generic materials is, in effect, offering something a cheaper generic tutor cannot: alignment with exactly how the school's own assessments are marked. contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: how does the fee reasoning differ?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is where most Gurgaon families start, and for fee purposes it is worth understanding what you are actually paying for: a tutor's time including travel, full attention for the session length booked, and use of the student's own materials and study space. Home tutoring tends to carry the fullest fee of the formats discussed here because it bundles travel time and full undivided attention together, and for a PYP or early MYP student, or for a subject where a parent wants to observe part of a session, that bundle is usually worth it.

Online tuition removes travel from the equation, and fees here often reflect that: the tutor's time is spent entirely on teaching rather than partly on the road. It also opens access to a specialist tutor who may not be reachable for a home visit at all, which matters more for a less common HL subject, or for TOK and Extended Essay guidance, than for a well-covered subject like DP Mathematics AA. Shared whiteboards and annotated past papers work well for most content, though a student who needs someone physically present to stay engaged may not get full value from the lower travel overhead.

Hybrid arrangements, mostly home with occasional online sessions worked in around traffic, illness or a clashing school activity, let a family capture most of home tuition's benefit while keeping some of online's flexibility. The honest trade-off for fee purposes is this: home tuition prices in travel and presence, online tuition prices in reach and flexibility, and neither is inherently the better-value option; it depends on whether presence or reach matters more for this particular student and subject.

contentBlocks.heading: What should a demo clarify before you agree to a fee?
contentBlocks.body:
Judging IB tuition fees in Gurgaon fairly starts at the demo. A demo or trial session should do more than show whether a tutor is likeable; it should give a family enough evidence to judge whether a quoted fee is justified. IB Gram verifies a tutor's board experience, the levels and subjects actually taught, and any examining or moderating experience before a profile ever reaches a shortlist, but a demo is where a family checks that verification against what actually happens in a session.

Ask directly what session length is being quoted for, sixty or ninety minutes are both common, and whether that length is fixed or can flex around a topic that needs more time on a given day. Ask whether coursework mentoring, help with an IA approach or an Extended Essay draft, is included in the standard fee or arranged separately, since this varies and is worth knowing before, not after, a student is mid-draft. Ask how progress will be communicated to parents and how often, since a fee that includes no feedback loop is worth less than one that does, even at the same number.

During the demo itself, watch whether the tutor teaches to the syllabus and level you described, or falls back on generic material; whether they check the student's understanding before moving on; and whether the pace matches your child rather than a standard lesson plan. A tutor who cannot clearly explain what is included in their fee, session length, coursework support, feedback, before a family commits is not necessarily wrong for the role, but it is a reasonable reason to ask more questions before agreeing to anything.

contentBlocks.heading: What actually sets an IB tuition fee in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Ordered roughly from biggest effect to smallest, the factors that move an IB tuition fee in Gurgaon are: stage and level, since DP Higher Level work close to the exam session asks more of a tutor than PYP or general MYP support; subject scarcity, since a specialist in a less commonly taught HL subject or in TOK and Extended Essay guidance is harder to find than a general subject tutor; the tutor's own experience, including whether they have examining or moderating experience against IB criteria specifically, not just years of general teaching; session length, since a ninety minute session naturally costs more than a sixty minute one; travel versus online delivery, since a home visit prices in the tutor's travel time in a way an online session does not; and coursework mentoring, since structured IA or EE support is a more specialised service than general subject revision.

Pricing is usually structured in one of a few ways: per session, which suits a family that wants flexibility and is not yet sure how many sessions a week the student needs; monthly, which suits a settled arrangement where the schedule is fixed; or as a package tied to a specific goal, a set of sessions running up to a mock or exam session, for instance. None of these structures is inherently better; the right one depends on how settled the arrangement already is and how far out from an assessment the family is planning.

Red flags run in both directions. A fee that looks unusually low for a specialist DP Higher Level subject close to the exam session is worth questioning: it can mean a tutor who is newer to this specific board, spread across too many students to give real attention, or vague about what is actually included. A fee that looks unusually high is equally worth questioning, particularly if the tutor cannot clearly explain what makes their support different, examining experience, a track record with this exact syllabus, coursework mentoring included as standard. The questions in the demo, session length, what is included, how progress is communicated, are what actually expose whether a fee reflects real value, not the number alone.

contentBlocks.heading: How do you know a fee is delivering value over time?
contentBlocks.body:
IB tuition fees in Gurgaon are only good value if they keep delivering, and that has to be judged over weeks, not from a single session. In the first few weeks, value looks like better habits: a student who used to leave an IA draft to the last night now starts earlier, or one who confused command terms now reads evaluate and describe correctly. These are not yet visible in a school report, but they are what a fee is actually buying in the early stage of an arrangement.

By four to six weeks, a family should be able to point to something more concrete tied to the fee: a specific criterion where marks have moved, a topic the student now attempts without shutting down, or a timed past paper completed within the limit for the first time. If a review at this point shows nothing concrete, that is the moment to have a direct conversation about the fee and what it is buying, rather than assuming a higher fee elsewhere would automatically fix it. Sometimes the honest issue is teaching style, not price.

It is worth being clear about what a fee cannot buy. No tutor can guarantee a grade, whatever they charge, and a student who starts support close to the exam session has less runway than one who starts a year out regardless of fee. A high fee does not buy a guaranteed outcome, and a family should be wary of any suggestion that it does. And some students, particularly ones who are simply overloaded rather than struggling with the subject, are better served by a lighter schedule than by paying for more hours this term.

Agreeing a fee in Gurgaon should not involve guesswork on either side, and getting the details right before the first paid session saves both the family and the tutor from misunderstandings later. Before that first session, share what the tutor will need: recent school assessments, the current syllabus or unit outline, and, for DP or MYP students, any IA, EE or Personal Project brief already issued. This lets the fee reflect real preparation rather than the tutor spending the first paid hour finding out where the student actually stands.

The free consultation or first query is where IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, and it is also the right moment to ask directly how the fee is structured, per session, monthly or as a package, and what it includes: session length, coursework mentoring, and how often progress updates come to parents. A demo or trial session happens before any fee is agreed, subject to tutor availability, and it is worth using that session to confirm everything discussed in the query actually matches what happens in the room.

Once lessons begin, at home, online or hybrid depending on what suits the family, keep the arrangement under review rather than fixed for the whole year. A simple check-in every four to six weeks, whether the fee still reflects the support being given, whether the format still suits the student, keeps both sides honest. And if something is not matching what was agreed, whether that is session length, included support or communication, raising it directly and asking for a different match if needed costs far less than quietly living with a mismatch.

contentBlocks.heading: How Stage and Tier Shift an IGCSE Tutor's Fee
contentBlocks.body:
Stage and tier are usually the single biggest factor behind an igcse tutor fees gurgaon quote, ahead of almost everything else a family asks about. A tutor teaching Grade 9 Core-tier content is working with a narrower, more predictable syllabus than a tutor guiding a Grade 10 Extended-tier student toward the ceiling of what Cambridge or Edexcel actually examines. That difference in demand shows up in how tutors price their time, and it is the first thing worth understanding before comparing any two quotes side by side.

Cambridge's Core and Extended split, and Edexcel's Foundation and Higher equivalent, matter here specifically because they are not just easier and harder versions of the same content; Extended and Higher tiers require depth a tutor genuinely needs experience to teach well, not just content knowledge. A tutor who has only ever taught Core or Foundation may not be the right, or the fairly priced, choice for a family whose child has just moved up to Extended.

Grade 10 proximity to the real exam series adds its own pressure on top of tier. A tutor picking up a Grade 10 student a few weeks before the May/June or October/November series is working under real time pressure, often needing to compress a term's worth of consolidation into a handful of sessions, and that urgency is a legitimate factor in how a fee is set. A family starting early, in Grade 9 or the first half of Grade 10, generally has more room to find a fair fee without the pressure of an approaching exam series forcing a faster, more expensive arrangement.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Scarcity and Syllabus Depth: Two Different Fee Drivers
contentBlocks.body:
Two separate things move a fee at the subject level, and families often confuse them. The first is scarcity: how many tutors in Gurgaon genuinely teach a given syllabus well. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 both have relatively deep tutor pools because the subject is universal, so fees tend to sit in a predictable range. A less common Cambridge science combination, or a specific English syllabus like 0511 with its speaking component folded into the grade, has a shallower pool of genuinely experienced tutors, and scarcity alone can push a fee upward independent of how difficult the content actually is.

The second driver is depth of assessment structure. Cambridge sciences split marks across multiple choice, theory and a practical component through Paper 5 or Paper 6, and a tutor who can coach practical technique, not just theory, is offering something a theory-only tutor cannot. That extra capability is a legitimate reason for a fee difference, and a family should ask directly whether practical coaching is included rather than assuming it comes bundled with a general science tutor.

English syllabuses illustrate both drivers at once. First Language English 0500's coursework portfolio route needs a tutor comfortable mentoring extended writing across drafts, a genuinely different skill from drilling comprehension technique for a reading paper, and Literature in English 0475 needs someone who can discuss set texts in depth rather than teach generic essay structure. A fee that reflects this kind of specific capability is not the same as a fee inflated simply because a subject sounds impressive; asking a tutor directly what part of the syllabus they are strongest in is a fair way to judge which is which.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Which Fee Structure Fits?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the format most Gurgaon families searching igcse tutor fees gurgaon start from: a verified tutor teaching the student at the family's own kitchen table, in their own sector or society, with travel folded into how the session is priced. A home tutor's fee reflects not just subject and tier but the practical cost of committing to a regular evening slot in a specific corridor, which is why two families paying for the same subject and tier can see different figures once location enters the picture.

Online tuition removes the travel variable from the fee conversation almost entirely, which is part of why families comparing quotes often find online priced differently from an equivalent home tutoring arrangement. A tutor teaching from anywhere in or beyond Gurgaon can reach a family regardless of corridor, and a shared whiteboard with annotated past papers covers most subject content just as well as an exercise book would at the kitchen table. What online does not remove is subject scarcity or tier: a genuinely experienced Extended-tier specialist online still reflects that scarcity in how their time is priced, travel or no travel.

Hybrid, a regular home tutor plus an occasional online session with a subject specialist who is not local, is how many families balance both fee logics at once. It keeps the convenience of a consistent home tuition relationship while accessing a harder-to-find specialist without paying a full travel premium for an occasional session. It also gives a family a sensible fallback when a home session cannot happen, a school trip, illness, sudden traffic, without losing the week's session outright.

Stated plainly, the trade-off is this: home tuition prices in convenience and consistency; online prices in access without travel; hybrid blends both at the cost of a student adapting between two formats across a term. None is inherently cheaper or more expensive in isolation, because the biggest drivers, tier, subject scarcity and session length, apply across all three.

heroSubtitle: A fee should have a clear explanation behind it, not just a figure. This page sets out every factor that moves an IGCSE tutor's fee in Gurgaon, how pricing is actually structured, what a demo should clarify before any payment, and the red flags that separate a fair fee from a vague one.
introSummary: Igcse tuition fees gurgaon searches usually want one answer, what actually moves the figure, and the honest answer is several factors together: stage and level, subject scarcity, the tutor's experience including any examining background, session length, and whether lessons run at home, online or hybrid. IB Gram leads with home tutoring, a verified tutor teaching at your own address in your sector or society, while online and hybrid remain genuine alternatives with their own honest trade-offs on cost and convenience. Nowhere on this page is a rupee figure quoted, since fees vary by exact match and should be discussed directly once your child's board, tier and subject are known. What this page gives instead is the structure behind the number: what raises it, what should never inflate it, and the questions that expose a fee that does not add up.

contentBlocks.heading: How Board, Grade and Tier Change an IGCSE Tutor's Fee
contentBlocks.body:
Stage and level is usually the first factor that moves a fee, and it starts with the board itself: Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are both typically two-year courses across Grades 9 and 10, but they differ enough in exam series, Cambridge running February/March, a series offered only in India, plus May/June and October/November, against Edexcel's January and May/June, that a tutor genuinely fluent in one board's rhythm is not automatically as strong on the other's.

Grade matters too. A Grade 9 student starting IGCSE content for the first time often needs a different kind of support, building foundations, than a Grade 10 student close to the exam series, revising and drilling past papers under time pressure, and tutors experienced specifically with exam-proximity work tend to be in higher demand during the months leading into a session.

Tier changes things further. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core, topping out at grade C, and Extended, reaching A*, and a tutor who teaches Extended confidently at the hardest end of the syllabus is not the same as one comfortable only with Core content. This tier-specific depth is one of the clearer, more defensible reasons a fee can differ between two tutors teaching what looks, on paper, like the same subject.

None of this justifies a vague answer about pricing. A tutor or agency should be able to explain, in plain language, which of these factors is actually driving the figure being discussed for your child specifically, not just point at the subject name.

contentBlocks.heading: Why Subject Scarcity Moves an IGCSE Tuition Fee in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics tutors are relatively easier to find at both tiers, since Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) are common subjects with a large pool of tutors comfortable across Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher. This relative availability tends to keep Maths tutoring fees more predictable than some other subjects.

Sciences can be scarcer at the specialist end. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, examined from 2023, weight multiple choice at 30%, theory at 50%, and practical assessment, through Paper 5 or Paper 6, at 20%, and a tutor genuinely comfortable coaching all three components, not just theory, is harder to find than a general science graduate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, untiered with practical skills inside the written papers, need a slightly different kind of specialist again.

English scarcity depends heavily on the exact syllabus code. Cambridge First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511, and Literature in English 0475 are different subjects, and a tutor who specialises in coursework-route English under 0500 is a narrower specialism than a general English tutor, which can affect how readily a matching agency can find someone for that specific code, in your specific corridor, at your specific slot.

Subject scarcity in your igcse tuition fees Sushant Lok or igcse tuition fees DLF Phase 3 search is really a supply question: how many tutors near you teach this exact syllabus code, at this tier, and are free at the slot you need, not a fixed rule about which subjects always cost more.

contentBlocks.body:

Most Gurgaon international schools enter Grade 10 students for the May/June exam series, with internal mocks or pre-boards set months earlier by the school itself. Session frequency, and therefore the overall hours booked in a given month, tends to rise in the weeks before a mock or the exam series and fall afterward, which is a structural reason the total booked in a busy month looks different from a quieter one, in hours rather than any fixed rate changing.

A tutor's per-session rate does not need to change for the monthly total to shift; more sessions in a demanding month, fewer in a quieter one, moves the total on its own. A family budgeting across a school year should think in terms of this rhythm, not a single flat figure that applies identically every month regardless of the calendar.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: How the Format Changes the Fee
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition, a verified tutor teaching at your own address, typically carries the highest fee per hour of the formats compared here, since it includes a tutor's travel time and the fully individual attention of one-to-one teaching. For a student who needs undivided attention, or who is easily distracted by a screen, this is often worth it, but it is the format where cost structure matters most to understand clearly before committing to a term.

Online one-to-one tuition removes the tutor's travel consideration from the equation, which can make it somewhat less costly than an equivalent home session, while keeping the individual attention. A shared whiteboard with annotated past papers covers most of what a home session offers for most subjects, though not every student engages with a screen the same way they engage with a tutor in the room.

Hybrid arrangements blend a weekly home or online one-to-one session with an occasional small group or coaching centre session for broader revision, which can moderate the overall monthly total while still keeping individual attention on the family's priority subjects. This is a genuine middle path, not a compromise on quality, provided the split is deliberate rather than accidental.

A coaching centre batch or a live online group class is usually the least costly per hour of all the formats, since the cost is shared across several students, but it comes with the least individual attention and the least control over pacing, a trade-off worth weighing honestly against what your child specifically needs.

contentBlocks.heading: Does a Tutor's Experience Justify a Higher IGCSE Tuition Fee?
contentBlocks.body:
Experience is a real factor, but only some kinds of experience actually justify a higher fee. Years teaching this specific board, familiarity with the exact syllabus code and tier, and any examining or moderating experience with Cambridge or Edexcel are all defensible reasons a more experienced tutor might charge more than one newer to IGCSE specifically.

Years of general teaching experience, on a different board entirely, is a weaker justification, since strong CBSE or generic tutoring experience does not automatically transfer to Cambridge IGCSE's tiering or Edexcel's grading in the way a family might assume. Ask directly how many years of experience are with this exact board, not just teaching overall.

A red flag worth watching for is a fee that seems unusually high without a clear reason attached to it, board experience, tier depth, or examining background, stated plainly. Equally, a fee that seems unusually low is worth questioning too: ask whether the tutor has actually taught this syllabus code before, or whether the session length or group size quietly differs from what was first discussed.

contentBlocks.heading: Why the Programme Stage Is the Biggest Fee Factor
contentBlocks.body:
Stage moves an IB home tutor's fee more than almost anything else, and it helps to understand why. The IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers ages 3 to 12, organised around six transdisciplinary themes such as Who we are and Sharing the planet, taught through units of inquiry rather than a fixed syllabus, with no external examinations and the PYP exhibition arriving in the final year. Coaching at this stage tends to sit toward the lower end of the fee range, since the work is broader and less specialised than exam-focused tuition further up the school.

The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans five years, MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria scored out of 8, with the criterion total out of 32 converting to a final 1 to 7 grade. A MYP tutor in Gurgaon working criterion by criterion, especially around the Personal Project in MYP 5 or the Community Project earlier, is doing more targeted, assessment-literate work than general homework help, and fees usually reflect that. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and school-dependent, which is one more variable a tutor needs to know before quoting anything.

By the Diploma Programme (DP), fees generally climb again. The two-year course (DP1 and DP2) runs six subjects across six groups, three or four at Higher Level (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (150 hours), each graded 1 to 7, with Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) adding up to 3 more points toward a 45-point maximum, and 24 as the minimum for the diploma. An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon working HL content, especially in the run-up to the May session, is typically at the top of the fee range, since the subject knowledge required is deepest here and the stakes for the student are highest.

MYP (MYP 1-5) criterion-based marking (four criteria, A-D, each 0-8) needs targeted, assessment-literate coaching.
MYP eAssessment in MYP 5 is optional and school-dependent, adding a variable a tutor must account for.
DP (DP1 and DP2), Higher Level especially, sits at the top of the fee range given the depth required.
TOK and Extended Essay support is usually priced and scheduled separately from regular subject sessions.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Scarcity: Why Two IB Tutors Rarely Cost the Same
contentBlocks.body:
Subject scarcity is the second-biggest lever on an IB home tutor's fee, and it explains why two tutors teaching the same grade can be priced quite differently. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI), each at Higher Level and Standard Level, and AA HL tutors, particularly ones comfortable with the harder end of the syllabus, tend to be in shorter supply in Gurgaon than generalist maths tutors, which shows up in the fee. The same pattern holds for IB Physics, Chemistry and Biology at Higher Level: the core overlaps with Standard Level, but the extra depth demands a tutor who has actually taught that depth before, not one who is extrapolating from a textbook.

IB English A and B work differently. Fees here often track fluency with command terms, define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent, and the ability to mark a student's writing against them precisely, rather than raw subject rarity, since English tutors are more plentiful than, say, a Higher Level Chemistry specialist. A tutor who can show, in a trial class, exactly why a response sits at describe-level rather than evaluate-level is offering something narrower and more valuable than general essay feedback, and that specificity is part of what a fee is paying for.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sit in their own fee category again, since this work is closer to structured mentoring than syllabus delivery: draft feedback, argument structure, referencing, spaced across DP1 and DP2. A tutor guiding an EE well needs research supervision skills as much as subject knowledge, and that combination is rarer than either skill alone, which tends to place EE and TOK support toward the higher end of what a family pays for, hour for hour, even though the sessions themselves may be less frequent than regular subject tuition.

Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana has a concentration of IB and international schools, among them Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge. Families search ib home tutor fees Gurugram and ib home tutor fees Gurgaon almost interchangeably, since both names describe the same city. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; they are named only to explain the calendar pressure families here recognise, not to claim any relationship.

Most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May session, with November used mainly by a minority of schools and by retake candidates. Each school fixes its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually months ahead of May, and demand for tutoring, and with it, fee pressure, tends to rise sharply in the weeks before those mocks, simply because many families are asking for the same specialist subjects at once. A tutor's calendar fills, and a family booking late in that window sometimes finds fewer options at their preferred price than a family who started earlier in the term.

This is worth factoring into any fee conversation: a rate agreed in September, before mock season, may not be the rate on offer in January if demand has shifted, and a tutor's willingness to hold a slot at a fixed fee through a busy period is itself something to ask about. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports come through the school or the IB's own official channels, and a tutor working from these directly, rather than generic material, is usually worth the fee, since May results, released in early July, are the outcome the whole term's spending was aimed at.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Which Costs More, and Why?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram leads every conversation with home tutoring, because it is the format most Gurgaon families ask for first: a verified home tutor at the family's own table, in their own sector or society. Home tuition generally carries the highest fee of the three formats, for a reasonable structural reason rather than a market whim: a home tutor's fee has to account for travel time to and from the session, not just the session itself, and that time has to come from somewhere in the pricing.

IB online tutor arrangements in Gurgaon typically sit below home tuition on fee, since removing travel removes a real cost for the tutor, and this widens the pool of tutors a family can consider, since a specialist based anywhere becomes reachable. What online lessons cannot fully replace is a tutor watching a student's handwriting or working in real time, which matters more for some subjects, IB Maths and the sciences especially, than others. A family weighing a lower online fee against a scarcer HL specialist should weigh the subject need first and the fee difference second.

Hybrid arrangements split the two deliberately: home sessions for a core subject where in-person attention pays off most, online for a specialist add-on or for weeks when travel is impractical. The combined fee usually lands between a pure home tuition rate and a pure online rate, and it is worth asking a tutor directly how they structure a hybrid week rather than assuming it is simply an average of the two. None of these three formats is inherently the better value; value depends on what the student actually needs and how consistently the family can commit to the format chosen.
items: Home tuition: highest typical fee of the three, reflecting a tutor's travel time as well as teaching time.
Online tutoring: usually the lowest fee, since travel cost disappears; widens the pool of specialists available.
Hybrid: fee usually lands between the two, structured around which sessions happen where each week.
Subjects needing close attention to handwriting or working, IB Maths and sciences especially, benefit most from home tuition.
Ask a tutor directly how a hybrid week is priced rather than assuming a simple average.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Free Trial Should Clarify Before You Agree Any Fee
contentBlocks.body:
A demo class exists to answer a question a fee quote alone cannot: is this tutor actually worth what is being asked. IB home tutors in Gurgaon are verified by IB Gram for board experience, subject and level taught, and familiarity with local school calendars before a tutor is ever shortlisted, which removes the most basic mismatches before a family even reaches the trial stage. But verification checks that a tutor is qualified to teach the syllabus; it does not, on its own, tell a family whether the fee for this particular tutor represents good value for their child.

That is what the free trial or demo class is for. Watch how the tutor explains a wrong answer, not just a right one. Ask them to mark a past response against a real criterion or command term on the spot; a tutor who does this fluently has usually taught the exact syllabus for real. Ask, too, how sessions will be structured week to week, what preparation happens between lessons, and how progress will be reported back, since these service details are part of what a fee is paying for, not an afterthought to it.

Before agreeing any fee, ask about the practical edges as well: what happens if a session is missed, whether the rate is fixed for the term or can shift, and how a switch to a different tutor would be handled if the fit turns out to be wrong after all. A coaching or tuition provider that answers these plainly, before money changes hands, is behaving the way a fair pricing structure should. One that avoids the question, or rushes past the trial toward payment, is one worth being cautious about, whatever number is on the table.
items: Ask the tutor to mark a past answer against a real criterion or command term during the trial.
Confirm exactly which syllabus, strand and level the tutor has actually taught before, not just claims to teach.
Ask how sessions are structured week to week and how progress gets reported to parents.
Clarify whether a quoted rate is fixed for the term or can change as demand shifts.
Ask what happens to the fee arrangement if a family requests a different tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Moves an IB Home Tutor's Fee in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Ranked roughly from biggest effect to smallest, six things move an IB home tutor's fee in Gurgaon. Programme stage comes first: DP, especially Higher Level close to the May session, generally costs more than MYP, which generally costs more than PYP, because the depth of subject knowledge required rises at each stage. Subject scarcity comes second: a Higher Level Maths AA or Physics specialist is harder to find than a general subject tutor, and fees reflect that gap in supply. Tutor experience comes third, and this covers more than years taught; direct experience teaching this specific board, and, where relevant, examining or moderating experience, tends to command a higher fee than a long but board-generic teaching career. Families searching for the best IB home tutor fees in Gurgaon are usually asking how to judge this kind of value, not looking for the single lowest number.

Session length and frequency come fourth: a 90-minute session naturally costs more than a 60-minute one, and a family booking several sessions a week sometimes secures a better per-session rate than one booking occasionally, though this varies tutor to tutor. Format, home, online or hybrid, comes fifth, largely for the travel-cost reasons already covered. Coursework and IA mentoring, when it is a separate, structured commitment rather than an occasional add-on to regular sessions, tends to be priced on its own, since it demands sustained attention to one piece of work over weeks rather than a single lesson's content.

Pricing itself is usually structured in one of three ways: per session, useful for occasional or trial-based tutoring; monthly, common for regular ongoing arrangements; or as a package, often used around an intensive period like pre-mocks revision. None of these structures is inherently better; the right one depends on how consistent the family's need actually is. As for red flags: a fee that looks unusually low for a Higher Level specialist subject is worth double-checking against the tutor's actual board experience, since it may signal a generalist stretched into a subject they do not know deeply. A fee that looks unusually high is worth checking against a genuine trial class and a clear explanation of what is included, rather than accepted on reputation alone. In both directions, the free demo or trial class is the honest test: it shows what the fee is actually buying before a family commits to a term of it.
items: Programme stage: DP Higher Level near the May session typically costs most; PYP typically costs least.
Subject scarcity: HL Maths AA or HL sciences generally cost more than generalist subjects.
Tutor experience, including examining or moderating experience where relevant, moves a fee upward.
Session length and frequency change both the per-session rate and the overall term cost.
Coursework or IA mentoring, when structured as its own commitment, is usually priced separately.

contentBlocks.heading: Is a Higher Fee Always Better Value?
contentBlocks.body:
Not automatically, and it is worth saying that plainly. Whatever IB home tutor fees in Gurgaon a family is quoted, judge them against the student's actual progress, not against the number alone. Not every IB tutor in Gurgaon who charges more is automatically the better choice for a specific student. A higher fee usually buys more experience, sharper subject depth or a specialist strand match, HL Maths AA rather than a generalist, say, but only if that experience is actually what the student needs right now. A DP1 student who mainly needs steady, consistent practice and encouragement may get better value from a solid, moderately priced tutor who shows up reliably than from an expensive specialist who is brilliant but stretched thin across several families. Value is about fit as much as credentials.

The clearest way to judge value is against progress, not against the fee itself. Real progress in the first month of any arrangement looks like specific, checkable improvement, a criterion moving from a 4 to a 6, a command term finally landed correctly, past papers being timed and marked properly, rather than a vague sense that things are going well. No tutor can guarantee a grade, whatever the fee, and any arrangement that implies otherwise is not describing how IB assessment actually works. A review every four to six weeks, checking specific gaps against what has actually improved, is the honest way to know whether a fee is earning its keep.

It is also fair to say some families are paying for more tutoring than they need. A student who is broadly on track, with one or two soft spots, may do better with occasional, well-targeted sessions before a specific paper or mock than with a fixed weekly arrangement running all year regardless of need. Fee decisions work best when they follow the student's actual calendar, more support before mocks and the exam session, less afterward, rather than staying flat by habit.
items: A higher fee is worth it only if the extra expertise matches what the student actually needs now.
Judge value against specific, checkable progress: a criterion score, a command term, a timed past paper.
No tutor can guarantee a grade, at any fee; treat any such promise as a warning sign.
A review every four to six weeks shows whether a fee is earning its keep.

From that conversation, a shortlist of verified tutors matched to the exact request comes back, each one suited to the subject, level and format asked for. A free trial or demo class happens before any fee is agreed, which is the point to ask every question covered on this page: syllabus fit, how sessions are structured, how a fixed or flexible rate works, and what happens if a different tutor is needed later. This is not a sales step to get through quickly; it is the evidence a family actually needs before committing a term's budget to one tutor.

Once a fee and a tutor both feel right, lessons begin at home, online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability and the family's own schedule. The arrangement is not locked in stone: a family can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong, and the intensity of tutoring can rise before mocks and step down afterward as the school calendar demands. A fair fee, in the end, is simply one that matches a specific tutor's time and expertise to a specific student's need, checked against a trial class rather than assumed from a number alone.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: There is no single figure that is honest to quote, because fees move with programme stage, subject scarcity, a tutor's experience and whether lessons run at home, online or hybrid. A Higher Level specialist subject close to the May session generally costs more than general PYP support, and a home tutor's fee accounts for travel time in a way an online lesson does not. Rather than a number, ask what specifically is driving the quote you have been given: stage, subject, experience or format, since that tells you far more about whether it is fair than the figure alone.

faqs.question: Why do two IB tutors in Gurgaon quote such different fees for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Usually because they differ on one of a few specific factors, not because one is simply overpriced. Experience teaching this exact board and level, rather than a related one, is a common driver, as is whether the subject is in short supply locally, HL Maths AA and HL sciences especially. Format matters too: a home tutor's fee reflects travel time that an online tutor's does not. Before assuming either quote is wrong, ask each tutor directly about their board experience and use a free trial to judge whether the difference in fee matches a real difference in what is on offer.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for an IB tutor with examining experience?
faqs.answer: It can be, particularly for Higher Level subjects close to the exam session, since a tutor who has marked real scripts or moderated real work understands exactly how marks are lost and gained in a way pure subject knowledge does not always capture. It is not automatically worth it for every student at every stage; a MYP student needing steady criterion-based practice may not need an examiner's depth yet. Ask what the experience specifically adds for your child's current need, and use a trial class to see it demonstrated, rather than paying for the credential alone.

faqs.question: Are monthly or per-session fees better for IB home tuition in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: It depends on how consistent the family's need is. Per-session pricing suits occasional or trial-based tutoring, when a family is not yet sure how many sessions a week are needed. Monthly pricing suits an ongoing, regular arrangement and can be easier to plan around. A package, often built around an intensive period like pre-mocks revision, suits a short, focused push. None is inherently cheaper or better value; the right structure follows the actual pattern of need, which is worth discussing directly with a prospective tutor rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor's fee in Gurgaon change depending on whether we are in New Gurgaon or on Dwarka Expressway?
faqs.answer: Travel can be a small factor in a specific tutor's quote, but it rarely explains a large difference on its own. A tutor already based near Sector 84 in New Gurgaon may quote slightly differently for that corridor than for a family further away on Dwarka Expressway near Sector 110, purely on travel time, but subject, stage and experience move a fee far more than the sector does. If a quoted difference seems large and is attributed mainly to location, it is worth asking the tutor to explain the reasoning directly.

faqs.question: Does the fee cover a tutor waiting if a home session starts late because of traffic or school pickup?
faqs.answer: This is worth asking directly, since practice varies by tutor rather than following one fixed rule. Evening traffic on corridors like Southern Peripheral Road or Dwarka Expressway can genuinely stretch a short trip, and school pickup or activities sometimes push a session's start later than planned. Some tutors build a short buffer into a session without additional cost; others treat a late start as reducing the session's length. Ask this before the first paid session, not after a late start has already happened, so both sides know what to expect.

faqs.question: What is a fair way to judge whether an IB tutoring fee is too high?
faqs.answer: Judge it against a genuine trial class, not against a figure you have seen elsewhere. Watch whether the tutor can mark a past answer against a real criterion or command term fluently, confirm they have actually taught this exact strand and level before, and ask how sessions and progress reporting are structured. A fee tied to genuine board-specific expertise and a clear structure is easier to justify than the same fee tied to vague reassurance. If a tutor cannot demonstrate the expertise a fee implies during a trial, that mismatch matters more than the number itself.

faqs.question: Should I be suspicious of an unusually low fee for an IB tutor in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: It is worth a closer look, particularly for a Higher Level or otherwise scarce subject, since a fee well below what board-specific expertise typically commands sometimes signals a generalist tutor stretched into a subject they have not taught in depth before. It does not always mean the offer is bad; a newer tutor building experience may genuinely price lower while still teaching well. The way to find out is the same either way: a free trial class where the tutor demonstrates real familiarity with the syllabus, rather than accepting or rejecting the fee on the number alone.

faqs.question: Does switching from CBSE or ICSE mid-year change what IB home tuition costs?
faqs.answer: Not directly through the fee structure itself, though it can change how many sessions a family needs in the short term. A student switching boards mid-course often needs a period of catch-up alongside regular pacing, since the IB's own assessment style, criterion-based MYP marking or command-term-driven DP papers, differs from what the student is used to. This sometimes means a temporarily higher session frequency rather than a different rate, and it is worth discussing that ramp-up directly with a prospective tutor so the plan, and its cost over the term, is clear from the start.

faqs.question: What should a free trial class clarify before I agree to any fee?
faqs.answer: It should show, concretely, what the fee is buying: teaching quality, syllabus fluency and how the tutor plans to structure the term ahead. Watch the tutor explain a wrong answer, not just a right one, and ask them to mark a past response against a real criterion so you can judge their command of the syllabus directly. Ask how sessions are structured, how progress is reported, and whether the rate is fixed or can shift with demand. A trial that answers all of this honestly is worth more than any number quoted before it.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee arrangement if my child's tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: The arrangement does not have to be honoured out of obligation if the fit is genuinely wrong. IB Gram lets a family ask for a different tutor at any point, and lessons continue at home, online or hybrid without losing the term's progress or being locked into a fee for a match that is not delivering. Raise the concern directly and early rather than waiting out a full term hoping it improves on its own; a short conversation about what specifically is not working usually resolves faster than most families expect.

You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks a short set of questions about board, syllabus, level and schedule, and a shortlist follows within a working day or two, subject to tutor availability. contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE in Gurgaon: Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel and What Comes After Grade 10
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon usually means one of two boards: Cambridge IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Both are typically taken as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and both feed into further study rather than ending a student's schooling; most students move on to the IB Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or a switch to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Whether a family is looking for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon or an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Gurugram, the same board, series and tier questions apply before a fee can be sensibly quoted, and an IGCSE Grade 9 and 10 tutor needs to move between two different demands across those years: building foundation early and sprinting toward exam technique later.

Cambridge and Edexcel run their exam series on different calendars, and this is where fees connect to timing. Cambridge series run in February/March (a series offered only in India), May/June and October/November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. A family whose child sits the February/March series is planning a different revision runway to one sitting May/June, and a tutor's fee for the final stretch before either series usually reflects a tighter, more intensive schedule than a routine term-time session.

Grading itself differs too. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G, though some syllabuses now have 9-1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1 across the board. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at grade C, Extended reaches A*. Tier matters for fees because Extended-tier tuition usually goes deeper into content and past-paper technique than Core, and a tutor confident teaching Extended content commands a fee that reflects that ceiling. None of this is complicated once it is laid out, but a tutor who does not know which board, series and tier a student is on cannot price a fee sensibly, which is exactly why IB Gram's matching conversation asks for all three before a shortlist is built.

Cambridge series: February/March (India only), May/June, October/November.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth Behind an IGCSE Tutor's Fee in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Subject scarcity is one of the biggest single factors behind an IGCSE tutor's fee in Gurgaon, and the syllabus detail explains why some subjects are harder to staff than others. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, splits Core candidates into Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), and Extended candidates into Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator); Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier. A tutor confident teaching non-calculator method under time pressure, and drilling the calculator papers separately, is doing genuinely different work across the two papers, and that combined skill set is not common.

The sciences add another layer. Cambridge IGCSE sciences, examined from 2023, split into Paper 1 multiple choice for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, Paper 3 theory for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, and a practical component assessed through Paper 5 (a practical test) or Paper 6 (an alternative to practical), whichever the school has chosen. The weighting sits at 30% multiple choice, 50% theory and 20% practical, so a tutor who only drills theory content is leaving a fifth of the mark scheme untouched. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 carrying the practical skills questions inside the written papers rather than as a separate assessment.

English is where families are often surprised by how many syllabuses exist under one subject name. Cambridge offers First Language English 0500 (a reading paper, then either directed writing and composition or a coursework portfolio), English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511 (reading and writing plus listening, with 0511 counting speaking into the final grade and 0510 reporting speaking separately), and Literature in English 0475. Pearson Edexcel offers English Language A (4EA1), English Language B (4EB1) and English as a Second Language (4ES1). A tutor fluent in one English syllabus is not automatically ready for another, and asking which exact syllabus code the school follows before a trial session is one of the more useful questions a parent can ask.
items: Cambridge Maths 0580: Core sits Papers 1 and 3; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4.
Edexcel Maths 4MA1: Foundation or Higher tier, two calculator papers each.
Cambridge sciences weight theory 50%, multiple choice 30%, practical 20%.
Edexcel sciences are untiered, with practical skills assessed inside written papers.
English has several syllabuses: First Language, ESL 0510/0511, Literature 0475, or Edexcel equivalents.

The same question, phrased as igcse home tutor fees Manesar, comes up often, and the honest answer is that scarcity of willing tutors matters more than raw distance: a home tutor willing to travel here regularly for one or two students a week is a genuinely scarcer resource than one working the denser central sectors. Families in Manesar who need a specialist subject, rather than a generalist, often find that online or hybrid lessons open up a wider shortlist than home-only searches allow.

contentBlocks.heading: School Calendars That Shape IGCSE Tutoring Fees in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Families across Gurgaon send children to a number of schools offering international curricula, among them Pathways World School Aravali, Pathways School Gurgaon, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, Heritage Xperiential Learning School, The Shri Ram School Aravali and DPS International Edge. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel; these names are included only to describe the calendar pressures families in Gurgaon generally deal with, not to claim any relationship with a school or to state which board any particular school follows.

What matters for a fee is the shape of the school year, not the school's name. Most international schools in Gurgaon run unit tests through the term, a set of pre-mock or mock assessments ahead of the real exam series, and a longer revision stretch before the session itself. A tutor's weekly fee tends to stay level through routine term time and step up in the weeks immediately before mocks or the final exam series, because the sessions themselves get denser: more past papers, more marking against real mark schemes, more targeted revision on weak topics rather than working through the syllabus in order.

Holidays complicate the picture too. Winter break and festival breaks often see families either pause tuition entirely or, just as often, ask for intensive catch-up sessions when the ordinary school week is not competing for the student's time. A tutor who is asked to compress two weeks of a slower routine week into an intensive holiday block is doing a different job, and a fair fee usually reflects that. Coursework and portfolio deadlines, where a syllabus includes them, sit on their own calendar entirely and are worth flagging to a prospective tutor early, since coursework mentoring inside academic integrity rules is a different, additional commitment to ordinary revision teaching and is one of the clearer reasons a fee can rise for a particular stretch of term.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: What Changes an IGCSE Tutor's Fee in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is IB Gram's lead format for IGCSE support in Gurgaon: a verified tutor comes to the student's own home, in their own sector or society, and teaches on the family's schedule with no commute for the student after a full school day. This is usually the most comfortable format for younger Grade 9 students and for subjects where a tutor needs to see a student's handwritten working in real time, such as Mathematics method marks or annotated science diagrams. Because a home tutor's fee has to account for travel time across Gurgaon's corridors, and because a home lesson typically runs as a fixed slot in the tutor's week, home tuition fees tend to sit at a different point to online fees for otherwise identical teaching.

An IGCSE online tutor in Gurgaon removes the travel cost entirely, which is one honest reason online lessons are often priced differently, and it opens up specialists who would never realistically travel to a given corridor, particularly for scarcer combinations like Extended-tier sciences or a specific English syllabus. A shared whiteboard and annotated past papers cover most of what a home session does, though a live online lesson asks more of the student's own concentration, since there is no one physically in the room keeping the session on track, and younger students in particular can drift during a screen-based hour in a way they rarely do at a kitchen table.

Hybrid arrangements, most home sessions with occasional online ones worked in around travel, exams or illness, are common and usually priced as a blend of the two rather than as a separate tier. For a family in a corridor like Manesar where home options are thinner, starting hybrid, with an online specialist for the hardest subject and a nearer home tutor for the rest, is often the most sensible way to balance fee, fit and travel. None of the three formats is universally cheaper or better; the honest answer is that the right one depends on the subject, the student's age and how well they concentrate without someone in the room.
items: Home tutoring: no student commute after school, but travel shapes the tutor's own fee.
Online tutoring: removes travel cost, opens up scarcer subject specialists.
Younger students often concentrate better in person than on a screen.
Hybrid blends home and online, useful where home options are thin.
The right format depends on subject, age and how the student concentrates, not on price alone.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Verifies an IGCSE Home Tutor in Gurgaon Before You Agree a Fee
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists only tutors whose profiles have been verified before they are ever suggested to a family, and a demo or trial session sits before any longer commitment so the family can judge fit directly rather than trusting a profile alone. Verification covers board experience specific to Cambridge or Edexcel, the levels and tiers a tutor has actually taught, and background checks appropriate to someone who will be teaching inside a family's home. None of this guarantees a particular outcome for a particular student, since no tutor can guarantee a grade, but it does mean a family is not choosing blind from a phone list.

What a parent should check themselves, alongside IB Gram's own verification, is more specific than it sounds. Ask which syllabus code the tutor has actually taught, not just which board; a tutor who has taught Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 Extended is not automatically ready for Edexcel's 4MA1 Higher tier, since the paper structure and command style differ. Ask how recently they have taught the current specification, since syllabuses are revised periodically and a tutor working from an outdated version of the content can teach confidently and still miss what the current mark scheme actually rewards. And ask, plainly, what happens if the trial session does not go well: a fee agreement should never be locked in before that question has a clear answer.

The demo session itself is where a fee starts to make sense as a number rather than an abstraction. A tutor who spends the trial working through a genuine past paper question with the student, marking it against the actual mark scheme rather than a general impression, is showing exactly the skill a family is paying for. A trial that stays generic, with no reference to the syllabus code or paper structure at all, is a signal to ask more questions before agreeing anything longer term, whatever the quoted fee happens to be.
